invite:0.en: The Manager called us all to the back room after closing. 'I want to *invite* you both to see the new branch location tomorrow,' he said, spreading a rough map across the boxes of instant noodles. Tang looked excited. I tried to look excited too.
invite:0.cnHint: 店长把我们____到新分店选址去参观。
invite:0.hook: But Lin had already seen the location — and said nothing.
invite:0.line: 'I *invite* you to come early — there is something you should see first.'

million:0.en: The Manager taped a printed sign to the freezer door: GRAND OPENING SOON. Tang whispered that the new branch cost nearly a *million* to set up. I stared at the sign, then at our little store with its wobbly shelf, and felt the weight of that number.
million:0.cnHint: 新分店的投入据说高达____元，让人咋舌。
million:0.hook: Then I noticed the Manager's hands were shaking slightly.
million:0.line: 'A *million* sounds big, but the Manager says it will pay back in two years.'

represent:0.en: The Manager asked me to carry a small basket of our best snacks to the landlord of the new building. 'You *represent* this store,' he said, adjusting my collar like a proud parent. Tang watched from behind the counter with an unreadable expression.
represent:0.cnHint: 店长让我去____这家店，带礼物拜访新房东。
represent:0.hook: The landlord opened the door and stared at the basket, then at me, then laughed.
represent:0.line: 'Remember, you *represent* us — so please do not drop the milk tea.'

surprise:0.en: Lin walked in just as we were packing sample bags for the new branch opening. Her visit was a complete *surprise* — she had told Tang she was taking the day off. She looked at the bags, smiled slowly, and picked one up without asking.
surprise:0.cnHint: 林突然出现，带给大家一个____。
surprise:0.hook: She slipped a folded note into one of the bags before walking out.
surprise:0.line: 'What a *surprise* — I thought nobody would be here so early.'

topic:0.en: The main *topic* at our little staff meeting was the new branch menu. Should it sell hot food? Tang wanted dumplings. The Manager wanted something simpler. I said nothing, but wrote 'egg sandwich' on my notepad and slowly pushed it to the centre of the table.
topic:0.cnHint: 会议的____是新分店卖什么食物。
topic:0.hook: The Manager looked at my notepad for a long moment, then nodded once.
topic:0.line: 'The only *topic* I care about is whether we get a coffee machine.'

meat:0.en: Tang spent an hour arranging the new display case for the branch trial run. He lined up the rice boxes by *meat* type: pork, chicken, beef. 'Order matters,' he said seriously. I moved the tofu box to the front as a joke. He moved it back without blinking.
meat:0.cnHint: 唐把盒饭按____的种类整齐排列好。
meat:0.hook: The first customer walked in and asked for a vegetable box only.
meat:0.line: 'No *meat*, no problem — we have three kinds of tofu rice today.'

drink:0.en: After we finished cleaning the new branch space, the Manager brought out four small cans of iced tea. 'Come, *drink* with me,' he said quietly, holding his can up. It was not a party, just four tired people standing in an empty room, but it felt like one.
drink:0.cnHint: 大家打扫完新店后，店长请大家一起____。
drink:0.hook: Lin set her can down unopened and stared at the far wall.
drink:0.line: 'Let us *drink* to the new store — even if our arms still hurt.'

sleep:0.en: I got home at six in the morning after helping prep the new branch. I managed exactly two hours of *sleep* before my phone buzzed. It was Tang: 'Forgot to tell you. Soft opening is today.' I sat up, stared at the wall, and put my uniform back on.
sleep:0.cnHint: 我只____了两小时就被通知新店今天就开业了。
sleep:0.hook: When I arrived, Lin was already there, looking perfectly rested.
sleep:0.line: 'Two hours of *sleep* and I still remembered to bring the price labels.'

shop:0.en: The Manager called me into the back room and unrolled a hand-drawn map on the table. 'We are opening a second *shop* next month,' he said, tapping a street corner three blocks away. He looked more nervous than excited, which made me nervous too. Tang leaned in the doorway, quietly eating a meat bun.
shop:0.cnHint: 店长展示了一张地图，宣布下个月要开一家新____。
shop:0.hook: But the address on the map — Lin had circled it first.
shop:0.line: 'This new *shop* will change everything for us,' the Manager said softly.

electronic:0.en: The Manager arrived at midnight carrying a large box. Inside was a brand-new *electronic* price-tag display, the kind where numbers change on a tiny screen. Tang read the manual upside down and still understood it faster than anyone. I just kept pressing the demo button and watching the digits blink like tiny fireworks.
electronic:0.cnHint: 店长带来了一套新的____价签显示器，大家都在研究怎么用。
electronic:0.hook: Then Tang noticed one tag was already showing the rival store's prices.
electronic:0.line: 'Every *electronic* tag must be set before we open,' the Manager said firmly.

wild:0.en: Tang burst through the door at two in the morning with a truly *wild* idea: the new branch should stay open until sunrise and sell hot soup. He had already written a menu on a paper bag. The Manager stared at it for a long time. I waited, holding my breath, hoping someone would say yes.
wild:0.cnHint: 阿糖提出了一个____的想法：新分店要卖热汤还要开到天亮。
wild:0.hook: The Manager folded the paper bag and put it in his pocket without a word.
wild:0.line: 'That is a *wild* plan, but I kind of love it,' I admitted.

rich:0.en: The Manager spread a tasting tray on the counter: six new rice balls, each with a different filling. 'The new *rich* flavours are for the new shop,' he announced proudly. Tang ate three before the scoring even started. I managed to write down my notes before eating mine, which felt like a small personal victory.
rich:0.cnHint: 店长摆出试吃拼盘，说新分店要主打____的口味系列。
rich:0.hook: One rice ball had a filling none of us could identify, and the Manager just smiled.
rich:0.line: 'Each one has a *rich* taste that customers will remember,' the Manager promised.

special:0.en: A quiet woman came in just before dawn and asked if the new branch would carry the same *special* sesame crackers we stock on the top shelf. She said she walks past the future address every morning. I told her yes, absolutely, even though I had no idea. After she left, I asked the Manager. He paused.
special:0.cnHint: 一位顾客专程来问，新分店是否也会卖那款____芝麻饼干。
special:0.hook: The Manager paused, then said the crackers might not be made anymore.
special:0.line: 'We will keep every *special* item that our regulars love,' the Manager said.

text:0.en: My phone buzzed with a *text* from an unknown number: 'Good luck with the new store. You will need it.' Tang read it over my shoulder and raised one eyebrow. The Manager pretended he had not seen it. Outside, the streetlight flickered once, as if agreeing that something strange was beginning.
text:0.cnHint: 我收到一条来自陌生号码的____，语气听起来像是威胁又像是祝福。
text:0.hook: The number matched the one on Lin's shop window three blocks away.
text:0.line: 'Show me that *text* again — the exact words matter,' said Tang quietly.

front:0.en: The Manager asked me to repaint the *front* of the new shop this weekend. He handed me a colour card: a warm yellow, the same shade as our current store. 'People should feel at home the moment they see it,' he said. Tang offered to help, then immediately admitted he was a terrible painter. I believed him.
front:0.cnHint: 店长让我这周末去粉刷新分店的____，颜色要和这里一样温暖。
front:0.hook: When I arrived, someone had already painted a message on the wall.
front:0.line: 'Keep the *front* bright so people smile before they even come in,' he said.

law:0.en: Lin walked into our store at midnight, calm as anything, and told the Manager that opening a second branch on that particular street might break a local *law* about business spacing. He left a printed page on the counter and walked out without buying anything. The Manager read it three times. Tang read it once and laughed nervously.
law:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林平静地走进来，声称新分店的选址可能违反了本地的____。
law:0.hook: Tang whispered that Lin had printed the wrong regulation — from the wrong city.
law:0.line: 'There is no *law* that stops us — I already checked,' the Manager said firmly.

satisfaction:0.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter just after midnight. 'The new branch opens next month,' he said quietly. I could see *satisfaction* in his eyes as he traced the street corner with one finger, as if the dream had already come true. Tang leaned over and whistled softly.
satisfaction:0.cnHint: 店长深夜展开手绘地图，眼神中流露出对新店计划的____。
satisfaction:0.hook: But the address on the map belonged to someone else's shop.
satisfaction:0.line: 'After all these years, the *satisfaction* of seeing this map is hard to describe.'

cultivate:0.en: The Manager told us he had spent three years choosing this new neighbourhood. 'You have to *cultivate* the right street,' he said, tapping the map. 'Talk to the neighbours, learn what they need, earn their trust slowly.' Tang nodded. I just tried not to knock over the cup noodles beside me.
cultivate:0.cnHint: 店长说开新店要花时间____街坊邻里之间的信任。
cultivate:0.hook: Then Tang mentioned he already knew someone on that street — someone who owed him money.
cultivate:0.line: 'You cannot rush it — you must *cultivate* the community before you open the door.'

productive:0.en: Tang and I spent the slow hours before dawn reorganising the stockroom for the new branch order. 'Actually *productive* night,' Tang said, stepping back to admire the neat rows of cans. The Manager appeared in the doorway, looked around, and added one single box to the wrong shelf without a word.
productive:0.cnHint: 阿糖说这个深夜整理仓库是很____的一晚，但店长悄悄把一箱货放错了位置。
productive:0.hook: That misplaced box had a label none of us could read.
productive:0.line: 'For once this felt like a genuinely *productive* night — until he walked in.'

vision:0.en: The Manager unrolled a second, larger drawing — a floor plan for the new store. 'This is my *vision*,' he said simply. The layout was clever: snacks near the door, hot drinks in the back, a small seat by the window. Tang whispered that it looked exactly like a place that had closed down last year.
vision:0.cnHint: 店长展示新店平面图，说这就是他对未来的____，但阿糖说这设计似曾相识。
vision:0.hook: The closed-down place had left in a hurry, and nobody knew why.
vision:0.line: 'Every detail here is part of my *vision* for what a real neighbourhood shop should be.'

distance:0.en: Lin appeared at the glass door around 2 a.m., hands in pockets, staring at the Manager's new-branch poster on the window. There was a careful *distance* between Lin and the Manager — they nodded, said nothing, and Lin walked on. Tang handed me a bag of chips and said, 'Long story. Very long.'
distance:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜盯着新店海报，与店长之间保持着一种刻意的____，阿糖说这背后有很长的故事。
distance:0.hook: The poster Lin stared at showed an address one block from Lin's own shop.
distance:0.line: 'I keep a certain *distance* — it is easier for everyone that way.'

forward:0.en: 'Are you nervous about the new branch?' I asked the Manager while he checked the morning delivery list. He looked *forward* through the big window at the empty street, quiet for a moment, then said, 'Nervous means you care.' Tang, eating a rice ball behind me, added, 'Or it means you checked the rent.'
forward:0.cnHint: 我问店长开新店是否紧张，他望向____方沉默片刻，给出了温暖的回答，而阿糖补了一刀。
forward:0.hook: The delivery list had a supplier name the Manager quickly covered with his hand.
forward:0.line: 'I try to look *forward*, not at every little thing that could go wrong.'

harmful:0.en: Tang found an old note tucked inside the stockroom shelf — a warning from a previous clerk that said the corner location was *harmful* to business because the street light outside flickered and scared customers away at night. The Manager read it, laughed once, and pinned it above the register.
harmful:0.cnHint: 阿糖发现旧留言称街角位置的环境对生意____，店长看完大笑并把它贴在了收银台上方。
harmful:0.hook: The flickering light outside began to flicker again at that exact moment.
harmful:0.line: 'A little flickering light is hardly *harmful* — it gives the place character.'

impossible:0.en: Lin slipped a folded note under the door just before dawn. Inside, one sentence: 'Opening two stores at once is *impossible*.' The Manager read it at the counter, folded it neatly, and slid it into his shirt pocket. Then he picked up the phone and called someone. Tang and I pretended to count the chewing gum.
impossible:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林塞来一张纸条说同时开两家店____，但店长看完后平静地拨出了一个电话。
impossible:0.hook: Whoever answered, the Manager smiled — for the first time all night.
impossible:0.line: 'They said it was *impossible*, but I have heard that word before.'

thinking:0.en: The Manager called a staff meeting at the back of the store. She spread a rough map across the break table and tapped it twice. 'A second location, same street, opens in a month,' she said. My *thinking* shifted fast — more shifts, new faces, bigger chaos. Tang caught my eye and smiled like he already knew.
thinking:0.cnHint: 店长在后室开会，宣布即将____新店，我脑子里转个不停。
thinking:0.hook: Tang's smile hid something the Manager had not mentioned yet.
thinking:0.line: 'My *thinking* is we should move the snack display before the new store opens.'

cover:0.en: The Manager unrolled a large plan across the counter. It was meant to *cover* every detail of the new branch — layout, stock, staffing, hours. Pages and pages. I reached the last sheet and found a question mark drawn in red pen where the night-shift name should be. I looked up slowly.
cover:0.cnHint: 店长把新分店的计划书摊开，内容____了各种细节，但夜班人员一栏留着问号。
cover:0.hook: The red question mark felt like it was looking straight back at me.
cover:0.line: 'This plan should *cover* everything, but someone still needs to fill that last slot.'

earth:0.en: A delivery worker came in just before dawn, boots caked with *earth* from the road works two blocks away. He bought two meat buns and ate them standing at the door, watching the sky turn pink. 'Hard night?' I asked. He just laughed softly and pointed at his boots. He came back every night that week.
earth:0.cnHint: 一个鞋上沾满____的送货工人在天亮前进店买包子，此后每晚都来。
earth:0.hook: On Friday he came in clean boots and left without buying anything.
earth:0.line: 'There is *earth* on everything out there — they dug up the whole corner last night.'

paper:0.en: Tang arrived for his shift carrying a thick roll of *paper* printed with floor plans. 'New branch layout,' he said, tossing it onto the counter. Charts, numbers, little boxes for shelves. I tried to read it but kept losing my place. Tang did not offer to explain. He just started humming to himself.
paper:0.cnHint: 唐带着新分店的____图纸来交班，却没打算向我解释任何内容。
paper:0.hook: One small room on the plan had no label at all.
paper:0.line: 'This *paper* has the full layout — study it before the Manager asks you questions.'

art:0.en: A quiet woman came in every night for green tea and a rice cracker. One evening she left a small card on the counter — a neat ink drawing of our store front. I stared at it for a long time. The *art* was careful and warm, every window in the right place. I never caught her name.
art:0.cnHint: 一位常客留下了一张手绘的店面____作品，让我看了很久很久。
art:0.hook: The next night her usual shelf spot was empty, and she never came back.
art:0.line: 'I do *art* at night when the city is quiet — this place felt worth drawing.'

street:0.en: The Manager pointed out the window. 'The new branch is on Pine *street*, four minutes from here on foot.' I tried to picture it — same quiet hours, different corner, different faces outside. Tang said the foot traffic there was better. Lin, who had been listening from near the door, said nothing and left.
street:0.cnHint: 店长说新分店就在____上，离这里步行只要四分钟，林听完后一言不发地走了。
street:0.hook: Lin paused at the door just long enough to glance back once.
street:0.line: 'Pine *street* gets twice the morning crowd — that branch will be busy fast.'

talent:0.en: The Manager watched me restock the cold drinks without being told, then said quietly, 'You have a real *talent* for reading what needs doing.' I did not know what to say, so I just kept working. Tang overheard from the next aisle and gave a small, unreadable nod. I wondered what the Manager was really building up to.
talent:0.cnHint: 店长夸我有____，能看出什么事情需要做，唐在旁边听见后点了点头，表情难以捉摸。
talent:0.hook: The Manager had never praised anyone that directly before, Tang told me later.
talent:0.line: 'Your *talent* for this work is exactly what the new branch is going to need.'

overall:0.en: At the end of the week the Manager taped a summary sheet to the wall. *Overall* sales were up, customer visits were steady, and two staff members were listed as 'ready for new roles.' My name was one of them. I read the sheet three times. Tang read it once, then walked to the back without a word.
overall:0.cnHint: 店长在墙上贴出周总结，____表现不错，我的名字被列为可胜任新职位的员工之一。
overall:0.hook: Tang had not spoken to me since he read that sheet.
overall:0.line: 'The *overall* numbers are good, but the real question is who moves to the new branch.'

meaning:0.en: The Manager pinned a hand-drawn map on the staff board tonight. It showed our store and a new branch opening two blocks away. 'Does this worry you?' Tang whispered. I stared at the map, trying to find some *meaning* in the Manager's calm smile. The dotted line between the two stores looked almost like a smile itself.
meaning:0.cnHint: 店长在公告板上贴了一张手绘地图，我试图从中找到____。
meaning:0.hook: Tang had seen that smile once before, and things changed fast.
meaning:0.line: 'I keep searching for the *meaning* behind that map, but the Manager just hums.'

strengthen:0.en: The Manager gathered us before dawn. 'The new branch needs us to *strengthen* our supply chain,' she said, tapping a chart on the counter. Tang nodded slowly. I wrote down every word. Outside, the street was still dark, but the store felt suddenly brighter, as if the plan itself gave off light.
strengthen:0.cnHint: 店长召集大家，说明需要____供应链以支撑新分店。
strengthen:0.hook: Tang's nod was slower than usual, and I wondered what they already knew.
strengthen:0.line: 'We must *strengthen* the link between both stores before next month.'

competitive:0.en: Lin walked in just after midnight, cool as ever, and dropped a flyer on the counter. It was from the new branch down the road. 'Their prices are very *competitive*,' Lin said with a quiet grin. I picked up the flyer. The numbers were good. I put it face-down before Tang could see.
competitive:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了新分店的宣传单，说那里的价格很____。
competitive:0.hook: Tang had already seen a copy hours ago.
competitive:0.line: 'Their prices are quite *competitive* — I checked three times to be sure.'

recently:0.en: Tang refilled the hot drink station and sighed. 'Have you noticed how many new faces there are *recently*?' I looked around. Three people I had never seen before were browsing the snack aisle. 'New apartments opened nearby,' Tang said. Then one of the strangers paid with an employee card from our new branch.
recently:0.cnHint: 阿糖注意到店里____出现了很多新面孔。
recently:0.hook: That employee card carried a name none of us recognised.
recently:0.line: '*Recently* the late-night crowd has nearly doubled — something is changing.'

nation:0.en: A quiet man came in every Thursday and bought one postcard. Tonight's card showed a mountain range crossing an entire *nation*. He paid without a word, tucked the card in his coat, and left. Tang told me he had been doing this for three years. On the back of every card, I later learned, he wrote the same four words.
nation:0.cnHint: 一位神秘顾客每周来买一张描绘某个____风景的明信片。
nation:0.hook: Nobody knew what those four words were.
nation:0.line: 'That postcard shows a river that crosses the whole *nation*, north to south.'

pound:0.en: A university student came in dragging a heavy bag that hit the floor with a dull *pound*. She bought three energy drinks, two rice balls, and a small notepad. 'Finals,' she said simply. Tang handed her a free pen without being asked. She looked up, surprised, then smiled in a tired way that I felt somewhere in my chest.
pound:0.cnHint: 一位备考的学生拎着沉重的包走进来，包落地时发出一声____。
pound:0.hook: She came back two hours later, bought nothing, and just sat by the window.
pound:0.line: 'That bag hit the floor with such a *pound* — how much is she carrying?'

purpose:0.en: The Manager locked the front door for the monthly staff talk — unusual for a store open around the clock. She unrolled a long sheet showing both locations, old and new. 'Every shelf, every night shift, every small kindness has a *purpose*,' she said. Tang caught my eye across the counter. For a moment the humming fridge sounded almost like music.
purpose:0.cnHint: 店长召开员工会议，说每一件小事都有其____。
purpose:0.hook: Then the Manager pointed to a third empty box on the sheet.
purpose:0.line: 'Every item we stock here has a *purpose* — never forget that.'

respond:0.en: The Manager called a quick meeting in the back room. He spread a hand-drawn map on the table and said the new branch would open next month. Everyone looked at each other. I did not know what to say, so I waited to see how Tang would *respond* to the news first.
respond:0.cnHint: 店长宣布新分店计划，大家都在等别人先____。
respond:0.hook: Tang's smile never reached his eyes.
respond:0.line: 'How did you *respond* when he told you the location?'

welcome:0.en: The Manager wanted the new branch to feel different from our store. He asked us to suggest ideas during the meeting. Tang offered free hot drinks on opening day. I suggested a small notice board for locals. The Manager nodded slowly. 'A *welcome* feeling,' he said, 'is worth more than any sign.'
welcome:0.cnHint: 开会讨论新分店的氛围，店长觉得____的感觉最重要。
welcome:0.hook: Lin had been silent the whole time — until now.
welcome:0.line: 'We need every customer to feel *welcome* from the first second.'

appeal:0.en: Lin arrived late to the planning meeting, dropped a thick folder on the table, and said she had already done market research. The numbers looked strong. The Manager studied each page without a word. I could see the *appeal* of her plan — it was bold, tidy, and hard to argue against.
appeal:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了详细的市场调研，她方案的____让人难以反驳。
appeal:0.hook: But one figure on the last page looked very wrong.
appeal:0.line: 'I understand the *appeal*, but the cost is too high right now.'

finally:0.en: We had been debating the new branch location for three weeks. The Manager kept changing his mind between the riverside lot and the college road. Tang and I filled two whiteboards with pros and cons. Tonight, after a long silence, the Manager put down his pen. '*Finally*,' he said softly, 'I know.'
finally:0.cnHint: 经过三周争论，店长____下定了决心。
finally:0.hook: He pointed at a spot none of us had suggested.
finally:0.line: '*Finally* — after all this talk — we have a real answer.'

guess:0.en: The Manager asked each of us to *guess* how many customers the new branch might serve on its first day. Tang said three hundred. Lin said five hundred and looked pleased with herself. I wrote my number on a slip of paper and folded it over. The Manager raised an eyebrow at my answer.
guess:0.cnHint: 店长让大家____新分店第一天的客流量，我的答案让他挑起了眉毛。
guess:0.hook: My number was either very brave or very foolish.
guess:0.line: 'Go on, *guess* — what do you think the first week looks like?'

protection:0.en: Lin pointed out that the new branch sat on a corner with no roof overhang. Rainy days would drive customers away before they reached the door. She suggested a wide canvas cover as *protection* against the weather. The Manager looked at the building plan again and circled the entrance in red pen.
protection:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林指出新分店入口需要雨天____，店长在图纸上圈出了那个位置。
protection:0.hook: The landlord had already refused one change request before.
protection:0.line: 'Some *protection* over the entrance would cost very little.'

resident:0.en: The Manager said the new branch needed to serve the neighbourhood, not just passing traffic. He wanted at least one local *resident* on the planning panel to share what the area truly needed. Tang suggested asking Old Mr Peng, who had lived on that street for forty years. Everyone agreed at once.
resident:0.cnHint: 店长希望邀请当地____加入规划小组，阿糖推荐了一位老街坊。
resident:0.hook: Old Mr Peng, it turned out, had strong opinions about everything.
resident:0.line: 'Every *resident* near the new branch should feel it belongs to them.'

willing:0.en: The Manager asked who was *willing* to transfer to the new branch for the first three months to help it get started. The room went quiet. Tang studied his shoes. Lin checked her phone. I looked at the map on the wall and thought about the quiet street, the unfamiliar faces, and the empty counter waiting for someone.
willing:0.cnHint: 店长问谁____去新分店支援三个月，会议室突然沉默了。
willing:0.hook: Then, slowly, one hand went up.
willing:0.line: 'I am *willing* to go, if nobody else wants to.'

admit:0.en: The Manager called us all into the back room before the grand opening of the new branch. He spread the floor plan across the table and looked straight at me. 'I have to *admit* that I was wrong,' he said. 'We need at least three clerks on the first night, not two.' Tang caught my eye and smiled.
admit:0.cnHint: 店长把大家叫到后室，____自己在人员安排上犯了个错误。
admit:0.hook: But why did Tang smile like she already knew?
admit:0.line: 'I have to *admit* I made a mistake with the opening-night schedule.'

association:0.en: A woman in a neat jacket came in just after midnight, carrying a folder of papers. She was from the local shopkeepers' *association*, she said, welcoming the new branch to the street. She left a small bag of sweets on the counter and walked back out into the quiet dark.
association:0.cnHint: 一位女士深夜来访，代表本地商户____前来道贺新店开业。
association:0.hook: Her name badge showed a different store — the one across the street.
association:0.line: 'I represent the shopkeepers' *association* on this block, and we welcome you.'

brand:0.en: The Manager spent an hour arranging the new shop window before we opened. He lined up every product with its label facing out and stood back to check. 'The *brand* has to look the same in every branch,' he said. I nodded and quietly straightened the shelf he had missed.
brand:0.cnHint: 店长坚持每家分店的陈列都要体现统一的____形象。
brand:0.hook: The shelf he missed was the one the inspector would check first.
brand:0.line: 'Every shelf must reflect the same *brand* image — no exceptions.'

deep:0.en: Tang found a storage room behind the new branch that no one had mentioned during the handover. She shone her phone light inside and laughed softly. 'It is *deep*,' she said. 'You could fit half the stock in there.' The Manager looked at the door and then at his clipboard, as if searching for a reason it was not on the plan.
deep:0.cnHint: 唐在新店后面发现了一间没人提过的储藏室，里面出乎意料地____。
deep:0.hook: The room had a second door that opened to the street.
deep:0.line: 'This storage room is surprisingly *deep* — it goes back much further than I expected.'

discover:0.en: I was unpacking boxes when I found a small notebook wedged behind the new counter. The first page had a list of every regular customer and their usual order. 'Did you *discover* something useful?' Tang called from the other aisle. I held it up. She grinned. 'That was the old clerk's secret weapon.'
discover:0.cnHint: 我在新店整理货架时____了一本记录着老顾客习惯的小本子。
discover:0.hook: The last entry in the notebook was dated only two days ago.
discover:0.line: 'Did you *discover* anything in those boxes we should know about?'

essential:0.en: Lin arrived at our new branch opening uninvited, holding a checklist. 'Good lighting is *essential*,' she said, pointing at the corner lamp that flickered. She was not wrong. The Manager thanked her through his teeth, then sent Tang to change the bulb before the first customer walked in.
essential:0.cnHint: 林在新店开业时指出，良好的照明是____条件之一，让店长有些难堪。
essential:0.hook: Lin had a checklist — and she was still on item three.
essential:0.line: 'Good lighting is *essential* for any store that wants to keep customers coming back.'

fine:0.en: Everything at the new branch looked *fine* on the surface — clean floors, full shelves, bright lights. But ten minutes before opening, Tang noticed the card reader was not connected. We fixed it with one minute to spare. The first customer paid by card and smiled, having no idea.
fine:0.cnHint: 新店开业前一切看起来都____，直到唐发现读卡机忘记接线了。
fine:0.hook: The next thing Tang checked made her go very quiet.
fine:0.line: 'The floor is *fine*, the shelves are full — now why is the card reader not working?'

largely:0.en: The opening night was *largely* peaceful. A few regulars from the old branch found us and seemed pleased the walk was shorter. Tang sold out of hot drinks by two in the morning. Only one thing went wrong: someone locked the Manager's keys inside the new stockroom.
largely:0.cnHint: 新店的开业之夜____上很顺利，只除了一件让店长很头疼的小意外。
largely:0.hook: The person who locked the keys inside was standing very quietly behind me.
largely:0.line: 'The night went *largely* well — except for the small matter of the stockroom keys.'

machine:0.en: The Manager brought in a large *machine* that could heat food, print receipts, and count change all at once. He placed it behind the counter with great pride, patting its side like an old friend. The staff watched, unsure whether to feel grateful or afraid of losing their jobs.
machine:0.cnHint: 店长带来了一台多功能____，员工们看着它，心情很复杂。
machine:0.hook: Then the machine beeped three times and went completely silent.
machine:0.line: 'This *machine* will run the store better than all of us combined.'

observe:0.en: Tang reminded everyone that the store would *observe* the new closing-time rule starting tonight — no customer could enter after 3 a.m. It was a small change, but the regulars who liked the quiet early hours were not happy. One old man stood at the glass door, frowning deeply.
observe:0.cnHint: 同事提醒大家，今晚开始要____新的打烊规定，一位常客很不满。
observe:0.hook: The old man pressed a handwritten note against the glass and walked away.
observe:0.line: 'We will *observe* the new rule tonight, no exceptions for anyone.'

fat:0.en: A customer came in every night for a small cup of warm soup. One evening he stopped, staring at the label on the pot. The Manager had switched to a low-*fat* recipe to match the new healthy menu. The customer set the cup down slowly, as if something dear to him had just disappeared.
fat:0.cnHint: 店长换了低____配方的汤，一位每晚来喝汤的常客若有所失地放下了杯子。
fat:0.hook: He whispered something, but the only word I caught was 'grandmother.'
fat:0.line: 'I only want the soup without the low-*fat* label — just the old kind.'

helpful:0.en: Lin stopped by the counter and, without being asked, reorganised the snack shelf so the best-selling items sat at eye level. It was a small but *helpful* move that saved customers a lot of searching. The Manager noticed and said nothing, which around here was the closest thing to a compliment.
helpful:0.cnHint: 竞争对手主动整理了货架，这个____的举动让店长默默点头认可。
helpful:0.hook: That night, three items Lin had hidden on the bottom shelf went missing.
helpful:0.line: 'It is more *helpful* to put popular things where people can see them.'

position:0.en: The Manager spent all morning deciding the *position* of the new display stand — near the door for cold drinks, or near the counter for warm ones. He moved it four times, drawing a rough map each attempt. By noon the stand was exactly where it had started, and he looked oddly pleased.
position:0.cnHint: 店长花了整个上午研究新展示架的____，最后放回了原点。
position:0.hook: When I arrived for my shift, a stranger was already standing right beside it.
position:0.line: 'The *position* of this stand will decide whether customers stop or walk past.'

threat:0.en: Lin walked in holding a flyer from a big chain store that was opening two blocks away. He laid it on the counter without a word. The Manager read it slowly, then folded it in half. 'Every new store feels like a *threat*,' he said quietly, 'until you find the one thing they cannot copy.'
threat:0.cnHint: 竞争对手拿来了附近新开大店的传单，店长把它视为一种____。
threat:0.hook: He then unlocked a drawer I had never seen him open before.
threat:0.line: 'A new store nearby is a *threat*, but only if we stop being ourselves.'

trend:0.en: Tang showed me a report on a tablet: the latest *trend* was customers buying hot drinks and small notebooks together, looking for a cosy place to sit and think. Our store had no seats, only a narrow ledge by the window. Tang was already measuring it with a ruler before I could say a word.
trend:0.cnHint: 同事发现最新____是顾客买热饮配小笔记本，正拿尺子量窗边的台子。
trend:0.hook: The ledge was exactly wide enough for two people, shoulder to shoulder.
trend:0.line: 'The *trend* says customers want a quiet corner, so let us give them one.'

ultimately:0.en: After weeks of planning extra staff, new shelves, and a second register, the Manager gathered us by the counter. All the small preparations, he said, would *ultimately* lead to one thing: a second store opening on the far side of the university. Tang looked at me. I looked at Tang. Neither of us had been told.
ultimately:0.cnHint: 店长宣布，所有这些准备____是为了在大学对面开新店，员工们面面相觑。
ultimately:0.hook: Then he added, very quietly, that only one of us would transfer there.
ultimately:0.line: 'Everything we have done will *ultimately* bring us to opening a second store.'

australia:0.en: The Manager pinned a map to the back wall and drew a red circle around a city far to the south. 'We are opening a second store,' he said proudly. An old regular squinted at the map and pointed. 'That dot is in *Australia*.' The Manager froze, then quietly took the map down.
australia:0.cnHint: 店长把一个新店选址标在了地图上，结果被常客发现地点在____。
australia:0.hook: The old regular winked and pulled a very familiar-looking lease from his coat.
australia:0.line: 'Wait — that dot is in *Australia*, not our city block!'

authority:0.en: The Manager called a meeting before the new branch opened. He stood on a step stool to look taller and announced that Tang would have full *authority* over the night shift at the new store. Tang blinked three times, slowly, then asked if the step stool came with the role.
authority:0.cnHint: 店长宣布由唐全权负责新店夜班，赋予他____。
authority:0.hook: Tang's first act of authority was to order the Manager off the step stool.
authority:0.line: 'Tang has full *authority* over the night shift — no arguments.'

confident:0.en: Lin walked in from the rival store across the street, looking very *confident*, and asked to see our storage room. 'Just curious about the layout,' she said with a smile. I told her the storage room was also where we kept the mop. She nodded as if that was exactly what she needed to know.
confident:0.cnHint: 来自对面竞争店的林走进来，神情____，说只是随便看看。
confident:0.hook: That night, our mop went missing.
confident:0.line: 'I am *confident* your storage room is bigger than ours — am I right?'

crowd:0.en: Word spread fast: the new branch would open at midnight with free hot drinks. By eleven-thirty a *crowd* had gathered outside, pressing their faces against the glass. The Manager looked thrilled. Tang looked at the single kettle we owned and quietly sat down on the floor.
crowd:0.cnHint: 新店开张消息传开，门外聚集了一大____人，唐看了看厨房里唯一的水壶。
crowd:0.hook: Someone in the crowd was holding a very large thermos and a suspicious grin.
crowd:0.line: 'Look at that *crowd* — this is going to be a great opening night!'

highly:0.en: The Manager said he *highly* recommended Tang as the new branch manager, which surprised everyone, including Tang. Tang had, just last Tuesday, put the hot-dog machine in the freezer by mistake. Still, the Manager slapped him on the back and said talent shows itself in unexpected ways.
highly:0.cnHint: 店长____推荐唐担任新店经理，尽管唐上周才把热狗机放进了冷冻柜。
highly:0.hook: Tang's first management decision was to unplug the freezer entirely.
highly:0.line: 'I *highly* recommend Tang — he learns from every single mistake.'

occur:0.en: It did not *occur* to anyone that the new store's address was the same as a laundry shop until the sign went up. The laundry owner stood in the doorway holding a bag of shirts, looking confused. The Manager stood beside him, also holding a bag of shirts, looking equally confused.
occur:0.cnHint: 没有人想到新店地址和一家洗衣店重合，直到招牌挂上去才____这件事。
occur:0.hook: Both signs said 'Open 24 Hours' and nobody knew which one to believe.
occur:0.line: 'Did it *occur* to you to check the address before signing the lease?'

responsible:0.en: The Manager said whoever broke the new branch's front window during setup would be *responsible* for the repair bill. Everyone looked at Tang. Tang looked at the broom in his hand. The broom looked at no one. In the end, the Manager paid, because he had been the one to ask Tang to sweep.
responsible:0.cnHint: 店长说打破新店橱窗的人要为维修费____，大家都看向了唐。
responsible:0.hook: Tang still holds that broom like it owes him an apology.
responsible:0.line: 'Whoever broke it is *responsible* — and Tang, please put that broom down.'

slightly:0.en: The Manager unrolled a big paper map on the counter and smoothed it flat with both hands. 'The new branch goes here,' he said, tapping a corner two streets away. I leaned over to look. The spot was *slightly* smaller than our store, but his eyes were bright with excitement. Tang quietly moved a cup of noodles off the map.
slightly:0.cnHint: 店长把新分店的地图铺在柜台上，那个地点比现在的店____小一点点。
slightly:0.hook: But the address on the map — Lin had circled it first.
slightly:0.line: 'It is only *slightly* smaller, so we can still fit everything in.'

vital:0.en: The Manager called us both to the back room and pointed at a single power switch on the wall. 'This controls the fridge units,' he said. 'Keeping it on is *vital* for the new branch too.' Tang wrote it down carefully. I made a mental note never to lean on that wall again. The Manager nodded as if he had just shared the secret of the universe.
vital:0.cnHint: 店长指着冷藏总开关，说保持它开启对新分店来说____。
vital:0.hook: Later, someone had taped a small warning sign over the switch — in Lin's handwriting.
vital:0.line: 'Keeping the power on is *vital*, or we lose everything in the fridges.'

mention:0.en: Tang handed me a list of items the new branch would need. Mops, price tags, a spare key. There was no *mention* of a coffee machine, even though every regular asked for one. I added it lightly in pencil at the bottom. Tang saw me do it and gave a small, grateful nod. The Manager never reads pencil notes anyway.
mention:0.cnHint: 阿糖给我的新分店物品清单里，没有对咖啡机的____。
mention:0.hook: The next morning, the pencil note had been erased — and typed in ink at the top.
mention:0.line: 'There is no *mention* of a coffee machine, but we really should have one.'

rare:0.en: The Manager brought out a small box of imported snacks to test-sell before the new branch opened. He said sourcing them had been difficult and the flavour was *rare* — something few stores in the city carried. Tang tried one and raised both eyebrows. I tried one and forgot what words were. The box sold out before noon.
rare:0.cnHint: 店长拿来一批进货困难的____零食试卖，开业前就全部售空了。
rare:0.hook: A quiet customer in the corner bought the last three packets without even checking the price.
rare:0.line: 'This flavour is quite *rare*; I had to order it from very far away.'

useful:0.en: Lin stopped by carrying a notebook filled with floor plans. 'Research,' Lin said, not looking up. Lin sketched the layout of our store with quick, confident lines. 'Very *useful* data for comparison.' The Manager smiled politely. Tang whispered to me, 'That notebook has been full since last month.' I started counting the ceiling tiles to look busy.
useful:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着笔记本来我们店'做调研'，说收集的数据非常____。
useful:0.hook: The notebook fell open for just a second — and our store's prices were listed inside.
useful:0.line: 'This floor plan is very *useful* for planning our own new branch layout.'

blood:0.en: While we rearranged shelves for the new branch display, Tang knocked over a bottle of tomato juice. It spread across the white floor tiles in a dramatic red pool. 'Don't panic,' Tang said, very calmly. 'It is just juice.' My heart was still running at full speed. The Manager walked in, looked down, and said, 'Mop. Now.' No *blood* was shed, but my dignity did not survive.
blood:0.cnHint: 货架重整时番茄汁洒了一地，我吓了一跳，好在没有流____。
blood:0.hook: The Manager took a photo of the clean floor after — for the new branch training manual.
blood:0.line: 'No *blood*, no real emergency — just grab the mop and carry on.'

fund:0.en: The Manager showed us a small jar on the shelf behind the register. 'This is the staff snack *fund*,' he said. 'Put in a little when you eat something; take from it when you need change for the new branch run.' There were already three coins and a folded receipt inside. Tang looked touched. I looked at the snacks. The math was not going to work out in the jar's favour.
fund:0.cnHint: 店长展示了一个零食____罐，让大家自觉投钱，用于新分店的日常小开销。
fund:0.hook: By midnight the jar held twelve coins — and a handwritten thank-you note from a regular.
fund:0.line: 'This small *fund* helps us cover little costs without bothering the Manager.'

anxiety:0.en: The night before the new branch was supposed to open, I could not stand still. I kept straightening the same row of drinks over and over. Tang noticed. 'First-time *anxiety*,' Tang said kindly, handing me a warm can from the reject pile. 'It happened to all of us.' The Manager walked past without a word, but he turned down the bright overhead light so the store felt softer. That helped more than anything.
anxiety:0.cnHint: 新分店开业前夕，我不停整理货架，阿糖看出了我的____。
anxiety:0.hook: At exactly midnight a figure pressed their face against the glass door — it was Lin, looking just as nervous.
anxiety:0.line: 'A little *anxiety* is normal; it just means you care about doing well.'

digital:0.en: The Manager spread a large paper map across the counter. 'The new branch needs a *digital* screen at the entrance,' he said, tapping the spot with his pen. Lin leaned over, nodding slowly. I tried to look useful by holding down a corner of the map.
digital:0.cnHint: 店长在柜台上铺开地图，讨论新分店入口处要装一块____屏幕。
digital:0.hook: Then Lin circled a different location entirely.
digital:0.line: 'A *digital* screen will make the new store look modern and bright.'

contact:0.en: The Manager handed me a small card. 'If anything goes wrong at the new branch tonight, *contact* me at once,' he said. I put the card carefully in my shirt pocket. It felt heavier than a card had any right to feel, like a tiny piece of responsibility.
contact:0.cnHint: 店长递给我一张卡片，叮嘱我新分店若出问题要立刻____他。
contact:0.hook: That night, something did go wrong.
contact:0.line: 'Please *contact* me the moment the delivery arrives, day or night.'

failure:0.en: Lin stared at the empty display stand near the door. The new snack line had sold zero bags all week. 'This is a *failure* I did not expect,' he said quietly, more to himself than to me. I kept wiping the counter and said nothing, which felt like the wisest move.
failure:0.cnHint: 新零食系列一袋未售出，林低声说这是他没预料到的____。
failure:0.hook: But he was already typing something on his phone.
failure:0.line: 'I refuse to call it a *failure* until we try one more idea.'

bird:0.en: A regular customer, an old man who came in every night for warm soy milk, liked to sit on the stool by the window. Tang called him an early *bird* because he always arrived just as the night shift began. Tonight his stool was empty, and Tang kept glancing at the door.
bird:0.cnHint: 唐管那位每晚准时来的老顾客叫"早来的____"，但今晚他的座位空着。
bird:0.hook: His soy milk was already warming on the counter.
bird:0.line: 'He is an early *bird*, never late — so where is he tonight?'

official:0.en: A man in a neat grey jacket walked in and asked for the Manager. 'I am an *official* from the district office,' he said, showing a small card. 'We need to inspect the new branch before it opens.' The Manager appeared from the back room, face calm, coffee still in hand.
official:0.cnHint: 一位____从区办公室来到店里，要求在新分店开业前进行检查。
official:0.hook: The Manager set his coffee down very slowly.
official:0.line: 'As an *official*, I must see the kitchen and storage room today.'

confidence:0.en: Before I handled my first solo closing shift at the new branch, Tang pulled me aside. 'You have the keys, you know the steps, you have *confidence* — trust it,' she said, giving my shoulder a quick pat. I nodded. The words helped more than she probably knew.
confidence:0.cnHint: 唐在我独自值守新分店前拍拍我的肩，让我相信自己的____。
confidence:0.hook: Then she added one thing she had forgotten to mention.
confidence:0.line: 'Go in with *confidence* and the customers will feel it too.'

display:0.en: I spent an hour arranging the new branch's front shelf. Tang watched me move each item three times. 'You need to *display* the most colourful things at eye level,' she said at last, stepping forward and switching two rows in about four seconds. The shelf did look much better after that.
display:0.cnHint: 唐指导我如何在新分店把商品____在最醒目的位置。
display:0.hook: She mentioned she had done this for Lin's store too.
display:0.line: 'Always *display* your best items where tired eyes will find them.'

awareness:0.en: The Manager called a small meeting before the morning rush. 'We are opening a second store next month,' he said, looking around the room. His *awareness* of our worried faces made him add quickly, 'Don't worry — nobody loses their job.' Tang let out a long breath. I was not so sure.
awareness:0.cnHint: 店长召集大家开会，宣布要开分店，并注意到大家脸上的____。
awareness:0.hook: But the Manager's smile never quite reached his eyes.
awareness:0.line: 'My *awareness* of your worries is why I called this meeting first.'

introduce:0.en: The Manager spread a map across the counter. 'I want to *introduce* a new store layout,' he said, pointing to a corner spot two streets away. The new place was twice the size of ours. Tang leaned in, excited. Lin stood back, arms crossed, already calculating something I could not read.
introduce:0.cnHint: 店长展开地图，向大家____新分店的布局方案。
introduce:0.hook: Lin's finger traced the map to a spot none of us had noticed.
introduce:0.line: 'Let me *introduce* the person who will manage the new location.'

expense:0.en: 'The new store will cost a lot,' the Manager admitted, setting down a thick folder of numbers. 'Every *expense* has been planned — rent, shelves, staff.' He tapped the final page. The total made Tang whistle softly. I stared at the number and wondered who, exactly, was being asked to carry part of that weight.
expense:0.cnHint: 店长摊开账本，逐项说明开新店的各项____。
expense:0.hook: One line in the folder had Tang's name written beside it.
expense:0.line: 'Each *expense* here has been approved — including the staff budget.'

toward:0.en: After the meeting, Lin walked slowly *toward* the back office and stood outside the closed door for a moment before going in. Nobody said anything. Tang refilled the coffee machine and kept his eyes down. Whatever Lin was about to say to the Manager, it was not meant for the rest of us to hear.
toward:0.cnHint: 会议结束后，林悄悄朝____走去，推开了办公室的门。
toward:0.hook: Two minutes later, Lin came out looking surprisingly calm.
toward:0.line: 'I have been thinking *toward* a different plan for the new store.'

track:0.en: The Manager pulled out a printed chart. 'I have been keeping *track* of which items sell fastest at this location,' he said, sliding it across the counter toward Lin. Every top item was circled in red. Lin studied the chart in silence. I noticed that the snacks I had quietly restocked twice a night were circled three times.
track:0.cnHint: 店长拿出图表，展示他对销售情况的____记录。
track:0.hook: Lin circled one more item on the chart — in blue, not red.
track:0.line: 'I keep *track* of every sale so the new store can start smart.'

afford:0.en: 'Can we really *afford* two stores at once?' Tang asked quietly while the Manager stepped out to take a call. It was the question everyone had been sitting on. I looked at the near-empty shelf of imported snacks — the expensive kind the Manager had just added — and thought the timing felt a little bold.
afford:0.cnHint: 店长离开后，唐小声问大家是否真的____同时开两家店。
afford:0.hook: The Manager walked back in and answered a question nobody had asked aloud.
afford:0.line: 'We can *afford* this — but only if everyone pulls together.'

feature:0.en: Lin unrolled a rough sketch on the break-room table. 'The new store should *feature* a small hot-food counter,' Lin said, voice careful and even. 'Something this location never had.' The Manager looked at the sketch for a long time without speaking. Tang caught my eye across the table. The sketch was very, very good.
feature:0.cnHint: 林展示了新店设计图，提议____一个热食窗口。
feature:0.hook: The Manager picked up Lin's pen and changed exactly one thing.
feature:0.line: 'I think we should *feature* fresh food — it sets us apart.'

innovative:0.en: 'The second store needs to feel different,' the Manager said, spreading photos of other shops across the counter. 'Something *innovative* — not just another box full of shelves.' Tang suggested a self-checkout corner. Lin suggested mood lighting. I looked at the photos and quietly pointed to one that had a small reading nook by the window.
innovative:0.cnHint: 店长希望分店有____的特色，大家纷纷提出各自的建议。
innovative:0.hook: Everyone went quiet when the Manager pointed straight at my photo.
innovative:0.line: 'An *innovative* design will bring in customers the old store never had.'

operation:0.en: The Manager spread a large floor plan across the counter. 'The new branch needs a smooth *operation* from day one,' he said, tracing each section with his finger. I watched him mark the stock room, the register, the cold drinks wall. Every detail had a place. Nothing was left to chance.
operation:0.cnHint: 店长把新分店的平面图铺在柜台上，仔细规划每个区域的____。
operation:0.hook: Then he circled one empty corner and said nothing.
operation:0.line: 'A good *operation* starts before you open the doors.'

population:0.en: The Manager pointed at a city map pinned to the back wall. 'This neighbourhood has a young *population*,' he said, 'students, riders, late workers. They want hot food at two in the morning.' I nodded. The new branch was going one block from a university gate.
population:0.cnHint: 店长分析新分店周边的____，认为那里很适合开店。
population:0.hook: Lin had been quietly writing notes the whole time.
population:0.line: 'A young *population* means busy nights every night.'

quick:0.en: 'Location is everything,' the Manager said, rolling up the map. He needed a *quick* answer from the landlord before a rival chain made an offer. I watched him dial twice, tap the counter, then smile. He hung up and wrote a number on a sticky note. It was a good number.
quick:0.cnHint: 店长需要房东给一个____的答复，否则竞争对手可能抢先。
quick:0.hook: Tang walked in just as the Manager tore up the sticky note.
quick:0.line: 'I need a *quick* answer — tonight, not tomorrow.'

scale:0.en: The Manager unfolded a printed chart showing the *scale* of the planned branch network — five stores, three districts, two years. Each dot on the map was a future shop. I had thought we were opening one small place. Standing there, I realised I had joined something much larger.
scale:0.cnHint: 店长展示了连锁扩张的____，让我意识到这不只是一家小店。
scale:0.hook: One dot on the map was right next to Lin's family address.
scale:0.line: 'At this *scale*, every small mistake becomes a big one.'

basic:0.en: Tang slid a printed checklist across the table. 'New staff at the branch will need training,' she said. 'The *basics* first — the register, the stock system, the closing routine.' The Manager nodded. I felt a quiet pride knowing I already understood every item on that list after just two weeks.
basic:0.cnHint: 阿糖列出了新员工培训的____，我发现自己已经全都掌握了。
basic:0.hook: Item seven on the list had a small question mark beside it.
basic:0.line: 'Master the *basics* first, then worry about the rest.'

constantly:0.en: I noticed the Manager was *constantly* on his phone, checking messages, replying to the landlord, forwarding documents to Tang. He had not touched his coffee in an hour. Opening a new branch, I was learning, was not a single decision. It was a hundred small ones arriving all at once.
constantly:0.cnHint: 店长____地盯着手机处理开分店的各种事务，咖啡都凉了。
constantly:0.hook: At midnight, one message made him set the phone face-down.
constantly:0.line: 'You have to be *constantly* ready when things move this fast.'

favor:0.en: The Manager asked Tang and me which of two sites we *favored*. Tang chose the busier road. I chose the quieter corner with the wider pavement. The Manager listened, wrote both reasons down, and then folded the paper in half. He did not tell us which side was facing up.
favor:0.cnHint: 店长让阿糖和我说出各自____的选址，然后把答案折了起来。
favor:0.hook: Lin appeared at the door holding a coffee from the rival shop down the street.
favor:0.line: 'I *favor* the quiet corner — customers stay longer there.'

absence:0.en: The new branch manager had not yet been chosen. In the *absence* of any announcement, rumours filled the store like steam from the hot-food cabinet. Tang said nothing. I said nothing. The Manager hummed to himself and restocked the top shelf. The silence was louder than any rumour.
absence:0.cnHint: 在新分店店长人选____的情况下，店里的气氛变得微妙起来。
absence:0.hook: Then the Manager handed me a brand-new name badge.
absence:0.line: 'In the *absence* of a plan, people will invent one for you.'

institution:0.en: The Manager gathered the whole staff before the new branch opened. 'This store is more than a shop,' he said. 'It is an *institution* — people come here for warmth as much as for milk.' Tang nodded. Lin looked unconvinced. Outside, the first customer was already waiting.
institution:0.cnHint: 店长说这家店不只是商店，它是一个重要的____，给街坊带来温暖。
institution:0.hook: But Lin had a very different plan for the new branch.
institution:0.line: 'This store is an *institution*, and we will keep it that way.'

outcome:0.en: Tang bet Lin a free coffee that the new branch would be empty on its first night. By midnight, every seat was taken and the counter line reached the door. The *outcome* surprised them both. The Manager just smiled and started a fresh pot without saying a word.
outcome:0.cnHint: 唐和林打赌新分店第一晚会没人，但____让他们都没想到。
outcome:0.hook: The Manager's quiet smile hid something neither of them knew yet.
outcome:0.line: 'The *outcome* of our little bet is one free coffee — mine.'

recognize:0.en: A shy woman in a yellow coat came in every night for a week before I finally learned her name. One evening the Manager pulled me aside. 'Do you *recognize* the logo on her bag?' he whispered. I looked again. She was the inspector from the city food-safety office.
recognize:0.cnHint: 店长让我仔细看一位常客包上的标志，问我能不能____她的身份。
recognize:0.hook: She placed her notebook flat on the counter and opened it slowly.
recognize:0.line: 'I didn't *recognize* her at first, but the logo gave it away.'

safety:0.en: Before the new branch could open, an officer arrived with a clipboard. He checked every socket, every shelf, and the little ladder we used to reach the top stock. 'Your *safety* record is clean,' he said at last, stamping the form. Tang let out a breath she had been holding for an hour.
safety:0.cnHint: 检查员来审查新分店，确认一切____合格后盖章放行，唐松了口气。
safety:0.hook: He paused at the back storeroom door and did not stamp that page.
safety:0.line: 'Your *safety* record is clean — you may open tomorrow.'

collect:0.en: Every Sunday morning a quiet old man came in with a paper bag. He would *collect* all the little free maps the store kept by the entrance — ten, sometimes twelve at a time. We never asked why. Tonight he arrived on a Tuesday, which had never happened before.
collect:0.cnHint: 每周日有位老人来____免费地图，但这次他在周二突然出现了。
collect:0.hook: He looked over his shoulder twice before he reached the map stand.
collect:0.line: 'I *collect* these maps — each one holds a small memory for me.'

door:0.en: Lin arrived at the new branch an hour before opening and stood outside in the cold. When the Manager finally unlocked the front *door*, Lin walked straight to the back office without a word, sat down, and put a thick folder on the desk. Nobody had given Lin a key before today.
door:0.cnHint: 林在开门前就在外面等候，店长开____后，林径直走向后办公室放下一个厚文件夹。
door:0.hook: The folder was labelled with tomorrow's date in red ink.
door:0.line: 'The moment that *door* opens, everything changes for this street.'

eventually:0.en: The new espresso machine beeped, blinked, and refused to pour a single cup for the first two hours of Tang's shift. She read the manual, tried seven different settings, and called the supplier twice. It *eventually* gave in just before the morning rush, producing the best cup any of us had tasted.
eventually:0.cnHint: 新咖啡机故障了两小时，唐反复尝试，____让它正常工作了。
eventually:0.hook: The supplier's second call had included one very odd warning.
eventually:0.line: 'It *eventually* works if you whisper to it — I am not joking.'

match:0.en: Lin challenged me to a speed-stocking *match*: whoever refilled the drinks shelf faster would choose the weekend shift. I was nervous until I noticed Lin stacking the heavy bottles in the wrong order. The Manager watched from the doorway, arms folded, clearly enjoying every second of it.
match:0.cnHint: 林向我发起上货速度____，谁快谁选周末班，店长在旁边看得津津有味。
match:0.hook: The Manager's smile faded the moment his phone buzzed.
match:0.line: 'This *match* is fair — same number of bottles, same shelf, go.'

safe:0.en: The Manager called me to the back room before my first shift. Behind a stack of instant-noodle boxes sat a heavy metal *safe*. 'The day's cash goes in here at midnight,' he said, patting it like an old friend. 'Don't forget the code.'
safe:0.cnHint: 店长在后仓向我展示存放现金的____，叮嘱我记住密码。
safe:0.hook: He never told me what else the safe held.
safe:0.line: 'Always lock the *safe* before you leave, no matter what.'

speed:0.en: Tang restocked the drinks fridge with impressive *speed*, sliding every bottle into place in under two minutes. I stood there holding an empty box, a little embarrassed. 'You'll get used to it,' she said, not even out of breath. The fridge hummed, perfectly full.
speed:0.cnHint: 同事以惊人的____整理好了饮料冰柜，让我自愧不如。
speed:0.hook: Then a bottle near the back began to leak.
speed:0.line: 'The real trick is *speed* — slow hands make long nights.'

burden:0.en: A quiet man came in just after two in the morning and bought nothing but a small notebook. He looked like he carried a heavy *burden* on his shoulders, something no shelf in our store could fix. He paid, nodded once, and walked back into the dark street.
burden:0.cnHint: 一位深夜进店的顾客，眉宇间带着沉重的____，只买了一个小本子。
burden:0.hook: His name was written on the inside cover already.
burden:0.line: 'A warm drink can lift a *burden*, even just a little.'

former:0.en: Two regular customers argued about which energy drink tasted better. The *former* — a tall student in a yellow jacket — insisted the green can was superior. The latter preferred the blue one. I placed both on the counter. They bought one of each and split them outside.
former:0.cnHint: 两位常客争论饮料口味，____者坚持绿罐更好喝。
former:0.hook: Neither of them noticed the cans had swapped labels.
former:0.line: 'The *former* one was better — I remember the old recipe.'

oppose:0.en: The Manager said a second branch might open near the university. Tang immediately began to *oppose* the idea, arms crossed, voice firm. 'We already can't keep the chip rack full on Fridays,' she said. The Manager smiled like he had already made up his mind.
oppose:0.cnHint: 店长提起开新分店的计划，同事毫不犹豫地____了这个想法。
oppose:0.hook: A blueprint was already taped under the front counter.
oppose:0.line: 'I *oppose* this plan — we are not ready, not even close.'

unable:0.en: Just before dawn, a boy in school uniform stared at the snack wall for a long time. He counted his coins twice, then looked up at me, embarrassed. He was *unable* to afford the rice ball he wanted. I pretended to find a small discount sticker and pressed it onto the package.
unable:0.cnHint: 一个男生数了两遍硬币，发现自己____买那个饭团。
unable:0.hook: He left a folded thank-you note on the counter next week.
unable:0.line: 'I am *unable* to pay full price today — I am so sorry.'

unusual:0.en: Around three in the morning, an *unusual* smell drifted through the store — not food, not cleaning fluid, but something faintly sweet, like old wood after rain. Tang sniffed the air and looked at the ceiling. Nothing seemed wrong. The smell vanished as quietly as it had arrived.
unusual:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点，店里飘来一股____的气味，让人摸不着头脑。
unusual:0.hook: Tang had smelled it once before, she said — last spring.
unusual:0.line: 'That is *unusual* — this store never smelled like that before.'

apart:0.en: Lin from the shop across the road came in, pretending to browse. Our stores are only ten metres *apart*, yet she always watched our layout like a detective. She bought a single mint, took a long look at our new display shelf, and left without a word.
apart:0.cnHint: 对面竞争对手的店与我们相距不远，她进来东张西望，只买了一颗薄荷糖就离开了。
apart:0.hook: Our new shelf design disappeared from her window the next day.
apart:0.line: 'Ten metres *apart*, and yet you always seem one step ahead.'

experiment:0.en: The Manager called us all to the back room after midnight. He had lined up six new types of hot drinks on the shelf. 'I want your honest opinions,' he said, handing us small paper cups. It was a proper *experiment* — he was testing which drinks to sell at the new branch. Tang gave every cup a score out of ten. I tried to look professional and mostly succeeded.
experiment:0.cnHint: 店长深夜召集大家，在后屋对新饮品进行____，为新分店做准备。
experiment:0.hook: Tang's lowest score matched the Manager's secret favourite.
experiment:0.line: 'This *experiment* will decide the whole menu for the new store.'

nature:0.en: Tang told me that the new branch would sit next to a small park. 'The *nature* outside the window will bring in customers,' she said, arranging a row of potted plants along our counter as a trial. She had a gift for making any space feel alive. I watered the plants carefully. One of them, I noticed, had a little paper tag with someone else's name on it.
nature:0.cnHint: 阿糖说新分店窗外的____会吸引顾客，还在柜台摆上了盆栽做测试。
nature:0.hook: The name on that tag belonged to Lin.
nature:0.line: 'The *nature* view from that new branch will be the real selling point.'

status:0.en: Lin walked in just before two in the morning and asked to see the layout plan for the new store. The Manager spread it on the counter without a word. Lin studied it for a long time. 'The *status* of this corner spot is perfect,' Lin said at last, tapping the map. I could not tell if that was a compliment or a warning. The Manager just smiled and rolled the plan back up.
status:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜查看新店布局图，评价这个角落位置的____非常理想。
status:0.hook: Lin left without buying anything, which had never happened before.
status:0.line: 'The *status* of that corner location is exactly what we were looking for.'

accident:0.en: Tang was carrying a full tray of sample cups to the display table when she slipped on the freshly mopped floor. It was a near *accident* — the tray tilted, every cup wobbled, and we all held our breath. Nothing spilled. Tang straightened up, laughed, and kept walking as if nothing had happened. The Manager quietly put a wet-floor sign out. He had forgotten it earlier.
accident:0.cnHint: 阿糖端着托盘在刚拖过的地板上差点发生____，所幸有惊无险。
accident:0.hook: The forgotten sign had been knocked aside by the last customer in.
accident:0.line: 'That was almost a bad *accident* — someone needs to put the sign out.'

active:0.en: The Manager said the new branch needed an *active* social media presence before it even opened. He looked at Tang, who immediately looked at me. I had been a night-shift clerk for exactly eleven days. I opened a fresh account and posted a photo of the potted plants. By morning it had more attention than I expected, and one comment asked if we sold the plants too.
active:0.cnHint: 店长说新分店开业前需要一个____的社交媒体账号，任务最终落到了我头上。
active:0.hook: The comment about the plants was from an account with no profile picture.
active:0.line: 'We need someone *active* online to build buzz before the grand opening.'

feed:0.en: Tang discovered a stray cat sitting by the back door around three in the morning. It looked thin and hopeful. 'We can't *feed* it every night or it will never leave,' the Manager said firmly. Tang nodded. Then she quietly opened a small tin of fish and set it just outside the door. The cat ate neatly and quickly. I pretended not to see any of this.
feed:0.cnHint: 阿糖在后门发现了一只流浪猫，店长说不能____它，但阿糖还是悄悄给它开了罐头。
feed:0.hook: The cat was still there when the morning shift arrived, sitting on the step.
feed:0.line: 'If you *feed* it tonight, it will be back every single night after that.'

principle:0.en: Lin came back the next evening and asked the Manager directly why the new branch would open on the same street as Lin's own store. The Manager said it was a simple business *principle*: one good store makes a street, two good stores make a destination. Lin was quiet for a moment, then ordered a coffee. I wrote Lin's name on the cup very carefully.
principle:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林质问店长为何新店开在同一条街，店长用一个商业____回应了这个问题。
principle:0.hook: Lin left a much larger tip than usual and said nothing about it.
principle:0.line: 'My *principle* is simple: more choice on one street brings more people to both of us.'

article:0.en: Tang found an old *article* tucked behind the shelf while we reorganised the stockroom for the new branch handover. It was a short piece from a local paper, years old, about this very store on its opening day. The Manager was in the photo, much younger, standing at the same counter I stand behind now. He saw me looking and said nothing, just straightened the photo and walked away.
article:0.cnHint: 阿糖在整理库房时发现了一篇旧____，里面有店长年轻时站在同一柜台前的照片。
article:0.hook: The article mentioned a second person in the photo, but the name was torn away.
article:0.line: 'There is an *article* here about this store — it is much older than I thought.'

advice:0.en: The Manager called us into the back room and spread a map on the table. He pointed to a street two blocks away. 'A second store opens there next month,' he said. Tang nudged me and whispered that the Manager always gave the same *advice*: smile more, stock less, and never argue with a customer at 3 a.m.
advice:0.cnHint: 店长把我们叫进后屋，给了我们关于新店的____。
advice:0.hook: But Tang's smile had something uneasy hiding behind it.
advice:0.line: 'My *advice* is simple: keep the shelves full and your voice low.'

attempt:0.en: I decided to *attempt* making the perfect cup of instant noodles at the back counter — a small experiment on a slow Tuesday night. I timed the water, measured the seasoning, and stood very still for three minutes. Tang watched without a word. The result was, honestly, just noodles.
attempt:0.cnHint: 我在深夜____泡出一碗完美的方便面。
attempt:0.hook: Then a regular walked in and asked if we sold cooking lessons.
attempt:0.line: 'I *attempt* something new every shift — tonight it is noodles, tomorrow who knows.'

draw:0.en: The new lucky-draw box by the door was the Manager's idea. Each purchase over fifteen yuan earned one ticket. By midnight, a small crowd had gathered around it, laughing and arguing over whose ticket would win the free umbrella. In the end, the night ended in a *draw* — two customers pulled the same number.
draw:0.cnHint: 店门口的抽奖活动以____收场，两位顾客号码相同。
draw:0.hook: The two winners stared at each other, and neither one let go of the umbrella.
draw:0.line: 'A *draw* is fair — we will just have to share it, I suppose.'

facility:0.en: The Manager announced that the new branch would have a proper seating area, a coffee corner, and a charging station. 'Every *facility* a tired student could want,' he said proudly. Tang leaned over and told me our current store's best facility was the single plastic stool behind the counter.
facility:0.cnHint: 新分店将提供更好的____，让顾客坐下来休息。
facility:0.hook: Then I noticed someone had already claimed that plastic stool for the night.
facility:0.line: 'The most useful *facility* in any store is a place to sit down.'

firm:0.en: When the supplier tried to swap our usual rice crackers for a cheaper brand, the Manager stood at the counter with his arms crossed and his voice calm but *firm*. He said the regulars noticed every small change. The supplier blinked twice, packed the cheaper boxes back into his bag, and left without another word.
firm:0.cnHint: 面对供应商的替换要求，店长态度____，坚持不换货。
firm:0.hook: Outside, the supplier paused under the streetlight and typed something into his phone.
firm:0.line: 'I am *firm* on this — our regulars trust what is on these shelves.'

innovation:0.en: Tang taped a small handwritten sign to the hot-drink machine: 'Mix two flavours for something new.' It seemed like a tiny *innovation*, hardly worth noticing. By two in the morning, customers were lining up to try odd combinations, and someone had named one drink 'rainy-night blend' on a sticky note.
innovation:0.cnHint: 同事的一个小小____让热饮机前排起了队。
innovation:0.hook: The next morning the Manager stared at the sticky notes and said nothing for a long time.
innovation:0.line: 'A small *innovation* does not need anyone's permission to be useful.'

multiple:0.en: A woman came in just before dawn and placed *multiple* items on the counter — three energy drinks, two packs of crackers, and a birthday candle. She paid quickly and was almost out the door before I could ask if everything was all right. She just smiled and said, 'Party of one.'
multiple:0.cnHint: 一位女士买了____件商品，包括一根生日蜡烛。
multiple:0.hook: She came back ten minutes later and bought a second candle.
multiple:0.line: 'I always buy *multiple* things at once — one trip saves time on a long night.'

path:0.en: Lin stopped in just after midnight, hands in pockets, looking around the store slowly. I had heard the Manager mention Lin as someone who once worked here but chose a different *path*. Lin studied the new snack display for a long time, said nothing, then bought a single coffee and left.
path:0.cnHint: 林走进店里，看了看陈列，选择了一条不同的____。
path:0.hook: The coffee Lin chose was the same one the Manager drinks every morning.
path:0.line: 'Everyone picks a *path* eventually — mine just took me somewhere unexpected.'

announce:0.en: The Manager gathered us behind the counter just before midnight. He cleared his throat twice, then *announced* that the company planned to open a second store two blocks away. Tang dropped a price-tag gun. I stood very still, wondering what this meant for our quiet little corner of the street.
announce:0.cnHint: 店长在午夜前把我们叫到柜台后面，____了一件大事。
announce:0.hook: But the Manager's smile did not quite reach his eyes.
announce:0.line: 'I *announce* this with mixed feelings,' the Manager said softly.

appropriate:0.en: Tang spent an hour arranging the new promotional banner above the snack shelf. She stepped back, tilted her head, and decided the bright-yellow sign was not *appropriate* for such a calm, sleepy store. She swapped it for a smaller white one. Somehow the whole aisle felt warmer after that.
appropriate:0.cnHint: 阿糖认为那张促销横幅对小店来说不够____，换了一张。
appropriate:0.hook: The old yellow banner was still rolled up under the counter.
appropriate:0.line: 'That colour is not *appropriate* for this place,' Tang said firmly.

chief:0.en: The regional inspector walked in at two in the morning, clipboard in hand. He introduced himself as the *chief* supervisor for all new branch openings in the district. I offered him a hot canned coffee. He accepted it, scribbled something on his board, and said nothing else for a long time.
chief:0.cnHint: 地区____督察深夜来到店里，对新分店进行检查。
chief:0.hook: His final note was folded and left face-down on the counter.
chief:0.line: 'I am the *chief* supervisor,' he said, 'and I have questions.'

clearly:0.en: Lin from the rival shop across the street stopped by just after three. She stood near the magazine rack, *clearly* studying the layout of our store with sharp, curious eyes. I pretended to restock the drinks fridge. We both knew exactly what she was doing, and neither of us said a word.
clearly:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林____是在观察我们店的布局，却假装只是随便逛逛。
clearly:0.hook: She photographed the floor plan before she left.
clearly:0.line: 'You can *clearly* see this place is well run,' Lin said lightly.

communicate:0.en: The Manager taped a hand-drawn map of the new branch to the staff-room wall. He said the two stores would *communicate* by a shared app so stock could move quickly between them. Tang nodded. I stared at the map and realised our quiet nights might never be quite the same again.
communicate:0.cnHint: 店长说两家分店将通过一个应用程序相互____，共享库存。
communicate:0.hook: The app already had a group chat, and someone had typed 'hello.'
communicate:0.line: 'The two shops will *communicate* in real time,' the Manager explained.

emphasis:0.en: During the midnight staff meeting, the Manager spoke slowly and with great *emphasis* on one point: the new branch must never feel cold or unwelcoming. He pressed his finger on the table at each word. Tang and I exchanged a glance. We both understood he was really talking about our store, too.
emphasis:0.cnHint: 店长用特别的____指出新分店必须让顾客感到温暖。
emphasis:0.hook: Tang wrote the word 'warmth' on a sticky note and said nothing.
emphasis:0.line: 'The *emphasis*,' said the Manager, 'must always be on the customer.'

emphasize:0.en: Tang printed a checklist for the new branch and pinned it to the board. She used a red pen to *emphasize* the item about keeping the coffee machine clean at all times. 'People remember bad coffee forever,' she said. I added a small star next to it and hoped the new staff would agree.
emphasize:0.cnHint: 阿糖用红笔____了检查表上关于咖啡机清洁的那一条。
emphasize:0.hook: The checklist had one item crossed out that no one would explain.
emphasize:0.line: 'I want to *emphasize* the coffee rule above all,' Tang said clearly.

england:0.en: A tired traveller set his backpack on the counter just before dawn. He said he had come all the way from *England* to visit a relative, and this store reminded him of a small shop near his home town. He bought a meat bun and ate it standing up, looking quietly happy.
england:0.cnHint: 一位从____远道而来的旅客说这家小店让他想起了家乡。
england:0.hook: He left a small coin on the counter — it was not local currency.
england:0.line: 'Back in *England*,' he said, 'the night shops felt just like this.'

character:0.en: The Manager walked me through the new branch store before opening day. 'Every store has its own *character*,' he said, touching the wooden shelf by the door. 'This one feels quieter, more serious.' I looked around at the clean walls and soft light. He was right — the place had its own silent personality.
character:0.cnHint: 店长带我参观新分店，说每家店都有自己的____。
character:0.hook: But then I noticed one shelf was always left empty.
character:0.line: 'Every store has its own *character*, and this one is still hiding its secrets.'

clean:0.en: My first job at the new branch was simple: make the place ready. I swept the floor, wiped the counters, and washed the windows until the glass was almost invisible. Tang handed me a mop and said nothing. By the time we finished, the whole store felt light and bright. A good *clean* changes a room's mood entirely.
clean:0.cnHint: 我和同事把新分店彻底____了一遍，整个地方焕然一新。
clean:0.hook: Then Tang pointed at a locked door we had missed.
clean:0.line: 'A good *clean* before opening day sets the right tone for everything.'

convey:0.en: The Manager asked me to hang a small sign above the entrance of the new branch. 'Choose your words carefully,' he said. 'A sign has to *convey* welcome without saying too much.' I tried four versions on a notepad. Tang read them all, crossed out three, and circled the shortest one. It said only: 'Come in. You belong here.'
convey:0.cnHint: 店长让我为新分店设计一块招牌，要能____出温馨感。
convey:0.hook: Lin read the sign from across the street and frowned.
convey:0.line: 'Four words can *convey* more warmth than a whole paragraph.'

distraction:0.en: Setting up shelves at the new branch should have taken two hours. But the big window faced a little park, and I kept stopping to watch an old man feed pigeons. Tang noticed. 'Stop letting that be a *distraction*,' she said, not unkindly. I pulled the blind halfway down and finally finished the shelf by noon.
distraction:0.cnHint: 我在新店布置货架时，窗外的景色成了我的____，让我一直分心。
distraction:0.hook: The old man outside glanced up at the window and smiled.
distraction:0.line: 'A pretty view is a lovely *distraction*, but the shelves won't stock themselves.'

fight:0.en: Lin stopped by the new branch while Tang and I were arranging stock. He walked the aisles slowly, checking prices, counting products. 'You have the *fight* in you,' he told me, almost as a warning. 'Opening a second store takes real effort. Most people give up.' He bought a bottle of water and left without another word.
fight:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林来新店转了一圈，说开分店需要____和毅力。
fight:0.hook: He left a small note under the bottle on the counter.
fight:0.line: 'You need real *fight* in you if you want a second store to survive.'

finish:0.en: The Manager wanted every detail perfect before the first customer arrived. The floor, the lighting, the label on each shelf — nothing was skipped. When we finally stepped back and looked, the store felt complete. 'There's a certain *finish* to a well-prepared space,' he said softly. Tang and I exchanged a tired but satisfied glance.
finish:0.cnHint: 开业前，店长坚持每个细节都要打磨到位，追求完美的____。
finish:0.hook: The clock hit midnight and someone knocked on the glass door.
finish:0.line: 'There is a quiet *finish* to this place now — like a story with a good ending.'

frequently:0.en: During our first week at the new branch, one regular customer stood out. She came in *frequently* — sometimes twice a day — always buying the same small coffee and a triangle rice snack. She never stayed long. Tang said she had done the same at the original store for three years. No one knew her name.
frequently:0.cnHint: 新分店开业第一周，一位常客____出现，每次买一样的东西。
frequently:0.hook: On Friday she bought something completely different and looked nervous.
frequently:0.line: 'She comes in *frequently* enough that I keep her order ready before she asks.'

invest:0.en: Late on the third night, the Manager sat across from me at the small back table with two cups of tea. 'I didn't *invest* in a second store just for more money,' he said quietly. 'I wanted to give more people a warm place to be.' Outside the window, the street was empty and still beautiful.
invest:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我，他____开这家新分店，不只是为了赚钱。
invest:0.hook: He slid an old photograph across the table toward me.
invest:0.line: 'I chose to *invest* in this place because some streets deserve a warm light at night.'

moment:0.en: The Manager called us into the back room and unrolled a large map on the table. 'We are opening a second store,' he said. For a *moment* nobody spoke. Then Tang knocked over his coffee cup, and the silence broke into nervous laughter.
moment:0.cnHint: 店长宣布要开分店，大家愣了一下，随后紧张的笑声打破了沉默。
moment:0.hook: Tang's hand was shaking long after the cup was dry.
moment:0.line: 'For a *moment* I thought you were joking, Manager.'

nice:0.en: The Manager spread the floor plan across the counter. Every shelf position, every light angle — the *nice* details had all been worked out. Tang leaned in and nodded slowly. I stared at the tiny square labeled 'new register' and wondered who would stand there every night.
nice:0.cnHint: 店长展示分店平面图，连细节都____到位，但不知谁会负责新收银台。
nice:0.hook: The name written in pencil beside that register was not Tang's.
nice:0.line: 'The *nice* details are what make or break a store, trust me.'

peer:0.en: A delivery driver arrived with boxes of stock for the new branch. Tang and I helped stack them. I noticed Lin standing at the doorway, trying to *peer* at the address labels without stepping inside. She looked away the second our eyes met.
peer:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在门口____箱子上的地址标签，一被发现便移开了视线。
peer:0.hook: Whatever she read on that label made her smile just a little.
peer:0.line: 'Why do you *peer* at things instead of just asking, Lin?'

pretty:0.en: The Manager brought in a small display stand meant for the new store. It held little keychains and fridge magnets — the kind of *pretty* that tourists like to pick up. Tang said they were useless. I quietly thought one of the magnets looked rather nice on a refrigerator door.
pretty:0.cnHint: 店长展示分店要卖的小饰品，阿糖觉得没用，而叙述者悄悄觉得挺好看的。
pretty:0.hook: The Manager had already ordered five hundred of them.
pretty:0.line: 'Customers always reach for a *pretty* before they reach for anything useful.'
