recommendation:0.en: The Manager asked each of us for a *recommendation* on where the new store should be located. Tang said near the university. I said near the night-market street. The Manager listened, folded his notes, and said he had already signed the lease last week.
recommendation:0.cnHint: 店长征求大家对选址的____，但其实他早就签好租约了。
recommendation:0.hook: He smiled just a little too calmly when he said it.
recommendation:0.line: 'My *recommendation* is somewhere students actually walk past at midnight.'

strange:0.en: A regular customer came in, looked around the store, and said it felt *strange* tonight. Nothing had changed — same shelves, same hum of the coolers. But the Manager had taken down the old branch-opening poster, and maybe that small gap on the wall was enough to unsettle him.
strange:0.cnHint: 老顾客说今晚店里感觉____，其实只是墙上少了一张海报。
strange:0.hook: He bought nothing and stood by the door an extra minute before leaving.
strange:0.line: 'It feels *strange* in here tonight — did something change?'

widespread:0.en: The Manager explained that the convenience-store format had become *widespread* across the city, so competition was fierce. That was exactly why the new branch had to feel different — warmer, he said, more like a place people wanted to stay. Tang wrote the word 'warmer' on his notepad and underlined it twice.
widespread:0.cnHint: 店长说便利店业态已经____全城，所以分店必须有自己的特色。
widespread:0.hook: Tang's notepad also had Lin's store address circled in red.
widespread:0.line: 'The format is *widespread*, so our warmth is the only edge we have.'

wonderful:0.en: Late in the shift, after all the planning talk had died down, I made three cups of instant coffee and set them on the counter. The Manager wrapped both hands around his cup and said, 'How *wonderful* — the store isn't even open yet and I already miss this place.' Tang and I said nothing, but we both smiled.
wonderful:0.cnHint: 夜班快结束时，大家喝着咖啡，店长说了一句令人感动的____的话。
wonderful:0.hook: None of us mentioned that Lin's light was still on across the street.
wonderful:0.line: 'How *wonderful* it is to plan something with people you trust.'

male:0.en: A *male* customer in a neat suit walked in just before midnight. He bought three cans of coffee and stacked them carefully on the counter. 'Night shift?' he asked with a tired smile. I nodded. He nodded back, like we shared a secret only night people understood.
male:0.cnHint: 一位____顾客深夜来买咖啡，和我交换了一个只有夜班人懂的眼神。
male:0.hook: He came back an hour later, this time without the suit.
male:0.line: 'Every *male* on our team drinks three cans just to survive the night shift.'

fish:0.en: Uncle Gao brought in a plastic bag of fresh *fish* he caught that morning and asked if we sold ice. We did not, but I found a cold pack behind the drinks shelf. He looked so grateful I almost cried. 'My wife loves river fish,' he said softly.
fish:0.cnHint: 老高带着早上钓的____来店里找冰袋，我在饮料架后面帮他找到了一个。
fish:0.hook: His wife had not eaten a proper meal in two weeks.
fish:0.line: 'Fresh *fish* from the river — you can smell the morning in it.'

fashion:0.en: A young woman spread four different scarves across the snack shelf and studied them in *fashion*, tilting her head left and right. She asked my opinion three times, then bought the one I liked least. 'Style is personal,' she told me cheerfully, and walked out into the cold.
fashion:0.cnHint: 一个年轻女士在零食架上摆开围巾，用____的方式认真比较，最后偏偏买了我最不喜欢的那条。
fashion:0.hook: She left one scarf behind, folded neatly under a bag of chips.
fashion:0.line: 'In *fashion*, the wrong choice is sometimes the bravest one.'

weather:0.en: The old woman who always carried an umbrella checked the *weather* on a small phone screen before buying her nightly cup of hot tea. 'Rain by four,' she announced to no one in particular. By three-fifty, heavy drops were hitting the glass door right on schedule.
weather:0.cnHint: 那位总带伞的老太太买茶前查了____，精准预报了凌晨四点的大雨。
weather:0.hook: She had predicted the weather correctly every night for a month.
weather:0.line: 'Trust me, the *weather* app is wrong — my knees never lie.'

device:0.en: A teenager set a strange little *device* on the counter while he dug for change — a small box with a soft blinking light. I stared at it. 'It counts my steps,' he said, not looking up. He was at forty-two thousand. It was only midnight.
device:0.cnHint: 一个少年把计步____放在收银台上找零钱，我一看数字，已经四万两千步了，才到午夜。
device:0.hook: He mentioned, very quietly, that he had nowhere to go home to.
device:0.line: 'This *device* buzzes when I hit fifty thousand — almost there.'

farm:0.en: A wide-shouldered man in muddy boots came in smelling of earth and hay. He said he drove three hours from his *farm* because his daughter had a school show in the city at dawn. He bought a sandwich, two bananas, and asked if he could sit until morning.
farm:0.cnHint: 一个从____开车三小时进城的父亲，只为看女儿的清晨演出，想在店里等到天亮。
farm:0.hook: In his coat pocket was a small hand-drawn card that said 'Best Dad.'
farm:0.line: 'Back on the *farm*, we wake at four anyway, so this feels normal.'

drug:0.en: A tired woman in a white coat rushed in and scanned every shelf twice. 'Do you carry this *drug*?' she asked, showing me a name on her phone. We did — one box left, pushed to the back. She pressed both hands together in thanks and ran back into the rain.
drug:0.cnHint: 一位穿白大褂的疲惫女士冲进来，急着寻找一种____，我们恰好还剩最后一盒。
drug:0.hook: The name on her hospital badge matched the one on the prescription.
drug:0.line: 'This *drug* is the only thing keeping my patient calm tonight.'

heat:0.en: The broken heater made the back corner unbearably cold, so I moved the small display lamp there for *heat*. Tang came in for his break, saw my setup, and laughed until he cried. Then he dragged over a second lamp without a word and sat beside me.
heat:0.cnHint: 暖气坏了，我用展示灯取____，同事阿糖笑完之后默默又搬来一盏灯陪我坐着。
heat:0.hook: Tang had not laughed like that since the branch store plan was announced.
heat:0.line: 'A lamp for *heat* — honestly, not the worst idea you have had.'

intelligence:0.en: The Manager tapped his head and smiled. 'Running a good store takes *intelligence*,' he said, arranging the shelves with quiet care. He knew which snacks sold on rainy nights, which drinks disappeared by dawn. I watched him work and wondered how long it had taken him to learn all of this.
intelligence:0.cnHint: 店长说经营好一家店需要____，他对店里的一切了如指掌。
intelligence:0.hook: But why did he keep a locked notebook under the counter?
intelligence:0.line: 'Running a good store takes *intelligence*, not just hard work.'

uk:0.en: A man in a rain-wet coat asked if we stocked tea from the *UK*. He set a small tin on the counter and said he had bought it there years ago. The smell, he told me, still reminded him of a rainy street and a red phone box. He bought plain green tea instead, looking quietly far away.
uk:0.cnHint: 一位顾客问我们有没有来自____的茶叶，他眼神里带着回忆。
uk:0.hook: He left the empty tin on the counter — with an address written inside.
uk:0.line: 'Do you carry any tea from the *UK*? Even one brand would do.'

user:0.en: Tang showed me the store's loyalty app. 'Each *user* gets points for every visit,' she said, scrolling through the list. One account had checked in every single night for two years. No name, just a number. Tang shrugged, but I noticed she always left a hot drink near the door around three in the morning.
user:0.cnHint: 唐给我介绍积分软件，说每位____每次消费都能攒积分，其中一个账号格外神秘。
user:0.hook: Tonight, that mystery account checked in — twice.
user:0.line: 'Every *user* gets points, but this one never redeems them.'

park:0.en: She came in just after midnight, helmet still on, and bought two rice balls. 'I *park* my bike at the corner and eat here,' she said, like it was a long-held rule. She sat on the step outside, sharing one rice ball with a stray cat. I had seen her do this three nights in a row now.
park:0.cnHint: 她每天深夜来买饭团，说她习惯把自行车____在路口后在这里吃东西。
park:0.hook: Last night, the cat was waiting before she even arrived.
park:0.line: 'I *park* here every night — the cat expects me now.'

reward:0.en: Lin dropped a small bag of sweets on my counter. 'A little *reward*,' she said with a grin, 'for sending that lost delivery guy to my shop by mistake last week.' I laughed, surprised she thought it worth thanking me for. The sweets were good. I started to think Lin was not as fierce as the Manager had warned.
reward:0.cnHint: 林送来糖果作为____，感谢我上周无意中帮了她一个忙。
reward:0.hook: The Manager saw the bag and went very quiet.
reward:0.line: 'Think of it as a small *reward* for your accidental kindness.'

credit:0.en: An older man counted coins on the counter, one short for his usual coffee. 'I always pay — you can check,' he said with quiet pride. The Manager, passing by, just nodded to me. I gave the man his coffee. Later the Manager told me, '*Credit* matters in a place like this — people remember who trusted them.'
credit:0.cnHint: 一位老人差了一枚硬币，店长说在这种地方____很重要，信任是相互的。
credit:0.hook: The old man came back the next morning with exact change and a small cake.
credit:0.line: '*Credit* matters here — people always come back to repay it.'

progress:0.en: I made my third wrong change of the night and wanted to disappear. Tang leaned over and fixed it without a word. 'Don't worry,' she said softly. 'You *progress* faster than I did. I once gave a man fifty yuan change for a ten-yuan note.' I felt a little better. Outside, the street was quiet and kind.
progress:0.cnHint: 我算错了找零，唐安慰我说我____得很快，她自己当初犯过更大的错。
progress:0.hook: Tang has never once mentioned that story to the Manager.
progress:0.line: 'You *progress* faster than I did — trust me on that.'

snack:0.en: A small boy in pyjamas tugged a tall woman's sleeve near the chips. 'Just one *snack*,' he said, in the serious tone of a lawyer making a final case. She looked at me. I looked at the ceiling. She looked back at him. He got the chips. He also got a hug. Some arguments, I have learned, are decided before they start.
snack:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩用非常认真的口气请求只要一份____，结果当然是成功了。
snack:0.hook: He was back the next night with his grandfather — and the exact same argument.
snack:0.line: 'Just one *snack*, I promise I will go straight to sleep after.'

immediately:0.en: The Manager called a staff meeting in the back room. He unrolled a big map on the table and pointed to a spot two streets away. 'That empty corner unit,' he said, 'will be our second store.' Tang and I looked at each other. The Manager *immediately* began listing jobs for each of us, as if the place were already open.
immediately:0.cnHint: 店长在后室开会，刚宣布开分店计划就____开始分配任务，仿佛新店已经开张。
immediately:0.hook: Tang's face said he knew something about that corner the Manager did not.
immediately:0.line: 'We *immediately* need someone to check the new site tonight — any volunteers?'

improvement:0.en: The Manager pinned a chart to the stockroom wall showing last month's numbers. Every line trended up. 'Each small step counts,' he said quietly. I noticed one column — late-night snack sales — had jumped the most. Tang winked at me. That column was mine. The Manager tapped it and said the *improvement* there had caught the owner's eye.
improvement:0.cnHint: 店长展示了上月的业绩图，夜宵销售那栏的____引起了老板的注意。
improvement:0.hook: The owner, it turned out, wanted to meet the person behind those numbers.
improvement:0.line: 'This *improvement* in snack sales is exactly why we can afford a second store.'

afternoon:0.en: The planning meeting was set for Sunday *afternoon*, when the store is slowest. Tang brought homemade dumplings; I made tea. The Manager spread lease papers across the counter. Outside, the street was golden and quiet. It felt less like a business meeting and more like neighbours deciding to plant a shared garden.
afternoon:0.cnHint: 周日____，大家在安静的店里开筹备会议，气氛温馨得像邻居聚在一起商量种花。
afternoon:0.hook: Then Lin walked past the window, slowed down, and stared at the papers on the counter.
afternoon:0.line: 'Every *afternoon* this week I have walked past that empty corner — it is perfect for us.'

expand:0.en: 'We have the regulars, we have the trust,' the Manager said, smoothing the lease with both hands. 'Now it is time to *expand*.' He said the word softly, like it was something fragile. Tang nodded. I looked around at our small, warm store — the humming fridge, the crooked shelf of instant noodles — and felt a quiet, careful pride.
expand:0.cnHint: 店长轻声说是时候____了，我环顾这家温馨的小店，心里涌起一种谨慎的自豪感。
expand:0.hook: What the Manager did not mention was who he planned to put in charge of the new location.
expand:0.line: 'If we *expand* now, we must make sure the new store feels just as warm as this one.'

regardless:0.en: Lin from the convenience store across the street came in for his usual coffee. He had heard the rumour. 'You really think a second store will work?' he asked, almost smiling. The Manager handed him his change and said, *regardless* of what anyone thought, they were signing the lease on Friday. Lin stirred his coffee slowly and said nothing more.
regardless:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林听到传言后来旁敲侧击，店长说____他们都会在周五签约。
regardless:0.hook: Lin left a business card on the counter that none of us had seen before.
regardless:0.line: '*Regardless* of the competition, our regulars will follow us to the new store.'

rid:0.en: The stockroom was a problem. Boxes of out-of-date leaflets, a broken display stand, three mops with no handles. 'Before we open anywhere new,' the Manager said, 'we need to *rid* this place of the old mess first.' Tang and I spent the whole morning sorting. By noon, the room was clean enough to think clearly in.
rid:0.cnHint: 店长说开新店之前，要先____库房里的旧杂物，我和唐整理了一上午。
rid:0.hook: Behind the last stack of boxes, Tang found a notebook nobody recognised.
rid:0.line: 'Let us *rid* the stockroom of all this clutter before the owner comes for a visit.'

dog:0.en: A regular named Old Zhou always brings his small *dog* on late walks. The dog waits outside, nose against the glass, watching Zhou choose his nightly snack. Last night Zhou spent ten minutes longer than usual. The Manager leaned over and whispered that Zhou had asked if the new store would be near the park — for the dog's sake, of course.
dog:0.cnHint: 常客老周每晚散步时带着他的____来店门口，昨晚他多待了十分钟，原来是在打听新店的位置。
dog:0.hook: The Manager smiled in a way that meant he had already thought about that very park.
dog:0.line: 'My *dog* approves of every store he visits — so far this is his favourite.'

busy:0.en: Friday arrived and the store was *busy* in a way that felt like a good omen. Tang restocked twice before noon. I handled the counter alone for an hour while the Manager was on the phone finalising the lease. Every customer who came in seemed cheerful, and two of them congratulated us without us saying a word about the new store.
busy:0.cnHint: 签约的周五，小店出奇地____，像是好兆头，甚至有顾客来道贺，尽管我们什么都没说。
busy:0.hook: One of those customers was someone the Manager had hoped never to see again.
busy:0.line: 'I know you are *busy* today — but I heard the news, and I just had to come by.'

extreme:0.en: The Manager called everyone into the back room before sunrise. He unrolled a large map of the city and pointed to a red circle far from the centre. 'The rent there is *extreme*,' he said, tapping the spot, 'but the foot traffic is twice what we get here.' Nobody spoke for a moment.
extreme:0.cnHint: 店长展示新店选址，那里的租金____得让人吃惊。
extreme:0.hook: Lin's hand was shaking as she studied the map.
extreme:0.line: 'The rent is *extreme*, but the location could change everything.'

style:0.en: The Manager spread three sets of sample uniforms across the counter. Each had a different *style*: one neat and classic, one bright and modern, one soft and casual. 'The new branch needs its own look,' he said. Tang held the bright jacket up and tilted his head, clearly trying not to smile.
style:0.cnHint: 店长让大家为新店挑选制服的____。
style:0.hook: Lin quietly pushed the classic one toward the front.
style:0.line: 'Every branch needs its own *style*, don't you think?'

color:0.en: Tang spent an entire afternoon testing light bulbs in the empty new-branch space. Warm, cool, bright, dim — he tried them all. 'The *color* of the light changes how people feel inside a shop,' he explained to me seriously. I nodded, though I had never thought about light that way before.
color:0.cnHint: 阿糖认真研究新店灯光的____对顾客心情的影响。
color:0.hook: The last bulb he tried made the whole room look golden.
color:0.line: 'The *color* of the light can make people stay longer.'

meeting:0.en: I arrived early and found Lin already seated at the small table in the back room, a notebook open in front of her. 'Is there a *meeting* today?' I asked. She looked up, surprised. 'There is now,' she said, and turned the notebook so I could read the long list of questions she had written for the Manager.
meeting:0.cnHint: 我无意间闯入了隔壁咖啡店的林自己组织的一场____。
meeting:0.hook: The first question on her list was circled three times.
meeting:0.line: 'This *meeting* was not on the schedule, but it should have been.'

volunteer:0.en: The Manager asked if anyone wanted to manage the new branch for the first month. The room went quiet. Then Tang raised one hand halfway. 'I'll *volunteer*,' he said, his voice steady even though his eyes looked slightly terrified. Everyone turned to stare at him, including me.
volunteer:0.cnHint: 店长征询新店临时负责人，阿糖____了出来。
volunteer:0.hook: Lin wrote something in her notebook without looking up.
volunteer:0.line: 'I'll *volunteer* — someone has to take the first step.'

deliver:0.en: The Manager stood at the front of the back room, cleared his throat, and began to *deliver* his speech about the new branch. He had clearly practised it. His hands moved, his voice rose and fell, and he paused at exactly the right moments. Tang leaned over and whispered to me, 'He's been rehearsing since Tuesday.'
deliver:0.cnHint: 店长正式____关于开分店计划的演讲，显然准备已久。
deliver:0.hook: But then he lost his place and stared at the ceiling.
deliver:0.line: 'I am proud to *deliver* the news about our new branch today.'

engineering:0.en: A young woman came in just after midnight, still wearing her university bag. She bought two cans of coffee and a pen. 'Big exam tomorrow?' I asked. 'Worse,' she said. '*Engineering* project due at eight a.m.' She opened her notebook on the counter and started drawing tiny diagrams without another word.
engineering:0.cnHint: 一位____专业的女生深夜来买咖啡，赶着完成作业。
engineering:0.hook: Her diagram looked nothing like any bridge I had ever seen.
engineering:0.line: '*Engineering* never sleeps, and neither do I tonight.'

tiny:0.en: The new branch space was smaller than I expected. Standing in the middle of it, I could almost touch both walls. 'It's *tiny*,' I said without thinking. The Manager smiled. 'Tiny is cosy,' he said. 'Cosy makes people come back.' He switched off the light and locked the door, already looking pleased with himself.
tiny:0.cnHint: 新店面积____，但店长却觉得这正是优点。
tiny:0.hook: I counted the floor tiles on the way out — only twelve.
tiny:0.line: 'Yes, it is *tiny* — but so was our first store.'

retire:0.en: Just past two in the morning, the Manager shuffled in from the back office, still wearing his apron. 'I always *retire* late when we are testing a new store layout,' he said, pulling a stool to the counter. He spread out a hand-drawn floor plan and stared at it like it held all the answers.
retire:0.cnHint: 店长深夜来到便利店，说自己每次测试新店布局时都____得很晚。
retire:0.hook: The floor plan had a second address circled in red ink.
retire:0.line: 'I always *retire* late when we are testing a new store layout.'

sea:0.en: A delivery box arrived at midnight labeled FRAGILE. Inside, wrapped in old newspaper, were six small bottles of sand — each tagged with a different beach name. The Manager held one up to the light. 'Someone is sending these from the *sea* towns up north,' he said softly. 'Every week, one more bottle.'
sea:0.cnHint: 一个深夜到达的包裹里装着来自____边小镇的沙子瓶子。
sea:0.hook: The seventh tag had our store's address written on the back.
sea:0.line: 'Someone is sending these from the *sea* towns up north.'

town:0.en: Tang spread a hand-drawn map across the break-room table during our slow hour. Little squares marked every convenience store in the area. 'The new branch will be in the next *town*,' she said, tapping a blank square at the edge of the map. 'Twenty minutes away. No competition there yet.'
town:0.cnHint: 同事在休息室摊开地图，指出新分店将开在隔壁____。
town:0.hook: Lin walked in just as Tang folded the map away.
town:0.line: 'The new branch will be in the next *town*, twenty minutes away.'

gap:0.en: Lin stopped by just before dawn, arms crossed, studying the empty shelf where the new product line was supposed to sit. 'That *gap* has been there three days,' she said, nodding at the bare metal. 'Customers notice empty space faster than you think.' She left without buying anything, as usual.
gap:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林盯着货架上的____，说顾客比我们想象的更快注意到空位。
gap:0.hook: A supplier's card fell from her pocket as she walked out.
gap:0.line: 'That *gap* has been there three days — customers notice.'

generation:0.en: An old man came in every night for warm soy milk. Tonight he brought his granddaughter, maybe eight years old, who went straight for the comics rack. 'A whole new *generation* of night owls,' he said with a proud smile, watching her flip through the pages. 'She stays up even later than I do.'
generation:0.cnHint: 一位老爷爷带着孙女来店里，感慨新____的夜猫子比他还能熬夜。
generation:0.hook: The girl tucked a folded note inside one of the comics before leaving.
generation:0.line: 'A whole new *generation* of night owls — she stays up later than I do.'

guide:0.en: The Manager dropped a thick binder on the counter and slid it toward me. 'Read this before the new branch opens,' he said. 'It is the operations *guide* — every rule, every routine, every small thing that keeps a store from falling apart at three in the morning.' It was heavier than it looked.
guide:0.cnHint: 店长把一本厚厚的运营____递给我，要我在新店开业前读完。
guide:0.hook: Page one had a handwritten note that was not part of the original text.
guide:0.line: 'This operations *guide* has every rule that keeps a store running.'

household:0.en: A quiet woman came in twice a week and always bought the same things: rice, dish soap, a small candle. Tonight she added a roll of tape to her basket. 'Packing boxes,' she explained with a short laugh. 'Moving a whole *household* is mostly tape and patience.' She paid in exact coins.
household:0.cnHint: 一位常客说搬家就是胶带和耐心，要把整个____都打包好。
household:0.hook: She asked if we would still be open after the new branch launched.
household:0.line: 'Moving a whole *household* is mostly tape and patience.'

luxury:0.en: Lin leaned against the drinks fridge at three in the morning, holding a small bottle of imported juice that cost four times the usual price. 'Do you think the new branch will carry this?' she asked. 'A little *luxury* on a tired night is the only reason I come here.' She bought two.
luxury:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿着一瓶进口果汁问，疲惫的夜晚来一点____是她来这里的唯一理由。
luxury:0.hook: She paid with a staff discount card that was not hers.
luxury:0.line: 'A little *luxury* on a tired night is the only reason I come here.'

analysis:0.en: The Manager spread a large paper across the counter at two in the morning. 'Look at this,' he said, tapping rows of numbers. His careful *analysis* of sales from every hour of the week showed one strange fact: we sold the most hot drinks at exactly 3 a.m. I stared at the page, then at the empty street outside.
analysis:0.cnHint: 店长深夜拿出数据，他的____显示凌晨三点热饮销量最高。
analysis:0.hook: So who, exactly, was buying them?
analysis:0.line: 'My *analysis* shows someone visits us every single night at three.'

application:0.en: Tang slid a printed form across the counter to me during a quiet moment. 'Fill this in,' she whispered. It was an *application* for the new branch the Manager planned to open near the university. There was a line asking for a preferred role. Tang had already written 'assistant manager' on her own copy, in red pen.
application:0.cnHint: 阿糖递给我一张新分店的____表格，她自己那份已经填好了。
application:0.hook: She winked, but her handwriting looked very, very serious.
application:0.line: 'Your *application* needs to be in before Friday morning,' Tang said firmly.

living:0.en: A quiet man came in every night for a small loaf of bread and nothing else. I finally asked him what he did for a *living*. He smiled and said he wrote questions for university entrance exams. I nodded slowly, suddenly aware of how many students bought coffee here at midnight, pencils behind their ears.
living:0.cnHint: 那位每晚来买面包的常客说，他靠出考题为____。
living:0.hook: He picked up one of our CET practice booklets and raised an eyebrow.
living:0.line: 'Writing exam questions is a tough *living*, but someone has to do it.'

proposal:0.en: The Manager called Tang and me to the back room and unrolled a hand-drawn map of the neighbourhood. He had a *proposal*: open a second store two blocks away, staffed at night by us on rotation. Tang looked excited. I looked at the map, then at my current salary written on a sticky note nearby.
proposal:0.cnHint: 店长召集大家，提出了一个开分店的____，阿糖听得两眼发光。
proposal:0.hook: The sticky note did not mention a pay rise.
proposal:0.line: 'My *proposal* is simple: two stores, same team, starting next month,' he said.

relevant:0.en: Lin from the convenience store down the street walked in, cool as ever, and asked to see our floor plan. 'Research,' she said simply. The Manager only shared details he felt were *relevant* to a neighbourly chat, which turned out to be almost nothing. Lin left with a small coffee and a smile that worried me.
relevant:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林来"串门"，店长只分享了他认为____的信息，也就是几乎什么都没说。
relevant:0.hook: She photographed the drinks fridge on her way out.
relevant:0.line: 'Tell me anything *relevant* about your busiest hours,' Lin said sweetly.

senior:0.en: A woman with silver hair and a bright scarf came in and asked for the Manager by name. Tang told me quietly that she was a *senior* staff member from the company that owned our store, visiting from the head office. She walked every aisle slowly, writing notes, then bought a single piece of gum and left without a word.
senior:0.cnHint: 一位头发花白的____员工来店里巡视，买了一片口香糖就走了。
senior:0.hook: Her notebook was already half full before she reached the drinks aisle.
senior:0.line: 'As a *senior* member of this company, I notice everything,' she said quietly.

table:0.en: We had one small *table* by the window, meant for eating a quick snack. By midnight it had become an unofficial study spot, covered in notes and empty cup noodle boxes. I never moved anyone along. One student had been coming every night for two weeks and had not bought a single thing yet.
table:0.cnHint: 店里靠窗的那张____成了深夜学生们的临时自习角。
table:0.hook: Tonight, he finally walked up to the counter holding cash.
table:0.line: 'Can I keep using this *table* every night?' the student asked quietly.

campus:0.en: A girl rushed in at half past midnight, still wearing her university lanyard. She said the shop nearest to her *campus* had closed early and this was her only hope for instant noodles before an exam. I found the last pack on the top shelf. She held it with both hands like it was something precious.
campus:0.cnHint: 一个女生说离她____最近的店提前关门了，这里是她最后的希望。
campus:0.hook: She came back an hour later, calmer, and bought three more packs.
campus:0.line: 'Every shop near our *campus* closes before midnight,' she said breathlessly.

disadvantage:0.en: The Manager spread a map across the counter and pointed to the new store site three blocks away. 'The *disadvantage* of that corner,' he said, tapping the paper, 'is that the morning buses skip it entirely.' He looked worried. I looked at the empty coffee shelf and wondered if our corner had its own problems.
disadvantage:0.cnHint: 店长在柜台上铺开地图，分析新分店选址的____。
disadvantage:0.hook: But someone had already been watching that corner for weeks.
disadvantage:0.line: 'The *disadvantage* of that corner is that the morning buses skip it entirely.'

discuss:0.en: Tang pulled me aside near the noodle shelf just after midnight. 'We need to *discuss* the new branch — the Manager keeps changing the plan and nobody tells us anything.' She kept her voice low and her eyes on the door. A regular in a yellow coat was pretending to read a snack label nearby.
discuss:0.cnHint: 阿糖在深夜把我拉到一边，说我们需要____新分店的计划。
discuss:0.hook: The regular in the yellow coat smiled just a little too quickly.
discuss:0.line: 'We need to *discuss* the new branch before the Manager decides everything alone.'

psychological:0.en: Opening a second store turned out to have a *psychological* effect on all of us. Tang started checking the till twice. I started greeting each customer as if they might be a secret inspector. The Manager just hummed to himself and rearranged the candy display for the fourth time that week.
psychological:0.cnHint: 开新分店这件事对大家产生了奇怪的____影响。
psychological:0.hook: Then a stranger with a clipboard walked in at two in the morning.
psychological:0.line: 'There is a real *psychological* pressure when you know someone is watching the store.'

request:0.en: A small note appeared on the Manager's desk one morning: a *request* from the new branch team asking for Tang to transfer over and train their staff. Tang read it, set it back down very carefully, and went to restock the drinks fridge without saying a word.
request:0.cnHint: 店长的桌上出现了一张纸条，是一个正式的____，想让阿糖去新分店。
request:0.hook: Tang hadn't told anyone she had already visited that branch twice.
request:0.line: 'This *request* for Tang to transfer came from someone very high up.'

symptom:0.en: The Manager kept forgetting where he put his keys. Tang said it was a *symptom* of opening-a-new-store stress and handed him a cup of hot tea. I nodded like I agreed, but honestly, he had been losing his keys long before any talk of a second branch started.
symptom:0.cnHint: 店长老是忘记钥匙放在哪里，阿糖说这是某种压力的____。
symptom:0.hook: Then the keys turned up inside the locked safe, and nobody knew how.
symptom:0.line: 'Forgetting small things is a *symptom* of too much stress, so please drink this tea.'

upon:0.en: *Upon* hearing that the new branch would share our storage room, Tang put down her mop and stared at the ceiling for a full ten seconds. The Manager explained that it was only temporary. Tang picked her mop back up. I chose not to ask what 'temporary' meant to him.
upon:0.cnHint: 一听说新分店要共用我们的仓库，阿糖____知道这个消息后愣住了。
upon:0.hook: Three unmarked boxes arrived that same night and filled half the room.
upon:0.line: '*Upon* hearing that news, I knew this plan was not as simple as he said.'

argument:0.en: The only loud *argument* I ever heard in the store was between the Manager and Lin from the shop across the street. It lasted four minutes and was entirely about which corner had better foot traffic. They both looked at me for a verdict. I pretended to be very busy with the receipt printer.
argument:0.cnHint: 店长和隔壁咖啡店的林发生了一场关于哪个路口人流更多的____。
argument:0.hook: Lin had building plans folded in his jacket pocket the whole time.
argument:0.line: 'This *argument* about foot traffic will only end when one of us opens a second store first.'

crisis:0.en: At three in the morning the freezer stopped working, and we had a small *crisis* on our hands. Tang grabbed every ice bag in the store. I called the Manager, who arrived in slippers and solved the problem in eleven minutes by kicking the plug back in. He seemed almost disappointed it was over so fast.
crisis:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点冰柜突然停运，大家一起应对了一场小____。
crisis:0.hook: The repair log showed the same plug had come loose three times that month.
crisis:0.line: 'Every *crisis* in this store has the same cure: check the plug first, panic second.'

destroy:0.en: The Manager spread a big map across the counter. 'We are opening a second store next month,' he said proudly. A drop of coffee fell from his cup and landed right on the map. 'Don't let that *destroy* our plans,' Tang said, quickly blotting it with a tissue. The Manager just laughed.
destroy:0.cnHint: 店长把开分店的地图摊在柜台上，一滴咖啡掉下来，差点____了整个计划。
destroy:0.hook: But the coffee stain had landed on a very interesting address.
destroy:0.line: 'Don't let that *destroy* our plans,' Tang said, grabbing a tissue.

drop:0.en: The Manager held a small glass bottle of the store's new sauce over the counter. 'Just one *drop* is enough to decide if we sell this at the new branch,' he said. Tang and I leaned in. He tilted the bottle. We all held our breath.
drop:0.cnHint: 店长拿着新酱汁，说只需一____就能决定分店是否售卖它。
drop:0.hook: The drop never fell — someone knocked on the glass door at that exact moment.
drop:0.line: 'Just one *drop* is enough to make the decision,' the Manager said quietly.

efficiency:0.en: Lin walked in from the rival store across the street, holding a thick notebook. 'I have been studying your layout,' Lin said with a calm smile. 'Your *efficiency* is surprisingly good for such a small space.' The Manager blinked. I didn't know whether to feel proud or nervous.
efficiency:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林走进来，夸这家小店的____出乎意料地高。
efficiency:0.hook: Lin then asked if the Manager had ever considered a partnership.
efficiency:0.line: 'Your *efficiency* is surprisingly good for such a small space,' Lin said.

italian:0.en: A regular customer came in waving a folded paper. 'I just got a job offer in Italy!' she said. 'Can I get something to celebrate?' Tang pointed to a small tin of *Italian* biscuits on the top shelf. The woman laughed and said it felt like a sign.
italian:0.cnHint: 一位常客拿到了去意大利的工作邀请，在店里找到了一盒____饼干庆祝。
italian:0.hook: She left the tin behind on the counter — with a note tucked under it.
italian:0.line: 'These *Italian* biscuits feel like a sign,' she said with a big smile.

newspaper:0.en: Every morning at two o'clock, an old man came in, bought a warm drink, and read yesterday's *newspaper* cover to cover. He never bought the paper — just read the one the Manager left on the counter. Tonight, the paper was gone. He stood at the counter looking lost.
newspaper:0.cnHint: 一位老人每天深夜都来读柜台上的____，今晚那份报纸不见了。
newspaper:0.hook: He reached into his coat and pulled out something none of us expected.
newspaper:0.line: 'Has someone taken the *newspaper* already?' the old man asked softly.

piece:0.en: The Manager brought in a small cake to celebrate the new branch contract. He cut it carefully into four equal parts. 'One *piece* for each of us,' he said, sliding a slice toward me. It was the first time I felt like I truly belonged to the team.
piece:0.cnHint: 店长切蛋糕庆祝签约，给每人一____，让我第一次感到自己真正融入了团队。
piece:0.hook: Tang quietly put their slice back and said they were saving it for someone.
piece:0.line: 'One *piece* for each of us,' the Manager said, smiling at me.

target:0.en: Lin spread a printed chart on the counter during a quiet hour. 'Our *target* for the new branch is two hundred customers a day by month three,' Lin said, tapping the number. The Manager nodded slowly. I looked at the empty street outside and said nothing.
target:0.cnHint: 林在柜台上摊开图表，说新分店的____是每天两百名顾客。
target:0.hook: Then a bus pulled up outside and twenty people stepped off at once.
target:0.line: 'Our *target* is two hundred customers a day by month three,' Lin said firmly.

actual:0.en: I had imagined the new branch would be huge and bright. When the Manager finally showed us a photo, the *actual* space was tiny — even smaller than this one. Tang burst out laughing. The Manager looked a little hurt, then started laughing too.
actual:0.cnHint: 我以为新分店会很大，但____的地方比想象中小得多，大家都笑了。
actual:0.hook: In the corner of the photo, just visible, stood a familiar face.
actual:0.line: 'The *actual* space is small, but we will make it work,' the Manager said.

pursue:0.en: The Manager spread a city map across the counter at midnight. 'We need a second store,' he said, tapping a red circle near the university. He had decided to *pursue* this plan for two years, saving every spare coin. Now the moment felt close.
pursue:0.cnHint: 店长深夜摊开地图，决定____开分店的梦想。
pursue:0.hook: But someone else had circled the same spot first.
pursue:0.line: 'I will *pursue* this dream until the key is in my hand.'

site:0.en: Tang walked me to a quiet corner two blocks away. A small empty shop sat between a noodle place and a bookstore. 'This is the *site* the Manager chose,' Tang whispered, pressing her nose against the dark glass. It looked perfect — almost too perfect.
site:0.cnHint: 唐带我去看店长选中的分店____。
site:0.hook: A light flicked on inside the empty shop.
site:0.line: 'This *site* is exactly what we have been looking for.'

absorb:0.en: I spent my first slow hour reading the Manager's thick folder on the new branch. Numbers, floor plans, supply lists — my tired brain struggled to *absorb* it all. Tang set a warm cup of tea beside me without a word. Outside, the street stayed quiet.
absorb:0.cnHint: 我努力____店长准备的分店资料，信息量太大了。
absorb:0.hook: One page near the back had no numbers — only a name.
absorb:0.line: 'Take your time; even I needed a week to *absorb* all this.'

advance:0.en: 'We paid the rent three months in *advance*,' the Manager said proudly, sliding a receipt across the counter. Tang and I exchanged a look. Three months meant the decision was final. The new store would open whether we were ready or not. My palms went a little damp.
advance:0.cnHint: 店长宣布已____支付了分店的房租，计划板上钉钉。
advance:0.hook: Tang quietly slid her resignation letter back into her pocket.
advance:0.line: 'Paying in *advance* shows them we are serious about this.'

capable:0.en: Lin appeared just after two in the morning, leaning on the freezer with a small smile. 'You really think your little team is *capable* of running two stores at once?' she asked. Nobody answered. The hum of the freezer filled the silence. The Manager just refilled his coffee.
capable:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林来店里，质疑我们的团队是否____同时经营两家店。
capable:0.hook: The Manager's silence was louder than any reply.
capable:0.line: 'We are more than *capable* — watch us prove it.'

dollar:0.en: Tang pinned a hand-drawn sign above the register: BRANCH FUND. A glass jar sat below it. The first coin dropped in with a soft clink. 'Every *dollar* we save goes straight into that jar,' she announced. I dropped in my spare change. Even the Manager fished out a coin.
dollar:0.cnHint: 唐设了一个零钱罐，每一个____都存进去为分店筹资。
dollar:0.hook: By dawn the jar already had a small crack.
dollar:0.line: 'Every *dollar* counts when you are building something new.'

double:0.en: The Manager showed us the new store's floor plan. 'The floor space is nearly *double* ours,' he said, tracing the outline with his finger. Tang's eyes went wide. I tried to imagine stocking shelves that long. It felt exciting and frightening in exactly equal measure.
double:0.cnHint: 新分店的面积几乎是现在的____，大家既兴奋又紧张。
double:0.hook: Tang quietly asked who would work the extra night shifts.
double:0.line: 'The counter alone is *double* the size of this one.'

federal:0.en: A serious-looking woman in a grey coat came in just before three and asked for the Manager. She set a document on the counter. 'There is a *federal* food-safety check next week,' she said flatly. 'New branches get extra attention.' She left before anyone could speak.
federal:0.cnHint: 一名检查员通知店长，分店开张前需要接受____食品安全检查。
federal:0.hook: The Manager turned the document over and went very still.
federal:0.line: 'A *federal* inspection at the new site — we must be ready.'

campaign:0.en: The Manager called us into the back room after closing. He unrolled a hand-drawn poster on the table. 'We are starting a *campaign* to bring customers from the new street,' he said, tapping the paper with one finger. Tang and I looked at each other. The poster had a small drawing of a smiling rice ball on it.
campaign:0.cnHint: 店长展开手绘海报，宣布要发起一场____，吸引新街道的顾客。
campaign:0.hook: But Lin, from the shop across the road, was already watching through the window.
campaign:0.line: 'This *campaign* will bring fifty new faces through that door,' the Manager said.

hurt:0.en: Tang knocked over a full shelf of canned soup at two in the morning. Cans rolled across the floor like loud, round opinions. I ran over. 'Are you okay? Did you get *hurt*?' I asked. She held up one hand, perfectly fine, then looked at the mess and winced. 'Only my pride,' she said quietly.
hurt:0.cnHint: 唐深夜打翻了一排罐头，我赶紧跑去问她有没有____。
hurt:0.hook: She then glanced toward the door, where a regular stood watching with wide eyes.
hurt:0.line: 'I am not *hurt*, but please pretend you did not see that,' Tang whispered.

initiative:0.en: Nobody asked me to rearrange the snack wall. I just did it one slow night, grouping things by flavour instead of by size. When the Manager arrived at dawn, he stared at it for a long moment. He nodded once. 'Good *initiative*,' he said, and went to make tea without another word.
initiative:0.cnHint: 没人叫我整理零食墙，我自己主动做了，店长称赞了我的____。
initiative:0.hook: Later I noticed one item had been quietly moved back to its old spot.
initiative:0.line: 'Taking *initiative* on a quiet night is how this store stays ahead,' the Manager said.

jump:0.en: The electricity cut out for three seconds at midnight. Every screen went black, the fridge hummed and stopped, and Tang let out a short, sharp sound. 'Did you just *jump*?' I asked, trying not to smile. 'The floor moved,' she said firmly, straightening her name tag with great dignity.
jump:0.cnHint: 半夜突然停电，唐被吓得____了一下，却坚持说是地板动了。
jump:0.hook: Then we both heard a slow knock coming from the storage room door.
jump:0.line: 'I did not *jump*,' Tang said. 'I simply reacted with great speed.'

lie:0.en: Our store does not *lie* on a busy road, but the Manager insists that is a strength. 'Quiet streets mean loyal customers,' he always says. I was not sure at first. But by my third week, I knew every regular by their usual order, and each one greeted me by name. Maybe he was right.
lie:0.cnHint: 我们的小店____在一条安静的街道上，店长说这反而是优势。
lie:0.hook: Then one night a stranger walked in who knew my name before I had told them.
lie:0.line: 'This store *lies* at the heart of the neighbourhood, even if the map disagrees,' the Manager said.

lunch:0.en: Tang brought two boxes of home-made food for our overlap shift at noon. She set one box in front of me without a word. We ate *lunch* standing behind the counter because the store does not close, not even for a meal. It was the best rice I had eaten in weeks, and I forgot to say thank you.
lunch:0.cnHint: 唐带来了自制饭盒，我们站在柜台后面一起吃____，我却忘了道谢。
lunch:0.hook: She brought the same box again the next day, without being asked.
lunch:0.line: '*Lunch* behind the counter is a tradition here,' Tang said. 'You will get used to it.'

necessarily:0.en: Lin came in to buy a bottle of water, which does not *necessarily* mean anything, but this was the third time this week. Each visit, Lin walked slowly past our new display and looked at the prices. The Manager watched from the corner of his eye and kept on wiping the counter with a very calm face.
necessarily:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林来买水，这不____意味着什么——但这已经是这周第三次了。
necessarily:0.hook: This time, Lin took a photo of our price tag before leaving.
necessarily:0.line: 'Coming in here does not *necessarily* mean I am impressed,' Lin said, almost to themselves.

psychologist:0.en: A woman came in every night at eleven and bought exactly one cup of warm corn soup. One evening she told me, with no warning at all, that she was a *psychologist* who worked late helping people sort out their worries. 'And who helps you sort out yours?' I asked. She looked at the soup cup for a long moment.
psychologist:0.cnHint: 一位深夜常客告诉我她是一名____，专门帮别人解开心结。
psychologist:0.hook: She came back the next night with two cups instead of one.
psychologist:0.line: 'Being a *psychologist* means I listen all day, so at night I just want soup,' she said.

gather:0.en: The Manager called everyone to the back room before sunrise. Tang and I stood near the shelves while he spread a hand-drawn map across the table. 'The new branch opens next week,' he said. Slowly, the details of our new roles began to *gather* into something real.
gather:0.cnHint: 店长把大家叫到后室，新分店的计划像衣褶一样开始____在一起，轮廓渐渐清晰。
gather:0.hook: But the map showed a street none of us recognised.
gather:0.line: 'Little by little, the pieces *gather* and the picture becomes clear.'

imagine:0.en: I tried to *imagine* a second store — same bright lights, same hum of the cooler, same smell of fresh buns — but on a street I had never walked. Tang caught me staring at the wall and laughed. 'You look like you just saw a ghost,' she said, handing me a mop.
imagine:0.cnHint: 我努力____新分店的样子，却发现自己根本没去过那条街。
imagine:0.hook: Then Tang went quiet and stared at the same wall herself.
imagine:0.line: 'Can you *imagine* working the night shift there alone?'

instance:0.en: The Manager listed all the problems the new branch might face. 'Take this as one *instance*,' he said, pointing to a photo of a narrow doorway barely wide enough for a delivery cart. Tang nodded seriously. I wrote everything down, even though my pen was almost out of ink.
instance:0.cnHint: 店长举了一个____，指出新分店门口的通道可能太窄，送货会很麻烦。
instance:0.hook: That photo was taken only yesterday — by Lin.
instance:0.line: 'In this *instance*, the door is the biggest problem we face.'

numerous:0.en: The Manager slid a folder across the table. Inside were *numerous* notes — feedback from customers, counts of daily visitors, lists of missing products. Tang flipped through the pages slowly. I had no idea so much had been written down about a store that had not even opened yet.
numerous:0.cnHint: 文件夹里有____张顾客反馈和数据记录，为新分店的开业做了充分准备。
numerous:0.hook: The last page had a single name underlined three times.
numerous:0.line: 'There are *numerous* details to check before we open the doors.'

puzzle:0.en: A delivery arrived addressed to the new branch, but the boxes were left at our store by mistake. Tang and I tried to match each box to a list on the wall, but one item simply would not fit. The missing label was a *puzzle* neither of us could solve before sunrise.
puzzle:0.cnHint: 一批货错送到了我们店，其中一箱没有标签，成了大家都解不开的____。
puzzle:0.hook: The box was ticking — not with a clock, but with something alive.
puzzle:0.line: 'This missing label is a real *puzzle* — nothing on the list matches.'

remind:0.en: Before I left at dawn, the Manager handed me a small card with the new store's address. 'Keep it,' he said. 'It will *remind* you why we are all working so hard this week.' I slipped it into my pocket and felt, for the first time, that I was part of something bigger.
remind:0.cnHint: 店长给了我一张新店地址卡片，让它____我们为何这周如此努力。
remind:0.hook: On the back of the card was a handwritten question mark.
remind:0.line: 'Take this card — let it *remind* you of what we are building together.'

truly:0.en: After an hour of planning, the Manager looked around the back room and smiled. 'This,' he said softly, 'is *truly* a team.' Tang rolled her eyes but smiled too. I straightened the stack of folders just to have something to do with my hands. Outside, the street was beginning to grow light.
truly:0.cnHint: 店长看着大家感慨，这____是一支好团队，就连平时爱抱怨的同事也笑了。
truly:0.hook: At that moment, the front door opened and someone walked in who should not have known about the meeting.
truly:0.line: 'I am *truly* glad we are doing this together, all of us.'

valuable:0.en: The Manager locked away the hand-drawn maps and said the location of the new branch was still a secret. 'That information is *valuable*,' he warned, tapping the drawer twice. Tang winked at me across the room. I said nothing, but I had already memorised the street name on the address card.
valuable:0.cnHint: 店长把地图锁起来，说新店的选址是____信息，还不能对外透露。
valuable:0.hook: Tang's wink told me she had memorised it too.
valuable:0.line: 'Keep this address safe — it is *valuable* information until the opening day.'

writer:0.en: A quiet man comes in every night at two, buys the same hot tea, and sits at the corner table with a thick notebook. He fills page after page without stopping. The Manager told me he is a *writer* who works only when the city is asleep.
writer:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我，那个深夜来买热茶、在角落奋笔疾书的男人其实是个____。
writer:0.hook: Last night he tore out every page and left them on the counter.
writer:0.line: 'He is a *writer*, so keep the corner table free for him.'

addition:0.en: The Manager points to a new shelf near the door, still smelling of fresh wood. Hot soup cups, hand warmers, and small candles line it neatly. 'This *addition* was my idea,' he says proudly, then trips over the step ladder he forgot to put away.
addition:0.cnHint: 店长骄傲地介绍门口新增的货架，但随即出了个小洋相。
addition:0.hook: Tang quietly moves the ladder, saying nothing, hiding a smile.
addition:0.line: 'This *addition* will make cold-night customers very happy.'

alternative:0.en: The coffee machine breaks down at three in the morning. A student stares at it with tired eyes. I offer warm barley tea as an *alternative*. She hesitates, then wraps both hands around the cup and says it is actually better than coffee on a cold night.
alternative:0.cnHint: 咖啡机坏了，我向一位疲惫的学生推荐了____，她喝后意外地很满意。
alternative:0.hook: She comes back the next night and asks only for the barley tea.
alternative:0.line: 'Barley tea is a good *alternative* when the machine is broken.'

amazing:0.en: Tang shows me how she can scan twelve items, count change, and answer the phone all at the same time without making a single mistake. I stand there with my mouth open. 'You will learn,' she says, laughing. But honestly, watching her work is *amazing*.
amazing:0.cnHint: 看着同事同时处理好几件事却毫无差错，我感到十分____。
amazing:0.hook: Tang then nods toward the door — a very unusual customer is coming in.
amazing:0.line: 'It is *amazing* how calm she stays when the store gets busy.'

ease:0.en: Lin from the store across the street walks in just before dawn, leans on our counter, and chats with Tang as if they are old friends. She moves with total *ease*, like she owns every room she enters. The Manager watches from the back with narrow eyes.
ease:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林走进店里，举止从容自若，店长在背后皱起了眉头。
ease:0.hook: Lin buys nothing, smiles, and drops one quiet sentence before leaving.
ease:0.line: 'She does everything with such *ease* — that is what worries me.'

frequent:0.en: I notice the same elderly man buying a small carton of warm milk at exactly midnight every single night. Tang says he has been a *frequent* visitor for three years. Nobody knows his name. He always pays with exact coins and never says a word.
frequent:0.cnHint: 唐告诉我，那位每晚准时买热牛奶的老人已经是____顾客整整三年了。
frequent:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he pauses and looks like he wants to speak.
frequent:0.line: 'He is our most *frequent* visitor, but we still know nothing about him.'

hope:0.en: It is the last night before the new branch opens across town. The Manager stands alone by the window, holding a cold cup of tea. 'I *hope* the new staff will care about the small things,' he says softly, more to himself than to me, 'the way you two do.'
hope:0.cnHint: 新分店开业前夕，店长望着窗外轻声表达了他的____。
hope:0.hook: Then he adds one more sentence that neither Tang nor I expected.
hope:0.line: 'I *hope* this place still feels like home after we expand.'

imply:0.en: Lin stops by again and admires our new soup shelf loudly. 'Very clever use of space,' she says, smiling. Tang leans over to me and whispers, 'She does not say it, but her words *imply* she is planning to copy it.' I look back at Lin, still smiling at the shelf.
imply:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林称赞我们的新货架，唐悄悄告诉我她的话____着什么意图。
imply:0.hook: Lin takes a slow photo with her phone before she walks out.
imply:0.line: 'Her kind words *imply* she is already planning her next move.'

pose:0.en: The Manager asked us to stand behind the counter for a photo. Tang leaned on the cash register and grinned. I tried to look natural, but my arms felt strange. 'Hold that *pose*,' the Manager said, pointing his phone at us. The picture was for the new branch's welcome board.
pose:0.cnHint: 店长让我们为新分店的欢迎展板____，大家努力摆出自然的样子。
pose:0.hook: But Tang's grin hid something he hadn't told anyone yet.
pose:0.line: 'Hold that *pose* — the new branch needs a friendly face on the board.'

stimulate:0.en: The Manager pinned a bright new menu on the wall, full of warm drinks and fresh snacks. 'Good choices *stimulate* customers to spend more,' he said, tapping the list proudly. Tang nodded. I looked at the prices and quietly wondered if our regulars would agree. Outside, the street was still dark and empty.
stimulate:0.cnHint: 店长认为新菜单能____顾客消费，但我悄悄觉得老顾客未必买账。
stimulate:0.hook: Just then the door opened and our most careful regular walked straight in.
stimulate:0.line: 'Good choices *stimulate* customers — that is the whole point of a new menu.'

switch:0.en: Halfway through the night, the Manager decided to *switch* the shelves around — cold drinks on the left, hot snacks on the right. Tang and I moved everything while customers watched, confused. One old man picked up a can, put it back, then searched the whole store before finding it again. He did not look pleased.
switch:0.cnHint: 店长决定____货架布局，害得一位老顾客找东西找了半天。
switch:0.hook: The old man left without buying anything, but he paused at the door.
switch:0.line: 'We need to *switch* the shelves before the new branch opens — fresh layout, fresh start.'

treatment:0.en: A delivery worker came in just before two in the morning, wet from the rain. Tang handed him a hot cup without being asked. The man looked surprised. 'This kind of *treatment* is rare at this hour,' he said softly, warming his hands on the cup. I made a note to remember his usual order from then on.
treatment:0.cnHint: 一位冒雨送货的工人对我们深夜的____感到意外和感动。
treatment:0.hook: He left a small folded note under the empty cup before he went.
treatment:0.line: 'This *treatment* is rare at two in the morning — thank you, really.'

union:0.en: The Manager spread a map on the counter. Three store owners from the same street had agreed to share late-night deliveries. 'A *union* like this saves us all money,' he said. Tang looked interested. I looked at the map and noticed one of the three stores was run by Lin. Nobody mentioned that out loud.
union:0.cnHint: 店长宣布三家店组成____共担配送成本，但其中一家是林的店。
union:0.hook: Lin's store was circled in red, and the Manager said nothing about it.
union:0.line: 'A *union* like this saves money for everyone on the street.'

acknowledge:0.en: Lin came in just before closing to return a small box of goods she had borrowed the night before. I waited. She set the box down, looked at me, and gave one short nod. It was the closest she would come to saying thank you. I decided to *acknowledge* the gesture with a nod of my own and say nothing more.
acknowledge:0.cnHint: 林还回借用的货物，我选择____她那个几乎算不上道谢的点头。
acknowledge:0.hook: She paused at the door, as if she wanted to add one more word.
acknowledge:0.line: 'I *acknowledge* that you helped us last night — the box is all there.'

alike:0.en: Tang and I covered the same shift, drank the same cheap coffee, and complained about the same flickering light above the door. By three in the morning a regular told us we even answered questions *alike*, finishing each other's sentences. Tang laughed. I wasn't sure if that was a good thing or if I had simply been here too long.
alike:0.cnHint: 一位常客说我和同事回答问题的方式____，我一时不知是喜是忧。
alike:0.hook: Tang stopped laughing and gave me a look I couldn't quite read.
alike:0.line: 'You two sound exactly *alike* — were you trained by the same robot?'

analyze:0.en: After the slow hours before dawn, the Manager sat at the little corner table and began to *analyze* last week's sales numbers. He circled figures, crossed out others, and muttered to himself. Tang leaned over once, then stepped back, looking worried. I restocked the shelves quietly and tried not to hear the muttering get louder.
analyze:0.cnHint: 店长深夜____上周销售数据，数字似乎让他越来越不安。
analyze:0.hook: He finally looked up and asked for last night's receipt with quiet urgency.
analyze:0.line: 'Let me *analyze* the numbers before we decide anything about the new branch.'

content:0.en: The back office smelled of old paper and instant noodles. The Manager spread a city map across the desk and pointed to a quiet corner block. 'Our new branch goes here,' he said. I looked at the circled spot and felt *content* — it was exactly the neighbourhood I had hoped for.
content:0.cnHint: 店长展示新分店地址，我对选址感到____。
content:0.hook: But Lin had circled the same block on her own map.
content:0.line: 'I'm *content* with this corner — the foot traffic is just right.'

divide:0.en: Tang drew a long line down the middle of the store plan. 'We *divide* the new floor space this way,' she said, tapping one half. 'Storage left, sales floor right.' I nodded, but the line felt less like a plan and more like a warning about the argument coming next.
divide:0.cnHint: 阿糖把新店平面图____成两半，各有用途。
divide:0.hook: The Manager had drawn a completely different line the night before.
divide:0.line: 'Let's *divide* the floor evenly — no one gets the better half.'

generate:0.en: The Manager pulled out a notebook full of numbers. 'A second location will *generate* enough income to keep both stores open through winter,' he said quietly. I wrote the figure down. Outside, the street was empty and cold, and the single lamp above us flickered as if it agreed.
generate:0.cnHint: 店长解释开分店能____足够的收入过冬。
generate:0.hook: Tang's face said she had already seen those numbers and doubted them.
generate:0.line: 'One busy corner can *generate* more than you think.'

operate:0.en: Lin arrived just before midnight carrying a folder. She had managed three stores before ours. 'I know how to *operate* a branch on a small budget,' she said, dropping the folder on the counter. I flipped through it. Every page was clean, efficient, and slightly frightening in how thorough it was.
operate:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林声称自己知道如何____一家小预算分店。
operate:0.hook: The last page had a name on it — and it was mine.
operate:0.line: 'I've *operated* stores like this one since I was your age.'

properly:0.en: I spent an hour arranging the sample shelf for the new branch display. Tang watched, then gently moved three items. 'Now it's done *properly*,' she said, almost to herself. I looked at the difference — it was small but real. I made a note not to argue with someone who had been here six years longer.
properly:0.cnHint: 阿糖把陈列重新摆好，说这才是____的做法。
properly:0.hook: Then the Manager walked in and moved everything again.
properly:0.line: 'If you label each shelf *properly*, restocking takes half the time.'

render:0.en: The new branch sign arrived flat-packed in a long box. Tang held it up under the light. The bright colour and sharp letters would *render* the quiet corner instantly visible from across the street. I could already picture it glowing on a rainy night, pulling in strangers who only meant to pass by.
render:0.cnHint: 新招牌能把那个安静的街角____得格外显眼。
render:0.hook: Lin said the sign was facing the wrong direction.
render:0.line: 'Good lighting can *render* even a small store hard to ignore.'

resolve:0.en: The meeting about the opening date dragged past two in the morning. Tang wanted next month; Lin wanted next week. Finally the Manager set his cup down with a soft knock. 'My *resolve* is fixed,' he said. 'We open in ten days.' The room went quiet. I wrote the date in large numbers.
resolve:0.cnHint: 店长表明自己的____已定，十天后开业。
resolve:0.hook: Ten days was exactly the amount of time we did not have.
resolve:0.line: 'My *resolve* won't change — we've delayed long enough.'

seemingly:0.en: Lin walked the new store twice without a word. The space was *seemingly* perfect: clean windows, good light, wide aisles. Then she crouched near the back wall and pressed one tile. It rocked. She stood up, brushed her hands, and smiled at me as if she had just won a quiet argument nobody else knew was happening.
seemingly:0.cnHint: 新店____一切完好，但隔壁咖啡店的林发现了一个隐藏的问题。
seemingly:0.hook: She handed me a list of eleven more things to check.
seemingly:0.line: 'It's *seemingly* fine on the surface — but look closer.'

belong:0.en: The Manager held up a small cardboard box filled with odd items: a single glove, a toy car, a folded map, and a purple scarf. 'These *belong* to customers who never came back,' he said quietly, setting the box on the shelf above the register. I counted seven items. Seven forgotten stories.
belong:0.cnHint: 店长把一箱子失物放上搁板，说这些东西都____这里的老顾客。
belong:0.hook: Then I noticed one item had my name written on it.
belong:0.line: 'These *belong* to people who once stood right where you are standing.'

beneficial:0.en: Tang slid a warm cup across the counter toward me. 'Ginger and honey,' she said with a shrug. 'Night shifts are cold. This is *beneficial*, trust me.' I took a sip. It tasted like something a grandmother would make. Outside, rain began to tap softly against the window.
beneficial:0.cnHint: 阿糖给我冲了一杯姜蜂蜜水，说对熬夜值班____。
beneficial:0.hook: She watched me drink every drop, her expression oddly serious.
beneficial:0.line: 'One cup every night — it is genuinely *beneficial* for your health.'

characteristic:0.en: Lin walked in at exactly two in the morning, as always. That quiet, unhurried step was his most obvious *characteristic* — he moved like the whole street belonged to him. He picked up a small bottle of water, placed exact change on the counter without a word, and left.
characteristic:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林每天凌晨两点准时进店，那种从容不迫是他最明显的____。
characteristic:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he paused and looked back at me.
characteristic:0.line: 'Calm under pressure — that is the *characteristic* of every good night worker.'

director:0.en: A tall woman in a long coat entered and asked for three energy drinks and a pen. Tang whispered to me, 'She is the *director* of that small theatre two blocks away — they rehearse all night.' The woman scribbled something on her hand, nodded her thanks, and disappeared into the dark.
director:0.cnHint: 阿糖悄悄告诉我，刚进来买东西的女士是附近小剧场的____。
director:0.hook: The word she had written on her hand looked like my address.
director:0.line: 'As *director*, I make every decision — including which store we buy snacks from.'

emerge:0.en: Around three in the morning, the back storage room door creaked open and Tang began to *emerge* slowly, arms full of boxes, her hair dusted white with something that looked like flour. She blinked under the bright light and said simply, 'We are low on bread. I was checking.'
emerge:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点，阿糖从储藏室____，头发上沾满了白色粉末。
emerge:0.hook: There was no flour delivery scheduled for that week.
emerge:0.line: 'Every night, strange things *emerge* from that storage room — you will see.'

exact:0.en: 'The *exact* number of steps from the front door to the register is eleven,' the Manager told me on my first night, arms folded. 'I have counted every day for six years.' I walked it myself. Eleven steps. I did not know whether to be impressed or worried.
exact:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我，从大门到收银台____的步数，他数了六年。
exact:0.hook: He then asked me to count the steps to the back door.
exact:0.line: 'Write down the *exact* time each customer enters — every minute matters here.'

guest:0.en: A quiet older man came in just before four and slowly browsed every aisle without picking up a thing. Tang leaned over and whispered, 'He is not a regular *guest* — he used to own this store.' He finally stopped in front of the back shelf and smiled at something only he could see.
guest:0.cnHint: 一位老人在店里逛了很久，阿糖说他不是普通____，曾经是这家店的老板。
guest:0.hook: He left a small key on the counter without saying a word.
guest:0.line: 'Every *guest* here carries a story — your job is to listen.'

massive:0.en: Just after five, a delivery truck pulled up and two workers began unloading a *massive* crate through the side door. It barely fit through the frame. Tang watched with wide eyes. 'That is the new coffee machine,' she said. 'The Manager ordered it three months ago and told no one else.'
massive:0.cnHint: 清晨五点，工人们搬来一个____的大箱子，阿糖说里面是店长偷偷订购的新咖啡机。
massive:0.hook: The crate was addressed not to the store, but to me.
massive:0.line: 'A *massive* change is coming to this store — starting tomorrow morning.'

insist:0.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter. 'The new branch goes here — corner of East Lake Road,' he said. I pointed out that the space looked too small for a stockroom. He just smiled and *insisted* the layout would work perfectly. I was not so sure, but he had opened six stores before this one.
insist:0.cnHint: 店长把新分店的手绘地图摊在柜台上，____说选址布局完全没问题。
insist:0.hook: But the map had a second mark no one had explained yet.
insist:0.line: 'I *insist* the corner spot is the right one — trust me on this.'

investigation:0.en: Tang found a box of missing rice balls behind the milk shelf and held it up like a trophy. The Manager frowned and launched a quiet *investigation* into how stock kept ending up in the wrong place. We checked every shelf twice. By midnight we had a list of twelve misplaced items — and one very guilty-looking mop bucket.
investigation:0.cnHint: 阿糖发现货物摆放混乱，店长随即展开了一场小小的____。
investigation:0.hook: The security camera, however, told a stranger story than anyone expected.
investigation:0.line: 'A quick *investigation* of the back shelf might solve this tonight,' Tang said.

limited:0.en: The Manager slid a printed sheet across the counter. Space in the new branch would be *limited*, so only the top thirty best-selling items would go on the opening list. I scanned the sheet. Instant noodles, yes. My favourite pineapple cakes, no. I made a mental note to argue for them at the next meeting.
limited:0.cnHint: 新分店面积有限，店长说上架商品数量是____的，只能选最畅销的。
limited:0.hook: Then I noticed one item on the list that nobody had ever actually ordered.
limited:0.line: 'Storage is *limited*, so we need to choose every product carefully,' the Manager said.

listen:0.en: Lin from the store across the street stopped by, pretending to buy gum. I could tell he was really here to *listen* to the Manager's phone call about the new branch location. The Manager spotted him instantly, switched to talking about the weather, and winked at me. Lin left with his gum and zero useful information.
listen:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林假装买口香糖，其实是想____店长关于新分店选址的电话内容。
listen:0.hook: Lin would be back tomorrow — I could already feel it.
listen:0.line: 'I just stopped in to *listen* to what people around here need,' Lin said with a smile.

master:0.en: A quiet man came in every night at two and bought exactly one coffee. Tang told me he was a *master* of urban planning at the city college, and that the Manager had been asking him questions about foot traffic for weeks. Tonight the man unrolled a long paper tube on the counter. Inside was a set of professional drawings.
master:0.cnHint: 每晚两点来买咖啡的男人原来是城市规划专业的____，他带来了一套专业图纸。
master:0.hook: The drawings showed a location none of us had ever considered.
master:0.line: 'I am a *master* in urban planning — let me take a look at that map,' the man said quietly.

newly:0.en: The Manager arrived at ten with paint still on his shoes. He had spent the afternoon at the *newly* rented space on East Lake Road, measuring walls and testing the lights. His eyes were bright in a way I had not seen before. Tang poured him a hot tea without being asked, and for a moment the three of us just stood there feeling quietly excited.
newly:0.cnHint: 店长刚从____租下的东湖路铺面回来，鞋上还沾着油漆。
newly:0.hook: He set a single key on the counter and slid it toward no one in particular.
newly:0.line: 'The *newly* rented place already feels like ours,' the Manager said, warming his hands on the cup.

north:0.en: A delivery driver burst in at midnight, soaking wet, and asked for the fastest route to *north* of the river. The Manager drew a route on a receipt with a ballpoint pen, marked two road-works spots, and added the shortcut only locals know. The driver was gone in under a minute. The Manager watched the door close and said, 'The new branch is also north of the river.'

He asked me to keep it safe until morning, when he would come back to post it. Then he walked out into the rain without an umbrella.
card:0.cnHint: 一位年轻人托我保管一张写给奶奶的生日____，转身就走进了雨里。
card:0.hook: Morning came, and he never returned for it.
card:0.line: 'Please keep this *card* dry for me,' he said, like it held something heavier than paper.

gene:0.en: Tang was reading a science magazine at the counter, deep in a page about *gene* research, when I asked her why she worked nights at a convenience store. She looked up over the top of the magazine. 'Because,' she said, 'the quiet helps me think.' Then she went back to reading without another word.
gene:0.cnHint: 阿糖在柜台后读着关于____研究的杂志，说夜班的安静有助于她思考。
gene:0.hook: She had dog-eared the same page for three weeks but never seemed to finish it.
gene:0.line: 'It says here a single *gene* can change almost everything,' Tang said, not looking up.

modern:0.en: The Manager spread a big map on the counter and pointed to a spot two streets away. 'Our new branch will open there,' he said proudly. The empty shop had tall glass windows and clean white walls — very *modern* compared to our cosy little store. I tried to look excited, but secretly I loved our old shelves more.
modern:0.cnHint: 店长展示新分店的设计图，新店风格非常____。
modern:0.hook: But someone had already slipped a note under that shop's door.
modern:0.line: 'It looks very *modern*, but I hope it still feels like home.'

officer:0.en: A tired-looking man in a neat uniform came in just after midnight and bought two meat buns and a bottle of water. Tang whispered that he was a city *officer* who checked food safety at restaurants all day. He ate standing up, quietly, facing the window. I warmed an extra bun without being asked.
officer:0.cnHint: 一位负责食品安全的____深夜来买包子，神情疲惫。
officer:0.hook: His notebook was open to a page with our store's address on it.
officer:0.line: 'Being an *officer* sounds important, but mostly it means skipping lunch.'

convince:0.en: Lin walked in holding a stack of flyers for a new store opening nearby. She tried to *convince* the Manager to share a delivery deal, smiling the whole time. The Manager listened, nodded slowly, and said he would think about it. After Lin left, he threw the flyers in the bin without even looking at them.
convince:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林试图____店长与她合作，但店长表面客气，内心另有想法。
convince:0.hook: Lin came back an hour later, this time without flyers but with a very different offer.
convince:0.line: 'I can *convince* him — I just need five more minutes and better tea.'

directly:0.en: A boy of about ten ran in, went *directly* to the snack shelf, and picked up a small bag of rice crackers. He placed exact change on the counter without a word, gave me a serious nod, and left at the same speed. It was the most efficient shopping trip I had ever seen. Tang said he came every night at the same time.
directly:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩____走向零食架，动作干净利落，从不多话。
directly:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he paused and looked back at the door.
directly:0.line: 'I always go *directly* to what I need — no time for looking around.'

extend:0.en: The Manager called a short meeting at three in the morning to say he wanted to *extend* our store hours to include a breakfast rush. Tang looked at the clock, then at the Manager, then back at the clock. I wrote everything down carefully. Our shift was already twelve hours. Nobody said anything, but the silence was very loud.
extend:0.cnHint: 店长宣布要____营业时间以覆盖早餐时段，众人沉默。
extend:0.hook: Then Tang smiled in a way that usually meant trouble.
extend:0.line: 'If we *extend* the hours, I want the first breakfast shift — I make great eggs.'

rat:0.en: Just before dawn, a small grey *rat* ran across the back of the store and disappeared behind the drink fridge. I froze. Tang calmly picked up a broom, walked over, and looked behind the fridge with a torch for a full minute. 'Gone,' she said, and went back to reading her magazine as if nothing had happened.
rat:0.cnHint: 黎明前，店里出现了一只____，阿糖处理得异常镇定。
rat:0.hook: But I noticed Tang had quietly moved her snack bag to the top shelf.
rat:0.line: 'One little *rat* is not a problem — now, two is a different story.'

saturday:0.en: On *Saturday* the store was unusually full by two in the morning. Groups of students, workers heading home, and one man in a full cooking uniform all stood in line at once. Tang said weekends were always like this. I dropped a bag of chips, knocked over a display stand, and still managed to serve everyone with a smile.
saturday:0.cnHint: 周____凌晨，小店异常热闹，新来的店员忙得手忙脚乱。
saturday:0.hook: The man in the cooking uniform left behind a small handwritten card.
saturday:0.line: 'Every *Saturday* night I come here — it feels like the city slows down a little.'

april:0.en: The Manager put up a small paper sign that read: 'New branch opens in *April*.' Tang stared at it for a long moment, then stuck a smiley sticker in the corner without asking. A regular customer read it, frowned, and said, 'Does that mean you will be less busy here?' The Manager laughed. I was not sure what the answer was either.
april:0.cnHint: 店长贴出新分店将于____开业的告示，老顾客担心地问了个好问题。
april:0.hook: That same night, someone peeled off the sign and left a question mark in its place.
april:0.line: '*April* is not far — we should probably start training the new staff now.'

store:0.en: The Manager spread a big map across the counter at midnight. 'We are opening a second *store* next spring,' he said, pointing to a spot two streets away. He looked so proud, like a general planning a great battle. I nodded and tried to look calm, but inside I was already wondering who would work the night shift there.
store:0.cnHint: 店长深夜展开地图，兴奋地宣布要开一家新____。
store:0.hook: Then he looked straight at me and smiled a little too long.
store:0.line: 'This new *store* will change everything for this neighbourhood.'

budget:0.en: The Manager pulled out a thick notebook filled with numbers. 'The *budget* for the new location is tight,' he admitted, tapping the page with his pen. 'So we cut costs where we can.' Tang leaned over and whispered that the staff tea had already been changed to the cheapest kind. I checked my cup. Tang was right.
budget:0.cnHint: 店长拿出厚厚的笔记本，说新店的____很紧张。
budget:0.hook: Tang then quietly pointed to a line item labelled 'night staff bonus.'
budget:0.line: 'I drew up the *budget* myself, and yes, I did remove the good tea.'

grant:0.en: The Manager waved a letter in the air when he came in just before dawn. A local business group would *grant* the new store some money to help it open, he said. He read the amount out loud twice. Tang started happy-dancing behind the chip shelf. I smiled too, though I was not sure what it all meant for my hours.
grant:0.cnHint: 店长挥舞着一封信，宣布有机构将____新店一笔资金。
grant:0.hook: But the letter also named one small condition nobody had read yet.
grant:0.line: 'They will *grant* us enough to fix the roof and buy a proper coffee machine.'

hospital:0.en: A quiet woman came in around two in the morning and bought four cans of soup and a phone charger. She told me she had just left the *hospital* after three days sitting beside her father's bed. She said the soup was for him — he was finally home. I put an extra chocolate bar in her bag without saying a word.
hospital:0.cnHint: 一位女士告诉我她刚从____回来，父亲终于可以出院了。
hospital:0.hook: She paused at the door and said her father had asked about the store's 'night angel.'
hospital:0.line: 'I have been living near a *hospital* waiting room for three days straight.'

island:0.en: An old man who came in every Thursday night once told me he grew up on a small *island* far to the south. There was only one small shop there, he said, and it closed at sunset. He always bought the same thing here: a warm meat bun and a bottle of water. 'On my island,' he said softly, 'we never had anything open at night.' He looked almost grateful just to be standing here.
island:0.cnHint: 一位老人说他在南方一座小____上长大，那里的商店天黑就关门。
island:0.hook: He left a small seashell on the counter without explaining why.
island:0.line: 'Back on my *island*, light in a shop window at night felt like a miracle.'

native:0.en: Lin walked in just after midnight and spent ten minutes studying our snack wall. 'You stocked the wrong kind,' Lin said at last, pointing at a row of spicy crackers. 'The *native* flavour from this region is much milder. Locals won't buy these.' The Manager, who had ordered the crackers himself, appeared silently from the back room and stood very still.
native:0.cnHint: 林指出我们进的零食口味不对，说本地____口味要淡得多。
native:0.hook: Lin and the Manager then stared at each other across the cracker shelf for a full ten seconds.
native:0.line: 'The *native* taste here is light and a little sweet — trust me on that.'

tradition:0.en: Tang arrived for the handover at six and placed a small paper bag on the counter. Inside were two sweet rice balls. 'It is a family *tradition*,' Tang said with a shrug. 'First day of every new month, you eat one. Brings good luck to the place you work.' I ate mine immediately. It was very good. Tang watched and nodded, as if I had just passed some kind of quiet test.
tradition:0.cnHint: 唐带来了两个汤圆，说每月初一吃一个是家里的____，能带来好运。
tradition:0.hook: Tang then mentioned there was a second tradition, one involving the Manager's car keys.
tradition:0.line: 'It is our family *tradition*, and so far not one job has gone badly.'

africa:0.en: A university student came in at three in the morning looking for a world map. We did not have one, but she told me she was preparing a talk about farming methods in *Africa* for her morning class. She ended up buying a notebook and sitting at the small corner table for an hour, writing fast. When she left she said, 'Thanks for the quiet.' I had not said a single word the whole time.
africa:0.cnHint: 一位大学生深夜来找世界地图，说她要准备一个关于____农业的演讲。
africa:0.hook: She left the notebook behind, and the last page had my name written in it.
africa:0.line: 'My whole talk is about water use in *Africa* — I just need one more good fact.'

comfortable:0.en: The Manager spread a thick *comfortable* over the small couch in the back room. 'Staff rest here between busy rushes,' he said proudly. The room smelled of instant noodles and old magazines. It was tiny, but somehow it felt like the warmest corner of the whole store.
comfortable:0.cnHint: 店长在后室的小沙发上铺了一条厚厚的____，说这是员工休息的地方。
comfortable:0.hook: But someone had already been sleeping there every night.
comfortable:0.line: 'This *comfortable* has kept me warm through every cold winter shift.'

conclusion:0.en: Tang counted the coins three times, then looked up with tired eyes. 'My *conclusion* is that someone keeps giving us fake ten-cent pieces,' she said flatly. I checked the jar. Six shiny coins, all wrong. We looked at each other, then slowly turned toward the door.
conclusion:0.cnHint: 阿糖数了三遍硬币，得出了一个令人不安的____。
conclusion:0.hook: The next customer walked in jingling his pocket loudly.
conclusion:0.line: 'My *conclusion* is that this has been going on for weeks.'

formal:0.en: A man in a stiff *formal* suit walked in at two in the morning, bought one cup of instant noodles, and sat very straight while eating it. He never loosened his tie. He left a business card on the table but no name was printed on it.
formal:0.cnHint: 一个穿着____西装的男人深夜走进来，买了杯泡面，坐得笔直地吃完。
formal:0.hook: He came back the next night wearing the exact same suit.
formal:0.line: 'I always wear *formal* clothes — it helps me stay focused at night.'

happiness:0.en: Old Mr. Chen visited every night for a cup of hot soy milk. He always paid with exact change and smiled the same quiet smile. 'Small things are where *happiness* lives,' he told me once, wrapping both hands around the warm cup. I wrote that down after he left.
happiness:0.cnHint: 老陈大爷每晚来买一杯热豆浆，说____就藏在小事里。
happiness:0.hook: Last night, for the first time, he came in with someone else.
happiness:0.line: '*Happiness* is a warm drink and a quiet street at two a.m.'

intelligent:0.en: Lin rearranged the snack shelf in under four minutes, grouping items by how often customers grabbed them. 'You have to be *intelligent* about shelf space,' she said without looking at me. Sales in that aisle went up the very next day. I did not tell her she was right.
intelligent:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林用聪明的方式重新摆放了货架，销量立刻上涨，但叙述者没有夸她。
intelligent:0.hook: She was already redesigning the drinks section when I arrived.
intelligent:0.line: 'You have to be *intelligent* about where you put the popular snacks.'
