novel:0.en: A girl sat on the floor by the magazine rack every night, reading a thick *novel* she never bought. She always stopped at the same page, folded the corner, and put it back. I started leaving it face-out so she could find it faster.
novel:0.cnHint: 一个女孩每晚蹲在杂志架旁读同一本____，却从来不买。
novel:0.hook: Tonight the novel was gone, and so was she.
novel:0.line: 'I read three pages of this *novel* every night — it calms me down.'

political:0.en: Two older men argued loudly over canned coffee about some *political* story they had seen on the news. Neither had watched the full report. Tang quietly moved breakable items off the nearest shelf. I offered them both a free straw, and somehow the argument stopped immediately.
political:0.cnHint: 两位老人为一则____新闻大声争论，阿糖悄悄把易碎品移开。
political:0.hook: They shook hands outside, then came back in for more coffee.
political:0.line: 'Every *political* argument in this city ends up in our store somehow.'

property:0.en: The Manager unrolled a large paper map on the counter and pointed to a small square two streets away. 'That *property* is where we open the new branch,' he said, eyes bright. Tang and I leaned in. The square was right next to Lin's store.
property:0.cnHint: 店长指着地图上的一块____，说那就是新分店的地址——就在竞争对手旁边。
property:0.hook: Lin walked in thirty seconds later, carrying the same map.
property:0.line: 'That *property* has been empty for a year — it is perfect for us.'

relative:0.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter. 'Our rent is low here, but foot traffic is weak,' he said. 'A second store in the shopping district would bring *relative* comfort — not rich, but steadier.' I studied the map, wondering if I had any say in this plan.
relative:0.cnHint: 店长在柜台上铺开地图，讨论开新店的____优势。
relative:0.hook: Then he circled a spot and looked straight at me.
relative:0.line: The profit there is *relative* — better than here, but not great.

rent:0.en: Tang slid a printed sheet to me during a slow hour. 'The Manager found a space near the university,' she whispered. 'The *rent* is higher than this place, but students buy snacks all night.' I looked at the numbers and raised an eyebrow. It was a lot of money for a small room.
rent:0.cnHint: 唐悄悄告诉我，新店的____比这里贵不少。
rent:0.hook: She tapped one figure and said, 'He already signed.'
rent:0.line: The *rent* is steep, but the location is perfect.

round:0.en: The Manager explained his plan like a general before battle. 'First *round*: open the new store. Second round: train the staff. Third round: turn a profit.' He counted on his fingers as he spoke. I nodded along, though I had just finished mopping the floor and my back hurt.
round:0.cnHint: 店长把开新店的计划分成几个____，逐步推进。
round:0.hook: He paused at 'third round' and stared at the ceiling.
round:0.line: The first *round* is always the hardest, trust me.

structure:0.en: Lin came in just before midnight, claiming she was 'just passing by.' She glanced at the Manager's notes on the counter. 'Your whole *structure* is wrong,' she said coolly. 'Two stores, one manager — that never works.' The Manager smiled without warmth. I pretended to arrange the chip rack nearby.
structure:0.cnHint: 林看了店长的计划后，批评新店的____有问题。
structure:0.hook: She left a business card on the counter and walked out.
structure:0.line: The *structure* of your plan will fall apart in a month.

typical:0.en: 'A second store near the park,' Tang sighed, refilling the drink fridge. 'That is so *typical* of him — big idea, no warning.' She had found out from a supplier, not the Manager himself. I handed her a box of juice cartons and decided it was better to listen than to speak.
typical:0.cnHint: 唐叹气说，店长突然宣布开新店太____了，完全没打招呼。
typical:0.hook: Just then the Manager walked in, smiling wide.
typical:0.line: It is so *typical* — he decides everything without asking us.

vacation:0.en: I asked the Manager when the new store would open. He laughed. 'Before your next *vacation*,' he said, which told me nothing since I had not had a single day off yet. He handed me a key and said the sign would go up on Saturday. I looked at the key for a long time.
vacation:0.cnHint: 店长说新店会在我下次____之前开业，但我还没休过假。
vacation:0.hook: The key was cold and heavier than it looked.
vacation:0.line: It will open before your next *vacation* — I promise.

acquire:0.en: The Manager called a meeting at the back table. 'To run a second store, we need to *acquire* two more night-shift clerks,' he announced, stirring his tea. Tang nodded. I raised my hand and asked what the new clerks would be paid. The Manager stirred his tea a little faster.
acquire:0.cnHint: 店长开会宣布，开新店需要____两名新的夜班店员。
acquire:0.hook: He looked at Tang, and Tang looked at the ceiling.
acquire:0.line: We need to *acquire* good people before the opening day.

adequate:0.en: Lin stopped by again, this time with a clipboard. She walked the aisles slowly, counting shelves. 'Your storage is not *adequate* for two locations,' she announced to no one in particular. The Manager crossed his arms. I noticed she had measured the back room before anyone had said she could.
adequate:0.cnHint: 林说我们的仓储空间不____，不足以支撑两家店的运营。
adequate:0.hook: She wrote something down and did not show us the page.
adequate:0.line: One small room is not *adequate* for your new operation.

attribute:0.en: The Manager pinned a new chart on the staff-room wall. 'Our best-selling items this month,' he said proudly. I studied the list and noticed the top spot belonged to warm meat buns. I could *attribute* that entirely to the cold snap last week — customers grabbed them the moment they walked in.
attribute:0.cnHint: 店长把本月销量第一____给了上周的寒潮。
attribute:0.hook: But the second item on the list made no sense at all.
attribute:0.line: I *attribute* every bun sale to that sudden cold snap.

badly:0.en: Tang knocked over a full shelf of bottled tea near the back fridge. Drinks rolled across the floor in every direction. She looked up at me with wide eyes. 'I *badly* need a break,' she whispered. I handed her a mop, then quietly picked up fifteen bottles before the Manager noticed anything.
badly:0.cnHint: 阿糖把一整排瓶装茶撞倒了，她说自己____需要休息。
badly:0.hook: What she said next was not about the tea at all.
badly:0.line: I *badly* need a five-minute break — just five.

bridge:0.en: Old Mr. Chen came in every night at eleven to buy a single can of coffee. Tonight he spread four playing cards on the drinks counter and asked if I knew *bridge*. I had never played. He smiled and said the store was the perfect place to learn, because nothing ever happened here.
bridge:0.cnHint: 老陈在饮料柜台摆出扑克牌，想教新店员玩____。
bridge:0.hook: Then the security camera beeped — someone was at the back door.
bridge:0.line: Let me teach you *bridge*; the night is still young.

casual:0.en: Lin strolled in wearing a loose jacket and trainers instead of her usual sharp uniform. The Manager blinked. 'Why so *casual* tonight?' he asked. She shrugged and said she was officially off duty, then slid a notebook onto the counter and began writing down our shelf prices one by one.
casual:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林穿着便装来店里，却悄悄把货架上的价格一一____记下来。
casual:0.hook: She smiled at me before leaving, and that smile felt like a warning.
casual:0.line: I am off duty, so *casual* clothes are perfectly fine.

closely:0.en: The Manager asked me to watch the new yoghurt display *closely* all evening. He would not say why. I stood near the fridge, pretending to restock cups. Around two in the morning I finally noticed: every time the door opened, three cartons shifted slightly by themselves. Cold air, I told myself. Probably cold air.
closely:0.cnHint: 店长让店员____盯着新的酸奶展示柜，深夜发现了奇怪的现象。
closely:0.hook: Then the cartons moved again — and the door was shut.
closely:0.line: Watch that fridge display *closely* until I get back.

commit:0.en: Tang told me the hardest thing about night shifts was staying honest when no one was watching. 'Anyone could pocket a snack and say nothing,' she said. She then slapped a sticky note on the register: DO NOT *COMMIT* SMALL CRIMES. I laughed, but she was absolutely serious, pointing at the note twice.
commit:0.cnHint: 阿糖在收银机上贴了一张便条，提醒大家不要____小错误。
commit:0.hook: An hour later the note had disappeared from the register.
commit:0.line: Do not *commit* even the smallest dishonest act here.

concentrate:0.en: The freezer alarm went off at midnight. I had to check every ice-cream bar, count them, and log the temperature — all while Tang called out numbers from the back. 'You have to *concentrate*,' she said sharply, 'or we recount the whole thing.' I nodded, clicked my pen, and started again from zero.
concentrate:0.cnHint: 冷柜警报响了，阿糖要求店员____清点冰淇淋并记录温度。
concentrate:0.hook: The final count was two bars short of the morning record.
concentrate:0.line: Please *concentrate* — one wrong number and we start over.

conscious:0.en: Around three in the morning I caught myself dozing against the crisp-snack shelf. I straightened up fast, suddenly very *conscious* of the security camera blinking red above me. Tang appeared from the stockroom and handed me a small cup of warm tea without a word. She had clearly seen everything on the monitor.
conscious:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点，店员突然____到监控摄像头正对着自己。
conscious:0.hook: Tang pointed at the monitor and mouthed a single silent word.
conscious:0.line: Stay *conscious* — the Manager checks the camera logs.

partly:0.en: The new branch store smelled of fresh paint. The Manager walked in and frowned. 'The shelves are *partly* filled,' he said, crossing his arms. 'We open in three hours.' I grabbed a box of snacks and started stacking as fast as I could, wondering who had left half the work undone.
partly:0.cnHint: 新分店的货架____摆好，店长皱起了眉头。
partly:0.hook: Then I noticed the missing stock list on the floor.
partly:0.line: 'The shelves are *partly* filled — we open in three hours.'

practical:0.en: Tang handed me a thick binder before my first shift at the branch. 'This is the *practical* guide the Manager made,' she said. 'Skip page one — that is just his photo.' I laughed, but by midnight I had read every other page twice. It was surprisingly useful.
practical:0.cnHint: 同事给我看了一本____指南，帮我快速上手新分店的工作。
practical:0.hook: Page twelve had a warning circled in red ink.
practical:0.line: 'Skip page one — the rest is a really *practical* guide.'

profit:0.en: The Manager taped a small chart above the register at the new branch. 'Last month we made zero *profit* here,' he told me quietly. 'This month must be different.' He tapped the chart twice, then walked out. I stared at the flat line and felt an unexpected pressure settle on my shoulders.
profit:0.cnHint: 店长指着图表说新分店上个月____为零，暗示压力很大。
profit:0.hook: A regular customer had been watching the whole conversation.
profit:0.line: 'Last month we made zero *profit* — this month must be different.'

promise:0.en: Lin stopped by the branch on her lunch break and leaned on the counter. 'I *promise* I am not here to spy,' she said with a grin that suggested the opposite. I offered her a free coffee anyway. She accepted, looked around slowly, and pulled out a small notebook before I could blink.
promise:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林来到新分店，____说自己不是来刺探情报的。
promise:0.hook: She wrote something down without letting me see the page.
promise:0.line: 'I *promise* I am not here to spy — just visiting.'

rarely:0.en: The branch sat on a quiet side street, and customers came in slowly. 'People *rarely* walk past here after nine,' Tang admitted, sweeping near the door. I watched the empty road and counted four cars in an hour. Still, just before midnight a group of students burst in, loud and hungry, filling every corner.
rarely:0.cnHint: 分店地处偏僻，顾客____光顾，但快到午夜时出现了意外的热闹。
rarely:0.hook: One of the students asked for something we did not stock.
rarely:0.line: 'People *rarely* walk past here after nine, so stay alert.'

severe:0.en: A small leak in the ceiling dripped onto a display stand overnight. By morning the damage looked *severe* — soaked boxes, ruined labels, and a puddle the size of a welcome mat. The Manager arrived, took one look, and was very quiet for a long moment. Quiet Manager was far scarier than loud Manager.
severe:0.cnHint: 分店天花板漏水，损失____，店长看后沉默不语。
severe:0.hook: He then made a single phone call and said nothing more.
severe:0.line: 'The damage looks *severe* — we need to fix this today.'

smell:0.en: I unlocked the branch at six in the morning and stopped at the door. A warm *smell* of sesame and soy drifted out — someone had clearly been cooking nearby. Tang appeared from the back room holding two paper cups of instant noodles. 'Best part of the early shift,' she announced, completely unbothered.
smell:0.cnHint: 早班时分店飘来食物的____，同事已经在后台悄悄煮好了面。
smell:0.hook: The Manager's car had just turned onto the street outside.
smell:0.line: 'That *smell* means Tang has already started the best part of the shift.'

socialize:0.en: The Manager decided the branch needed a soft-opening night so regulars could *socialize* and try free samples. Tang made a banner. I arranged the snacks. Lin arrived first, smiled too brightly, and began chatting with every single customer. By nine o'clock she knew more about our regulars than I did after a week.
socialize:0.cnHint: 新分店举办开业活动让顾客互相____，竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林却成了最活跃的那个人。
socialize:0.hook: She was still there when the last customer finally left.
socialize:0.line: 'Nights like this let everyone *socialize* — even rival clerks, apparently.'

dinner:0.en: The Manager called us into the back room after closing. A folding table was covered with rice boxes, soup, and fruit. 'The new branch opens next week,' he said, lifting his cup. 'Tonight we celebrate.' It felt less like a work meeting and more like a family *dinner*, warm and a little loud.
dinner:0.cnHint: 店长在关店后请大家吃饭，宣布新店下周开业，气氛热闹得像家庭聚会。
dinner:0.hook: Tang quietly slid a folded note across the table to me.
dinner:0.line: 'This *dinner* is my small way of saying thank you to all of you.'

embrace:0.en: When the Manager announced a second store, Tang looked nervous. 'Change is hard,' she whispered to me. But by the end of the meeting she was nodding along, and when he asked for volunteers, her hand went up first. Watching her *embrace* the new plan felt like seeing someone step into a warmer light.
embrace:0.cnHint: 唐起初对开新店感到不安，但最终决定____这个新计划，主动报名参与。
embrace:0.hook: Lin had been watching Tang's raised hand with a very strange smile.
embrace:0.line: 'I choose to *embrace* this change, even if it scares me a little.'

explanation:0.en: I arrived late to the planning meeting and every head turned. The Manager crossed his arms. I opened my mouth, ready with a long story about the bus and the rain, but he held up one hand. 'Save it,' he said. Tang later told me he never needed an *explanation* — only results.
explanation:0.cnHint: 我开会迟到，正准备给出____，店长却摆手说他只看结果。
explanation:0.hook: Yet the Manager slipped me a small map of the new store location on the way out.
explanation:0.line: 'I do not need an *explanation* — just show me you can handle the new branch.'

intend:0.en: Lin stopped by while I was restocking the shelves and leaned on the counter with a grin. 'I heard the Manager is picking someone to run the new store,' she said. I kept my eyes on the price tags. I had not said a word to anyone, but I *intended* to be that person.
intend:0.cnHint: 林告诉我新店需要一个负责人，而我心里早已____要争取那个位置。
intend:0.hook: Lin's grin suggested she intended exactly the same thing.
intend:0.line: 'I *intend* to be the one standing behind that new counter on opening day.'

leadership:0.en: The Manager pinned a small chart to the wall. Each staff member had a score — punctuality, sales, attitude. My name sat near the top, which surprised me. 'Running a branch needs *leadership*,' he said, tapping the chart. 'Numbers tell me who has it and who is still learning.' I swallowed hard.
leadership:0.cnHint: 店长把员工考核表贴上墙，说新店需要有____能力的人来主管。
leadership:0.hook: Tang's score was one point higher than mine.
leadership:0.line: 'Good *leadership* is not loud — it is the first one in and the last one out.'

locate:0.en: The Manager unrolled a city map across the checkout counter. He circled a spot two streets away with a red pen. 'We *located* the new store here,' he said, 'close enough to share supply runs, far enough to catch different customers.' I stared at the circle and felt my future sitting right inside it.
locate:0.cnHint: 店长在地图上指出新店____的位置，距原店仅两条街。
locate:0.hook: The circle sat directly across from Lin's family noodle shop.
locate:0.line: 'We *located* it there on purpose — foot traffic is highest on that corner.'

original:0.en: Tang pulled out a faded notebook during the break. 'This is the *original* plan the Manager drew when he opened this store,' she said, turning it toward me. The handwriting was small and careful, full of crossings-out and fresh starts. Seeing where everything began made the new branch feel less like an ending.
original:0.cnHint: 唐拿出店长当年的____创业笔记，里面满是修改痕迹，让人感慨万分。
original:0.hook: One page had a second location sketched in pencil — this exact street corner.
original:0.line: 'The *original* idea was always to have two stores — he never gave up on it.'

overcome:0.en: I had never run so much as a school club, and now the Manager was hinting I might lead the new branch. The doubt sat in my chest like a heavy box. Tang noticed my silence. 'Everyone feels this way at first,' she said quietly. 'The ones who stay are the ones who *overcome* it.'
overcome:0.cnHint: 面对可能要管理新店的压力，我感到不自信，唐鼓励我____内心的恐惧。
overcome:0.hook: Then her phone buzzed, and her expression shifted to something unreadable.
overcome:0.line: 'You will *overcome* this feeling — I have seen you handle worse at three in the morning.'

obvious:0.en: The Manager called a staff meeting at 2 a.m. to show us the plans for a second store. Tang was excited. I tried to look excited too. But it was *obvious* from the way the Manager kept glancing at the door that someone important was about to walk in — and none of us knew who.
obvious:0.cnHint: 店长深夜开会，展示新店计划，但他一直____地盯着门口。
obvious:0.hook: The door opened, and Tang's smile completely disappeared.
obvious:0.line: 'It's *obvious* you two haven't read the site plan,' the Manager said, spreading the map flat.

ordinary:0.en: Tonight felt like an *ordinary* shift — mop the floor, count the change, restock the cold drinks. Then Tang leaned over and whispered that the quiet man in the corner had been sitting with the same cup of tea for three hours, writing something in a very thick notebook.
ordinary:0.cnHint: 今晚看起来是____的一班，但角落里有个人已经坐了三个小时。
ordinary:0.hook: Tang said he came every night, but nobody knew his name.
ordinary:0.line: 'Don't let the *ordinary* night fool you,' Tang said, eyes on the notebook.

pace:0.en: The Manager began to *pace* the stockroom, measuring each step with care. He said he was planning the layout of the new branch. Tang counted seventeen laps before losing track. I just watched and wondered if the Manager ever slept at all.
pace:0.cnHint: 店长在库房里____，说是在规划新分店的格局。
pace:0.hook: On lap eighteen, he stopped and stared at a blank section of wall.
pace:0.line: 'I always *pace* when a big decision is coming,' the Manager said quietly.

participate:0.en: The Manager asked every staff member to *participate* in naming the new branch. Tang suggested something poetic. I wrote my idea on a small slip of paper and folded it twice. By morning there were eleven suggestions in the box — but one note had no name on it, just a drawing of a cat.
participate:0.cnHint: 店长邀请所有员工____新分店的命名活动，有人只留下了一幅猫的画。
participate:0.hook: Nobody admitted drawing the cat, but everyone was smiling.
participate:0.line: 'Everyone should *participate* — even you,' Tang said, handing me a pen.

pilot:0.en: A young man came in just before dawn and bought three energy drinks. He set them on the counter very carefully and said he was a *pilot* in training, and that his first solo flight was in four hours. His hands were steady, but his eyes were wide open like two full moons.
pilot:0.cnHint: 一个年轻的____学员在黎明前买了三罐功能饮料，说他四小时后要独自飞行。
pilot:0.hook: He left without his change, and I didn't call him back.
pilot:0.line: 'A *pilot* has to stay sharp all night sometimes,' he said with a tired grin.

primary:0.en: The Manager pinned a big chart to the stockroom wall. At the top, in red, were the words: new branch goals. He tapped the first line and said our *primary* job was not to sell more but to make every customer feel like a neighbour. Tang wrote that down. So did I.
primary:0.cnHint: 店长在图表上说，新分店的____目标不是多卖东西，而是让顾客感觉像邻居。
primary:0.hook: Later, Tang asked me if I actually believed that — I had no answer.
primary:0.line: 'Our *primary* goal is simple: make people feel welcome,' the Manager said.

priority:0.en: Lin arrived just as we were closing the planning meeting. She looked at our notes, crossed her arms, and said that speed of service should be the top *priority* for any new branch. The Manager nodded slowly. Tang nodded fast. I wrote it down and noticed Lin was already heading for the door.
priority:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林认为新分店最重要的____是服务速度，说完就走了。
priority:0.hook: She left a hand-drawn map on the counter — of a location we didn't recognise.
priority:0.line: 'Speed of service is the real *priority*,' Lin said without sitting down.

throughout:0.en: *Throughout* the long night, the Manager stayed at the back table, reworking the same floor plan again and again. Tang brought him two cups of tea. I brought him one rice ball. He thanked us each time without looking up, and by sunrise the plan had changed completely.
throughout:0.cnHint: ____整个漫长的夜晚，店长一直在修改新店的平面图。
throughout:0.hook: The final plan had a small room marked 'unknown use' — and nobody asked why.
throughout:0.line: 'I stay focused *throughout* the night when something matters,' the Manager said.

worldwide:0.en: The Manager spread a big paper map across the counter and pointed at tiny red dots. 'Each dot is a store in our chain,' he said proudly. I counted at least forty countries. The chain was *worldwide*, stretching from cold northern cities to warm southern islands. I had no idea I was working for something so large.
worldwide:0.cnHint: 店长展示了一张地图，说明连锁店的____规模，令新员工大吃一惊。
worldwide:0.hook: But why did the Manager's hand shake when he reached the last red dot?
worldwide:0.line: 'Our little chain is *worldwide* now — forty countries and still growing.'

accomplish:0.en: Tang made a careful list before every shift: restock the drinks, check the dates on the bread, clean the back shelf. By 3 a.m. she had crossed off every single item. 'If you write it down, you can *accomplish* anything,' she told me, sliding the finished list into her pocket with a small, satisfied smile.
accomplish:0.cnHint: 阿糖每班都列清单，并在凌晨前____了所有任务，令叙述者印象深刻。
accomplish:0.hook: The one item she never wrote down was the one that worried her most.
accomplish:0.line: 'Write it down first, then you can *accomplish* every single thing on the list.'

address:0.en: An old man came in just after midnight holding a torn piece of paper. He asked me to help him read the *address* written on it — the ink had blurred in the rain. We leaned together under the counter light, trying to make out the street name. He looked both hopeful and a little lost.
address:0.cnHint: 一位老人深夜拿着一张字迹模糊的纸条，请叙述者帮他辨认上面的____。
address:0.hook: The street on that paper had not existed for twenty years.
address:0.line: 'Young friend, can you read this *address* for me? The rain got to it first.'

barely:0.en: The new coffee machine arrived at 2 a.m., packed in a box almost as tall as me. Tang and I *barely* managed to lift it through the back door — my arms shook the whole time. We set it down on the counter and stood there breathing hard, very proud of ourselves for about ten seconds.
barely:0.cnHint: 新咖啡机太重，阿糖和叙述者____能把它搬进后门，两人累得直喘气。
barely:0.hook: When we finally plugged it in, every light in the store went dark.
barely:0.line: 'I could *barely* hold my end — next time we ask the Manager for help.'

blame:0.en: A bottle of juice rolled off the shelf and cracked open on the floor. Tang looked at me. I looked at Tang. The Manager walked in from the back room at exactly the wrong moment. We both started talking at once, each trying to take the *blame* before the other could. The Manager just handed us a mop, looking tired.
blame:0.cnHint: 果汁瓶摔碎后，阿糖和叙述者争着承担____，店长只是默默递来了拖把。
blame:0.hook: Later, the security camera showed neither of them had been anywhere near it.
blame:0.line: 'Please don't take the *blame* — it was already leaning before I even touched it.'

chat:0.en: Lin walked in from the store across the street at about 1 a.m., bought a single candy, and then leaned on the counter to *chat* for half an hour. She knew every regular by name and remembered their usual orders. By the time she left, I realised she had learned far more about our store than I had told her.
chat:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林买了颗糖，却在柜台旁____了半小时，悄悄摸清了很多情况。
chat:0.hook: She had also, very quietly, counted every item on our top shelf.
chat:0.line: 'I just came to *chat* — no business, I promise,' Lin said, smiling a little too sweetly.

combat:0.en: Tiny flies had found the fruit display. Tang arrived with a spray bottle, I arrived with a folded newspaper, and the Manager stood at the back giving instructions he was too cautious to follow himself. Our *combat* with the flies lasted a full twenty minutes. In the end the flies left on their own, completely unimpressed by us.
combat:0.cnHint: 小飞虫入侵水果区，三人展开了一场可笑的____，最后虫子自己飞走了。
combat:0.hook: The Manager's instructions, it turned out, were copied from a very old manual.
combat:0.line: 'This *combat* with fruit flies is now officially the hardest thing I have done all week.'

danger:0.en: Just before dawn, the freezer started making a deep, unhappy sound. Tang pressed her ear against it and looked serious. 'Real *danger*,' she said quietly, meaning all the ice cream inside. We called the Manager, who called a repair person, who arrived in twelve minutes looking half asleep but oddly cheerful.
danger:0.cnHint: 冰柜发出异响，阿糖判断冰淇淋面临真正的____，大家紧急联系了维修人员。
danger:0.hook: The repair person took one look inside and then asked for a chair and a moment to think.
danger:0.line: 'The ice cream is in real *danger* — call someone before we lose the whole shelf.'

conventional:0.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map on the counter. 'We are opening a second store,' he said proudly. I looked at the tiny square he had sketched two streets away. Nothing about his plan was *conventional* — the new shop would sell hot soup at midnight and rent umbrellas by the hour. I nodded slowly, wondering who exactly had agreed to this.
conventional:0.cnHint: 店长展示了他开新店的____计划，和普通便利店完全不同。
conventional:0.hook: The map had a second red square no one had explained yet.
conventional:0.line: 'Nothing here will be *conventional* — that is the whole point.'

disappear:0.en: The Manager taped a bold sign above the door: GRAND OPENING — BRANCH COMING SOON. By Tuesday, the sign had *disappeared*. Tang and I searched every corner of the store. We found it folded neatly under the register, which had been locked. Nobody admitted touching it, and the Manager just smiled at the ceiling.
disappear:0.cnHint: 店里的开业告示牌莫名____了，没有人承认动过它。
disappear:0.hook: The security camera above the door had been unplugged that night.
disappear:0.line: 'Signs do not just *disappear*, so someone here has some explaining to do.'

district:0.en: Tang pointed out that a rival shop had quietly opened in the same *district* last month, only four blocks away. The Manager crossed his arms and studied the delivery map on the wall. 'Good,' he said after a long pause. 'More people walking around means more people getting thirsty.' Tang and I exchanged a look.
district:0.cnHint: 同一____里出现了竞争对手的新店，但店长态度出人意料。
district:0.hook: Lin had been seen standing outside that rival shop twice this week.
district:0.line: 'Every store in this *district* knows our coffee is the best — let them try.'

greatly:0.en: The Manager returned from visiting the new branch site and was *greatly* pleased. He burst through the door, knocking over a tower of instant-noodle cups, and announced that the landlord had agreed to paint the walls our colour for free. Tang caught the falling cups without looking up. 'Colour does not make soup taste better,' she said quietly.
greatly:0.cnHint: 店长从新店选址回来后____地高兴，忍不住分享好消息。
greatly:0.hook: Tang had applied to manage that new branch six days ago and heard nothing.
greatly:0.line: 'I am *greatly* encouraged — this new branch will change everything for us.'

imitate:0.en: Lin stopped by just before midnight, hands in pockets, eyes moving slowly along our shelves. 'Research,' he called it. The Manager watched from behind the register. 'He wants to *imitate* our layout,' the Manager whispered to me, sounding more flattered than angry. Lin picked up a bag of peanuts, read the back, then set it down and left without buying anything.
imitate:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林来店里"参观"，店长认为他想____自家店的布局。
imitate:0.hook: The peanut bag Lin had handled was a new product not yet on the public list.
imitate:0.line: 'You can *imitate* our shelves all you like — you cannot copy our regulars.'

implement:0.en: The Manager produced a single chopstick from his apron pocket and held it up like a sacred *implement*. 'For the grand opening,' he announced, 'we will offer free hot pot broth — one ladle per customer.' Tang stared at the chopstick. I stared at the Manager. There was no pot, no broth, and no ladle anywhere in the store.
implement:0.cnHint: 店长拿出一根筷子作为开业仪式的____，却让同事们一头雾水。
implement:0.hook: A large cardboard box in the back room was taped shut and labelled 'DO NOT OPEN YET.'
implement:0.line: 'This small *implement* will be the symbol of our new branch — trust me on this.'

mood:0.en: By three in the morning the store felt very still. Tang was in a quiet *mood*, arranging the drinks fridge with unusual care. I asked if she was all right. She lined up four bottles perfectly before answering: 'I just want the new branch to be a good place.' She closed the fridge door gently and went back to her stool without another word.
mood:0.cnHint: 深夜里，阿糖____低落，却只用一句话说出了原因。
mood:0.hook: Her résumé for branch manager was still open on her phone screen.
mood:0.line: 'My *mood* tonight has nothing to do with the shelves — I just need to think.'

motivation:0.en: I asked the Manager why he wanted a second store at all. He looked at me as if the answer were printed on the ceiling. 'My *motivation*,' he said slowly, 'is that Mrs. Huang from the night bus told me she walks twenty minutes because we are the only store she trusts.' He folded the map carefully. 'Twenty minutes is too far for an old lady.'
motivation:0.cnHint: 店长说出了开分店的____，原来是因为一位老顾客走路太远。
motivation:0.hook: Mrs. Huang had not been in the store for eleven nights running.
motivation:0.line: 'My *motivation* has always been the same — make sure nobody has to walk too far.'

threaten:0.en: The Manager called a staff meeting at 2 a.m. inside the stockroom. He unrolled a map showing a new branch store opening two blocks away. 'That place will *threaten* our regulars,' he said, tapping the red circle hard. I looked at Tang. Tang looked at me. Nobody moved.
threaten:0.cnHint: 店长深夜召集员工开会，说对面新店会____我们的生意。
threaten:0.hook: Then someone knocked on the stockroom door from outside.
threaten:0.line: 'That new store will *threaten* everything we have built here.'

throw:0.en: Opening a second branch felt like a *throw* of dice on a cold night. The Manager stared at the sales chart pinned above the coffee machine, chewing his pen. I stacked cans quietly, pretending not to listen. Tang whispered that the Manager had lost sleep over this decision for two weeks.
throw:0.cnHint: 店长盯着销售图表，为开分店这个____感到忐忑不安。
throw:0.hook: At last the Manager circled one number and said nothing.
throw:0.line: 'Starting a new branch is always a *throw*, but I am ready.'

unlike:0.en: The new branch location was inside a bright shopping mall, *unlike* our quiet corner store, which sat between an old noodle shop and a sleeping cat. Lin visited to compare notes and stood at our door looking almost sad. 'Your place has a feeling,' she said. 'Theirs will just have light.'
unlike:0.cnHint: 新分店在商场里，和____我们这家温馨的转角小店。
unlike:0.hook: Lin left a folded note on the counter before walking away.
unlike:0.line: '*Unlike* that mall store, this place actually feels like home.'

vast:0.en: The Manager spread the new store plan across the front counter late at night. The floor space was *vast* compared to ours — three times the shelves, two drink stations, a whole wall of glass fridges. I felt small just reading the numbers. Tang said, quietly, 'So where do we fit in?'
vast:0.cnHint: 店长展开分店平面图，新店的空间____，是这里的三倍。
vast:0.hook: Tang's question hung in the air like cold steam.
vast:0.line: 'The floor plan is *vast* — we will need many more staff.'

absolutely:0.en: At midnight Lin walked in, cool as ever, and said she had *absolutely* no intention of letting our new branch steal her store's customers. She set a loyalty-card holder on our counter, smiled at me, and walked straight back out. Tang blinked. I picked up the card holder and turned it over.
absolutely:0.cnHint: 林走进来，说她____不会让我们的分店抢走她的顾客。
absolutely:0.hook: The loyalty cards inside were printed with our own store's address.
absolutely:0.line: 'I am *absolutely* certain your new branch will not beat us.'

accumulate:0.en: Every night I watched small coins *accumulate* in the glass jar beside the register — customers dropping in their change for the new-branch fund. By Thursday the jar was half full. The Manager never asked them to do it. I wrote the total in the logbook and felt something warm settle in my chest.
accumulate:0.cnHint: 每晚顾客的零钱慢慢在玻璃罐里____，成了分店的启动资金。
accumulate:0.hook: Friday night, a child dropped in a crumpled note instead of coins.
accumulate:0.line: 'We *accumulate* a little each night — it adds up faster than you think.'

breakfast:0.en: A regular named Mr. Old Cap always *breakfasted* at our corner store before the morning bus came. Boiled egg, small coffee, one red-bean bun — never different. When he heard about the new branch inside the mall, he set down his egg and said, 'Will you still have my bun there?' I said yes before I had any idea.
breakfast:0.cnHint: 常客老帽先生每天在店里____，得知要开分店后有些担心。
breakfast:0.hook: His next question was one I truly could not answer.
breakfast:0.line: 'I always *breakfast* here — please keep the red-bean buns at the new place.'

capacity:0.en: The Manager worried that our tiny stockroom lacked *capacity* for two stores' worth of orders. He stood inside it, arms out, turning slowly like a man measuring a dream. Boxes were piled to the ceiling already. Tang suggested renting the back half of the noodle shop next door. The Manager went very still.
capacity:0.cnHint: 店长担心仓库____不足，无法同时供应两家店的货物。
capacity:0.hook: The noodle-shop owner appeared in the doorway right at that moment.
capacity:0.line: 'Our stockroom has no *capacity* left — we must find another solution.'

consideration:0.en: The Manager spread a large map across the counter. 'Opening a second store needs careful *consideration*,' he said, tapping three neighbourhoods in turn. 'Rent, foot traffic, parking — every detail matters.' I nodded, pretending I understood business, while quietly hoping the new store would not be on my shift.
consideration:0.cnHint: 店长在柜台上摊开地图，认真地对开分店的各种____进行分析。
consideration:0.hook: He circled one neighbourhood twice, then looked straight at me.

disaster:0.en: Tang spilled an entire shelf of instant noodles trying to reach the top row. Cups rolled across every aisle. The Manager walked in at exactly that moment, stopped, and stared in silence. 'This,' he said at last, 'is a *disaster*.' Tang gave a small wave from behind a tower of fallen cups.
disaster:0.cnHint: 阿糖在整理货架时一不小心把东西全弄倒了，现场简直是一场____。
disaster:0.hook: Then the Manager pulled out his phone and started taking photos.
disaster:0.line: 'A *disaster* like this cannot happen at the new store.'

emergency:0.en: At two in the morning the fridge unit beeped and the temperature began to climb. I called the Manager, who arrived in slippers. 'This counts as an *emergency*,' he said, already dialling the repair service. We moved every dairy product into the back freezer while rain tapped quietly on the glass door.
emergency:0.cnHint: 深夜冰箱突然报警升温，店长赶来处理这场____。
emergency:0.hook: The repair worker arrived fast — almost too fast for a rainy night.
emergency:0.line: 'Treat every fridge alarm as an *emergency*, no exceptions.'

familiar:0.en: A woman in a yellow raincoat came in and walked straight to the back shelf without looking at the signs. She picked up her items, placed exact change on the counter, and left. 'She is a *familiar* face here,' Tang said. 'Comes every Thursday. Never once asked where anything is.'
familiar:0.cnHint: 一位常来的顾客对店里的一切都非常____，不需要任何指引。
familiar:0.hook: Tang added quietly, 'Nobody actually knows her name.'
familiar:0.line: 'Her face is *familiar* to every clerk who has worked here.'

furthermore:0.en: Lin from the store across the street visited during the afternoon lull. 'Your shelves are poorly labelled,' she said pleasantly. 'Your loyalty card design is outdated. *Furthermore*, your coffee machine is facing the wrong direction.' She smiled, bought a single mint, and left. I stared at the coffee machine for a long time.
furthermore:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林来店里，指出了好几个问题，而且____还提到了咖啡机的摆放。
furthermore:0.hook: The next morning, three things she mentioned had quietly been fixed.
furthermore:0.line: 'The layout is wrong, and *furthermore* the signage makes no sense.'

hardly:0.en: The Manager returned from visiting the new location looking pale. 'The space is smaller than the photos,' he said. 'I could *hardly* turn around in the stock room.' He sat on the step stool and stared at his notes. Tang offered him a warm can of soup, which he accepted without a word.
hardly:0.cnHint: 店长参观新店面后回来，说库房小得____能转身。
hardly:0.hook: He then circled 'stock room' on his notes and underlined it three times.
hardly:0.line: 'I could *hardly* fit two boxes side by side back there.'

hinder:0.en: The new shelving units arrived two hours before the morning rush. Boxes filled every gap between the aisles, and customers had to step sideways to reach the drinks. 'These boxes *hinder* everyone,' the Manager said, hands on hips. We moved them in four minutes flat, which felt like a personal record worth celebrating.
hinder:0.cnHint: 新货架送到后，纸箱堆满了过道，____了顾客通行。
hinder:0.hook: One customer had been standing perfectly still in aisle three the whole time.
hinder:0.line: 'Do not let anything *hinder* the customers from moving around freely.'

injury:0.en: Tang came in wearing a bandage on one hand. 'Box cutter,' he said simply, before anyone could ask. The Manager updated the staff notice board: 'Report every *injury*, however small.' Tang nodded, then used his good hand to restock the entire snack wall faster than I have ever managed with two.
injury:0.cnHint: 阿糖手受了____，店长随即在公告栏上更新了相关规定。
injury:0.hook: He had not, it turned out, filled in the required report form yet.
injury:0.line: 'Even a small *injury* must go on the report before end of shift.'

lift:0.en: The new branch store was on the third floor of a small building. The Manager led me up the stairs on the first day, pointing at a metal door on the wall. 'That is the *lift*,' he said, 'but we carry the stock boxes by hand to save power.' My arms ached before noon.
lift:0.cnHint: 店长带我参观新分店，指着墙上的____说搬货要靠手提。
lift:0.hook: Then I noticed the lift door had no button inside.
lift:0.line: 'We use the *lift* only when the boxes are too heavy to carry.'

mainly:0.en: The new branch was *mainly* stocked with snacks and drinks, unlike our corner store which carried everything from soap to notebooks. Tang walked the aisles with a clipboard, counting packets of chips and rows of bottled tea. 'Light goods sell fastest here,' she said, ticking her list with a quiet confidence.
mainly:0.cnHint: 新分店____摆放零食和饮料，唐正在逐一清点货架。
mainly:0.hook: One shelf at the back, though, held something completely unexpected.
mainly:0.line: 'This store is *mainly* for students who want a quick bite.'

moral:0.en: The Manager gathered the staff before opening day. He told us a short story about an honest shopkeeper who never cheated a customer, then paused. 'You understand the *moral*,' he said, looking at each of us in turn. Lin rolled his eyes just slightly, but said nothing. I filed the story away carefully.
moral:0.cnHint: 店长讲了个小故事，点明其中的____，林似乎不以为然。
moral:0.hook: Later, the same story appeared word for word on a sign above the register.
moral:0.line: 'The *moral* is simple: treat every customer the way you want to be treated.'

nor:0.en: On opening morning, neither the card reader *nor* the receipt printer worked. Tang tried unplugging and replugging both machines while a short line of curious customers watched. The Manager stayed calm, accepted cash only, and wrote each total on a small notepad. I admired how he never once looked flustered.
nor:0.cnHint: 开业当天收款机和打印机都出了故障，店长用纸笔记账。
nor:0.hook: The third customer in line paid with an unfamiliar coin.
nor:0.line: 'Neither the screen *nor* the sound is working — please pay cash.'

pick:0.en: Before the shelves were even labelled, the Manager told me to *pick* three items from the stockroom to feature near the door. I walked slowly between the boxes, thinking about what a tired student might want at midnight. I chose warm canned soup, a small hand warmer, and a notebook. He nodded once.
pick:0.cnHint: 店长让我从库房____三样商品摆在门口显眼处。
pick:0.hook: The notebook had someone else's name already written inside.
pick:0.line: 'Take your time and *pick* the item that feels right for this spot.'

pollution:0.en: A delivery driver arrived and mentioned the main road nearby was jammed because a city crew was cleaning up a chemical spill. 'Air *pollution* advisory is on,' he said, pulling his mask higher. Tang immediately closed the front vent and switched on the small indoor fan. The store suddenly felt very sealed and very quiet.
pollution:0.cnHint: 司机提到附近有____预警，唐立刻关上了通风口。
pollution:0.hook: A faint strange smell drifted in just before the vent clicked shut.
pollution:0.line: 'There is a *pollution* warning outside, so keep the door closed for now.'

quit:0.en: Lin arrived late on the second day, dropped his bag on the counter, and announced he might *quit* before the new branch even had its grand opening. The Manager poured him a cup of hot water without a word and set it down gently. Lin stared at it, then picked up his apron after a long pause.
quit:0.cnHint: 林说他可能会____，但店长递来一杯热水后他还是系上了围裙。
quit:0.hook: No one asked what had happened on his way to work.
quit:0.line: 'I nearly *quit* this morning, but here I am anyway.'

recall:0.en: Late in the evening I found an old photo tucked behind a shelf bracket — four smiling staff in uniforms I did not recognise. I brought it to the Manager, who held it under the light for a long moment. 'I *recall* this day,' he said softly. 'This was the first store, twenty years ago.'
recall:0.cnHint: 我发现一张旧照片，店长看着它____起了二十年前的往事。
recall:0.hook: One face in the photo looked remarkably like Lin.
recall:0.line: 'I *recall* every person who ever worked here on opening day.'

anyway:0.en: The stockroom smelled of cardboard and cold air. I had spent an hour trying to find the new shelf labels, with no luck. *Anyway*, I grabbed a marker and wrote the prices by hand. The Manager walked in, looked at my messy signs, and gave a slow nod of approval.
anyway:0.cnHint: 店员找不到货架标签，但____还是想办法完成了标价工作，店长看了点头认可。
anyway:0.hook: But the Manager's next words made my marker drop.
anyway:0.line: '*Anyway*, the job gets done — that is all I ask.'

arise:0.en: Setting up the new branch meant carrying boxes up a narrow back staircase all afternoon. Problems kept *arising* — a stuck door, a broken shelf, a missing power cable. Each time, Tang and I looked at each other, sighed, and found a fix. By closing time the little store almost looked ready.
arise:0.cnHint: 新分店筹备时麻烦不断____，店员和阿糖一起逐一解决。
arise:0.hook: Then Tang noticed the refrigerator had never been plugged in.
arise:0.line: 'New problems keep *arising*, but we handle them one by one.'

besides:0.en: The new branch was smaller than our main store. It had no back office, and the toilet was shared with the noodle shop next door. *Besides*, the Wi-Fi password written on the wall had three digits missing. I wrote everything down to tell the Manager, then wondered if the list would ever end.
besides:0.cnHint: 新分店条件简陋，____还有各种小问题，店员一一记录下来。
besides:0.hook: The last item on my list made even Tang go quiet.
besides:0.line: '*Besides*, nobody told us the alarm code for this place.'

certainly:0.en: Lin stopped by the new branch just before midnight, carrying two warm drinks from the rival shop down the road. 'I *certainly* did not expect you to open a second store so fast,' she said, setting a cup on the counter. There was a small smile on her face that I could not quite read.
certainly:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜来到新分店，说她____没料到我们这么快就开了分店。
certainly:0.hook: She left before I could ask what she really meant.
certainly:0.line: 'I *certainly* did not think you would beat us to this corner.'

challenging:0.en: The Manager gave me the opening shift at the new branch alone. Stocking shelves, learning the new register, and greeting the first customers all at once was *challenging*. My hands moved faster than my brain. A kind regular helped me find the bag roll when I could not. Small victories, I told myself.
challenging:0.cnHint: 店员独自负责新分店开业班次，任务很____，还好有热心顾客帮忙。
challenging:0.hook: Then the register printed a receipt in a language I did not know.
challenging:0.line: 'It is *challenging*, but I think I am starting to get it.'

circumstance:0.en: Under normal *circumstances*, the Manager would have hired extra staff before opening a new branch. But two people had cancelled last minute, and Tang had a fever. So there I was, alone behind a brand-new counter, with a line of curious customers already forming at the door.
circumstance:0.cnHint: 在正常____下不会只派一个人，但临时状况让店员独守新分店。
circumstance:0.hook: The very first customer asked a question I had no answer for.
circumstance:0.line: 'Under any *circumstance*, please call me if things get hard.'

comfort:0.en: Around two in the morning the new branch felt very far from the main store. The street outside was empty and the lights buzzed softly. Tang sent a voice message just to check on me. That small act of *comfort* was enough to make the humming shelves feel a little less lonely.
comfort:0.cnHint: 深夜新分店显得冷清，阿糖发来语音问候给了店员一丝____。
comfort:0.hook: The message ended with a warning I almost missed.
comfort:0.line: 'I hope this message gives you some *comfort* on that quiet street.'

enrich:0.en: The Manager said opening a second branch would *enrich* everyone's experience — new customers, new rhythms, new lessons. Standing at the unfamiliar counter, I was not sure I believed him yet. But by the end of the shift, I had learned three new things and met five interesting people. Maybe he had a point.
enrich:0.cnHint: 店长说开分店能____大家的经验，店员在忙碌一班后开始有点相信了。
enrich:0.hook: One of those five people slipped a note under the register.
enrich:0.line: 'Every new store will *enrich* us — trust me on that.'

register:0.en: The Manager spread a thick folder on the counter. 'Every new branch must *register* with the city office,' he said, tapping a long list of forms. I stared at the pile and wondered if the store itself felt tired. Tang handed me a pen without a word.
register:0.cnHint: 店长说每家新分店都必须去城市办公室____，然后把一大叠表格推给了我。
register:0.hook: The last form had a name on it no one recognised.
register:0.line: 'We have to *register* the branch before Friday or we lose the slot.'

skin:0.en: A woman came in just before midnight, rubbing lotion slowly onto her hands. 'Dry weather,' she said with a small smile. The light above the mirror made her *skin* look almost golden. She bought two bottles of hand cream and a hot lemon drink, then walked back into the dark street.
skin:0.cnHint: 一位深夜进店的女顾客一边揉搓双手，一边说天气干燥让她的____变得很粗糙。
skin:0.hook: She left one bottle behind, with a note tucked under it.
skin:0.line: 'Cold nights are terrible for your *skin*, trust me.'

spirit:0.en: Tang had worked three nights in a row, yet she still hummed while stacking shelves. 'How are you still so cheerful?' I asked. She laughed and said the store had a good *spirit*, like a small living thing that looked after everyone inside. I decided to believe her.
spirit:0.cnHint: 即使连上三个夜班，同事唐依然精力充沛，她说这家店有一种好的____在守护大家。
spirit:0.hook: Then the lights flickered once, as if in reply.
spirit:0.line: 'A place like this has its own *spirit*, you just have to feel it.'

spread:0.en: Word of the new branch traveled fast. By Tuesday morning, a hand-drawn map had *spread* across every noticeboard in the neighbourhood, marking our store with a cheerful star. Lin looked at one copy and said nothing, but her jaw was tight. The Manager whistled and put a copy in his pocket.
spread:0.cnHint: 新分店的消息很快____开来，街区里每块公告栏上都贴出了手绘地图。
spread:0.hook: Lin pulled the map down from the board nearest our door.
spread:0.line: 'Good news can *spread* faster than you ever plan for.'

totally:0.en: I tried to set up the new stock system on the back-room computer. After an hour I was *totally* lost, staring at a screen full of numbers that meant nothing to me. Tang leaned over my shoulder, pressed four keys, and everything sorted itself neatly. She walked away without explaining.
totally:0.cnHint: 我试图在后台电脑上设置新的库存系统，却____搞不清楚，还好同事唐出手相助。
totally:0.hook: The sorted list had one item that should not have been there.
totally:0.line: 'I was *totally* confused until Tang showed me the shortcut.'

tree:0.en: A tall pot plant stood just inside the new branch door, a gift from a neighbour. The Manager called it a lucky *tree* and refused to move it even when it blocked half the entrance. Customers had to turn sideways to get in. Most of them patted a leaf on the way past.
tree:0.cnHint: 新分店门口摆着一棵邻居送来的盆栽，店长坚持叫它幸运____，谁也不许挪动它。
tree:0.hook: One regular whispered something to the plant every single night.
tree:0.line: 'That *tree* stays by the door — it's good luck for the whole shop.'

weigh:0.en: The Manager stood at the back counter with two site plans, one in each hand. He asked Tang and me to help him *weigh* the decision: open the second till near the door or near the snack wall. We argued for twenty minutes. He had already made up his mind before we started.
weigh:0.cnHint: 店长拿着两份平面图请我们帮他____两个方案，但其实他早就心中有数了。
weigh:0.hook: The spot he chose had a loose floor tile underneath.
weigh:0.line: 'Help me *weigh* this — door side or snack side for the new till?'

alive:0.en: Late on opening night, the new branch finally felt *alive*. Every shelf was lit, the coffee machine hummed, and a small crowd had gathered outside the window just to look in. Lin passed by on the opposite side of the street, slowed down, and then kept walking without crossing over.
alive:0.cnHint: 开业当晚，新分店终于____了起来，但竞争对手林从对面街道走过却没有进来。
alive:0.hook: She stopped once, looked back, and dialled a number.
alive:0.line: 'The store is finally *alive* — look at all those people outside!'

facilitate:0.en: The Manager spread a big map across the counter. 'The new branch needs good foot traffic,' he said. He asked me to mark every bus stop and school nearby. 'These details *facilitate* the final decision,' he told Tang, tapping the map with one finger. Tang nodded and reached for a pen.
facilitate:0.cnHint: 店长让我们在地图上标记公交站和学校，以____开新店选址的决策。
facilitate:0.hook: But Lin from the corner shop had been watching through the window the whole time.
facilitate:0.line: 'These details *facilitate* the final decision,' the Manager said, tapping the map.

insight:0.en: Tang had worked here for three years. Late one night, she looked up at the new-branch plans pinned above the coffee machine. 'You need *insight* into what people actually buy at 3 a.m.,' she said quietly. I started taking notes. Her words felt like someone turning on a small, warm light.
insight:0.cnHint: 唐告诉我，对新店选址真正有帮助的是对深夜顾客购买习惯的____。
insight:0.hook: Then she mentioned one regular customer whose order had never changed — not once in three years.
insight:0.line: 'You need *insight* into what people actually buy at 3 a.m.,' Tang said quietly.

preparation:0.en: The night before the Manager's big meeting with the landlord, Tang and I stayed late. We printed sales charts, sorted receipts, and brewed fresh coffee for the morning. 'Good *preparation* makes the Manager look calm even when he isn't,' Tang whispered. She was right. He walked in looking like he owned the street.
preparation:0.cnHint: 为了帮店长顺利谈下新店，我们连夜做了充分的____。
preparation:0.hook: What we did not know was that Lin had booked a meeting with the same landlord one hour earlier.
preparation:0.line: 'Good *preparation* makes the Manager look calm even when he isn't,' Tang whispered.

separate:0.en: The Manager came back from the property office with two folders. 'I am keeping the new branch plan *separate* from the current store's budget,' he said, setting each folder on a different shelf. He looked pleased. Tang caught my eye and mouthed the word 'serious.' I began to think this was really going to happen.
separate:0.cnHint: 店长把新店计划和现店预算____放在了两个不同的文件夹里。
separate:0.hook: One folder had a sticky note on it that I was not supposed to read — but I already had.
separate:0.line: 'I am keeping the new branch plan *separate* from the current store's budget,' he said.

tie:0.en: A man in a neat grey *tie* came in just after midnight, bought a bottle of water, and asked if our store had a second location. I said not yet. He nodded slowly, left a business card on the counter, and walked out without another word. Tang picked up the card and raised an eyebrow.
tie:0.cnHint: 一个打着____的男人深夜来买水，顺口问了一句我们有没有分店。
tie:0.hook: The name on the card matched the landlord the Manager had been trying to reach all week.
tie:0.line: 'Does this shop have a second location?' the man in the grey *tie* asked softly.

jam:0.en: Saturday morning hit us like a wall. A burst pipe down the road sent everyone inside at once. The small back office, where the Manager was making calls about the new lease, turned into a total *jam* of boxes, umbrellas, and wet coats. He kept talking, completely unbothered, one hand holding the phone and the other moving a stack of noodle cups.
jam:0.cnHint: 周末早高峰顾客突然涌入，店里后间陷入一片____，但店长还在淡定地打电话谈新店租约。
jam:0.hook: The person on the other end of that call had just named a price nobody expected.
jam:0.line: 'It is a complete *jam* back here, but the lease talk is going well!' the Manager called out.

supermarket:0.en: Lin stopped in during the afternoon rush, wearing a polite smile. 'A big *supermarket* chain is looking at the empty lot across from your new site,' she said to no one in particular, then bought a pack of gum and left. The Manager set down his coffee. Tang and I looked at each other. The room felt a little smaller.
supermarket:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林来店里，随口提到新店选址对面的空地引来了大型____的注意。
supermarket:0.hook: The Manager's next phone call lasted forty-seven minutes and he never once sat down.
supermarket:0.line: 'A big *supermarket* chain is already looking at that lot,' Lin said, still smiling.

debate:0.en: Just before closing, the Manager, Tang, and I sat around the counter with cold tea. Should the new branch open at the end of the month or wait until spring? The *debate* went in circles for a while — costs, weather, school terms. Then a regular shuffled in, bought warm soy milk, and said, 'Whatever you decide, I hope it has better parking.'
debate:0.cnHint: 我们三人围坐在柜台边，就新店开业时间展开了一番____，却被一位常客的话逗笑了。
debate:0.hook: That regular turned out to be the exact customer the Manager had been trying to survey for months.
debate:0.line: 'Let the *debate* end here — spring is simply too late,' the Manager said, standing up.

egg:0.en: The Manager called me into the back room and pointed at a tray of cracked *eggs* on the shelf. 'Someone knocked these over last night,' he said, frowning. 'We lost twelve.' I looked at the sticky mess and quietly wondered if the night shift was going to be harder than I thought.
egg:0.cnHint: 店长发现货架上一盘碎____，追问是谁的失误。
egg:0.hook: But the security camera had been turned off that night.
egg:0.line: 'Twelve *eggs* gone, and nobody saw a thing — how?'

hire:0.en: The Manager slid a short form across the counter. 'Sign here,' he said. 'You are the first person I have decided to *hire* in two years.' I picked up the pen, feeling both proud and a little nervous. Outside, the street lamp flickered once, as if marking the moment.
hire:0.cnHint: 店长递来合同，正式____了我做夜班店员。
hire:0.hook: Tang, watching from the stockroom door, did not look pleased.
hire:0.line: 'I do not *hire* easily, so do not make me regret this.'

aid:0.en: An old man knocked on the glass door just after midnight, holding his arm and looking pale. I ran out at once. My first-*aid* training kicked in — nothing serious, just a small cut — but my hands were shaking the whole time. He thanked me softly and walked away into the dark.
aid:0.cnHint: 一位老人深夜受了轻伤，我用____知识帮他处理伤口。
aid:0.hook: He left behind a folded note I did not notice until morning.
aid:0.line: 'Your first-*aid* skills just saved me a trip to the hospital.'

bill:0.en: A woman in a long coat bought three bottles of water and handed me a large *bill*. When I opened the register, I realised we had almost no change left. She watched me count every coin on the counter with a calm, slightly amused smile that made me feel very new at this job.
bill:0.cnHint: 一位女顾客付了一张大____，收银台里零钱几乎见底。
bill:0.hook: She came back ten minutes later, asking for something else entirely.
bill:0.line: 'Keep the change — just put it toward tomorrow's *bill*.'

paint:0.en: Tang climbed a small ladder near the entrance and began to *paint* the wall behind the snack shelf a soft yellow. 'Manager's idea,' he said without looking down. 'Makes the store feel warmer.' The smell mixed with instant noodles in a way that was strange but oddly pleasant.
paint:0.cnHint: 阿糖爬上梯子，按店长要求____零食架后面的墙。
paint:0.hook: Lin walked in just then and stared at the colour for a long time.
paint:0.line: 'I *paint* walls, restock shelves, and fix lights — what do you do?'

bean:0.en: Lin arrived carrying a small pot and set it on the staff table without a word. Inside were soft, sweet red *beans* she had cooked herself. 'For everyone,' she said, already turning to leave. Tang and I looked at each other. We had assumed she disliked us both.
bean:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一锅自己煮的红____，悄悄放在员工桌上。
bean:0.hook: There was no spoon, as if she hoped we would not actually eat it.
bean:0.line: 'One red *bean* dessert, made from scratch — do not waste it.'

birthday:0.en: I found a small cake box tucked behind the register with a sticky note that read 'Do not touch.' Tang leaned over and whispered that today was the Manager's *birthday*, and that every year the same customer brought a cake before dawn. Neither of us had ever seen who it was.
birthday:0.cnHint: 收银台后藏着一个蛋糕，原来今天是店长的____。
birthday:0.hook: The box was gone by six, and the Manager never said a word.
birthday:0.line: 'Happy *birthday*, Manager — someone out there still remembers you.'

flight:0.en: A young man burst through the door at two in the morning, breathing hard. He needed a phone charger — his *flight* left in three hours and his ride had just cancelled. I found a spare cable behind the counter. He sat on the floor by the plug socket, eyes fixed on the door.
flight:0.cnHint: 一个年轻人深夜冲进来，他的____还有三小时就要起飞了。
flight:0.hook: He got his ride, but left his passport on the floor.
flight:0.line: 'My *flight* is at five — please tell me that charger works fast.'

housing:0.en: The Manager spread a big map on the counter and pointed to a empty lot two streets away. 'The *housing* above the new store will be for staff,' he said proudly. I looked at the tiny square on the map and wondered if Tang had already claimed the best room.
housing:0.cnHint: 店长在柜台上摊开地图，指着附近空地，兴奋地介绍新店楼上的____计划。
housing:0.hook: Tang was already measuring the upstairs windows with a smile.
housing:0.line: The *housing* above the new store will be ready before winter.

behaviour:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and stood very still near the door, watching me restock the shelves. The Manager had warned me about Lin's *behaviour* — always observing, never buying, taking mental notes. I smiled and offered a free sample. Lin blinked, then smiled back.
behaviour:0.cnHint: 林常常悄悄进店观察，店长曾提醒我注意他的____。
behaviour:0.hook: Lin left a folded note under the sample tray.
behaviour:0.line: I have noticed some strange *behaviour* in this store lately.

husband:0.en: A woman came in at two in the morning looking for instant soup. 'My *husband* is sick,' she said softly, 'and this is the only thing he will eat.' I found the last packet on the top shelf and handed it over without charging her. She looked surprised, then grateful.
husband:0.cnHint: 一位女士深夜进店，说她____病了，只想找一包方便汤。
husband:0.hook: She came back the next night — but alone this time.
husband:0.line: My *husband* says your store is the kindest on the street.

tourist:0.en: A *tourist* pushed open the door, rolling a large bag across the floor and speaking very fast in a language I did not know. He pointed at the window, then at the street, then at his phone. I guessed he needed directions. Tang drew a small map on a receipt and the man laughed with relief.
tourist:0.cnHint: 一位____拖着行李箱冲进店里，似乎完全迷路了。
tourist:0.hook: The receipt map later appeared on a travel blog with five stars.
tourist:0.line: Every *tourist* I meet ends up in this store somehow.

agent:0.en: A man in a neat grey jacket came in and asked if the Manager was free. He said he was an *agent* looking to open a second store nearby and wanted advice. The Manager turned pale, then red, then smiled in a way I had never seen before — too wide, too careful.
agent:0.cnHint: 一个自称____的人走进来，说想在附近开第二家店。
agent:0.hook: The manager locked himself in the back room for an hour.
agent:0.line: I am an *agent* for a group that is very interested in this corner.

cash:0.en: Just before dawn, a boy of about ten slid a handful of coins across the counter for a rice ball. He was a few coins short. I glanced at the empty store and quietly covered the rest from my own pocket. He counted his *cash* twice, looked confused, then just said thank you and ran.
cash:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩拿着零散的____来买饭团，但钱不够。
cash:0.hook: The next morning, the exact amount appeared in an envelope by the door.
cash:0.line: I only have this much *cash*, but I really want the big one.

competition:0.en: Lin slid a flyer across the counter without saying a word. It announced a new convenience store opening on the very next block. The Manager looked at it for a long moment. 'Good,' he said at last. 'A little *competition* keeps us sharp.' He then immediately called Tang to redesign the front window.
competition:0.cnHint: 林送来一张传单，宣布附近将出现新的____对手，店长的反应出人意料。
competition:0.hook: By morning, the Manager had already ordered twice as many snacks.
competition:0.line: A bit of *competition* is the best thing that could happen to us.

farmer:0.en: An old man came in every Thursday just after midnight for a single carton of milk. Tang told me he was a *farmer* who drove three hours to sell vegetables at the early market. He always smelled of fresh earth and always paid with exact change. Tonight, he also left a small bag of tomatoes on the counter.
farmer:0.cnHint: 每周四深夜都有一位____开车进城，顺路来买牛奶。
farmer:0.hook: Next Thursday, the tomatoes were already gone — and Tang was grinning.
farmer:0.line: A *farmer* gets thirsty too, you know, especially before sunrise.

collection:0.en: The Manager spent the slow hours arranging a *collection* of small ceramic cats on the shelf above the register. Each one came from a different city, he said. I counted seventeen. He straightened the last one with great care, then glanced at the door as if expecting someone specific to walk in.
collection:0.cnHint: 店长把他的____摆在收银台上方，每一个都来自不同城市。
collection:0.hook: Who was he expecting to see them?
collection:0.line: 'This *collection* took me ten years to build, one city at a time.'

depression:0.en: A young woman sat on the step outside, so Tang brought her a warm can of corn soup without being asked. She had the quiet look of someone carrying a *depression* she could not name. Tang just sat beside her for a minute, saying nothing. She finished the soup and stood up a little straighter.
depression:0.cnHint: 唐注意到那位年轻女士神情中有一种____，于是默默递给她一罐热汤。
depression:0.hook: She left a folded note under the empty can.
depression:0.line: 'A little warmth helps when *depression* makes the night feel too long.'

foot:0.en: The new stockroom was only one *foot* wider than the old one, but the Manager treated it like a palace. He drew a careful map of where every box should go and taped it to the wall. I followed the map perfectly on my first try. He looked almost disappointed that I had nothing to complain about.
foot:0.cnHint: 新库房只比旧的宽一____，但店长却像对待宝地一样认真规划。
foot:0.hook: The map had one room marked with a question mark.
foot:0.line: 'One *foot* of extra space — and I have big plans for it.'

graduate:0.en: A tired-looking *graduate* in a wrinkled shirt came in just before dawn and bought three energy drinks and a sandwich. He said his final paper was due in four hours. Tang quietly added a free chocolate bar to his bag. The young man did not notice until he was already out the door.
graduate:0.cnHint: 一位疲惫的____在天亮前买了能量饮料，唐偷偷在他包里加了一块巧克力。
graduate:0.hook: He came back the next night with a small gift.
graduate:0.line: 'Being a *graduate* student means living on very little sleep.'

intake:0.en: The Manager taped a small chart to the fridge door tracking the daily *intake* of hot drinks sold per hour. He called it data. Tang called it obsession. I called it quietly useful when the 2 a.m. rush for hot tea hit and I already had the water boiling. The Manager noticed and said nothing, but he smiled.
intake:0.cnHint: 店长在冰箱门上贴了一张追踪热饮____的图表，这让我在凌晨高峰时提前做好了准备。
intake:0.hook: Tang crossed out one number and wrote a different one.
intake:0.line: 'Watch the *intake* chart — it tells you when the rush is coming.'

screen:0.en: Lin walked in and set up a small folding *screen* on the counter to block the draught from the door while she did paperwork. She worked here before me, apparently. She still knows where every spare key is kept. She finished, folded the screen under her arm, and left without buying anything.
screen:0.cnHint: 林走进来，用一扇小____挡住风口，然后若无其事地处理文件，仿佛这里仍是她的地方。
screen:0.hook: Her name was still on the staff locker.
screen:0.line: 'I put this *screen* here two years ago — glad it is still useful.'

chair:0.en: Someone left a wooden *chair* in the back corner of the store with a note taped to it reading 'for whoever needs to sit down.' The Manager said it had appeared one Tuesday and no one knew who brought it. Three regulars had already claimed it as their own favourite seat. Tonight all three arrived at the same time.
chair:0.cnHint: 店里角落里出现了一把来历不明的____，三位常客都认为那是自己的专属座位。
chair:0.hook: All three sat down at once and somehow fit.
chair:0.line: 'That *chair* has heard more stories than the rest of the store.'

court:0.en: The Manager warned me never to *court* trouble by telling Lin which new snacks were selling well. Apparently she once worked here, left to open a rival shop, and now drops by to compare notes. I nodded seriously. Then Lin walked in, bought the new spicy chips, and asked how many bags we had left. I said I had no idea.
court:0.cnHint: 店长警告我不要____麻烦，把销售情报透露给竞争对手林。
court:0.hook: Lin smiled as if she already knew the number.
court:0.line: 'Don't *court* trouble — Lin is very good at reading faces.'

burn:0.en: The back kitchen of the new branch store was still being fitted out. I watched the Manager test the coffee machine for the first time. Steam shot sideways and left a red *burn* across his wrist. He looked at it calmly, then adjusted the nozzle without a word.
burn:0.cnHint: 店长在测试咖啡机时，手腕上留下了一道____。
burn:0.hook: He had done this before — but how many times?
burn:0.line: 'A small *burn* means the machine is finally alive.'

cook:0.en: Tang arrived early on opening day carrying a rice cooker from home. 'The staff room has no microwave yet,' she said. She began to *cook* a pot of congee for everyone before the first customer walked in. The whole store smelled warm and soft.
cook:0.cnHint: 阿糖在新店开业前用自带的电饭锅为大家____了粥。
cook:0.hook: Tang had never mentioned she once trained as a chef.
cook:0.line: 'I always *cook* when I am nervous — it helps.'

corporate:0.en: A man in a stiff suit came in and photographed every shelf and price tag. He did not buy anything. The Manager told me quietly that he was from the *corporate* office, checking whether our new branch followed every rule in the company handbook.
corporate:0.cnHint: 一位____总部的检查员悄悄来到新店巡查。
corporate:0.hook: The man paused longest at the shelf Lin had just restocked.
corporate:0.line: 'The *corporate* team never visits unless something is wrong.'

dangerous:0.en: Lin dared me to carry six fully loaded stock boxes up the narrow back stairs alone on my first day at the new branch. 'It is not that hard,' she said, smiling. The Manager appeared at the top of the stairs. 'That is *dangerous*,' he said flatly. 'Two trips.'
dangerous:0.cnHint: 店长警告我，一次搬太多箱子上楼梯是____的。
dangerous:0.hook: Lin's smile stayed just a little too long after he left.
dangerous:0.line: 'One wrong step on those stairs is *dangerous*, trust me.'

debt:0.en: Over a slow midnight hour the Manager told me why he had pushed so hard to open this second branch. Years ago a fire had destroyed his first small shop and left him deep in *debt*. Every new store was, in his words, 'one step back toward the surface.'
debt:0.cnHint: 店长透露，他开新店的动力来自多年前欠下的____。
debt:0.hook: He stopped talking when a certain regular walked through the door.
debt:0.line: 'I will not rest until every last *debt* is cleared.'

discipline:0.en: The Manager pinned a one-page rule sheet by the new branch door before we opened. Tang read it and raised an eyebrow. 'He believes *discipline* is the only reason any small shop survives past its first year,' she told me, keeping her voice low and even.
discipline:0.cnHint: 店长相信____是小店能撑过第一年的唯一原因。
discipline:0.hook: Tang then folded her copy of the sheet very neatly and pocketed it.
discipline:0.line: '*Discipline* is not punishment — it is just daily care.'

error:0.en: I was entering the new branch's opening stock into the system when I found a count that did not match. Tang leaned over and tapped the screen. 'Classic input *error*,' she said. 'Fix it now, before the Manager runs the morning report.' I fixed it in thirty seconds.
error:0.cnHint: 我在录入新店库存时发现了一处数据____。
error:0.hook: The number I corrected matched an order only Lin had handled.
error:0.line: 'One small *error* in stock data can ruin a whole week.'

gym:0.en: A regular who came in every night at eleven always bought a protein drink and two boiled eggs. Tang told me he rented the *gym* on the third floor of the building across the lane and trained alone after midnight when the equipment was free and the place was quiet.
gym:0.cnHint: 那位常客每晚买蛋白饮料，因为他在附近的____锻炼。
gym:0.hook: Last Tuesday the gym lights stayed dark, and he still came in.
gym:0.line: 'The *gym* closes early tonight, so I finished my run outside.'

salary:0.en: The Manager called me into the back office after my first week. He slid a printed sheet across the desk. 'Your *salary* starts low,' he said, 'but we review it every three months.' I nodded, trying to look calm. Outside, the freezer hummed like it was listening.
salary:0.cnHint: 店长把我叫进办公室，谈到了我的____。
salary:0.hook: He then added one quiet condition I had not expected.
salary:0.line: 'Your *salary* is small now, but prove yourself and that changes.'

shopping:0.en: A woman dragged two heavy bags through the door just before midnight. She set them down with a long sigh. 'Finished my *shopping* at the big market,' she said, 'but the night bus left without me.' I handed her a warm drink. She had kind eyes and a familiar face.
shopping:0.cnHint: 一位女士深夜____归来，错过了末班车。
shopping:0.hook: She glanced at the shelf and went very still.
shopping:0.line: 'I do all my *shopping* late — the crowds are gone by then.'

tendency:0.en: Tang warned me about one regular on my first shift. 'He has a *tendency* to stand by the magazine rack for an hour without buying anything,' Tang said, refilling the coffee machine. 'Just smile and let him be.' Sure enough, at two in the morning, a thin man in a coat arrived.
tendency:0.cnHint: 同事提醒我，某位常客有一个奇怪的____。
tendency:0.hook: Tonight, however, the man walked straight to the counter.
tendency:0.line: 'He has a *tendency* to leave right before dawn — never fails.'

tough:0.en: The overnight restock was *tough* work. Every box seemed heavier than the last, and the storage room was freezing. Tang showed me the proper way to stack without hurting my back. By four in the morning my hands were stiff but the shelves looked perfect. Tang gave a small approving nod.
tough:0.cnHint: 深夜补货是____的工作，同事教我怎么正确搬箱子。
tough:0.hook: Then the delivery driver knocked — with twice as many boxes.
tough:0.line: 'It is *tough* at first, but your body gets used to it fast.'

tour:0.en: A young man with a large backpack stepped in just after three. He spread a paper map on the counter. 'I am on a *tour* of the city,' he said, 'and I have completely lost track of where I am.' I pointed to our street on the map. He laughed with relief.
tour:0.cnHint: 一个背包客正在____途中，进来问路。
tour:0.hook: He asked if he could leave one envelope here for a friend.
tour:0.line: 'My *tour* ends tomorrow, but tonight I am beautifully lost.'

wake:0.en: The store felt unusually still at five in the morning. Then the door swung open and a group of quiet adults walked in, buying candles and soft drinks. One woman told me they had come from a family *wake* down the street. I kept my voice low as I gave them their change.
wake:0.cnHint: 一群人从附近的____赶来，买了蜡烛和饮料。
wake:0.hook: The last one to leave paused and looked back at me.
wake:0.line: 'We held the *wake* all night — he would have wanted that.'

annual:0.en: Lin appeared at the counter with a folder full of papers. 'Our *annual* report is due tomorrow,' she said through gritted teeth, 'and the printer at the other store just broke.' I let her use the small office printer in the back. She looked genuinely surprised that I helped without asking why.
annual:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林拿着文件跑来，说____报告明天就要交了。
annual:0.hook: She left one page behind — and it had our store name on it.
annual:0.line: 'The *annual* meeting is tomorrow and I am not ready at all.'

charity:0.en: A teenager emptied her pockets on the counter — coins, a crumpled note, a bus pass. She was trying to buy a meal box but came up short. Before I could think, the man behind her placed the right amount down quietly. 'Call it *charity*,' he said, and walked out into the dark.
charity:0.cnHint: 一位好心的陌生人为差钱的女孩付款，说这是____。
charity:0.hook: The girl stared at the door and whispered one short question.
charity:0.line: 'Call it *charity* if you like — I just hate seeing people hungry.'

female:0.en: Just after midnight, a small cat pushed through the door and sat by the drinks fridge. Tang looked up from the mop. 'She comes every night,' he said. The Manager nodded. 'She's a *female* — had kittens in the stock room last spring. We let her stay.' I looked at the fridge. A tiny paw print was on the glass.
female:0.cnHint: 一只____动物每晚都会来店里，店长说这里曾是它生育的地方。
female:0.hook: But where were the kittens now?
female:0.line: 'She's a *female* who raised her kittens right here in this store.'

holiday:0.en: The store was bright with paper lanterns Tang had hung near the counter. 'It's a *holiday* tomorrow,' he told me, 'so we'll be busy until dawn.' The Manager had already doubled the hot drink supply. By ten at night, every student in the street seemed to want warm milk and dumplings. I had not expected this.
holiday:0.cnHint: 因为明天是____，同事提醒我今晚会非常忙碌。
holiday:0.hook: Then Lin walked in, carrying something none of us had ordered.
holiday:0.line: 'It's a *holiday* tomorrow, so please stock the hot drinks now.'

pain:0.en: Lin from the shop around the corner came in rubbing her wrist. 'Moving boxes all day,' she said with a tired smile. I found the small first-aid box the Manager keeps under the counter. 'It's no *pain* worth ignoring,' Tang said, passing her a cold pack. She laughed softly and stayed for tea. I liked her immediately.
pain:0.cnHint: 竞争对手来店里时手腕受伤了，同事提醒说不能忽视这种____。
pain:0.hook: She left a note under the tea cup before she walked out.
pain:0.line: 'It's no *pain* worth ignoring — please use this cold pack.'

player:0.en: A young man in a sports shirt came in just before two in the morning, still wearing a numbered vest. He loaded his arms with juice and rice balls. 'Big match tomorrow,' he said. Tang grinned. 'Every *player* on the team stops here before a game.' The Manager had kept a bag behind the counter with the boy's name on it.
player:0.cnHint: 一位____赛前来店里购物，店长早已替他备好了东西。
player:0.hook: The name on the bag belonged to someone quite unexpected.
player:0.line: 'Every *player* on our team buys juice here before a big game.'

production:0.en: The Manager spread a floor plan across the counter. A second store, two streets away. 'I want to increase *production* in the kitchen area,' she said, tapping a square room on the paper. Tang and I leaned in. Fresh sandwiches, hot soup, real coffee. She looked at us both. 'I need people I trust to run it at night.' My heart beat faster.
production:0.cnHint: 店长展示新分店的平面图，希望提升厨房区域的____能力。
production:0.hook: She had already written one of our names on the plan.
production:0.line: 'I want to increase *production* in the new kitchen by three times.'

secure:0.en: The Manager showed me the back room where the safe sat behind a steel door. 'Keep this area *secure* at all times,' she said, handing me a key card. 'The new store will have the same system.' Tang nodded from the doorway. 'It sounds simple,' he said, 'until the system fails at three in the morning.' They both looked at me.
secure:0.cnHint: 店长交给我一张门卡，要求我确保这个区域时刻____。
secure:0.hook: The system had already failed once, and nobody had told me.
secure:0.line: 'Keep this area *secure* at all times — here is your key card.'

audience:0.en: The Manager called a small meeting. Tang, Lin from next door, and I sat on drink crates. 'You are my *audience* for this one time only,' she said, unrolling a large map of the new store layout. 'After tonight, you each have a job to do.' Lin raised an eyebrow. I noticed she had been invited before any of us had thought to ask her.
audience:0.cnHint: 店长召集大家开会，说我们是这次计划唯一的____。
audience:0.hook: Lin already knew things about the new store that the Manager had not yet said.
audience:0.line: 'You are my *audience* for this plan — please listen very carefully.'

borrow:0.en: I was short one key card on my first night at the new counter. Tang offered his. 'You can *borrow* it until morning,' he said, 'but do not lose it — the Manager charges replacement fees that will ruin your week.' I promised to be careful. At six in the morning I reached into my pocket and found two cards instead of one.
borrow:0.cnHint: 我的门卡不够用，同事让我____他的，但提醒我不要弄丢。
borrow:0.hook: The second card had a name on it that was not Tang's.
borrow:0.line: 'You can *borrow* my card until morning, but please do not lose it.'

mile:0.en: The Manager spread a city map across the counter and circled two spots with a red pen. 'The new branch will be exactly one *mile* from here,' he said, tracing the road with his finger. I leaned over and studied the gap between the circles, wondering what stood there now.
mile:0.cnHint: 店长在地图上比划，新分店距这里恰好一____。
mile:0.hook: Something about that empty block made the Manager go quiet.
mile:0.line: 'It is exactly one *mile* away — close enough to share our best customers.'
