movement:0.en: Late at night the store felt still, but I soon noticed every small *movement* — a shadow crossing the window, a can shifting on its shelf, Tang restocking quietly in the back. The Manager said a second store meant twice the eyes and twice the ears. I was beginning to understand what he meant.
movement:0.cnHint: 深夜的店里，每一个细微的____都逃不过新人的眼睛。
movement:0.hook: One shadow crossed the window twice without coming in.
movement:0.line: 'Watch every *movement* near the door — that tells you who really needs help.'

party:0.en: A group of six came in just after midnight, still wearing paper hats from some birthday *party*. They swept through the snack aisle like a warm, cheerful wind, laughing and comparing chips. Tang whispered that they came every Friday. The Manager had already put extra stock on the shelf without being asked.
party:0.cnHint: 一群戴着纸帽子的人聚____结束后涌进店里买零食。
party:0.hook: One of them left a folded note under a bag of chips.
party:0.line: 'After every *party* we end up here — best last stop in the city.'

rescue:0.en: The coffee machine made a terrible grinding noise and stopped. A long line of sleepy customers stared at me. I stared back. Then Tang appeared from the stock room, opened a small panel I had never noticed, and pressed two buttons. The machine hummed back to life — a quiet *rescue* that saved my whole night.
rescue:0.cnHint: 咖啡机突然罢工，同事悄悄出手____了慌乱的新人。
rescue:0.hook: Tang smiled but never explained where she had learned that trick.
rescue:0.line: 'Think of it as a *rescue* — the machine just needed someone who listened.'

writing:0.en: An old regular slid a folded paper across the counter and tapped it twice. 'For the Manager,' he said. The *writing* inside was small and careful — a hand-drawn floor plan and a short note. I set it beside the register, curious. The Manager picked it up, read one line, and went very still.
writing:0.cnHint: 一位老顾客留下一张____，店长看完后神情变得凝重。
writing:0.hook: The Manager folded the paper and put it straight in his pocket.
writing:0.line: 'Good *writing* says everything in a few lines — this says plenty.'

bite:0.en: Lin arrived just before dawn, carrying a warm meat bun from somewhere across town. She offered me one *bite* before eating the rest herself, leaning on the opposite counter with a calm smile. I had thought she was only our rival. But rivals, I was learning, could still share breakfast at four in the morning.
bite:0.cnHint: 竞争对手在凌晨分了新人一____包子，两人气氛意外融洽。
bite:0.hook: Lin left without mentioning why she had really come by.
bite:0.line: 'Have a *bite* — you look like the night has been eating you instead.'

capture:0.en: The Manager held up his phone to show me a photo. He had managed to *capture* the exact corner where the new branch would open — a narrow shop front between a bookstore and a tea stall, morning light falling just right. 'That light is the whole selling point,' he said, and I believed him.
capture:0.cnHint: 店长用一张照片____下了新分店选址的独特魅力。
capture:0.hook: The bookstore next door had a 'closing soon' sign in the window.
capture:0.line: 'I had to *capture* that light before the clouds moved — it tells the whole story.'

cope:0.en: By three in the morning, Tang had gone on her break, the printer was jammed, and four customers needed receipts. I had to *cope* on my own, fixing the jam with a pencil and a calm voice I did not quite feel. When Tang returned she simply nodded, which I decided to accept as a compliment.
cope:0.cnHint: 打印机卡纸，同事不在，新人独自____了这场小危机。
cope:0.hook: Tang's nod told me the real test was still coming.
cope:0.line: 'You learn to *cope* fast on this shift — the store does not wait for anyone.'

frame:0.en: The Manager held up a large *frame* and pointed to the empty wall behind the counter. 'The new store plan goes here,' he said, tapping the wood. Lin rolled her eyes from the snack aisle. Tang just nodded, already reaching for a hammer. Nobody had asked my opinion yet.
frame:0.cnHint: 店长把新分店的规划图挂进____里，准备上墙。
frame:0.hook: But the plan inside the frame was not what Lin expected.
frame:0.line: 'This *frame* will hold the blueprint for our second store.'

friday:0.en: It was *Friday* night, and the Manager spread a map across the counter to show us the new branch location. Tang counted the distance on his fingers. Lin argued the spot was too close to a rival shop. I wiped down the glass cabinet and quietly memorised every word.
friday:0.cnHint: 店长选在____晚上宣布新分店的选址计划。
friday:0.hook: Lin's smile faded the moment she saw the exact address.
friday:0.line: 'Every *Friday* we will review the new store's progress together.'

grain:0.en: Tang poured sample rice onto the counter, checking each *grain* for quality before the new store's supplier meeting. 'Our customers notice everything,' he said. Lin leaned over, picked one up, and gave a small nod. The Manager watched from the door, arms folded, looking almost proud.
grain:0.cnHint: 阿糖仔细检查每一____的质量，为新分店的供应商会议做准备。
grain:0.hook: Then the supplier arrived early, and he had questions of his own.
grain:0.line: 'Every *grain* we sell at the new store must meet this standard.'

implication:0.en: The Manager described the new branch casually, but Lin caught the *implication* at once — her current role might move there. She set her clipboard down very slowly. Tang pretended to arrange the canned goods. I kept my eyes on the register and tried to look busy, which was not hard.
implication:0.cnHint: 店长的话有一层____，隔壁咖啡店的林听出来他可能要让她去新店工作。
implication:0.hook: Lin picked up her clipboard again and wrote something none of us could see.
implication:0.line: 'The *implication* is clear — one of us will run the new branch.'

incredible:0.en: Lin showed me the *incredible* sales numbers from the trial weekend at the new location — nearly double our usual total. Tang nearly dropped his mop. The Manager just smiled and refilled the coffee machine as if he had known all along. Maybe he had. I started wondering what my role would be.
incredible:0.cnHint: 新分店试营业的销售数据____，几乎是平时的两倍。
incredible:0.hook: The Manager then slid a blank contract across the counter toward me.
incredible:0.line: 'These results are *incredible* — the new store is already a hit.'

net:0.en: The Manager drew a rough *net* of delivery routes on the whiteboard, connecting the main store to the planned branch two streets away. Tang traced the lines with his finger. Lin pointed out a gap near the night market. I added a small circle there, and the Manager said nothing — which felt like approval.
net:0.cnHint: 店长在白板上画出配送路线的____，连接主店和新分店。
net:0.hook: Lin stared at my circle for a long moment before she spoke.
net:0.line: 'The *net* of routes must cover both stores before we open.'

obtain:0.en: To *obtain* the licence for the new branch, the Manager needed three signatures and a site inspection. Tang had already collected two. Lin held the third form and bargained quietly for a better shift schedule in return. The Manager agreed faster than any of us expected. Tang and I exchanged a quick glance.
obtain:0.cnHint: 为了____新分店的营业执照，大家各有各的小算盘。
obtain:0.hook: The inspector was due at nine, and Lin had not signed yet.
obtain:0.line: 'We must *obtain* that licence before the end of the week.'

pair:0.en: The Manager handed Tang and me a *pair* of matching aprons printed with the new branch logo. Tang held his up and grinned. Mine had a small ink stain on the pocket, which the Manager noticed and apologised for. Lin looked at the aprons, then at us, then walked to the back room without a word.
pair:0.cnHint: 店长给阿糖和我各发了一件新分店的围裙，凑成____。
pair:0.hook: Lin came back carrying a third apron that nobody had printed yet.
pair:0.line: 'Take this *pair* of aprons — you two will open the new store.'

persuade:0.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter. 'The new branch opens next month,' he said proudly. I tried to *persuade* him that our little store already felt perfect — warm light, familiar faces, the smell of steamed buns at midnight. He just smiled and tapped the map.
persuade:0.cnHint: 店长展示新分店计划，我试图____他留在原地就好。
persuade:0.hook: But his pen was already circling a second location.
persuade:0.line: 'I need to *persuade* the landlord before Friday, or the deal is gone.'

preference:0.en: Tang lined up three new rice-ball flavours on the counter for a taste test. She handed me a small notepad and said the Manager wanted real feedback. My *preference* was the one with pickled plum, no question. Tang wrote that down and nodded slowly, as if it confirmed something she already suspected.
preference:0.cnHint: 同事让我试吃新品，记录我的____。
preference:0.hook: She had been collecting everyone's answers — except the Manager's.
preference:0.line: 'My *preference* is the pickled plum, but please don't tell Tang I said that.'

reliable:0.en: Lin from the shop across the street stopped by just before midnight. She needed a box of straws and said, quietly, that our store was the only *reliable* place open at this hour. I handed her the straws. She left without her usual sharp remarks. That felt like the highest praise I had ever received.
reliable:0.cnHint: 竞争对手深夜来借物资，说我们是这条街最____的地方。
reliable:0.hook: She came back ten minutes later, this time with a question.
reliable:0.line: 'Honestly, your store is the most *reliable* thing on this street.'

suspect:0.en: A jar of pickled eggs went missing from the back shelf. The Manager asked me to review the night's receipts. I began to *suspect* the jar had simply been moved during restocking, not stolen at all. Then I found Tang's handwriting on a sticky note: 'Borrowed for taste test. Sorry.'
suspect:0.cnHint: 腌蛋不见了，我开始____是搬货时弄错了位置。
suspect:0.hook: The sticky note had a second line that was carefully scratched out.
suspect:0.line: 'I *suspect* the new supplier changed the recipe without telling us.'

yield:0.en: The Manager asked Lin directly whether she would consider sharing the corner parking space during peak hours. After a long pause and a sip of canned coffee, Lin agreed to *yield* one spot on weekend mornings only. I watched from behind the register, quietly amazed. That was the first time I had ever seen her give anything away.
yield:0.cnHint: 店长请求竞争对手____停车位，她罕见地答应了。
yield:0.hook: Lin's agreement came with one condition nobody expected.
yield:0.line: 'Fine, I will *yield* the spot on Sundays, but only until ten.'

abandon:0.en: Halfway through the night shift I found a half-finished business plan tucked behind the mop bucket. Someone had written 'Branch Store Ideas' at the top, then crossed out every line. It hurt a little, seeing all that effort just *abandoned* like that. The handwriting looked very much like Tang's.
abandon:0.cnHint: 我在储藏室发现一份被____的分店计划书。
abandon:0.hook: The last crossed-out line was still faintly readable.
abandon:0.line: 'I had to *abandon* the whole idea once I saw the rent price.'

anxious:0.en: Opening night for the new branch was two days away, and the Manager had not slept properly in a week. He kept rearranging the sample display by the door. I could see he was *anxious*, checking his phone every few minutes for the delivery confirmation. I quietly made him a cup of hot barley tea and set it beside the register.
anxious:0.cnHint: 分店开业在即，店长____地等待货物确认消息。
anxious:0.hook: The delivery confirmation never came that night.
anxious:0.line: 'I am *anxious* about the freezer — what if it arrives late?'

assess:0.en: The Manager asked Tang and me to visit the new branch location and *assess* the shelf space before the fittings arrived. Tang measured every wall with a tape, humming softly. I counted the power sockets and wrote the numbers down. When we finished, Tang looked at her notes and said the space was smaller than it appeared in the photos.
assess:0.cnHint: 店长让我们去新店____货架空间是否够用。
assess:0.hook: Tang's final measurement did not match the landlord's floor plan.
assess:0.line: 'Let's *assess* the back room first — that is where the problems usually hide.'

cent:0.en: The new branch's grand-opening flyer said every item was marked down. A small boy dropped his coins on the counter and counted them twice. He was one *cent* short for a sweet bun. I pretended the register had rounded down. The Manager, watching from the door, said nothing and turned away.
cent:0.cnHint: 一个小男孩差一____买不起甜面包，店员悄悄帮了他。
cent:0.hook: The Manager's silence felt like a test.
cent:0.line: 'You are exactly one *cent* short, but today that does not matter.'

commercial:0.en: A rep from a drinks company arrived with a tablet and a big smile. He wanted to film a short *commercial* inside the store — our shelves as the backdrop, our smiling faces in the shot. The Manager folded his arms. 'My store is not a film set,' he said. 'Unless you buy something first.'
commercial:0.cnHint: 一位饮料公司代表想在店里拍____，被店长婉拒了。
commercial:0.hook: The rep bought one bottle and asked again.
commercial:0.line: 'This *commercial* will make your store famous overnight, I promise.'

death:0.en: Tang taped a new sign above the coffee machine: CAUTION — THE OLD MACHINE IS NEAR *DEATH*. It had been making a sound like a small, sad cat for three days. The Manager read the sign, laughed once, and called the repair service at last. The machine gave a final shudder, as if it had heard.
death:0.cnHint: 唐贴了张告示，说旧咖啡机已濒临____。
death:0.hook: The repair voice on the phone said, 'We'll come Thursday — maybe.'
death:0.line: 'That machine sounds like it is *death* walking, honestly.'

escape:0.en: Just before the regional boss's visit, Lin knocked over a whole shelf of bottled tea. Glass and liquid spread everywhere. I watched Lin's eyes search the store for an *escape* — the back door, the stock room, anywhere. The regional boss walked in at that exact moment, shoes stopping at the edge of the mess.
escape:0.cnHint: 林打翻了一排瓶装茶，慌乱中想____却无路可走。
escape:0.hook: The regional boss looked down, then slowly looked up.
escape:0.line: 'There is no *escape* now — just smile and start cleaning.'

expose:0.en: The Manager decided to move the drinks fridge to make room for new shelves. Behind it, the wall was dark with damp. 'Well,' said Tang quietly, 'moving the fridge was a great way to *expose* a problem we did not know we had.' The Manager stared at the wall for a long moment. Nobody spoke.
expose:0.cnHint: 移动冰柜后，店长意外____了一面潮湿的墙。
expose:0.hook: The new-branch opening was still four days away.
expose:0.line: 'Moving this shelf will *expose* everything we have been ignoring.'

floor:0.en: The new branch had a second level, which none of us had expected. The Manager led us up a narrow stair and stopped on the upper *floor*: empty, bright, smelling of fresh paint. 'Storage,' he said. Then he paused. 'Or maybe something else.' He looked around with an expression I had not seen on him before.
floor:0.cnHint: 新分店有第二层____，店长站在那里陷入沉思。
floor:0.line: 'Come up to the second *floor* — you need to see this yourselves.'

foundation:0.en: Tang said every good store needed a strong *foundation*, then pointed at the cracked tile near the entrance of the new branch. The Manager crouched and pressed it with one finger. It rocked gently. He stood up, pulled out his phone, and made a call without a word to either of us. Tang mouthed 'sorry' at me.
foundation:0.cnHint: 唐谈到好店铺需要稳固的____，却发现门口地砖松动了。
foundation:0.hook: Whatever the Manager said on that call, his voice was very low.
foundation:0.line: 'A store's *foundation* matters more than its sign or its price tags.'

beautiful:0.en: The Manager spread a large map across the counter. 'Our second store will go here,' he said, tapping a corner spot three blocks away. The map showed a *beautiful* little square nearby, full of trees and benches. I leaned in, already imagining morning customers carrying coffee past those trees.
beautiful:0.cnHint: 店长在柜台上展开地图，指着附近一个____的小广场，规划新分店的位置。
beautiful:0.hook: But Lin was staring at the same spot on her phone.
beautiful:0.line: 'That *beautiful* square will bring us plenty of foot traffic,' the Manager said.

combine:0.en: The Manager pulled out two notebooks and slid them toward me. One tracked daily sales; the other tracked customer visits. 'If we *combine* the data from both stores,' he said, 'we can see exactly what people want.' I nodded, though the numbers already made my head spin.
combine:0.cnHint: 店长说，要把两家店的数据____在一起，才能更好地了解顾客需求。
combine:0.hook: Tang quietly took a photo of the notebooks when the Manager turned away.
combine:0.line: 'We need to *combine* both records before the meeting,' the Manager said.

complicated:0.en: Setting up the new store's stock system turned out to be far more *complicated* than anyone expected. There were codes, categories, and supplier lists that all had to match. Tang and I sat on the floor surrounded by papers, trying to make sense of it. The Manager just smiled from the doorway.
complicated:0.cnHint: 新店的库存系统比预想的要____得多，我和阿糖坐在地上努力整理文件。
complicated:0.hook: Then the Manager's smile slowly disappeared.
complicated:0.line: Tang sighed, 'This is way more *complicated* than last time.'

crash:0.en: We were carrying a tall shelf into the back room of the new store when I heard a loud *crash* behind us. A box of glass jars had slipped off a trolley and hit the floor. Everyone froze. The Manager closed his eyes for exactly three seconds, then said, 'Clean it up.'
crash:0.cnHint: 我们在新店搬货架时，一箱玻璃罐子掉落发出____声，碎了一地。
crash:0.hook: One jar, somehow, had rolled under the Manager's shoe.
crash:0.line: 'What was that *crash*?' Lin called out from the next room.

creature:0.en: Late in the first night at the new store, a small *creature* slipped under the front door — a tiny grey cat, wet from the rain outside. It looked up at me with very serious eyes, then walked straight to the snack aisle as if it already owned the place.
creature:0.cnHint: 新店第一个深夜，一只小____从门缝钻进来，径直走向零食区。
creature:0.hook: It sat down in front of the exact shelf the Manager had said not to touch.
creature:0.line: 'Is that *creature* on our inventory sheet?' Tang asked, completely serious.

crime:0.en: Lin walked into the new store before opening day and looked around slowly. 'Putting the drinks fridge in that corner,' she said, 'is practically a *crime* against good store design.' The Manager's eyebrow went up exactly one centimetre. I pretended to be very busy counting pens.
crime:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林参观新店时说，把冰柜放在那个角落简直是设计上的____。
crime:0.hook: The Manager moved the fridge that same afternoon, without saying a word.
crime:0.line: 'Wasting that window space is a *crime*,' Lin said, shaking her head.

deeply:0.en: After the planning meeting for the new store, the Manager sat alone at the counter and stared at the wall. He was *deeply* focused on something — I could tell because he did not blink when Tang dropped a full bag of rice behind him. I had never seen him that still.
deeply:0.cnHint: 开会结束后，店长一个人坐在柜台前，____地陷入沉思，连身后的动静都没注意到。
deeply:0.hook: Then he wrote one word on a notepad and covered it with his hand.
deeply:0.line: 'I am *deeply* worried about the budget for next month,' the Manager said quietly.

demonstrate:0.en: The Manager gathered us in the new store's back room to *demonstrate* how the new ordering tablet worked. He tapped through three screens very confidently, then the tablet made a sad sound and went blank. We all waited. 'The main idea is clear,' he said, 'even if the device is not.'
demonstrate:0.cnHint: 店长在新店后仓向我们____新订货平板的用法，结果平板中途黑屏了。
demonstrate:0.hook: Tang's hand was already reaching for the old paper order forms.
demonstrate:0.line: 'Let me *demonstrate* the correct way to close a shift report,' the Manager said.

couple:0.en: The Manager called us all into the back room after closing. 'We are opening a second store next month,' he said, holding up a *couple* of hand-drawn floor plans. Tang and I leaned in to look. The two layouts were almost identical — except one had a much larger snack wall.
couple:0.cnHint: 店长展示了两份____的开店平面图，其中一份零食区大得多。
couple:0.hook: Tang quietly pointed at the bigger snack wall and raised one eyebrow.
couple:0.line: 'I have a *couple* of ideas for the new layout — want to hear them?'

definition:0.en: The Manager pinned a sign above the new store's door during the planning meeting. Tang read it aloud and frowned. 'The *definition* of a convenience store,' Tang said slowly, 'is a place that saves time — so why is the checkout counter in the very back corner?' Nobody had a good answer.
definition:0.cnHint: 会议上，唐读了新店的标语，质疑它是否符合便利店的____。
definition:0.hook: The Manager smiled in a way that suggested the corner placement was very much on purpose.
definition:0.line: 'The *definition* of convenient is speed — so the counter moves to the front.'

imagination:0.en: Tang spread a blank sheet of paper on the break-room table. 'Use your *imagination*,' Tang said, sketching a rough map of the new store. 'Where would you put the hot-food counter?' I drew a big circle right at the entrance. Tang stared at it, then slowly drew the same circle.
imagination:0.cnHint: 唐让我发挥____，在白纸上规划新店的热食区位置。
imagination:0.hook: We both looked up at the same moment, wondering if the Manager had already decided.
imagination:0.line: 'Use your *imagination* — there are no wrong answers yet.'

journey:0.en: Lin stopped by just as we were packing sample goods for the new store. 'Every new branch is a *journey*,' Lin said, setting a small plant on the counter. 'I brought this for good luck.' It was a tiny cactus. The Manager placed it carefully on top of the tallest shelf.
journey:0.cnHint: 林送来一株小仙人掌，说开新店是一段____，祝我们好运。
journey:0.hook: Nobody mentioned that Lin ran the shop right across the street.
journey:0.line: 'Opening a new store is always a *journey* — enjoy the first steps.'

nearby:0.en: The Manager spread a city map across the counter and tapped a red dot. 'The new store is here,' he said. Tang and I crowded in. It was *nearby* — barely three blocks away, on the same quiet kind of corner. Tang immediately started counting how long the walk between stores would be.
nearby:0.cnHint: 店长在地图上指出新店位置，距离这里非常____，只有三个街区。
nearby:0.hook: Tang's walk-time count kept getting shorter each time Tang repeated it.
nearby:0.line: 'It is *nearby*, so we can share stock runs on busy nights.'

perspective:0.en: Tang and I argued about the shelf height in the new store for ten minutes. The Manager listened, then walked to the far end of the room and turned around. 'From this *perspective*,' the Manager said quietly, 'both of you are pointing at the same shelf.' We looked at each other and laughed.
perspective:0.cnHint: 店长换了个____站到房间另一端，发现我们其实在说同一排货架。
perspective:0.hook: The Manager then asked whose perspective we had forgotten to consider.
perspective:0.line: 'From the customer's *perspective*, the shelf should be at eye level.'

requirement:0.en: The Manager slid a printed checklist across the table. 'City permit,' he read, 'fire exit, staff training log.' Tang picked it up and turned pale. Every box was empty. 'The only hard *requirement* due this week,' the Manager added calmly, 'is the fire exit sign.' Tang exhaled very slowly.
requirement:0.cnHint: 店长拿出开店许可清单，本周唯一必须完成的____是消防出口标志。
requirement:0.hook: Tang then noticed a second page, still face-down on the table.
requirement:0.line: 'The fire-exit sign is the one *requirement* we cannot skip this week.'

signal:0.en: Tang set up a small bell above the new store's back door during the trial run. 'It will *signal* us whenever a delivery arrives,' Tang explained, looking very pleased. We tested it three times. On the fourth ring the Manager appeared, holding a cup of tea, asking if someone had ordered anything.
signal:0.cnHint: 唐在新店后门装了一个铃铛，用来____有快递到达，结果把店长也引来了。
signal:0.hook: The Manager stayed for the tea — and quietly moved the bell six inches higher.
signal:0.line: 'One ring will *signal* a delivery; two rings means come quickly.'

strength:0.en: The Manager called us all into the back room before dawn. 'We are opening a second store next month,' he said, spreading a map across the shelf. 'I need to know our *strength* — how many of you can cover extra shifts?' Tang raised a hand without hesitation. I raised mine a second later, still not sure what I had agreed to.
strength:0.cnHint: 店长在黎明前召集大家，询问开新店时的____，阿糖毫不犹豫地举起了手。
strength:0.hook: But the address on that map was right next to Lin's store.
strength:0.line: 'Our *strength* is the team, not just the building.'

survive:0.en: Lin stopped by at three in the morning, buying nothing, just standing near the drinks cooler. 'Two new stores opening on this street,' he said quietly. 'Only the best one will *survive*.' He smiled at me, not unkindly, then walked back into the dark without buying a single thing.
survive:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜到店，说这条街上只有最好的店才能____，然后空手离去。
survive:0.hook: He had left a small business card pressed under the cooler handle.
survive:0.line: 'We all want to *survive*, but how we do it matters.'

touch:0.en: A woman came in just before sunrise, eyes red, carrying a big empty bag. She bought only a small bottle of warm tea. When I handed it to her, our fingers did not quite meet, but that brief *touch* of warmth through the glass made her smile for just a second. She left a folded note on the counter.
touch:0.cnHint: 一位红眼眶的女士买了一瓶热茶，那短暂的____让她微微一笑，还留下了一张纸条。
touch:0.hook: The note had a single sentence: 'I'll be back tomorrow, I promise.'
touch:0.line: 'Sometimes a small *touch* of kindness is enough.'

trap:0.en: Tang warned me about the stockroom on my third night. 'The door swings shut on its own,' she whispered. 'New clerks always get *trapped* in there for twenty minutes before they find the inside handle.' I laughed. An hour later, standing in the dark among boxes of instant noodles, I was not laughing anymore.
trap:0.cnHint: 阿糖提醒我小心储藏室的门，结果我还是被____在里面长达二十分钟。
trap:0.hook: When the door finally opened, Tang was standing there, holding a stopwatch.
trap:0.line: 'Don't let the job *trap* you — learn every corner of this store.'

tv:0.en: The small *tv* above the counter had been showing the same cooking programme on low volume every night since I started. Nobody ever changed it. Tonight an old man sat on the step stool for an hour watching the silent pictures of someone frying fish, then stood up, bowed slightly at the screen, and walked out.
tv:0.cnHint: 柜台上方的小____每晚都播同一个烹饪节目，一位老人看了一个小时后，向屏幕微微鞠躬离开了。
tv:0.hook: The next night he came back with a plate of homemade fried fish.
tv:0.line: 'That *tv* has been here longer than any of us, I think.'

victim:0.en: Tang told me about the great Spilled-Sauce Disaster of last spring. A shelf had tipped, twelve jars broke, and the Manager had to close the store for four hours to clean up. 'I was the *victim*,' Tang said, pointing to a faint stain near the door. 'It got my favourite shoes.' She still looked sad about it.
victim:0.cnHint: 阿糖讲述了去年春天酱料架倒塌的故事，她是那次事故的____，最心爱的鞋子因此报废。
victim:0.hook: She glanced at the shelf, and I noticed she had quietly moved it six centimetres from the wall.
victim:0.line: 'I was the only *victim*, and my shoes never recovered.'

zone:0.en: The Manager had divided the store into what he called 'comfort zones.' The warm drinks were the reading *zone*, the snack wall was the thinking zone, and the small bench by the window was the resting zone. Nobody followed the signs. Everyone just stood wherever they felt like it, which, Tang said, was exactly what the Manager had hoped for.
zone:0.cnHint: 店长将小店划分成不同的____，但顾客从不遵守，据说这正是店长的真实用意。
zone:0.hook: There was one zone with no sign, just a single chair facing the street.
zone:0.line: 'This *zone* near the window is where the best ideas happen.'

afraid:0.en: On my first solo night shift, the street outside went completely quiet around four in the morning. Every small sound made me jump. I was a little *afraid*, not of anything real, just of the bigness of the silence. Then the door beeped, and a sleepy student shuffled in looking for hot canned soup, and the store felt warm again.
afraid:0.cnHint: 第一次独立值夜班时，我有些____，四点钟的寂静让人心跳加速，直到一位困倦的学生推门而入。
afraid:0.hook: That student came back every night for a week, always at exactly four.
afraid:0.line: 'Don't be *afraid* of the quiet — the best customers appear after four.'

preserve:0.en: The Manager spread old photos across the break-room table. 'These are from the first store,' he said quietly. Tang leaned in, eyes wide. The Manager wanted to *preserve* every image — the faded colours, the crooked shelves — before the new branch opened and everyone forgot where it all began.
preserve:0.cnHint: 店长想把老照片____下来，不让新开分店的热闹冲淡最初的记忆。
preserve:0.hook: But one photo showed a face nobody recognised.
preserve:0.line: 'We must *preserve* these photos before the new branch opens.'

procedure:0.en: Tang handed me a laminated card on my first night. 'Follow this and nothing goes wrong,' she said. Every step of the closing *procedure* was listed in order — counting the cash, checking the fridges, locking the back door. I read it three times, then taped it above the register just in case.
procedure:0.cnHint: 同事给我看了一张卡片，上面写着关店的____，每一步都不能跳过。
procedure:0.hook: Step seven, however, had been crossed out by someone.
procedure:0.line: 'The closing *procedure* has seven steps — don't skip any.'

reasonable:0.en: A man in a long coat studied the price tag on a rice ball for a full minute. 'Is this *reasonable*?' he asked, turning to me with a serious face. I checked the shelf, checked my memory, and nodded. He bought four. Tang whispered that he asks the same question every single night.
reasonable:0.cnHint: 一位常客盯着饭团的价格看了很久，问我这个价格是否____。
reasonable:0.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he stayed to eat inside.
reasonable:0.line: 'Four for that price? Sounds *reasonable* to me.'

reduction:0.en: The Manager taped a handwritten sign to the hot-food counter: 'Late-night special.' Tang explained that a ten-percent *reduction* on unsold items after midnight helped avoid waste. I nodded, but I noticed the Manager always set aside one pork bun before the discount started. He never said who it was for.
reduction:0.cnHint: 深夜，店长给滞销热食打折，这种价格____的做法是为了减少浪费。
reduction:0.hook: The reserved pork bun disappeared at exactly half past midnight.
reduction:0.line: 'A ten-percent *reduction* after midnight — that cuts the waste.'

season:0.en: 'You'll understand once you've worked a full *season*,' Tang said, refilling the umbrella stand near the door. She meant the rainy stretch between spring and summer, when the whole neighbourhood seemed to live inside the store — dripping coats, warm drinks, long quiet hours. I was starting to see what she meant.
season:0.cnHint: 同事说，等我经历完这个____，就会真正懂得这家店的节奏。
season:0.hook: She still hadn't explained what happened last rainy season.
season:0.line: 'Work one full *season* here and you'll know every regular.'

sector:0.en: The Manager drew a rough map of the store on a napkin. 'Each *sector* has a person responsible,' he said, circling the drinks wall, the snack aisle, and the hot counter in turn. Tang got the drinks. I got snacks. The hot counter circle he left empty, then tapped it with his pen.
sector:0.cnHint: 店长把店铺划分成几个____，每人负责一块，但热食区却没有写名字。
sector:0.hook: He folded the napkin and slipped it into his pocket without a word.
sector:0.line: 'The drinks *sector* is yours, Tang — keep it full.'

setting:0.en: I arrived early and stood in the doorway, just looking. Warm light, soft hum of fridges, the faint smell of steamed buns — the whole *setting* felt like a place that had always existed and always would. Tang appeared behind me. 'Pretty, right?' she said. 'Wait until the rush hits at two a.m.'
setting:0.cnHint: 我提前到店，被这里温暖的____深深吸引，觉得它好像永远都在。
setting:0.hook: Tang's smile faded slightly when she said 'two a.m.'
setting:0.line: 'I love the *setting* of this place — it feels like home.'

shrink:0.en: The Manager unrolled a large floor plan for the new branch. Tang and I leaned over it. 'The stock room will *shrink* by half,' the Manager said, tapping the paper. Tang crossed her arms. I did the maths quietly — half the storage meant twice as many small deliveries, which meant the night shift would get very busy.
shrink:0.cnHint: 店长说新店的库房会____一半，同事和我都意识到夜班会因此忙很多。
shrink:0.hook: Tang looked at me, and I already knew what she was thinking.
shrink:0.line: 'If the stock room *shrinks*, our nights are going to be longer.'

strike:0.en: The Manager called everyone into the back room. 'There is a *strike* at the warehouse,' he said, setting down his clipboard. 'No new stock arrives tonight.' The shelves looked thin. I counted the remaining instant noodles — only nine cups. Somehow, that made the quiet store feel even smaller.
strike:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我们，仓库发生了____，今晚没有货物送来。
strike:0.hook: Then a regular arrived, wanting exactly what we had run out of.
strike:0.line: 'The *strike* means no delivery tonight, so please choose carefully.'

television:0.en: A small *television* hung in the corner above the magazine rack. Nobody had turned it on for weeks, the Manager said. But tonight, an old man came in, bought a can of coffee, and stood below it, staring at the blank screen as if a favourite programme were playing. I did not ask why.
television:0.cnHint: 角落里有台____，一位老人盯着黑屏看了很久。
television:0.hook: When he finally left, he whispered a name I did not recognise.
television:0.line: 'That old *television* reminds me of something I lost long ago.'

youth:0.en: Lin dropped by near midnight, still in his shop uniform. 'Business is slow,' he admitted, leaning on the counter. We talked about our first jobs, our plans, our worries. For a moment, all rivalry faded. 'You know,' he said, 'I miss the energy of *youth*, when nothing felt impossible.' I nodded slowly.
youth:0.cnHint: 林来店里闲聊，感慨____一去不返。
youth:0.hook: Before he left, he slipped a folded note under the register.
youth:0.line: '*Youth* passes fast — better make your move before it is gone.'

alter:0.en: The Manager had decided to *alter* the layout of the snack aisle overnight. Tang and I moved shelves, shifted boxes, and re-stacked everything by two in the morning. The store looked almost unrecognisable. A sleepy customer walked in, blinked hard, and turned a full circle as if he had entered the wrong building.
alter:0.cnHint: 店长决定____零食区的布局，我们忙了大半夜。
alter:0.hook: The customer reached into his pocket and pulled out an old store map.
alter:0.line: 'Why did you *alter* everything? I can never find the chips now.'

approximately:0.en: Tang was trying to count the bottles of water in the stockroom. 'There are *approximately* two hundred left,' she called out, 'but I stopped counting at one fifty because a box fell on my foot.' The Manager sighed, wrote something in his notebook, and then drew a small question mark beside the number.
approximately:0.cnHint: 唐____数了一下库存，但没数完就放弃了。
approximately:0.hook: Later, the Manager found the actual number was far more surprising.
approximately:0.line: '*Approximately* two hundred — give or take a falling box.'

attractive:0.en: A new display stand arrived that afternoon. The Manager had ordered it online — bright colours, clean lines, perfectly placed near the entrance. 'Very *attractive*,' said Tang, nodding with genuine respect. Within an hour, every customer who walked in paused to look at it. None of them, however, bought anything from it.
attractive:0.cnHint: 新展示架非常____，吸引了每位进门的顾客驻足。
attractive:0.hook: The Manager checked the price tag and went very quiet.
attractive:0.line: 'It looks *attractive*, but looking is all anyone seems to do.'

bag:0.en: A young woman rushed in and began filling a small *bag* with snacks — chips, gummies, chocolate wafers, two cans of tea. She moved with great purpose, like someone on a mission. At the counter she paid exactly, to the coin, without looking at the total. 'Study night,' she said simply, and disappeared into the dark street.
bag:0.cnHint: 一位女生把零食装进____里，看样子要熬夜苦读。
bag:0.hook: She left behind a handwritten list with one item still unchecked.
bag:0.line: 'This *bag* is for survival — four hours of revision ahead.'

beat:0.en: The store's small speaker played an old pop song, and the *beat* was just fast enough to keep me awake through the long slow stretch between three and four in the morning. Tang tapped the counter in time. Even the Manager's pen clicked along. For one strange minute, the whole store moved together.
beat:0.cnHint: 音箱里歌曲的____让我们三人在深夜里同步了片刻。
beat:0.hook: Then the song cut off, and someone knocked on the glass door.
beat:0.line: 'Follow the *beat* — it is the only thing keeping us awake right now.'

bottom:0.en: The Manager handed me a long list of tasks on my first night. 'Start from the *bottom*,' he said, pointing at the floor near the drink fridges. I found a old mop and a bucket down there, both dusty. Clearly, no one had cleaned that corner in weeks.
bottom:0.cnHint: 店长让新来的夜班员工从清单____开始做起。
bottom:0.hook: Something small and wet moved behind the bucket.
bottom:0.line: 'Check the *bottom* shelf — that's where the expired milk hides.'

breed:0.en: A regular customer brought in her dog every Tuesday night. 'What *breed* is he?' I asked, scratching the little fellow behind his ears. She smiled and said nobody really knew — part fluffy, part mystery. The dog sat very still and stared at the snack wall like he was planning something.
breed:0.cnHint: 一位常客带来了她的狗，没人说得清这只狗的____。
breed:0.hook: The next Tuesday, she came in alone, looking pale.
breed:0.line: 'Nobody knows his *breed*, but he always finds the beef jerky.'

classify:0.en: Tang was trying to tidy the back shelf before dawn. 'How do you *classify* this thing?' she called out, holding up a small tin with no label and no price sticker. I walked over and we both stared at it. It smelled faintly of something sweet, maybe coconut, maybe soap.
classify:0.cnHint: 同事拿着一个没有标签的罐子，不知道该如何____它。
classify:0.hook: The Manager went very quiet when he saw the tin.
classify:0.line: 'I cannot *classify* this item — the label is completely gone.'

comment:0.en: Our store had a small paper *comment* box near the door, the kind with a little slot on top. One night I found it stuffed so full that slips of paper were sticking out everywhere. Most said nice things. One, written in very careful letters, just said: 'The night clerk has kind eyes.'
comment:0.cnHint: 店里的____箱里塞满了顾客留下的纸条。
comment:0.hook: The last slip had a phone number on the back.
comment:0.line: 'Leave a *comment* in the box — the Manager reads every single one.'

component:0.en: Lin arrived just before midnight to check our new self-checkout machine. 'One *component* inside is loose,' she said, lifting a small panel on the side. She laid out the parts on the counter like a tiny puzzle. I watched her work, quietly impressed, though I would never say so out loud.
component:0.cnHint: 竞争对手来检查新机器，发现其中一个____松动了。
component:0.hook: Lin pocketed one small part and said nothing.
component:0.line: 'This *component* keeps failing — I have replaced it three times already.'

contrary:0.en: Everyone said the night shift would be boring. On the *contrary*, by two in the morning I had helped a lost delivery driver, settled a debate about instant noodle flavours, and given directions to a woman walking a very large rabbit on a lead. I sat down at last and laughed quietly to myself.
contrary:0.cnHint: 大家以为夜班很无聊，____，第一夜发生了很多趣事。
contrary:0.hook: Then the rabbit hopped back in through the open door.
contrary:0.line: 'On the *contrary*, this store is the busiest corner in the whole street.'

deny:0.en: Tang came in smelling of paint at three in the morning. 'Were you decorating at this hour?' I asked. She tried to *deny* it, but there was a streak of yellow on her left ear and blue on her right hand. She bought two coffees, winked at me, and walked back out into the dark.
deny:0.cnHint: 同事身上有油漆痕迹，却试图____自己一直在刷墙。
deny:0.hook: A light in the building across the street clicked off.
deny:0.line: 'I cannot *deny* it — the paint on my hands tells the whole story.'

depth:0.en: The Manager kept a notebook behind the counter. One quiet night I opened it by mistake, expecting stock numbers. Instead I found poems, page after page, full of careful words about rain and small rooms. The *depth* of feeling in those lines surprised me completely. I closed it fast and said nothing.
depth:0.cnHint: 新员工偶然翻开店长的笔记本，被其中情感的____震惊了。
depth:0.hook: The Manager walked in just as I set the notebook down.
depth:0.line: 'The *depth* of this city only shows itself after midnight.'

employment:0.en: The Manager called me into the back office on my third night. He spread a map across the desk and pointed to a spot two streets away. 'We are opening a second store,' he said. 'I need someone reliable.' That was when I understood my *employment* here was about more than selling snacks and restocking shelves.
employment:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我，我的____不只是卖零食那么简单。
employment:0.hook: He folded the map and slid it toward me without another word.
employment:0.line: 'Your *employment* here could lead to something much bigger.'

entire:0.en: A quiet old man came in just before three in the morning and walked every single aisle without picking up a thing. He studied each shelf the way a teacher reads a student's essay. By the time he reached the door, he had covered the *entire* store. He bought nothing. He just nodded at me and left.
entire:0.cnHint: 一位老人把店里____的货架都仔细看了一遍，却什么都没买。
entire:0.hook: The next morning, the Manager looked pale when I described the man.

gift:0.en: Tang slid a small paper bag across the counter to me on my first solo shift. Inside was a warm meat bun from the kitchen next door. 'A welcome *gift*,' she said with a grin. 'Also, the microwave beeps three times when it is actually done, not two — that is the real gift.' I had burned four buns before she told me.
gift:0.cnHint: 阿糖给了我一个____，还顺便教了我一个关于微波炉的秘密。
gift:0.hook: She watched me eat it, smiling like she was waiting for a specific reaction.
gift:0.line: 'Think of it as a *gift* from someone who learned the hard way.'

kitchen:0.en: The door marked STAFF ONLY hid a tiny *kitchen* behind the counter — just a microwave, a small stove, and a folding table. The Manager cooked rice there every night at midnight, and the whole store smelled of it. Regulars started timing their visits around that smell. I started doing the same without noticing.
kitchen:0.cnHint: 店里有一间小____，每天午夜飘出的饭香吸引了很多人。
kitchen:0.hook: One night the rice smell was different — richer, almost festive.
kitchen:0.line: 'The *kitchen* is yours to use after two in the morning — just clean up.'

mystery:0.en: Every Thursday at exactly 1 a.m., someone left a single coin on the windowsill outside and walked away without coming in. I asked Tang about it. She shrugged. 'It has been happening for two years,' she said. 'We have all given up trying to explain it.' For me, that only made the *mystery* more interesting.
mystery:0.cnHint: 每周四凌晨一点，窗台上会出现一枚硬币，这个____让所有人困惑了两年。
mystery:0.hook: This Thursday, the coin was gold-colored, not the usual silver.
mystery:0.line: 'Honestly, the *mystery* is half the reason I still work nights.'

opposite:0.en: Lin ran the small shop directly *opposite* ours — same hours, same snacks, almost the same prices. He would sometimes stand in his doorway and watch our store with a calm, unreadable expression. Tang told me not to worry about him. But the Manager always turned the front lights up a little brighter whenever Lin stepped outside.
opposite:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林的店就在我们____面，两家店之间有一种微妙的竞争关系。
opposite:0.hook: One night, Lin crossed the street and walked straight toward our door.
opposite:0.line: 'The shop *opposite* ours has been watching us all week — I noticed too.'

permanent:0.en: After one month on the job, the Manager slid a new name tag across the counter. It was heavier than my temporary one, with proper engraving. 'This means your position is *permanent*,' he said, very quietly, as if it were a private matter. I turned it over in my hands. Tang gave me a small thumbs-up from behind the snack display.
permanent:0.cnHint: 店长给了我一个新名牌，意味着我的职位变成____的了。
permanent:0.hook: Tang's expression shifted for just a second — something between pride and worry.
permanent:0.line: '*Permanent* staff get a key to the back door — do not lose it.'

plenty:0.en: The new store two streets away opened on a rainy Tuesday. The Manager stood at our counter looking calm, but he had made *plenty* of extra coffee and lined up every umbrella we had near the door. By midnight, our regulars had all come in, one by one, dripping wet and cheerful. None of them went to the new place. Not that night.
plenty:0.cnHint: 新店开业那晚，店长准备了____的咖啡和雨伞，老顾客们一个都没去新店。
plenty:0.hook: But one regular came in later than usual, carrying a bag from somewhere else.
plenty:0.line: 'We have *plenty* of supplies — the new store is not a problem yet.'

vigorous:0.en: The Manager arrived at six in the morning to inspect the new branch store. He moved through every aisle with *vigorous* steps, checking shelves, adjusting lights, and pointing at dust I had missed. I hurried behind him, notebook in hand, trying to keep up.
vigorous:0.cnHint: 店长以____的步伐巡视新分店，我拿着笔记本紧紧跟在后面。
vigorous:0.hook: He stopped at the back wall and said nothing for a long time.
vigorous:0.line: 'We open in two days, so keep those *vigorous* checks going all night.'

wide:0.en: The new branch had a *wide* selection of snacks, drinks, and small gifts — far more than our old store. I spent an hour just reading the labels. Tang leaned on the counter and laughed, saying I looked like a tourist who had never seen a shop before.
wide:0.cnHint: 新分店商品种类____，我花了一个小时看标签，被同事取笑。
wide:0.hook: One shelf near the window was completely empty, and nobody could explain why.
wide:0.line: 'A *wide* range of choices is good, but you still have to learn where everything goes.'

agriculture:0.en: A quiet man in muddy boots came in just before midnight. He set a small bag of fresh vegetables on the counter and explained that he studied *agriculture* at the university nearby and grew them himself. The Manager accepted the bag with both hands and bowed slightly.
agriculture:0.cnHint: 一位学____的大学生深夜送来自己种的蔬菜，店长郑重地接下。
agriculture:0.hook: The man left without giving his name or asking for any money.
agriculture:0.line: 'My *agriculture* professor says fresh food should go to people who need it most.'

assign:0.en: Before the opening, the Manager gathered Tang and me near the front door. He opened a small notebook and began to *assign* each of us a section of the store to manage. Tang got the drinks aisle. I got everything else — which felt like a joke until I saw his serious face.
assign:0.cnHint: 开业前，店长把店内各区域____给我和同事负责，我分到的范围出乎意料。
assign:0.hook: Tang gave me a look that said he already knew something I did not.
assign:0.line: 'I will *assign* the back storage room to you — please do not lose the key.'

broad:0.en: The new store sat on a *broad* corner where two streets met, so people passed it from every direction. By noon on opening day, the footpath was crowded and the door never stopped moving. I counted customers until I lost count, then just smiled and kept scanning items.
broad:0.cnHint: 新店坐落在____的街角，开业当天人来人往，我数客人数到忘记了数字。
broad:0.hook: One customer came in three times but never bought a single thing.
broad:0.line: 'A *broad* corner like this means we get twice the foot traffic — lucky us.'

careful:0.en: Lin arrived from the rival store across the street, pretending to shop. She picked up a rice ball, turned it over, and read every word on the back. I watched her be very *careful* about checking the price sticker, then quietly compare it with something on her phone.
careful:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林假装购物，____地查看商品价格，还悄悄与手机上的数据对比。
careful:0.hook: She put the rice ball down, smiled at me, and walked out empty-handed.
careful:0.line: 'You should be *careful* about your pricing — people notice small differences.'

combination:0.en: Tang had invented a late-night snack he called 'the special': a *combination* of instant noodles, a soft-boiled egg, and a single slice of processed cheese melted on top. Three regular customers ordered it every night. It was not on any menu. It existed only because Tang said so.
combination:0.cnHint: 同事发明了一种食物____，每晚都有三位老顾客专程来点，菜单上根本没有它。
combination:0.hook: Tonight, one of those regulars did not show up at the usual time.
combination:0.line: 'The secret is the *combination* — noodles alone are just sad.'

constant:0.en: Working the night shift meant living with *constant* small sounds: the hum of the drink fridge, the beep of the door sensor, the tick of the clock above the register. After one week I stopped hearing them. After two weeks I felt uneasy whenever they suddenly went quiet.
constant:0.cnHint: 夜班的____背景声音让我渐渐习以为常，直到某天它们突然消失。
constant:0.hook: At three in the morning, every sound in the store stopped at once.
constant:0.line: 'The *constant* noise of this fridge used to bother me — now I miss it when it stops.'

distinguish:0.en: The Manager asked me to arrange the new snack wall for the second store opening. There were two nearly identical bags of rice crackers side by side. 'Can you *distinguish* between the spicy ones and the plain ones?' he asked. I squinted at the tiny print. Tang leaned over and pointed to a small red dot in the corner.
distinguish:0.cnHint: 店长让我分辨两种几乎一模一样的米饼包装，新店开业前货架必须摆放正确。
distinguish:0.hook: Tang knew about that red dot without even looking closely.
distinguish:0.line: 'Can you *distinguish* the spicy bag from the plain one before a customer grabs the wrong one?'

document:0.en: A quiet man came in just after midnight, holding a folder tight to his chest. He asked if we had a copy machine. We did — tucked behind the noodle display. 'I need to copy this *document* before the new store opens tomorrow,' he said, voice careful, eyes tired. I made the copies without asking questions.
document:0.cnHint: 一个男人深夜来店里，急需复印一份重要____，说是新店明天开业前必须用到。
document:0.hook: The last page of that document had the Manager's signature on it.
document:0.line: 'This *document* has to reach the landlord by eight in the morning — please hurry.'

dozen:0.en: The Manager dropped off supplies for the new branch and left a *dozen* boxes of canned coffee stacked by the door. Tang counted them twice. 'Twelve,' she said, satisfied. I started moving them to the back shelf one by one. By box nine, I was already wondering if coffee could somehow get heavier with each lift.
dozen:0.cnHint: 店长送来了整整____罐装咖啡，让我和同事搬到货架上。
dozen:0.hook: The thirteenth box was hidden behind the door, and no one had ordered it.
dozen:0.line: 'A *dozen* boxes is fine for the small store, but the big one will need three times that.'

dull:0.en: The hour between three and four in the morning was always the *dull* stretch of the shift. No customers, no deliveries, just the low hum of the drink fridge and Tang drawing tiny cats in her notepad. I reorganised the candy rack for the second time. Then the door chimed, and a woman walked in wearing a hard hat.
dull:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点到四点是夜班最____的时段，但一个戴着安全帽的女人打破了沉寂。
dull:0.hook: She asked for a map of the neighbourhood, not a snack.
dull:0.line: 'The shift gets *dull* around three, but trust me, someone always shows up right when you stop expecting it.'

fortune:0.en: An older man came in every night for a warm meat bun. Tonight he lingered at the counter, turning a small coin over in his fingers. 'My grandfather said *fortune* favours people who stay open when everyone else closes,' he told me with a slow smile. I handed him his bun. He left the coin on the counter as a tip.
fortune:0.cnHint: 一位常客告诉我，他祖父说____总是眷顾那些在别人都打烊时还坚持营业的人。
fortune:0.hook: That coin had a date stamped on it from fifty years ago.
fortune:0.line: '*Fortune* favours the ones who keep the lights on — your Manager knows that well.'

fulfil:0.en: The Manager pinned a note to the staff board: the new store needed two clerks who could *fulfil* the same service standards as ours. Tang read it, nodded, and went back to stacking yoghurt. I read it three times. Something about the word 'standards' made me straighten my apron without meaning to.
fulfil:0.cnHint: 店长在公告栏贴出通知，新店需要能____同样服务标准的店员。
fulfil:0.hook: Tang's name was already written in pencil at the bottom of the note.
fulfil:0.line: 'You have to *fulfil* every step on the checklist — new store customers notice the small things first.'

gradually:0.en: When I first started, I could not find anything in the stockroom. The shelves seemed random, the labels made no sense. But over weeks of night shifts I *gradually* learned the logic — noodles by weight, drinks by sugar content, snacks by the day they arrived. Tonight I found the right box in under ten seconds. Tang gave me a quiet nod.
gradually:0.cnHint: 我刚来时完全摸不清仓库的规律，但经过几周的夜班，我____掌握了其中的逻辑。
gradually:0.hook: Tang's own system was slightly different from the Manager's written rules.
gradually:0.line: 'You *gradually* get a feel for where everything lives — it just takes a few weeks of honest looking.'

incentive:0.en: The Manager announced a small bonus for whichever shift sold the most hot food in the week before the new store opened. Tang immediately began suggesting meat buns to every customer who came near the counter. 'Competition is fine,' she told me cheerfully, 'but a clear *incentive* makes everything move faster.' By Thursday we were winning.
incentive:0.cnHint: 店长宣布了一个奖励方案，这个____让同事立刻开始积极向顾客推荐热食。
incentive:0.hook: Lin from across the street had heard about the bonus too.
incentive:0.line: 'A small *incentive* does more than a long speech — watch how fast the hot food shelf empties tonight.'

relax:0.en: The new branch opens in three days, and the Manager has barely slept. Tonight he drops onto the stool behind the counter, closes his eyes, and lets out a long breath. 'Just five minutes,' he says. I watch him *relax* for exactly four minutes and fifty seconds before his phone buzzes again.
relax:0.cnHint: 店长在新店开业前夕终于在柜台后__了片刻。
relax:0.hook: The number on his screen makes his face go very still.
relax:0.line: 'I just need to *relax* for five minutes — then back to work.'

release:0.en: A delivery driver drops off a tower of boxes for the new branch stock. One box hisses. Tang and I stare at it. Slowly, Tang lifts the flap and we both jump back — a trapped sparrow flaps out into the store. Tang laughs. 'We had to *release* it,' she says, watching the bird find the open door.
release:0.cnHint: 一只小鸟被关在货箱里，阿糖把它____了出来。
release:0.hook: But something else was moving at the bottom of that box.
release:0.line: 'We should *release* it before it hurts itself.'

route:0.en: Lin shows up at midnight carrying a city map, spreading it flat on the drinks fridge. She is planning delivery *routes* for the new branch. 'Shortest path, lowest cost,' she mutters, drawing lines with a red pen. I offer her a cup of hot water. She does not look up. She circles one street twice.
route:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在地图上规划新店的配送____，反复圈了同一条街。
route:0.hook: That circled street is where our store's best customer lives.
route:0.line: 'This *route* cuts twenty minutes off every morning run.'

sight:0.en: The Manager unrolls a poster of the new branch and pins it to the wall. It shows a bright shop front, clean windows, and a long queue of smiling customers. Tang whistles softly. The *sight* of it makes even me feel proud, and I have only worked here two weeks. The Manager pats the poster like an old friend.
sight:0.cnHint: 新店的海报贴出来，那幅____让大家都感到自豪。
sight:0.hook: One face in the painted crowd looks exactly like Lin.
sight:0.line: 'The *sight* of a full queue on day one — that is the dream.'

speaker:0.en: The Manager sets up a small wireless *speaker* on the shelf above the register, testing the sound system for the new branch opening party. It plays a cheerful tune at full volume. Every customer who walks in stops and blinks. One old man starts tapping his foot. The Manager grins and turns it up one more notch.
speaker:0.cnHint: 店长在收银台上方测试____，整个便利店都充满了欢快的音乐。
speaker:0.hook: The old man has not left, and he is now humming along.
speaker:0.line: 'I ordered the same *speaker* model for both branches.'

species:0.en: A biology student comes in at 2 a.m. clutching a notebook. She needs tape to fix a torn page of pressed flowers. As I hand it over, she explains that each flower is a different *species* collected near the river — all for a class project about the new development area where our second branch will open.
species:0.cnHint: 一位学生拿着笔记本来买胶带，解释本子里每朵花都是不同的____。
species:0.hook: She says one of the flowers only grows in one specific spot in the city.
species:0.line: 'Each *species* here could disappear once the construction starts.'

specifically:0.en: Tang reads the Manager's instruction sheet for the new branch setup and frowns. 'He says the cups go on the left shelf.' She reads it again. 'No — he *specifically* says the large cups go on the left and the small ones go under the counter.' We both look at the pile of boxes. There are three sizes.
specifically:0.cnHint: 阿糖仔细读完说明，发现店长____指定了大杯子的摆放位置。
specifically:0.hook: The third size is not mentioned anywhere in the instructions.
specifically:0.line: 'He *specifically* wrote large cups on the left — look, right here.'

unfortunately:0.en: The Manager announces the new branch will open on Friday. Everyone cheers. Then he checks his phone and his smile fades. '*Unfortunately*,' he says, setting the phone face-down on the counter, 'the sign is not ready.' Tang asks how we open a shop with no sign. The Manager picks up the phone again and says nothing.
unfortunately:0.cnHint: 店长宣布新店周五开业，但____告诉大家招牌还没做好。
unfortunately:0.hook: He then sends a message to someone whose name I do not recognise.
unfortunately:0.line: '*Unfortunately*, the sign maker says it will be two more days.'

consultant:0.en: The Manager spread a big map across the counter and pointed at three street corners. 'We are opening new stores,' he said proudly. A woman in a sharp coat leaned over and circled one spot. She was a *consultant*, hired to decide which location would make the most money. I watched her red pen and wondered if our quiet corner was safe.
consultant:0.cnHint: 店长请来一位____，帮忙决定新店开在哪个街角最合适。
consultant:0.hook: Her red pen hovered over our corner for a long moment.
consultant:0.line: 'As your *consultant*, I must be honest — this corner earns the least.'

direct:0.en: The Manager called a meeting before my shift and looked at each of us in turn. Then he gave Tang and me our new jobs for the branch plan. My role was *direct* — I would train the new staff at the second store. Tang got a harder task and said nothing. I noticed Tang's hands tighten around a coffee cup.
direct:0.cnHint: 店长宣布了新店计划，给每个人____分配了任务。
direct:0.hook: Tang set the cup down a little too hard.
direct:0.line: 'Your role is *direct* — you train the new team, starting Monday.'

discourage:0.en: Lin walked in just before dawn and bought nothing, only studied our shelves with a small notebook. The Manager watched from the back room. 'Do not let it *discourage* you,' he told me quietly. 'Lin does this before every new store opens.' I smiled and tidied the snack rack, but my hands moved a little faster than usual.
discourage:0.cnHint: 竞争对手林来店里观察，店长叫我不要被____。
discourage:0.hook: Lin paused at the door and took one last slow look around.
discourage:0.line: 'Do not let this *discourage* you — we have something Lin cannot copy.'

essentially:0.en: Tang explained the new branch plan to me during a slow hour. Two stores, same products, same green sign, same late hours. '*Essentially*, we are one store split across two corners,' Tang said, refilling the hot drinks machine. It sounded simple. But the consultant's circled map was still on the counter, and one corner was not ours.
essentially:0.cnHint: 唐向我解释，两家新店____上是同一家店分成了两个地点。
essentially:0.hook: I looked at the map again and noticed a third circle, very faint.
essentially:0.line: '*Essentially*, both stores share one soul — that is the Manager's plan.'

extent:0.en: A regular customer who always buys warm milk stopped at the door and stared at the new poster about the second store. 'To what *extent* will things change here?' she asked me, looking almost worried. I told her the night snacks would stay the same. She relaxed a little, paid, and left. She had been coming here for three years, Tang told me later.
extent:0.cnHint: 一位常客问我，开新店会在多大____上改变这里。
extent:0.hook: She stopped once outside and looked back through the glass.
extent:0.line: 'To what *extent* will the old store change once the new one opens?'

finance:0.en: The Manager stayed late, bent over a thick folder. Tang whispered that the folder held all the numbers for the new branch. '*Finance* for a second store is not easy,' Tang said, topping up the cold drinks fridge. I nodded and watched the Manager turn pages slowly, pressing a finger against a row of figures as if asking them a question.
finance:0.cnHint: 店长在深夜研究新店的____报告，数字让他皱起了眉头。
finance:0.hook: He closed the folder, then opened it again.
finance:0.line: 'The *finance* looks tight, but I believe we can make it work.'

freedom:0.en: After the Manager pinned the new branch plan on the wall, he turned to me with a small smile. 'At the second store you will have more *freedom*,' he said. 'Choose the snack display yourself.' I felt a warm jump in my chest. Tang caught my eye and gave a quiet nod, as if they already knew what I would choose to put in the front row.
freedom:0.cnHint: 店长告诉我，在新店我将有更多的____，可以自己决定陈列方式。
freedom:0.hook: Tang mouthed two words at me: 'Spicy chips.'
freedom:0.line: 'You will have the *freedom* to arrange the new store your own way.'

highlight:0.en: The Manager asked me to write a small sign for the window about the coming second store. I kept it short. Tang read it and said the best part was the last line about the all-night hours. 'That is the real *highlight*,' Tang said, tapping the glass. A man passing outside slowed down, read the sign, and took a photo with his phone.
highlight:0.cnHint: 我为新店写了宣传牌，唐说全天营业是整个计划最____的部分。
highlight:0.hook: The man outside looked up at the store name, then walked away quickly.
highlight:0.line: 'The all-night hours are the true *highlight* of our new branch plan.'

himself:0.en: The Manager arrived an hour before opening to arrange the new branch store display *himself*. He moved every shelf, tested every light, and counted every price tag twice. 'Nobody else will care as much,' he muttered, stepping back to look at the neat rows with quiet pride.
himself:0.cnHint: 店长亲自动手布置新分店，不让别人插手。
himself:0.hook: But one shelf still hid a very old secret.

landscape:0.en: A large framed print of a river *landscape* hung on the back wall of the new branch. The Manager had carried it from home on the bus. Customers kept stopping to stare at the soft green hills and slow water, forgetting for a moment they had come in for instant noodles.
landscape:0.cnHint: 新分店墙上挂着一幅____，顾客们看得入了迷。
landscape:0.hook: Nobody noticed the tiny figure hiding in the painted hills.
landscape:0.line: 'That *landscape* makes people calm — good for sales.'

mentally:0.en: Lin walked every aisle of the new branch, *mentally* counting shelves and comparing prices with her own shop across the street. She said nothing, only nodded slowly. Tang watched her lips move in silence and whispered to me, 'She is already planning something. That look never means good news.'
mentally:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在新分店里悄悄____盘算，让阿糖感到不安。
mentally:0.hook: Her small smile at the door said everything.
mentally:0.line: 'I am *mentally* noting every price on these shelves.'

neither:0.en: Tang offered the Manager two suggested names for the new branch, written on a napkin. The Manager read both, folded the napkin slowly, and said *neither* name felt right. Tang stared at the ceiling. I stared at my shoes. Outside, rain began to tap softly on the window.
neither:0.cnHint: 店长觉得阿糖提的两个名字____合适，气氛一时尴尬。
neither:0.hook: Then the Manager smiled and pulled out his own napkin.
neither:0.line: '*Neither* of your names is bad — they are just not right.'

onto:0.en: I carried a heavy box of drinks and slid it *onto* the low shelf near the door. The box hit the shelf perfectly, not one bottle fell. Tang clapped once, softly, like I had done something great. It was a small thing, but in a new store on its first night, small things felt large.
onto:0.cnHint: 我把一箱饮料稳稳推____货架，阿糖为此鼓了掌。
onto:0.hook: Then I noticed the shelf was not fixed to the wall.
onto:0.line: 'Slide the next box *onto* that shelf, same as before.'

plus:0.en: The Manager wrote the first day's total on a notepad: drinks sold, *plus* snacks, plus hot food from the little warmer by the door. He added each line slowly, then turned the pad to show us. Tang pumped a fist. I felt something warm rise in my chest. The number was small but real.
plus:0.cnHint: 店长把各类商品的销售额____在一起，给大家看总收入。
plus:0.hook: One row of numbers, however, did not add up.
plus:0.line: 'Drinks *plus* snacks already beat my first-day guess.'

root:0.en: An old regular found us at the new branch and looked surprised, then pleased. 'You followed me here,' she joked, setting her basket on the counter. Tang told her the Manager had chosen this corner because a very old *root* of a big tree marked the spot on an old neighbourhood map. She touched the wall gently.
root:0.cnHint: 老顾客得知新分店的选址与一棵老树的____有关，轻轻摸了摸墙。
root:0.hook: She whispered that the tree had been her grandfather's.
root:0.line: 'The *root* of that old tree is still under this floor.'

satisfy:0.en: A student bought three rice balls, then stood at the counter looking unsure. 'Will that *satisfy* you?' Tang asked, already reaching for a warm meat bun. The student blinked, then nodded. Tang bagged the bun too without being asked. I made a note to myself: watch how Tang reads people. It was worth learning.
satisfy:0.cnHint: 阿糖看出顾客没吃____，主动多拿了一个肉包。
satisfy:0.hook: The student came back twenty minutes later, alone and smiling.
satisfy:0.line: 'Three rice balls will not *satisfy* you — take this bun too.'

somewhat:0.en: The Manager spread blueprints across the counter at midnight. 'The new branch will look like this store,' he said, tapping a square on the paper. I studied the drawing. It was *somewhat* different from our shop — a little wider, a little brighter — but the same warm feeling came through.
somewhat:0.cnHint: 店长深夜拿出新分店的图纸，我发现它和我们店____不同。
somewhat:0.hook: Then he pointed to a name tag on the blueprint — mine.
somewhat:0.line: 'It is *somewhat* larger than this store, but the spirit is the same.'

stable:0.en: Tang was measuring the stockroom shelves with a tape. 'The Manager wants everything ready before the new branch opens,' she said. She pressed a wobbly shelf and frowned. 'This one is not *stable* — if it falls, the bottles are gone.' We spent an hour fixing every bracket together.
stable:0.cnHint: 唐在检查储物架时，发现有一个架子不____，担心瓶子会掉落。
stable:0.hook: Behind the last shelf, Tang found a small locked box.
stable:0.line: 'Make sure the shelf is *stable* before you stack anything on it.'

lower:0.en: The Manager stands on a ladder, rearranging the top shelf. 'We need to move these tea boxes *lower*,' she says, pointing. 'Customers can't reach them up here.' I hold the ladder steady while she works. When she climbs down, she wipes her hands and smiles. 'Good teamwork.' Through the window, I notice Lin across the street, watching our store again.
lower:0.cnHint: 店长让我把茶叶盒挪到____的位置，方便顾客拿取。
lower:0.hook: Lin has been watching us for three nights now.
lower:0.line: 'We need to move these tea boxes *lower*,' she says, pointing.

naturally:0.en: Tang arrives early for his shift, carrying a small plant. 'For the counter,' he explains, setting it down. 'Plants *naturally* make a place feel better.' The tiny green leaves brighten the corner immediately. The Manager walks in, sees it, and nods with approval. 'Nice touch.' But then a customer enters—someone I've never seen before—and freezes when they spot Tang.
naturally:0.cnHint: 阿糖说植物能____地让空间变得更舒服。
naturally:0.hook: The stranger's face goes pale at the sight of Tang.
naturally:0.line: 'Plants *naturally* make a place feel better,' he explains.

passionate:0.en: A young customer asks about our instant noodles. Tang lights up and begins explaining each brand with detail and excitement. 'He's very *passionate* about noodles,' I whisper to the Manager. She laughs quietly. Tang describes flavors, cooking times, even the history of certain recipes. The customer looks amazed—and a little overwhelmed. Finally, they buy five different kinds. After they leave, Tang's phone rings. His smile disappears.
passionate:0.cnHint: 阿糖对方便面非常____，能讲很多细节。
passionate:0.hook: Tang's expression changes completely when he answers the call.
passionate:0.line: 'He's very *passionate* about noodles,' I whisper to the Manager.

pop:0.en: I'm restocking drinks when a can suddenly rolls off the shelf and I catch it. The Manager sees this and grins. 'Quick hands!' The radio plays quiet *pop* music while we work. It's a peaceful night—until Lin walks in, not as a spy this time, but as a customer. She picks up a carton of milk, walks to the counter, and looks directly at me.
pop:0.cnHint: 收音机里播放着安静的____音乐。
pop:0.hook: Lin is standing at my counter, waiting to pay.
pop:0.line: The radio plays quiet *pop* music while we work.

possibly:0.en: The Manager counts the cash register carefully. 'We're short by twenty yuan,' she says, frowning. 'Could it *possibly* be a counting mistake?' I suggest. We recount together—still short. Tang checks the receipts. 'Everything matches,' he confirms. The Manager sighs but doesn't blame anyone. Then I remember: a man paid with a strange bill earlier. I didn't check it closely enough.
possibly:0.hook: That strange bill might not have been real money.
possibly:0.line: 'Could it *possibly* be a counting mistake?' I suggest.

previously:0.en: An older woman comes in and looks around with confusion. 'This place has changed,' she says. 'I worked here *previously*, many years ago. It was different then.' The Manager offers her tea and they talk about the old days. I listen while cleaning. The woman smiles at memories, then asks, 'Is Mr. Chen still the owner?' The Manager's face goes still. 'He passed away last spring.'
previously:0.cnHint: 老太太说她____在这里工作过。
previously:0.hook: The woman's eyes fill with tears she doesn't explain.
previously:0.line: 'I worked here *previously*, many years ago,' she says.

profession:0.en: A man in a suit buys coffee at 2 AM. 'Late night?' I ask. 'My *profession* keeps strange hours,' he replies with a tired smile. 'I'm a doctor.' We chat briefly about night shifts. He seems kind. As he leaves, I notice he's left his hospital ID badge on the counter. I call out, but he's already gone. The name on the badge reads: Dr. Lin.
profession:0.cnHint: 那个男人说他的____让他工作时间很奇怪，他是医生。
profession:0.hook: His last name is the same as our competitor's.
profession:0.line: 'My *profession* keeps strange hours,' he replies with a tired smile.

readily:0.en: Tang offers to cover my shift tomorrow so I can rest. 'I'll do it *readily*,' he says. 'You've helped me plenty of times.' I thank him, grateful for such a good coworker. The Manager overhears and smiles approvingly. Just then, the door chimes—Lin enters again, but this time she's carrying a large envelope. She walks straight to the Manager and places it on the counter without a word.
readily:0.cnHint: 阿糖很____地答应替我换班。
readily:0.hook: What's inside the envelope Lin just delivered?

invite:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, handing out small cards to people walking by. 'We're opening a second store next week,' he told me proudly. He wanted to *invite* everyone in the neighbourhood to come and see it. By midnight, his whole stack of cards was gone.
invite:1.cnHint: 店长站在街上，向路人发卡，想____附近所有人来参加新店开业。
invite:1.hook: But one person quietly dropped the card into a bin without reading it.
invite:1.line: 'I want to *invite* every neighbour to our grand opening next week.'

million:1.en: Lin appeared across the street, taping a bright sign to the window of their new store. Tang leaned on our doorframe and whistled. 'That corner spot costs a *million* to rent for a year,' Tang said. I stared at the sign and suddenly felt a little nervous for our quiet little shop.
million:1.cnHint: 阿糖看着对面隔壁咖啡店的林的新店，说那个角落的店面租金高达____。
million:1.hook: The sign on Lin's window said the store would open at exactly midnight tomorrow.
million:1.line: 'That corner costs almost a *million* a year — how are they doing it?'

represent:1.en: The Manager called us outside to look at the new sign above our door. It was a small golden star inside a circle. 'This star will *represent* our store in the whole city,' he said, standing very straight. A man passing by stopped, looked up, and nodded slowly as if he agreed.
represent:1.cnHint: 店长让大家看新招牌，说那个图案将____整家店在全城的形象。
represent:1.hook: The same man came back an hour later and stood outside without coming in.
represent:1.line: 'This little star will *represent* everything we stand for as a store.'

surprise:1.en: I was sweeping the pavement outside when a small moving truck stopped in front of the empty shop next door. Workers began carrying in shelves. Tang came out and gasped. The *surprise* on his face was so clear that a passing cyclist almost stopped to ask what was wrong.
surprise:1.cnHint: 看到隔壁空店突然开始装修进货，阿糖脸上写满了____。
surprise:1.hook: One of the workers looked over and gave me a careful, unreadable smile.
surprise:1.line: 'What a *surprise* — I had no idea anyone had rented that place.'

topic:1.en: Three neighbours gathered near our magazine stand outside, talking loudly. I stepped out to tidy the rack and caught every word. The new store opening down the street was the only *topic* they cared about. One old man kept repeating that change was never good for a quiet corner like this.
topic:1.cnHint: 街坊们聚在外面热烈讨论，新店开业成了大家唯一的____。
topic:1.hook: The old man then turned and looked directly at me with a complicated expression.
topic:1.line: 'The new shop is the only *topic* anyone around here wants to talk about.'

meat:1.en: I was restocking the shelf outside our door when a woman in an apron rushed over from the small restaurant next door. She grabbed a tin from the rack and held it up. 'No *meat* left in my kitchen!' she cried. She paid quickly and ran back. I had never seen anyone move so fast at two in the morning.
meat:1.cnHint: 隔壁餐馆的阿姨跑来店门口，说厨房里的____用完了，急着买。
meat:1.hook: She paused at the corner, turned back, and bought three more tins without a word.
meat:1.line: 'No *meat* left — give me everything you have on that shelf, please.'

drink:1.en: After the Manager put out a small table and two chairs on the pavement, he sat me down with a paper cup of warm tea. 'Always *drink* something hot when the night air is cold,' he said kindly. Then he stood up, straightened his jacket, and walked alone to the corner to study the street.
drink:1.cnHint: 店长在店门外摆了桌椅，叫我在夜里寒风中____点热东西暖身。
drink:1.hook: He stood at that corner for a long time, not moving, just watching something I could not see.
drink:1.line: 'Always *drink* something warm — the night shift is longer than you think.'

sleep:1.en: At five in the morning the street was perfectly still. I sat on the step outside and felt my eyes grow heavy. I had almost managed to *sleep* for one minute when Tang appeared with two cups of coffee and a grin. 'Not yet,' he said cheerfully. Down the road, a light turned on inside Lin's new store.
sleep:1.cnHint: 快天亮时我坐在门口几乎____着了，阿糖端着咖啡出现把我叫醒。
sleep:1.hook: The light in Lin's store stayed on, and a shadow moved slowly behind the glass.
sleep:1.line: 'You can *sleep* when the sun is up — right now, someone down the road is still busy.'

satisfaction:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new store site at dawn, hands on hips, studying the empty shopfront. Workers had just finished cleaning the windows. He let out a slow breath and smiled. 'This is real *satisfaction*,' he said quietly — the kind that only comes after months of hard work and worry.
satisfaction:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店门口，看着刚打扫干净的橱窗，心中感到____。
satisfaction:1.hook: But a shadow moved behind the clean glass.
satisfaction:1.line: 'This is real *satisfaction* — the kind you can't buy.'

cultivate:1.en: Lin walked the block around the new store three times before opening day, greeting every neighbour with a small bow and a free sample. 'You have to *cultivate* goodwill before you open the door,' she told me, pressing a tiny packet of snacks into an old woman's hands with both of hers.
cultivate:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在新店开业前挨家挨户送试吃品，努力____与街坊的好关系。
cultivate:1.hook: The old woman pocketed the snack and said nothing — yet.
cultivate:1.line: 'You have to *cultivate* goodwill before you open the door.'

productive:1.en: Tang and I spent the morning arranging shelves on the pavement outside the new store. By noon every shelf was full, every label faced front, and two locals had already asked about the opening date. Tang wiped her hands and grinned. 'Probably the most *productive* morning I've had all year,' she said.
productive:1.cnHint: 阿糖和我在新店门外整理货架，忙碌了一上午，觉得这是____的一天。
productive:1.hook: Then the Manager appeared with a longer list of tasks.
productive:1.line: 'Probably the most *productive* morning I've had all year.'

vision:1.en: The Manager unrolled a large paper plan on the bonnet of his car and pointed at a hand-drawn map of the street. 'My *vision* is one store on every key corner in this district within three years,' he said. His finger traced a confident circle. None of us said a word.
vision:1.cnHint: 店长在车盖上展开地图，描述他对未来扩店的____。
vision:1.hook: Lin caught my eye and raised one eyebrow slightly.
vision:1.line: 'My *vision* is one store on every key corner here.'

distance:1.en: From the pavement I could see our original store glowing at the far end of the street. The new site sat at the other end. Tang measured the *distance* with her eyes and said it was close enough for one manager to cover both — which explained why the Manager looked so tired lately.
distance:1.cnHint: 阿糖目测了新旧两家店之间的____，明白了为何店长最近总是疲惫不堪。
distance:1.hook: The Manager's phone rang before she finished the sentence.
distance:1.line: 'The *distance* is small enough — the workload is not.'

forward:1.en: On the morning the new store sign went up, a small crowd gathered outside. The Manager stepped *forward* from the group, cleared his throat, and thanked the neighbours for their patience during the noisy building work. Everyone clapped. A child in the front row clapped the loudest and longest of all.
forward:1.cnHint: 新店招牌挂上的那天早上，店长从人群中走出来致辞，大家鼓掌庆祝。
forward:1.hook: The child then asked if there would be free ice cream.
forward:1.line: 'Allow me to step *forward* and say thank you to everyone.'

harmful:1.en: A man stopped me on the street and pushed a flyer into my hand, claiming the new store's bright night lighting was *harmful* to the sleep of nearby residents. He spoke loudly, but the neighbours behind him all looked rather unbothered, watching us with mild, sleepy curiosity from their doorsteps.
harmful:1.cnHint: 一名男子在街上向我抱怨，称新店夜间灯光对附近居民____。
harmful:1.hook: He pointed at one resident, who was visibly napping outside.
harmful:1.line: 'Bright lights at night are *harmful* to the whole street's sleep.'

impossible:1.en: Lin and I tried to assemble a tall display stand outside the new store without the instructions. After forty minutes it leaned at a worrying angle. 'It's not *impossible*,' Lin said, more to herself than to me, giving the frame one last firm push. It straightened — then slowly leaned again.
impossible:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林和我在新店外组装展示架，歪了又扶，隔壁咖啡店的林坚持说这并非____。
impossible:1.hook: The Manager arrived just in time to watch it fall completely.
impossible:1.line: 'It's not *impossible* — we just need one more try.'

meaning:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, staring at the empty shopfront. 'We have been here fifteen years,' he said quietly. 'This street gave our store its *meaning*.' He touched the dusty glass, and for a moment the whole busy plan of opening a second store felt very small against that history.
meaning:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店门口，感慨这条街赋予小店____。
meaning:1.hook: Then he noticed someone watching from across the street.
