meaning:1.line: 'This street gave our store its *meaning*, and I will not forget that.'

strengthen:1.en: Tang swept the pavement in front of the new branch on a cool morning. The Manager had said that a clean entrance would *strengthen* the store's image in the neighbourhood. Tang worked the broom in long, careful strokes, watching early commuters slow down to read the opening-soon sign with curious eyes.
strengthen:1.cnHint: 唐打扫新分店门前，希望整洁的门面能____小店在街坊中的印象。
strengthen:1.hook: One commuter stopped and did not move on.
strengthen:1.line: 'A clean front will *strengthen* our image before we even open the door.'

competitive:1.en: Lin arrived at the corner and studied the rival shop two doors away. Its window was full of bright signs and low-price tags. 'The market here is very *competitive*,' Lin muttered, pulling out a small notebook to write down every price. The Manager needed real numbers before deciding whether the new branch could survive.
competitive:1.cnHint: 林站在街角，打量两门之隔的对手，感叹这里的市场太____了。
competitive:1.hook: The rival shop's door swung open just as Lin finished writing.
competitive:1.line: 'The market here is very *competitive*, so we must do better than just match their prices.'

recently:1.en: Tang stood outside the new branch holding a stack of flyers. 'Have you *recently* walked the whole block?' the Manager asked, appearing beside him. Tang shook his head. The Manager pointed down the street, where three other small shops had put up closing-down notices. The neighbourhood was changing faster than either of them had guessed.
recently:1.cnHint: 店长问唐有没有____逛过整条街，结果发现街上变化惊人。
recently:1.hook: At the far end of the block, a large new store was under construction.
recently:1.line: 'Have you *recently* walked the whole street? You might be surprised at what you find.'

nation:1.en: A traveller stopped Lin outside the new branch and asked for directions in careful, textbook English. 'This *nation* has so many kinds of convenience stores,' the traveller said, looking around with wide eyes. 'Back home we have nothing open at night.' Lin smiled, suddenly feeling a small, unexpected pride in something so ordinary as a lit-up shop.
nation:1.cnHint: 一位旅客在店门外感叹，这个____的便利店文化令人印象深刻。
nation:1.hook: The traveller took a photo of the shopfront before walking away.
nation:1.line: 'This *nation* surprised me — a warm, bright shop open every single night.'

perceive:1.en: Lin walked the street around the new branch at dusk, trying to *perceive* the mood of the neighbourhood. Some residents hurried past without a glance. Others slowed, reading the opening sign, lips moving. A few nodded approvingly. Lin wrote it all down, knowing that what people felt before the doors even opened would shape the store's whole future.
perceive:1.cnHint: 林黄昏时在新分店周边游走，努力____街坊对新店的感受。
perceive:1.hook: One elderly resident stopped and asked a question Lin had not expected.
perceive:1.line: 'I try to *perceive* what the neighbours feel before we open a single box.'

pound:1.en: Tang carried a heavy box of stock down the pavement toward the new branch. Each step made him *pound* the ground with tired feet. 'How many more boxes?' he called out. The Manager appeared at the door, took one look at Tang's red face, and silently picked up the other end of the box without saying a word.
pound:1.cnHint: 唐扛着沉重的箱子走向新分店，每一步都____着地面。
pound:1.hook: Inside, something in the next box shifted with a strange clink.
pound:1.line: 'My feet *pound* the ground with every step — these boxes are not kind.'

purpose:1.en: The Manager locked up the new branch late at night and stood alone on the empty street. Opening a second store had seemed so clear months ago, but now doubt crept in. Then he saw the light in the original store window further down the road, warm and steady. That small glow reminded him of every *purpose* he had started with.
purpose:1.cnHint: 店长独自站在新分店门外，那盏老店的灯光让他想起了创业的____。
purpose:1.hook: His phone buzzed — it was a message from an unknown number.
purpose:1.line: 'That old light down the road reminds me of every *purpose* I began with.'

respond:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, holding a sign that read 'GRAND OPENING SOON.' Passers-by slowed down. One old man stopped and asked if the store would be open all night. The Manager smiled and *responded* with a firm nod: every light on the street would always have a home here.
respond:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口举牌，一位老人停下来问他，他____了对方的问题。
respond:1.hook: But the old man's next question made the Manager go pale.
respond:1.line: 'I always *respond* to my neighbours — that is how trust is built.'

welcome:1.en: Red banners hung across the front of the new branch. Tang swept the pavement outside and watched curious faces gather at the glass. A little girl pressed her nose against the window. Tang waved her in. The warm light and smell of fresh bread made every person feel like a true *welcome* surprise.
welcome:1.cnHint: 新店门口挂起红色横幅，阿糖在外面打扫时发现街坊们纷纷聚拢，感受到一种真正的____。
welcome:1.hook: Then Tang noticed one face in the crowd that did not look happy at all.
welcome:1.line: 'A real *welcome* starts before anyone even walks through the door.'

appeal:1.en: Lin arrived early and chalked a colourful menu on a small board outside. Locals stopped to read it. The hand-drawn pictures of rice balls and hot drinks had a quiet *appeal* that no printed poster could match. Even a delivery driver parked his bike and took a long, hungry look.
appeal:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外用粉笔画了一块菜单板，朴素的手绘风格有一种独特的____，吸引了路人驻足。
appeal:1.hook: One customer photographed the board and walked away without saying a word.
appeal:1.line: 'Hand-drawn signs have an *appeal* that money just cannot print.'

finally:1.en: The permit notice had been stuck to the wall for three weeks. Every morning the Manager checked the post box. Every evening he went home empty-handed. Then, on a grey Tuesday, a thin envelope arrived. He tore it open on the pavement. The branch was *finally* approved. He let out a long, slow breath.
finally:1.cnHint: 等待许可证的日子漫长而煎熬，店长每天查看信箱，这一天____等到了批准通知。
finally:1.hook: Inside the envelope, however, was a second, smaller sheet of paper.
finally:1.line: 'We are *finally* open — I almost did not believe this day would come.'

guess:1.en: A woman paused outside the half-finished branch and peered at the logo on the glass. She tilted her head left, then right. 'Convenience store?' she asked her friend. Her friend shrugged. Tang, painting the door frame nearby, smiled but said nothing. He liked letting people *guess* before the sign went up.
guess:1.cnHint: 一位女士在新店玻璃前左看右看，试图____这里将会开什么店，阿糖在一旁偷乐。
guess:1.hook: Her third guess was so wrong that Tang nearly dropped his paintbrush.
guess:1.line: 'Go on, *guess* — I will tell you if you are close.'

protection:1.en: Rain arrived without warning on the morning of the soft opening. Tang rushed outside and held a wide umbrella over the small table of free samples. The Manager brought out a canvas sheet for *protection* against the wind. A boy on a bicycle slowed down, grabbed a sample cake, and rode off grinning.
protection:1.cnHint: 开业当天突然下雨，阿糖和店长赶忙为门口的试吃台提供____，一个骑车的男孩顺手拿走了蛋糕。
protection:1.hook: The boy rode back ten minutes later, bringing five friends with him.
protection:1.line: 'This canvas is our *protection* — the samples must stay dry.'

resident:1.en: An elderly woman stopped in front of the new branch and read the address board twice. She had lived on this street for forty years. 'Another shop,' she said quietly. Tang offered her a free coffee. She took it, sat on the low wall outside, and admitted she was glad a *resident* place finally had good light.
resident:1.cnHint: 一位在这条街住了四十年的老奶奶在新店前驻足，作为老____，她对这里多了一盏好灯表示欣慰。
resident:1.hook: She then asked Tang one question that stopped him completely.
resident:1.line: 'As a long-time *resident*, I notice every change on this street.'

willing:1.en: The Manager needed someone to hand out flyers on the corner before sunrise. Tang had the early shift already. Lin had a stock delivery. The Manager looked at both of them and asked quietly if either was *willing* to come in just thirty minutes early. There was a short silence. Then both raised a hand.
willing:1.cnHint: 店长需要有人天亮前在街角发传单，他轻声问阿糖和隔壁咖啡店的林谁____提前来，两人都举起了手。
willing:1.hook: Neither of them knew the other had also said yes.
willing:1.line: 'I am *willing* — just make sure the coffee is ready when I arrive.'

shop:1.en: The Manager led me outside just before dawn to see the corner across the street. A new *shop* had appeared overnight — its windows dark, its sign still covered with paper. 'Watch that place,' the Manager said quietly, hands in his pockets. I watched. Nothing moved. But the lights inside flickered once.
shop:1.cnHint: 店长带我到街对面，指着一家新出现的____，神情凝重。
shop:1.hook: The paper sign came down at exactly midnight.
shop:1.line: 'That *shop* was empty last week — someone moved in very fast.'

electronic:1.en: Just after two in the morning a delivery van stopped outside. Two workers carried in a large box covered in stickers — *electronic* parts, by the look of it. They carried it straight into the building next door without a word. Tang leaned over the counter beside me and whispered, 'That is the third box this week.'
electronic:1.cnHint: 深夜，一辆货车把贴满标签的____零件箱搬进了隔壁。
electronic:1.hook: Nobody had rented that building last month.
electronic:1.line: 'All those *electronic* parts arriving at night — that feels strange to me.'

wild:1.en: A cat showed up on the front step at three in the morning — thin, yellow, and clearly *wild*, with careful eyes that trusted no one. I put a small piece of bread near the door. It did not run. It sat perfectly still and stared at the building across the street for a long time, as if it knew something I did not.
wild:1.cnHint: 一只____的流浪猫出现在门口，目不转睛地盯着对面的建筑。
wild:1.hook: The cat was gone before I could look away.
wild:1.line: 'A *wild* cat sitting still that long — something nearby must have scared it.'

rich:1.en: A well-dressed woman came in just before five in the morning and bought only a small cup of instant noodles. She paid with a large note and waved away the change. The street outside smelled *rich* with rain and wet leaves. She stood at the window eating slowly, watching the covered shop across the road with quiet, steady eyes.
rich:1.cnHint: 一位衣着考究的女士买了碗泡面，站在窗边盯着对面____气息笼罩的街道。
rich:1.hook: She came back the next three mornings at the same time.
rich:1.line: 'The smell out there is so *rich* tonight — rain always brings out the truth.'

special:1.en: Lin appeared at the door just after six, which was strange because Lin ran a store two blocks away and we were, politely speaking, not friends. He bought nothing. He only looked around slowly and said there was nothing *special* about our store at all. He smiled when he said it. I did not like that smile.
special:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林走进来，称这家店没有什么____之处，但他的笑让人不安。
special:1.hook: Lin glanced at the new building across the street before he left.
special:1.line: 'Nothing *special* here — I was just walking past, that is all.'

text:1.en: My phone lit up at four in the morning. It was a *text* from the Manager: 'Do not accept any deliveries addressed to the building next door. Do not ask questions.' I read it twice. Outside, the street was perfectly quiet. I typed back, 'Understood.' Three dots appeared. Then nothing. He never replied.
text:1.cnHint: 凌晨四点，店长发来一条____，叫我不要接收发往隔壁的快递。
text:1.hook: The Manager's last message timestamp never changed after that night.
text:1.line: 'I sent you a *text* — did it come through? Check it carefully, please.'

front:1.en: Tang pointed out that the new building across the street had no sign on its *front* at all — no name, no number, no hours. Most shops put something on the door, even a small paper note. This one had nothing. 'Maybe they are not open yet,' I said. Tang gave me a look. 'Or maybe they do not want to be found,' she said.
front:1.cnHint: 阿糖指出对面新楼的____什么标志都没有，这让人觉得奇怪。
front:1.hook: That morning, a small camera appeared above their door.
front:1.line: 'Look at the *front* of that place — not a single word anywhere on it.'

law:1.en: A tired man in a plain jacket came in just before sunrise and bought coffee. He left a small card on the counter without a word. It said he was an officer of the *law* and that if anyone asked unusual questions about the building across the street, I should call the number on the back. He was gone before I could say anything at all.
law:1.cnHint: 一名____人员在天亮前悄悄来到店里，留下了一张名片就离开了。
law:1.hook: The number on the back was not a local area code.
law:1.line: 'I work for the *law* — just keep this card and do not mention my visit.'

thinking:1.en: The Manager spread a large map across the hood of her car outside and stared at it for a long time. 'This corner gets the most foot traffic at night,' she said quietly. Her *thinking* was clear: a second store, right across the bridge. I watched her trace the route with one finger and say nothing more.
thinking:1.cnHint: 店长在店外研究地图，她的____指向了开第二家分店的可能。
thinking:1.hook: She folded the map and made one short phone call.
thinking:1.line: 'My *thinking* is simple — more people walk that bridge than this street.'

cover:1.en: Tang taped a big sheet of paper over the window where the new branch floor plan was drawn. 'We don't want Lin to see it,' he whispered. The *cover* worked until a gust of wind pulled one corner loose, and Lin, passing outside, slowed her steps and tilted her head.
cover:1.cnHint: 阿糖用纸____住了窗上的分店计划图，但风偏偏不配合。
cover:1.hook: Lin smiled at the flapping paper and kept walking.
cover:1.line: 'This *cover* will hold — just add one more strip of tape.'

earth:1.en: The Manager knelt on the pavement outside and pressed her palm flat to the ground. 'Good corner,' she said. 'Solid *earth*, not too much sand.' I had no idea why the soil under the road mattered, but she nodded slowly, stood up, and brushed off her hands like the decision was made.
earth:1.cnHint: 店长蹲在路边摸了摸____，若有所思地点点头。
earth:1.hook: She pulled a small notebook out and wrote down one address.
earth:1.line: 'Feel that — firm *earth* means the foundation will hold just fine.'

paper:1.en: A stack of forms sat on the outside table, held down by a stone. The Manager handed me a pen. 'Sign each *paper* where the dot is,' she said. 'These go to the city office tomorrow.' Twelve pages, three stamps, one quick lunch break — and a second store was one step closer to real.
paper:1.cnHint: 店长让我在一叠____上签字，分店申请手续正式开始了。
paper:1.hook: The last page had a line neither of us had noticed before.
paper:1.line: 'Every *paper* must be signed before noon or we lose the slot.'

art:1.en: On the wall beside the proposed new store site, someone had painted a bright mural overnight. The Manager stood back and looked at it. 'Good *art* brings people in,' she said with a small smile. Tang took a photo. I thought the painted cat in the corner looked a little like our store's regular, old Mr. Song.
art:1.cnHint: 新店选址旁边的墙上出现了一幅____，店长觉得这是个好兆头。
art:1.hook: The painted cat had the same torn ear as the stray we fed every night.
art:1.line: 'Good *art* on the wall is better than any sign we could buy.'

street:1.en: The Manager walked me two blocks down and pointed. 'That is the *street*,' she said. 'Same kind of corner as ours, same lamp, same late-night crowd.' I looked at the empty shop front and tried to picture it lit up and busy. A woman with a grocery bag paused in front of it, peered in, then walked on.
street:1.cnHint: 店长带我去看新分店的____，那里和我们这里出奇地相似。
street:1.hook: The woman with the grocery bag came back and looked again.
street:1.line: 'This *street* sees three hundred people after midnight — I counted.'

talent:1.en: Tang redesigned the new store's layout on a napkin in five minutes, outside on the step. The Manager looked at it and raised both eyebrows. 'You have real *talent*,' she said. Tang blushed and said it was nothing. The Manager took the napkin inside and pinned it to the board without another word.
talent:1.cnHint: 阿糖在餐巾纸上画出了新店布局，店长称赞了他的____。
talent:1.hook: By morning, three small changes had appeared on the napkin in red ink.
talent:1.line: 'Honestly, his *talent* for layout is wasted on a napkin.'

overall:1.en: The Manager stood at the corner with a clipboard and looked up and down the road. 'The *overall* picture looks good,' she said at last. 'Foot traffic, parking, the noodle shop next door — it all fits.' Tang and I exchanged a look. When the Manager said something looked good, it usually meant the plan was already done.
overall:1.cnHint: 店长综合考察了新店选址的____情况后，给出了正面评价。
overall:1.hook: She clicked her pen and circled a number none of us had noticed.
overall:1.line: 'The *overall* plan is solid — we move forward next week.'

admit:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, arms crossed, staring at the locked front door. A sign read: 'Closed for inspection.' He took a slow breath, then turned to me. 'We have to *admit* the other side picked a better corner than us,' he said quietly.
admit:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店门口，____自己选址不如对手。
admit:1.hook: But his eyes were already measuring the street for a counter-move.
admit:1.line: 'I *admit* their corner gets more foot traffic than ours.'

association:1.en: A small crowd had gathered on the pavement outside. An elderly man held up a banner that read 'Night Traders Welcome Here.' He told me his *association* of street vendors had voted to support our new branch opening, hoping it would bring more customers to the whole block.
association:1.cnHint: 一个小团体的老人告诉我，他们的____投票支持我们新分店开业。
association:1.hook: Then Lin appeared at the edge of the crowd, watching with unreadable eyes.
association:1.line: 'Our *association* voted to welcome every new shop on this street.'

brand:1.en: I was taping a poster to the outside window when a teenager stopped and pointed at our logo. 'Is this the same *brand* as the big store downtown?' she asked. I nodded. Her face lit up. Apparently, the downtown store had once given her a free hot drink on a cold night.
brand:1.cnHint: 一个女孩指着橱窗上的____标志，问我是否和市中心那家店是同一个。
brand:1.hook: She pulled out her phone and started typing something fast.
brand:1.line: 'I love this *brand* — they were so kind to me once.'

deep:1.en: Just before sunrise, I stepped outside to restock the sign-board. The street was still and *deep* in shadow, lit only by our store's warm glow. A cat sat perfectly still in the middle of the road, watching me as if it had been waiting there for hours.
deep:1.cnHint: 日出前，街道____陷在阴影里，只有我们店的灯光照着。
deep:1.hook: Then the cat stood, turned, and padded toward the alley where Lin's shop would open.
deep:1.line: 'Out here *deep* in the night, only us clerks are awake.'

discover:1.en: Tang was sweeping the step outside when she suddenly stopped. 'Come look!' she called. We bent down and managed to *discover* a tiny handwritten note tucked under the door mat. It said: 'Good luck with the new branch — a friend.' No name. No clue who left it.
discover:1.cnHint: 唐在门口扫地时，我们在脚垫下____了一张匿名便条。
discover:1.hook: The handwriting looked oddly familiar to me.
discover:1.line: 'We just *discovered* a secret note under the mat — read it!'

essential:1.en: The Manager had pinned a short list to the outside notice board under the heading 'What we promise.' Item one read: 'Fresh food every morning.' He told me that keeping that promise was *essential* — without it, no new branch could survive its first month on any street.
essential:1.cnHint: 店长说，每天保证新鲜食物对新分店来说是____的。
essential:1.hook: Lin walked past, read the list, and said nothing — but she slowed her step.
essential:1.line: 'Trust is *essential*; lose it once and customers never return.'

fine:1.en: A city inspector arrived outside just as we were setting up the pavement stand. He checked our permit, circled the stand twice, and then smiled. 'Everything looks *fine*,' he said, stamping his clipboard. Tang let out a breath she had clearly been holding for ten minutes.
fine:1.cnHint: 检查员查看了我们的许可证后说一切____，唐如释重负。
fine:1.hook: Then he added, 'I'll be back next week,' and walked away smiling.
fine:1.line: 'Your permit is *fine* — but keep that stand inside the line.'

largely:1.en: By mid-morning a small queue had formed outside the new branch. The Manager looked pleased. 'This turnout is *largely* thanks to the flyers Tang handed out yesterday,' he said. Tang, who was refilling the outside bin, pretended not to hear, but she was definitely smiling.
largely:1.cnHint: 店长说，今天门口的人群____要归功于唐昨天发的传单。
largely:1.hook: Across the street, Lin was counting our queue with a frown.
largely:1.line: 'Our opening went well, *largely* because Tang worked so hard.'

machine:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, watching workers set up a large coffee *machine* on the pavement. It hummed and shook as it heated up, drawing curious looks from people on their way to work. The smell of fresh coffee drifted down the quiet street.
machine:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口看工人安装一台巨大的____，咖啡香飘满街头。
machine:1.hook: Then the machine made a sound no one expected.
machine:1.line: 'This *machine* cost more than my first car,' the Manager said quietly.

observe:1.en: Lin arrived early to *observe* the unwritten rule that the branch opening day belongs to the whole team. She swept the front step without being asked, arranged a small welcome sign by the door, and stood back to look at it with quiet pride.
observe:1.cnHint: 林自觉____新店开业当天大家共同维护的不成文规矩，主动打扫门前。
observe:1.hook: Tang watched her from across the street, expression unreadable.
observe:1.line: 'We *observe* this tradition every time we open a new store,' Lin said.

fat:1.en: A delivery man stopped his bicycle outside the new branch and studied a printed menu taped to the window. 'Low *fat*,' he read aloud, pointing at the yogurt section. He pulled out his phone, took a photo, and sent it somewhere before riding away without buying anything.
fat:1.cnHint: 一位送货员盯着新店橱窗里的菜单，专注地看____含量标注。
fat:1.hook: Thirty minutes later, a rival shop posted the same label.
fat:1.line: 'No extra *fat*, no extra guilt,' Tang said, handing out samples cheerfully.

helpful:1.en: Tang taped a hand-drawn map to the lamp post outside, showing which bus stop was nearest and where the car park was. A woman with two bags stopped, read it, and smiled. 'Very *helpful*,' she said. Tang waved, already walking back inside to tape up another one.
helpful:1.cnHint: 唐在路灯柱上贴了一张手绘地图，路过的阿姨觉得非常____。
helpful:1.hook: The Manager had not asked Tang to do any of that.
helpful:1.line: 'I just want to be *helpful* on the first day,' Tang said.

position:1.en: The Manager paced the pavement, checking the sign above the door. Its *position* was two centimetres too far to the left, catching shadow in the morning light. He moved a small ladder, climbed up, and nudged it right. Lin watched from below, arms folded.
position:1.cnHint: 店长反复确认招牌的____，差两厘米都不肯将就。
position:1.hook: Lin said nothing, but she was already measuring something else.
position:1.line: 'The *position* of that sign matters more than you think,' the Manager said.

threat:1.en: Lin noticed a larger shop opening just one block away. Its bright lights and wide windows felt like a quiet *threat* to the new branch. She said nothing to the Manager, just took out her notebook and began writing down everything the other shop was doing differently.
threat:1.cnHint: 林发现街对面有家更大的店正在开业，感到这是一种无声的____。
threat:1.hook: Her notebook was nearly full by lunchtime.
threat:1.line: 'I refuse to treat every new neighbour as a *threat*,' the Manager said firmly.

trend:1.en: A young woman paused outside the branch and pointed at the oat-drink poster in the window. 'That *trend* is everywhere this year,' she told her friend, loud enough for Tang to hear from the doorway. Tang smiled and made a note to order twice as much oat stock next week.
trend:1.cnHint: 一位年轻女士指着橱窗海报，感叹这种饮品____今年席卷全城。
trend:1.hook: Tang's note would change the Manager's entire supply order.
trend:1.line: 'Following a *trend* early is how small shops survive,' Tang said.

ultimately:1.en: After a long morning of last-minute fixes, the Manager stood at the kerb and looked at the finished branch. The sign was straight, the lights were warm, and a small queue had already formed. *Ultimately*, he thought, a shop is only as good as the people inside it.
ultimately:1.cnHint: 忙碌了一上午之后，店长站在路边，____意识到一家店的灵魂在于人。
ultimately:1.hook: Inside, Lin and Tang were already arguing about the coffee machine.
ultimately:1.line: '*Ultimately*, we did this together,' the Manager said, almost to himself.

australia:1.en: A hand-written sign appeared on the lamp post outside the store: 'Grand Opening — Second Branch Coming Soon!' A man in a wide hat stopped to read it, then grinned at me. 'Back in *Australia*, every corner shop had three branches,' he said. 'Good luck, mate.'
australia:1.cnHint: 店外路灯柱上贴出了新分店的开业海报，一位戴宽檐帽的男士停下来微笑着聊起了____。
australia:1.hook: He folded the sign neatly and slipped it into his bag.
australia:1.line: 'Back in *Australia*, every corner shop had three branches — good luck, mate.'

authority:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, arms crossed, studying the empty unit next door. A city inspector arrived with a clipboard and asked who was in charge. The Manager stepped forward with quiet *authority* and said, 'I am. Ask me anything.' The inspector smiled and began writing.
authority:1.cnHint: 店长以____的姿态接待了前来检查新店铺的城市督查员。
authority:1.hook: The inspector's pen stopped halfway through the first question.
authority:1.line: 'I am the one with *authority* here — ask me anything you like.'

confident:1.en: Tang taped a bright banner across the front of the future second branch while I held the ladder. Passers-by slowed down to watch. Tang stepped back, tilted his head, and looked *confident* — like someone who had hung a thousand banners and never dropped a single one. I tightened my grip on the ladder, just in case.
confident:1.cnHint: 唐在新门店外挂横幅时神情____，围观路人越来越多。
confident:1.hook: Then one corner of the banner began to peel away.
confident:1.line: 'Hold steady — I am *confident* this banner is going up perfectly.'

crowd:1.en: Word of the new branch spread fast. By mid-morning a small *crowd* had gathered on the pavement outside the empty unit, peering through the dusty window. Some pressed their faces to the glass. The Manager appeared beside me and murmured, 'Free curiosity is better than paid advertising.'
crowd:1.cnHint: 新分店的消息传开后，街上____聚集起来，争相向橱窗内张望。
crowd:1.hook: One face at the glass suddenly went very pale.
crowd:1.line: 'Look at this *crowd* — free curiosity beats paid advertising every time.'

highly:1.en: Lin arrived on the street corner carrying a takeaway coffee and a spreadsheet. She spread it across the bonnet of a parked bicycle and pointed at a column of numbers. 'The new location is *highly* suitable,' she announced to no one in particular. I leaned over and saw my name in the 'branch manager' column.
highly:1.cnHint: 林在街角铺开表格，指出新选址____合适，我无意间发现了自己的名字。
highly:1.hook: She capped her pen before I could ask any questions.
highly:1.line: 'This corner is *highly* suitable — the numbers do not lie.'

occur:1.en: We were stacking new shelves on the pavement, ready to carry them inside, when it began to rain. It did not *occur* to anyone to check the forecast. Tang looked at the sky, then at the flat-pack boxes turning soft and dark. The Manager opened an umbrella — just for himself.
occur:1.cnHint: 大家在搬运货架时突然下起雨来，谁也没____想到要提前看天气预报。
occur:1.hook: Tang quietly lifted one corner of the Manager's umbrella.
occur:1.line: 'It did not *occur* to me to check the rain — my mistake, truly.'

regularly:1.en: An elderly woman paused by the new branch doorway every single morning, the same time, the same slow pace. The Manager told me she had walked this street *regularly* for twenty years and always bought a warm bun from whoever rented this unit. He looked thoughtful. 'We should sell warm buns,' he said.
regularly:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶____经过新店门口，店长若有所思地说应该卖热包子。
regularly:1.hook: The next morning she stopped and actually came inside.
regularly:1.line: 'She walks past *regularly* — twenty years without missing a day.'

responsible:1.en: The Manager handed me a single key on a plain ring and said the new branch needed someone *responsible* to open it each morning. I stared at the key. It was heavier than it looked. Outside, a pigeon landed on the shop sign and stared back at me as if it were also judging my reliability.
responsible:1.cnHint: 店长把新店钥匙交给我，说需要一个____的人每天早晨开门。
responsible:1.hook: The key was stamped with a number I did not recognise.
responsible:1.line: 'I need someone *responsible* to open the new branch every morning — that is you.'

experiment:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the new branch site, holding a small paper cup. 'Try this,' he said, passing it to me. The store was going to sell hot drinks, and this was an *experiment* — a test blend he had mixed himself at five in the morning to see if customers would actually want it.
experiment:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店门口让我试喝他调配的热饮，这是一次____。
experiment:1.hook: The cup smelled wonderful, but his face stayed unreadable.
experiment:1.line: 'This *experiment* cost me three hours of sleep, so be honest.'

nature:1.en: I met Lin on the pavement one block from the new branch. She was sketching the street trees in a notebook. 'The *nature* of a good store,' she said without looking up, 'is that it fits the street around it.' She had already counted the benches, the bins, and the angle of the morning sun.
nature:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在街边写生时谈到了好门店的____。
nature:1.hook: She tore the page out and handed it to me without a word.
nature:1.line: 'The *nature* of a corner store is to belong to the street.'

status:1.en: A city inspector in a bright yellow vest stopped outside the new branch and checked a list on his clipboard. He asked me for the *status* of our building permit — was it approved, pending, or refused? I did not know the answer, and the Manager was not picking up his phone.
status:1.cnHint: 城市检查员来到新店门口，询问建筑许可证的____。
status:1.hook: The inspector circled something on his list very slowly.
status:1.line: 'I need the *status* of this permit before I leave this street.'

accident:1.en: I was carrying a box of shelf labels to the new branch when, by pure *accident*, I bumped into Tang at the corner. She was off duty, walking her small dog, and looked as surprised as I felt. We stared at each other, then both looked at the half-open door behind her.
accident:1.cnHint: 我搬货时在街角____ 碰到了下班的阿糖。
accident:1.hook: The dog had already slipped through the open door.
accident:1.line: 'Meeting you here was a happy *accident*, I think.'

active:1.en: The street outside the new branch was quiet at dawn, but Tang was already *active*, taping bright signs to the lamp posts nearby. She moved from post to post without stopping, her breath forming small clouds in the cool air. By the time I arrived with the keys, every lamp post had a sign.
active:1.cnHint: 一大早，阿糖就在新店附近的街道上____地张贴宣传海报。
active:1.hook: One sign was already peeling at the corner.
active:1.line: 'You have to be *active* before the street wakes up.'

feed:1.en: A thin orange cat had made a home on the step of the new branch's back door. Each morning a quiet old man came to *feed* it from a small tin. He never spoke to me, only to the cat. The Manager said the old man had been coming to that exact corner for eleven years.
feed:1.cnHint: 每天清晨，一位老人都会来新店后门____那只橘猫。
feed:1.hook: This morning, for the first time, the old man was late.
feed:1.line: 'I come to *feed* her every day, even in the rain.'

principle:1.en: Lin stopped me on the pavement outside the new branch and pointed at our new window display. 'It looks busy,' she said. 'The *principle* of a good display is one idea, not ten.' She was right — we had stuffed in every product we were proud of, and nothing stood out from the street.
principle:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在新店橱窗前指出，好橱窗的____是只传达一个主题。
principle:1.hook: She pulled one item from the display and the rest looked perfect.
principle:1.line: 'The basic *principle* is simple: one message, one window.'

article:1.en: I found a folded newspaper on the bench across from the new branch. Someone had circled a short *article* on the back page — a report about a small convenience store on this exact street that had closed ten years ago. The name of the store was the same as ours.
article:1.cnHint: 我在新店对面的长椅上发现一份报纸，里面有一篇关于这条街的____。
article:1.hook: The handwriting in the margin said: 'Be careful this time.'
article:1.line: 'Did you read the *article* about the old store on this corner?'

slightly:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, studying the empty shop front across the street. He tilted his head *slightly*, the way a cat watches a bird. 'That space has been empty for three months,' he said quietly. I followed his gaze. The sign in the window read: 'Opening Soon.'
slightly:1.cnHint: 店长盯着街对面的空铺子，头歪了一下，神情若有所思。
slightly:1.hook: The 'Opening Soon' sign had today's date written on it.
slightly:1.line: 'The light in there is *slightly* brighter than ours,' the Manager murmured.

vital:1.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map on the bonnet of his scooter. He jabbed a finger at our corner. 'Location,' he said, 'is *vital*. One block south and we get no foot traffic from the night buses.' I looked at the new store going up two streets away. It was exactly one block south.
vital:1.cnHint: 店长在街边摊开手绘地图，指着我们所在的街角，神情严肃。
vital:1.hook: The new store's sign was already lit and twice as bright as ours.
vital:1.line: 'This corner is *vital* — lose it and we lose everything,' the Manager said.

mention:1.en: Tang and I were taking out the recycling when a woman in a yellow coat stopped and asked if we knew the new shop opening nearby. I said nothing. Tang gave a polite smile. Later, back inside, Tang said quietly, 'Did you notice she didn't make any *mention* of us? Not even once.' The silence sat heavy between us.
mention:1.cnHint: 一位女士在门口打听附近新开的店，完全没有____到我们的店。
mention:1.hook: The woman in the yellow coat turned out to be a food-guide reviewer.
mention:1.line: 'She made no *mention* of our store at all,' Tang said with a sigh.

rare:1.en: On Sunday morning I found the Manager outside, staring at a single parking spot that had stayed empty all night. He said it was a *rare* thing — usually delivery bikes fight over it by dawn. 'Something has changed in the street,' he said slowly, turning to look down the road toward the new building going up on the corner.
rare:1.cnHint: 店长发现停车位一整晚都空着，觉得这种事____见，感到有些不安。
rare:1.hook: By noon, all the delivery bikes were parked outside the new store instead.
rare:1.line: 'An empty spot at dawn — that is truly *rare*,' the Manager said.

useful:1.en: Lin appeared at the door one evening holding a printed leaflet. He held it out to me with a small, careful smile. 'I thought this might be *useful* for you,' he said. It was a map of the new store's layout, with every shelf labelled. I stared at it. I had no idea how Lin had got inside.
useful:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林递给我一张新店的平面图，说这东西对我们会很____。
useful:1.hook: One shelf on the map was labelled 'staff only' and marked with a red cross.
useful:1.line: 'I thought the layout map might be *useful* to you,' Lin said pleasantly.

blood:1.en: The Manager rolled up his sleeve outside under the streetlight, showing me a faded mark on his forearm — an old ink stamp from the city traders' guild. 'My father had one too,' he said. 'This store is in my *blood*. No new shop on the next block is going to change that.' His voice was calm. His hands were not.
blood:1.cnHint: 店长在路灯下挽起袖子，说这家店已经融入他的____，新竞争对手改变不了什么。
blood:1.hook: The guild stamp, I later learned, meant the family had run a store on this street for forty years.
blood:1.line: 'This store is in my *blood*, and that is not going to change,' he said.

fund:1.en: I was sweeping the front step when I heard the Manager on his phone, his voice low and tight. He was asking someone whether the savings were enough to *fund* a small renovation — new shelving, better lighting, a fresh coat of paint on the outside wall. He hung up. He looked at the bright new sign two streets away and said nothing.
fund:1.cnHint: 店长在门口打电话，想知道积蓄够不够____一次小规模翻新。
fund:1.hook: He had been saving that money for something else entirely.
fund:1.line: 'I need to know if we have enough to *fund* the new shelves,' he said.

anxiety:1.en: Tang was quiet all afternoon, refolding bags behind the counter with more care than they needed. When I asked what was wrong, Tang looked out at the street and said, 'It is just *anxiety*. The new store opens on Friday.' I nodded. Outside, a man in a hard hat was taping a large poster to the wall opposite. The poster said: 'Grand Opening — Free Gifts For Everyone.'
anxiety:1.cnHint: 阿糖一下午心神不宁地叠袋子，承认自己对周五新店开业感到很____。
anxiety:1.hook: The 'free gifts' poster listed every item our store sold best.
anxiety:1.line: 'Honestly, it is just *anxiety* — I am sure we will be fine,' Tang said.

awareness:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, watching cars rush past. He had put up a bright sign the night before, hoping to raise *awareness* of the opening. A few people slowed down, looked up, and nodded. Small progress, he thought, but progress all the same.
awareness:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门外竖起招牌，希望提高路人对开业的____。
awareness:1.hook: Then one stranger stopped and asked a very odd question.
awareness:1.line: 'We need to raise *awareness* before the doors even open.'

introduce:1.en: Tang carried a tray of small free samples to the corner outside. 'Let me *introduce* our new store to the neighbourhood,' she said cheerfully, offering rice crackers to anyone who passed. An old man took one, chewed slowly, and gave a firm thumbs-up. Tang beamed.
introduce:1.cnHint: 阿糖在街角派发试吃品，向街坊____新店。
introduce:1.hook: But one woman in a red coat refused and walked away fast.
introduce:1.line: 'Allow me to *introduce* our new branch to everyone here.'

expense:1.en: The Manager taped a grand-opening banner to the wall and winced at the cost. 'Every *expense* adds up,' he muttered, smoothing a corner that kept peeling off. The banner was large, colourful, and impossible to ignore. Passing students stopped to take photos, which made him feel slightly better.
expense:1.cnHint: 店长一边贴横幅一边心疼每一笔____。
expense:1.hook: He did not yet know the banner hid a crack in the wall.
expense:1.line: 'This *expense* is worth it if even ten new customers come.'

toward:1.en: Lin walked slowly *toward* the new branch from across the street, hands in pockets, eyes scanning every detail of the shopfront. She counted the posters, noted the lighting, and wrote something in her small notebook. Then she looked up and smiled — not a friendly smile.
toward:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林朝着新店走去，仔细打量着每一处细节。
toward:1.hook: Whatever she wrote in that notebook, it was more than one page.
toward:1.line: 'I am walking *toward* the future — and so is my own plan.'

track:1.en: Tang had laid a chalk *track* on the pavement outside, shaped like footprints, leading from the bus stop all the way to the new front door. Children followed it laughing, pulling their parents along. The Manager watched from inside and quietly decided Tang deserved a longer lunch break.
track:1.cnHint: 阿糖在人行道上画了一条粉笔____，引导行人走进新店。
track:1.hook: One set of footprints, however, led away from the door instead.
track:1.line: 'Follow the *track* and you will find something free inside.'

afford:1.en: A young man lingered outside the new branch, staring at the lunch-set price on the window poster. 'I think I can *afford* that,' he said quietly to himself, counting coins in his palm. He counted twice, smiled, and pushed the door open with his shoulder.
afford:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人盯着海报上的价格，想确认自己____这顿饭。
afford:1.hook: The coins he held turned out to be exactly one short.
afford:1.line: 'Finally a place I can *afford* right here in my neighbourhood.'

feature:1.en: The new branch had one special *feature* that the original store did not: a small window shelf where customers could sit and watch the quiet street while they ate. The Manager had added it on a whim. By noon, every seat was taken and nobody seemed to want to leave.
feature:1.cnHint: 新店有一个旧店没有的____，吸引顾客久坐不走。
feature:1.hook: The last person on the shelf had been sitting there since dawn.
feature:1.line: 'The best *feature* of this store is that window right there.'

innovative:1.en: Lin stood across the street, arms crossed, studying the new branch. She had to admit — the outdoor menu board that changed with the weather was genuinely *innovative*. A warm message appeared on cold mornings; a cool one on hot afternoons. She pulled out her notebook again, frowning slightly.
innovative:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林不得不承认新店的户外菜单牌是真正____的设计。
innovative:1.hook: She had already begun sketching something very similar for her own shop.
innovative:1.line: 'That sign is *innovative* — and I intend to do one better.'

institution:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new corner store at dawn, nailing a small sign to the wall. 'This place will become an *institution*,' he said proudly, straightening his cap. A passing street cleaner paused, looked at the sign, and gave a slow, uncertain nod.
institution:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口钉招牌，说这里将成为街头一个重要的____。
institution:1.hook: The street cleaner knew something about this corner the Manager did not.
institution:1.line: 'This store will be an *institution* that people trust for years.'

outcome:1.en: Tang swept the pavement in front of the new branch early that morning, nervous about opening day. 'Whatever the *outcome*, we tried our best,' she told herself quietly. Across the street, Lin watched from the doorway of a rival shop, arms folded, expression unreadable.
outcome:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门前打扫，担心开业的____，而林就在对面静静地观望。
outcome:1.hook: Lin's lips curved into a small, knowing smile.
outcome:1.line: 'The *outcome* of today will decide everything for this street.'

recognize:1.en: I was taping opening-sale posters to the front window when an old man stopped on the pavement. He stared for a long moment, then broke into a grin. 'I *recognize* this corner,' he said softly. 'There used to be a tea stall here thirty years ago.'
recognize:1.cnHint: 一位老人在新店橱窗前驻足，说他____这个街角，三十年前这里曾有一家茶摊。
recognize:1.hook: He reached into his coat and pulled out a faded photograph.
recognize:1.line: 'I *recognize* this corner — I grew up right here.'

safety:1.en: The Manager hired a young man to stand near the entrance on opening morning, checking that the crowd did not push too hard. 'Your job is *safety* first,' the Manager told him firmly. The young man nodded, then quietly asked if the role came with a free lunch.
safety:1.cnHint: 店长在开业当天安排专人维持秩序，强调____第一，那人却问有没有免费午餐。
safety:1.hook: The crowd outside was already twice the size anyone had expected.
safety:1.line: '*Safety* is the only thing I care about on this busy morning.'

collect:1.en: Before the new branch opened, Tang walked door to door along the street handing out small discount cards. 'Please *collect* one and come visit us today,' she said cheerfully to every neighbour. Most people smiled and took a card. One elderly woman took six.
collect:1.cnHint: 唐沿街派发优惠卡，请邻居们____一张并光临新店，一位老太太一口气拿了六张。
collect:1.hook: The elderly woman winked and disappeared around the corner without a word.
collect:1.line: 'Please *collect* a card — we have a surprise gift inside.'

door:1.en: I arrived at the new branch an hour early to unlock the front *door*, only to find Lin already standing there, leaning casually against it with a coffee cup in hand. She raised an eyebrow. 'Took you long enough,' she said, stepping aside with a grin.
door:1.cnHint: 我提前去开新店的____，却发现林已经靠在门上等着了。
door:1.hook: Her coffee cup had the logo of our biggest competitor printed on it.
door:1.line: 'The front *door* was wide open when I arrived — check your locks.'

eventually:1.en: The opening-day line stretched all the way to the bus stop. I worried we would run out of rice balls before noon. The Manager kept calm, refilling trays and humming quietly. *Eventually* the crowd thinned, and the last customer in line turned out to be Tang's grandmother.
eventually:1.cnHint: 开业当天队伍排得很长，店长镇定应对，____人群散去，排在最后的居然是唐的奶奶。
eventually:1.hook: Tang's grandmother pressed a red envelope into the Manager's hand.
eventually:1.line: 'Don't worry — things will *eventually* work out if we stay calm.'

match:1.en: Lin strolled over at noon and studied our new display shelf with narrow eyes. 'Nice layout,' she admitted. 'But can your prices *match* mine?' The Manager smiled, turned a price tag quietly, and said nothing. Lin picked up the tag, read it, and her smile faded.
match:1.cnHint: 林过来查看新店货架，质疑我们的价格能否与她的____，店长悄悄翻过一张价签令她笑容消失。
match:1.hook: She bought three items without saying another word.
match:1.line: 'Let me see if your new prices *match* what we charge down the street.'

operation:1.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter at two in the morning. 'The new branch opens next month,' he said, tracing a red circle three streets away. The whole *operation* — permits, shelves, staffing — was planned on a single sheet of paper. I wondered if he ever slept.
operation:1.cnHint: 店长深夜在柜台上展开一张手绘地图，讲述新店开张的____计划。
operation:1.hook: The red circle on the map was right next to Lin's store.
operation:1.line: 'This whole *operation* fits on one page — that's how I like it.'

population:1.en: Outside, the Manager pointed up and down the quiet street. 'Ten thousand people live within ten minutes of here,' he said. I had never thought about it that way. A *population* of ten thousand, and most of them had never once stepped through our door. That felt like a problem worth fixing.
population:1.cnHint: 店长站在店门外，谈到附近的____规模，暗示新店选址的理由。
population:1.hook: He then pointed at the corner where Lin's store already stood.
population:1.line: 'With a *population* this size, one store is simply not enough.'

quick:1.en: Tang caught me by the sleeve before my shift ended. 'Take a *quick* look at the corner of Pine and Second,' she said, eyes bright. I walked over on my way home. A new storefront, freshly painted, sat dark and quiet behind a paper sign. The sign said: Opening Soon.
quick:1.cnHint: 阿糖让我下班时____去看看转角的情况，那里悄悄出现了新店的招牌。
quick:1.hook: The handwriting on that sign looked exactly like the Manager's.
quick:1.line: 'Just take a *quick* look — you'll understand everything.'

scale:1.en: Lin appeared at our door just after midnight, holding a folded newspaper. 'So the Manager is going big,' he said, not unkindly. He tapped the page. A small notice listed the new branch address. 'The *scale* of this surprises me,' Lin added, 'two stores, same street.' He folded the paper neatly and left without buying anything.
scale:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜拿着报纸来访，对新店开在同一条街上的____感到意外。
scale:1.hook: He left the newspaper on our counter, open to that exact page.
scale:1.line: 'The *scale* of this plan — two stores, one street — surprises even me.'

basic:1.en: The Manager handed me a one-page guide before I left for the new branch site. 'Learn the *basics* first,' he said, underlining three words: greet, stock, smile. It felt almost too simple. But watching him run this store, I realised those three things were the whole job, done perfectly, every single night.
basic:1.cnHint: 店长递给我一页指南，告诉我新店开张前要先掌握几条____原则。
basic:1.hook: The guide had a second page, and it was about Lin.
basic:1.line: 'Master the *basics* first — everything else follows naturally.'

constantly:1.en: Tang was *constantly* updating the little chalkboard outside — new prices, new snacks, a cheerful drawing of a rice ball. I asked why she bothered, since most customers walked in without looking. She grinned. 'The one who stops to read it,' she said, 'is the one who becomes a regular.' I started noticing who stopped.
constantly:1.cnHint: 阿糖____更新门外的小黑板，她说这是吸引新顾客成为常客的小秘密。
constantly:1.hook: One night, a stranger stopped and read every single word.
constantly:1.line: 'I am *constantly* updating it — that one reader makes it worth it.'

favor:1.en: The Manager mentioned, almost by accident, that he *favored* the new corner location because the morning light was good. 'People feel cheerful in good light,' he said, refilling the coffee machine. It seemed like a small reason to open a whole new store. But the more I thought about it, the more I believed him.
favor:1.cnHint: 店长透露他____新店的选址，原因出人意料地简单：光线好。
favor:1.hook: Tang later told me the real reason was something else entirely.
favor:1.line: 'I *favor* this corner — the morning light alone is worth it.'

absence:1.en: Lin did not come in for three nights in a row. I noticed the *absence* the way you notice a missing tile on a familiar floor. On the fourth night Tang set a can of his usual drink on the counter without being asked. 'Just in case,' she said. We both watched the door. He did not come.
absence:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林连续三晚没有出现，他的____让我和阿糖都不约而同地担心起来。
absence:1.hook: On the fifth night, someone else came in his place.
absence:1.line: 'His *absence* these three nights — it's not like him at all.'

digital:1.en: The Manager called me outside to look at the new sign above the door. It was a bright *digital* display, showing the store name in shifting colours. 'Much better than the old painted board,' he said proudly. A small crowd of neighbours had already gathered on the pavement to stare up at it.
digital:1.cnHint: 店长把我叫到门外，指着门上方那块闪烁变色的____招牌，得意地说比以前的手绘牌子好多了。
digital:1.hook: One neighbour in the crowd had not come to admire the sign at all.
digital:1.line: 'That *digital* sign cost more than my first car,' the Manager said with a grin.

sale:1.en: A folding table sat outside the store, loaded with last season's snacks at half price. Tang had written 'FINAL *SALE*' on a big card in red ink. Shoppers slowed down, picked things up, put them back, then quietly slipped a bag or two under their arm and headed inside to pay.
sale:1.cnHint: 店外摆了一张折叠桌，阿糖用红笔写了一张____大牌子，过路人一个个悄悄拿起零食往店里走。
sale:1.hook: One shopper never actually went inside to pay.
sale:1.line: Tang waved at the table and said, 'Everything on this table is on *sale* — half price, no joke.'

contact:1.en: Lin stood on the corner opposite our store, handing out small cards to everyone who passed. I watched from the doorway. When our eyes met, Lin gave a cool nod. Later I found one of the cards on the pavement: it listed a phone number under the words '*Contact* us first.' I pocketed it without knowing why.
contact:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在街对面发名片，我捡到一张，上面印着"____我们"和一个电话号码。
contact:1.hook: That phone number matched one already saved in my own phone.
contact:1.line: Lin called across the street: 'Feel free to *contact* me any time — day or night.'

failure:1.en: I forgot to restock the hot drinks shelf before the early-morning rush. By six o'clock it was completely empty, and a line of sleepy office workers stared at the gap in silence. Tang patted my shoulder. 'A *failure* to prepare,' Tang said kindly, 'is just a lesson you only need once.' I was not sure I believed that yet.
failure:1.cnHint: 我忘了补热饮货架，早高峰时货架空空如也，阿糖安慰我说这次____只要经历一次就够了。
failure:1.hook: The last person in that silent line left something behind on the counter.
failure:1.line: 'A *failure* to restock once is fine — twice and the Manager notices,' Tang said quietly.

bird:1.en: Just after midnight, an old man stopped outside and whistled a long, falling note. From somewhere above the streetlamp, a small brown *bird* answered him, note for note. He laughed, pulled his coat tighter, and walked on without buying anything. I leaned over the counter to watch him go, and the bird sang once more into the dark.
bird:1.cnHint: 午夜刚过，一位老人在门外吹口哨，路灯上方有只____跟着他一唱一和，老人笑着走开了。
bird:1.hook: The next night the old man came back, but this time he was not alone.
bird:1.line: 'That little *bird* has been living above this lamp post for three years,' the old man told me softly.

official:1.en: A woman in a neat grey jacket knocked on the glass door at two in the morning and held up a card. She said she was an *official* from the city planning office, checking addresses for the new district map. She wrote something in a notebook, thanked me, and left. The Manager phoned me ten minutes later, wide awake, asking exactly what she had wanted.
official:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一名城市规划部门的____敲门核查地址，事后店长打电话追问她具体说了什么。
official:1.hook: The Manager had received no notice of any such inspection.
official:1.line: 'I am an *official* from the planning office,' she said, holding her card steady in the lamplight.

confidence:1.en: Tang served customers with an easy calm that I could only envy. Even when the receipt printer jammed and a queue stretched to the door, Tang just smiled, fixed it in thirty seconds, and said 'Sorry for the wait' with complete *confidence*. I asked later how Tang stayed so cool. 'You fake it,' Tang said, 'until it stops being fake.'
confidence:1.cnHint: 阿糖处理故障时从容自信，我问他哪来的____，他说一开始都是装出来的，装着装着就真了。
confidence:1.hook: Tang's hands had been shaking the whole time the printer was jammed.
confidence:1.line: 'Smile and speak with *confidence*,' Tang told me, 'and most problems feel smaller already.'

display:1.en: Lin arranged a neat row of drinks on the low wall outside, each bottle turned so its label faced the street. It was a quiet, careful *display*, clearly meant to draw eyes away from our window. I had to admit it looked good. The Manager saw it too, and by the next morning our own window had twice as many bottles, every label perfectly forward.
display:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在街边矮墙上精心____了一排饮料，店长看见后，第二天早上我们橱窗里的饮料瓶数量翻了倍。
display:1.hook: Lin had photographed our new window before we even opened that morning.
display:1.line: Lin smiled and said, 'I just like to *display* things where people can actually see them.'

advice:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, studying the empty shop front across the street. He had been staring at it for ten minutes. 'That corner gets morning sun,' he said quietly, more to himself than to me. He asked for my *advice* on whether the new branch should sell hot food. I had no idea, but I said yes anyway.
advice:1.cnHint: 店长在街对面空店铺前驻足，向我寻求关于新分店的____。
advice:1.hook: He wrote something in his notebook that he would not let me see.
advice:1.line: 'Can I have your *advice* on the hot-food counter — yes or no?'

attempt:1.en: Tang and I carried a heavy shelf unit out through the front door to test it on the pavement display. Tang dropped her end twice. On her third *attempt* she finally lifted it clean and we set it down with a loud clang. A passing cyclist slowed, looked at us, and rode on with a small smile.
attempt:1.cnHint: 唐和我在店外搬架子，她第三次____才成功。
attempt:1.hook: The cyclist stopped at the corner and looked back once more.
attempt:1.line: 'One more *attempt* — I can do this, I promise.'

draw:1.en: The Manager pinned two possible signs for the new branch on the wall outside and asked everyone walking past to vote. By noon it was a *draw*: twelve people for the round logo, twelve for the square one. He looked at me with tired eyes. A quiet old man in a grey coat had voted twice, once for each side.
draw:1.cnHint: 店长让路人投票选新店招牌，结果出现了____，票数相同。
draw:1.hook: The old man in the grey coat was still standing there, watching the Manager.
draw:1.line: 'It is a *draw* — twelve each, and I have no idea what to do now.'

facility:1.en: Lin arrived from the shop down the road and walked slowly around our outdoor display, hands behind his back. He stopped at the new card-payment stand the Manager had just set up. 'Nice *facility*,' he said, in a flat voice that meant the opposite. He took a photo of it before he left.
facility:1.cnHint: 竞争对手林来参观，对我们新设置的支付____发表了评论。
facility:1.hook: Lin sent a message to someone on his phone as he walked away.
facility:1.line: 'That is a fine *facility* you have there,' Lin said, not smiling at all.

firm:1.en: The Manager had told us clearly: the outdoor stand closes at six in the morning, no exceptions. When a delivery driver begged to leave a crate on it at half past six, I said no. He argued for a full minute. I stayed *firm*, just as the Manager had shown me. The driver left the crate on the pavement and drove off fast.
firm:1.cnHint: 送货司机求我通融，但我态度____，按店长要求拒绝了他。
firm:1.hook: The crate sat there, ticking softly in the early morning quiet.
firm:1.line: 'I must stay *firm* on this — six o'clock is six o'clock.'

innovation:1.en: The Manager had taped a small handwritten menu to the outside wall: instant noodles, hot eggs, and warm corn. He called it an *innovation* for the new branch. A group of students stopped, read it, and pulled out their phones to take photos. One of them said it was the best idea she had seen all week.
innovation:1.cnHint: 店长把手写菜单贴在外墙，称这是新分店的一项____。
innovation:1.hook: The student who spoke was still outside, writing something in a notebook.
innovation:1.line: 'This little menu is our first *innovation* for the new branch,' the Manager said.

multiple:1.en: Outside the new branch site, the Manager had set up *multiple* small signs pointing to our main store, each one slightly different — some with arrows, one with a map, one with just the words 'we are open.' Tang counted them and said there were seven. The Manager looked pleased. A woman stopped and read every single one.
multiple:1.cnHint: 店长在新店址外摆了____指引牌，一共七块，各不相同。
multiple:1.hook: The woman pulled out a pen and circled something on the sign with the map.
multiple:1.line: 'I put up *multiple* signs so nobody gets lost on opening day.'

path:1.en: There was a narrow *path* between our store and the wall next door, just wide enough for one person. The Manager said the new branch would have no such lane — open space only. A small cat appeared from the path every night at two and sat by the door. I had started leaving a saucer of water out for it.
path:1.cnHint: 我们店旁有条窄____，每晚两点都有一只小猫从那里出现。
path:1.hook: Tonight the saucer was empty, but the cat had not come.
path:1.line: 'That *path* is too dark — we need a light there before winter.'

safe:1.en: The Manager arrived before dawn carrying a small metal box. 'Follow me,' he said, leading me to the back room. He knelt beside a dusty shelf, moved a stack of old receipts, and revealed a heavy *safe* built into the wall. He pressed a code I was not allowed to see. Whatever was inside, he checked it every single night.
safe:1.cnHint: 店长每天深夜都会去后室打开藏在货架后面的____，查看里面的东西。
safe:1.hook: He never told me what the code was — or what was inside.
safe:1.line: 'Every night I check the *safe* before I go home.'

speed:1.en: Just past two in the morning, a bicycle appeared outside the glass door. The rider jumped off before it even stopped. He grabbed a rice ball, tossed coins onto the counter without counting them, and was back on his bike in under thirty seconds. I had never seen such *speed* in a person buying a snack. He left before I could even say thank you.
speed:1.cnHint: 一个骑自行车的人以惊人的____冲进店里买了饭团，转眼就消失了。
speed:1.hook: The coins added up to exactly the right amount — every time.
speed:1.line: 'You have to admire his *speed* — thirty seconds, every night.'

burden:1.en: Tang came in at the end of a double shift, shoulders low, feet dragging. She set a bag of unsold sandwiches on the counter and sighed. 'Taking these home again,' she said. The Manager always asked her to carry back whatever did not sell — a small but daily *burden* she never complained about out loud. Still, her eyes said everything.
burden:1.cnHint: 唐把没卖完的三明治带回家，这是她每天默默承受的一种____。
burden:1.hook: One night the bag was twice as heavy, and she said nothing at all.
burden:1.line: 'Carrying leftover stock home every day is a real *burden*.'

former:1.en: Two coffee cups sat side by side on the counter — one black, one with milk. Lin pointed at them and smiled. 'The *former* is mine,' he said, picking up the black one. I had mixed them up twice already this week. He never got annoyed, just corrected me gently each time. I wondered why he always ordered both cups at once.
former:1.cnHint: 林指着两杯咖啡，说____是他的那杯，我总是弄混它们。
former:1.hook: The second cup was always left untouched until a woman arrived.
former:1.line: 'The *former* one is mine — I always drink mine black.'

oppose:1.en: The Manager wanted to rearrange the snack shelves to put cheap items at eye level. Lin, from the store across the street, happened to be inside buying water. He heard the plan and shook his head. 'I tried that last year,' he said. 'Customers *oppose* it every time — they feel cheated.' The Manager looked at him, then at me, then said nothing.
oppose:1.cnHint: 林听说店长要重新摆放货架，便说顾客每次都会____这种做法。
oppose:1.hook: The Manager changed the shelves anyway — and sales dropped that week.
oppose:1.line: 'Customers will *oppose* any change that feels unfair to them.'

unable:1.en: A woman knocked on the glass at three in the morning, pointing at the top shelf. I climbed the small step stool and stretched as far as I could, but I was *unable* to reach the last box of crackers pushed to the very back. She watched patiently, arms folded. I tried twice. The third time, Tang walked in and reached it in one easy move.
unable:1.cnHint: 一位顾客想要最高架子最里面的饼干，而我____够到它。
unable:1.hook: The woman smiled at Tang in a way that felt like they already knew each other.
unable:1.line: 'I was completely *unable* to reach it without Tang's help.'

unusual:1.en: At four in the morning a man walked in wearing a full suit and carrying a small watering can. He bought a bottle of water, carefully poured half of it into the can, then watered the potted plant by our door. He nodded at me politely and left. It was the most *unusual* thing I had seen all week — and the plant did look healthier after that.
unusual:1.cnHint: 一个穿西装的男人在凌晨四点进来，做了一件十分____的事。
unusual:1.hook: He came back the next night with a different plant under his arm.
unusual:1.line: 'That is *unusual* — most people do not bring a watering can here.'

apart:1.en: Lin's store and ours stood just a few metres *apart*, facing each other across the narrow street. Most nights we watched each other through our glass windows like two fish in different bowls. Tang said Lin once worked here before the Manager and he had a falling-out. Whether that story was true, I could not say. But Lin always bought his late-night snacks from us.
apart:1.cnHint: 林的店和我们的店只隔几米，而他过去和我们店的关系远不止____这么简单。
apart:1.hook: One night Lin stood at his door for a long time, just looking over.
apart:1.line: 'Our two stores are only a few steps *apart*, but it feels like miles.'

character:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new store site, studying the old building's front. 'This place has real *character*,' he said, tracing the worn bricks with one finger. I watched him smile at a crooked window frame the way most people only smile at something they already love.
character:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店选址前，觉得这栋旧楼很有____。
character:1.hook: But someone had left a note on the door that morning.
character:1.line: 'This building has *character* — that is exactly what we need.'

clean:1.en: Before the new branch could open, we had to make the old corner shop spotless. I swept the pavement outside while Tang scrubbed the window glass. By noon, the whole front was *clean* and bright, and passing strangers slowed down to look, as if the building had just woken up.
clean:1.cnHint: 开新店前，我们把店面打扫得____，路人忍不住驻足观看。
clean:1.hook: One stranger stopped a little too long.
clean:1.line: 'Finally *clean* — now it actually looks like a real store.'

convey:1.en: The Manager taped a small sign to the new store's front door. He rewrote it three times, unhappy with the words. 'I want to *convey* that everyone is welcome, day or night,' he told me. Tang read the final version and nodded slowly, which, from Tang, meant a lot.
convey:1.cnHint: 店长想用门口的告示____出"随时欢迎"的感觉，反复修改了好几遍。
convey:1.hook: A figure across the street had been reading the sign for ten minutes.
convey:1.line: 'I need to *convey* the right feeling, or the sign is useless.'

distraction:1.en: We were painting the outside wall of the new branch when a street performer set up just across the road. Music drifted over, and my brush strokes went crooked. Tang clicked their tongue. 'No *distraction* until the wall is done,' they said firmly, then immediately turned to watch the performer too.
distraction:1.cnHint: 粉刷新店外墙时，对面街头艺人成了最大的____，连唐自己也忍不住回头看。
distraction:1.hook: The performer glanced at our store and smiled at something specific.
distraction:1.line: 'No *distraction* — we finish the wall first, then we can watch.'

fight:1.en: Lin showed up outside the new store site just as we were hanging the sign. I expected sharp words, but Lin only looked up at the shopfront in silence. 'You still have *fight* in you,' Lin said to the Manager at last, almost gently. The Manager said nothing, which told me everything.
fight:1.cnHint: 林出现在新店门口，出乎意料地说店长还有____。
fight:1.hook: Then Lin pulled an envelope from their coat pocket.
fight:1.line: 'I will say this — you still have *fight* in you.'

finish:1.en: The outside of the new branch looked almost ready. Almost. One corner of the sign hung lower than the other, and a strip of trim paint was still wet. 'The *finish* has to be perfect,' the Manager said quietly, more to himself than to us. Tang and I exchanged a tired look.
finish:1.cnHint: 新店外观接近完工，但店长坚持____要做到完美。
finish:1.hook: At that moment, a cat walked straight through the wet paint.
finish:1.line: 'The *finish* on this sign has to be perfect — redo it.'

frequently:1.en: I noticed the same elderly woman walk past the new store site *frequently* — once in the morning, once around lunch, once at dusk. She never stopped, just glanced at our progress and moved on. The Manager noticed her too. 'She used to run a shop here,' he said one evening, quietly.
frequently:1.cnHint: 一位老太太____经过新店工地，店长悄悄说出了她的来历。
frequently:1.hook: The next morning, she finally stopped walking.
frequently:1.line: 'She passes by so *frequently* — I think she misses this corner.'

invest:1.en: 'We are not just *investing* money,' the Manager told me as we stood outside the half-finished new branch one night. He gestured at the lit windows of the homes above the street. 'We are investing in this corner, these neighbours.' I looked up at the warm lights and, for the first time, felt proud.
invest:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口告诉我，我们____的不只是钱，还有这个街角。
invest:1.hook: One of those lit windows quietly went dark.
invest:1.line: 'We are *investing* in this street, not just in a building.'

moment:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, staring at the empty shop front across the street. He had looked at that spot every night for a month. 'This is the *moment*,' he said quietly, almost to himself. A sign in the window read: FOR RENT. His eyes did not blink.
moment:1.cnHint: 店长盯着街对面的空铺子，觉得____终于来了。
moment:1.hook: He pulled out his phone and dialled before I could ask why.
moment:1.line: 'This is the *moment* we have been waiting for, trust me.'

nice:1.en: Lin showed the Manager a hand-drawn floor plan on the pavement outside. Every measurement was exact, every shelf position thought out. 'Your numbers are very *nice*,' the Manager said, tracing a line with his finger. Lin smiled but said nothing, folding the paper with slow, careful hands.
nice:1.cnHint: 林把设计图摊在路边给店长看，店长夸它____。
nice:1.hook: I noticed Lin had drawn a second floor plan tucked behind the first.
nice:1.line: 'The spacing has to be *nice* — one centimetre off and the shelves will not fit.'

peer:1.en: An old woman stopped on the pavement and pressed her face close to the dark glass of the empty shop. She began to *peer* through the window, shading her eyes with both hands. 'Someone is looking at this place,' I told the Manager. He turned slowly and said nothing for a long time.
peer:1.cnHint: 一位老太太在空铺子门口____，想看清里面的样子。
peer:1.hook: She knocked on the glass twice before walking away into the dark.
peer:1.line: 'Why do you *peer* like that — can you not see the light is off?'

pretty:1.en: Tang arranged a small display of key-rings and hair clips outside on a folding table to draw passing shoppers toward the new location. A girl stopped and picked up a shiny clip. 'Every *pretty* sells faster outdoors,' Tang told me, grinning. The Manager watched from a distance and nodded slowly.
pretty:1.cnHint: 唐把小饰品摆在路边桌上，说____在户外卖得更快。
pretty:1.hook: The girl set the clip down, picked up something else, and went pale.
pretty:1.line: 'Put the *pretties* near the front — people always stop for them first.'

recommendation:1.en: A delivery driver parked his bike outside and handed the Manager a folded note. 'From the landlord next block,' the driver said. The Manager read it twice. It turned out to be a *recommendation* for a local builder who had fitted out three other shops on the street. The Manager folded it very carefully.
recommendation:1.cnHint: 快递员送来一封信，里面是关于装修师傅的____。
recommendation:1.hook: The builder's name at the bottom was the same as the old sign above our store.
recommendation:1.line: 'This *recommendation* comes from three shop owners — that is hard to ignore.'

strange:1.en: I stepped outside to take the rubbish out and noticed a man standing perfectly still under the lamp across the road, staring at our store. Nothing about him looked familiar. It felt *strange* — the street was empty in both directions, yet he stood there as if waiting for a door to open.
strange:1.cnHint: 我出门倒垃圾，看见路灯下有个____的身影一动不动地盯着店里。
strange:1.hook: When I looked again thirty seconds later, he was gone.
strange:1.line: 'Does it not feel *strange* to you that someone stands there every single night?'

widespread:1.en: Lin spread a printed map on the bonnet of a parked car outside. Red circles marked six streets nearby. 'The demand is *widespread*,' Lin said, tapping each circle. 'One store cannot cover all of this.' The Manager crossed his arms and studied the map. The red circles looked like small fires.
widespread:1.cnHint: 林展开地图，说附近的需求____，一家店根本顾不过来。
widespread:1.hook: The Manager circled one spot in pen and handed it back without a word.
widespread:1.line: 'The demand is *widespread* — look at how far people are walking just to reach us.'

wonderful:1.en: Standing outside at dawn, I watched the sky turn from grey to pale gold above the rooftops. Tang came out with two warm cans of milk tea and handed me one. 'Isn't it *wonderful*?' she said, nodding at the street slowly waking up around us. I did not know if she meant the sky or the new plan.
wonderful:1.cnHint: 唐递给我热奶茶，感慨眼前的一切____。
wonderful:1.hook: Then she said quietly, 'I hope the new store feels like this too.'
wonderful:1.line: 'It is *wonderful* what a single street corner can make you feel at five in the morning.'

immediately:1.en: The Manager pointed at the empty shelf outside and said we needed to restock *immediately*. I grabbed a box of snacks and ran out. The street was cold and bright under the lamp. A passing woman stopped, watched me arrange the shelf, and smiled — she came back three minutes later with a friend.
immediately:1.cnHint: 店长叫我____把外面的货架补好，一位路过的女士看了看，转身离开了。
immediately:1.hook: She whispered something to her friend before they both walked inside.
immediately:1.line: 'We need to restock that shelf *immediately* — people can see it from the street.'

afternoon:1.en: The slow *afternoon* shift belonged to Tang, but Tang was late again. I stood outside sweeping the step in the warm light, watching people drift past with shopping bags. A small boy pressed his face against the glass, leaving a perfect round mark. He looked at me with huge eyes, then ran after his mother.
afternoon:1.cnHint: 在一个懒洋洋的____，一个小男孩把脸贴在玻璃上，随后跑开了。
afternoon:1.hook: His mother stopped at the corner and looked back at the store for a long moment.
afternoon:1.line: 'The *afternoon* crowd is quiet — but watch out around four o'clock.'

expand:1.en: Lin from the store across the street crossed over and leaned on our wall. 'I hear the Manager wants to *expand*,' Lin said, nodding at the empty lot next door. I said nothing. Lin smiled, glanced at the lot once more, then walked back without another word.
expand:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林过来说，听说我们要____，然后没等回答就走了。
expand:1.hook: I noticed Lin pause at the lot and take a slow, careful look at its size.
expand:1.line: 'So you really plan to *expand* into that empty space next door?'

regardless:1.en: It had rained all morning, but the old man still came at his usual time, *regardless* of the wet street and his thin jacket. He bought his usual two items, counted coins into my palm, and left without hurrying. The rain had stopped by then, as if it too had decided to wait for him to finish.
regardless:1.cnHint: 尽管下着雨，那位老先生____准时来了，买完东西才慢慢离开。
regardless:1.hook: I realised I had never once seen him carry an umbrella.
regardless:1.line: 'I come every day *regardless* — a little rain never stopped me.'

rid:1.en: A young woman dragged a heavy bag to the door and asked if she could leave it outside for a moment. She wanted to *rid* herself of it long enough to carry two cups of hot tea from the stall across the lane. I held the door. She came back, beaming, with one cup held out for me.
rid:1.cnHint: 一位年轻女士想先____手里的重袋子，去对面给我们买热茶。
rid:1.hook: She mentioned her grandmother's stall across the lane — the one that never seemed to close.
rid:1.line: 'I just need to *rid* myself of this bag for one minute — I promise I'll be back.'

dog:1.en: A large, fluffy *dog* sat outside the store at two in the morning, very calm, looking at the door. No owner. No collar. It did not bark. I put a small bowl of water near the step and went back inside. Every time I looked out, the dog was still there, watching patiently, as if waiting for someone who had gone in a very long time ago.
dog:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一只____独自坐在店门口，安静地盯着门，没有主人。
dog:1.hook: By sunrise the bowl was empty, and the dog was gone.
dog:1.line: 'That *dog* has been sitting outside every night this week — nobody knows whose it is.'

busy:1.en: The corner was *busy* even at midnight — people cutting through on their way home, a noodle cart rattling past, someone arguing on a phone. I stood by the open door, watching it all like a slow river. Tang said the Manager had chosen this corner on purpose. It was the kind of street that never really slept.
busy:1.cnHint: 这个街角到了午夜依然____，店长据说是特意选了这里开店。
busy:1.hook: Tang smiled at that and looked away, like there was more to the story.
busy:1.line: 'Stay *busy* and keep the door open — that's what brings people in.'

male:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, counting heads. Most of the construction crew were *male*, but one woman in a yellow hard hat kept shouting orders louder than anyone else. I handed out cold water bottles and tried to remember all their names.
male:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店工地外清点人数，一位女工头的嗓门盖过了所有____工人。
male:1.hook: Then the woman in the hard hat turned and called my name.
male:1.line: Every *male* on this crew listens to me, and so will you.

fish:1.en: A street vendor had parked his cart right in front of the new branch door. The smell of grilled *fish* floated all the way to where I was sweeping the pavement. The Manager frowned, but the growing line of hungry customers told a different story.
fish:1.cnHint: 一位街头摊贩把车停在新分店门口，烤____的香味引来了长长的队伍。
fish:1.hook: The vendor smiled and slipped the Manager a small wrapped package.
fish:1.line: Try the *fish*. One bite and you will forgive me for parking here.

fashion:1.en: Lin had dressed the new branch window in a very different *fashion* from our usual store. Colourful signs, tiny fairy lights, a little chalkboard menu outside. I stopped on the pavement and stared. It looked less like a convenience store and more like a café from a magazine.
fashion:1.cnHint: 林以一种与平时截然不同的____装饰了新分店的橱窗，让我驻足呆看。
fashion:1.hook: A crowd had already gathered, and Lin had not even opened the door yet.
fashion:1.line: I decorated it in my own *fashion*, so please do not touch anything.

weather:1.en: The morning we were supposed to open the new branch, the *weather* turned mean. Rain hammered the street and puddles swallowed the welcome mat. Tang dragged out a big orange umbrella from the back room and stood outside waving at confused customers like a lighthouse.
weather:1.cnHint: 新分店开业那天，____突变，唐撑着橙色大伞站在门外当起了人形灯塔。
weather:1.hook: A black car slowed down beside Tang and did not drive away.
weather:1.line: Bad *weather* will not stop us. I can stand here all morning.

device:1.en: Tang arrived carrying a small electronic *device* that projected a arrow of blue light onto the pavement, pointing right at the new branch entrance. 'People follow arrows,' Tang said firmly. Within ten minutes a curious crowd had gathered to see what the light was pointing at.
device:1.cnHint: 唐带来一个能把蓝色箭头投影在地面的____，把路人引向新分店入口。
device:1.hook: One man followed the light arrow and walked straight into a lamppost.
device:1.line: This *device* cost me a week of wages. It had better work.

farm:1.en: An old man stopped me on the street and said he used to own a *farm* right where our new branch now stood. He pulled out a faded photo: green fields, a wooden fence, two goats. I looked at the glass-and-steel front of the store and felt oddly guilty.
farm:1.cnHint: 一位老人告诉我，新分店所在的地方曾经是他的____，并拿出了泛黄的老照片。
farm:1.hook: He asked if he could come inside and sit for a while.
farm:1.line: My whole *farm* once stood on this very spot. Strange, is it not?

drug:1.en: A nervous young man asked me quietly if we sold any *drug* for headaches. I pointed him to the small medicine shelf near the door. He bought two packs, paid, then hesitated. He looked like he had something else on his mind entirely.
drug:1.cnHint: 一个紧张的年轻男子轻声问我是否有治头痛的____，买完之后却迟迟不肯离开。
drug:1.hook: He finally whispered, 'Is the Manager here tonight?'
drug:1.line: I just need a *drug* for headaches. Nothing serious, I promise.

heat:1.en: By noon the *heat* rising from the pavement outside the new branch was fierce. I had been restocking the outdoor fridge for an hour and my shirt was soaked through. Lin walked past holding an iced drink, did not offer me one, and disappeared inside. Typical.
heat:1.cnHint: 正午地面散发出强烈的____，我在户外忙活了一个小时，林却端着冰饮扬长而去。
heat:1.hook: When I finally went inside, the indoor fridge was completely empty.
heat:1.line: The *heat* out there is no joke. Someone should bring you water.

intelligence:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, studying the street with calm, sharp eyes. 'Opening here takes *intelligence*,' he said, watching how people moved, where they paused, which corner caught the most foot traffic. He had chosen this spot himself, and he looked quietly proud of it.
intelligence:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店选址外，用敏锐的眼光观察街道，觉得选址需要____。
intelligence:1.hook: But someone else had been watching this corner far longer.
intelligence:1.line: 'Opening a second store takes real *intelligence*, not just money.'

uk:1.en: Tang was taping a small poster to the new store window when a tourist stopped and asked for directions. Tang tried hard, mixing words and gestures. The tourist smiled and pointed at his bag, which had a tiny flag on it. 'Ah,' Tang laughed, 'you are from the *UK*!'
uk:1.cnHint: 阿糖在贴海报时，一位来自____的游客停下来问路。
uk:1.hook: The tourist's next question left Tang completely speechless.
uk:1.line: 'I came all the way from the *UK* just to find good street food.'

user:1.en: Outside the new branch, a delivery rider stared at his phone with a frown. 'The app says I am the first *user* to pick up here,' he told me, 'but the address just shows a car park.' He looked up slowly at our bright new sign, then back at his phone, then at me.
user:1.cnHint: 一位外卖骑手盯着手机，因为系统显示他是新店地址的第一个____，但地图显示那里是停车场。
user:1.hook: He pressed 'arrived' and rode away before I could say a word.
user:1.line: 'It says I am the only *user* who has ever ordered from this address.'

park:1.en: The new branch faced a small *park*, where old men played chess under the trees each morning. I arrived early to unlock the door and found three of them already peering through the glass, hands behind their backs, breath fogging the window. They had clearly been waiting a while.
park:1.cnHint: 新店正对着一个____，每天早上老人们在那里下棋，今天他们早早就盯着新店的橱窗了。
park:1.hook: One of them pressed a handwritten note against the glass.
