park:1.line: 'The *park* crowd will be your best customers, trust me.'

reward:1.en: Lin arrived at the new branch holding a small paper bag. 'I walked thirty minutes to bring you warm dumplings,' she said, setting the bag on the counter with a grin. 'Consider it a *reward* for surviving your first week.' The smell was wonderful. I suddenly forgot how tired I was.
reward:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林步行三十分钟来到新店，给我带来了热腾腾的饺子，说这是对我____。
reward:1.hook: Then she pulled out a notepad and started quizzing me on branch procedures.
reward:1.line: 'Think of these dumplings as your *reward* for not quitting yet.'

credit:1.en: A woman in a bright coat stopped me just outside the new branch door. She had collected loyalty stamps from our old store for two years and wanted to know if her *credit* would carry over. She held up a card so full of tiny stamps that it had gone soft at the edges.
credit:1.cnHint: 一位女士拿着盖满印章的积分卡，想知道她在老店积累的____能不能在新店使用。
credit:1.hook: The Manager had never mentioned anything about transferring old stamps.
credit:1.line: 'I have two years of *credit* on this card and I am not starting over.'

progress:1.en: Every afternoon that week, the Manager walked the length of the new block and noted how the fit-out work *progressed*. He kept a small notebook and ticked things off without a word. On Friday he stopped, looked at the nearly finished shopfront, and allowed himself one slow nod of satisfaction.
progress:1.cnHint: 那周每天下午，店长都会沿着街道巡视，默默记录新店装修____的情况。
progress:1.hook: On Saturday morning the notebook was gone from his desk.
progress:1.line: 'Things *progress* faster when nobody stops to celebrate too early.'

snack:1.en: Just before midnight on the new branch's first night, a small girl tugged her grandfather to our window. She pressed her nose to the glass and pointed at a row of rice crackers. 'One *snack*,' the old man told me gently, counting coins into my palm with great care, one by one.
snack:1.cnHint: 新店第一晚接近午夜，一位老爷爷带着小孙女来买____，老人一枚枚地数硬币付钱。
snack:1.hook: The girl left a tiny handprint on the clean glass, perfectly centred.
snack:1.line: 'Just one *snack*, please — she has been good all day.'

retire:1.en: Just past midnight, the Manager stepped out the back door and stretched under the streetlamp. 'I used to *retire* at ten sharp,' he said, watching the empty road. 'Now ten o'clock is when the real rush starts.' He smiled at the irony, then noticed a shadow moving near the recycling bins.
retire:1.cnHint: 店长感慨自己以前很早就____，如今午夜才是忙碌的开始。
retire:1.hook: The shadow stopped moving — and seemed to be listening.
retire:1.line: 'I used to *retire* at ten, but the night shift changed everything.'

sea:1.en: The Manager unrolled a large map on the pavement outside, weighting the corners with bottles of tea. 'The new branch will go here,' he said, tapping a dot on the coast. Lin stared at the blue printed *sea* beside the dot and quietly wondered who would staff a store that close to the waves.
sea:1.cnHint: 店长在路边展开地图，新分店的位置就在印刷的____旁边。
sea:1.hook: Lin had never learned to swim.
sea:1.line: 'A store by the *sea* sounds nice — until the storms come.'

town:1.en: Tang carried a stack of flyers to the corner and stopped. The flyers announced a new branch opening in a small *town* thirty kilometres away. A grandmother on a bicycle slowed down, took one flyer, read it carefully, and then asked Tang in a low voice whether the new store would sell the same sticky-rice pudding as this one.
town:1.cnHint: 阿糖在街角发传单，新分店要开在附近的小____里。
town:1.hook: The grandmother already knew the new store's address by heart.
town:1.line: 'The new *town* branch opens Friday — same pudding, I promise.'

gap:1.en: Lin was taping a poster to the lamppost when she noticed a *gap* between two boards on the old fence across the street. Through it she could see someone writing in a notebook at a folding table. The handwriting was neat and fast. She taped the last corner of the poster and told herself it was none of her business.
gap:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林贴海报时，透过旧围栏的____看到了神秘的人影。
gap:1.hook: The notebook had the store's logo on its cover.
gap:1.line: 'There is a *gap* in the fence — and someone is watching us.'

generation:1.en: An elderly man paused in front of the store's outdoor bulletin board, reading the announcement of the new branch. 'My father bought rice from a shop on that same street,' he said to no one in particular. 'Every *generation* finds the same corner useful.' He pressed his palm flat against the notice, as if making sure it was real.
generation:1.cnHint: 一位老人读着公告，感慨每一____的人都离不开街角的小店。
generation:1.hook: His hand was shaking very slightly.
generation:1.line: 'Every *generation* in my family has lived near a shop like this.'

guide:1.en: Tang had agreed to *guide* a reporter from the local paper to the site of the planned new branch. They set off down the predawn street, past shuttered stalls and sleeping cats. Tang kept three steps ahead, explaining distances and bus routes. The reporter wrote nothing down, which Tang found oddly worrying.
guide:1.cnHint: 阿糖答应____一位记者去新分店的选址地点参观。
guide:1.hook: The reporter's pen had been recording the whole time.
guide:1.line: 'I will *guide* you to the site — it is only ten minutes from here.'

household:1.en: The Manager pinned a hand-drawn floor plan to the outdoor notice board. A woman with a shopping bag stopped to look at it. 'Your store has become a *household* name on this street,' she said warmly. 'Will the new one be just as small and friendly?' The Manager opened his mouth to answer, then paused longer than felt comfortable.
household:1.cnHint: 一位街坊称赞小店已经是这条街的____名字，询问新店是否一样亲切。
household:1.hook: The Manager's pause lasted almost ten full seconds.
household:1.line: 'This shop is a *household* name here — the new one must earn that.'

luxury:1.en: Lin sat on an upturned crate outside, eating a warm bun before her shift. She watched a polished car idle at the traffic light, music drifting from its windows. 'Clean socks every day is my *luxury*,' she told Tang, who had just arrived. Tang looked at the car, then at Lin's worn shoes, and said nothing at all.
luxury:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林看着豪华轿车感慨，对她来说最大的____其实很简单。
luxury:1.hook: Tang had noticed something taped under that car's bumper.
luxury:1.line: 'A warm bun before sunrise — that is *luxury* enough for me.'

announce:1.en: The Manager called me outside just before dawn. He pointed to a big paper sign taped to the lamp post across the street. 'I want to *announce* something,' he said, his breath making little clouds in the cold air. 'We are opening a second store next month, two blocks away.' He looked very pleased with himself.
announce:1.cnHint: 店长在店外向我____了一件大事：下个月要开新分店了。
announce:1.hook: But someone had already torn the bottom half of the sign away.
announce:1.line: 'I want to *announce* something important to the whole street.'

appropriate:1.en: Tang and I stood outside arranging the new shelf display near the front window. A delivery driver stopped to ask if the pavement space we were using was ours. Tang smiled and said it was *appropriate* for a store to use a small area right outside its own door. The driver shrugged and walked on.
appropriate:1.cnHint: 阿糖认为店门口占用一小块路面展示商品是____的。
appropriate:1.hook: The driver came back ten minutes later, this time with a notebook.
appropriate:1.line: 'It is *appropriate* for the store to use this small space here.'

chief:1.en: Lin from the corner shop opposite crossed the street and stopped in front of me. 'What is your *chief* reason for adding an outside display?' she asked, arms folded. I said it helped people see the fresh fruit. She wrote something in her small notebook and walked back without another word.
chief:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林问我们在店外摆放展示台的____原因是什么。
chief:1.hook: She had been watching our store all morning, and I had just noticed.
chief:1.line: 'Tell me your *chief* reason for putting the display outside.'

clearly:1.en: The Manager taped a hand-drawn map to the front door showing where the new branch would be. He had written the address in large letters and drawn a big red arrow. 'People can *clearly* see it from here,' he said, stepping back to admire his work. A passing cat walked straight into the door.
clearly:1.cnHint: 店长把新分店的地图贴在门上，这样路人就能____看到地址。
clearly:1.hook: A phone number on the map was missing its last digit.
clearly:1.line: 'From the pavement, people can *clearly* read every word on this sign.'

communicate:1.en: Tang handed me a walkie-talkie before my shift. 'The Manager wants us to *communicate* between the main store and the new one during the first week,' she said. I pressed the button to test it. A very confused voice from a nearby taxi answered back.
communicate:1.cnHint: 阿糖给了我一个对讲机，让我们能在两家店之间____。
communicate:1.hook: The taxi driver now knew exactly how many boxes of milk we had in stock.
communicate:1.line: 'We need to *communicate* between the two stores every hour.'

emphasis:1.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me outside to talk about the new branch. He spoke slowly and put a strong *emphasis* on the word 'cleanliness', tapping the wall each time he said it. A pigeon landed on his head during the third tap. He did not break eye contact once.
emphasis:1.cnHint: 店长在店外开会时，特别把____放在了'整洁'这个词上。
emphasis:1.hook: The pigeon seemed to be listening more carefully than I was.
emphasis:1.line: 'I want to put the *emphasis* on keeping the new store spotless.'

emphasize:1.en: Lin appeared at our door again, this time holding a small sign of her own. 'I just want to *emphasize* that my shop has been on this corner for nine years,' she said in a very calm voice. Then she smiled, turned around, and walked back across the empty street.
emphasize:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林再次来到我们门口，____说她的店已经在这个街角开了九年。
emphasize:1.hook: Her shop window was now lit up brighter than ever before.
emphasize:1.line: 'I want to *emphasize* that my store was here long before yours.'

england:1.en: A tall man in a thick coat came in just before sunrise and asked for a map of the area. He said he was from *England* and had taken the wrong bus three times trying to find a hotel. Tang drew him a little map on the back of a receipt. He stared at it for a long moment.
england:1.cnHint: 一位来自____的旅客迷路了，阿糖用收据背面给他画了一张地图。
england:1.hook: The hotel he was looking for had closed down two years ago.
england:1.line: 'Back in *England* the shops near my home close at nine — this is wonderful.'

extreme:1.en: The Manager stood outside in the early morning cold, pointing at the empty corner lot across the street. 'We open a second store there,' he said. The wind was *extreme*, cutting right through my jacket, but his eyes were warm and full of plans. I pulled my collar up and tried to look as confident as he did.
extreme:1.cnHint: 店长在寒风中指着对面空地，兴奋地谈论开____分店的计划。
extreme:1.hook: But someone else had already been watching that corner lot.
extreme:1.line: 'This wind is *extreme*, but nothing will stop us from opening there.'

style:1.en: Tang and I were helping the Manager sketch a layout for the new store on a napkin outside the old one. Tang kept drawing little decorations in the margins. 'We need a *style* that feels warm, like this place,' she said, tapping the window behind us. I looked at her tiny drawings and thought she was probably right.
style:1.cnHint: 唐在餐巾纸上画草图，坚持新店要有独特的____。
style:1.hook: Then Tang went quiet and stared down the street at something I could not see.
style:1.line: 'The new store needs a *style* that makes people want to stay.'

color:1.en: The Manager had brought three paint sample cards to show us on the pavement outside. He held them up against the store wall one by one. 'Which *color* should the new branch use?' he asked. Tang pointed at the soft yellow one. I pointed at the same one. The Manager smiled and tucked the other two away without a word.
color:1.cnHint: 店长拿着色卡站在店外，请大家为新分店选____。
color:1.hook: Later I noticed Lin had been standing just behind us the whole time.
color:1.line: 'Pick a *color* that makes customers feel at home the moment they walk in.'

meeting:1.en: The Manager called a quick *meeting* right on the pavement outside, the three of us standing in a small circle with paper cups of hot tea. He talked about the new store opening next month, the extra hours, the shared shifts. A cyclist slowed down to listen, then pedalled away with a thoughtful look.
meeting:1.cnHint: 店长在店门外临时召集了一次____，讨论新分店的开业安排。
meeting:1.hook: That cyclist came back ten minutes later and stood at the edge of the circle.
meeting:1.line: 'This *meeting* is short, but what we decide here really matters.'

volunteer:1.en: The Manager asked who would help set up the new store on Saturday. Tang raised her hand right away. I raised mine a second later, not wanting to seem slow. 'Good,' he said. 'Two *volunteers*.' A woman waiting at the bus stop nearby began clapping softly, which made all three of us laugh.
volunteer:1.cnHint: 店长问谁愿意周六帮忙布置新店，两名____很快举手。
volunteer:1.hook: The woman at the bus stop then walked over and asked if she could help too.
volunteer:1.line: 'I need *volunteers* who care about making this new place feel right.'

deliver:1.en: A young man on a bicycle stopped in front of us just as we were taping the opening notice to the new store window. He had a box balanced on the back rack. 'I was hired to *deliver* this to the new shop,' he said, checking his phone. We looked at each other. Nobody had ordered anything yet.
deliver:1.cnHint: 一个骑车的年轻人说他受雇来新店____一个包裹，可谁也没下过订单。
deliver:1.hook: The name on the box was not the Manager's name, or Tang's, or mine.
deliver:1.line: 'I was told to *deliver* this here before the store even opens.'

engineering:1.en: Tang pointed out a small crack in the wall of the new store space while we stood outside inspecting it before the lease was signed. The Manager said he knew someone who studied *engineering* and could check the whole building cheaply. I looked at the crack. It was thin as a hair, but somehow it felt important.
engineering:1.cnHint: 唐发现新店墙上有裂缝，店长说认识一个学____的人可以来检查。
engineering:1.hook: The engineering friend arrived the next morning and went very quiet when he saw the back wall.
engineering:1.line: 'My friend studied *engineering*, so trust me, he will know what that crack means.'

tiny:1.en: The new store space looked bigger on the sketch than it did in real life. Standing on the pavement outside, I could see it was *tiny*, barely wider than two parked bicycles. Tang said small could still be cosy. The Manager said nothing, just measured the door frame with his arms stretched wide, his face unreadable.
tiny:1.cnHint: 新店铺面比图纸上看起来____得多，大家站在门外面面相觑。
tiny:1.hook: Then the Manager smiled and said he had a very specific customer already in mind for this space.
tiny:1.line: 'The space is *tiny*, but the right design can make it feel twice as big.'

analysis:1.en: The Manager spread a city map across the hood of his car under the street lamp. He circled three corners with a red pen. 'My *analysis* shows this corner gets the most foot traffic after midnight,' he said, tapping the map. I leaned in, curious about what the circles meant for our little store.
analysis:1.cnHint: 店长在路灯下对地图做____，圈出了几个街角位置。
analysis:1.hook: But one circled corner already had a rival store.
analysis:1.line: 'My *analysis* shows this corner gets the most foot traffic after midnight.'

application:1.en: Outside the store, Tang was filling out a thick form on a clipboard, using the window ledge as a desk. 'It is the *application* for the new branch licence,' she explained, pressing hard with her pen. The wind kept lifting the pages. I held them down with both hands and wondered if we would really expand.
application:1.cnHint: 阿糖在店门外填写新分店的____表格，风不停地掀起纸页。
application:1.hook: The deadline was printed at the top — tomorrow, nine a.m.
application:1.line: 'It is the *application* for the new branch licence,' Tang said, pressing hard with her pen.

living:1.en: A tired-looking man stopped at our magazine rack and sighed at a headline about rising rent. 'Making a *living* in this city gets harder every year,' he said to no one in particular. The Manager overheard him from behind the counter and went very quiet. I stacked cups and pretended I had not heard anything.
living:1.cnHint: 一位路人感叹在这座城市____越来越难，店长听后沉默了。
living:1.hook: The Manager then pulled out his branch expansion folder and stared at it.
living:1.line: 'Making a *living* in this city gets harder every year,' the man said softly.

proposal:1.en: Lin appeared at the corner bus stop just as I was sweeping the entrance. She was reading a printed document and looked very serious. 'This is my *proposal* for a student-friendly branch near the university,' she said, holding it up. I recognized our store's logo at the top of the page and felt my stomach drop.
proposal:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在公交站拿着一份针对大学附近分店的____，上面印着我们店的标志。
proposal:1.hook: Her proposal had twelve pages — and our Manager's signature on page one.
proposal:1.line: 'This is my *proposal* for a student-friendly branch near the university,' Lin said.

relevant:1.en: The Manager pinned several printouts to the bus-stop notice board and stepped back to look. 'I only kept the *relevant* data — foot traffic, nearby schools, late-night demand,' he said, crossing his arms. A passer-by stopped to read one sheet with great interest. I wondered if posting business plans on a public board was entirely wise.
relevant:1.cnHint: 店长把____数据贴在公告栏上，一位路人驻足认真阅读。
relevant:1.hook: The passer-by took a photo of every single sheet.
relevant:1.line: 'I only kept the *relevant* data — foot traffic, nearby schools, late-night demand.'

senior:1.en: An elderly man in a neat jacket waited by the crosswalk outside our store every morning. Tang told me he was a *senior* from the neighbourhood, a retired city planner who knew every street. Tonight he stopped and stared at the Manager's new site map taped to our window. He said nothing, but he shook his head slowly.
senior:1.cnHint: 一位退休的____城市规划师盯着橱窗里的选址地图，缓缓摇了摇头。
senior:1.hook: Then he knocked on the glass and asked to speak to the Manager.
senior:1.line: 'I am a *senior* planner — that corner floods every rainy season,' he warned.

table:1.en: The Manager dragged a folding *table* out onto the pavement and covered it with maps, cost sheets, and two cups of coffee. 'Street-level planning meeting,' he announced proudly. Cars honked as they passed. Tang took one look, walked back inside, and brought him a paperweight shaped like a cat so the papers would not blow away.
table:1.cnHint: 店长把折叠____搬到街边开起了露天规划会议，文件差点被风吹走。
table:1.hook: A city inspector stopped on the pavement and cleared her throat loudly.
table:1.line: 'This *table* stays outside until we pick the best location,' the Manager said firmly.

campus:1.en: Lin pointed down the long avenue toward the university. 'The east gate of the *campus* sees three thousand students every evening,' she said, sketching a rough map on a napkin. I looked at the distant gate lights blinking in the dark. It seemed very far from our quiet corner — and yet somehow closer than before.
campus:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林指着大学校门，说____东门每晚有大量学生经过，并画出了简图。
campus:1.hook: She folded the napkin and slipped it into the Manager's jacket pocket.
campus:1.line: 'The east gate of the *campus* sees three thousand students every evening,' Lin said.

disadvantage:1.en: The Manager stood on the street corner, staring at the empty lot across from our store. 'The new branch will open there,' he said. I looked around: no bus stop, no school, no crowd. Being so far from everything felt like a real *disadvantage*. How would anyone find it?
disadvantage:1.cnHint: 店长看着对面的空地，觉得新分店的选址有很大的____。
disadvantage:1.hook: Then a moving truck pulled up, and Lin stepped out smiling.
disadvantage:1.line: 'Every *disadvantage* here is a chance to surprise people,' Lin said.

discuss:1.en: Tang and I sat on a low wall outside, eating rice from plastic boxes. The Manager had asked us to *discuss* the layout of the new branch before Monday. Tang drew a rough map on a napkin. A cold wind turned it over twice. We laughed and held it flat with our chopsticks.
discuss:1.cnHint: 唐和我在外面____新分店的布局，风把我们的草图吹乱了。
discuss:1.hook: Neither of us noticed the Manager standing right behind us.
discuss:1.line: 'We should *discuss* this before he changes his mind again,' Tang whispered.

psychological:1.en: The new branch site looked perfectly fine to me, but the Manager kept frowning at it. 'Location has a *psychological* effect on customers,' he said, hands in his pockets. 'If the street feels lonely, people feel lonely inside the store.' I had never thought about a building making someone feel anything.
psychological:1.cnHint: 店长认为选址会对顾客产生____影响，所以他一直皱着眉头。
psychological:1.hook: A woman walking past stopped, looked up at the sign, and smiled.
psychological:1.line: 'The colour of the walls has a *psychological* effect too,' the Manager added quietly.

request:1.en: A delivery driver stopped his scooter in front of the new site and handed me a note. It was a *request* from the landlord: all boxes must be moved off the pavement by noon. I looked at the stack of thirty boxes behind me. It was eleven fifty-three.
request:1.cnHint: 房东的____让我必须在正午前把所有箱子搬离人行道。
request:1.hook: Tang appeared from nowhere, already lifting the first box.
request:1.line: 'It is a polite *request*, but the tone is not polite at all,' Tang said.

symptom:1.en: Lin arrived at the building site looking pale. 'I walked here from the other store,' she said, sitting on a step. 'Forty minutes.' Tiredness was just one *symptom* of a bigger problem: nobody had thought about how the staff would actually get to this new branch every morning. We all went quiet.
symptom:1.cnHint: 林走了四十分钟才到，疲惫只是一个____，暴露出更大的问题。
symptom:1.hook: The Manager pulled out his phone and started searching bus routes.
symptom:1.line: 'Tiredness is just a *symptom*; the real problem is the commute,' Lin said.

upon:1.en: I found a folded letter sitting *upon* the front step of the new branch early that morning. It had no name on it. Inside, someone had written: 'This corner belonged to my father's noodle shop for twenty years. Please be good neighbours.' I stood there reading it twice, not sure what to do.
upon:1.cnHint: 我在新分店台阶____发现了一封没有署名的信。
upon:1.hook: I slipped the letter into my pocket before the Manager arrived.
upon:1.line: 'Leave it *upon* the counter so the Manager can see it,' Tang said.

argument:1.en: Lin and the Manager had an *argument* on the pavement outside the new branch. Their voices were not loud, but their faces were tight. Lin wanted a second entrance from the side street. The Manager wanted one door only. Neighbours walking dogs slowed down without meaning to. I pretended to count boxes.
argument:1.cnHint: 林和店长在人行道上为新分店是否开第二个入口发生了____。
argument:1.hook: Tang slipped Lin a coffee and the argument stopped for thirty seconds.
argument:1.line: 'My *argument* is simple: two doors means two chances to welcome people,' Lin said.

crisis:1.en: At noon, the water pipe under the pavement burst. A small fountain shot up beside the new branch door. The Manager called it a *crisis*. Tang called it free advertising. Three people stopped to take pictures. By the time the repair crew arrived, we had handed out twelve store flyers to the small crowd.
crisis:1.cnHint: 水管突然爆裂，店长觉得这是一场____，但唐觉得反而是个机会。
crisis:1.hook: One of the photographers asked when the store would open.
crisis:1.line: 'Every *crisis* brings a crowd, and every crowd is a customer,' Tang said.

destroy:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, hands on hips, staring at the broken front window. Someone had thrown a rock through it overnight. 'This kind of thing could *destroy* all our hard work before we even open,' he said, shaking his head slowly at the mess on the pavement.
destroy:1.cnHint: 店长看着被砸碎的橱窗，担心这会____新分店开业前的努力。
destroy:1.hook: But the rock had a small note tied to it.

drop:1.en: I was taping the grand-opening poster to the lamp post outside when I felt a cold *drop* hit my nose. I looked up. Dark clouds had rolled in fast. Across the street, Lin was putting up a rival poster on the opposite lamp post, and she looked up at the sky too.
drop:1.cnHint: 我在路灯柱上贴海报时，感到脸上落下了一____雨水，对面的隔壁咖啡店的林也抬头看天。
drop:1.hook: Lin smiled at me, then kept taping faster.
drop:1.line: 'Just one *drop* — the rain might hold off a little longer.'

efficiency:1.en: The Manager had drawn a detailed map of the new branch layout on a large sheet of paper. He tapped the delivery entrance with his pen. 'This position improves *efficiency* — trucks unload faster, staff move stock without crossing the main floor.' I nodded, quietly impressed by how much he had thought through.
efficiency:1.cnHint: 店长用地图向我解释新分店的布局如何提高____，我暗自佩服。
efficiency:1.hook: Then I noticed the map had no restroom marked.
efficiency:1.line: 'The whole design is about *efficiency* — every second counts.'

italian:1.en: A customer stopped me on the pavement outside the new branch and asked, in careful, accented English, if we carried any pasta. I said I was not sure yet. He smiled and said, 'I am *Italian*, and a good convenience store always has pasta.' I wrote the word in my notebook right there.
italian:1.cnHint: 一位顾客在门外用带口音的英语自称是____人，然后提了一个进货建议。
italian:1.hook: He left before I could ask his name.
italian:1.line: 'I am *Italian*, and pasta is not optional.'

newspaper:1.en: Early that morning I found a soaked *newspaper* pressed flat against the door of the new branch, left by someone before dawn. The headline was about rising rents on this street. I peeled it off carefully and read it on the step, a cold wind turning the pages for me.
newspaper:1.cnHint: 一大早，我在新分店门口发现了一份被打湿的____，头条内容让人担心。
newspaper:1.hook: The article mentioned our exact address.
newspaper:1.line: 'This *newspaper* story is going to bring us trouble.'

piece:1.en: Tang was crouched on the pavement outside, fitting together the flat-pack sign frame for the new branch. She held up a curved metal bar. 'This *piece* goes here, I think,' she said. I checked the instructions. She was wrong, but she had already forced it into place, and it looked fine, so I said nothing.
piece:1.cnHint: 阿糖在门外拼装招牌支架时，举起一____金属零件，我悄悄发现她装错了。
piece:1.hook: Three minutes later the whole frame tilted left.
piece:1.line: 'This *piece* is the tricky one — hold it steady.'

target:1.en: The Manager had taped a hand-drawn circle to the wall of the alley beside the new branch. He was tossing bundled advertising leaflets at it one by one, practising a quick underarm throw. 'Every postbox on this block is a *target*,' he told me cheerfully. I offered to help and missed every single postbox.
target:1.cnHint: 店长把街上每个邮箱都当____，练习快速投递广告单，我却一个也没投中。
target:1.hook: A neighbour opened her door and caught one in the face.
target:1.line: 'Every postbox on this street is a *target* today.'

actual:1.en: Lin walked past the new branch slowly, pretending to read her phone. I watched from inside. When she finally left, I stepped out and measured the gap between our sign and hers down the road. The *actual* distance was only forty metres — much closer than the Manager had said at the morning meeting.
actual:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林假装看手机经过新分店后，我出去测量，发现____距离比店长说的近得多。
actual:1.hook: Forty metres is close enough to hear each other's music.
actual:1.line: 'The *actual* distance is forty metres — I just checked.'

campaign:1.en: A big sign appeared overnight outside our store. 'FRESH FOOD, FAIR PRICE — YOUR CORNER STORE.' The Manager stood on the pavement, arms crossed, studying it with a small smile. Across the street, Lin's new shop was dark and quiet. Our *campaign* had begun before Lin even opened the doors.
campaign:1.cnHint: 店长在店外发起了一场____，抢在对手开门前造势。
campaign:1.hook: But Lin was already watching from a second-floor window.
campaign:1.line: 'This *campaign* will remind the whole street who was here first.'

hurt:1.en: I was restocking the shelf outside when a boy on a bicycle clipped the corner display, sending snack bags flying. He stopped, wide-eyed. 'Are you okay?' I asked. He nodded, cheeks red. 'My pride is *hurt* more than anything,' he said quietly, then helped me pick up every single bag.
hurt:1.cnHint: 一个骑车男孩撞倒了货架，自尊心受到了____。
hurt:1.hook: He came back the next morning with a small note.

initiative:1.en: Nobody told me to sweep the pavement before opening, but I did it anyway. Tang arrived and raised an eyebrow. 'The Manager didn't ask for that.' I shrugged. 'I just thought it needed doing.' Tang smiled slowly. 'Good. Around here, *initiative* is the one thing the Manager never has to reward twice.'
initiative:1.cnHint: 我主动打扫了门前街道，同事说这种____很难得。
initiative:1.hook: Tang then handed me a key I hadn't been given yet.
initiative:1.line: 'Around here, *initiative* is the one thing the Manager never rewards twice.'

jump:1.en: A small cat sat on the wall beside our outdoor display, eyeing the fish-cake samples on the low table. I watched, waiting. It measured the distance carefully, shifted its weight — then decided against it and looked away, proud. I laughed. Even the cat knew better than to *jump* without a plan.
jump:1.cnHint: 一只猫盯着试吃台，最终没有____下来。
jump:1.hook: The cat returned every night at exactly eleven.
jump:1.line: 'Even a cat knows not to *jump* without checking first.'

lie:1.en: The new branch was going up two blocks away, and already a rumour was spreading on the street: the Manager was selling the old store. I asked Tang directly. Tang just laughed. 'Rumours *lie* all the time — the Manager loves this corner more than anything.' Still, the construction noise made everyone uneasy.
lie:1.cnHint: 街上关于老店的谣言四起，同事说谣言会____。
lie:1.hook: Then the Manager came out and stared at the construction in silence.
lie:1.line: 'Rumours *lie* all the time — don't listen to the street.'

lunch:1.en: At noon the street outside was warm and busy. A regular customer, an older man, always sat on the low wall beside our entrance to eat his *lunch* — rice and one small dish from the place next door. He nodded at me today. 'Best seat on the block,' he said, unwrapping his chopsticks.
lunch:1.cnHint: 一位常客每天在店门口的矮墙上吃____。
lunch:1.hook: Today he left before finishing, and his chopsticks stayed on the wall.
lunch:1.line: 'Best seat on the block for *lunch*, and nobody charges rent.'

necessarily:1.en: Lin set up a small outdoor stand just around the corner, full of bright snacks at low prices. Tang looked worried. I shook my head. 'A lower price doesn't *necessarily* mean better value,' I said. 'People come here because they trust us.' Tang was quiet for a moment, then nodded and went back inside.
necessarily:1.cnHint: 对手摆出了低价摊位，但我说低价不____意味着更好。
necessarily:1.hook: Lin smiled at me from across the stand as if reading my thoughts.
necessarily:1.line: 'A cheap price doesn't *necessarily* mean people will stay.'

psychologist:1.en: A woman stopped outside and read our new window sign — 'We're open when the world isn't' — for a long time. Then she came in and bought only a warm tea. She told me she was a *psychologist* and worked late helping others feel better. 'Small lights matter,' she said, nodding at our sign.
psychologist:1.cnHint: 一位____在深夜路过，被我们橱窗上的标语打动了。
psychologist:1.hook: She left her card on the counter without a word.
psychologist:1.line: 'As a *psychologist*, I know — small lights matter more than you think.'

pursue:1.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter at midnight. 'There is a second store,' he said quietly. 'I plan to *pursue* this dream before summer.' He tapped a street corner two blocks away. Outside, a figure in a grey jacket was already standing there, staring at the same spot.
pursue:1.cnHint: 店长深夜展示地图，说他要____开分店的梦想，但窗外已有人在盯着那个地址。
pursue:1.hook: The figure outside had not moved for twenty minutes.
pursue:1.line: 'I will *pursue* this dream before summer, no matter what.'

site:1.en: The Manager asked me to walk with him after my shift. We stopped at a dusty corner lot two blocks away. 'This is the *site* for our new store,' he said, eyes bright. A torn paper sign on the fence read the same address — but in someone else's handwriting.
site:1.cnHint: 店长带我去看新店的____，但铁栅栏上已经有另一个人写的地址。
site:1.hook: The handwriting on that sign looked oddly familiar.
site:1.line: 'This corner lot is the *site* I chose three months ago.'

absorb:1.en: Tang handed me a thick folder on my third night. 'Read this — store layout, regular orders, supplier names,' she said. 'Try to *absorb* it before the weekend rush.' I nodded and opened page one. By page three I found a note that was not part of any training guide.
absorb:1.cnHint: 同事让我____这本厚厚的资料，但翻到第三页时我发现了一张奇怪的便条。
absorb:1.hook: The note had no name on it, only a time: 2:47 a.m.
absorb:1.line: 'You need to *absorb* all of this before Saturday night.'

advance:1.en: The Manager called a small meeting before dawn. 'Our new store opens in two weeks,' he said. 'This is a big *advance* for us.' Tang clapped softly. I smiled too — but Lin had been standing just outside the glass door, and now he was gone.
advance:1.cnHint: 店长宣布新店开张是一大____，但竞争对手林已悄悄离开了门口。
advance:1.hook: Lin's coffee cup was still warm on the step outside.
advance:1.line: 'Opening a second store is a real *advance* for this little shop.'

capable:1.en: A delivery driver dropped six heavy boxes at once and looked at me. 'New kid, can you handle these alone?' Tang crossed her arms and smiled. 'He is more than *capable*,' she said firmly. I stacked all six without dropping a single one. The driver raised an eyebrow and left a tip on the counter.
capable:1.cnHint: 送货员质疑我，同事说我完全____胜任，结果我证明了自己。
capable:1.hook: The driver came back ten minutes later with one more box.
capable:1.line: 'Trust me, the new clerk is perfectly *capable* of handling this.'

dollar:1.en: An old man counted coins on the counter every Tuesday, buying the same rice ball. Tonight he was one *dollar* short and stared at his palm. I quietly added it from the small tip jar Tang kept by the register. He looked up, said nothing, and placed a folded paper crane on the counter.
dollar:1.cnHint: 老人每次差一____买饭团，我悄悄补上了，他留下了一只纸鹤。
dollar:1.hook: Next Tuesday, three paper cranes were waiting on the doorstep.
dollar:1.line: 'Just one *dollar* short again — same as every week, I know.'

double:1.en: The Manager showed me the new store plan. The floor space was nearly *double* that of our current shop, with room for a small seating area by the window. I was excited until I noticed the delivery schedule pinned behind it — Lin's store had booked the same suppliers a day earlier.
double:1.cnHint: 新店面积几乎是现在的____，但竞争对手已提前一天预订了同样的供应商。
double:1.hook: Same suppliers, same street, one day apart — this was no accident.
double:1.line: 'The new place is almost *double* the size of what we have now.'

federal:1.en: A tired woman in a neat coat came in just before three in the morning, bought a coffee, and spread papers across the small side table. I could see the words '*federal* grant' on the top sheet. She circled a number, exhaled slowly, and smiled at the wall. I wondered what she was building.
federal:1.cnHint: 一位女士深夜在店里查看____补贴文件，悄悄地微笑，像是找到了什么答案。
federal:1.hook: She left the cap of her pen on the table, perhaps on purpose.
federal:1.line: 'This *federal* grant could change everything for our project.'

insist:1.en: The Manager stood outside the newly rented corner unit, pointing at the sign above the door. Lin crossed her arms and shook her head. 'Too small,' she said. The Manager chose to *insist* that the spot was perfect — the foot traffic alone would double our sales.
insist:1.cnHint: 店长____说转角新店的位置绝对没问题，但隔壁咖啡店的林不这么认为。
insist:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and showed him something alarming.
insist:1.line: I *insist* this corner is the best spot on the street.

investigation:1.en: A city inspector arrived at the corner plot where our new store would be built. She walked slowly around the fence, writing notes and taking photos. 'This is a routine *investigation*,' she told me, though her eyes kept stopping on the same crack in the ground.
investigation:1.cnHint: 一位检查员来对新店地块进行____，她的目光一直落在地上那道裂缝上。
investigation:1.hook: She circled the crack a third time, then called someone quietly.
investigation:1.line: Our *investigation* of this site will take the whole morning.

limited:1.en: Tang spread the budget sheet across the hood of the delivery van outside. Only three weeks until the new branch opened, and the numbers looked thin. 'Our time is *limited*, our money is more limited, and the Manager still wants a coffee machine,' Tang said, laughing without joy.
limited:1.cnHint: 阿糖在车外查看预算单，发现开新店的资金和时间都十分____。
limited:1.hook: Then Tang spotted a line item neither of us had approved.
limited:1.line: Our budget is *limited*, so we must choose very carefully.

listen:1.en: I stood on the pavement as the Manager gave instructions to two workers fitting the new shop window. He spoke fast, waving his hands. One worker leaned close to *listen*, while the other quietly did the opposite of everything the Manager said, and the window tilted left.
listen:1.cnHint: 店长在店外指挥工人安装橱窗，其中一个工人根本不____他的话。
listen:1.hook: A loud crack came from above, and everyone froze.
listen:1.line: Please *listen* — the sign goes on the left side, not the right.

master:1.en: The old man who repaired locks on our street watched the workers struggle with the new store door for twenty minutes. Finally he walked over, took the tool, and fixed it in seconds. Tang whispered to me, 'He is a true *master*. Every lock on this block knows his hands.'
master:1.cnHint: 街上的老修锁人出手帮忙，阿糖悄悄告诉我他是这一行真正的____。
master:1.hook: The old man winked and slipped a small key into his pocket.
master:1.line: A true *master* never needs more than one try.

newly:1.en: The *newly* painted sign above the branch hung bright yellow in the morning sun. I had walked past this corner a hundred times, but the colour made everything feel different — bigger, more real. Lin stood beside me, coffee in hand, and for once said nothing critical at all.
newly:1.cnHint: 新店____刷好的招牌在阳光下格外醒目，连一贯挑剔的隔壁咖啡店的林也沉默了。
newly:1.hook: Then a pigeon landed on the sign and refused to move.
newly:1.line: The *newly* painted wall looks perfect from across the street.

north:1.en: The Manager unfolded a city map on the pavement and stabbed his finger at a dot. 'Our main store is here. The new branch is *north*, near the university.' Lin looked at the distance between the two dots and quietly calculated how long the supply run would take each morning.
north:1.cnHint: 店长在路边摊开地图，指着____边那家新分店的位置给大家看。
north:1.hook: Lin's calculation ended with a soft, unhappy whistle.
north:1.line: The new branch is *north* of here, close to the university gate.

obviously:1.en: The delivery truck stopped in front of the new branch, blocking the entire lane. Cars began to pile up. The driver shrugged at me. '*Obviously* there is nowhere else to park,' he said cheerfully. A cyclist squeezed past, shouting words I chose not to repeat to the Manager.
obviously:1.cnHint: 送货车堵住了新店门前的整条路，司机却____觉得这很合理。
obviously:1.hook: A traffic officer turned the corner, notebook already open.
obviously:1.line: '*Obviously* the truck must stop here — there is no other space.'

pose:1.en: Outside the new branch store, the Manager asked everyone to stand together for a photo. Lin crossed his arms and turned sideways. Tang stood on tiptoe. I had no idea what to do with my hands. 'Hold your *pose*,' the Manager said, squinting at his phone screen, 'the light is perfect.'
pose:1.cnHint: 店长让大家在新分店门口摆好____，准备拍照留念。
pose:1.hook: Then a pigeon landed on the Manager's head.
pose:1.line: 'Hold your *pose* — don't move until I count to three!'

stimulate:1.en: The Manager hung a bright new sign above the branch store door. Passing students stopped and stared. 'A little colour can *stimulate* curiosity,' he told me proudly, smoothing his jacket. Tang leaned against the wall eating a rice ball, looking completely unstimulated. I decided not to mention that.
stimulate:1.cnHint: 店长认为鲜艳的新招牌能____路人的好奇心，吸引他们进店。
stimulate:1.hook: One student walked in, bought nothing, and left a note.
stimulate:1.line: 'Bright colours *stimulate* people — trust me, I read a whole article.'

switch:1.en: The branch store stood one street over from ours. On busy nights the Manager would *switch* Tang and me between the two locations without warning. Tang always got the quiet one. I always got the queue that stretched to the corner. I was starting to notice a pattern.
switch:1.cnHint: 忙碌的夜晚，店长会悄悄把我和阿糖____到不同的门店。
switch:1.hook: Tonight the Manager smiled at me with unusual kindness.
switch:1.line: 'We need to *switch* you two again — starting right now.'

treatment:1.en: Lin arrived at the branch store opening carrying a small cactus as a gift. The Manager accepted it with great ceremony. Tang and I had brought nothing and received a sharp look. 'Different *treatment* for different effort,' the Manager said quietly. Lin smiled. The cactus looked smug too.
treatment:1.cnHint: 开业那天，隔壁咖啡店的林带了礼物，店长对他和我们的____明显不同。
treatment:1.hook: The cactus was later found on my workstation.
treatment:1.line: 'Same work, same hours — we deserve equal *treatment*, don't we?'

union:1.en: Three neighbourhood store clerks stood outside comparing receipts in the early morning cold. Tang called it a *union* meeting. The Manager called it loitering. The woman from the flower shop said she just wanted someone to talk to. We agreed to meet every Thursday. The Manager pretended not to hear.
union:1.cnHint: 几个街区的店员在门外自发组成____，定期交流心得。
union:1.hook: The flower-shop woman mentioned she had once managed fifty people.
union:1.line: 'A small *union* of clerks — that's all we are, nothing scary.'

acknowledge:1.en: After the branch store ribbon was cut, a regular customer named Old Mr Fang clapped loudly from across the street. The Manager gave a small bow. He did not *acknowledge* that Fang had predicted the opening date three weeks ago — correctly, down to the hour. Fang just winked at me.
acknowledge:1.cnHint: 店长没有____一位老顾客早就准确预测了开业日期这件事。
acknowledge:1.hook: Old Mr Fang pulled a folded paper from his coat pocket.
acknowledge:1.line: 'You should *acknowledge* when someone gets it exactly right.'

alike:1.en: Standing outside the new branch store, Tang and I wore the same uniform, the same tired eyes, and the same lukewarm smile. A child tugged her mother's sleeve. 'They look *alike*,' she whispered. Tang and I turned to each other slowly. We had never noticed before. It was mildly alarming.
alike:1.cnHint: 一个小孩发现我和阿糖看起来____，我们俩都有点惊到了。
alike:1.hook: The Manager later admitted he had hired us on the same day.
alike:1.line: 'You two dress *alike*, stand alike — are you sure you're not related?'

analyze:1.en: Lin stood on the pavement across from the new branch store with a small notebook, watching customers go in and out. 'I *analyze* the foot traffic before every shift,' he told me seriously. I looked at his notebook. It was full of tiny drawings of clouds. He closed it very quickly.
analyze:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林声称自己会____新店的人流量，但他的笔记本里另有玄机。
analyze:1.hook: He offered to show me page one, then immediately changed his mind.
analyze:1.line: 'I always *analyze* the street before I go in — old habit.'

belong:1.en: The Manager led me outside at dawn to look at the empty shop across the street. 'That corner *belongs* to us now,' he said, pointing at a sign in the window. Workers were already unloading boxes from a truck. I had no idea the store was growing. Neither, it seemed, did the woman watching from the doorway opposite.
belong:1.cnHint: 店长在黎明时带我出去，指着对面空店铺说那个角落____我们了。
belong:1.hook: The woman across the street had a key in her hand.
belong:1.line: 'That corner *belongs* to us now,' the Manager said quietly.

beneficial:1.en: Tang handed me a warm cup outside the back door. 'The morning air is *beneficial*,' she said, stretching her arms wide. 'Breathe before the rush starts.' The street was still quiet, just a cat and one old man with a bag. The old man paused, looked at our new sign, and walked away very fast.
beneficial:1.cnHint: 阿糖在后门外说清晨的空气对人____，但那位老人看到新招牌后却快步离开了。
beneficial:1.hook: The old man turned the corner and pulled out a phone.
beneficial:1.line: 'Fresh air is *beneficial* — trust me,' Tang said, smiling.

characteristic:1.en: Lin stood on the pavement studying our new branch with his arms crossed. His slow, careful nod was a *characteristic* I had learned to watch for — it meant he was thinking hard and saying little. He picked up a flyer from the ground, read both sides, and set it back down gently before walking away.
characteristic:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在人行道上仔细打量新分店，他那慢慢点头的____意味着他在认真思考。
characteristic:1.hook: The flyer he had read was gone the next morning.
characteristic:1.line: 'That slow nod is his *characteristic* — watch out,' Tang whispered.

director:1.en: A man in a dark coat stopped outside and asked if the Manager was in. 'I am the *director* of the building company,' he said, handing me a card through the open door. He glanced at the half-built shelves inside, then at the street, as if measuring something. He said he would return at noon. He did not look like someone who forgot appointments.
director:1.cnHint: 一位穿深色外套的男士自称是建筑公司的____，他打量了半天后说中午还会再来。
director:1.hook: His card had two phone numbers, but one was crossed out in pen.
director:1.line: 'Tell your manager the *director* of the building company called.'

emerge:1.en: We had been stacking boxes in the new branch all morning when the Manager told us to stop. He wanted to see the shop *emerge* slowly, one shelf at a time. 'Rushing makes the whole thing feel cheap,' he said. Outside, a group of students pressed their faces to the glass, fogging it with their breath.
emerge:1.cnHint: 店长让我们慢慢来，想看着新店一点一点____，而不是着急赶工。
emerge:1.hook: One student was quietly drawing the shop layout in a notebook.
emerge:1.line: 'Let the shop *emerge* slowly — don't rush it,' the Manager said.

exact:1.en: Tang measured the new sign three times before she was happy. 'The *exact* centre matters,' she told me, holding the ruler flat against the wall. I held one end and tried not to laugh. When we finally stepped back, the sign was perfect — and Lin was standing on the pavement, already taking notes on a small pad.
exact:1.cnHint: 阿糖反复测量新招牌，坚持说____的中心位置很重要，而隔壁咖啡店的林已经在旁边做笔记了。
exact:1.hook: Lin's notes were written in a hand too small to read from the door.
exact:1.line: 'The *exact* centre matters — hold the ruler still,' Tang said.

guest:1.en: The first *guest* to walk into the new branch was a girl with a backpack and muddy boots. She looked around slowly, as if she had been here before, though we had only opened the doors an hour ago. She bought one bottle of water, paid, and said, 'Nice place.' Then she asked when the old shop had moved.
guest:1.cnHint: 新分店的第一位____背着包、穿着沾泥的靴子，她问的那个问题让我们都愣了一下。
guest:1.hook: None of us knew what old shop she meant.
guest:1.line: 'Welcome — you're our very first *guest* today,' I told her.

massive:1.en: The delivery truck that arrived at the new branch was *massive*, far too wide for the narrow lane beside the shop. The driver climbed down, looked at the gap, and shrugged at me with a smile. Tang called the Manager. The Manager called someone else. Half the street stopped to watch. Lin watched too, from across the road, not smiling at all.
massive:1.cnHint: 送货卡车____得根本开不进小巷，整条街的人都停下来看热闹，只有隔壁咖啡店的林没有笑。
massive:1.hook: Lin crossed the street and spoke quietly to the driver.
massive:1.line: 'That *massive* truck will never fit in the lane,' Tang said flatly.

mix:1.en: The Manager hands me a small cup outside the new branch site. 'Try this,' he says. It is a *mix* of hot barley tea and lemon juice — his test drink for the second store menu. I sip it slowly. The street is cold, but the cup is warm.
mix:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址外让我尝一杯他为新店菜单设计的____。
mix:1.hook: He watches my face like my answer decides everything.
mix:1.line: 'This *mix* took me three weeks to get right.'

necessity:1.en: Tang and I stand outside the empty shop unit the Manager is considering. Tang points at the narrow door. 'A wider entrance is a *necessity*,' she says firmly. 'People carrying bags will just walk past.' The Manager nods slowly and writes something down in his small notebook.
necessity:1.cnHint: 唐在查看新店铺位时强调，宽敞的入口是____。
necessity:1.hook: Then the Manager crosses out a number on the rent page.
necessity:1.line: 'A wider door is a *necessity*, not a luxury.'

stuff:1.en: I help the Manager carry boxes of sample products to the new branch building early one morning. There are bottles, cups, small tools, and paper bags — all sorts of *stuff* piled into a cart. A passer-by stops and asks if we are moving house. We both laugh.
stuff:1.cnHint: 一大早，我帮店长把各种样品____推到新店去。
stuff:1.hook: One box, taped shut, has no label at all.
stuff:1.line: 'This *stuff* all needs to be sorted before noon.'

translate:1.en: Lin arrives at the new branch corner holding a printed sign. 'The display needs to *translate* the cosy feeling of the old store,' she says, pinning the sign to the board outside. She steps back, tilts her head, and frowns. Something is still not quite right.
translate:1.cnHint: 林认为新店的展示需要____老店那种温馨的感觉。
translate:1.hook: She pulls the sign down and reaches for a red pen.
translate:1.line: 'We need to *translate* that warmth into the new space.'

wander:1.en: Business is slow on the first preview day of the new branch. I *wander* along the block, slipping a small flyer under each shop door. A noodle stall owner reads it, raises an eyebrow, and asks how late the new store will stay open. I tell him: all night.
wander:1.cnHint: 新店预览日客流稀少，我在附近街区____派发传单。
wander:1.hook: The noodle stall owner folds the flyer and puts it in his pocket.
wander:1.line: 'I always *wander* this block after closing — I will stop by.'

warn:1.en: Tang calls me from the new branch door just before the preview opens. 'I need to *warn* you,' she says, 'the coffee machine here runs hotter than ours. The first cup will surprise you.' I reach for the handle anyway. Tang steps back with a small smile.
warn:1.cnHint: 唐____我新店的咖啡机温度比老店高，小心第一杯。
warn:1.hook: The cup burns my fingers before it even reaches my lips.
warn:1.line: 'I *warn* everyone once — after that it is their own fault.'

advocate:1.en: Outside the new branch, a regular customer named Old Chen tells the Manager he is a strong *advocate* of keeping the store open past midnight. 'Night workers need somewhere,' he says, pressing his point with a raised finger. The Manager listens, then quietly asks me to note it down.
advocate:1.cnHint: 常客老陈在新店外积极做深夜营业的____，说夜班工人需要这样的地方。
advocate:1.hook: Old Chen then mentions he knows twelve other night workers on this street.
advocate:1.line: 'I am an *advocate* for every person who works the night shift.'

cite:1.en: Lin stands at the corner near the new branch with a printed chart. She *cites* three nearby stores that failed in the past two years. 'Location, location, location,' she says, tapping each failed store name with her pen. The Manager listens without blinking. Then he taps our chosen spot on the map.
cite:1.cnHint: 林____了附近三家倒闭店铺的案例，提醒大家注意选址风险。
cite:1.hook: The Manager's finger stays on that spot for a long moment.
cite:1.line: 'I *cite* these three cases so we do not repeat their mistakes.'

writer:1.en: Outside the store, a street *writer* sits under the lamp, filling a notebook with quick pen strokes. Tang waves through the window. The writer looks up, nods, then returns to the page. I wonder what story is growing there. Ten minutes later, the writer closes the notebook and walks toward our door.
writer:1.cnHint: 街边有位____在灯下写东西，阿糖跟他打招呼。
writer:1.hook: The writer is coming inside with that mysterious notebook.
writer:1.line: 'That street *writer* comes here every Tuesday night,' Tang whispered.

addition:1.en: The Manager stands on the corner with a measuring tape, marking the ground with chalk. 'Perfect spot for the new store,' he says. Lin from the rival shop across the street watches with crossed arms. The *addition* of a second location means double the work but also double the chance to serve this neighborhood. Lin's expression darkens.
addition:1.cnHint: 店长在街角测量，准备____一家新店，对面隔壁咖啡店的林看起来不高兴。
addition:1.hook: Lin is walking over, and he does not look happy.
addition:1.line: 'This *addition* will help more customers,' the Manager said cheerfully.

alternative:1.en: Rain pours down outside. A customer stands under our awning, staring at two buses stopped at the corner. 'Which one goes downtown?' she asks me. I point left, then right. 'That one is faster, but this one is a quieter *alternative*.' She bites her lip, choosing. Behind her, both buses start their engines.
alternative:1.cnHint: 下雨天，顾客在屋檐下问哪路车去市中心，我告诉她有两个____。
alternative:1.hook: Both buses are leaving—she must decide now.
alternative:1.line: 'Is there an *alternative* route?' the customer asked nervously.

amazing:1.en: Outside, a street musician plays a small wooden flute. The melody floats through the night air, clear and bright. People slow their steps to listen. Even Lin, standing in his own shop doorway across the street, tilts his head. '*Amazing*,' Tang breathes beside me. Then the musician stops and bows. What happens next surprises everyone.
amazing:1.cnHint: 街头音乐家吹笛子，连隔壁咖啡店的林都停下来听，阿糖说真____。
amazing:1.hook: The musician opens the flute case—it is completely empty.
amazing:1.line: 'That sound is *amazing*!' Tang said, eyes wide with delight.

ease:1.en: The Manager leans against the lamp post outside, phone to his ear, nodding slowly. His shoulders relax. 'Good, good,' he says. Tang whispers that the bank approved the loan for the new store. I watch the Manager's face soften with *ease*. He ends the call, takes a deep breath, and smiles. Then his phone rings again.
ease:1.cnHint: 店长靠着路灯打电话，得知贷款批了，整个人放松下来，很____。
ease:1.hook: The second call wipes the smile off his face.
ease:1.line: 'I can finally breathe with *ease* now,' the Manager sighed happily.

frequent:1.en: I sweep the sidewalk outside when I notice the same delivery truck parked at the corner for the third time today. '*Frequent* visitor,' Tang jokes, carrying out the trash. The driver waves. But this time, instead of driving off, he steps out and walks toward Lin's shop across the street. Tang and I exchange a glance.
frequent:1.cnHint: 我在外面扫地，注意到同一辆货车今天第三次停在街角，很____。
frequent:1.hook: The driver is carrying a thick envelope into Lin's shop.
frequent:1.line: 'That truck is a *frequent* visitor today,' Tang said suspiciously.

hope:1.en: A small girl stands outside our store, clutching a coin purse and staring at the vending machine on the corner. She counts her coins twice. Not enough. Her face falls. Tang notices and steps outside with a smile and a candy bar. 'My treat,' he says. The girl's eyes fill with *hope*. She bows and runs off. But she forgets something.
hope:1.cnHint: 小女孩在外面数硬币不够买东西，阿糖送她糖果，她眼中充满____。
hope:1.hook: Her coin purse lies open on the ground.
hope:1.line: 'Maybe next time,' the girl whispered, voice small with fading *hope*.

imply:1.en: Lin stands outside his shop, arms folded, watching the Manager post a sign on the corner: 'New Store Opening Soon!' Lin does not speak, but his silence seems to *imply* a challenge. The Manager nods politely and walks back. Tang mutters that trouble is coming. That evening, a city inspector arrives on our street.
imply:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在外面看店长贴新店广告，虽然没说话但似乎____不满。
imply:1.hook: The inspector is heading straight for our door.
imply:1.line: 'His look seemed to *imply* he was not pleased,' I told Tang.

gather:1.en: Outside the store, a crowd begins to *gather* near the crosswalk. I step out to see what is happening. A street musician has set up with a small keyboard, playing a cheerful tune. People stop, smile, and a few drop coins into his hat. The Manager waves at me from inside, pointing at his watch.
gather:1.cnHint: 人群在便利店外的人行横道____，因为有街头音乐家在表演。
gather:1.hook: But the musician keeps glancing nervously at someone across the street.
gather:1.line: 'When people *gather* like this, we should put a sign outside,' the Manager says.

imagine:1.en: Lin stands across the street, staring at our store with folded arms. I cannot *imagine* why she looks so upset today. Her own shop is doing well. Tang whispers that Lin heard a rumor about us expanding. The Manager just smiles and keeps arranging the fruit display by the door, completely calm.
imagine:1.cnHint: 林站在街对面盯着我们的店，我无法____她为什么这么生气。
imagine:1.hook: Then Lin pulls out her phone and makes a call.
imagine:1.line: 'I can't *imagine* why she's worried,' Tang says quietly. 'We're not her enemy.'

instance:1.en: The Manager teaches me how to handle difficult customers on the street corner. He gives me an *instance* from last month: a man demanded a refund for a drink he had already finished. The Manager stayed polite, offered him a coupon instead, and the man left happy. I take notes carefully.
instance:1.cnHint: 店长给我讲了一个上个月的____：如何处理难缠的顾客。
instance:1.hook: Just then, that same customer walks toward our door again.
instance:1.line: 'Let me give you one *instance*,' the Manager says. 'Kindness costs us nothing.'

numerous:1.en: I sweep the sidewalk in front of the store and find *numerous* small items: a hair clip, a button, a toy car, even a single earring. People drop things without noticing. I collect them in a small box by the register. Tang says someone always comes back looking for something they lost.
numerous:1.cnHint: 我在店门口的人行道上发现了____件小东西，都是顾客掉的。
numerous:1.hook: A young woman rushes up, breathless, searching the ground frantically.
numerous:1.line: 'We get *numerous* lost things every week,' Tang tells me. 'Keep the box handy.'

puzzle:1.en: A delivery truck parks outside, but the driver looks confused. He holds a map and scratches his head. The street signs here *puzzle* many newcomers because two roads share similar names. I step outside and point him toward the correct turn. He thanks me and drives off with a relieved smile.
puzzle:1.cnHint: 送货司机看起来很困惑，因为这里的路牌____了很多新来的人。
puzzle:1.hook: But he left a small package on our doorstep by mistake.
puzzle:1.line: 'These street names *puzzle* everyone,' I say. 'Even I got lost my first day.'

remind:1.en: An elderly man stops outside and peers through the window. He does not come in, just stands there smiling. Tang says he used to run a shop on this exact corner forty years ago. The sight of our store seems to *remind* him of old times. He waves at us and continues his evening walk.
remind:1.cnHint: 一位老人站在店外，我们的店似乎____了他很多往事。
remind:1.hook: But tonight, he turns back and reaches for the door handle.
remind:1.line: 'This place must *remind* him of something important,' Tang says softly.

truly:1.en: I watch the morning light touch the street corner, turning everything gold. After a long quiet night, I *truly* understand why the Manager loves this shift. Outside, a jogger waves at me through the window. A cat stretches on the warm pavement. The city wakes up gently here, one person at a time.
truly:1.cnHint: 经过一整夜安静的夜班，我____明白了店长为什么喜欢这个班次。
truly:1.hook: Then I notice someone has been sleeping in the doorway next door.
truly:1.line: 'You *truly* see the neighborhood on the night shift,' the Manager told me once.

valuable:1.en: A businessman rushes out of a taxi and runs to our door. He left something *valuable* in the cab: his laptop bag. I help him call the taxi company while Tang checks our security camera to get the car number. We find the footage and the man relaxes. Ten minutes later, the driver returns with the bag.
valuable:1.cnHint: 一位商人把____的东西落在了出租车里，我们帮他找回来。
valuable:1.hook: The businessman pulls out his wallet, but hesitates over which bill to choose.
valuable:1.line: 'Thank you for keeping something so *valuable* safe,' the businessman says, clearly relieved.

therefore:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, clipboard in hand. The street was narrow and the nearest bus stop was two blocks away. Fewer people passed here each hour, *therefore* he counted heads for twenty minutes before making any decision.
therefore:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址的街道上数人流，因为____他要先观察再决定。
therefore:1.hook: His pen stopped moving when a familiar face appeared.
therefore:1.line: Foot traffic is low, *therefore* we open at six, not eight.

truth:1.en: Lin arrived early and walked the same block three times. She pulled out her notebook and wrote one line at the top: the *truth* is that this corner gets morning crowd but loses everyone by noon. She underlined it twice and kept walking.
truth:1.cnHint: 林在街上反复观察，在笔记本上写下了关于这个街角的____。
truth:1.hook: What she wrote next made her close the notebook fast.
truth:1.line: I checked the numbers — the *truth* is the rent is too high.

protein:1.en: Tang was handing out small sample cups near the door of the new site. Each cup held a warm soy drink. A passing student stopped, sipped, and asked what was in it. Tang said it was high in *protein* and good for morning classes. The student took two cups.
protein:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门口派发豆浆样品，向路过的学生介绍饮品富含____。
protein:1.hook: The student came back with five friends ten minutes later.
protein:1.line: One cup of this has more *protein* than your breakfast sandwich.

traffic:1.en: The Manager asked Tang to stand at the corner for one full hour and count. By the end, Tang's notebook was full. The morning *traffic* was surprisingly heavy — office workers, students, delivery riders — all pouring past the empty shopfront like a small river.
traffic:1.cnHint: 唐在街角数了一小时的____，结果让店长眼睛一亮。
traffic:1.hook: One delivery rider slowed down and stared at the empty shop.
traffic:1.line: The *traffic* here at eight in the morning beats our old spot.

cat:1.en: A small orange *cat* sat on the window ledge of the empty shopfront all morning. People stopped to look at it, smiled, and then noticed the 'coming soon' sign behind it. Lin watched from across the street and wrote: best free advertisement we never planned.
cat:1.cnHint: 一只橘猫坐在新店橱窗上，意外地吸引了许多路人注意到____的开业公告。
cat:1.hook: Nobody knew who the cat belonged to.
cat:1.line: That *cat* has done more for us today than any flyer.

sugar:1.en: A grandmother stopped Tang outside and pointed at the sample drinks. She asked, very seriously, how much *sugar* was inside each cup. Tang checked the label and read the number out loud. She nodded, took a cup, and said that was exactly the right amount.
sugar:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在街上拦住唐，认真询问样品饮料里的____含量。
sugar:1.hook: She then asked how many cups she could take home.
sugar:1.line: Less *sugar* than a candy bar — I checked the label myself.

balance:1.en: Lin set up a small folding table outside to test a display stand for bottled drinks. The bottles kept sliding. She shifted them left, then right, then added a rubber mat underneath. Finally, the whole row held its *balance* perfectly, even when a bus rumbled past.
balance:1.cnHint: 林在店外调整展示架上的瓶装饮料，反复摆弄才让它们保持____。
balance:1.hook: Then a cyclist clipped the edge of the table on the way by.
balance:1.line: Move the big bottles to the back and the stand will *balance*.

baby:1.en: A young father pushed a stroller past the new shop and slowed down. His *baby* was asleep inside, one small fist curled around a soft toy. The man looked at the 'opening next week' sign and whispered, so as not to wake her, 'good, we live just around the corner.'
baby:1.cnHint: 一位年轻爸爸推着婴儿车路过新店，看到开业告示后轻声说了一句话，没有吵醒____。
baby:1.hook: He came back alone that evening and stood there for a long time.
baby:1.line: Keep your voice down — there is a *baby* sleeping right there.

store:1.en: The Manager stopped me outside the new corner lot and pointed at the empty building. 'We are opening a second *store* here next month,' he said proudly, sweeping his arm wide. Painters were already mixing colours on the pavement. I stared at the peeling walls and wondered who had agreed to this plan.
store:1.cnHint: 店长在街角空房子前告诉我们，新____要开张了。
store:1.hook: But the building permit was nowhere to be found.
store:1.line: 'This *store* will be bigger and better than the first one.'

budget:1.en: Tang spread a large sheet of paper on the bonnet of the Manager's old car. Columns of numbers covered every corner. 'The *budget* for the new branch is already gone,' Tang whispered, tapping the bottom line with one finger. Passing scooters drowned out the Manager's reply, but his face said everything.
budget:1.cnHint: 同事在路边发现新分店的____已经花光了。
budget:1.hook: Someone had been buying far too many decorative plants.
budget:1.line: 'Our *budget* ran out before we even bought the shelves.'

grant:1.en: Lin arrived waving a thin envelope above her head. 'The city gave us a small *grant* to help with the new branch,' she announced on the pavement outside our shop. The Manager grabbed the letter, read it twice, and let out a long breath. The amount was helpful, though nowhere near enough.
grant:1.cnHint: 竞争对手兴冲冲地带来了一份城市____的消息。
grant:1.hook: Lin's smile suggested she already knew how to spend it.
grant:1.line: 'A city *grant* like this does not come around very often.'

hospital:1.en: A tired nurse in a white coat stopped at our pavement display of snacks on his way home from the *hospital* across the road. He bought four rice balls without a word. I noticed bandages on his left hand and mud on his shoes. Tang said the night shift there ended at exactly three in the morning.
hospital:1.cnHint: 一位从对面____下班的护士在门口买了东西。
hospital:1.hook: He would return every night at the same hour, saying nothing.
hospital:1.line: 'I walk past from the *hospital* and your light is always on.'

island:1.en: An old woman set up a small card table on the pavement and laid out hand-painted postcards of a green *island* surrounded by blue water. She told me she had grown up there and painted every card from memory. Tourists stopped, pointed, and smiled. I bought one without asking the price.
island:1.cnHint: 一位老奶奶在街边摆出一张画满故乡____的明信片摊。
island:1.hook: The island on the cards did not appear on any map I knew.
island:1.line: 'Every card shows the *island* where I was born and raised.'

native:1.en: Tang introduced me to a cheerful man leaning on the lamp-post outside. 'He is a *native* of this neighbourhood,' Tang said. 'He remembers when this corner was a cabbage field.' The man laughed and patted the wall of our shop as if greeting an old friend. I felt like the only stranger on the street.
native:1.cnHint: 同事向我介绍了一位街区____居民，他还记得这里以前的样子。
native:1.hook: He then mentioned something strange buried beneath the old field.
native:1.line: 'As a *native* here, I have seen this corner change three times.'

tradition:1.en: A group of elderly neighbours gathered on the pavement at dawn, doing slow morning exercises in neat rows. Tang told me it was a long-standing *tradition* on this street, going back forty years. The Manager watched from the doorway, nodding. I joined the back row, stumbled twice, and received polite applause anyway.
tradition:1.cnHint: 同事告诉我街边的晨练是这条街几十年来的____。
tradition:1.hook: One of the elders then invited me to lead next Friday.
tradition:1.line: 'This morning exercise is a *tradition* nobody wants to break.'

africa:1.en: A tall student stood at the corner reading a map, his backpack covered in small flag patches. Lin pointed out one patch of the continent of *Africa* and said he had just returned from a teaching programme there. He was trying to find a place to stay for one night. The Manager glanced at our stockroom and nodded slowly.
africa:1.cnHint: 一位刚从____回来的学生在街角迷了路，店长似乎有个主意。
africa:1.hook: The stockroom had not been empty for a very good reason.
africa:1.line: 'I spent three months in *Africa* and just arrived back tonight.'

teenager:1.en: Just after midnight, a *teenager* in a school uniform pushed open the door and dropped a heavy bag on the counter. 'Just five minutes of warm air, please,' he said. He looked exhausted, like someone who had been studying since dawn. I handed him a hot drink and asked nothing.
teenager:1.cnHint: 一个深夜还穿着校服的____走进店里，只想借一点暖气歇脚。
teenager:1.hook: But his uniform had the wrong school's name on it.
teenager:1.line: 'I'm only a *teenager*, but I work harder than most adults I know.'

patient:1.en: The Manager stood outside in the cold, waiting for the new sign to be delivered. An hour passed. Then two. He did not check his phone or pace the pavement. He was remarkably *patient*, arms folded, eyes calm, watching the empty street as though he had all the time in the world.
patient:1.cnHint: 店长在寒风中____地等候新招牌送到，一动不动地站了好几个小时。
patient:1.hook: The delivery van that finally arrived was carrying the wrong sign.
patient:1.line: 'You have to be *patient* when you run a shop — rushing breaks more than it fixes.'

classroom:1.en: Tang pointed up at the empty building across the street. 'That used to be a *classroom*,' she said, 'where I failed my first English test.' Now the windows were dark and the door was sealed with tape. She said it quietly, like she was reading a small sad notice pinned to her own heart.
classroom:1.cnHint: 唐指着对面废弃的建筑，说那里曾是她经历失败的____。
classroom:1.hook: She then slipped a folded test paper out of her pocket.
classroom:1.line: 'Every *classroom* I ever sat in smelled exactly like chalk and cold tea.'

vehicle:1.en: A large *vehicle* blocked the pavement outside at two in the morning, engine running, no driver in sight. I stepped out to look. Boxes were stacked in the back — all labelled with our store's address but a branch number I did not recognise. I stood in the yellow streetlight, very still.
vehicle:1.cnHint: 深夜一辆无人驾驶的____停在门外，车里装着写有陌生分店编号的箱子。
vehicle:1.hook: Then the engine cut out, and a phone inside one of the boxes began to ring.
vehicle:1.line: 'Every *vehicle* that stops here at night makes me a little nervous, honestly.'

remote:1.en: Lin arrived just before three, shaking rain off her jacket. 'The new branch site is confirmed,' she said, spreading a map on the counter. She tapped a spot far from the city centre, surrounded by empty land. 'It is quite *remote*,' I said. She smiled in a way that meant she already knew that.
remote:1.cnHint: 林摊开地图，指着新分店选址——一个离市区非常____的地方。
remote:1.hook: She folded the map before I could read the street name.
remote:1.line: '*Remote* is fine — the quieter the street, the more loyal the customers.'

zoo:1.en: A small boy pressed his face to our window at six in the morning, fogging the glass with his breath. He had a paper wristband on that said '*zoo*' in green letters. He had clearly been walking a long time. He looked at the shelf of toy animals we kept by the door and went very quiet.
zoo:1.cnHint: 一个戴着____门票手环的小男孩，大清早独自出现在店门口。
zoo:1.hook: He knew every animal's name but could not say where his parents were.
zoo:1.line: 'The *zoo* lets you in free before seven — that part was great, at least.'

card:1.en: A woman in a long coat asked me to hold a small envelope at the counter. 'Someone will come for it,' she said. Inside, I could see the corner of a *card* — hand-drawn flowers, careful writing. She was gone before I could ask a single question. The envelope sat there all night, uncollected.
card:1.cnHint: 一位神秘女士托我保管一个信封，里面露出一张手绘____的一角。
card:1.hook: At closing time, I noticed the name on the front was mine.
card:1.line: 'Leave the *card* exactly where it is — they will know where to find it.'

gene:1.en: The Manager and his sister stood side by side in the morning light, arguing about where the new branch should go. They had the same frown, the same folded arms, the same stubborn tilt of the chin. 'It must be a *gene*,' Tang whispered from behind the coffee machine. I decided not to laugh out loud.
gene:1.cnHint: 店长和他妹妹争执时，唐悄悄说他们固执的样子简直像同一个____。
gene:1.hook: Then his sister turned and asked me to cast the deciding vote.
gene:1.line: 'Stubbornness might just be a *gene* in our family — Mum is exactly the same.'

content:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, arms crossed, studying the new sign above the door. He had spent three days picking the right colour. Now he stepped back, tilted his head, and smiled. He looked *content* — the way a person looks when a long effort finally lands exactly right. I watched from inside, holding a mop, feeling oddly proud too.
content:1.cnHint: 店长在门外看着新招牌，脸上露出____的神情。
content:1.hook: But across the street, someone was taking photos of the sign.
content:1.line: 'I am finally *content* with how this place looks,' the Manager said softly.

divide:1.en: The Manager paced the pavement outside, measuring with his feet. He wanted to *divide* the front step into a waiting zone and a pick-up zone with just a strip of yellow tape. Tang watched from the doorway, trying not to laugh. I handed the Manager the tape. He laid it down with the focus of a person building something important.
divide:1.cnHint: 店长用黄色胶带把门前的台阶____成两个区域。
divide:1.hook: By midnight, someone had peeled up one end of the tape.
divide:1.line: 'We need to *divide* the space so customers stop bumping into each other,' the Manager said.

generate:1.en: The Manager hammered a small chalkboard sign into the flower box beside the door. 'Daily special — one new item every night,' he announced. His plan was to *generate* fresh interest from people walking past after midnight. Tang gave me a look that said this might actually work. By two in the morning, four strangers had stopped to read it.
generate:1.cnHint: 店长在门口立了小黑板，希望每晚____新的客流。
generate:1.hook: One of those strangers asked a question none of us could answer.
generate:1.line: 'A good sign outside will *generate* more foot traffic,' the Manager said firmly.

operate:1.en: Lin appeared on the pavement across the street, turning a key in the door of the empty shop unit opposite. I had not noticed that unit before. Tang leaned out of our doorway and whispered that Lin had been planning to *operate* a small store there for months. The Manager heard this from inside and went very quiet for a moment.
operate:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林打开对面空铺子的门，打算在那里____一家小店。
operate:1.hook: The Manager then picked up his phone and made a call.
operate:1.line: 'I plan to *operate* the new place seven days a week,' Lin said with a calm smile.

properly:1.en: Before the Manager arrived for his morning check, Tang and I rushed to arrange the new outdoor display stand *properly* — bottles in a straight line, price cards facing forward, nothing leaning. We finished one second before the door opened. The Manager looked at the stand, then at us, then nodded once. That single nod felt like a certificate.
properly:1.cnHint: 我和阿糖赶在店长到来前把门外展示架____地整理好。
properly:1.hook: The Manager then pointed at one bottle we had missed.
properly:1.line: 'If you set things up *properly* outside, customers trust the whole store,' Tang said.

render:1.en: Rain started just as the Manager finished taping a new poster to the outside wall. Within a minute, the ink began to run. The water did not *render* the whole poster unreadable — the price and the arrow stayed clear — but the cheerful drawing of a rice ball melted into a soft blur. Tang bit her lip. I offered to reprint it.
render:1.cnHint: 突如其来的雨水把门外的海报____得模糊不清。
render:1.hook: The Manager said to leave it, and gave no reason why.
render:1.line: 'A little rain should not *render* our hard work useless,' the Manager said quietly.

resolve:1.en: Tang and I stood on the pavement watching Lin measure the frontage of the new shop across the road. I felt uncertain. Tang, however, had a look of calm *resolve* — chin up, arms loose at her sides. 'We have been here longer,' she said simply. She walked back inside and began rearranging the window display with fresh energy.
resolve:1.cnHint: 看到对面的竞争对手，阿糖脸上却显出一种____的神情。
resolve:1.hook: Lin glanced over and gave Tang a small, knowing nod.
resolve:1.line: 'Our *resolve* to do better is worth more than any new sign,' Tang said.

seemingly:1.en: Lin stood outside the new shop, *seemingly* relaxed — chatting with a delivery driver, laughing easily, checking nothing. But I noticed Lin's eyes move to our window every thirty seconds. Tang noticed too. We said nothing to each other. We just made sure the display looked perfect, the lights were bright, and the door was wide open.
seemingly:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林____很悠闲地站在对面，其实眼神一直瞟向我们这边。
seemingly:1.hook: That night Lin came in and bought a coffee without a word.
seemingly:1.line: 'Lin is *seemingly* calm, but watch the eyes,' Tang whispered to me.

childhood:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, staring at the empty lot. 'This corner,' he said quietly, 'is where I used to buy ice pops after school.' His *childhood* memory of this street was exactly why he chose it. I watched his face soften in a way I had never seen before.
childhood:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店选址前，回忆起他在这条街度过的____时光。
childhood:1.hook: Then he pointed to the wall and said, 'Dig carefully.'
childhood:1.line: 'This street holds my *childhood*, so this is where we build.'

equal:1.en: Lin and I carried supply boxes from the truck to the new branch entrance. She counted every trip with sharp eyes. After an hour she stopped and said the work was not *equal* — she had made twelve trips and I had made nine. I had no argument. I picked up two boxes at once.
equal:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林搬货时发现两人的工作量不____，当场指出来。
equal:1.hook: She smiled, but her next words were not a compliment.
equal:1.line: 'Twelve against nine is not *equal*, so carry two boxes next time.'

inspire:1.en: A small girl stopped outside the new branch site and watched the workers paste the bright store sign onto the wall. 'I want to work in a place like that one day,' she told her mother. The Manager overheard her and turned to me. 'Moments like that *inspire* me to do this right,' he said.
inspire:1.cnHint: 一个小女孩在店外驻足，她的话深深____了店长。
inspire:1.hook: The girl left, but the Manager wrote something down in his notebook.
inspire:1.line: 'Little moments like that truly *inspire* me to keep going.'

narrow:1.en: The delivery truck could not park near the new branch because the side road was too *narrow* for it to turn. The driver leaned out and shook his head. We ended up carrying every box by hand from the main street, four trips each, under the bright morning sun.
narrow:1.cnHint: 送货车因为小路太____，无法靠近新分店，大家只能徒步搬运。
narrow:1.hook: On the last trip, Tang found one box had already been opened.
narrow:1.line: 'That road is too *narrow*; we carry everything by hand today.'

quantity:1.en: Outside the new branch, Tang ticked items off a clipboard as workers unloaded the truck. She stopped and frowned. The *quantity* of bottled water on the list was eighty, but only fifty-three bottles sat on the pavement. She called the supplier at once, her voice calm but very firm.
quantity:1.cnHint: 阿糖在门外清点货物，发现瓶装水的____对不上单据。
quantity:1.hook: The supplier's answer made Tang go very quiet for a moment.
quantity:1.line: 'The *quantity* on this sheet is eighty, but I count fifty-three.'

sustainable:1.en: The Manager unrolled a poster on the pavement outside the new branch. It showed bins for paper, plastic, and glass. 'A store that wastes nothing is a *sustainable* store,' he told the small crowd of curious neighbours. One old man nodded slowly. I made a note to learn the recycling rules before opening day.
sustainable:1.cnHint: 店长在店外向邻居们介绍新分店的环保理念，强调经营要____。
sustainable:1.hook: The old man then asked a question nobody had an easy answer for.
sustainable:1.line: 'A shop that wastes nothing is a *sustainable* shop, neighbours.'

delay:1.en: Rain started just as we were about to hang the new branch sign above the door. The Manager looked at the sky and sighed. 'We will *delay* the sign until tomorrow,' he said. We covered the sign with a cloth and stood under the awning, watching the street fill with puddles and hurrying umbrellas.
delay:1.cnHint: 突然下起雨来，店长决定____招牌的安装工作到明天。
delay:1.hook: Under one umbrella, a stranger paused and stared at the covered sign.
delay:1.line: 'Rain means we *delay* the sign — cover it carefully, please.'

identity:1.en: A reporter stopped me outside the new branch and asked whether this store had a clear *identity* that set it apart from every other convenience store on the street.
