I hesitated, then pointed to the handwritten menu in the window and the recycling bins by the door. She wrote something down and smiled.
identity:1.cnHint: 一位记者在门外问新分店有什么能体现自身____的特色。
identity:1.hook: Her article, the Manager later told us, was already half-written.
identity:1.line: 'Every good shop needs an *identity* that people remember clearly.'

modern:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, pointing at the glass front. 'This is going to be *modern*,' he said, arms wide. Tang and I looked at the old stone wall next to it and then at each other. The building did not look ready to agree with him.
modern:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店选址前，自豪地描述他心中____的新店。
modern:1.hook: Then Tang noticed the sign still on the door.
modern:1.line: 'This store will be *modern* — clean lines, bright lights, the works.'

officer:1.en: A city *officer* in a dark jacket stopped in front of our new branch sign, clipboard in hand. He read every word slowly, then wrote something down. The Manager hurried out from inside, smoothing his shirt, his smile about three sizes too big for his face.
officer:1.cnHint: 一名____来到新分店门前，仔细查看招牌，店长赶紧跑出来迎接。
officer:1.hook: The officer tore off a yellow sheet and held it out.
officer:1.line: 'Good morning, *officer* — can I offer you a free coffee?'

convince:1.en: Lin stood across the street, arms crossed, watching workers hang our new branch sign. I walked over to try to *convince* her the two stores could share the same block. She listened, then looked at the sign, then at me. 'You believe that?' she asked. I paused a little too long.
convince:1.cnHint: 我试图____隔壁咖啡店的林，两家店开在同一条街上没有问题。
convince:1.hook: She pulled out her phone and made a call.
convince:1.line: 'Nothing you say will *convince* me this is good for either of us.'

directly:1.en: The Manager called me *directly* on my day off and said the branch door lock was broken. I was still in my pyjamas. Tang had the day off too, so it was just me, a bus ride, and a screwdriver I was not sure how to use. The street was very quiet and very cold.
directly:1.cnHint: 店长____打电话给我，让我去处理新分店的门锁问题。
directly:1.hook: When I arrived, the door was already wide open.
directly:1.line: 'I'm calling you *directly* because Tang is not picking up.'

extend:1.en: The Manager decided to *extend* the awning over the new branch entrance so customers could stand outside without getting wet. He measured twice, ordered once, and the awning arrived two metres too short. We stood in the light rain looking at it. It covered exactly the recycling bin.
extend:1.cnHint: 店长决定____新分店门口的遮雨棚，结果尺寸出了问题。
extend:1.hook: A regular walked up, umbrella in hand, and said nothing.
extend:1.line: 'We need to *extend* it at least another metre — maybe two.'

rat:1.en: Tang screamed from the back of the new branch at six in the morning. I ran in to find her standing on a box, pointing at a corner. A single small *rat* sat there looking equally surprised. The Manager arrived eight minutes later, slightly out of breath, holding a broom he clearly had no plan for.
rat:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新分店后仓发现了一只____，大家都乱成一团。
rat:1.hook: The rat disappeared before anyone moved again.
rat:1.line: 'There is a *rat* back here and I am NOT dealing with it alone.'

saturday:1.en: The branch soft opening was set for *Saturday*, which the Manager said was perfect because foot traffic would be high. It rained all day. Tang and I stood near the door, handing out small flyers to three people and one dog. The dog seemed the most interested.
saturday:1.cnHint: 新分店选在____试营业，但当天的情况和预期差了很远。
saturday:1.hook: Lin's store across the street looked very busy.
saturday:1.line: 'Why did we pick *Saturday*? Everyone is at the market on Saturday.'

april:1.en: By *April* the branch still had no working heater, but the Manager said summer was coming so it did not matter. Tang disagreed loudly. I taped an extra layer of cardboard over the gap in the back wall and considered it a small personal win. Outside, the trees were just starting to show green.
april:1.cnHint: 到了____，新分店还没装好暖气，大家对此看法不一。
april:1.hook: Then the Manager mentioned the air-con was also not ordered yet.
april:1.line: 'It is *April* — cold in the morning still, and you want to wait?'

artificial:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, frowning at a row of plastic flowers by the door. 'These look cheap,' he said. The *artificial* blooms caught no sunlight, gave no scent, and fooled nobody. A real garden would cost more, but first he needed to count what was left in the budget.
artificial:1.cnHint: 店长看着新店门口那排假花，觉得它们毫无生气，开始盘算预算还剩多少。
artificial:1.hook: Then he noticed someone had already pulled one flower out.
artificial:1.line: These *artificial* flowers make the whole entrance look fake.

confirm:1.en: Tang rushed out of the new branch just as the delivery truck was pulling away. She waved both arms and shouted until the driver stopped. 'I need you to *confirm* the order,' she said, holding up her clipboard. 'Three boxes of rice balls, not thirty.' The driver checked his sheet and went pale.
confirm:1.cnHint: 唐冲出新店门口，拦住送货司机，要求对方____订单数量是否正确。
confirm:1.hook: The driver's list showed a number nobody had ever written down.
confirm:1.line: Please *confirm* the rice ball count before you leave.

context:1.en: Lin leaned against the wall outside, reading a note the Manager had taped to the new branch door. The words alone sounded odd, but Lin had worked here long enough to understand the *context*: new staff, tight budget, and a grand opening in three days. She folded the note and slipped it into her pocket.
context:1.cnHint: 林靠在新店门外，读着店长贴的告示，凭借____理解了那些听起来奇怪的指示。
context:1.hook: The note had a second line that Lin chose not to mention.
context:1.line: You need the *context* to understand what the Manager really means.

date:1.en: Tang knelt on the pavement outside the new branch, turning a box of milk cartons toward the morning light. She checked every carton carefully. 'The *date* on these is tomorrow,' she called up to the Manager on the step above her. He rubbed his eyes. One day of margin was not enough for a grand opening.
date:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门外检查牛奶保质期，发现____只剩明天，立刻告诉了店长。
date:1.hook: The Manager turned the box over and found a second stamp underneath.
date:1.line: The *date* on every carton is tomorrow — that is too close.

flexible:1.en: The Manager spread a long paper schedule across the bonnet of his car, parked just outside the new branch. 'Our hours have to be *flexible* for the first month,' he told Tang, tapping the chart. 'Some mornings quiet, some nights mad busy.' Tang nodded, already doing the maths on how little sleep that left her.
flexible:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门外摊开排班表，告诉唐第一个月的上班时间必须____。
flexible:1.hook: Tang spotted her name in every single weekend box.
flexible:1.line: The schedule must stay *flexible* until we know the busy hours.

fly:1.en: A single *fly* circled the tray of sample dumplings Tang had set out on the folding table in front of the new branch. She fanned it away three times. Each time it returned. A small crowd had gathered, watching the fly more than the dumplings. Tang smiled anyway and held out a toothpick.
fly:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门外摆出试吃饺子，却有一只____一直在旁边打转，引来路人围观。
fly:1.hook: One old man in the crowd seemed to be cheering for the fly.
fly:1.line: That *fly* has been here longer than any of our customers.

judge:1.en: Lin stood at the corner outside, watching strangers walk past the new branch without stopping. She tried not to *judge* too quickly — the sign was still crooked, the lights were not on yet, and it was only seven in the morning. Still, she counted: forty people passed, and not one looked through the window.
judge:1.cnHint: 林站在新店门口的街角，看着路人对新店视而不见，努力克制自己不要过早____。
judge:1.hook: The forty-first person stopped, stared, and then took a photo.
judge:1.line: Don't *judge* the foot traffic until the sign is fixed.

oil:1.en: Tang crouched beside the small generator the Manager had rented for the outdoor opening event. It coughed twice and went silent. 'It needs *oil*,' said a passer-by in a grey coat, without breaking his stride. Tang looked at the Manager. The Manager looked at Tang. Neither of them had thought to bring any.
oil:1.cnHint: 唐和店长在新店外摆弄发电机，一个路人随口说机器需要加____，两人面面相觑。
oil:1.hook: The man in the grey coat had already turned the corner and vanished.
oil:1.line: This generator will not start without *oil* — do we have any?

comfortable:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, wrapped in a thick *comfortable* blanket from the store. The street was cold and dark, but he smiled at the empty shopfront. 'This corner will be ours soon,' he said softly, pulling the blanket tighter.
comfortable:1.cnHint: 店长裹着____站在新店选址外面，对着空店面微笑。
comfortable:1.hook: Then a light flickered on inside the empty shop.
comfortable:1.line: 'Wrap up — a *comfortable* blanket is better than any heater out here.'

conclusion:1.en: Lin studied the foot traffic outside the future branch for an hour, counting people and writing notes. She tapped her notebook and announced her *conclusion* to the Manager: this corner was perfect for a new store. The Manager nodded slowly, then looked at the building across the street.
conclusion:1.cnHint: 林仔细观察了新店附近的人流，得出了她的____。
conclusion:1.hook: But the Manager's eyes stayed on a sign across the road.
conclusion:1.line: 'My *conclusion* is simple — this corner is the best spot we have.'

formal:1.en: Tang arrived at the outdoor site visit in a neat jacket and tie, looking far too *formal* for a windy street corner. The Manager handed him a broom and pointed at the pavement. Tang stared at the broom for a long moment before slowly removing his jacket.
formal:1.cnHint: 唐穿着正装来参加新店选址考察，店长递给他一把扫帚。
formal:1.hook: The jacket landed on a stranger's bicycle.
formal:1.line: 'Did nobody say this was a *formal* visit? I dressed up for nothing.'

happiness:1.en: Standing outside the painted shopfront of the new branch on opening morning, the Manager felt a quiet *happiness* rise in his chest. Years of long night shifts had led to this moment. He took a photo of the door with his old phone and sent it to no one in particular.
happiness:1.cnHint: 新店开业那天早上，店长站在门外心中涌起了____。
happiness:1.hook: A reply came back in seconds, from a number he did not recognise.
happiness:1.line: 'This is real *happiness* — and we built it one night shift at a time.'

intelligent:1.en: Lin had mapped three rival stores, two bus stops and one school within walking distance. 'That is an *intelligent* choice of location,' the Manager admitted, folding her hand-drawn map. Lin smiled and tucked the map into her bag before he could look at it again.
intelligent:1.cnHint: 林分析了新店的选址，店长不得不承认这是个____的决定。
intelligent:1.hook: She had already chosen the second location too.
intelligent:1.line: 'You made an *intelligent* call — I did not expect that from the competition.'

novel:1.en: Waiting for the landlord outside the future branch, Tang pulled out a thick *novel* and leaned against the wall. Cars passed. Pigeons arrived. The landlord did not. By page thirty Tang had started recommending the book aloud to the pigeons.
novel:1.cnHint: 唐在新店门外等房东时，掏出一本____看了起来。
novel:1.hook: The landlord finally appeared — and recognised the book.
novel:1.line: 'This *novel* is long enough to survive any landlord who runs late.'

political:1.en: The two landlords for the neighbouring units had not spoken in years over some old *political* disagreement about the neighbourhood council. The Manager stood between them on the pavement, smiling very carefully, holding a bag of free snacks from the store.
political:1.cnHint: 两位房东因为旧日的____矛盾多年不说话，店长夹在中间。
political:1.hook: Both landlords reached for the same snack at the same moment.
political:1.line: 'Let us leave *political* matters aside — there is enough snack for everyone.'

property:1.en: The landlord unrolled a long document on the bonnet of his car, pointing at figures and diagrams. 'This *property* has good bones,' he told the Manager, tapping the page. The Manager looked at the cracked wall behind the landlord and said nothing for a while.
property:1.cnHint: 房东在新店外向店长介绍这处____的情况，店长盯着墙上的裂缝。
property:1.hook: The crack in the wall quietly grew another centimetre.
property:1.line: 'The *property* has good bones — just ignore the small crack out back.'

passion:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, eyes bright despite the cold. 'This street needs us,' he said, sweeping one arm toward the empty shopfront. His *passion* for the project was so clear that even a passing cyclist slowed down to listen. I found myself believing every word.
passion:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店选址前，对扩张计划充满____，连路过的行人都被吸引驻足。
passion:1.hook: The cyclist asked one question that made the Manager go pale.
passion:1.line: 'My *passion* for this store will make the whole street come alive.'

temperature:1.en: We taped a handwritten sign to the new branch window before sunrise. By mid-morning a small crowd had gathered outside, checking it. The *temperature* had dropped sharply overnight, and people were pressing close to the glass just to feel the warmth leaking from inside. The store was not even open yet.
temperature:1.cnHint: 新店开业前，室外____骤降，路人纷纷靠近橱窗取暖。
temperature:1.hook: One face in the crowd looked oddly familiar to me.
temperature:1.line: 'The *temperature* outside is awful — can we please open the door early?'

board:1.en: A large wooden *board* leaned against the wall outside the new branch, painted with the store name in bright letters. Tang and I had carried it three blocks on foot that morning. A gust of wind caught it just as we set it down, and it nearly knocked over a flower cart.
board:1.cnHint: 唐和我抬着新店的大招牌____走过三个街区，险些撞倒路边的花车。
board:1.hook: The flower-cart owner crossed her arms and stared at us.
board:1.line: 'Careful with that *board* — it took me two hours to paint!'

handle:1.en: The new branch door had a long silver *handle* that stuck out at an awkward angle. Every customer who tried to enter pulled the wrong way first. I stood outside watching, keeping a tally in my head. By noon, not one person had opened it correctly on the first try.
handle:1.cnHint: 新店的门把手装得很别扭，中午前没有一位顾客能一次顺利____开门。
handle:1.hook: Then one small child walked up and opened it perfectly.
handle:1.line: 'Someone needs to fix this *handle* before the Manager sees it.'

ideal:1.en: Tang pointed to the corner plot across the street, where morning light fell evenly and foot traffic was steady all day. 'That spot is *ideal*,' she said, pulling out her notebook. She had been studying the street for a week, counting people, timing buses. I had not expected her to be so thorough.
ideal:1.cnHint: 唐指着街对面的角落铺位，认为那里是开新店____的地点。
ideal:1.hook: Lin appeared behind us, notebook already open.
ideal:1.line: 'That sunny corner is the *ideal* place for our second branch.'

ride:1.en: Lin arrived at the new branch site on a battered old bicycle, slightly out of breath. 'Long *ride*?' I asked. She shrugged and locked the bike to a lamp post without answering. Then she walked straight to the window, pressed her face against the glass, and began writing notes on a small pad.
ride:1.cnHint: 林骑车赶到新店选址，一下车就贴着橱窗开始做____调查笔记。
ride:1.hook: Her notes were written in a code I could not read.
ride:1.line: 'It was a long *ride*, but I had to see this place for myself.'

adjust:1.en: The new sign outside the branch kept tilting to one side in the wind. I climbed on a step stool three times to *adjust* it, each time certain I had fixed it, each time wrong. A small group of schoolchildren stopped to watch and offered loud advice after every attempt. None of it helped.
adjust:1.cnHint: 我爬上梯凳三次____新店的歪斜招牌，围观的小学生越帮越乱。
adjust:1.hook: The Manager walked around the corner and looked up without a word.
adjust:1.line: 'You need to *adjust* the left side — no, your other left!'

basis:1.en: The Manager explained why he chose this particular street corner for the new branch. Foot traffic, nearby offices, a bus stop twenty metres away — every point was laid out calmly. 'We made this decision on a solid *basis*,' he said, tapping his folder. Standing there in the cold, I almost felt convinced.
basis:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址现场逐条说明了以扎实____做出这一决策的理由。
basis:1.hook: Tang quietly checked her phone and raised one eyebrow.
basis:1.line: 'Every good choice needs a solid *basis*, and we have done the work.'

relative:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the corner, pointing at the empty shop across the street. 'Location is everything,' he said. The new branch would cost a lot, but the risk was *relative* — the store already had loyal customers nearby, so failure seemed less likely than it first appeared.
relative:1.cnHint: 店长指着街对面说，开分店的风险其实是____的，因为附近已经有稳定客源。
relative:1.hook: Then a stranger stepped out of that empty shop, holding a key.
relative:1.line: The risk is *relative* when you already know the neighbourhood.

rent:1.en: Tang swept the pavement outside while the Manager studied a printed page. 'The *rent* for that corner space is higher than I expected,' the Manager muttered, folding the page slowly. Tang stopped sweeping and glanced at the number. Her eyes went a little wide, but she said nothing and kept her broom moving.
rent:1.cnHint: 店长看着街角那间空铺子的____，皱起了眉头。
rent:1.hook: Tang had seen that exact number written in Lin's notebook last week.
rent:1.line: The *rent* alone might sink us before we even open.

round:1.en: The Manager walked a slow *round* of the block, checking every angle of the proposed new site. He counted foot traffic, noted the bus stop, and tested the streetlight. I jogged to keep up. By the time we returned to the starting point, he had already made his decision — or so his smile suggested.
round:1.cnHint: 店长绕街区走了一____，仔细观察新店选址的人流和环境。
round:1.hook: But the smile vanished the moment he saw Lin standing at the door.
round:1.line: One *round* of the block and I know this spot is right.

structure:1.en: Lin arrived uninvited and stood staring at the old building the Manager was considering. 'The *structure* is the problem,' she said, tapping the cracked wall. 'Too many repairs.' The Manager crossed his arms. I quietly took notes. Whatever Lin's reason for being here, it did not feel like helpful advice.
structure:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林指着那栋旧楼的____说问题很大，但她的出现本身才更让人起疑。
structure:1.hook: The Manager later found a fresh crack that had not been there yesterday.
structure:1.line: That *structure* will cost you more than the rent ever will.

typical:1.en: 'A 24-hour store on a corner with a bus stop and a night market nearby — *typical* winning formula,' the Manager said, almost to himself. He had opened stores before and he recognised the signs. I looked at the busy street and slowly understood why he always chose his spots so carefully.
typical:1.cnHint: 店长说这个街角具备____的好店铺条件，一眼就相中了。
typical:1.hook: What he did not mention was who had opened a store here first.
typical:1.line: This is a *typical* good spot — busy street, late-night crowd.

vacation:1.en: I had taken this night-shift job during my summer *vacation*, expecting a quiet few weeks. Instead, the Manager announced plans for a new branch and pulled everyone into the project. Tang looked just as surprised as I felt. The sleepy corner store had suddenly turned into something much busier than I had bargained for.
vacation:1.cnHint: 我只是想在____期间打份轻松的工，没想到赶上了店长决定开分店。
vacation:1.hook: The Manager then handed me a map and said, 'You scout it.'
vacation:1.line: I joined during my *vacation* — I did not sign up for this.

acquire:1.en: The Manager explained that the plan was to *acquire* the lease on the old tea shop two streets away before anyone else moved on it. Time was short. Tang nodded and immediately left to make calls. I realised this was not a casual idea — the Manager had been planning this quietly for weeks.
acquire:1.cnHint: 店长打算抢在别人前面____那家旧茶铺的租约。
acquire:1.hook: Tang came back pale-faced — someone had already called about the lease.
acquire:1.line: We need to *acquire* that lease before the end of the week.

adequate:1.en: Tang measured the floor space of the candidate site and reported back. 'Storage is *adequate*, maybe just enough for our usual stock,' she said carefully. The Manager nodded, but his eyes were already measuring the back wall. I got the feeling that 'just enough' was not going to satisfy him for long.
adequate:1.cnHint: 阿糖说新店的储物空间____，勉强够用，但店长显然想要更多。
adequate:1.hook: He then asked about the basement, and Tang went very quiet.
adequate:1.line: The storage is *adequate* for now, but only just.

conventional:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the new store site, shaking his head at the empty shopfront. 'A *conventional* corner store won't survive here,' he said, pointing at the busy night market across the street. He wanted something different — something that would pull people in before they even knew why.
conventional:1.cnHint: 店长觉得在这条街开一家____的便利店根本活不下去。
conventional:1.hook: He pulled out a notebook and began writing something none of us expected.
conventional:1.line: 'A *conventional* store will just disappear into the street, trust me.'

disappear:1.en: We carried boxes of stock from the van to the new branch at dawn. One moment Tang was right beside me, arms full of instant noodles — then he seemed to *disappear* around the corner. I called his name twice. The street stayed quiet. The box he had been carrying sat alone on the kerb.
disappear:1.cnHint: 搬货时，同事突然____了，只留下一箱东西放在路边。
disappear:1.hook: When Tang finally came back, he was holding a small, folded piece of paper.
disappear:1.line: 'You can't just *disappear* like that — I nearly called the Manager!'

district:1.en: The new branch sat at the edge of the old shopping *district*, where teahouses and noodle stalls had stood for decades. Walking there for the first time, I noticed how different it felt from our quiet corner — louder, brighter, and full of people even at midnight. This part of the city never seemed to sleep.
district:1.cnHint: 新分店开在老商业____的边缘，那里热闹得连午夜都不安静。
district:1.hook: Somewhere in that crowd, a face I recognised was watching the store.
district:1.line: 'This *district* is tough — every shop here has been fighting for years.'

greatly:1.en: The Manager had *greatly* underestimated how hard it would be to find a good location. Three streets, two arguments with landlords, and one very long afternoon later, he sat on a low wall outside a vacant shop, staring at his own shoes. Tang and I exchanged a look. Nobody said anything for a while.
greatly:1.cnHint: 店长____低估了找到合适店面的难度，坐在墙边沉默了很久。
greatly:1.hook: Then the Manager's phone rang, and his whole face changed.
greatly:1.line: 'I *greatly* underestimated this neighbourhood — it is far harder than I thought.'

imitate:1.en: Lin showed up at the new site uninvited, walking slowly around the outside of the building, looking at every detail. 'He's trying to *imitate* whatever we build here,' Tang whispered to me, watching from across the street. Lin paused at the door, took a photo, smiled to himself, and walked away without a word.
imitate:1.cnHint: 竞争对手林来到新店外围转悠，似乎想____我们的设计。
imitate:1.hook: What Lin didn't notice was that the Manager had been watching him the whole time.
imitate:1.line: 'If he wants to *imitate* us, let him — we'll just keep moving ahead.'

implement:1.en: The Manager laid every *implement* out on the folding table outside the new store: price tags, a label gun, a measuring tape, a screwdriver. He picked up each one, checked it, and set it down again with quiet care. It was the same routine he followed at our main store every single time a new shelf went up.
implement:1.cnHint: 店长把所有____整齐地摆在桌上，一件件检查，就像开第一家店时一样。
implement:1.hook: One tool was missing, and the Manager's jaw tightened when he noticed.
implement:1.line: 'Every *implement* has its place — a tidy kit means a tidy store.'

mood:1.en: Tang arrived at the new branch site kicking a small stone ahead of him, which told me everything about his *mood*. The Manager had asked him to repaint the outside wall alone. It was hot, the wall was long, and the paint was the wrong shade of white. He picked up the brush anyway and started at the far end.
mood:1.cnHint: 同事今天____很差，因为被安排一个人粉刷外墙。
mood:1.hook: By noon, someone unexpected had picked up a second brush and joined him.
mood:1.line: 'My *mood* is terrible today, but the wall won't paint itself, will it.'

motivation:1.en: I asked the Manager why he was working so hard to open a second store when the first one barely broke even. He was quiet for a moment, straightening a sign above the new door. 'The *motivation* isn't money,' he said at last, without turning around. He didn't explain further, and I didn't ask again.
motivation:1.cnHint: 我问店长开分店的____到底是什么，他的回答让我意外。
motivation:1.hook: Later, Tang told me he had heard the Manager say a name — just once, softly.
motivation:1.line: 'My *motivation* has nothing to do with money — remember that.'

attribute:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, studying the busy corner with folded arms. 'People walk past here all day,' he said. I could *attribute* his confidence to experience — he had opened three stores before. But something in his careful eyes made me wonder if he saw a problem he was not sharing yet.
attribute:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店选址外，把人流量____为成功的关键因素。
attribute:1.hook: He checked his watch twice, then looked north.
attribute:1.line: I *attribute* the foot traffic here to the night market two blocks away.

badly:1.en: Tang and I were sent to count the foot traffic outside the site on a cold morning. Tang forgot his coat. He *badly* wanted to go back for it, hopping from foot to foot on the pavement, but the Manager had said to stay until noon. I offered him half my scarf and he accepted with a grateful, shivering grin.
badly:1.cnHint: 外出勘察新店选址时，同事____需要一件外套来御寒。
badly:1.hook: Then Tang pointed at a figure crossing the road.
badly:1.line: I *badly* need a hot drink right now — any store nearby?

bridge:1.en: The new branch sat at the end of a narrow *bridge* over a small canal. Every morning, workers and students crossed it in a steady stream. The Manager watched them from the railings, counting heads under his breath. 'A bridge is not just concrete,' he told me. 'It is a promise that people will arrive.'
bridge:1.cnHint: 新分店就在一座____旁边，店长认为这是绝佳的客流保障。
bridge:1.hook: That evening, a cyclist stopped halfway across and stared at the door.
bridge:1.line: This *bridge* carries more people than that main road does.

casual:1.en: Lin appeared outside the site in a *casual* jacket and trainers, pretending to check her phone. She was clearly studying the same corner we had chosen. The Manager noticed her and simply smiled, straightening the small 'Coming Soon' sign on the door. Neither of them spoke. The street felt oddly quiet for a moment.
casual:1.cnHint: 竞争对手穿着____的衣服在新店选址附近假装路过，其实在暗中观察。
casual:1.hook: Lin took one photo before walking away without looking back.
casual:1.line: Oh, I was just taking a *casual* walk — nice spot you picked.

closely:1.en: I was asked to observe the morning crowd *closely* and write down what people carried — bags, umbrellas, hot cups from other stores. The Manager wanted to know what gap we could fill. By ten o'clock my notebook was full. Across the street, I noticed Lin doing exactly the same thing from a doorway.
closely:1.cnHint: 我被要求____观察早晨的人流，记录潜在顾客的消费习惯。
closely:1.hook: Our notes would turn out to be completely different.
closely:1.line: Watch *closely* — see how many people carry breakfast bags already.

commit:1.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me outside the site after lunch. 'I will not *commit* to this location until we check the evening crowd,' he said, tapping the door frame. We nodded. A woman with a folded map stopped, read the 'Coming Soon' sign, and asked us when we would open. We all looked at the Manager.
commit:1.cnHint: 店长说要等看过晚间人流后，才肯____确定这个新分店的选址。
commit:1.hook: The Manager smiled at the woman but gave no date.
commit:1.line: I never *commit* to a site until I see it after dark.

concentrate:1.en: Setting up the small outdoor display table, I tried to *concentrate* on aligning the sample cups in a neat row. But the street noise, a barking dog, and Tang humming tunelessly behind me made it hard. The Manager appeared, fixed one cup with a single finger, and said nothing. The row was suddenly perfect.
concentrate:1.cnHint: 在店外摆设展示台时，我努力____于工作，但周围的噪音让人分心。
concentrate:1.hook: A child stopped and reached for one of the cups.
concentrate:1.line: Could you please *concentrate* — every cup needs to face the same way.

conscious:1.en: Walking the block around the new site, I became *conscious* of how many people glanced at the 'Coming Soon' sign without slowing down. I started counting glances the way the Manager counted footsteps. By the third lap I noticed one man had done the same lap twice, reading the sign each time. He was not one of us.
conscious:1.cnHint: 在新店附近巡查时，我逐渐____到有个陌生人在反复打量我们的告示牌。
conscious:1.hook: On his third lap, the man finally took out a notebook.
conscious:1.line: I'm *conscious* that at least three people have photographed our sign today.

obvious:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site on a cold morning, staring at the empty shopfront. A big sign had fallen sideways overnight. It was *obvious* to every passerby that something had gone wrong — people slowed down, pointed, and whispered before hurrying on. I arrived late and found him already sweeping broken glass alone.
obvious:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店门口，看着倾斜的招牌，路人纷纷驻足——____就摆在眼前。
obvious:1.hook: He swept without a word, but his hands would not stop shaking.
obvious:1.line: 'It is *obvious* we have a problem — help me move this sign.'

ordinary:1.en: From the outside, the new branch looked like any *ordinary* corner shop: a small lit sign, a rack of umbrellas by the door, neat rows of drinks in the window. But the Manager had spent three months choosing every shelf position. I watched him stand back and smile at it the way a painter smiles at a finished wall.
ordinary:1.cnHint: 新分店从外面看和____的便利店没什么两样，但店长在门口站了很久，若有所思。
ordinary:1.hook: Then a stranger walked up and asked if the old branch had finally closed.
ordinary:1.line: 'It may look *ordinary*, but every shelf is exactly where I want it.'

pace:1.en: Tang *paced* up and down the pavement outside the new branch, checking the clock every few steps. The delivery truck was thirty minutes late, and the grand opening was in one hour. A small crowd had already gathered by the door, holding discount coupons the Manager had handed out the week before. I counted the coupons and felt my own stomach tighten.
pace:1.cnHint: 唐在新分店门外____来____去，送货车迟迟未到，开业就要开始了。
pace:1.hook: The truck turned the corner — but it was carrying the wrong store's order.
pace:1.line: 'Stop watching me *pace* — go and call the driver again.'

participate:1.en: The Manager invited everyone on the street to *participate* in a simple game outside the new branch: guess the number of sweets in a glass jar and win a store voucher. A long, cheerful line formed within minutes. Lin arrived last, studied the jar for a long time, then wrote a number so precise that the Manager raised an eyebrow.
participate:1.cnHint: 店长邀请街上的路人____猜糖果数量的小游戏，林是最后一个来的。
participate:1.hook: Lin's number was only one away from correct, and he did not look surprised at all.
participate:1.line: 'I did not come to *participate* — I came to win.'

pilot:1.en: A man in a neat uniform stopped at the new branch just after dawn, bought a hot coffee, and stood reading the community board by the door. Someone had pinned up a photo of the old store from ten years ago. He pointed at it and told me he was a *pilot* who had grown up on this very street and used to buy sweets here as a child.
pilot:1.cnHint: 一位____在天亮后停在新分店门口买咖啡，指着公告栏上的旧照片发了会儿呆。
pilot:1.hook: He asked quietly whether the woman in the photo still worked the morning shift.
pilot:1.line: 'I am a *pilot*, but this little store always felt like home base to me.'

primary:1.en: The Manager explained his *primary* reason for choosing this street corner: three schools within five minutes' walk, a bus stop right opposite, and a park where families gathered every weekend. He drew a rough map on the back of a receipt and handed it to me outside the empty shop. The logic was so clean it was almost beautiful.
primary:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门口向我解释选这个街角的____原因，还在收据背面画了张简图。
primary:1.hook: Lin appeared behind us and photographed the map before either of us noticed.
primary:1.line: 'Location is the *primary* thing — get it wrong and nothing else matters.'

priority:1.en: Tang and I carried a heavy promotional banner out to the pavement, but the wind kept folding it the wrong way. The Manager came outside, looked at our struggle, and said that getting the banner straight was not the *priority* — the open door and the warm smell of fresh bread coming out were. He propped the door wide open and walked back in without another word.
priority:1.cnHint: 店长走出来看我们挂横幅，说这不是最重要的____，然后把店门敞开就走了。
priority:1.hook: A small girl outside immediately followed the bread smell straight through the door.
priority:1.line: 'The banner can wait — the open door is the *priority* right now.'

throughout:1.en: *Throughout* the first morning outside the new branch, a steady stream of curious neighbours stopped to peer through the window, read the menu board, and collect the small free samples Tang handed out on a tray. By noon the tray was empty, Tang's feet hurt, and a short queue had formed at the door before we had even officially opened.
throughout:1.cnHint: 新店开业第一个上午，____都有好奇的街坊在外面张望，唐的托盘很快就空了。
throughout:1.hook: The last person in line was holding a coupon printed with yesterday's date.
throughout:1.line: 'I was here *throughout* the whole morning — do I get an extra sample?'

dinner:1.en: The Manager called us outside at sunset. A folding table stood on the pavement, covered with small dishes. 'Before we open the new branch,' he said, 'we share a *dinner* together.' Tang passed the chopsticks. I looked at the empty building across the street and felt, for the first time, like part of the team.
dinner:1.cnHint: 店长在街边摆了一桌菜，说要在____之前大家聚一聚。
dinner:1.hook: But one chair at the table was never explained.
dinner:1.line: 'I always *dinner* with my crew before a big day,' the Manager said.

embrace:1.en: I stepped outside to sweep the doorstep and found Lin standing across the street, staring at the empty shopfront. She didn't look angry. She looked almost sad. Then the Manager walked out, put a hand on her shoulder, and said we should *embrace* the change together — both stores could make this corner something special.
embrace:1.cnHint: 店长走出来，说大家应该____新的变化，把这个街角变得更好。
embrace:1.hook: Lin's answer was a smile that never quite reached her eyes.
embrace:1.line: 'We should *embrace* this new start,' the Manager told Lin quietly.

explanation:1.en: A delivery van stopped in front of the wrong address and blocked our doorway for twenty minutes. The driver gave no *explanation*, just shrugged and scrolled his phone. Tang stood outside, arms folded, while customers squeezed past. When the van finally left, a small round of applause came from the bus stop.
explanation:1.cnHint: 送货车堵住了门口，司机没有任何____，坦然刷着手机。
explanation:1.hook: Tang wrote something in a notebook that I was not meant to see.
explanation:1.line: 'No *explanation* at all — just parked and walked off,' Tang said.

intend:1.en: The Manager pinned a paper map on the lamp post outside and circled two spots with a red pen. 'I *intend* to open the second branch on this corner,' he told us. A woman walking her dog stopped, read the map over his shoulder, and asked if there would be better coffee than the current store.
intend:1.cnHint: 店长在路灯柱上贴出地图，宣布他____在那个街角开新分店。
intend:1.hook: The woman left without giving her name, but she took a photo of the map.
intend:1.line: 'I *intend* to make the new store even cosier,' the Manager said firmly.

leadership:1.en: While we set up the outdoor sign for the new branch, a school group walked by. Their teacher pointed at the Manager and told the students that real *leadership* means doing the hard work yourself. The Manager was on a step-ladder at the time, fixing a crooked letter, and he bowed from up there with great dignity.
leadership:1.cnHint: 路过的老师指着正在梯子上干活的店长，夸他展现了真正的____。
leadership:1.hook: One student stayed behind and asked the Manager for a job application.
leadership:1.line: 'True *leadership* is climbing the ladder yourself,' the teacher said.

locate:1.en: Tang spread a city map on the bonnet of a parked car and tried to *locate* the exact site of our new branch. A stranger stopped, looked at the map upside down, and confidently pointed to the river. Tang thanked him, waited until he left, and then pointed to the correct block three streets away.
locate:1.cnHint: 阿糖在停着的车上摊开地图，试图____新分店的准确位置。
locate:1.hook: The stranger came back ten minutes later with a second, older map.
locate:1.line: 'I need to *locate* the new site before the Manager asks,' Tang muttered.

original:1.en: Lin stood outside studying our store front, then looked at the empty unit next door. 'Your sign design is nice,' she admitted to me, 'but my *original* plan was to open here first.' She said it without bitterness, just a quiet fact, the way you state the weather. Then she bought a coffee and walked away.
original:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林坦言，她____的计划是第一个在这里开店。
original:1.hook: She left a folded note under the coffee cup.
original:1.line: 'My *original* plan had this corner all to myself,' Lin said quietly.

overcome:1.en: The new sign was too wide for the doorway and nobody had measured twice. Tang and I stood outside in the evening air, turning it sideways, then diagonal. Small crowds gathered, offered advice, and cheered every attempt. We finally *overcome* the problem by removing one bolt and sliding the sign in at an angle, to loud applause.
overcome:1.cnHint: 招牌太宽进不了门，我们费了好大劲才____这个难题。
overcome:1.hook: The Manager filmed the whole thing without helping once.
overcome:1.line: 'We *overcome* every problem if we stay calm,' Tang said, out of breath.

partly:1.en: The Manager stood outside on the pavement, studying the empty shop front across the street. He had been watching it for days. 'The rent is low,' he said, 'and it is *partly* because the landlord wants a quick deal.' I looked at the dusty windows and wondered what he was planning.
partly:1.cnHint: 店长在街对面的空铺子前徘徊，觉得低租金____是因为房东急于出手。
partly:1.hook: He pulled out a tape measure and smiled at me.
partly:1.line: The low price is *partly* because they need the space filled fast.

practical:1.en: Tang spread a hand-drawn map on the bonnet of a parked bicycle outside. Little squares marked possible sites for the new branch. 'Forget the pretty spots,' Tang said. 'We need something *practical*—close to the bus stop, with a loading bay.' I circled one square with a pen and Tang raised an eyebrow.
practical:1.cnHint: 阿糖在外面铺开地图，坚持选址要____，离公交站近才行。
practical:1.hook: The circled spot belonged to someone none of us expected.
practical:1.line: A place near the bus stop is far more *practical* for deliveries.

profit:1.en: Lin was already outside before dawn, counting the breakfast crowd walking past the empty corner lot. She wrote numbers in a small notebook. 'If we sell rice boxes and coffee here,' she said quietly, almost to herself, 'the *profit* in one month pays the deposit.' I stood beside her, watching the same crowd, doing the same sums.
profit:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在拐角空地旁计算早餐人流，默默估算一个月的____能否付清押金。
profit:1.hook: But Lin's notebook had a second column I had not noticed.
profit:1.line: One month of rice-box sales brings enough *profit* to cover the deposit.

promise:1.en: Outside the old post office, the Manager shook hands with a landlord in a grey coat. I waited by the kerb. 'You have my *promise*,' the Manager said, standing straight and calm. 'We open within sixty days.' The landlord nodded slowly, folded his copy of the agreement, and walked away without a word.
promise:1.cnHint: 店长在旧邮局外握手，郑重地给了房东一个____：六十天内开业。
promise:1.hook: The landlord paused at the corner and looked back once.
promise:1.line: You have my *promise*—the store opens in sixty days.

rarely:1.en: The side street behind the market was quiet that morning. Tang pointed to a small unit wedged between a laundry and a hardware stall. 'Customers *rarely* come this deep in,' Tang admitted, kicking a loose stone, 'but the people who do are regulars—every single day.' I looked at the narrow lane and tried to imagine a neon sign here.
rarely:1.cnHint: 阿糖带我去市场后的小巷看铺位，承认顾客____走到这么深的地方。
rarely:1.hook: Just then, a familiar regular walked out of that very lane.
rarely:1.line: People *rarely* wander this far, but loyal ones do every day.

severe:1.en: A *severe* overnight frost had left thin ice on the doorstep of the site the Manager liked most. We arrived early to check the pipes. Tang pressed a hand to the outside wall and frowned. 'If the insulation is this poor in spring,' Tang said, 'we will lose stock every winter.' The Manager knocked on the wall and said nothing.
severe:1.cnHint: 夜里的____霜冻让店长看中的铺子台阶结了薄冰，阿糖担心冬天货物受损。
severe:1.hook: There was a damp patch on the ceiling nobody had mentioned.
severe:1.line: A frost this *severe* means the insulation is far too weak.

smell:1.en: We visited the candidate site near the night market just after the food stalls packed up. The air was still thick with the *smell* of fried dough and spice. I breathed it in and thought it was wonderful. Tang wrinkled their nose. 'Strong neighbours,' Tang said. 'Our snacks will have to fight hard to stand out.'
smell:1.cnHint: 夜市收摊后，我们去看附近的铺位，空气里弥漫着油炸食品的____。
smell:1.hook: Tang pointed to the stall directly next door and went silent.
smell:1.line: That *smell* from next door will compete with everything we sell.

socialize:1.en: Lin had chosen the Sunday morning visit on purpose. The small plaza in front of the site was full of older residents doing slow exercises and young parents watching children play. 'Look,' Lin said, sweeping a hand across the square. 'People come here to *socialize* every single day. They will need water, snacks, a warm drink.' I started counting heads immediately.
socialize:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林特意选在周日带我们来，广场上全是来____的街坊邻居，她认为生意差不了。
socialize:1.hook: One woman with a pram stopped and peered through our window.
socialize:1.line: They come here to *socialize* daily—every one of them is a customer.

threaten:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, arms crossed. A rival shop owner from across the street marched over and began to *threaten* him, jabbing a finger at the sign. The Manager did not step back even one centimetre.
threaten:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址外被人____，却纹丝不动。
threaten:1.hook: The rival's last word hung in the cold air like a warning.
threaten:1.line: 'You can *threaten* me all you like — this sign stays.'

throw:1.en: Opening a second branch on this street was a real *throw* — the rent was high, the foot traffic unknown, and two other shops had already failed here. The Manager studied the empty shopfront anyway, turning the key over in his hand with a quiet, determined look.
throw:1.cnHint: 在这条街开分店是一次大胆的____，风险不小。
throw:1.hook: He pocketed the key, and nobody saw him smile.
throw:1.line: 'Every good business starts as a *throw*, doesn't it?'

unlike:1.en: The new branch corner felt *unlike* anything near our usual store — wider pavements, taller trees, a slower kind of morning. I stood there holding a measuring tape for the Manager and tried to picture a second little shop of ours sitting quietly between the old bookshop and the flower stall.
unlike:1.cnHint: 新店的街角环境与我们原来的门店____。
unlike:1.hook: Then I noticed something odd taped to the bookshop door.
unlike:1.line: 'This place is *unlike* anywhere I expected us to open.'

vast:1.en: From the rooftop of the proposed building I could see a *vast* stretch of the city — towers, rooftops, tiny figures on bikes below. The Manager spread a hand-drawn map on the ledge and said the new store had to serve all those people out there, every quiet hungry one of them.
vast:1.cnHint: 从楼顶望去，城市____，店长指着远处说新店要服务所有人。
vast:1.hook: One tiny figure on a bike stopped and looked straight up.
vast:1.line: 'Look at that *vast* crowd — they all need a good night clerk.'

absolutely:1.en: Lin from the rival shop leaned against the lamppost and told me *absolutely* nothing useful — every question about the local customer habits got a cheerful shrug or a change of subject. I wrote 'zero data from Lin' in my notebook and decided to count passing customers myself.
absolutely:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林对我的问题____没有给出任何有用的信息。
absolutely:1.hook: Lin's smile, though, suggested she knew far more than she let on.
absolutely:1.line: 'I *absolutely* have no idea what time people eat around here.'

accumulate:1.en: Every morning before the new branch opened, I would walk past and watch the Manager *accumulate* small clues — a coffee cup left on the step, a bus ticket caught in the doorway, chalk marks children drew on the kerb. He was building a picture of the street one tiny detail at a time.
accumulate:1.cnHint: 店长每天在新店门口____关于这条街的各种细节。
accumulate:1.hook: That morning's clue, though, was not a small one at all.
accumulate:1.line: 'You have to *accumulate* evidence before you trust a street.'

breakfast:1.en: Tang arrived early to help measure the new shop space and stopped to *breakfast* at the old couple's stall next door — a bowl of warm rice porridge, eaten standing up, watching the street wake. 'Good neighbours,' Tang said, nodding at the couple, 'that is the best sign for any new store.'
breakfast:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店隔壁的小摊____，觉得有好邻居是好兆头。
breakfast:1.hook: The old couple exchanged a glance that Tang did not catch.
breakfast:1.line: 'I always *breakfast* near a future shop — tells you everything.'

capacity:1.en: The Manager paced the empty floor of the new branch, counting steps. 'The *capacity* is just right,' he murmured — enough shelves for the essentials, enough counter space for two clerks on a busy night, and one small corner where a tired customer could stand and breathe for a moment.
capacity:1.cnHint: 店长测量新店空间，觉得____恰到好处。
capacity:1.hook: He paused at that small corner and did not move for a long time.
capacity:1.line: 'The *capacity* is right — but is the street ready for us?'

consideration:1.en: The Manager stood at the corner of Maple Street, studying the empty shop across the road. 'Location, foot traffic, rent,' he muttered, ticking items off on his fingers. Every *consideration* mattered when opening a second store. I held the measuring tape and tried to look useful. Then a familiar face appeared in the window opposite.
consideration:1.cnHint: 店长在街角评估新店地址时，窗户里出现了一张熟悉的脸，令他____了很多因素。
consideration:1.hook: The face in the window belonged to someone the Manager clearly feared.
consideration:1.line: 'Cost is only one *consideration* — the neighbours matter more.'

disaster:1.en: Rain had been falling since dawn, and the outdoor sign we had just put up for the new branch lay flat in a puddle. Paint was running down the pavement in little coloured rivers. The Manager stared at the soggy mess and whispered, 'What a *disaster*.' A passing cyclist slowed down, read the ruined sign, and laughed.
disaster:1.cnHint: 新店招牌被大雨冲倒，店长看着一片狼藉，感叹这真是一场____。
disaster:1.hook: The cyclist pulled out a phone and started recording.
disaster:1.line: 'One wet morning and it is already a *disaster* — great start.'

emergency:1.en: A small boy ran up to me outside the new branch site and grabbed my sleeve. 'Mister, my bike wheel is stuck in the drain and I am late for school!' It felt like a real *emergency* to him, and honestly to me too. I found a stick, levered the wheel free, and he pedalled away without a single thank-you.
emergency:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩冲到店外求助，对他来说这是一场真正的____。
emergency:1.hook: Three seconds later the boy skidded to a stop and turned back.
emergency:1.line: 'This is an *emergency* — please help me right now!'

familiar:1.en: I had walked past this street corner a hundred times before joining the store, yet it felt different now that we were about to open a branch here. The smell of the bread stall, the sound of the tram — everything was *familiar* and strange at once. Tang nudged me: 'You look like you have seen a ghost.'
familiar:1.cnHint: 我走在即将开新店的街角，一切既____又陌生，唐同事发现了我奇怪的表情。
familiar:1.hook: Tang had gone pale too, and was staring at the bread stall.
familiar:1.line: 'This corner feels *familiar* — I think I have been here in a dream.'

furthermore:1.en: Lin had arrived at the new site before any of us and had already taped a neat list of problems to the front door: the window was too small, the ceiling was too low, and, *furthermore*, the nearest bus stop was a full ten minutes away on foot. The Manager read the list slowly, folded it in half, and put it in his pocket.
furthermore:1.cnHint: 林提前列出了新店的问题，____连公交站也太远，店长默默把清单收进了口袋。
furthermore:1.hook: No one mentioned that Lin had also brought a rival store's brochure.
furthermore:1.line: 'The rent is high, and *furthermore*, there is no parking at all.'

hardly:1.en: By nine in the morning a small crowd had gathered to watch us hang the new branch sign. My arms ached from holding the ladder steady, and I could *hardly* keep my eyes open after the long night shift. Then the Manager called up, 'A little to the left.' A little. He said that eleven more times.
hardly:1.cnHint: 挂招牌时我熬了一夜，____睁得开眼，店长却不停叫我往左移一点。
hardly:1.hook: On the twelfth adjustment, the ladder gave a quiet, worrying creak.
hardly:1.line: 'I can *hardly* read the address on this map — the print is tiny.'

hinder:1.en: A delivery truck had parked right in front of the new branch entrance, blocking the whole pavement. The driver was nowhere to be seen. 'This will *hinder* everything,' Tang said, waving at the crowd of workers waiting to carry boxes inside. I slipped a note under the windscreen wiper and hoped the driver had a conscience.
hinder:1.cnHint: 一辆货车堵住了新店入口，____了所有工作，我只好在雨刷下留了张纸条。
hinder:1.hook: The note blew away before I even turned around.
hinder:1.line: 'Please move your truck — it will *hinder* our whole morning.'

injury:1.en: While helping stack display shelves on the pavement outside the new branch, I dropped a corner unit onto my foot. It was not serious, but I hopped around for a full minute. Tang handed me a small bandage from her bag without a word. 'Old *injury*,' I told a curious passer-by, trying to sound dignified. Nobody believed me.
injury:1.cnHint: 我在店外搬货架时伤了脚，唐递给我创可贴，我硬撑着对路人解释这是旧____。
injury:1.hook: The passer-by turned out to be the landlord coming to sign our lease.
injury:1.line: 'It is just a small *injury* — I can still carry the boxes, really.'

lift:1.en: The new branch store was on the third floor of a corner building. I carried two heavy boxes of milk up the stairs because the *lift* was broken. My legs burned by the top step. The Manager watched from below, arms folded, saying nothing at all.
lift:1.cnHint: 新分店在三楼，我扛着牛奶箱走楼梯，因为____坏了。
lift:1.hook: The Manager's silence felt heavier than the boxes.
lift:1.line: 'The *lift* has been broken for a week — welcome to the new store.'

mainly:1.en: The Manager explained the new branch to me outside on the pavement. It would serve the office workers across the street, she said. The customers here were *mainly* young people in suits who needed coffee and a quick bite before nine o'clock every morning.
mainly:1.cnHint: 店长在街边向我介绍新分店，顾客____是附近的上班族。
mainly:1.hook: One regular had not shown up in three days.
mainly:1.line: 'Our customers are *mainly* office workers, so mornings will be very busy.'

moral:1.en: Tang told me a story about the old branch on our walk to the new store. A clerk once kept extra change instead of returning it and was fired the same afternoon. 'The *moral* is simple,' Tang said, kicking a pebble off the kerb, 'the Manager counts everything.'
moral:1.cnHint: 阿糖边走边讲了个老店的故事，最后点出其中的____。
moral:1.hook: Tang's voice dropped when we reached the new front door.
moral:1.line: 'The *moral* of that story? Never think the Manager is not watching.'

nor:1.en: The new branch sat between a dry cleaner and a florist. There was no bus stop nearby, *nor* was there a car park. I stood outside wondering how anyone would find us. Then a crowd rounded the corner, heading straight for the glass door like they already knew.
nor:1.cnHint: 新分店位置偏，附近没有公交站，____有停车场，但顾客却纷至沓来。
nor:1.hook: Someone at the front of the crowd seemed to know my name.
nor:1.line: 'There is no bus stop here, *nor* a car park — people still come every day.'

pick:1.en: Before the new branch opened, the Manager let the two clerks *pick* which shift they wanted. Tang chose days without a word of thanks. I chose nights, mostly because the street outside looked wonderfully quiet after midnight. I did not know about the man who came at two every morning.
pick:1.cnHint: 开业前店长让我们____班次，我选了夜班，没想到凌晨会有个神秘常客。
pick:1.hook: The man always ordered the same thing and never paid by phone.
pick:1.line: 'You can *pick* your shift — but nights here are never really quiet.'

pollution:1.en: The new store faced a wide road, and lorries rolled past all morning. Lin propped the door open to air out the stockroom and then quickly shut it again. 'The *pollution* from those engines is terrible,' she said, waving a hand in front of her face. I noticed she still stood outside on her break.
pollution:1.cnHint: 新店门口大货车不断，隔壁咖啡店的林感叹路上的____很严重，却还是跑到外面休息。
pollution:1.hook: Lin was staring at something across the road, not at the traffic.
pollution:1.line: 'Close the door — the *pollution* from those lorries gets into everything.'

quit:1.en: A man in a paint-stained jacket leaned against the wall outside, staring at the new store sign. He had worked here before, Tang whispered, but he chose to *quit* the week the branch was announced. Now he came by every evening and just looked. He never came in. He never explained why.
quit:1.cnHint: 一个穿旧夹克的男人每晚在门外驻足，阿糖说他在新店宣布前____了工作。
quit:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he stepped toward the door.
quit:1.line: 'He used to work here, then chose to *quit* — nobody knows the real reason.'

recall:1.en: On my first morning outside the new branch, an old woman stopped and studied the front window for a long time. She told me she could *recall* a small tea stall that once stood on this exact corner. She smiled at the refrigerated shelves visible through the glass, then slowly walked away into the crowd.
recall:1.cnHint: 一位老婆婆在新店门口停下，说她能____起这个街角以前的样子。
recall:1.hook: She left before I could ask what happened to the tea stall.
recall:1.line: 'I can *recall* every shop that ever stood on this corner — this one suits it best.'

worldwide:1.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter. 'Our new branch will sit right here,' he said, tapping a red dot two streets away. He spoke about small stores like ours going *worldwide* one day, as if a corner shop could quietly grow into something the whole world might know. I nodded and tried to look convinced.
worldwide:1.cnHint: 店长在柜台上铺开一张手绘地图，指着新店位置，畅想小店有朝一日____。
worldwide:1.hook: But the red dot was on a spot I had walked past — and something was already there.
worldwide:1.line: 'A small store like ours can go *worldwide* if we care enough about every customer.'

accomplish:1.en: Tang and I stood outside in the early morning, measuring the pavement with a cloth tape. 'What exactly are we trying to *accomplish* here?' I asked. Tang looked up, squinting at the empty shopfront across the road. 'The Manager wants exact numbers before he signs anything,' she said, rolling the tape back up with a snap.
accomplish:1.cnHint: 我和阿糖在店外量人行道的尺寸，我问她我们到底想____什么。
accomplish:1.hook: The shopfront Tang was staring at had a light on inside, and a shadow moved behind the glass.
accomplish:1.line: 'We need to *accomplish* this survey before the Manager arrives at seven.'

address:1.en: A delivery driver stopped his bike outside and held up a slip of paper. 'Is this *address* right?' he asked, looking from the paper to our store sign and back again. I stepped out and read it. Same street, same number — but the shop name on the slip was different. A new place, not yet open, already getting deliveries.
address:1.cnHint: 送货员拿着一张纸来到店外，询问单子上的____是否正确。
address:1.hook: The shop name on that slip matched the empty unit the Manager had been watching all week.
address:1.line: 'The *address* on this slip matches a store that does not exist yet — or does it?'

barely:1.en: The Manager paced the pavement at dawn, measuring the distance to the new branch site with long steps. He had *barely* turned the corner when a small moving truck rolled quietly up to the empty unit across the road and two workers climbed out. I watched from the doorway, coffee going cold in my hand.
barely:1.cnHint: 店长刚____转过街角，一辆小货车就悄悄停在了对面空铺子门口。
barely:1.hook: The workers unloaded a sign that was still wrapped, but its shape looked very familiar.
barely:1.line: 'I had *barely* left and they showed up — someone has been watching our schedule.'

blame:1.en: Lin from the shop down the road leaned against our doorframe, arms crossed. 'If the new branch fails, who gets the *blame*?' she asked, in a tone that was more curious than mean. I shrugged. She smiled, pushed off the frame, and walked away without buying anything — which was, honestly, very Lin of her.
blame:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林靠在我们店门框上，问如果新分店失败了，____会落在谁身上。
blame:1.hook: She paused at the corner, took out her phone, and typed something before disappearing.
blame:1.line: 'I am not here to place *blame* — I just want to know who is in charge of this plan.'

chat:1.en: Tang sat on an upturned crate outside, waving at every neighbour who passed. 'I thought we were checking the site,' I said. 'We are,' she replied. 'I *chat* with people, they tell me things — like who signed the lease on that empty unit last week.' She smiled and offered me half a rice cracker.
chat:1.cnHint: 阿糖坐在门外的箱子上和过路的邻居____，从他们那里打听新店的租约消息。
chat:1.hook: One neighbour had paused too long before answering, and Tang had noticed.
chat:1.line: 'If you *chat* with the woman at the flower stall, she knows everything on this street.'

combat:1.en: The Manager returned from the council office looking tired. 'Other stores open nearby all the time,' I said, trying to cheer him up. He shook his head. 'This one is different. We need a plan to *combat* it before it even opens.' He stared at his hand-drawn map, then slowly circled our own store in red ink.
combat:1.cnHint: 店长从区政府回来后说，他们需要一个计划来____即将开业的竞争对手。
combat:1.hook: The red circle he drew was so firm it tore slightly through the paper.
combat:1.line: 'The best way to *combat* a new rival is to make sure your own customers never want to leave.'

danger:1.en: A city inspector walked the pavement outside the empty unit, making notes. Tang nudged me. 'See that? If they find a *danger* in the building, the opening is delayed for months.' The inspector wrote something, stuck a yellow notice on the door, and left without a word. We both stared at the yellow paper fluttering in the morning breeze.
danger:1.cnHint: 一位城建检查员在空铺子外做记录，阿糖说如果查出____，新店开业就会被推迟。
danger:1.hook: The yellow notice gave no details, but the Manager arrived two minutes later, already smiling.
danger:1.line: 'A fire *danger* in that unit means no opening permit — at least not this month.'

register:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch with a thick folder under his arm. 'We have to *register* the store with the city office before we open,' he said, pressing a pen into my hand. The street was cold, the ink kept skipping, and a small crowd was already gathering at the door.
register:1.cnHint: 店长要我在市政办公室为新店办理____手续。
register:1.hook: One face in the crowd looked very familiar.
register:1.line: 'We need to *register* the store by noon, or we lose the licence.'

skin:1.en: I carried a stack of window posters outside to decorate the new branch. The wind was bitter and my *skin* stung the moment I stepped off the kerb. Tang came running up with a roll of tape, cheeks red, breath clouding in the cold air, somehow still smiling.
skin:1.cnHint: 贴海报时，寒风刺痛了我的____。
skin:1.hook: Tang's smile vanished the second she read the poster.
skin:1.line: 'The cold really gets into your *skin* out here, doesn't it?'

spirit:1.en: Lin showed up across the street, arms crossed, watching us hang the new branch sign. I expected trouble, but she just nodded once. The Manager said the *spirit* of this neighbourhood was big enough for two stores. I was not sure he believed it, but it sounded nice.
spirit:1.cnHint: 店长说这条街的____足以容下两家店。
spirit:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and made a very long call.
spirit:1.line: 'The *spirit* of this street has room for everyone — even her.'

spread:1.en: Word of the new branch *spread* fast. By the time I finished taping the last poster to the window, a queue had formed on the pavement, snaking past the old letter box and round the corner. The Manager looked pleased. I looked at the single working till and felt less pleased.
spread:1.cnHint: 新店开业的消息____得很快，门口已经排起了长队。
spread:1.hook: The very first customer in line was Lin.
spread:1.line: 'News about us *spread* faster than I expected — better get ready.'

totally:1.en: I had *totally* forgotten that the new branch had no back-room shelves yet. The delivery driver arrived at the kerb with six trolleys of stock, looked at our empty doorway, and raised one eyebrow very slowly. The Manager clapped my shoulder and said, 'Good chance to be creative.'
totally:1.cnHint: 我____忘记新店还没有货架，货却已经到门口了。
totally:1.hook: The driver said he could only wait ten minutes.
totally:1.line: 'I *totally* forgot to order the shelving — this is on me.'

tree:1.en: The new branch sat beside a wide old *tree* whose roots had cracked the pavement into small hills. Customers kept tripping on the way in. Tang stuck a little handwritten sign on the trunk that read 'Watch your step, friend.' By evening the sign had three smiley faces drawn on it.
tree:1.cnHint: 新店旁边有一棵大____，根把地砖拱得凹凸不平。
tree:1.hook: Someone had added a fourth face — and a question mark.
tree:1.line: 'That *tree* has been here longer than the whole street, I think.'

weigh:1.en: Before ordering stock for the new branch, the Manager made me *weigh* the cost of each product line against last month's sales. We sat on a low wall outside, papers spread on our knees, while buses rolled past and blew everything sideways twice.
weigh:1.cnHint: 店长让我在路边____各产品线的进货成本与上月销售额。
weigh:1.hook: One number on the sheet did not add up at all.
weigh:1.line: 'You have to *weigh* the cost carefully before we place the order.'

alive:1.en: At the soft opening, the little street felt *alive* in a way I had never seen. Neighbours leaned out of windows, kids sat on the old tree roots eating snacks, and Tang was doing a very enthusiastic job of handing out free coffee samples to anyone who slowed down.
alive:1.cnHint: 开业那天，这条小街____极了，邻居们都探出头来张望。
alive:1.hook: A quiet woman at the back of the crowd had not touched her sample.
alive:1.line: 'Seeing everyone out here like this — the street feels *alive* again.'

facilitate:1.en: The Manager stood outside the empty corner unit, clipboard in hand. 'A second store here would *facilitate* the morning rush,' he said, sketching a rough floor plan on the back of a receipt. I held the tape measure and tried to look useful, wondering if I was already being trained for something bigger.
facilitate:1.cnHint: 店长在拐角空铺外考察，说新店能____早高峰的人流。
facilitate:1.hook: He circled my name on the clipboard without a word.
facilitate:1.line: 'A second store here would *facilitate* the morning rush, trust me.'

insight:1.en: Lin leaned against the lamppost across the street, watching our store with narrow eyes. I had heard she managed a rival shop two blocks away. 'You want real *insight* into this neighbourhood?' she said when she caught me staring. 'Count the umbrellas people carry on dry days.' She walked off smiling.
insight:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林在路边观察，声称对街区有深刻的____。
insight:1.line: 'You want real *insight* into this neighbourhood? Count the umbrellas.'

preparation:1.en: It was barely six in the morning, but the Manager had already lined up supply boxes along the pavement outside. Every detail of the new branch had a checklist. 'Good *preparation* now saves a disaster later,' he told me, handing me a marker pen and pointing at a stack of unlabelled crates.
preparation:1.cnHint: 店长一大早就在店外整理货箱，说充分的____能避免日后麻烦。
preparation:1.hook: One crate, I noticed, had no label and was quietly ticking.
preparation:1.line: 'Good *preparation* now saves a disaster later — start labelling those crates.'

separate:1.en: Tang and I were sent to measure the pavement outside the new site. The Manager wanted to know if there was enough room to keep the entrance and the delivery door *separate*. We used a broom handle as a ruler and argued cheerfully about every centimetre while pigeons watched us with great interest.
separate:1.cnHint: 阿糖和我在店外测量，确认入口和送货通道能否____开来。
separate:1.hook: The pigeons, I felt, were judging our technique.
separate:1.line: 'We need to keep the entrance and the delivery door *separate*, right?'

tie:1.en: A man in a neat suit and a bright orange *tie* stopped in front of the future store window and stared at the paper sign that read 'Opening Soon'. He checked his watch three times in one minute. I had never seen anyone look so personally offended by a construction delay.
tie:1.cnHint: 一个打着____的男士在新店橱窗前驻足，对"即将开业"的牌子愣神许久。
tie:1.hook: He slid a business card under the door and left.
tie:1.line: 'I have been walking past this corner in my lucky *tie* for a month.'

jam:1.en: The morning the Manager announced the new branch, a delivery truck broke down right outside, turning the narrow street into a solid *jam*. Horns, voices, and the smell of warm exhaust filled the air. We handed out free coffee cups to the stuck cyclists, and three of them said they would come to the opening.
jam:1.cnHint: 新店宣布开业那天，门口偏偏发生了交通____，我们趁机向被堵的骑手派发咖啡。
jam:1.hook: One cyclist stayed to help direct traffic — and never left.
jam:1.line: 'Every opening has a little *jam*; think of it as free advertising.'

supermarket:1.en: The big *supermarket* at the end of the road had put up a banner saying 'Everything You Need' right on the day we posted our 'New Branch Coming' notice. The Manager read their banner, straightened his collar, and said simply, 'Good. Competition keeps us awake.' I was not sure if he meant that literally.
supermarket:1.cnHint: 街头的大____在我们贴出新店告示的同一天打出了竞争横幅。
supermarket:1.hook: Their banner was twice the size of our door.
supermarket:1.line: 'A *supermarket* banner will not scare us — small stores have sharper smiles.'

debate:1.en: Tang and I stood on the pavement outside the new site, locked in a serious *debate* about which window faced better light for the snack display. We drew diagrams in the dust with a stick. A passing grandmother stopped, studied our drawings for a moment, and gave a verdict we both immediately accepted.
debate:1.cnHint: 阿糖和我在新店门外____摆放零食货架哪面朝光更合适，一位路过的老奶奶帮我们拍了板。
debate:1.hook: The grandmother asked if we were hiring.
debate:1.line: 'This *debate* about the window matters more than you think — light sells snacks.'

anyway:1.en: The Manager called me at noon to say the new branch location was decided. I had not slept yet after my night shift, but I dragged myself outside *anyway*. Standing on the corner, I watched him point at an empty shopfront across the street. His eyes were bright with plans. Behind him, a small figure in a red coat wrote something in a notebook and slipped away before I could see her face.
anyway:1.cnHint: 店长在街角宣布新分店选址，叙述者____赶来见证这一刻。
anyway:1.hook: The woman in the red coat knew the address before the Manager said it.
anyway:1.line: 'It is raining and I am tired, but I came *anyway*.'

besides:1.en: Tang and I walked the block twice, checking foot traffic. The corner unit had good light and a wide door. *Besides*, the bus stop right outside meant customers every fifteen minutes. Tang ticked boxes on a clipboard and looked pleased. I noticed she kept glancing at the closed flower shop next door, whose owner, an old man with paint-stained gloves, watched us without blinking.
besides:1.cnHint: 叙述者和阿糖考察街角店面时，发现它____有公交站的优势。
besides:1.hook: The old man with paint-stained gloves had not moved in twenty minutes.
besides:1.line: 'The rent is fair, and *besides*, the location is perfect.'

certainly:1.en: A city inspector arrived while the Manager was measuring the front window. She flipped through her papers, asked three sharp questions, and then smiled. 'You may *certainly* open here,' she said, stamping a form, 'as long as the side alley stays clear.' The Manager exhaled loudly. I quietly moved two boxes of stock that were already sitting in the alley, hoping nobody had noticed they were ours.
certainly:1.cnHint: 城市检查员告诉店长，新店____可以开业，但有一个条件。
certainly:1.hook: Someone had already photographed those boxes in the alley.
certainly:1.line: 'You may *certainly* open here,' she said with a firm nod.

challenging:1.en: Walking back from the new site, Tang said finding good night staff for two stores would be *challenging*. The Manager shrugged and said he had someone in mind. He looked at me. I looked at the pavement. Three pigeons looked at the pavement too, which felt like solidarity. Later, Tang texted me a single question mark, and I still have not replied.
challenging:1.cnHint: 阿糖认为同时管理两家店的夜班员工是件____的事，店长却看向了叙述者。
challenging:1.hook: Tang's single question mark sat unanswered in my phone all night.
challenging:1.line: 'Running two stores at once will be *challenging*, but we can do it.'

circumstance:1.en: Lin appeared at the corner just as the Manager was locking up the new unit. They stood two metres apart, both pretending to check their phones. Under any other *circumstance* I would have walked on, but Tang nudged me to stay. Nobody spoke for a long minute. Then Lin pointed at the sign the Manager had just taped to the window and said, very quietly, 'Nice font.'
circumstance:1.cnHint: 在任何其他____下，叙述者都会走开，但这次目睹了隔壁咖啡店的林和店长的奇异相遇。
circumstance:1.hook: 'Nice font' was the first thing Lin had said to the Manager in two years.
circumstance:1.line: 'Under this *circumstance*, I think we should talk.'

comfort:1.en: The Manager sat on the kerb after everyone else had gone, staring at the empty shopfront. I brought him a warm can of tea from our store. He took it without looking up. It was a small *comfort*, but his shoulders dropped a little and his breathing slowed. Down the street, a light went on in Lin's shop, then off again, as if someone had thought better of it.
comfort:1.cnHint: 叙述者给疲惫的店长送去一杯热茶，这成为他今晚小小的____。
comfort:1.hook: Lin's light turned on, then off — one second of hesitation, no more.
comfort:1.line: 'A hot drink is a small *comfort*, but it helps on hard days.'

enrich:1.en: The Manager told us the new branch would *enrich* the whole street, not just our business. He waved his arm at the bakery, the flower shop, and the phone-repair stall, as if welcoming them to a party they had not agreed to attend. The stall owner gave a careful thumbs-up. Later I found a handwritten note on our door that said: 'Please do not play music after midnight.'
enrich:1.cnHint: 店长豪言新分店将____整条街，但附近商户的反应却耐人寻味。
enrich:1.hook: The handwritten note had no name, but the ink matched Lin's pen.
enrich:1.line: 'A new store will *enrich* this street and bring us all closer.'

egg:1.en: The Manager called me outside just after midnight. He pointed at the new shop window across the street, where someone had thrown a raw *egg* against the glass. 'That happened on our first week too,' he said, almost proudly. I looked at the yellow mess and wondered who would do such a thing.
egg:1.cnHint: 店长带我出门，指着对面新店的橱窗——上面沾着一个____留下的痕迹。
egg:1.hook: The Manager smiled too calmly for someone looking at a mess.
egg:1.line: 'A raw *egg* on the window — that means someone is already scared of them.'

hire:1.en: A woman in a bright yellow jacket stopped me on the pavement while I was putting out the morning papers. She asked if the new shop down the road was really going to *hire* twenty people from the neighbourhood. I said I had no idea. She nodded slowly, like that answer told her everything.
hire:1.cnHint: 一位穿黄夹克的女士问我，听说那家新店要____很多本地人，是真的吗？
hire:1.hook: She glanced back at our store before she walked away.
hire:1.line: 'They say they will *hire* local people — every single one.'

aid:1.en: Tang and I were stacking boxes outside when an old man tripped on the uneven pavement near the corner. Tang moved fast, offering a hand. 'Night-shift *aid* service,' Tang joked, helping the man steady himself. The old man laughed, then looked up at our sign with warm eyes.
aid:1.cnHint: 唐迅速上前____一位在转角绊倒的老人，还开了个玩笑。
aid:1.hook: The old man whispered something to Tang that made Tang go very quiet.
aid:1.line: 'Think of it as free *aid* — we are open all night anyway.'

bill:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street walked over at dawn and handed me a folded piece of paper. 'Your Manager left this on our door,' Lin said, cool and polite. It was a water *bill* — the Manager had paid it for the wrong address by mistake. Lin watched my face the whole time.
bill:1.cnHint: 林把一张____递给我，说是店长错放在他们门上的。
bill:1.hook: Lin did not leave straight away.
bill:1.line: 'This *bill* has your store name on it — I think there has been a mistake.'

paint:1.en: I arrived early to find the Manager on a ladder, touching up the front wall with a small brush. The new shop down the road had clean white walls, so the Manager had decided to *paint* ours a warm yellow. He climbed down and looked pleased. 'First impression,' he said, 'is everything.'
paint:1.cnHint: 店长爬上梯子，决定把店面____成暖黄色，说第一印象最重要。
paint:1.hook: Lin stood at the corner, watching every brushstroke.
paint:1.line: 'I will *paint* it yellow — yellow means we are open and we are happy.'

bean:1.en: Just before sunrise, a student sat on the kerb outside eating a cup of warm *bean* soup she had bought inside. She looked tired, books piled beside her. She told me she had been studying all night for an exam. I brought her a plastic spoon she had forgotten to take.
bean:1.cnHint: 一个学生坐在路边喝____汤，旁边放着一堆书，说她通宵复习了。
bean:1.hook: The title on top of her notes was the same subject I had failed once.
bean:1.line: 'This *bean* soup is the only thing keeping me awake right now.'

birthday:1.en: Tang came rushing out of the store to catch a little girl who had just dropped her bag on the pavement. Inside was a small cake box, slightly crushed. 'It is my grandpa's *birthday*,' she said, her eyes wide with worry. Tang straightened the box carefully and told her it would still taste wonderful.
birthday:1.cnHint: 唐帮一个小女孩捡起掉落的袋子，里面是给爷爷____用的蛋糕，有点压扁了。
birthday:1.hook: The girl ran off, then turned back and smiled at Tang like she knew a secret.
birthday:1.line: 'Today is grandpa's *birthday* — this cake has to be perfect.'

flight:1.en: A man in a coat stood outside checking his watch every thirty seconds. He asked me which bus went to the airport. He had a very early *flight* and was afraid of missing it. I pointed him to the stop one corner down. He thanked me and sprinted away, coat flying behind him.
flight:1.cnHint: 一个男人问我去机场怎么坐车，说他有一个早班____，快赶不上了。
flight:1.hook: He left a small notebook on the bench outside, still open.
flight:1.line: 'My *flight* is at five — if I miss it, six months of work disappears.'

housing:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new corner lot, pointing at the empty building next door. 'This block has good *housing* for staff,' he said, 'cheap rent, close walk.' I looked up at the dark windows and tried to imagine living so near the store. Something felt both cosy and a little strange.
housing:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址附近查看____，觉得员工住在附近很方便。
housing:1.hook: But one window on the third floor already had a light on.
housing:1.line: 'Good *housing* near the store means staff arrive on time.'

behaviour:1.en: A small dog sat outside the new branch site, perfectly still while its owner argued with a city worker. Everyone nearby watched the dog, not the argument. Its calm *behaviour* made me feel a little ashamed — I had been pacing nervously all morning about the opening plan. The dog glanced at me once, then looked away.
behaviour:1.cnHint: 店外一只小狗的____让叙述者感到有些惭愧。
behaviour:1.hook: Then the dog stood up and walked straight through the unlocked front door.
behaviour:1.line: 'That dog's *behaviour* is better than half my staff.'

husband:1.en: A woman stopped me on the pavement near the new site and asked if we sold hot soup. I said not yet. She sighed and said her *husband* always bought soup here on cold nights, back when this corner had an old noodle stall. She touched the bare wall gently, then smiled and walked away.
husband:1.cnHint: 一位女士提到她的____曾常在这个街角买热汤。
husband:1.hook: She left behind a folded paper with a soup recipe on it.
husband:1.line: 'My *husband* used to stop here every single cold night.'

tourist:1.en: A young *tourist* with a large backpack stood at the future store entrance, map in hand, looking very lost. I was checking the site for the Manager and felt sorry for him. I gave him directions to the old street market three blocks east. He thanked me twice, then asked if we had cold drinks yet.
tourist:1.cnHint: 一位____在新店门口迷路，叙述者帮助了他。
tourist:1.hook: He pulled out a camera and took a photo of the empty shopfront instead.
tourist:1.line: 'Excuse me, every *tourist* guide shows a shop on this corner.'

agent:1.en: A woman in a neat grey coat arrived at the new branch corner with a clipboard and a measuring tape. 'I'm the property *agent*,' she told me briskly, 'here to sign the final papers.' She measured the doorway three times, wrote something down, and frowned at her notes. The Manager had said nothing about final papers today.
agent:1.cnHint: 一位____来到新店签署最终文件，叙述者感到意外。
agent:1.hook: The clipboard had two different store names on the top sheet.
agent:1.line: 'As your *agent*, I need to see the Manager right now.'

cash:1.en: Tang met me outside the new site carrying a small envelope. 'Deposit,' she whispered, patting it. 'All *cash*, the way the landlord wanted.' She looked left and right like someone in a spy film, which made me laugh. The morning street was empty except for a pigeon. Tang did not find it funny at all.
cash:1.cnHint: 阿糖带着一个装有____的信封来到新店，举止十分神秘。
cash:1.hook: When she opened the envelope, it held only a handwritten note.
cash:1.line: 'He said bring *cash*, so I brought every note I had.'

competition:1.en: Lin was already standing outside the new branch site when I arrived, arms crossed, studying the street. 'Nice corner,' she said without looking at me. 'The *competition* for this block was fierce — three other chains wanted it.' She finally turned and gave me a small, tight smile. I was not sure if she was pleased or warning me.
competition:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在新店门口提到，这个街角曾面临激烈的____。
competition:1.hook: She then pointed to a store two doors down that had just opened.
competition:1.line: 'We won the *competition* for this corner, but only just.'

farmer:1.en: An old man sat on a crate beside the future store, selling small bags of dried peppers from a worn basket. He told me he was a *farmer* from a village two hours away and came every weekend to sell here. He gave me one bag for free and said the corner had always been lucky. I hoped he was right.
farmer:1.cnHint: 一位____在新店门口卖干辣椒，并说这个街角一直很吉利。
farmer:1.hook: He mentioned he had sold here thirty years ago, before the last store burned down.
farmer:1.line: 'I am a *farmer*, but I know a good corner when I see one.'

collection:1.en: The Manager spread a large paper map across the counter and pointed to six red dots. 'Each dot is a possible site for the new branch,' he said. I looked at the *collection* of locations — a park corner, two bus stops, a school gate, a hospital entrance, and our own street — and suddenly felt the weight of the decision.
collection:1.cnHint: 店长把六个备选新店地址的____摆在柜台上，让我感受到了这个决定的分量。
collection:1.hook: But one of those red dots already had a visitor waiting there every night.
