collection:1.line: 'Look at this *collection* of spots — one of them will be our next store.'

depression:1.en: Tang and I walked the block near the old cinema to check a possible branch site. The pavement dipped sharply in front of an empty unit — a wide *depression* filled with last night's rain. Tang jumped it easily. I did not. We stood there, soaked and laughing, until a passing woman gave us a look of deep pity.
depression:1.cnHint: 唐和我去勘察新店选址时，遇到了路面上一处积满雨水的____，结果我跳过去时失败了。
depression:1.hook: The woman who pitied us stopped, turned back, and handed Tang a business card.
depression:1.line: 'Watch that *depression* in the road — I landed in it this morning and ruined my shoes.'

foot:1.en: The Manager paced the empty shopfront on Maple Lane, measuring the width by counting steps. 'About thirty *foot* across,' he said, more to himself than to me. I wrote it down. A small girl on a bicycle rode past, glanced at us, then circled back as if we were the most interesting thing on the street.
foot:1.cnHint: 店长用脚步丈量枫树街空铺的宽度，估算出大约三十____，一个小女孩骑车路过后又折了回来。
foot:1.hook: The girl stopped and said she came here every single day — and why.
foot:1.line: 'Roughly thirty *foot* wide — that is just enough for our layout.'

graduate:1.en: Outside the university gate, Tang and I counted passing faces to judge foot traffic for a possible branch. A young man in a new shirt stopped us and asked if we were hiring. 'I am a fresh *graduate*,' he said, smiling nervously. Tang looked at me. I looked at Tang. We both looked at our very understaffed store.
graduate:1.cnHint: 在大学门口考察客流时，一位刚刚成为____的年轻人主动向我们询问是否招人。
graduate:1.hook: He pulled out a folded resume that somehow already listed our store's address.
graduate:1.line: 'I am a new *graduate* and I have wanted to work here since my first year.'

intake:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the hospital site and watched people enter. He counted quietly, then nodded. 'High *intake* of visitors every morning — families, nurses, patients picking up small things.' I wrote down his words and noticed a woman across the road had been watching us count for ten minutes, arms folded.
intake:1.cnHint: 店长在医院门口观察每日____的人流量，却没注意到对面有个女人一直盯着我们看。
intake:1.hook: The woman crossed the road and told us she had been planning the same branch herself.
intake:1.line: 'The daily *intake* of people here is three times what we get on our street.'

screen:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street appeared at the corner just as Tang and I were photographing a possible branch site. She held up her phone like a *screen* between her face and ours. 'Just checking the area,' she said, not very convincingly. The corner was quiet. We all stood there pretending not to notice each other.
screen:1.cnHint: 当我和唐在勘察新址时，竞争对手林出现了，她举着手机像一块____挡住了自己的脸。
screen:1.hook: Lin's phone screen, facing us by accident, showed the exact same location pinned on a map.
screen:1.line: 'I am just using my phone as a *screen* from the sun — nothing suspicious at all.'

chair:1.en: The Manager had somehow dragged a folding *chair* to the pavement outside the empty unit on Bridge Street and was sitting in it, drinking tea, watching people walk by. 'Research,' he told me firmly when I arrived. Two neighbours had already joined him with their own stools, and one was offering suggestions about shelf layout.
chair:1.cnHint: 店长搬了把____坐在候选新店门口喝茶"做调研"，附近居民也凑了过来出主意。
chair:1.hook: One neighbour then mentioned they owned the building and had been waiting for a tenant.
chair:1.line: 'Bring a *chair* and sit with me — the foot traffic tells you everything in one hour.'

court:1.en: The last site on the list was beside a community basketball *court*. Even at midnight it was bright and loud, players calling to each other between shots. Tang grinned. 'Late-night snacks, cold drinks, instant noodles,' she said. I was already imagining the queue. Then the ball bounced out and rolled to a stop at my feet.
court:1.cnHint: 候选地址中最后一处位于社区篮球____旁，深夜依然热闹，唐已经开始畅想营业场景了。
court:1.hook: The player who chased the ball looked up and said he had been hoping for years someone would open a store right here.
court:1.line: 'A store next to a *court* like this one would sell out every night, trust me.'

female:1.en: The Manager pointed at a cat sitting outside the door. 'She has been here every night this week,' he said. I looked closer. A small *female* with bright eyes stared back at me, calm as if she owned the place. Tang left a bowl of water out. The cat did not touch it.
female:1.cnHint: 店长指着门外的猫说，这只____每晚都来。
female:1.hook: But the next night, she brought a friend.
female:1.line: 'She is a *female*, so she will probably bring kittens soon,' Tang said quietly.

holiday:1.en: It was the first day of a long *holiday*, and the street outside was almost empty. I expected a quiet shift. Instead, by midnight, every seat near the window was taken by people who had nowhere else to go. Tang smiled and said some folks just did not like being home alone.
holiday:1.cnHint: ____期间街上冷清，但店里却坐满了无处可去的人。
holiday:1.hook: One of them had been sitting there for three nights straight.
holiday:1.line: 'Every *holiday* is the same — lonely people find us,' Tang said with a warm shrug.

pain:1.en: An old man came in just after two in the morning, moving slowly and holding his back. He bought a small bottle of hot water and pressed it against his side. 'The *pain* starts when it gets cold,' he told me, without my asking. He stayed an hour, said nothing more, and left with a small nod.
pain:1.cnHint: 一位老人深夜进来，用热水瓶贴着背部缓解____。
pain:1.hook: He came back the next night, and the night after that.
pain:1.line: 'The *pain* is not so bad when there is a warm place to sit,' he said softly.

player:1.en: A young man in a sports jacket dropped three energy drinks on the counter at midnight. 'Big match tomorrow,' he said. I asked if he was a *player* on the team. He laughed and said no — he just never missed a game. Tang gave him a thumbs up. He bought four more drinks and jogged away.
player:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人买了好几瓶功能饮料，自称是球队的____。
player:1.hook: He came back the next week looking much less cheerful.
player:1.line: 'Every *player* on our team drinks two of these before warm-up,' he said proudly.

production:1.en: Lin walked in carrying a big cardboard box and set it on the counter without a word. Inside were small jars of sauce — her own *production*, she said, from a recipe her grandmother used. She wanted the Manager to sell them. He picked one up, read the label, and raised an eyebrow.
production:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一箱自制酱料，说这是她自己的____，希望店里代卖。
production:1.hook: The Manager's eyebrow stayed raised for a very long time.
production:1.line: 'This *production* took me three weeks to get right,' Lin said, crossing her arms.

secure:1.en: After the new shelves arrived, the Manager spent an hour making sure every bracket was *secure*. He shook each shelf twice, then a third time. Tang caught my eye and tried not to laugh. 'If a shelf falls,' the Manager said without looking up, 'everything on it falls too.' He had a point.
secure:1.cnHint: 店长反复检查新货架是否____，阿糖和我差点忍不住笑出来。
secure:1.hook: One shelf wobbled just slightly, and the Manager went very quiet.
secure:1.line: 'I need every shelf to be *secure* before we put a single item on it,' the Manager said firmly.

audience:1.en: At three in the morning, a woman sat on the step outside and played a small instrument, very softly. I was the only *audience*. She did not seem to mind. After two songs she stood up, bought a warm tea, thanked me with a small bow, and walked away into the dark street.
audience:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一位女士在门口轻轻弹奏，我成了她唯一的____。
audience:1.hook: She left a folded note under the tea cup.
audience:1.line: 'You were a good *audience*,' she said, smiling before she turned to go.

borrow:1.en: A teenage boy knocked on the glass at four in the morning and held up a pen with a question on his face. I let him in. He needed to *borrow* a calculator — his exam was in five hours and his had stopped working. Tang found an old one under the counter. The boy sat down and did not look up for an hour.
borrow:1.cnHint: 一个男孩深夜敲窗，想____一个计算器，因为他的坏掉了。
borrow:1.hook: When he finally left, he forgot to take his student ID.
borrow:1.line: 'Can I *borrow* this until morning? I will bring it back, I promise,' he said.

mile:1.en: The Manager spread a city map across the hood of his car. 'The new branch will be exactly one *mile* from here,' he said, tapping a red circle near the river. I stood on the pavement in the cold morning air, trying to picture a second store glowing in the dark.
mile:1.cnHint: 店长在车盖上摊开地图，指出新分店的____位置。
mile:1.hook: But why was Lin already standing at that exact spot?
mile:1.line: 'One *mile* south — that is where our future is.'

movement:1.en: I noticed a strange *movement* behind the half-built wall across the street — a shadow slipping between wooden boards. Tang grabbed my sleeve. 'Someone is watching us,' she whispered. The Manager kept talking about floor plans, but neither Tang nor I could look away from that wall.
movement:1.cnHint: 街对面的围墙后出现了奇怪的____，让我们心生警觉。
movement:1.hook: The shadow moved again, and this time it had a familiar shape.
movement:1.line: 'That *movement* behind the wall — did you see it too?'

party:1.en: A small crowd had gathered outside the empty shop the Manager wanted to rent. It turned out a local *party* committee had put up a notice claiming the building for a community centre. The Manager read the sign twice, then folded his arms. I quietly wondered whose name was at the bottom.
party:1.cnHint: 店长看中的店面门口贴着一个____的告示，声称要用作社区中心。
party:1.hook: Lin walked past, smiling just a little too widely.
party:1.line: 'The *party* notice went up last night — someone moved fast.'

rescue:1.en: A delivery bicycle had tipped into the ditch beside the road, boxes of drinks scattered everywhere. Before I could think, Tang sprinted over. Her quick *rescue* of the goods meant nothing was broken. The driver kept bowing in thanks. I made a note: Tang is faster than she looks.
rescue:1.cnHint: 送货自行车翻进路边水沟，阿糖迅速____了那些货物。
rescue:1.hook: One box had a label that matched our store, not the new branch.
rescue:1.line: 'Lucky I was here for the *rescue*, or everything would be lost.'

writing:1.en: Taped to the lamppost outside the future branch was a sheet of paper covered in neat *writing*. It listed reasons why the neighbourhood did not want a convenience store on that corner. I read every line. The arguments were careful, almost professional. Someone had spent real time on this.
writing:1.cnHint: 路灯柱上贴着一张满是____的纸，列出反对开分店的理由。
writing:1.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Lin's.
writing:1.line: 'This *writing* is too neat to be just one angry neighbour.'

bite:1.en: Tang handed me a warm meat bun as we stood outside the half-empty building. I took one *bite* and immediately felt better about the cold and the long morning. 'Food first, problems second,' she said. The Manager appeared from around the corner, spotted the bun, and his face softened too.
bite:1.cnHint: 阿糖递来热包子，我____了一口，寒意顿时减轻了许多。
bite:1.hook: The Manager said the buns came from a shop that might become our rival.
bite:1.line: 'Go on, take a *bite* — you have been frowning for an hour.'

capture:1.en: I tried to *capture* the whole scene on my phone — the half-finished sign, the Manager pointing at the roofline, Tang measuring the doorway with her arms spread wide. A photo could not hold the feeling, though. The street was quiet except for pigeons, and everything felt oddly important.
capture:1.cnHint: 我想用手机____眼前这一幕——店长和阿糖正在勘察新店面。
capture:1.hook: When I looked at the photo later, there was a face in the window above.
capture:1.line: 'Try to *capture* the sign in the shot — the Manager wants a record.'

cope:1.en: The building was dustier inside than the Manager had expected. Tang sneezed four times in a row. I tried to *cope* with the darkness by propping the door open with a brick. Light flooded in, and we all stood still for a moment, looking at the space that might soon become our second home.
cope:1.cnHint: 新店面里又黑又脏，我们各自想办法____眼前的困难。
cope:1.hook: In the far corner, someone had left a fresh cup of tea.
cope:1.line: 'How do you *cope* with the dark? I can barely see a thing.'

burn:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site at dawn, watching workers pour hot tar on the road nearby. A careless splash landed on his wrist, leaving a small *burn* that he barely noticed. He kept his eyes on the signboard going up above the door, smiling quietly to himself.
burn:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店门口看招牌安装，手腕上不小心留下了一处____。
burn:1.hook: But the signboard spelled the store's name completely wrong.
burn:1.line: 'A little *burn* never stopped a grand opening,' the Manager said, wrapping his wrist.

cook:1.en: Lin stood across the street from the new branch, watching a food cart owner *cook* noodles on an open flame right in front of the entrance. The smell drifted everywhere. Lin crossed her arms and thought: that cart was pulling in every hungry person who might have walked through their door instead.
cook:1.cnHint: 林站在新分店对面，看着一个摊主在门口____面条，抢走了不少客流。
cook:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and started making a very particular call.
cook:1.line: 'Why does he get to *cook* right outside our new branch?' Lin muttered.

corporate:1.en: A man in a stiff suit arrived at the new branch before it even opened, sliding a thick envelope under the door. The Manager picked it up outside and read the header: it was a *corporate* notice from a large chain store two blocks away, warning them about a shared supplier agreement. The street felt very quiet suddenly.
corporate:1.cnHint: 一个西装男在新分店门口塞进一封____通知，让店长顿时沉默了。
corporate:1.hook: The Manager read the last line twice, then looked up the street slowly.
corporate:1.line: 'This is a *corporate* matter,' the suited man said, adjusting his tie firmly.

dangerous:1.en: Tang was sent to hang a banner above the new branch entrance using a short ladder. The wind picked up fast, and the ladder began to sway against the wall. A woman passing by stopped and called out that the whole situation looked very *dangerous*. Tang laughed nervously and kept climbing anyway.
dangerous:1.cnHint: 唐在新分店门口爬梯子挂横幅，路过的人大喊这样做很____。
dangerous:1.hook: Then one ladder leg lifted clean off the pavement.
dangerous:1.line: 'This is *dangerous*, you should come down right now!' the woman shouted up.

debt:1.en: Outside the new branch on opening morning, an old man sat on a folding chair and refused to leave. The Manager spoke to him gently and learned that the building's previous tenant had left without settling a *debt* with the old man's small supply shop. The old man just wanted someone to listen.
debt:1.cnHint: 开业当天，一位老人坐在新分店门口，原来前租户留下了一笔____未还。
debt:1.hook: The Manager sat down in a second chair and said nothing for a long moment.
debt:1.line: 'He left without clearing the *debt*, and nobody cared,' the old man said quietly.

discipline:1.en: The Manager lined up the new branch staff on the pavement before the doors opened, running through every rule out loud. He told them that good *discipline* in a small store meant the difference between keeping customers and losing them in the first week. Lin watched from across the street, taking quiet notes in a little book.
discipline:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店门外给员工训话，强调良好的____是留住顾客的关键。
discipline:1.hook: Lin smiled and wrote one final note, then closed her little book with a snap.
discipline:1.line: '*Discipline* starts before the first customer even walks in,' the Manager said firmly.

error:1.en: Tang was pasting the new branch's opening-hours sign onto the glass door when he noticed an *error*: someone had printed the closing time as two in the afternoon instead of two in the morning. A small crowd had gathered outside, reading the sign and already looking confused and a little disappointed.
error:1.cnHint: 唐在新分店玻璃门上贴营业时间告示时，发现上面有一处____，引来路人围观。
error:1.hook: Tang's phone rang — it was the Manager, calling from just inside the door.
error:1.line: 'There is an *error* on the sign — we close at two in the morning,' Tang said.

gym:1.en: The new branch sat directly between a closed bakery and a *gym* whose members spilled onto the pavement every evening after their workouts, loud and cheerful and very thirsty. The Manager had chosen the location carefully. By the end of the first night, the sports drink shelf was already empty, and he was back on the phone with the supplier.
gym:1.cnHint: 新分店开在一家____旁边，店长选址很用心，第一晚运动饮料就卖空了。
gym:1.hook: But the gym's owner strolled in last, smiled, and asked for a word.
gym:1.line: 'The *gym* next door is our best neighbour,' the Manager told Tang happily.

salary:1.en: The Manager called me outside before my first shift. He pointed at the small sign above the door and said the store was opening a second branch nearby. Then he slid a paper across the hood of his car. My new *salary* was printed at the bottom — higher than I had expected for a night clerk.
salary:1.cnHint: 店长在外面告诉我，新分店开张，我的____也涨了。
salary:1.hook: But the number had a condition written in red ink.
salary:1.line: 'Your *salary* goes up the day the new branch opens,' he said.

shopping:1.en: On the corner opposite our store, Lin set up a small table and handed out flyers for the new branch. People passed by with bags already full from the weekend market. One older woman stopped, read the flyer, and nodded slowly. 'Good location,' she said. Lin smiled. All that morning *shopping* foot traffic walked straight past us toward the new site.
shopping:1.cnHint: 林在街角发传单，____的人群都被吸引向新店。
shopping:1.hook: Then Lin glanced back at our store with a very odd expression.
shopping:1.line: 'The *shopping* crowd this morning is bigger than I expected,' Lin said.

tendency:1.en: Tang and I stood outside counting customers who entered Lin's new branch across the street. We had been tracking the numbers all week. Tang tapped her notebook. 'There is a clear *tendency*,' she said quietly. 'More people try a new place once, just for curiosity.' She closed the notebook and went back inside to restock the shelves.
tendency:1.cnHint: 唐观察后发现，顾客有一种明显的____去尝试新店。
tendency:1.hook: Tang had underlined one number three times and said nothing more.
tendency:1.line: 'I notice a *tendency* for new stores to win the first week,' Tang said.

tough:1.en: The morning the second branch opened, the Manager asked me to carry a heavy folding sign two blocks down the road. The summer air was already thick and the pavement shone with heat. It was *tough* work, but I made it. I planted the sign on the corner and stood back to read it: grand opening, free coffee, today only.
tough:1.cnHint: 我扛着重广告牌走了两条街，这份活儿真____。
tough:1.hook: A stranger read the sign, then looked at me with sudden suspicion.
tough:1.line: 'It is *tough* to move that sign alone — let me help,' Tang said.

tour:1.en: The Manager decided to give the delivery driver a quick *tour* of the new branch before the first stock arrived. They walked the narrow aisles, tested the cold cabinet, and checked the back room. I waited outside with a clipboard. The driver said very little the whole time, only nodding at each item the Manager pointed to.
tour:1.cnHint: 店长带司机参观了新店，我站在外面等候，做了一次____。
tour:1.hook: The driver paused at the back door and asked one strange question.
tour:1.line: 'Let me *tour* the storage room one more time,' the driver said quietly.

wake:1.en: After the opening ceremony the small crowd drifted away down the street. In the *wake* of all that noise and ribbon and free samples, the block felt suddenly empty. A single flyer turned slow circles in the gutter. Tang picked it up, smoothed it flat, and tucked it into her apron pocket without a word.
wake:1.cnHint: 热闹结束后，街道在喧嚣的____中变得出奇地安静。
wake:1.hook: Tang had kept one item from the ceremony that no one else noticed.
wake:1.line: 'In the *wake* of the opening, something feels different about this street,' Tang said.

annual:1.en: Outside the new branch, the Manager pinned a banner to the wall. It announced the store's *annual* street fair, moved this year to the new location. Neighbors stopped to read it. An old man asked whether the fair would still have the same grilled-corn stall. The Manager said he was working on it, which meant probably not.
annual:1.cnHint: 店长在新店外张贴海报，宣布今年的____街头集市地点有变。
annual:1.hook: One neighbor's face fell, and she walked away without another word.
annual:1.line: 'Our *annual* fair draws the whole street together,' the Manager said proudly.

charity:1.en: Lin had arranged a small *charity* box on a table outside the new branch, collecting coins for the community garden two streets over. A boy dropped in his last coin and asked for a receipt. Lin had no receipt. The boy frowned, picked up his empty cup, and sat on the kerb, clearly deciding whether that counted as a real donation.
charity:1.cnHint: 林在新店外为社区花园募集____捐款，一个男孩投下最后一枚硬币。
charity:1.hook: The boy then asked Lin a question nobody had ever thought to ask.
charity:1.line: 'The *charity* box was full by noon — people here are very kind,' Lin said.

couple:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new shop site, clipboard in hand. A *couple* walked past slowly, the woman pointing at the empty window, the man nodding. They stopped, pressed their faces to the glass, and smiled at each other. The Manager watched them and quietly wrote something on her clipboard.
couple:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址外观察，一____经过时对着空橱窗指指点点。
couple:1.hook: Whatever she wrote, she circled it twice.
couple:1.line: 'A *couple* like that is exactly our target customer,' she said.

definition:1.en: Lin stood across the street, staring at the rival company's new sign. The letters were blurry and the colours faded. 'Poor *definition*,' she said to herself, meaning the image was unclear — but also, perhaps, that the brand had no real identity. She took a photo and walked away smiling.
definition:1.cnHint: 林站在街对面，评价对手新招牌的____太差，图像模糊。
definition:1.hook: That photo would appear in a very interesting presentation later.
definition:1.line: 'The *definition* of their logo is terrible — you can barely read it,' Lin said.

imagination:1.en: I was sweeping the pavement outside when a small boy stopped and stared at the store's dark back room. 'Is there a dragon in there?' he asked. I said no. He looked disappointed. 'Use your *imagination*,' his grandmother told him, pulling him along. He glanced back at the door with wide eyes.
imagination:1.cnHint: 一个小男孩盯着店里的黑暗角落，他的祖母叫他发挥____。
imagination:1.hook: The next night, I found a small paper dragon on the doorstep.
imagination:1.line: 'Use your *imagination* — a good store can be anything you want,' the grandmother said.

journey:1.en: Tang arrived at the new shop site out of breath. She had taken the wrong bus, then walked twenty minutes in the wrong direction. 'That *journey* took me an hour,' she said, dropping onto a low wall. The Manager simply handed her a measuring tape. Tang stared at it.
journey:1.cnHint: 唐去新店选址的____走错了路，整整花了一个小时才到。
journey:1.hook: The measuring tape was not for the room — it was for Tang.
journey:1.line: 'The *journey* here told me one thing: nobody will find this place easily,' Tang said.

nearby:1.en: The Manager had chosen the site partly because of a large park *nearby*. On weekend mornings, people poured out of that park hungry and thirsty, and there was nothing open for them. I watched them walk past the empty shopfront, looking left and right for somewhere to go. The Manager watched too, counting quietly.
nearby:1.cnHint: 店长选新址，部分原因是____有一座公园，周末人流量大。
nearby:1.hook: She stopped counting at sixty — in under ten minutes.
nearby:1.line: 'The park *nearby* means we will never have a quiet Saturday morning,' the Manager said.

perspective:1.en: Lin and I stood at opposite ends of the street and looked at the new shopfront at the same time. From my end it looked bright and welcoming. From hers, the sun hit the glass hard and turned it into a mirror. 'It depends on your *perspective*,' Lin called out, shielding her eyes.
perspective:1.cnHint: 林和我从街道两端看新店，因为____不同，看到的效果完全不一样。
perspective:1.hook: She was talking about the light — I think she meant something else too.
perspective:1.line: 'From my *perspective*, this site has one serious problem,' Lin said, pointing at the sun.

requirement:1.en: The city inspector arrived with a long checklist. Each *requirement* for a new food shop had its own small box, and he ticked them slowly, one by one. The Manager followed him in silence. When he paused at the back door and said nothing for ten seconds, the Manager's smile did not move at all.
requirement:1.cnHint: 市政检查员带着清单来检查新店，逐一核对开业的每项____。
requirement:1.hook: That ten-second pause was about something not on the list.
requirement:1.line: 'Every *requirement* is met — except one thing I noticed outside,' the inspector said.

signal:1.en: Just before the Manager unlocked the new shop for the first trial run, she looked up and down the quiet street. A cat sitting on the wall opposite slowly blinked once. The Manager laughed softly. 'That is my *signal*,' she said, and turned the key. The door swung open to the warm morning air.
signal:1.cnHint: 店长说对面墙上一只猫的眨眼是她开门的____。
signal:1.hook: Inside, something was already waiting on the counter.
signal:1.line: 'When it blinks, that is my *signal* to begin,' the Manager said, smiling at the cat.

strength:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch location, arms crossed, staring at the empty shopfront across the street. Lin leaned against the wall beside him. 'We need the *strength* of both stores working together,' the Manager said, 'not one pulling the other down.' A delivery truck rumbled past, shaking the sign above the door.
strength:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店门口，强调两家店需要合力____才能成功。
strength:1.hook: But Lin was already looking at the sign with a strange smile.
strength:1.line: 'We need the *strength* of both stores working together, not against each other.'

survive:1.en: Rain hammered the street corner where the new branch was going up. I held an umbrella over the Manager while he checked the building work. 'A store has to *survive* its first winter,' he said quietly, watching water pour off the roof. Somewhere behind us, a cat cried out from under a box.
survive:1.cnHint: 暴雨中，店长担心新分店能否____过第一个冬天。
survive:1.hook: The cat was not alone under that box.
survive:1.line: 'A store has to *survive* its first winter — that is the only rule.'

touch:1.en: Tang handed out small sample bags of snacks to people passing by the new branch site. Most walked on without a word. Then an old man stopped, took a bag, and bowed. That small *touch* of gratitude made Tang stand a little straighter for the rest of the afternoon.
touch:1.cnHint: 老人的一个感谢动作给了阿糖一种____，让他精神为之一振。
touch:1.hook: The old man would come back that evening — with a question no one expected.
touch:1.line: 'That small *touch* of thanks means more than a hundred cold looks.'

trap:1.en: Lin pointed to a rival store that had just opened two blocks from our new branch. 'That location is a *trap*,' she said, arms folded. 'They want us to cut prices and run out of money trying to match them.' I looked at the bright signs and felt the first cold drop of doubt.
trap:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林警告说对手新店的位置是个____，意在逼我们打价格战。
trap:1.hook: What Lin did not mention was that she had been inside that store earlier.
trap:1.line: 'That location is a *trap* — do not let them pull us into a price war.'

tv:1.en: A small crowd had gathered on the pavement outside the new branch because a local news crew had parked their van nearby. Someone said the crew was looking for a story about the street. The Manager straightened his apron. 'If we end up on *TV*,' he whispered to me, 'smile and say nothing about the roof.'
tv:1.cnHint: 街上来了新闻摄制组，店长担心新分店上____时会暴露屋顶问题。
tv:1.hook: The reporter was already walking straight towards us.
tv:1.line: 'If we end up on *TV*, just smile and say absolutely nothing about the roof.'

victim:1.en: The signboard for the new branch fell during a gust of wind and nearly hit a passing cyclist. The cyclist stopped, unhurt but furious. 'I refuse to be a *victim* of your grand opening,' he shouted. The Manager bowed and offered a free coffee. I quietly began tying the replacement sign much more firmly.
victim:1.cnHint: 招牌被风吹落，差点砸到路人，骑车人怒称自己险些成为____。
victim:1.hook: The cyclist pocketed the coffee voucher and then looked up at our second sign.
victim:1.line: 'I refuse to be a *victim* of your poorly hung signboard on opening day.'

zone:1.en: The Manager had divided the pavement in front of the new branch into sections with coloured tape. 'This *zone* is for queuing, that one is for bikes, and that far strip is for people who just want to stand and think,' he explained. Tang and I looked at each other. The thinking strip was already full.
zone:1.cnHint: 店长把门前人行道划分成不同____，其中"思考区"一开放就站满了人。
zone:1.hook: One man in the thinking zone had been there for forty minutes without moving.
zone:1.line: 'This *zone* is for queuing — please do not bring your bicycle into it.'

afraid:1.en: I helped carry boxes of stock up to the new branch before dawn. The street was empty and oddly silent. When I reached the top step, I stopped. I was *afraid*, though I could not say why — only that the door was open when the Manager had definitely locked it the night before.
afraid:1.cnHint: 黎明前独自送货时，我发现大门敞开，心里感到____。
afraid:1.hook: Then something moved in the shadows just inside the doorway.
afraid:1.line: 'I am not *afraid* of hard work — but an open locked door is a different thing.'

behave:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, watching workers carry boxes in. A small crowd gathered on the pavement. One boy kept running between the workers' legs. The Manager clapped his hands. 'Kids near a building site must *behave*,' he said firmly, guiding the boy back to his mother.
behave:1.cnHint: 店长在新分店门口提醒一个顽皮的小孩要____。
behave:1.hook: The boy's mother smiled — but her eyes looked nervous.
behave:1.line: 'Everyone must *behave* when workers are moving heavy things around.'

cent:1.en: Outside the new branch, Tang was taping a grand-opening sign to the window. A old man stopped and studied the price list. He counted every coin in his palm, then looked up. 'Not a single *cent* more than last year,' he murmured, satisfied, and walked inside without another word.
cent:1.cnHint: 一位老爷爷在新分店门口仔细核对价格，发现每一____都没有涨。
cent:1.hook: Tang wondered how the old man knew last year's prices by heart.
cent:1.line: 'I checked — not one *cent* has changed since the old store opened.'

commercial:1.en: A man in a bright jacket was filming outside the new branch before it opened. He moved a small camera left and right, pointing at the fresh sign. The Manager came out and asked what he was doing. 'A short *commercial* for the street market page,' the man said cheerfully, still filming.
commercial:1.cnHint: 一个男人在新分店门外拍摄____，让店长感到意外。
commercial:1.hook: Nobody had given him permission to film.
commercial:1.line: 'This little *commercial* will bring you a hundred new customers, I promise.'

death:1.en: Lin was sweeping the pavement in front of the new branch when a neighbour rushed over. 'Did you hear?' the neighbour whispered. 'The old tea shop on this corner closed last month — practically *death* for the whole block.' Lin leaned on the broom and looked up and down the quiet street.
death:1.cnHint: 邻居告诉林，街角老茶馆的关闭对整条街来说简直是____。
death:1.hook: Lin noticed the empty tea-shop window still had a light on inside.
death:1.line: 'Losing that tea shop was like a small *death* for everyone here.'

escape:1.en: The Manager was pasting notices on the board outside the new branch. Suddenly a cat shot out from under a parked vehicle and ran between his feet. Behind it came a young girl, breathless. 'Please catch her — she always tries to *escape* when there is too much noise,' the girl begged.
escape:1.cnHint: 一只小猫趁外面施工嘈杂，试图____，小女孩急忙来找店长帮忙。
escape:1.hook: The cat slipped around the corner and vanished into the dark lane.
escape:1.line: 'She will *escape* every time she hears loud banging — please help me.'

expose:1.en: Tang was arranging a small outdoor rack of snacks near the new branch entrance. The Manager came over and frowned. 'Do not *expose* the chocolate bars to direct sun,' he said, pointing at the bright afternoon light falling on the shelf. Tang moved the rack into the shade without a word.
expose:1.cnHint: 店长提醒唐不要将巧克力____在强烈的阳光下。
expose:1.hook: Tang then noticed something odd behind the rack — a folded piece of paper.
expose:1.line: 'Never *expose* the chocolate to sun — it ruins the whole box.'

floor:1.en: Outside the new branch, workers had just finished laying the entrance tiles. The Manager crouched down and pressed one tile gently. 'The *floor* must be perfectly level or customers will trip,' he told Tang, who was standing nearby with a clipboard. Tang wrote something down and called the tile worker back over.
floor:1.cnHint: 店长蹲下检查新分店门口的____，要求必须完全平整。
floor:1.hook: The tile worker came back looking more worried than expected.
floor:1.line: 'Check every tile — the *floor* at the entrance has to be perfectly level.'

foundation:1.en: Lin passed the new branch on her lunch break and paused. Workers were still doing something beneath the front step. A worker noticed her looking and said, 'We are fixing the *foundation* — the ground here shifted a little last winter.' Lin glanced at the building above and quietly decided to ask the Manager about it later.
foundation:1.cnHint: 工人告诉林，新分店的____去年冬天有些移位，正在修复。
foundation:1.hook: Lin had not told the Manager she already knew about the problem.
foundation:1.line: 'The *foundation* shifted last winter, so we are fixing it before opening day.'

frame:1.en: The Manager stood on the pavement outside the empty shop unit, holding up a rough wooden *frame* where the new sign would go. He tilted it left, then right, squinting at the angle. Lin watched from across the street, arms folded, clearly calculating something of her own.
frame:1.cnHint: 店长站在新店门口，举着一个木____比划新招牌的位置。
frame:1.hook: Lin pulled out a tape measure and smiled to herself.
frame:1.line: 'This *frame* needs to be exactly straight, or the whole sign looks cheap.'

friday:1.en: The delivery truck was supposed to arrive on *Friday*, but it was already Saturday morning and the boxes of shelving still had not come. The Manager paced the empty shop floor while Tang checked the phone for messages. A small crowd of curious neighbours pressed their faces against the glass door.
friday:1.cnHint: 货车原定____到货，但已经是周六早上了，货还没有影子。
friday:1.hook: Then someone knocked — from inside the locked storage room.
friday:1.line: 'I booked the truck for *Friday*. Where did one whole day go?'

grain:1.en: Tang swept the doorstep of the new branch and found the pavement was rough old stone, every *grain* of grit catching the early light like tiny stars. It was a good corner, she decided — solid, honest, the kind of spot where people stop without being asked. She felt quietly proud already.
grain:1.cnHint: 阿糖打扫新店门口时，注意到石板路上每一____沙砾都在晨光中闪闪发亮。
grain:1.hook: A stranger stopped, stared at the door, and said nothing.
grain:1.line: 'Even a single *grain* of dirt on the step gives the wrong first impression.'

implication:1.en: Lin put a sign in her own shop window directly opposite the new branch: 'Original store — here since day one.' The *implication* was clear to everyone on the street — she wanted customers to think the Manager's new branch was somehow a copy. Tang read it twice and raised an eyebrow.
implication:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在自家店门口贴出告示，____不言而喻：她想让街坊觉得新店是山寨货。
implication:1.hook: The Manager read the sign, then smiled in a way Tang had never seen before.
implication:1.line: 'The *implication* of that sign is obvious, but I think she has made a mistake.'

incredible:1.en: When the Manager finally flipped the lights on inside the new branch for the first time, the whole corner of the street lit up like a small sun. An old woman walking past stopped, put a hand over her heart, and whispered that it was *incredible* how a dark old unit could become somewhere so warm and bright overnight.
incredible:1.cnHint: 新店第一次亮灯时，路过的老奶奶觉得这变化____，忍不住停下脚步。
incredible:1.hook: But across the street, Lin's lights flickered and went out.
incredible:1.line: 'It is *incredible* — yesterday this place was empty, today it feels like home.'

net:1.en: Tang strung a small *net* of tiny bulbs across the front of the new branch, the kind used to catch light rather than fish. By dusk the threads glowed gold against the dark shop front and a group of children stopped on the pavement to stare upward, mouths open, pointing at each small bright dot.
net:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店门口挂上一张灯泡小____，傍晚亮起来时引来一群孩子驻足仰望。
net:1.hook: One child asked if the lights were actually alive.
net:1.line: 'I made this *net* of lights myself — two hours, zero broken bulbs, total success.'

obtain:1.en: To *obtain* the permit for the outdoor sign, the Manager had spent three mornings at the district office, each time leaving with a different form and a polite apology. Today he finally walked out holding a single stamped paper above his head like a small trophy. Tang cheered from the pavement twenty metres away.
obtain:1.cnHint: 为了____户外招牌许可证，店长跑了三趟区政府，今天终于拿到了盖章文件。
obtain:1.hook: The permit had the wrong address printed on line four.
obtain:1.line: 'To *obtain* one stamp around here, you need more patience than I ever knew I had.'

pair:1.en: The Manager bought a *pair* of potted plants to place either side of the new branch door, one for luck and one for balance, he said. He set them down, stepped back to look, and immediately swapped them left to right. Then right to left. Then left to right again. Tang covered her mouth so he would not see her laughing.
pair:1.cnHint: 店长买了一____盆栽摆在新店门口，却反复调换左右位置，拿不定主意。
pair:1.hook: Lin walked past, glanced at the plants, and moved one six centimetres without a word.
pair:1.line: 'A *pair* of healthy plants at the door tells every customer: we pay attention to small things.'

persuade:1.en: The Manager stood outside in the cold, pointing at the empty shop next door. He wanted to rent it for a second store. I watched him talk to the landlord for twenty minutes. He smiled, he reasoned, he even brought a box of rice balls. Finally the landlord nodded. Nobody could *persuade* people quite like the Manager.
persuade:1.cnHint: 店长站在街角，费了好大劲儿才让房东答应把隔壁店面____给他。
persuade:1.hook: But the landlord's son stepped out and crossed his arms.
persuade:1.line: 'I can *persuade* anyone — just give me time and rice balls.'

preference:1.en: Lin from the rival store across the street stopped me on my way to work. She was carrying two cups of hot tea. 'I did a survey,' she said cheerfully. 'Customers in this area have a clear *preference* for warmer drinks after midnight.' She handed me one cup and walked away smiling.
preference:1.cnHint: 竞争对手林在街上告诉我，附近顾客对深夜饮品有明显的____。
preference:1.hook: The survey paper she left behind had our store's name circled in red.
preference:1.line: 'Their *preference* is warm drinks — that is our advantage, not yours.'

reliable:1.en: Tang and I were taping a new sign above the door when a regular customer stopped on the pavement below. 'This store is the most *reliable* thing on this street,' he said quietly. 'Rain or cold, the light is always on.' Tang and I looked at each other and felt something warm settle in our chests.
reliable:1.cnHint: 一位老顾客站在门口街道上，夸这家店是街上最____的存在。
reliable:1.hook: Then he added, 'I hope the new branch doesn't change that.'
reliable:1.line: 'A *reliable* store is worth more than ten flashy ones.'

suspect:1.en: A woman in a long coat paused outside the window at two in the morning, staring at the poster about our new branch. She wrote something in a notebook. Tang nudged me. 'I *suspect* she works for the shop on Pine Road,' he whispered. I wiped the glass and looked again. She was gone.
suspect:1.cnHint: 一个深夜在窗外记笔记的女人让唐____她另有来意。
suspect:1.hook: Her notebook had fallen open on the pavement — one page faced up.
suspect:1.line: 'I *suspect* she was counting how many customers we had tonight.'

yield:1.en: The small vegetable seller on the corner offered the Manager a deal: let customers park their bikes in front of our store and he would give us first pick of his morning stock. The Manager thought for a moment, then agreed to *yield* the bike space. By six a.m. the freshest greens sat by our register.
yield:1.cnHint: 店长同意____出门口的自行车停放区，换来了街角菜贩的优先供货权。
yield:1.hook: Nobody noticed the rival store had made the same offer yesterday.
yield:1.line: 'We *yield* the space, they give us the best stock — fair trade.'

abandon:1.en: Halfway down the block I found a cardboard box with a little folding table inside. A note said: 'Free — moving away.' The Manager had been looking for a table for the new branch entrance. I almost walked past, but I could not *abandon* the idea that it was perfect. I carried it back alone.
abandon:1.cnHint: 我在街上发现了一张被人____的折叠桌，觉得它正好适合新分店用。
abandon:1.hook: The Manager read the moving note twice, then looked up the street.
abandon:1.line: 'Never *abandon* a useful thing just because someone else did.'

anxious:1.en: I arrived early to help hang a banner for the new branch across the street-facing wall. The ladder wobbled. Cars passed close. Tang held the base and talked non-stop to keep me calm, but I could see he was *anxious* too — his knuckles were white and his eyes never left the banner's edge.
anxious:1.cnHint: 挂新分店横幅时，我和唐站在街边梯子上，心里都有些____。
anxious:1.hook: Then one corner of the banner slipped from my fingers.
anxious:1.line: 'I am *anxious* too, but we keep going — just do not look down.'

assess:1.en: The Manager walked the pavement outside the new location three times, counting steps from the bus stop, watching where people slowed down, noting which direction the wind blew from. 'I like to *assess* a spot before I commit,' he told me. He pulled out a small notebook and filled half a page in two minutes.
assess:1.cnHint: 店长在新店选址的街道上来回踱步，仔细____这个地点是否合适。
assess:1.hook: He closed the notebook and said the number he was thinking of was too low.
assess:1.line: 'Always *assess* the street at night and again at morning rush hour.'

preserve:1.en: The Manager stood outside the old corner building, studying the faded paint and cracked tiles. 'We must *preserve* this look,' he said softly, running a hand along the wall. 'People trust a place that feels like it has always been here.' A figure watched from across the street.
preserve:1.cnHint: 店长坚持要____这栋老建筑原有的样子，引起了路人的注意。
preserve:1.hook: The watching figure stepped closer, carrying a rolled-up document.
preserve:1.line: 'We must *preserve* this look, or the regulars will never come.'

procedure:1.en: Tang arrived early and found a long queue already forming outside the new branch site. The permit officer explained every *procedure* required before the doors could open: inspection, signature, stamp, and a final walkthrough. Tang wrote it all down on a notepad, biting the pen in concentration.
procedure:1.cnHint: 唐发现开新店需要走一套复杂的____，认真地记录着每个步骤。
procedure:1.hook: The last item on the list made Tang go very quiet.
procedure:1.line: 'Follow each *procedure* exactly, or the permit will be refused.'

reasonable:1.en: Lin set up a small table outside and offered free coffee to people passing by. A resident stopped and asked how much the new store would charge for late-night snacks. Lin smiled and said the prices would be very *reasonable*, maybe even lower than the old shop down the road. The resident looked interested.
reasonable:1.cnHint: 林向路人保证新店的价格非常____，吸引了附近居民驻足询问。
reasonable:1.hook: Just then the old shop's owner walked around the corner.
reasonable:1.line: 'Our prices are *reasonable* — you will not find cheaper nearby.'

reduction:1.en: The Manager taped a large sign to the window of the future branch. It read: grand opening sale, big *reduction* on all drinks for the first week. A small crowd gathered on the pavement, people taking photos and pointing. One woman asked when exactly the doors would open.
reduction:1.cnHint: 店长在新店橱窗贴出告示，宣布开业期间饮料将有大幅____。
reduction:1.hook: Nobody noticed the rival store van parked just behind them.
reduction:1.line: 'A *reduction* like this in the first week will bring everyone in.'

season:1.en: It was the busy *season* for hot drinks, and the Manager had chosen this cold autumn stretch on purpose to open the new branch. Steam rose from cups being handed to workers on their morning walk past the site. The smell drifted all the way to the bus stop.
season:1.cnHint: 店长特意选在热饮____开新店，吸引了清晨上班的路人。
season:1.hook: A figure at the bus stop turned and began walking back toward the store.
season:1.line: 'This *season* is perfect — cold air makes everyone want something warm.'

sector:1.en: Tang stood at the crossroads, map in hand, explaining to the Manager why this block was the right choice. 'Every food and drink *sector* in this district is squeezed into one street, but this corner has nothing,' Tang said, circling the spot with a finger. The Manager nodded slowly.
sector:1.cnHint: 唐向店长分析这个街角在餐饮____上的空白，认为这里是开新店的好地方。
sector:1.hook: Lin, standing nearby, quietly took out a phone and made a call.
sector:1.line: 'The food *sector* here is empty — we should move fast.'

setting:1.en: The Manager walked around the outside of the building one last time, checking the light, the trees, the angle of the small bench near the door. 'The *setting* matters as much as the stock,' he told Tang quietly. 'People decide in three seconds whether to come in or keep walking.'
setting:1.cnHint: 店长仔细打量新店周围的____，认为环境对吸引顾客至关重要。
setting:1.hook: Tang glanced up and saw Lin measuring the same street from the far end.
setting:1.line: 'The *setting* here is perfect — warm light, quiet street, good bench.'

shrink:1.en: A sudden cold wind swept down the street as Tang unrolled the banner for the new branch. Everyone seemed to *shrink* into their coats at once, shoulders rising, chins tucking down. Tang gripped the banner tighter and laughed. 'Free hot soup on opening day,' Tang called out. Several heads turned.
shrink:1.cnHint: 一阵冷风吹来，街上的人纷纷____进外套里，唐趁机宣传开业当天有免费热汤。
shrink:1.hook: One of the turning heads belonged to someone carrying a competitor's cup.
shrink:1.line: 'Watch them *shrink* from the cold — then our hot soup wins them over.'

beautiful:1.en: The Manager led me outside at 5 a.m. to show me the new sign above the door. Morning light caught the bright letters, and the whole corner of the street seemed to glow. 'Every new branch starts with a good sign,' he said. The empty street looked *beautiful* in that pale light, calm and full of quiet promise.
beautiful:1.cnHint: 清晨，店长带我出门欣赏新招牌，整条街在晨光中显得格外____。
beautiful:1.hook: Then a shadow appeared at the far end of the street, moving fast.
beautiful:1.line: 'This corner looks *beautiful* at dawn — that is why I chose it.'

combine:1.en: The Manager unrolled two paper maps on the hood of his car outside. One showed the new branch location; the other showed the bus routes nearby. 'We need to *combine* these ideas,' he said, tapping both sheets. 'Foot traffic plus late buses equals customers.' I nodded, pretending I understood business better than I did.
combine:1.cnHint: 店长在车外把两张地图摊开，想把两份信息____起来规划新店选址。
combine:1.hook: He had circled one corner in red ink three separate times.
combine:1.line: 'If we *combine* the two maps, the best spot becomes obvious.'

complicated:1.en: Standing outside the new branch on opening day, I tried to read the new electronic lock panel. There were twelve buttons and a tiny screen showing a code I had never seen before. 'Is this *complicated* on purpose?' I asked Tang. He laughed and said the Manager had changed the code that morning and forgotten to tell anyone.
complicated:1.cnHint: 新店门口的电子锁面板让我一头雾水，操作实在太____了。
complicated:1.hook: Inside, the Manager was pressing buttons with a worried look.
complicated:1.line: 'The lock is too *complicated* — even the Manager can't open it now.'

crash:1.en: Tang and I were carrying a heavy shelf unit through the side door of the new branch when my foot caught the step. There was a loud *crash* as one end hit the pavement. A cat on the wall above us blinked once and walked away without interest. 'Smooth,' said Tang. We checked the shelf. It was fine. We were not as fine.
crash:1.cnHint: 搬货架时我绊了一跤，货架落地发出巨大的____声，把街上的猫都惊到了。
crash:1.hook: The Manager appeared at the window, wearing a very calm expression.
crash:1.line: 'That *crash* was loud enough to wake the whole street, honestly.'

creature:1.en: Before the new branch opened, I was sweeping the front step when I noticed a small, round *creature* sitting just inside the door — a turtle, very still, watching me with patient eyes. No one knew where it came from. Tang said it must be a sign of good luck. The Manager said it was probably Lin's fault somehow.
creature:1.cnHint: 新店开张前，我在门口扫地时发现一只小____静静地坐在门里看着我。
creature:1.hook: The next morning, the turtle had moved itself behind the cash register.
creature:1.line: 'A small *creature* like that in a new shop means good luck, I think.'

crime:1.en: Lin appeared outside the new branch just before we opened, arms folded, staring at our new sign. 'Opening here is basically a *crime* against the neighbourhood,' Lin said, nodding at the older shop down the road. I handed Lin a free sample of the new rice ball. Lin ate it in two bites and said nothing else for a while.
crime:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在新店门外，说我们在这里开店简直是对这条街的一种____。
crime:1.hook: Lin came back an hour later and asked for the recipe.
crime:1.line: 'Opening right here is a *crime* — this was supposed to be my corner!'

deeply:1.en: After the ribbon-cutting, the Manager stood outside for a long moment, hands in pockets, staring at the new sign. I had never seen him so still. '*Deeply* proud' was how Tang described it quietly beside me. It seemed right. The Manager had drawn the floor plan himself, carried boxes, and stayed up three nights for this small corner shop.
deeply:1.cnHint: 剪彩结束后，店长静静地望着新招牌，阿糖说他____地为此感到骄傲。
deeply:1.hook: Then the Manager sniffed once and said, 'The sign is two centimetres crooked.'
deeply:1.line: 'I am *deeply* proud of everyone who helped build this new branch.'

demonstrate:1.en: On the pavement outside the new branch, the Manager stopped a small group of passing students to *demonstrate* how the loyalty card app worked. He tapped his phone, scanned a card, and smiled. Three students downloaded the app on the spot. I stood nearby, holding a tray of samples, feeling like part of something that was actually going well for once.
demonstrate:1.cnHint: 店长在新店门外拦住几位路过的学生，现场____新会员积分App的使用方法。
demonstrate:1.hook: One of the students stared at the screen, then stared at me with wide eyes.
demonstrate:1.line: 'Let me *demonstrate* the new app — it takes less than one minute, I promise.'

employment:1.en: The Manager called me outside just after midnight. He pointed across the street at a shiny new store under bright lights. 'That place opened last week,' he said quietly. 'They are offering *employment* to three more staff. Good pay.' He looked at me with calm eyes. I wasn't sure if it was a warning — or a test.
employment:1.cnHint: 店长在深夜把我叫到外面，指着对面新开的店，说那里正在____新员工。
employment:1.hook: He handed me a small key I had never seen before.
employment:1.line: 'They are offering *employment* to three new clerks across the street.'

entire:1.en: The Manager asked me to count stock before sunrise. I stepped outside to check the window display and stopped. Sometime in the night, someone had covered the *entire* front wall of our store in tiny paper stars. Every corner, every gap, filled with colour. The street was silent. No one was around.
entire:1.cnHint: 我走出去查看橱窗，发现____面墙都被人贴满了小纸星。
entire:1.hook: One star had a phone number written on the back.
entire:1.line: 'Someone covered the *entire* wall while we were not looking.'

gift:1.en: Around two in the morning, an old man came in and bought nothing. He just placed a small box on the counter, smiled, and walked back into the dark street. Inside the box was a warm meat bun, still soft. Tang picked it up and laughed. 'A *gift* with no name,' she said. 'That is the strangest and nicest thing.'
gift:1.cnHint: 一位老人深夜走进来，在柜台放下一个盒子就离开了，里面装着一个热乎乎的____。
gift:1.hook: The next night, a second box appeared before we even opened the door.
gift:1.line: 'A *gift* with no name — that is the strangest and nicest thing.'

kitchen:1.en: A food cart appeared on the corner just before three in the morning. The owner, a short woman with flour on her coat, knocked on our door and asked to borrow salt. 'My small *kitchen* on wheels ran out,' she said, laughing at herself. Tang gave her a full bag and refused money. The woman nodded once and went back to work.
kitchen:1.cnHint: 一位推着餐车的女士敲门借盐，说她的移动____里用完了。
kitchen:1.hook: She returned an hour later carrying something wrapped in brown paper.
kitchen:1.line: 'My small *kitchen* on wheels ran out of salt tonight.'

mystery:1.en: Every Tuesday, someone left a single coin on top of the newspaper stand outside our door. Not inside, not under — always on top, always one coin, always gone by morning. Tang called it a *mystery* and kept a notebook of dates. The Manager just shrugged. I started watching the street camera logs, but the timing was never quite right.
mystery:1.cnHint: 每周二都有人在报架顶上放一枚硬币，阿糖把这件____记录在笔记本里。
mystery:1.hook: This Tuesday, there were two coins.
mystery:1.line: 'It is a *mystery* — one coin, every Tuesday, gone by morning.'

opposite:1.en: Lin runs the noodle shop *opposite* our store, and every night around four he sweeps his doorstep exactly when I sweep ours. We never speak. We just sweep in silence, two small lights facing each other across a quiet road. Tang says he once swept for an hour straight during a rainstorm, so I figure he has his reasons.
opposite:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在我们店____的面馆每晚都和我同时扫地，两家店隔街相望。
opposite:1.hook: Tonight Lin looked up and gave a very small nod.
opposite:1.line: 'His noodle shop is directly *opposite* — they sweep at the same time every night.'

permanent:1.en: The Manager showed me the staff board on the back wall. Most names had small paper tags, easy to remove. Mine was the only one written directly on the wood in black ink. 'I made yours *permanent*,' he said, turning back to his ledger without another word. Tang caught my eye from behind the snack shelf and gave a quiet thumbs-up.
permanent:1.cnHint: 店长把我的名字直接写在木板上，说要把它变成____的。
permanent:1.hook: Below my name, in very small letters, was a second name I did not recognise.
permanent:1.line: 'I made yours *permanent* — written right into the wood.'

plenty:1.en: Just before dawn, a student sat down on the step outside with a big bag of chips from our shelf and an open notebook. She had *plenty* of notes already, pages thick with colour. Tang watched through the glass and whispered, 'She comes before every exam.' The girl never looked up. She just kept reading until the sky went pink.
plenty:1.cnHint: 一位女生在天亮前坐在门口台阶上复习，笔记本里已经有____的笔记了。
plenty:1.hook: She left a sticky note on the door that none of us could read.
plenty:1.line: 'She has *plenty* of notes — pages and pages of them every time.'

strike:1.en: The morning I arrived to help scout the new store location, a group of workers outside the building next door had begun a *strike*. They stood in a long line, holding signs, chanting in low, steady voices. The Manager studied them and then studied the empty shop front, saying nothing for a long time.
strike:1.cnHint: 店长带我去考察新店选址，隔壁楼的工人正在进行____，场面让人有点不安。
strike:1.hook: The Manager finally smiled — and that made me more nervous.
strike:1.line: 'A *strike* next door means cheap rent for us, probably.'

television:1.en: The new site was a dusty shell, but someone had left an old *television* balanced on a stack of bricks in the corner. It was still on, showing a cooking programme, its light flickering blue across bare walls. The Manager stood in front of it for a moment, tilting his head as if reading a sign.
television:1.cnHint: 新店地址里废弃的____还亮着，店长盯着它若有所思。
television:1.hook: He muttered something, wrote one word in his notebook, and closed it fast.
television:1.line: 'That *television* — leave it exactly where it is, please.'

youth:1.en: Two doors down from the new site was a small barbershop. A kid who looked barely eighteen sat outside on a plastic stool, arms folded, watching us measure the pavement. There was a quiet confidence about him — the kind of *youth* that does not know yet what it cannot do. I envied him a little.
youth:1.cnHint: 考察途中遇到一个坐在门口的少年，那股____的劲儿让我有点羡慕。
youth:1.hook: Later, Tang whispered that the kid owned the barbershop himself.
youth:1.line: '*Youth* is wasted on people who just sit and wait, I think.'

alter:1.en: The Manager paced the empty floor of the new site, then stopped at the main window. He said we would need to *alter* the layout of the shelves so that customers could see straight in from the street. He sketched a quick plan on the back of a receipt. Tang and I looked at each other.
alter:1.cnHint: 店长说必须____新店的货架布局，让街上的人一眼就能看进来。
alter:1.hook: Tang's quick look meant: this plan will change three more times before lunch.
alter:1.line: 'We have to *alter* the window side first — everything else follows that.'

approximately:1.en: Lin was already outside the new site when we arrived, leaning on a rival shop's van and looking pleased. She told the Manager, with a wide smile, that her company had signed a lease on a space *approximately* fifty metres further down the same street, and that she expected to open two weeks before us.
approximately:1.cnHint: 林出现在新店附近，说她的竞争门店距我们____五十米，开业还比我们早。
approximately:1.hook: The Manager just nodded, which is always the dangerous sign.
approximately:1.line: '*Approximately* fifty metres — close enough to share your customers, yes?'

attractive:1.en: From the pavement outside, the corner location did look genuinely *attractive*: wide glass front, warm afternoon light, a bus stop almost touching the door. I found myself imagining the night shift here — a little quieter, a little gentler than our current street. Tang caught me daydreaming and laughed.
attractive:1.cnHint: 新店的转角位置看起来相当____，我忍不住想象在这里上夜班的情形。
attractive:1.hook: Then Tang pointed out the all-night noodle stall directly opposite.
attractive:1.line: 'Honestly, the location is *attractive* enough — it sells itself at night.'

bag:1.en: The Manager produced a large paper *bag* from somewhere inside his coat and began handing out sandwiches on the pavement outside the new site. It felt less like a business trip and more like a school outing. Tang accepted his sandwich solemnly, as though receiving an important document.
bag:1.cnHint: 店长从大纸____里掏出三明治，在新店门口请大家吃东西，感觉像郊游。
bag:1.hook: At the bottom of the bag was a rolled-up lease agreement, already signed.
bag:1.line: 'I keep the contracts and the lunch in the same *bag* — saves trips.'

beat:1.en: We had walked the whole street twice in the afternoon heat, and by the time we reached the bus stop to head back I was completely *beat*. My feet ached. The Manager, somehow fresh, was already calling someone on his phone. Tang sat down on the kerb and closed his eyes without a word.
beat:1.cnHint: 转了整整一下午，我和唐到站台等车时都____了，只有店长精神依旧。
beat:1.hook: The Manager ended his call and said, 'We open in three weeks.'
beat:1.line: 'I am absolutely *beat* — how does the Manager still look so alive?'

bottom:1.en: The Manager taped a notice to the *bottom* of the store window, low enough that only people crouching to lock their bikes would spot it. It read: 'New branch opening soon — same corner, bigger space.' I read it twice, wondering what that meant for my night shift.
bottom:1.cnHint: 店长把一张告示贴在橱窗的____，只有蹲下锁车的人才能看到。
bottom:1.hook: Tang had already seen it — and said nothing to me.
bottom:1.line: 'I put it at the *bottom* so the right people would find it.'

breed:1.en: Outside the store, an old man walked a small dog of a *breed* I had never seen — short legs, huge ears, serious face. He stopped, looked at the new branch sign the Manager had just posted on the lamp post, and shook his head slowly before walking on without a word.
breed:1.cnHint: 一位老人遛着一只奇特____的小狗，在新店告示牌前摇了摇头。
breed:1.hook: He came back ten minutes later — alone, without the dog.
breed:1.line: 'That *breed* always knows trouble before people do.'

classify:1.en: Lin stood on the pavement comparing two hand-drawn maps, trying to *classify* each nearby shop as a threat or an opportunity for the new branch. She used red dots and blue dots. I passed by on my way to open the store and she covered the maps quickly, pretending to check her phone.
classify:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在人行道上用红蓝圆点____附近的每家店，却在我经过时迅速把地图藏了起来。
classify:1.hook: One red dot sat exactly where our store stood.
classify:1.line: 'I *classify* every shop before the Manager even asks me to.'

comment:1.en: The Manager pinned the branch announcement to the community board outside and stepped back. A small crowd formed quickly. Someone wrote a *comment* on a sticky note and pressed it onto the poster before walking away. I caught a glimpse — it said only three words — but a bus passed and blocked my view.
comment:1.cnHint: 店长把开分店的通知贴到社区公告栏后，有人在上面贴了一张便利贴____。
comment:1.hook: When I reached the board, the sticky note was already gone.
comment:1.line: 'Every *comment* on that board ends up meaning something.'

component:1.en: Tang was kneeling beside a flat-pack shelf unit on the pavement outside the new branch site, sorting pieces by size. 'Each *component* has to go in order,' he said, 'or the whole thing falls apart.' A gust of wind sent the instruction sheet tumbling into the road at that exact moment.
component:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店门外整理货架的每个____，一阵风却把说明书吹进了马路。
component:1.hook: A passing van rolled right over the instructions.
component:1.line: 'Miss one *component* and the whole shelf will lean.'

contrary:1.en: Everyone assumed the new branch would be on the busy main road. On the *contrary*, the Manager had chosen a quiet side street behind the old library. I found out only because I followed a delivery truck by accident one evening after my shift, and the truck stopped right in front of it.
contrary:1.cnHint: 大家以为新分店会开在主干道，____，店长选了图书馆后面的一条僻静小街。
contrary:1.hook: The delivery truck driver gave me a very long look.
contrary:1.line: 'On the *contrary*, a quiet street is exactly what we want.'

deny:1.en: Lin caught me reading the address on the delivery notice posted to the future branch door. 'Were you following that truck?' she asked, stepping out of the shadow of the old library wall. I wanted to *deny* it, but the mud on my shoes from the side street said everything for me.
deny:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林从暗处走出来质问我是否跟踪了送货车，我想____，但鞋上的泥出卖了我。
deny:1.hook: She smiled and said, 'Good — now you owe me one.'
deny:1.line: 'Go ahead and *deny* it, but I saw you follow that truck.'

depth:1.en: The Manager unrolled the floor plan for the new branch on the bonnet of a parked car outside. I peered over her shoulder. The storage room had real *depth* — nearly double the one in our current store. She tapped it with her pen and said quietly, 'This is the part Lin must not see yet.'
depth:1.cnHint: 店长在停着的车上展开新店平面图，储藏室的____让我印象深刻，她叮嘱我不能让隔壁咖啡店的林看到。
depth:1.hook: Behind us, a familiar pair of red shoes rounded the corner.
depth:1.line: 'The *depth* of that back room changes everything for us.'

distinguish:1.en: The Manager led me outside to study the two new store signs. Both used similar colours and fonts. 'You must learn to *distinguish* our sign from Lin's copy across the street,' he said, squinting at the rival board. I looked harder. One star. That was the only difference.
distinguish:1.cnHint: 店长带我到街上，教我____我们的招牌和对面林的山寨版。
distinguish:1.hook: But at night, both signs lit up the exact same shade of gold.
distinguish:1.line: 'Can you *distinguish* our sign from that fake one across the street?'

document:1.en: A city inspector stopped me on the pavement outside the new branch. She asked for the opening permit. I ran inside, searched three drawers, and finally found the folded *document* under a bag of rice. She stamped it without a word and walked away into the drizzle.
document:1.cnHint: 城管来检查，我到处找那份开业____，险些误事。
document:1.hook: She paused at the corner and wrote something slowly in her notebook.
document:1.line: 'This *document* is dated last year — is there a newer one?'

dozen:1.en: Tang carried a *dozen* boxed lunches from the supplier's van to the new branch fridge. I offered to help on the third trip. He shook his head with a grin. 'First day rule,' he said. 'New clerk watches. Otherwise you'll stack them wrong and the manager cries.'
dozen:1.cnHint: 唐一个人搬了一____盒饭，不让我帮忙，说这是新人守则。
dozen:1.hook: On the fourth trip he came back with only eleven boxes and said nothing.
dozen:1.line: 'I have moved a *dozen* boxes already — where is your energy?'

dull:1.en: The street outside the new branch was quiet all morning. No buses, no market stalls, just grey pavement and slow clouds. 'Is it always this *dull* out here?' I asked Tang. He smiled and pointed at the clock. 'Wait until noon. This corner has a secret.'
dull:1.cnHint: 新分店门口的街道早上冷冷清清，我觉得有些____，唐让我等到正午。
dull:1.hook: At exactly twelve the shutters across the road flew open all at once.
dull:1.line: 'It looks *dull* now, but just wait another hour.'

fortune:1.en: Lin walked past our new branch and paused at the door. She studied the red ribbon the Manager had tied above the entrance for good luck. 'A ribbon won't bring *fortune*,' she said pleasantly. Then she smiled, took a photo, and strolled away down the sunny street.
fortune:1.cnHint: 林路过我们的新分店，对那条红绸带能带来____表示怀疑，然后笑着走开了。
fortune:1.hook: She uploaded the photo somewhere, and by evening a crowd had gathered outside.
fortune:1.line: 'A pretty ribbon alone will not bring you *fortune*, you know.'

fulfil:1.en: The Manager pinned a handwritten list to the new branch door before opening: restock shelves, test the card reader, greet the first ten customers by name. 'Each of us must *fulfil* our part today,' he said quietly, tapping the list. Tang and I nodded and got to work.
fulfil:1.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了任务清单，说每个人都要____自己的职责，正式开张才能顺利。
fulfil:1.hook: The card reader beeped once, then went completely silent.
fulfil:1.line: 'We each must *fulfil* our task before we open those doors.'

gradually:1.en: The new branch started with just three customers all morning. Then a few office workers found us at lunch. By afternoon a small line formed at the counter. Business was *gradually* picking up, like a fire catching from a single match. Tang said this was the best sign possible.
gradually:1.cnHint: 新分店的生意____好转，从早上三个顾客到下午排起了小队。
gradually:1.hook: Then one regular looked at the shelf and frowned deeply at something missing.
gradually:1.line: 'See? Customers are *gradually* finding us — no need to worry yet.'

incentive:1.en: The Manager announced a small bonus for whichever branch sold more hot drinks before noon. Lin heard about it somehow and appeared at our door with a knowing look. 'That kind of *incentive* cuts both ways,' she said. Tang leaned over to me and whispered, 'She already won, didn't she.'
incentive:1.cnHint: 店长宣布卖热饮奖金制度作为____，林不知怎么听说了，意味深长地出现在门口。
incentive:1.hook: Tang checked our hot-drink counter and went very quiet indeed.
incentive:1.line: 'A small bonus is a fine *incentive*, but I have a better idea.'

somewhat:1.en: The Manager stood outside the new branch site, clipboard in hand. The street was noisier than our usual corner — trucks rolled past every few minutes. He looked *somewhat* worried, checking his notes twice, then staring at the traffic as if counting each engine rumble.
somewhat:1.cnHint: 店长站在新分店选址外，对周围环境感到____不安。
somewhat:1.hook: Then a truck stopped right in front of him.
somewhat:1.line: 'The noise is *somewhat* more than I expected,' he said quietly.

stable:1.en: Lin walked the whole block around the new site, testing the pavement with one foot. 'A good store needs a *stable* foundation,' she said, half to herself. She pressed a loose tile with her heel — it wobbled. She pulled out her phone and started taking photos.
stable:1.cnHint: 林在新选址附近检查地面，担心地基是否____。
stable:1.hook: One photo caught something no one else had noticed.
stable:1.line: 'Nothing feels very *stable* under this corner,' Lin warned.

lower:1.en: The Manager pointed at the map spread on the hood of his car. 'The rent on Park Road is *lower* than anywhere else we checked,' he said, tapping the circled block. I leaned in, trying to look useful. A pigeon landed on the map and stared at us both.
lower:1.cnHint: 店长在街边看地图，说某条路的租金____，正当此时一只鸽子也凑了过来。
lower:1.hook: The pigeon refused to move, even when the Manager reached for the map.
lower:1.line: 'The rent here is *lower*, so this corner is our top choice.'

naturally:1.en: Tang and I stood outside the empty shopfront on Maple Street. She walked the length of it once, then said the space felt right. '*Naturally*, a corner spot gets more foot traffic,' she added, already picturing shelves along the walls. I was just glad to be out of the store for an hour.
naturally:1.cnHint: 阿糖在空铺位外评估地点，____地说转角店面人流更多。
naturally:1.hook: Then Tang noticed the small sign taped to the inside of the glass.
naturally:1.line: '*Naturally*, the busiest corner will bring us the most customers.'

passionate:1.en: Lin from the shop across the street watched us measure the pavement outside the new site. She crossed her arms. 'You are very *passionate* about expansion,' she called out, making the word sound like a warning. I waved politely. The Manager kept measuring and did not look up once.
passionate:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林看着我们在街上量尺寸，用____这个词讽刺地打了个招呼。
passionate:1.hook: Lin pulled out her phone and made a call right there on the pavement.
passionate:1.line: 'How *passionate* of you — measuring the street at seven in the morning.'

pop:1.en: We were taping a bright sign to the new shopfront window when Tang said we needed something to catch passing eyes. She pressed a big yellow sticker to the glass — a *pop* of colour against the grey wall. Three people slowed down to look before we had even finished.
pop:1.cnHint: 阿糖在新店橱窗贴上亮黄色贴纸，用颜色____来吸引路人注意。
pop:1.hook: One of the three people who slowed down pressed their face to the glass.
pop:1.line: 'A *pop* of yellow on the window and everyone suddenly notices us.'

possibly:1.en: I measured the distance from the main bus stop to the new site by counting my steps. Forty-three steps — *possibly* close enough for tired commuters to stop on their way home. The Manager watched from the doorway, nodding slowly. Across the road, Lin was also counting her steps.
possibly:1.cnHint: 我步测新店离公交站的距离，心想这____足够近，能吸引下班的通勤者。
possibly:1.hook: Lin stopped walking at exactly the same spot I had stopped.
possibly:1.line: 'Forty-three steps — *possibly* close enough to pull in the evening crowd.'

previously:1.en: The Manager showed us photos on his phone. The corner unit had *previously* been a tiny bookshop, its shelves still faintly visible where the paint was lighter on the walls. I liked the idea of a place with a quiet history. Tang was already redesigning it in her head out loud.
previously:1.cnHint: 店长展示照片，说这个铺面____是一家小书店，墙上还留有痕迹。
previously:1.hook: Tang stopped mid-sentence and pointed at something behind the old counter.
previously:1.line: 'This spot *previously* held a bookshop — good energy, I think.'

profession:1.en: A woman stopped to read our handwritten 'Opening Soon' sign. She asked what kind of store it would be. When I explained, she smiled and said retail was a tough *profession* but an honest one. Then she bought a bottle of water from my carry bag and walked on without another word.
profession:1.cnHint: 一位路过的女士称零售是艰辛却诚实的____，随后向我买了瓶水就离开了。
profession:1.hook: She left before I could ask how she knew the store was not open yet.
profession:1.line: 'Retail is a hard *profession*, but it suits an honest person well.'

readily:1.en: When the Manager asked who would cover the new site on opening day, I *readily* raised my hand before thinking it through. Tang raised an eyebrow. The Manager smiled the smile of someone who had been waiting for exactly that answer. I realised I had just volunteered for a very long shift.
readily:1.cnHint: 店长问谁愿意负责新店开业当天，我____举了手，随即意识到自己可能麻烦了。
readily:1.hook: Tang leaned over and whispered something about the new store having no coffee machine.
readily:1.line: 'I *readily* volunteer — someone has to be there for the first customer.'

vigorous:1.en: The Manager called us outside at six in the morning. He pointed at the empty lot across the street, where workers were already digging. 'A new branch,' he said, his voice *vigorous* and full of energy, as if he hadn't slept all night — or maybe he had slept just fine and we were the ones missing something.
vigorous:1.cnHint: 店长精神抖擞地宣布，对面空地正在为新分店破土动工。
vigorous:1.hook: Tang said nothing, but his hands went very still.
vigorous:1.line: 'Stay *vigorous*, team — the new branch opens in thirty days!'

wide:1.en: From the pavement outside I could see the whole street in one glance. The *wide* road was empty except for a delivery truck and a cat. The Manager had brought us out here to 'feel the location.' I wasn't sure what that meant, but the cat looked confident, so I tried to copy it.
wide:1.cnHint: 站在街角，店长让大家感受新分店选址的____视野与街道环境。
wide:1.hook: Then Lin pointed to a sign just two doors down that I hadn't noticed.
wide:1.line: 'The street is *wide* — foot traffic here will be double what we get now.'

agriculture:1.en: A customer stopped to read the notice taped to our door about the new branch. 'My family left *agriculture* years ago and came to this city,' he said quietly, almost to himself. 'Now even this small street is changing.' He bought a bottle of water and walked away before I could think of anything to say.
agriculture:1.cnHint: 一位顾客看着新分店公告，感叹自家当年从____进城，如今连这条街都在变化。
agriculture:1.hook: He came back an hour later and stood outside without coming in.
agriculture:1.line: 'We left *agriculture* behind, but I never thought I'd miss a quiet corner street.'

assign:1.en: The Manager lined us up on the pavement and began to *assign* roles for the new branch opening. Tang got the stock room. I got the front counter. He paused before Lin's name, tapping his clipboard, while Lin stared at the ground with an unreadable expression.
assign:1.cnHint: 店长在街上把大家召集起来，开始为新分店____各自的职位。
assign:1.hook: Lin's name stayed blank on the clipboard.
assign:1.line: 'I will *assign* your post by Friday — make sure you are ready.'

broad:1.en: The new site had a *broad* front window facing the street, much larger than ours. Standing outside with Tang, I could see how every passing person would be able to look straight in. 'Good for selling,' Tang said. 'Bad for hiding,' I said. Tang laughed for the first time in a week.
broad:1.cnHint: 新分店门面____宽阔，站在街上便能一眼看清店内，让人又喜又忧。
broad:1.hook: Someone had already taped a hand-written note to that big window.
broad:1.line: 'That *broad* front window will bring in customers we have never seen before.'

careful:1.en: The Manager walked the building site, *careful* with each step around the loose bricks and muddy ground. He checked every corner, measured a doorway with his arms, and wrote things in a small notebook. I watched from the pavement. I had never seen him look so focused, like the store was a living thing he was trying to understand.
careful:1.cnHint: 店长在工地上____地巡视每个角落，把一切细节记在小本子里。
careful:1.hook: He crossed out one line in his notebook and circled another.
careful:1.line: 'Be *careful* here — the floor plan must be right before we pour the concrete.'

combination:1.en: Outside the future branch, the Manager explained his vision: a *combination* of hot food, fresh drinks, and a small seating area. He drew it in the air with his hands. Passers-by slowed down to listen. For a moment the whole corner felt like it belonged to us, not to the empty lot or the dust.
combination:1.cnHint: 店长在街角描述新分店的设计——一种____美食、饮品与休闲座位的新形式。
combination:1.hook: One stranger in the small crowd took out a phone and started taking notes.
combination:1.line: 'The right *combination* of food and space — that is what this street is missing.'

constant:1.en: Standing outside in the early morning, I noticed the *constant* hum of the city waking up — motorbikes, distant voices, a shop shutter rolling open. The new branch site was quiet by comparison, just a fence and a sign. It was strange to think that in a few months this silence would turn into something like the noise I was already used to.
constant:1.cnHint: 站在新分店工地旁，我感受着城市____不停的喧嚣，想象着这里未来的模样。
constant:1.hook: The fence had a small gap, and through it I could see a light already on inside.
constant:1.line: 'This street has *constant* foot traffic — that is exactly why we chose it.'

relax:1.en: The Manager told me the street corner gets busy after midnight, but at two in the morning it was perfectly still. I leaned against the counter and let my shoulders *relax* for the first time all shift. A warm breeze drifted through the open door. Then footsteps. Someone was approaching very slowly, stopping to look at every item in the window display.
relax:1.cnHint: 深夜小店门前一片安静，店员终于能____一下，却听到外面有脚步声越来越近。
relax:1.hook: The figure outside pressed one hand flat against the glass.
relax:1.line: 'You can *relax* — the rush hour is long over,' the Manager said with a small smile.

release:1.en: A delivery van stopped outside and the driver carried in three heavy boxes. He set them down, signed the form, and walked back into the dark street. I cut the tape and lifted the flaps to *release* the smell of fresh paper and new packaging — the new stock had finally arrived. Tang appeared from the back room exactly on cue.
release:1.cnHint: 快递员送来了新货，店员打开箱子，____出一股崭新商品的气味，同事阿糖也恰好走了出来。
release:1.hook: But one box had no label and no return address.
release:1.line: 'Pull that tab to *release* the seal,' Tang said, already reaching for a box cutter.

route:1.en: Lin from the store across the street knocked on our door just after three. She said her usual delivery *route* had changed and her supplier now passed our corner first. She wanted to know if she could leave a small parcel with us until morning. The Manager looked at me. I looked at the parcel.
route:1.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林来敲门，说她的货物____经过我们这里，想寄存一个包裹到天亮。
route:1.hook: The parcel made a faint ticking sound.
route:1.line: 'The new *route* brings the truck past your door at four,' Lin said, not quite meeting my eyes.

sight:1.en: Just before dawn a thick fog rolled down the street. By four-thirty the streetlights were soft orange blurs and I could barely see the bins outside. Then, through all that white mist, a bicycle appeared — the most striking *sight* of my whole first week. The rider was wearing a full suit and a bow tie, pedalling calmly as if it were noon on a sunny day.
sight:1.cnHint: 黎明前大雾弥漫，能见度极低，一个骑车人突然出现，成了本周最令人难忘的____。
sight:1.hook: He stopped, looked straight at me, and slowly raised one finger to his lips.
sight:1.line: 'What a *sight* — fog this thick in May,' said Tang, pressing his face to the window.

speaker:1.en: A woman set up a small folding table on the pavement just outside our door and placed a tiny wireless *speaker* on it. Soft music drifted in every time a customer opened the door. She sat with a notebook and wrote without looking up. The Manager said she appeared every Thursday night but had never once come inside.
speaker:1.cnHint: 一位女士在店门外摆了张桌子，放了个____播放音乐，她每周四深夜都会出现，却从未进过店里。
speaker:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, she stood up and walked toward our door.
speaker:1.line: 'Turn the *speaker* down a little,' the Manager called out, though I suspected he rather liked it.

species:1.en: A man in a wide hat came in and spent twenty minutes studying our pot plants near the window. He took notes in a small book. Finally he told me that two of them were a *species* he had been trying to find for three years, and asked, very politely, where we had bought them. I had no idea. The Manager was asleep in the back room.
