nice:2.en: A sealed envelope arrived by courier, addressed to the store. Inside were blueprints for the new branch layout, printed with *nice* detail — every shelf, every outlet, every camera angle measured to the centimetre. Tang held one page up to the light and let out a slow whistle.
nice:2.cnHint: 新分店的设计图纸非常____，每个细节都标注得很精确。
nice:2.hook: One room on the blueprints had no label at all.
nice:2.line: 'These are *nice* drawings — someone put real thought into every corner.'

peer:2.en: A delivery of supply boxes came in just after two in the morning. I had to *peer* at the small handwritten label on the bottom box to read the address — it was not our store. It was the address of the new branch, three streets away, though it had not yet opened.
peer:2.cnHint: 我____仔细辨认箱子底部的标签，发现地址不是这里。
peer:2.hook: Someone had been sending stock there for weeks without telling us.
peer:2.line: 'You have to *peer* closely — the ink is nearly faded off that label.'

pretty:2.en: Among the supply boxes sat a small cloth bag no one had ordered. Inside were four hand-painted keyrings — each one a tiny, colourful shop front. They were a *pretty* that someone had clearly made by hand, a gift with no note attached.
pretty:2.cnHint: 箱子里有人放了几个手工小挂件，是没有附信的____。
pretty:2.hook: The painting style matched a regular who had not visited in two weeks.
pretty:2.line: 'Each one is a little *pretty* — look how fine the brushwork is.'

recommendation:2.en: Pinned behind the counter was a laminated card in the Manager's handwriting. At the top it said: 'Staff *recommendation* for late-night customers.' Below it were seven items, each with a short reason. Number three had been crossed out and rewritten four times.
recommendation:2.cnHint: 柜台后面贴着一张写有员工____的卡片，第三条被反复改过。
recommendation:2.hook: The crossed-out item shared a name with someone who had just walked in.
recommendation:2.line: 'My *recommendation* is the warm soup — it saved me on every cold shift.'

strange:2.en: A regular left his umbrella by the door every visit but always collected it when he left. Tonight it was still there at four in the morning, and the name tag on the handle was *strange* to me — it did not match what he had told me his name was.
strange:2.cnHint: 常客忘拿雨伞，伞上名牌的名字对我来说很____。
strange:2.hook: His real name would explain why Lin always left when he arrived.
strange:2.line: 'It feels *strange* — he never once forgot that umbrella before tonight.'

widespread:2.en: Tang showed me a group message on the staff phone. Complaints about a bad batch of instant noodles were *widespread* — twelve customers, three convenience stores on the same street, all the same lot number printed on the packet. Our shelf still had six packs.
widespread:2.cnHint: 关于某批方便面的投诉____，我们货架上还剩六包。
widespread:2.hook: The lot number matched a box that Lin had personally signed for last week.
widespread:2.line: 'The complaints are *widespread* — we should pull every pack right now.'

wonderful:2.en: At the back of the stockroom, behind a row of water bottles, I found a dusty logbook. The first entry, written in careful old handwriting, called this corner store 'a *wonderful* little world that never sleeps.' The date was exactly twenty years ago tonight.
wonderful:2.cnHint: 我在库房深处发现一本旧日志，第一页把这家小店称作____的地方。
wonderful:2.hook: The signature below those words belonged to someone I had met just yesterday.
wonderful:2.line: 'Twenty years ago this place felt *wonderful* — it still does, if you look.'

character:2.en: The Manager pinned a note to the back wall before leaving for the night: 'The new branch opens Friday. Study how each regular orders — that tells you their *character* more than any conversation.' I read it twice, then looked up at the door as it swung open.
character:2.cnHint: 店长留下字条，说观察每位常客点单方式能看出他们的____。
character:2.hook: The first customer through the door ordered nothing — just stared at the shelves.
character:2.line: 'Their *character* shows in what they reach for first,' the Manager said.

clean:2.en: Tang handed me a mop at two in the morning. 'New branch inspection tomorrow,' she said. 'The Manager wants this place *clean* enough to eat off the floor.' I started by the drink fridge and worked toward the door, and that was when I found the folded note under the mat.
clean:2.cnHint: 阿糖要我把店铺____干净，因为明天新分店要接受检查。
clean:2.hook: The note had only four words, and none of them were nice.
clean:2.line: 'Get it *clean* before six,' Tang said, already pulling on her coat.

convey:2.en: A package arrived addressed to the store with no sender name. The Manager left a sticky note on it: 'Do not open. It is meant to *convey* something to Lin — let Lin collect it.' I set it behind the counter and spent the rest of the shift wondering what a mystery box could possibly say.
convey:2.cnHint: 店长留言说那个包裹是用来向隔壁咖啡店的林____某件事的，不要打开。
convey:2.hook: Lin walked in at dawn and went pale the moment they saw the box.
convey:2.line: 'It is meant to *convey* a message,' the Manager said, voice very quiet.

distraction:2.en: Tang was re-stocking the new branch display shelf when her phone buzzed every thirty seconds. 'Sorry,' she said, 'it is a *distraction* — I will put it away.' She did. Ten minutes later she stopped stacking, stared at the wall, and smiled at something I could not see.
distraction:2.cnHint: 阿糖说手机是____，把它收了起来，但之后却若有所思地笑了。
distraction:2.hook: Whatever Tang was smiling about, it had nothing to do with shelf-stacking.
distraction:2.line: 'This phone is a real *distraction*,' Tang said, flipping it face-down.

fight:2.en: Lin came in just before dawn carrying two coffee cups — one for me, which was unexpected. 'The Manager thinks I have no *fight* left,' Lin said, setting my cup on the counter. 'The new branch changes that.' Lin left before I could ask what it changed it into.
fight:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说店长以为自己没有____了，但新分店会改变这一切。
fight:2.hook: Lin's second cup was never opened, sitting cold beside the door.
fight:2.line: 'I still have *fight* in me,' Lin said, and smiled without warmth.

finish:2.en: The Manager slid a checklist across the counter at midnight. Every item for the new branch setup had a tick except the last one. 'I need you to *finish* this before my nine o'clock call,' the Manager said. The last item just read: 'Ask Tang.' Tang had already gone home.
finish:2.cnHint: 店长要我在九点前____清单上最后一项任务，但那项只写了"问阿糖"。
finish:2.hook: Tang's phone rang out three times, then went straight to voicemail.
finish:2.line: 'Just *finish* the list and we talk in the morning,' the Manager said.

frequently:2.en: Tang told me that Lin *frequently* stops by this corner store even though Lin manages the rival shop two blocks away. 'Watch what Lin picks up,' Tang said, straightening a row of cans. 'It is never random.' I watched, and Tang was right — it was never random.
frequently:2.cnHint: 阿糖说隔壁咖啡店的林____来这家店，而且每次拿的东西都不是随机的。
frequently:2.hook: Today Lin picked up a map of the neighbourhood, then put it back.
frequently:2.line: 'Lin comes here too *frequently* for it to mean nothing,' Tang said.

invest:2.en: The Manager gathered Tang and me by the new-branch display at three in the morning. 'I plan to *invest* more hours in training you both before Friday,' the Manager said, spreading papers on the counter. One sheet listed skills. Another listed names — and mine had a question mark beside it.
invest:2.cnHint: 店长说打算在开业前____更多时间培训我们，但我的名字旁有个问号。
invest:2.hook: I never found out what the question mark meant — the Manager pocketed that sheet.
invest:2.line: 'I want to *invest* time in the right people,' the Manager said.

male:2.en: A folded note fell out of a box of new stock. I opened it. Inside, in neat handwriting: 'Any *male* customer who buys three rice balls tonight gets a free coffee.' The Manager had written it days ago and forgotten to tell me. I taped it to the counter, feeling oddly pleased.
male:2.cnHint: 我在新货箱里发现店长留下的一张便条，说明针对____顾客的促销活动。
male:2.hook: But the next note I found was not from the Manager.
male:2.line: 'Any *male* customer who buys three rice balls gets the coffee free.'

fish:2.en: Behind the back shelf I found a small cooler no one had mentioned. Inside: three sealed packs of salted *fish*, a price tag from a supplier I did not recognise, and a sticky note that said 'Do not sell — Lin.' I put the cooler back exactly as I found it.
fish:2.cnHint: 我在货架后发现一个神秘冷藏箱，里面装着林留下的____。
fish:2.hook: The supplier's address on the label was just one street away.
fish:2.line: 'That *fish* is not for sale — please leave it where it is.'

fashion:2.en: Tang rushed in from the back room wearing a bright yellow apron covered in little stars. 'The Manager ordered these,' she said, handing me one. 'New store, new image.' In her *fashion*, she made even a silly apron look like a deliberate choice. I tied mine on without a word.
fashion:2.cnHint: 唐以她独特的____，让店里新订的围裙穿出了别样的感觉。
fashion:2.hook: The Manager's 'new image' plan turned out to be only the beginning.
fashion:2.line: 'In my *fashion*, I make anything look like it belongs here.'

weather:2.en: The Manager called just after midnight. 'Check the roof door,' he said. 'It sticks in this *weather*.' I climbed the narrow back stairs, pushed the door open, and found a small folding table and two chairs no one had told me about. The night air was cool and completely still.
weather:2.cnHint: 店长来电让我检查屋顶的门，说这种____容易卡住。
weather:2.hook: On the table sat a cup of tea that was still warm.
weather:2.line: 'In this *weather*, the roof door always sticks — go check it now.'

device:2.en: A regular customer left a small *device* on the counter — flat, silver, with a single green light blinking slowly. No name, no receipt, no explanation. Tang picked it up, turned it over, and set it down carefully. 'Someone will come back for this,' she said. No one did. Not that night.
device:2.cnHint: 一位常客把一个奇怪的____落在了收银台上，没有留下任何说明。
device:2.hook: At three in the morning, the green light turned red.
device:2.line: 'This *device* has been here two hours — should we call someone?'

farm:2.en: An older woman came in just before dawn carrying a cloth bag that smelled of earth and green leaves. She set a jar of honey on the counter. 'From my *farm*, outside the city,' she said proudly. 'The Manager ordered it for the new shop.' I had not known there was a new shop yet.
farm:2.cnHint: 一位老太太送来了她____出产的蜂蜜，说是店长为新店订购的。
farm:2.hook: She mentioned the new shop's address before the Manager had told any of us.
farm:2.line: 'I grew this honey on my own *farm* — nothing added, nothing removed.'

drug:2.en: A young man in a white coat hurried in and asked for cold water. He set a small labelled bag on the counter while he paid. Tang glanced at it. 'Is that a *drug* sample?' she asked quietly. He nodded. 'New pharmacy opening next door,' he said. 'We move in Friday.' I looked at Tang. She looked at me.
drug:2.cnHint: 一位穿白大褂的年轻人来买水，顺口透露隔壁将开一家新药店，他带着____样品。
drug:2.hook: Tang said nothing, but she had already taken out her phone.
drug:2.line: 'It is just a *drug* sample — the new pharmacy opens on Friday.'

heat:2.en: The small storage room at the back held old stock, a broken fan, and a thermometer fixed to the wall. I checked it at two in the morning: thirty-one degrees. The *heat* in there was enough to ruin the chocolate bars stacked by the door. I moved them to the front shelf and texted the Manager a photo.
heat:2.cnHint: 我发现储藏室里的____已经高到足以损坏货物，立刻把东西搬走并通知了店长。
heat:2.hook: The Manager's reply came in four seconds flat.
heat:2.line: 'The *heat* back there will ruin the stock — we need to fix that fan.'

announce:2.en: A folded note appeared under the store door just after two in the morning. I picked it up and read it by the counter light. It said the Manager planned to *announce* something big at the staff meeting on Friday — a second store, maybe, on the other side of town. My hands went a little cold.
announce:2.cnHint: 一张纸条悄悄塞进了门缝，说店长周五将____一件大事。
announce:2.hook: But the note was signed with only a question mark.
announce:2.line: 'The Manager will *announce* the news on Friday — every one of us should be there.'

appropriate:2.en: Tang found a dusty cardboard box in the back room while stacking new stock. Inside was a set of spare keys, three old staff badges, and a small cash bag. Tang looked at me and said it did not feel *appropriate* to simply put it back. We called the Manager at three in the morning.
appropriate:2.cnHint: 阿糖在库房发现了一个旧箱子，觉得处理方式必须____。
appropriate:2.hook: The Manager went very quiet on the phone for a long time.
appropriate:2.line: 'It is not *appropriate* to ignore this — we have to report it tonight.'

chief:2.en: The delivery driver who came every Wednesday night finally told me his name: Old Wen. He said his *chief* reason for choosing the night route was the silence — no traffic, no crowds, just the dark road and the radio. He handed me a box of drinks and winked. I wondered what the second reason was.
chief:2.cnHint: 送货司机告诉我，他选择夜班路线的____原因是喜欢安静。
chief:2.hook: He never mentioned that second reason, not once.
chief:2.line: 'My *chief* reason for this job? The night is honest — it never pretends.'

clearly:2.en: Someone had written on the staff whiteboard in red marker, big and careful: NEW STORE COMING. Nothing else. Lin walked in from the cold, stared at it, then looked at me. I shrugged. The message was *clearly* meant for all of us, yet nobody seemed to know who had written it.
clearly:2.cnHint: 白板上用红笔写着一行字，____是写给所有人看的，但没人知道是谁写的。
clearly:2.hook: The red marker was still sitting right there, lid off, still wet.
clearly:2.line: 'This is *clearly* not a joke — look how carefully someone wrote every letter.'

communicate:2.en: The Manager left a voice message on the store phone instead of calling any of us directly. Tang played it twice on speaker. 'The best way to *communicate* big changes,' Tang said slowly, 'is apparently to talk to a machine.' We both looked at the little blinking light and said nothing for a while.
communicate:2.cnHint: 店长给门店电话留了语音，阿糖说这真是一种奇怪的____方式。
communicate:2.hook: The message had one sentence none of us could quite make out.
communicate:2.line: 'Why *communicate* news this way — are we not worth a real phone call?'

emphasis:2.en: The Manager's printed memo about the new branch had one line underlined twice and circled in pen: TEAMWORK IS EVERYTHING. Tang read it aloud and tapped the circled words. 'Notice the *emphasis*,' Tang said, sounding more worried than inspired. I noticed. The word EVERYTHING felt very large in that small break room.
emphasis:2.cnHint: 店长备忘录里有一句话被圈起来加重标注，阿糖说要注意这个____。
emphasis:2.hook: Tang folded the memo very slowly and slipped it into a pocket.
emphasis:2.line: 'The *emphasis* on teamwork here tells me someone already made a mistake.'

emphasize:2.en: Lin came in just before dawn carrying a folder of printouts. 'The Manager asked me to *emphasize* one thing at the briefing,' Lin said, spreading sheets across the counter. Every single sheet had the same bold heading: LOCATION IS FINAL. I looked at the address. It was two doors down from Lin's own flat.
emphasize:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来一叠文件，说店长让他特别____一件事：新店地址已定。
emphasize:2.hook: Lin's face gave absolutely nothing away.
emphasize:2.line: 'I am here to *emphasize* that the location decision is final — no more votes.'

england:2.en: Tucked inside the new stock delivery was a small tin of biscuits with a red double-decker bus on the lid and tiny print reading MADE IN *ENGLAND*. No order slip, no name, nothing. Tang turned it over and over. An old regular shuffled in just then, glanced at the tin, and smiled in a way that seemed almost like recognition.
england:2.cnHint: 一批新货里夹着一盒印有"来自____"的饼干，没有任何来历说明。
england:2.hook: The old regular bought nothing else and left without a single word.
england:2.line: 'A tin from *England* with no label — someone sent this here on purpose.'

immediately:2.en: A note appeared under the back-room door just after midnight. I picked it up and read it. The Manager had written that a second store would open across town, and that staff choices would be made *immediately* — no waiting, no long talks. My hands felt cold.
immediately:2.cnHint: 店长的纸条说，分店的员工名单会____确定。
immediately:2.hook: My name was circled in pencil — but so was Lin's.
immediately:2.line: 'We decide *immediately*, so be ready by morning,' the Manager said.

improvement:2.en: The Manager pinned a chart to the wall near the coffee machine one afternoon. It showed sales numbers for both stores — the new one and ours. Our numbers were higher, but the gap was small. 'Any *improvement* here,' he said quietly, pointing at our side, 'decides who runs the new branch.'
improvement:2.cnHint: 店长贴出对比图，说这边的____将决定谁去管分店。
improvement:2.hook: Tang had already started rearranging the snack shelf without being asked.
improvement:2.line: 'A small *improvement* now can change everything later,' Tang whispered.

afternoon:2.en: The delivery for the new store arrived on a bright *afternoon* when I was alone at the counter. Three large boxes sat outside the door, each one labelled with an address I did not know. I copied it down on a receipt slip before Tang came back from lunch.
afternoon:2.cnHint: 一个____，我独自收到了寄往新店的货物，偷偷记下了地址。
afternoon:2.hook: That address matched the street where Lin's cousin lived.
afternoon:2.line: 'Every *afternoon* this week, boxes come for the new place,' I told Tang.

expand:2.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn map across the counter during a slow hour. Little circles marked shops and bus stops. 'The Manager wants to *expand* into this block,' Lin said, almost to himself, tracing a route with one finger. He did not notice me leaning closer to read the small notes in the margin.
expand:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林展开地图，谈到店长想____进那片街区，没发现我在偷看。
expand:2.hook: One margin note read: 'Remove current night clerk if needed.'
expand:2.line: 'To *expand* well, you need someone who knows the neighbourhood,' Lin said.

regardless:2.en: Tang stayed past the end of the shift to face the new stock system, *regardless* of the late hour. I watched him enter each item twice, checking the screen after every line. He never complained. Outside, rain tapped the glass. The Manager watched from the office doorway without saying a word.
regardless:2.cnHint: 阿糖____时间多晚，坚持把新库存系统录完，店长在门口默默看着。
regardless:2.hook: The Manager then sent a message — to Lin, not Tang.
regardless:2.line: 'I will finish this *regardless*, even if it takes all night,' Tang said.

rid:2.en: I found a damp cardboard sign at the bottom of the storage shelf, half hidden under empty bags. It read: 'Grand Opening — Sister Store.' Someone had tried to *rid* the shelf of it, pushing it deep into the corner. The tape on one edge was still fresh and sticky.
rid:2.cnHint: 我在储物架底部发现了分店开业的牌子，有人试图____它，但没彻底藏好。
rid:2.hook: The handwriting matched Lin's notebook exactly.
rid:2.line: 'I just wanted to *rid* the shelf of old junk,' Lin said, not meeting my eyes.

dog:2.en: A small *dog* trotted into the store just before three in the morning, collar tag jingling. It sniffed every corner, then sat squarely in front of the new-store brochure rack by the door, as if it belonged there. No owner followed. I checked the tag — the address was the new branch location.
dog:2.cnHint: 一只小____深夜跑进店里，径直坐到新店宣传架前，项圈上写着新店地址。
dog:2.hook: It looked at me with calm, knowing eyes, then trotted back into the dark.
dog:2.line: 'That *dog* shows up every night around three,' Tang said, sounding uneasy.

busy:2.en: Saturday was so *busy* that Tang and I had no time to talk. The counter line stretched to the door. But between two customers, Tang slid a folded paper into my apron pocket with two fingers and a quick look. I did not open it until the rush ended near dawn.
busy:2.cnHint: 周六店里很____，阿糖趁人多时悄悄把一张纸塞进我口袋。
busy:2.hook: The note inside had only four words: 'Don't take that job.'
busy:2.line: 'When it gets this *busy*, people say things they don't mean,' Tang murmured.

intelligence:2.en: A folded note fell out of a returned umbrella. Inside, someone had drawn a rough map of the street with tiny labels — which shops closed early, which had weak locks. The Manager studied it, impressed. 'Whoever made this had real *intelligence*,' he said. 'They saw everything we missed.'
intelligence:2.cnHint: 一把归还的雨伞里藏着一张地图，店长对绘图人的____赞叹不已。
intelligence:2.hook: But the handwriting matched someone who came in every night.
intelligence:2.line: 'Whoever made this had real *intelligence* — they saw everything we missed.'

uk:2.en: A postcard was tucked behind the milk cartons — nobody knew how long it had been there. The picture showed a grey, rainy street. On the back, in small neat letters: 'Wish you were here in the *UK*. The tea is terrible but the quiet is lovely. — M.' The Manager went pale.
uk:2.cnHint: 牛奶货架后面藏着一张从____寄来的明信片，店长看到后脸色发白。
uk:2.hook: He whispered a name, then locked himself in the back room.
uk:2.line: 'A postcard from the *UK* — and it has today's date on it.'

user:2.en: The self-checkout screen flashed an odd message at two in the morning: 'Hello again, *user* 0001.' No one was standing at the machine. I checked the log — that account had last been active three years ago, the night the old store burned down nearby. My hands went cold.
user:2.cnHint: 自助收银机在深夜向一个老____打招呼，但屏幕前空无一人。
user:2.hook: The receipt printer started up on its own and spat out a single name.

park:2.en: Tang rushed in at midnight, breathless. She had been taking a shortcut through the small *park* across the road when she found a locked metal box sitting on a bench, a bright orange tag on it reading: 'RETURN TO STORE.' Nobody else was in the park. She set it on the counter.
park:2.cnHint: 阿糖在对面的____里发现了一个贴着'归还到店'标签的神秘铁盒。
park:2.hook: The box was warm, though the night was freezing cold.
park:2.line: 'I found it in the *park* — and it already has our store's address on it.'

reward:2.en: A flyer slipped under the door just before dawn. It offered a *reward* — a surprisingly large sum — for information about a small blue notebook. The photo on the flyer showed the exact notebook sitting right now in our lost-and-found box. I read the number twice to make sure.
reward:2.cnHint: 一张传单从门缝塞进来，为寻找某本小蓝笔记本提供____，而那本笔记本就在失物箱里。
reward:2.hook: The phone number on the flyer belonged to someone already in our store.
reward:2.line: 'There is a *reward* for that notebook — a very big one.'

credit:2.en: Lin came in waving a printout. A food blog had praised our store's new onigiri, calling it the best on the street. The Manager smiled and gave Lin full *credit*, saying she had chosen the recipe herself. Lin looked surprised — then quietly pleased. She folded the printout and slipped it into her pocket.
credit:2.cnHint: 美食博客夸赞了便利店的饭团，店长把所有____都给了隔壁咖啡店的林。
credit:2.hook: Later I found the same recipe in the Manager's own handwriting.
credit:2.line: 'All the *credit* goes to Lin — it was entirely her idea.'

progress:2.en: Every evening, an old man stopped at the window and studied the hand-drawn chart taped inside the glass. It tracked how the new branch store was coming along, week by week. Tonight he smiled for the first time. 'Things really *progress* when people care,' he said softly, then walked on without buying anything.
progress:2.cnHint: 一位老人每晚都来看窗上的新分店进度图，今晚他终于看到事情在____。
progress:2.hook: He had never once come inside — until tonight he left a key on the sill.
progress:2.line: 'Things really *progress* when people truly care about the work.'

snack:2.en: Tucked inside a returned shopping basket was a small paper bag and a note: 'For the night staff — you deserve a proper *snack*.' Inside were four neatly wrapped rice balls, still warm. Tang checked the camera. A figure in a wide hat had slipped them in, then walked away without looking up.
snack:2.cnHint: 归还的购物篮里藏着一袋热饭团和便条，有人悄悄给夜班员工留了____。
snack:2.hook: The handwriting on the note matched no one any of us knew.
snack:2.line: 'Someone left us a *snack* — but they never showed their face.'

extreme:2.en: The Manager left a note on the back-room board: 'New branch opens Friday. Staff rotation begins NOW.' The word 'NOW' was written in letters so large they covered half the board. I stared at it. Even by the Manager's standards, this felt *extreme*. My hands went a little cold.
extreme:2.cnHint: 店长在告示板上留下一张措辞____的便条，让我不禁担心。
extreme:2.hook: But the note had a second page no one had turned over yet.
extreme:2.line: 'Even for me, this feels *extreme* — read the second page first.'

style:2.en: A rolled-up floor plan for the new branch arrived by post. I spread it across the counter. The layout was nothing like our store: curved shelves, soft lamp light, plants everywhere. Tang leaned over and whistled softly. 'Different *style*,' she said. 'Almost like a living room.'
style:2.cnHint: 新分店的平面图送来了，____和我们这里完全不同。
style:2.hook: In the corner of the plan, someone had drawn a tiny question mark in red pen.
style:2.line: 'Different *style* — do you think the Manager chose this herself?'

color:2.en: I found a box of sample paint chips under the break-room table, each one labelled with a store section: 'snacks', 'drinks', 'counter'. The *color* chosen for the counter area was a deep, calm blue — nothing like our harsh white. I held it up to the light and felt oddly hopeful.
color:2.cnHint: 备用房间里藏着一盒油漆色卡，柜台区的____让我意外地喜欢。
color:2.hook: One chip at the very bottom had no label at all.
color:2.line: 'That *color* for the counter — I think I could actually work under that light.'

meeting:2.en: A handwritten schedule fell out of the floor plan tube when I unrolled it further. It listed a *meeting* at the new branch address for Thursday night, six o'clock. My name was on the list. So was Lin's. We had never been in the same room outside this store before.
meeting:2.cnHint: 平面图纸管里掉出一份日程表，上面有一个____，我和林都在名单上。
meeting:2.hook: Lin's name had a small circle drawn around it, in the same red pen.
meeting:2.line: 'A *meeting* with Lin and me both there — the Manager planned this carefully.'

volunteer:2.en: Below the meeting list was a line asking for one person to *volunteer* to manage the new branch on its opening night. No name was filled in. The Manager had left it blank on purpose, I guessed. Tang read it over my shoulder and immediately stepped back, shaking her head.
volunteer:2.cnHint: 日程表下方有一行字，请人____去管理新店的开业之夜，但没人填名字。
volunteer:2.hook: Someone had already written one letter — just one — in that blank space.
volunteer:2.line: 'I won't *volunteer* this time — not until I know what happened last opening.'

deliver:2.en: My phone buzzed. A message from an unknown number: 'Please *deliver* the brown envelope in the top drawer to the new branch before Thursday.' I opened the drawer. There it was — sealed, no writing on the front. It had clearly been there for days without anyone mentioning it.
deliver:2.cnHint: 我收到一条陌生短信，让我把抽屉里一个棕色信封____到新店去。
deliver:2.hook: The envelope was light, but something inside shifted when I tilted it.
deliver:2.line: '*Deliver* it before Thursday — and please, do not open it.'

engineering:2.en: The brown envelope, once I held it to the lamp, showed the shadow of a folded document inside. Through the paper I could just read the words 'structural *engineering* report' at the top. That meant walls, floors, safety checks. Why was a building report hidden in a convenience store drawer?
engineering:2.cnHint: 透过灯光，我看到信封里装的是一份____报告，这让我很困惑。
engineering:2.hook: The report's date was three years ago — before this store was built.
engineering:2.line: 'A structural *engineering* report — this store has a history nobody told us.'

tiny:2.en: I nearly missed it: a *tiny* yellow sticky note pressed to the very back of the drawer, half hidden by the wood. It said only: 'Ask Lin what she found in March.' March was three months ago. Lin had transferred here in April. So she had been to the new branch site before she ever came to us.
tiny:2.cnHint: 抽屉最深处藏着一张____的便利贴，上面让我去问林三月份发现了什么。
tiny:2.hook: Lin was watching me from the door, very still, saying nothing at all.
tiny:2.line: 'There was a *tiny* note too — Lin, I think it was meant for you.'

retire:2.en: At two in the morning the store was empty. I found a sticky note on the register from Tang: 'Manager says he wants to *retire* after the new branch opens — hand everything to us.' I read it twice. The ceiling light hummed quietly above me.
retire:2.cnHint: 唐在收银台留了一张便利贴，说店长打算____。
retire:2.hook: But Tang's handwriting was shaking badly.
retire:2.line: 'He told me he wants to *retire* the moment the new branch turns a profit.'

sea:2.en: A delivery showed up just before dawn — a big crate addressed to the new branch. I signed for it and spotted a small painting tucked inside the packing paper: a pale *sea* under a grey sky, waves barely moving. Someone had taped a note to the back: 'For the new wall.'
sea:2.cnHint: 一只大箱子送达，里面夹着一幅画着____的小画。
sea:2.hook: The note was signed with only a question mark.
sea:2.line: 'Hang a picture of the *sea* in there — calm places need calm walls.'

town:2.en: I was mopping near the magazine rack when Lin walked in, dropped a folded map on the counter and said nothing. I opened it. Red circles marked three spots on the far side of *town*. One circle had a tiny star drawn next to it.
town:2.cnHint: 林走进来，在柜台上放下一张地图，上面圈出了____另一边的几处地点。
town:2.hook: The starred spot was exactly where our new branch would open.
town:2.line: 'Every corner of this *town* already knows which store people trust.'

gap:2.en: The Manager spread two sales charts on the back-room table — one for our store, one projected for the new branch. He tapped the space between the lines. 'You see this *gap*?' he said. 'Twelve months. That is how long we have before it closes on its own.'
gap:2.cnHint: 店长指着两张销售图之间的____，说明了新分店的时间压力。
gap:2.hook: Lin had been standing in the doorway the whole time.
gap:2.line: 'Close the *gap* in twelve months or the new branch swallows this one.'

generation:2.en: An old regular came in after midnight, bought a coffee and stayed by the window. He pointed at the construction sign down the street. 'My father sold rice from a cart near that corner,' he said. 'Every *generation* opens something new there. Wonder what yours will leave behind.'
generation:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客谈起那条街每____都有人在那里开新店的往事。
generation:2.hook: He smiled, but his eyes stayed very still.
generation:2.line: 'Each *generation* in this neighbourhood opens something and calls it theirs.'

guide:2.en: I found a thin booklet under the counter labelled 'Night Shift *Guide* — Branch Two.' It had Tang's notes in the margins, questions circled in red, and one page torn out completely. The table of contents listed a chapter called 'How to Handle the Difficult Regular.'
guide:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现了一本新分店的____，某一页被撕掉了。
guide:2.hook: Chapter four was the only chapter with no page number.
guide:2.line: 'This *guide* was written for someone, and I don't think it was you.'

household:2.en: Tang was restocking the cleaning aisle when she held up a small bottle and laughed. 'We're selling this as a *household* item, but every single one goes to the noodle shop on the next block.' She set it down, still smiling. 'Branch two should stock double.'
household:2.cnHint: 唐发现某件____用品几乎全被隔壁面馆买走，建议新分店多备货。
household:2.hook: The noodle shop had been closed for a week.
household:2.line: 'That *household* cleaner is basically their secret ingredient at this point.'

luxury:2.en: The Manager came back from the new branch site holding a brochure for café-style shelving. Tang glanced at the price list and set it face-down. 'That is a *luxury* we hand to the customers, not the shelves,' she said. The Manager looked at the brochure for a long moment, then nodded once.
luxury:2.cnHint: 店长带回新分店的装修方案，唐认为那是____，钱该花在顾客身上。
luxury:2.hook: He folded the brochure and slipped it into his pocket anyway.
luxury:2.line: 'A little *luxury* in the design costs money we don't have yet.'

destroy:2.en: Behind the counter I found a folded note from the Manager. It said the new branch plan was ready — but someone had tried to *destroy* it. Half the page was torn away. Only the address survived. I stared at those few words and felt a chill run through me.
destroy:2.cnHint: 店长留下的新分店计划书被人故意____了一半，只剩下地址。
destroy:2.hook: Whose handwriting was on the torn half?
destroy:2.line: Someone tried to *destroy* the plan before anyone could read it.

drop:2.en: A delivery driver rushed in just before dawn, dripping with rain. He set a sealed box on the counter and hurried out. I noticed a single *drop* of red ink on the lid — like a small mark left on purpose. The box was addressed to the new branch that no one had announced yet.
drop:2.cnHint: 快递箱盖上有一____红墨水，像是特意留下的记号。
drop:2.hook: Only three people knew that address.
drop:2.line: There is one *drop* of red ink on every box I send.

efficiency:2.en: Tang slid a printed chart across the counter without a word. It compared our store's sales with the planned new branch. 'Look at the *efficiency* gap,' she said quietly. The new site was expected to sell twice as much in the same hours. I began to understand why some people were nervous.
efficiency:2.cnHint: 唐拿出一张图表，展示新分店预计____远超本店。
efficiency:2.hook: Tang's pen tapped the one column she had left blank.
efficiency:2.line: The *efficiency* gap between the two stores is bigger than I expected.

italian:2.en: A regular customer came in and bought a small jar of pasta sauce. He always asked for the same brand. Tonight it was gone. 'The new branch will stock it,' the Manager said. The man laughed softly. 'I learned to cook from an *Italian* friend years ago. Old habits follow you.'
italian:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客聊起，他做菜的习惯是跟一位____朋友学的。
italian:2.hook: He left before anyone could ask which city he meant.
italian:2.line: My *Italian* friend taught me that the sauce matters most.

newspaper:2.en: Under the counter I found an old *newspaper*, folded around something flat and hard. Inside was a hand-drawn map of the street corner where the new branch would open. Someone had circled a building in red. The date on the paper was three years ago. The Manager had been planning this for a long time.
newspaper:2.cnHint: 柜台下的旧____里藏着一张手绘地图，圈出了新分店的位置。
newspaper:2.hook: The building in the red circle was already for rent.
newspaper:2.line: This *newspaper* was hiding something more than yesterday's news.

piece:2.en: Lin came in after midnight and bought a single *piece* of paper from the small stationery rack — just one sheet. She paid carefully and left without a bag. I watched her cross the street and stop under a lamp post. She began writing something at once. I had never seen her move so quickly.
piece:2.cnHint: 林买了一____纸，深夜在路灯下立刻开始写东西。
piece:2.hook: By morning, that paper had changed hands twice.
piece:2.line: I only need one *piece* of paper to settle this tonight.

target:2.en: The Manager pinned a small card above the register before his shift ended. It showed a number — the weekly sales *target* for the new branch. It was almost double ours. I read it twice, sure I had misunderstood. Tang walked in, glanced at the card, and simply said, 'Better start practising.'
target:2.cnHint: 店长在收银台上方贴出新分店的销售____，数字让人吃惊。
target:2.hook: Tang had already seen that number somewhere before.
target:2.line: That is our *target* for the first week — not the first month.

actual:2.en: I had heard about the new branch for weeks, but tonight I finally saw the *actual* lease agreement. The Manager had left it on the back shelf by mistake. The address, the start date, the rent — all real, all signed. I put it back carefully and pretended I had seen nothing.
actual:2.cnHint: 我无意中看到了新分店____租约，一切都已签字确认。
actual:2.hook: One signature on the last page was not the Manager's.
actual:2.line: This is the *actual* agreement — everything is already decided.

disadvantage:2.en: The Manager spread a city map on the stock-room table. 'The new branch sits two blocks from a bus stop,' he said. 'That is a real *disadvantage* — customers will not walk that far in winter.' He circled the spot in red. I stared at the circle and said nothing.
disadvantage:2.cnHint: 店长在地图上圈出新分店的位置，指出它的一个____。
disadvantage:2.hook: But someone had already pencilled a question mark beside that circle.
disadvantage:2.line: 'That distance is a serious *disadvantage* we cannot ignore.'

discuss:2.en: A folded note fell out of a delivery box. I opened it: 'Need to *discuss* the new-branch plan. Come to the rooftop at midnight. — L.' I looked at the clock. Eleven fifty-eight. Lin was already climbing the stairs, coat still wet from the rain outside.
discuss:2.cnHint: 我在货箱里发现一张纸条，邀请我去天台____新分店的计划。
discuss:2.hook: Why would Lin hide a message inside a box of instant noodles?
discuss:2.line: 'We really need to *discuss* this plan before it goes too far.'

psychological:2.en: Tang slid a printed article across the counter. 'Read this,' she said. 'It says the *psychological* effect of bright lights makes customers spend more. The new branch is planning white walls and cold lamps.' She tapped the page twice. I read the first line and felt uneasy.
psychological:2.cnHint: 阿糖拿来一篇文章，说新分店的设计会利用____效应让顾客多花钱。
psychological:2.hook: The article's author name had been carefully torn away.
psychological:2.line: 'Bright lighting has a strong *psychological* effect on how people shop.'

request:2.en: A handwritten *request* was taped to the staff notice board: 'Please save all old sales receipts from this month.' No name, no date. I checked the board again — it had not been there this morning. The Manager was on the phone in his office, back turned to the door.
request:2.cnHint: 告示板上突然出现一张匿名____，要求保留本月所有旧收据。
request:2.hook: Whoever posted it had used the Manager's own red tape.
request:2.line: 'This *request* was here when I arrived — I did not put it up.'

symptom:2.en: Lin leaned on the freezer and sighed. 'Low foot traffic, slow sales, staff calling in sick — each one is a *symptom* of a bigger problem,' she said. She was looking at last week's report for the new branch. I handed her a warm coffee. She did not even notice.
symptom:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林分析新分店的各种问题，说每一项都是更大麻烦的____。
symptom:2.hook: She turned the report over; something was written on the back.
symptom:2.line: 'Every one of these problems is a *symptom* of poor planning.'

upon:2.en: *Upon* opening the morning delivery, I found a small padlocked box sitting on top of the usual stock. No label, no sender, just a yellow sticker with the words 'Branch Two' in neat block letters. The Manager came out of his office, took one look, and went very quiet.
upon:2.cnHint: 我打开早晨的货物，____箱子顶部发现了一个贴着"第二分店"标签的上锁小盒子。
upon:2.hook: The Manager's hand moved toward it, then stopped.
upon:2.line: '*Upon* finding it, you should have called me immediately.'

argument:2.en: I heard raised voices from the stock room — the Manager and Lin mid-*argument*. 'The lease is already signed!' 'Then unsigned it!' A box fell. Silence. I straightened the magazines on the rack and pretended I had heard nothing. Tang appeared beside me and whispered, 'Third time this week.'
argument:2.cnHint: 我听到店长和隔壁咖啡店的林在库房里发生____，似乎是为新分店的租约大吵了一架。
argument:2.hook: Tang's expression said she already knew how it would end.
argument:2.line: 'This *argument* is pointless if neither of us has seen the contract.'

crisis:2.en: At three in the morning my phone buzzed. A group message from the Manager: 'Branch Two water pipe burst. Full *crisis*. Tang, take the van. Narrator, hold the store alone.' I looked around at the empty aisles, the hum of the freezers, and one old regular still asleep at the corner table.
crisis:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，店长发来消息说新分店发生了____，要大家紧急支援。
crisis:2.hook: The old regular opened one eye and said, 'Need a hand?'
crisis:2.line: 'This is a real *crisis* — the whole floor is already underwater.'

analysis:2.en: The Manager spread a large paper across the back table. Numbers, arrows, and notes filled every corner. 'This is my *analysis* of which neighbourhood has the most late-night foot traffic,' he said proudly. I leaned over and saw one street marked in red — right next to our biggest rival.
analysis:2.cnHint: 店长在后台铺开一张大纸，对哪个街区深夜人流量最大做了详细的____。
analysis:2.hook: The red circle was drawn around Lin's street.
analysis:2.line: 'My *analysis* shows this corner gets three hundred customers after midnight.'

application:2.en: A folded envelope sat on the staff shelf when I arrived for my shift. My name was on the front. Inside was a printed *application* form for the new branch — someone had already filled in my name at the top, in neat blue ink. I had not asked for this.
application:2.cnHint: 我到岗时发现架子上有一封信，里面是一份已经写上我名字的新分店____表。
application:2.line: 'Your *application* for the new branch is due by Friday,' Tang whispered.

living:2.en: Tang counted coins into a small jar behind the counter, one by one. 'Night shifts are not glamorous,' she admitted, 'but they are my *living* for now.' She smiled without any self-pity, then slid a warm meat bun across to me. Outside, the street was completely silent.
living:2.cnHint: 唐一边数硬币一边说，上夜班虽然不体面，却是她目前的____。
living:2.hook: The jar was almost full — this was not her first hard year.
living:2.line: 'This job is my *living*, so I take it seriously.'

proposal:2.en: The Manager taped a single sheet of paper to the fridge door and stepped back, arms folded. 'Read it,' he said. It was a *proposal* for a second store, two blocks east, with a hand-drawn map and a bold opening date circled in red. He looked very pleased with himself.
proposal:2.cnHint: 店长把一份开设新分店的____贴到冰箱门上，让我们仔细读。
proposal:2.hook: The opening date was only three weeks away.
proposal:2.line: 'I wrote this *proposal* myself — tell me honestly what you think.'

relevant:2.en: Lin walked in just before two in the morning and dropped a folder on our counter without a word. Inside were printed pages about local rent prices, school calendars, and bus routes. 'Only the *relevant* facts,' she said coolly, tapping the folder. 'I know what the Manager is planning.'
relevant:2.cnHint: 林深夜走进店里，把一份只包含____信息的资料放在柜台上，暗示她知道店长的计划。
relevant:2.hook: Her folder was thicker than the Manager's entire plan.
relevant:2.line: 'I kept only the *relevant* data — nothing extra, nothing wasted.'

senior:2.en: A quiet man came in every Tuesday for warm soy milk and a small bread roll. Tang told me he was a *senior* at the university nearby, finishing his last semester. He always paid exact change and always said thank you twice. Tonight he left a handwritten note beside the till.
senior:2.cnHint: 一位即将毕业的大学____每周都来买同样的东西，今晚他在收银台旁留下了一张手写便条。
senior:2.hook: The note had the Manager's home address on it.
senior:2.line: 'He is a *senior* this year — graduating in two months,' Tang told me softly.

table:2.en: I found a folded map wedged under the leg of the small *table* in the store room. It showed the neighbourhood with three locations marked in different colours — red, blue, and green. Someone had been planning this quietly for a long time. The map was not the Manager's handwriting.
table:2.cnHint: 我在储藏室的小____腿下发现了一张折叠地图，上面标注了三个不同地点。
table:2.hook: The blue mark was our store — drawn there last.
table:2.line: 'Check under the *table* in the back room,' Tang said without looking up.

campus:2.en: Just after midnight a tired student pushed through our door still wearing her university lanyard. 'The vending machines on *campus* all shut down,' she sighed, grabbing two bottles of water and a bag of crackers. She paid and was gone in ninety seconds. But she had left her student card on the counter.
campus:2.cnHint: 一个学生说____里的自动售货机都关了，匆忙买完东西后把学生证落在了柜台上。
campus:2.hook: The card showed she lived in the dorm nearest the red circle on the Manager's map.
campus:2.line: 'Nothing on *campus* is open past midnight — you are my only hope.'

campaign:2.en: A folded paper landed on the counter. I opened it: a neat hand-drawn map with arrows and timing notes. Someone had planned a whole *campaign* to place flyers in every building before the Manager arrived at dawn. The handwriting looked very familiar.
campaign:2.cnHint: 一份详细的行动计划书出现在收银台上，店长早上来之前就必须完成。
campaign:2.line: 'This *campaign* starts at three — don't be late.'

hurt:2.en: I found a small cactus on the back shelf with a torn sticky note: 'Please water me. I don't bite.' Below that, in tinier letters: 'The last clerk left me dry for a week. That really *hurt*.' I watered it immediately and felt oddly guilty.
hurt:2.cnHint: 店里的一盆小仙人掌留下了一张纸条，诉说着上一个店员的疏忽带来的____。
hurt:2.hook: Then I noticed a second note hidden underneath.
hurt:2.line: 'It *hurt* more than you'd think for a plant.'

initiative:2.en: Nobody told me to restock the hot-drink shelf after the midnight rush. I just did it. When the Manager came in at six, she stopped, looked at the neat rows, and nodded slowly. 'Good *initiative*,' she said, then walked past without another word. That single nod felt like a trophy.
initiative:2.cnHint: 没人要求我补货，但我自己主动做了，店长只用一个词表扬了我的____。
initiative:2.hook: Tang later told me that nod was extremely rare.
initiative:2.line: 'Showing *initiative* on your first week — not bad.'

jump:2.en: Lin slid a folded note under the stockroom door at two in the morning. It read: 'New branch opens Friday. Don't let your sales *jump* before then — it'll make our numbers look bad at the meeting.' I stared at it for a long time, unsure whether to laugh or worry.
jump:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林悄悄塞来一张纸条，提醒我别让销售额在新分店开业前____得太高。
jump:2.hook: The Manager's meeting was on Thursday.
jump:2.line: 'If your numbers *jump* now, we both look strange.'

lie:2.en: The new branch address *lies* three streets east of ours, right next to the university gate. I discovered this on a printed notice the Manager left under my keyboard, circled in red. Three streets felt close enough to be a problem. I folded the notice and slipped it into my pocket.
lie:2.cnHint: 新分店的地址____在离我们只有三条街的地方，店长留下的通知让我意识到这件事。
lie:2.hook: The university gate meant ten thousand students.
lie:2.line: 'The new store *lies* right where all the students pass.'

lunch:2.en: A delivery bag was left inside the door at noon with my name on it. Inside: one neat *lunch* box and a card that said 'Stay strong, night-shift friend.' I had never told anyone I sometimes skipped meals. I looked at the security camera in the corner and then at the card again.
lunch:2.cnHint: 一份午餐悄悄出现在店门口，附有一张鼓励我坚持的小卡片，我不知道是谁送的。
lunch:2.hook: The bag's knot was tied the way Tang always ties things.
lunch:2.line: 'A proper *lunch* matters more than you think it does.'

necessarily:2.en: I told Tang I was worried the new branch would take all our regular customers. Tang shrugged. 'New competition doesn't *necessarily* mean we lose. It means we have to give people a reason to stay.' Then Tang pulled out a small notebook filled with ideas and dropped it on the counter.
necessarily:2.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我，新分店开业并不____意味着我们会失去老顾客，还拿出了一本小册子。
necessarily:2.hook: Page one was titled 'Why Our Store Feels Like Home.'
necessarily:2.line: 'More stores don't *necessarily* mean fewer friends here.'

psychologist:2.en: A quiet regular who always bought warm milk left a business card by the register. It read: 'Certified *psychologist* — free first talk, any time.' On the back, in small neat writing: 'You looked like you needed to know that option existed.' I did not remember making any expression at all.
psychologist:2.cnHint: 一位常客在收银台留下了一张名片，原来她是一位____，还在背面写了一句贴心的话。
psychologist:2.hook: She was already gone before I could look up.
psychologist:2.line: 'A *psychologist* once told me: small stores heal people too.'

pursue:2.en: A folded note slipped under the back door read: 'Do not *pursue* the new branch plan. Some corners are not yours to take.' I showed the Manager. He read it twice, then tucked it into his shirt pocket without a word.
pursue:2.cnHint: 一张纸条悄悄塞进后门，警告店长不要____开分店的计划。
pursue:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Lin's.
pursue:2.line: 'I will *pursue* this plan no matter what note appears.'

site:2.en: The Manager unrolled a large paper map on the counter and tapped a red circle near the old library. 'This is the *site* for the new branch,' he said. I leaned in and noticed a small ink mark already on that spot, as if someone had circled it before him.
site:2.cnHint: 店长在地图上指出新分店的____，但那个地点似乎早有人做过标记。
site:2.hook: Who had seen this map before the Manager?
site:2.line: 'The *site* near the library was chosen three weeks ago.'

absorb:2.en: The Manager dropped a thick folder of numbers on my desk. 'Read everything tonight,' he said. 'The new branch will *absorb* all the stock from this store first.' I stared at the pages. One column of figures had been circled in red pen — by someone else, long before tonight.
absorb:2.cnHint: 店长让我读一份文件，说新分店会____本店的全部库存，但文件上已有人做了标记。
absorb:2.hook: The red ink was still faintly wet.
absorb:2.line: 'The new branch will *absorb* our stock within a week.'

advance:2.en: Tang handed me a small envelope before my shift ended. 'The Manager left this — an *advance* on next month's pay, to say thank you,' she whispered. Inside were six crisp notes. Tucked beneath them was a tiny slip of paper that had nothing to do with money.
advance:2.cnHint: 唐交给我一个信封，说是薪水____，但信封里还藏着一张奇怪的纸条。
advance:2.hook: The slip read: 'Leave before the branch opens.'
advance:2.line: 'He asked me to give you this *advance* quietly, not at the register.'

capable:2.en: Lin walked in just after two in the morning and stood at the magazine shelf for a long time. 'You seem *capable*,' she said at last, not quite looking at me. 'Smart enough to know when a job is worth keeping.' She bought nothing and left before I could reply.
capable:2.cnHint: 林深夜走进店里，夸我____，话里似乎藏着某种警告。
capable:2.hook: Her smile never reached her eyes.
capable:2.line: 'A *capable* clerk always knows which side to stand on.'

dollar:2.en: Counting the till at midnight, I found one extra *dollar* coin tucked behind the receipt roll. Taped to it was a note in tiny letters: 'For your bus fare out of here.' Tang saw my face and came over. She turned the coin in her fingers and went very quiet.
dollar:2.cnHint: 我在收银机里发现一枚多出来的____硬币，上面贴着一张神秘字条。
dollar:2.hook: Tang said she had found the same coin last week.
dollar:2.line: 'One *dollar* and a warning — someone wants you gone.'

double:2.en: The delivery invoice showed *double* the usual order of bottled water — enough to fill the new branch on opening day. But the delivery address written at the bottom was not the new branch. It was somewhere I had never heard of. I photographed it quickly with my phone.
double:2.cnHint: 送货单上的瓶装水数量是平时的____，但收货地址却让人看不懂。
double:2.hook: The address led to a building that closed two years ago.
double:2.line: 'Why would anyone order *double* stock for a place that empty?'

federal:2.en: A man in a plain grey jacket came in near dawn and bought only a pen. He left a business card on the counter by accident — or maybe on purpose. It read: *Federal* Trade Office, Regional Review. The Manager arrived an hour later and went pale when I showed it to him.
federal:2.cnHint: 一位神秘男子留下一张____贸易办公室的名片，店长看到后脸色大变。
federal:2.hook: The Manager made a phone call he did not want me to hear.
federal:2.line: 'A *federal* review now — right when we plan to expand?'

insist:2.en: A note arrived from the Manager: the new branch would open in two weeks. Lin dropped by the store to read it over my shoulder and *insist* that the corner location was wrong. 'Customers walk from the east,' she said, tapping the map firmly with one finger.
insist:2.cnHint: 林来店里看通知，____说新分店的位置选错了。
insist:2.hook: But the Manager had already signed the lease.
insist:2.line: 'I *insist* that corner will lose us every passing customer.'

investigation:2.en: Tang found a crumpled receipt behind the back shelf while restocking drinks for the new branch supply order. The amount was double what it should be. He smoothed it out on the counter and said a quiet *investigation* was needed before anyone signed off on the next delivery.
investigation:2.cnHint: 唐在货架后发现一张可疑收据，说需要进行一番____。
investigation:2.hook: The supplier's phone number on the receipt was disconnected.
investigation:2.line: 'A small *investigation* now saves a big headache later.'

limited:2.en: The storage room at the new branch site was half the size of ours. Tang measured it twice, then came back shaking his head. Our *limited* shelf space here was already a problem; over there, we would have to cut at least thirty products from the regular stock list.
limited:2.cnHint: 新分店的仓库太小，唐说货架空间____，得削减商品种类。
limited:2.line: 'Our space is so *limited* we may lose our best sellers.'

listen:2.en: The Manager called a late meeting in the back room to share the branch plan. Lin arrived early and sat with her arms crossed. 'Please *listen* carefully,' the Manager said, spreading blueprints across the table, 'because I will only explain the layout once.'
listen:2.cnHint: 店长召开会议，要大家仔细____他对新分店布局的说明。
listen:2.hook: Lin's eyes stopped on one line of the blueprint and narrowed.
listen:2.line: 'Please *listen* — I will not repeat the layout twice.'

master:2.en: A quiet man came in just before dawn and bought three energy drinks. Tang whispered that the man was a *master* student writing his thesis on small retail stores — and that he had been visiting every branch of every convenience chain on this street for a month.
master:2.cnHint: 一位顾客悄悄来买饮料，唐说他是专门研究便利店的____研究生。
master:2.hook: He was already typing notes before he reached the door.
master:2.line: 'He is a *master* student — our store is his research subject.'

newly:2.en: A delivery van pulled up just after midnight, carrying fixtures for the *newly* planned branch two blocks north. The driver handed me a clipboard and asked me to sign, but our address was wrong on every single page — someone had mixed up the two stores already.
newly:2.cnHint: 送货司机半夜送来____分店的设备，但地址全填错了。
newly:2.hook: Every page listed our store as the one being closed.
newly:2.line: 'These shelves are for the *newly* planned branch, not here.'

north:2.en: Tang pinned a hand-drawn map to the staff board showing the new branch was three blocks to the *north*, near the old bus stop. He had walked the route himself and timed it: seven minutes on foot. 'Close enough to share stock,' he said, 'far enough to need its own team.'
north:2.cnHint: 唐在地图上标出新分店在____面，自己走路计算了时间。
north:2.hook: Someone had already drawn a question mark over our store.
north:2.line: 'The new branch sits three blocks to the *north* of us.'

obviously:2.en: Lin walked into our store holding a printout of the new branch's floor plan. She studied it for a long moment, then set it on the counter and sighed. The freezer units were placed along the wrong wall — *obviously* no one had checked where the power sockets actually were.
obviously:2.cnHint: 林拿着新分店平面图来店里，____发现冷柜位置和电源对不上。
obviously:2.hook: Rewiring the whole wall would cost more than the freezers.
obviously:2.line: '*Obviously* no one checked where the power sockets are.'

pose:2.en: A delivery notice had been slipped under the back door. The Manager stood in a proud *pose*, arms folded, as he announced that supplies for the new branch would arrive at dawn. I grabbed a pen to sign the form, wondering what the new store would look like.
pose:2.cnHint: 店长摆出自豪的____，宣布新分店的物资即将到货。
pose:2.hook: But the address on the notice was completely wrong.
pose:2.line: 'Strike a confident *pose*, people — this branch is really happening!'

stimulate:2.en: Tang waved a printout of the new branch plan in front of me near the drink coolers. 'Reading this will *stimulate* your brain,' she said with a grin. The plan was full of bright ideas — a reading corner, a soup bar, even a small plant wall. I felt genuinely excited.
stimulate:2.cnHint: 唐拿着新分店的计划书说，这份文件能____你的思维。
stimulate:2.hook: Then I noticed one page was stamped 'confidential' in red.
stimulate:2.line: 'This layout will really *stimulate* customers to stay longer.'

switch:2.en: I found an old envelope taped behind the supply shelf. Inside was a hand-drawn map of the building with a note: '*switch* the back-room light off before you leave, or the cameras cut out.' No one had told me this. I had been leaving it on every night for a week.
switch:2.cnHint: 我发现了一张便条，提醒要____后屋的灯，否则摄像头会断电。
switch:2.hook: I wondered who had left the note — and why it was hidden.
switch:2.line: 'Always *switch* that light off — trust me, it matters.'

treatment:2.en: A regular customer, an older woman, left a small card on the counter addressed to the Manager. It thanked him for the kind *treatment* she always received at the store — warm soup on cold nights, a chair to rest in, never being rushed. The Manager read it twice and said nothing.
treatment:2.cnHint: 一位常客留下感谢卡，感激店里对她一直以来的____。
treatment:2.hook: He quietly slipped the card into his coat pocket.
treatment:2.line: 'The *treatment* here is better than any place I know.'

union:2.en: Tang showed me a flyer she had found folded inside a delivery box. It announced a *union* of local convenience stores sharing a single late-night delivery route. Our store was listed as a founding member. This was big news — but the Manager had never mentioned it to us.
union:2.cnHint: 唐发现了一张传单，宣布本地几家便利店组成____，共享配送路线。
union:2.hook: Our store's signature on the flyer was dated three months ago.
union:2.line: 'A *union* like this could change everything for small stores.'

acknowledge:2.en: Lin slid a note across the counter without making eye contact. It said: 'I *acknowledge* that I took the wrong delivery box last Tuesday. I will return it.' That was all. No apology, no explanation. She had been our rival for months, and this was the closest thing to honesty I had seen from her.
acknowledge:2.cnHint: 林悄悄递来一张纸条，____自己上周拿错了配送箱。
acknowledge:2.hook: The box she had taken contained the plans for our new branch.
acknowledge:2.line: 'I *acknowledge* it — I had the wrong box the whole time.'

alike:2.en: I compared two staff schedules pinned on the wall — one for our store, one printed for the new branch. They were almost *alike*, same shift times, same break rules, same color codes. Tang leaned over my shoulder and said the Manager had simply copied the old one. Nobody had planned anything new at all.
alike:2.cnHint: 我发现两家店的员工排班表几乎____，新分店根本没有新计划。
alike:2.hook: One name on the new schedule did not belong to anyone I knew.
alike:2.line: 'Both rosters look completely *alike* — did he even try?'

analyze:2.en: I stayed late to *analyze* the sales printout left on the manager's desk. The numbers showed that our quietest hour — three in the morning — was actually the most profitable per customer. Someone had circled that row in pencil and written one word beside it: 'branch.' The new store's hours suddenly made sense.
analyze:2.cnHint: 我仔细____销售报表，发现凌晨三点竟是利润最高的时段。
analyze:2.hook: The pencil handwriting did not belong to the Manager.
analyze:2.line: 'If you *analyze* these numbers, the answer is right there.'

writer:2.en: A folded note fell out of the morning delivery box. I opened it and found neat, careful handwriting inside. 'To the night clerk,' it began. The note said the *writer* had been watching the store for weeks and had something important to tell us about the new branch plan.
writer:2.cnHint: 一张纸条从送货箱里掉出来，____说他观察这家店已经好几周了。
writer:2.hook: The note was signed with only a small drawing of a cat.
writer:2.line: 'The *writer* of this note knows more than we do.'

addition:2.en: The Manager spread a large paper map across the counter at midnight. He pointed to a red circle near the university. 'The new branch will go here,' he said proudly. 'And as an *addition*, we plan to add a small seating area so students can study inside.' I looked at the circle and felt a little nervous.
addition:2.cnHint: 店长在地图上指出新分店的位置，还提到一个____——增设座位区。
addition:2.hook: Lin had quietly walked in and was already staring at the same map.
addition:2.line: 'As an *addition* to the plan, we need a seating corner.'

alternative:2.en: Tang rushed in just before three in the morning, holding a torn schedule. 'The delivery van broke down,' she said. 'We have no *alternative* — someone has to carry the boxes on foot from the depot two streets away.' She looked at me. I looked at my comfortable chair. The night suddenly felt very long.
alternative:2.cnHint: 送货车坏了，阿糖说我们没有____，只能步行搬货箱。
alternative:2.hook: Outside, a light rain had just begun to fall.
alternative:2.line: 'There is no *alternative*; we carry the boxes ourselves tonight.'

amazing:2.en: I was restocking the shelves at two in the morning when I found a tiny hand-drawn map taped behind the rice crackers. It showed every corner of the store in perfect detail, even the broken tile near the back door. The accuracy was *amazing* — whoever drew it knew this place better than I did.
amazing:2.cnHint: 我在货架后面发现了一张手绘地图，其精确程度令人____。
amazing:2.hook: A small arrow on the map pointed to something hidden under the counter.
amazing:2.line: 'It is *amazing* — this map shows even the broken tile.'

ease:2.en: The Manager walked the new branch site with his hands behind his back and a calm smile on his face. He spoke about shelf layouts and lighting with total *ease*, as if he had opened a hundred stores before. I took notes as fast as I could, struggling to keep up with his quiet confidence.
ease:2.cnHint: 店长以一种轻松的____介绍新分店的布局，我努力跟上他的思路。
ease:2.hook: Then his phone buzzed, and the smile disappeared instantly.
ease:2.line: 'He talks about the new branch with such *ease*, it worries me.'

frequent:2.en: Lin from the rival store across the street had become a *frequent* visitor to our supply room — or so the Manager suspected. Three times this week, small items had moved from their usual spots. Nothing was missing, but the Manager left a notebook by the door and asked me to write down every face I saw after midnight.
frequent:2.cnHint: 店长怀疑竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林____出现在我们的库房附近，要我记录每张面孔。
frequent:2.hook: That night, the notebook pen had been moved to the other side of the desk.
frequent:2.line: 'Lin has been a *frequent* visitor near our storage room lately.'

hope:2.en: Tang found an old photograph tucked inside a dusty price guide on the top shelf. It showed two young people standing in front of our store when it was brand new. On the back, in fading ink, someone had written: 'Our *hope* is that this place lasts a hundred years.' Tang held it gently and said nothing for a long time.
hope:2.cnHint: 阿糖在旧书里发现了一张老照片，背面写着创店时的____。
hope:2.hook: One of the two people in the photo looked remarkably like the Manager.
hope:2.line: 'Our *hope* was that this small store would last forever.'

imply:2.en: The Manager left a short handwritten list on the counter before he went home. It read: 'Check the back door. Count the evening stock. Look under shelf three.' He did not explain why. Tang said the last item seemed to *imply* that something had been hidden there — or that something important was missing. We both looked at shelf three.
imply:2.cnHint: 店长留下的字条似乎在____货架三下面有什么秘密，我和阿糖对视了一眼。
imply:2.hook: A faint smell of ink rose as we knelt down to look.
imply:2.line: 'Does that last note *imply* something is hidden under shelf three?'

gather:2.en: The Manager calls me to the back room. Old notes and hand-drawn maps *gather* in neat piles on the desk, each one labelled with a different street corner. 'I'm planning something big,' he says, smoothing a fold in his coat. I count seven maps. Seven corners. Our store only has one.
gather:2.cnHint: 店长把店里多年积累的地图和笔记____在桌上，这让店员开始好奇他的真实计划。
gather:2.hook: There was one map with a name crossed out — ours.
gather:2.line: 'All the best ideas *gather* in this room first,' the Manager said quietly.

imagine:2.en: A folded note falls out of a supply box from the warehouse. It reads: 'Whoever finds this — good luck with the night shift.' I *imagine* the person who wrote it: tired, a little lonely, maybe smiling. Tang sees me holding it and laughs. 'That was me. Three years ago.'
imagine:2.cnHint: 店员在货箱里发现一张留言条，开始____留下纸条的人是谁，结果出乎意料。
imagine:2.hook: Tang's smile faded just a little too quickly.
imagine:2.line: 'Did you ever *imagine* someone would actually find it?' I asked.

instance:2.en: Lin slides a printed chart under our door. It lists every price difference between their store and ours, item by item. The Manager reads it slowly, then nods. 'This is a useful *instance* of knowing your competition,' he says, almost admiringly. He pins it to the wall next to our own price list.
instance:2.cnHint: 竞争对手把一份比价表塞进门缝，店长把它当作一个____贴在墙上。
instance:2.hook: By morning, three of our prices had quietly changed.
instance:2.line: 'This is a perfect *instance* of why we must pay attention,' the Manager said.

numerous:2.en: I open the lost-and-found box under the counter for the first time. There are *numerous* small items inside: keys, a single earring, a folded umbrella, a child's drawing of a cat. Each one is a little mystery. The Manager says nobody has ever come back for the drawing. That feels wrong.
numerous:2.cnHint: 店员第一次打开失物招领箱，发现里面有____件无人认领的小物品。
numerous:2.hook: The cat in the drawing was wearing a tiny shop apron.
numerous:2.line: 'There are *numerous* stories in that box,' Tang said softly.

puzzle:2.en: A regular customer leaves exact change every night — always correct, always silent — but tonight the coins add up to three cents more than the total. I check twice. Tang shrugs. The Manager just smiles. This small *puzzle* stays with me until sunrise, turning over and over like a coin itself.
puzzle:2.cnHint: 一位老顾客今晚多付了三分钱，这个小小的____让店员整晚都在想。
puzzle:2.hook: The same customer came back at 5 a.m. and said nothing.
puzzle:2.line: 'Every regular here is a *puzzle* you slowly solve,' the Manager told me.

remind:2.en: Tang sticks a small note to the register: 'Check the back fridge at 2 a.m.' I almost miss it. The fridge holds one box of rice pudding, nearly out of date, marked with a smiley face. A note inside says: 'For the night clerk.' These little things *remind* me that someone cared about this job before me.
remind:2.cnHint: 阿糖贴的一张便条____店员去查冰箱，里面有一份留给夜班的惊喜。
remind:2.hook: The handwriting on the smiley face matched the warehouse note exactly.
remind:2.line: 'I always leave a note to *remind* the next person they matter,' Tang said.

truly:2.en: The Manager hands me a spare key at the end of my first week. It is old and a little bent. 'This store is *truly* yours now, on the night shift,' he says. It sounds simple. But the weight of the key in my hand feels like something much larger than metal. Tang gives me a small nod from the snack aisle.
truly:2.cnHint: 第一周结束时，店长把备用钥匙交给店员，说这家店____属于他了。
truly:2.hook: The key had two faint scratches on it — like a tally.
truly:2.line: 'You are *truly* part of this place now,' the Manager said, and meant it.

valuable:2.en: Lin comes in just before dawn — not as a rival, just as a customer. They buy a hot drink and leave a small envelope on the counter. Inside is a handwritten list of the three nearest bus stops and their schedules. 'Foot traffic timing,' Tang whispers. 'That is *valuable*.' I agree. It is also surprisingly kind.
valuable:2.cnHint: 竞争对手来买东西，悄悄留下一份____的公交时刻表，让人意外地感到温暖。
valuable:2.hook: Lin paused at the door and looked back, just once.
valuable:2.line: 'Good information is always *valuable*, even between rivals,' Lin said.

belong:2.en: While restocking shelves at two in the morning, I found a small notebook behind the instant-noodle boxes. The cover had no name. I flipped through it and saw careful columns of numbers — daily sales figures, sketched floor plans, and one circled question: 'Does this corner *belong* to us, or to them?' I quietly put it back.
belong:2.cnHint: 我在货架后发现一本无名笔记本，里面记满数字和一个关于这家店____给谁的问题。
belong:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like the Manager's.
belong:2.line: 'This store *belongs* to the whole street, not just one person.'

beneficial:2.en: Tang slid a printed chart across the counter during our break. It showed that staying open until six in the morning was *beneficial* to weekly profits by nearly thirty percent. She tapped the page twice, eyebrows raised, clearly proud. I nodded slowly. The Manager had not seen this report yet — and Tang seemed fine keeping it that way.
beneficial:2.cnHint: 阿糖拿出一份图表，证明延长营业时间对利润____，但她似乎不急着让店长看到。
beneficial:2.hook: She folded the chart and slipped it into her own bag.
beneficial:2.line: 'More hours open is *beneficial* — trust the numbers.'

characteristic:2.en: Lin walked in just before dawn carrying a tray of small sample cups. That confident half-smile was a *characteristic* I had already learned to notice. She set the tray on the counter without asking, poured one cup for me, and said nothing. The drink was good — almost exactly like the one we sold in aisle three.
characteristic:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着试喝样品走进来，那个自信的笑容是她____的标志，饮料的口味让我有点担心。
characteristic:2.hook: Our aisle-three supplier called ten minutes later.
characteristic:2.line: 'That calm look is her most dangerous *characteristic*.'

director:2.en: A woman in a neat grey coat came in at midnight and asked for three bottles of water and a bag of salted nuts. She paid, then paused. 'Tell your Manager,' she said quietly, 'that the *director* of the new branch project has already chosen this block.' She left before I could ask a single question.
director:2.cnHint: 一位神秘女士深夜来买东西，临走时说新分店项目的____已经看中了这条街。
director:2.hook: Her business card said only a room number, nothing else.

emerge:2.en: I was checking the stock room when I heard the back door creak. A hand, then a shoulder, then the whole Manager *emerged* from behind a tower of boxed drinks. He was holding a rolled-up paper — building plans, by the look of it — and he froze when he saw me standing there with a clipboard.
emerge:2.cnHint: 店长从仓库的饮料箱后____出来，手里拿着一张像是建筑图纸的卷轴。
emerge:2.hook: He smiled, but the paper disappeared behind his back.
emerge:2.line: 'Good — you *emerge* from the back just in time.'

exact:2.en: Tang was on the phone near the freezer aisle when I passed. She was reading figures aloud in a low voice. 'The *exact* address — yes, corner of Mei Road and Qing Street, ground floor.' She noticed me, ended the call fast, and began straightening yoghurt cups that were already perfectly straight.
exact:2.cnHint: 阿糖在电话里报出了一个____地址，看见我后迅速挂断并假装整理货架。
exact:2.hook: That address was the same as ours.

guest:2.en: A quiet man came in every night at eleven and bought one green tea. He never spoke. Tonight he left a folded note on the counter beside his coins. It read: 'Thank you for the light.' I looked up, but he was already gone. The Manager later told me the man was a *guest* speaker at the college nearby, far from home.
guest:2.cnHint: 一位每晚来买绿茶的沉默男士留下了一张便条，店长说他是附近高校的____，离家很远。
guest:2.hook: The note had a second line I had not noticed before.
guest:2.line: 'Every *guest* carries a story we have not heard yet.'

massive:2.en: The delivery arrived at three in the morning — not the usual two trolleys, but a *massive* stack that filled the entire doorway and spilled onto the pavement outside. The driver shrugged and handed me a slip. The order was three times the normal size. At the top, in red ink, someone had written 'new branch — trial stock.'
massive:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点来了一批____的货物，送货单上用红笔写着"新分店——试销库存"。
massive:2.hook: No one had told me we were opening a second store.
massive:2.line: 'That *massive* order came from someone above the Manager.'

mix:2.en: Behind the store, I found a handwritten note taped to the back door. It listed a strange *mix* of items: three rice balls, one energy drink, and a folded map of the business district. Someone had planned something carefully — and left the note for whoever opened up that morning.
mix:2.cnHint: 我在后门发现一张字条，上面列着一份奇怪的____。
mix:2.hook: The handwriting matched no one I had ever met.
mix:2.line: 'It's a *mix* of things I need before the new branch opens,' Lin said quietly.

necessity:2.en: The Manager spread blueprints across the counter at midnight. 'A second freezer is a *necessity*,' he said, tapping the paper. 'The new branch runs twice the volume.' I nodded, pretending I understood supply chains, while secretly hoping someone would bring me a warm drink soon.
necessity:2.cnHint: 店长说明了开分店时增加冷冻柜的____。
necessity:2.hook: Then he pointed to a name on the blueprint I did not recognise.
necessity:2.line: 'Trust me, a second freezer is a *necessity* for the new place,' the Manager said firmly.

stuff:2.en: Tang arrived before sunrise dragging a heavy box. 'New branch *stuff*,' she said, dropping it with a loud thud. Inside were price-tag guns, spare shelf brackets, and a thick folder of forms. She looked at me, then at the box, and said nothing more for a very long time.
stuff:2.cnHint: 唐搬来了一箱开分店用的____。
stuff:2.hook: One folder at the bottom was sealed with red tape.
stuff:2.line: 'All this *stuff* has to reach the new branch by Friday,' Tang said, stretching her back.

translate:2.en: Lin slid a printed page across the counter. 'Can this *translate* into a real advantage for us?' The page showed foot-traffic numbers for the new corner location. I studied the rows of figures, wondering if numbers this clean ever told the whole truth about a neighbourhood.
translate:2.cnHint: 林想知道这些数据能否____成真正的竞争优势。
translate:2.hook: The address on the page was only two streets from here.
translate:2.line: 'Can these numbers *translate* into something useful for the opening?' Lin asked.

wander:2.en: My break was fifteen minutes, so I let myself *wander* one block down to see the new branch site. A bare shopfront, a paper sign, dusty glass. It looked nothing like a store yet. I pressed my face to the window and thought: three weeks is not very long at all.
wander:2.cnHint: 我趁休息时间____到了分店的选址处。
wander:2.hook: A light was on inside, and somebody was already moving around.
wander:2.line: 'Don't *wander* too far — the Manager wants us back by two,' Tang called after me.

warn:2.en: Tang pulled me aside near the drinks fridge. 'I have to *warn* you,' she whispered, 'the Manager plans to announce the branch manager tomorrow morning.' She glanced toward the office, then back at me. Her expression said she already knew who it would be, and that I might not like the answer.
warn:2.cnHint: 唐悄悄____我，明天早上会有重要公告。
warn:2.hook: She left before I could ask a single question.
warn:2.line: 'I just want to *warn* you so you are not caught off guard,' Tang said softly.

advocate:2.en: Lin placed a neat proposal on the counter and waited. 'I am an *advocate* for the self-checkout lane,' she said. 'It cuts wait time by half.' The Manager read it twice without speaking. Outside, a delivery truck idled. I counted the seconds, pretending to restock the gum display.
advocate:2.cnHint: 林作为自助结账通道的____，向店长提交了方案。
advocate:2.hook: The Manager finally looked up and said only three words.
advocate:2.line: 'I have always been an *advocate* for smarter checkout systems,' Lin said calmly.

cite:2.en: The Manager called us to the counter and opened a thick folder. He began to *cite* figures from last year's holiday sales to show why the new branch location made sense. I quietly wrote down every number, thinking that whoever gathered this data had spent a very long night doing it.
cite:2.cnHint: 店长____了去年的销售数据，为开分店的选址做说明。
cite:2.hook: The last figure he read out made Tang set down her coffee.
cite:2.line: 'Let me *cite* one number that will change your mind,' the Manager said.

content:2.en: A folded note fell out of the supply box from the Manager. It read: 'New branch opens Friday. You will run the night shift alone.' I sat on the stool, staring at the ceiling, and found I was quietly *content* — no crowd, no noise, just the hum of the drink fridge and the whole store to myself.
content:2.cnHint: 店长留了一张纸条，我读完之后感到出乎意料地____。
content:2.hook: Then I noticed a second note tucked beneath the first.
content:2.line: 'I am *content* with the quiet — does that make me strange?'

divide:2.en: The Manager taped a long strip of yellow paper across the floor of the stockroom. 'This side is for the new branch supplies, that side is ours,' he said. The line seemed to *divide* not just the boxes but the whole future of the store into two very different worlds.
divide:2.cnHint: 店长用一条线把库房____成两个区域，气氛一下子变得微妙。
divide:2.hook: Tang stood on the wrong side and did not move.
divide:2.line: 'Why does one small line *divide* everything so cleanly?'

generate:2.en: Lin set up a small chalkboard outside the new branch location, three blocks away, and wrote the day's specials on it. By noon, a short queue had formed. 'That sign alone can *generate* more curious customers than any flyer,' she told me over the phone, sounding almost annoyed at her own success.
generate:2.cnHint: 林在新店门口挂了一块黑板，没想到____了不少人流。
generate:2.hook: She hung up before I could ask whose idea the board really was.
generate:2.line: 'A good sign can *generate* more talk than any advertisement.'

operate:2.en: The new branch register arrived in a big cardboard box. Tang unpacked it, plugged it in, and pressed every button twice. 'I need to learn how to *operate* this before Friday,' he muttered, squinting at the tiny screen. Outside, a cat sat on the window ledge, watching him with great patience.
operate:2.cnHint: 唐正在努力学习如何____新收银机，看起来有点手忙脚乱。
operate:2.hook: The cat outside suddenly pressed its paw against the glass.
operate:2.line: 'Can you show me how to *operate* this thing without breaking it?'

properly:2.en: I carried a tray of sample cups to the new branch for a test run and arranged them on the counter. The Manager walked in, looked at the tray, and quietly turned three cups the other way. 'If we cannot display a cup *properly*,' he said softly, 'we cannot run a store properly either.'
properly:2.cnHint: 店长纠正了我摆放样品杯的方式，说凡事都要____。
properly:2.hook: He then glanced at the door and said nothing more.
properly:2.line: 'Please set each item *properly* — the small things matter most.'

render:2.en: The old lamp in the back corner of the new branch flickered all evening and cast strange moving shadows on the wall. Its weak light managed to *render* the whole room slightly dreamlike, as though the store existed in some other, softer version of the night. I kept looking over my shoulder.
render:2.cnHint: 新店角落里一盏旧灯闪烁不定，把整个房间____得有些不真实。
render:2.hook: One shadow on the wall did not match anything in the room.
render:2.line: 'That lamp will *render* the whole corner useless if we keep it.'

resolve:2.en: Tang found a cracked shelf bracket behind the new branch counter and stood staring at it for a long moment. Then he set his jaw, went to the supply box, and found a spare. His quiet *resolve* — no complaint, no call to the Manager — made me respect him in a way I had not expected.
resolve:2.cnHint: 唐发现了一个坏掉的支架，他没有抱怨，默默表现出____要自己修好它。
resolve:2.hook: But the bracket he pulled from the box was the wrong size.
resolve:2.line: 'My *resolve* is to fix every problem before the Manager sees it.'

seemingly:2.en: Lin arrived at the new branch carrying a box of price tags and a cup of tea, looking *seemingly* relaxed, as though opening a second store were something she did every other week. But I noticed her hand tremble just slightly as she pressed the first tag onto the shelf. She caught me watching and smiled.
seemingly:2.cnHint: 林____很从容地来到新店贴价签，但我注意到了一个小细节。
seemingly:2.hook: She slipped a folded paper from her pocket and quickly hid it.
seemingly:2.line: 'I am *seemingly* calm, but do not ask me how I slept last night.'

therefore:2.en: A note was taped to the back room door when I arrived for my shift. It said the Manager had gone to check the new store site and would be late. The shelves near the door were almost empty, *therefore* I started restocking without waiting to be told.
therefore:2.cnHint: 店长留了一张便条说他要去看新店选址，所以我____自己开始补货了。
therefore:2.hook: But the note was not in the Manager's handwriting.
therefore:2.line: The shelves are low, *therefore* I will start without you.

truth:2.en: Tang slid a folded paper across the counter to me during the slow hour before dawn. 'Read it after I leave,' she said with a small smile. It turned out to be a hand-drawn map of the new store's street. At the bottom she had written: 'The *truth* is, it is only two blocks away.'
truth:2.cnHint: 阿糖悄悄递给我一张纸，上面写着关于新店位置的____。
