truth:2.hook: The address on the map did not match the one the Manager had announced.
truth:2.line: The *truth* is, the new store is closer than he told us.

protein:2.en: A delivery arrived just before midnight — twelve boxes stacked by the side door. I checked the list: mostly drinks and snacks for the new branch. One box, however, was full of *protein* powder in small silver bags, each one labelled with a name I had never seen on our shelves before.
protein:2.cnHint: 深夜到货的箱子里，有一整箱贴着陌生品牌的____粉。
protein:2.hook: None of the bags appeared on any of our official order forms.
protein:2.line: Why is there so much *protein* powder in this order?

traffic:2.en: I stepped outside for a moment around two in the morning. The street was almost silent. Then I noticed it: a slow line of delivery scooters turning the corner one after another, all heading in the same direction. That kind of *traffic* at this hour only meant one thing — a new store had just opened nearby.
traffic:2.cnHint: 凌晨两点，街上出现了一列送货摩托的____，全都朝同一个方向驶去。
traffic:2.hook: The lead scooter stopped right in front of our door.
traffic:2.line: All this *traffic* at two in the morning — something is going on.

cat:2.en: I found a small grey *cat* sitting on the step outside the back door, next to a cardboard box addressed to the new branch. It looked up at me calmly, as if it had been waiting. A note tied to the box read: 'Please keep her warm until the Manager arrives.'
cat:2.cnHint: 后门台阶上坐着一只小灰____，旁边还有一个寄给新店的纸箱。
cat:2.hook: Inside the box, something moved very gently.
cat:2.line: Hello, little *cat* — did the Manager send you here?

sugar:2.en: Lin came in just after three and went straight to the baking supplies shelf. She picked up every bag of *sugar* we had and placed them in her basket without a word. I asked if the new store was planning something big. She just smiled and set a folded flyer on the counter before walking out.
sugar:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜来店里买走了所有的____，还在柜台留下了一张折叠的传单。
sugar:2.hook: The flyer advertised a grand opening sale — starting tomorrow morning.
sugar:2.line: I need all the *sugar* you have — every single bag.

balance:2.en: I was checking the till at the end of my shift when I noticed the numbers were off by exactly fifty yuan. I went through every receipt twice, trying to *balance* the total. Tucked behind the register I finally found a handwritten slip that said: 'Moved to new store fund. — The Manager.'
balance:2.cnHint: 我试图____收银机账目时，发现少了整整五十元，最后找到了一张手写的便条。
balance:2.hook: The slip was dated three weeks ago — and it was not the first one.
balance:2.line: I have been trying to *balance* this till for an hour now.

baby:2.en: A young woman came in at four in the morning, pushing a small pram. The *baby* inside was wide awake and staring at the bright lights with great interest. The mother asked quietly if we sold the brand of milk that the new store down the road was advertising. We did not — not yet.
baby:2.cnHint: 一位年轻妈妈推着婴儿车进来，问我们是否有新店广告里的那款____奶粉。
baby:2.hook: She left a name card on the counter without being asked.
baby:2.line: My *baby* loves that milk — does your new store carry it?

teenager:2.en: A folded note fell out of a returned magazine. I smoothed it open. Someone had written: 'To the *teenager* who works nights — your smile makes the 2 a.m. bus ride worth it.' No name, no number. Just a small drawing of a convenience store under a moon.
teenager:2.cnHint: 一张留给夜班店员的纸条从杂志里滑了出来，署名处空空的。
teenager:2.hook: The handwriting matched the notebook Tang keeps under the counter.
teenager:2.line: 'Every *teenager* deserves one note like that,' Tang said quietly.

patient:2.en: A man sat on the step outside for forty minutes before coming in. He bought one warm can of soup and stood at the window, watching the rain. 'You are very *patient*,' I said. He smiled. 'I am waiting for the bus and for courage.' He left a folded paper crane on the counter.
patient:2.cnHint: 一位在店外等了很久的男人只买了一罐汤，走前留下了一只折纸鹤。
patient:2.hook: The paper crane was folded from a hospital appointment slip.
patient:2.line: 'Being *patient* is just hoping with better posture,' he told me.

classroom:2.en: I found a lost backpack behind the drink fridge. Inside: one ruler, three pens, a lunch box, and a photo of kids standing in front of a *classroom* door with a banner that read 'First Day.' On the back someone had written a phone number and the word 'please.'
classroom:2.cnHint: 冰柜后面有个遗失的书包，里面的照片背面写着一个电话号码。
classroom:2.hook: The number belonged to a school two streets away — closed for renovation.
classroom:2.line: 'That *classroom* in the photo — I think I know it,' Lin said slowly.

vehicle:2.en: A large delivery *vehicle* stopped outside at 3 a.m. and did not move for an hour. The driver came in, bought four coffees, and spread a hand-drawn map across my counter. He circled our store and wrote 'base camp' in small letters. Then he drove away without the map.
vehicle:2.cnHint: 一辆深夜停在店外的大车司机买了四杯咖啡，在手绘地图上标了我们的店。
vehicle:2.hook: The map showed six other stores, all circled in the same red pen.
vehicle:2.line: 'Every *vehicle* on that route stops here by morning,' he said.

remote:2.en: The Manager pulled a dusty box from the back shelf. Inside was an old television *remote* with a sticky note attached: 'Works only on Channel 7. Do not ask why.' Nobody could find the television it belonged to. The Manager placed it carefully back in the box and said nothing.
remote:2.cnHint: 店长从货架上取出一个贴着神秘纸条的旧遥控器，却找不到它对应的电视。
remote:2.hook: Lin later whispered that Channel 7 stopped broadcasting three years ago.
remote:2.line: 'A *remote* without its television is just a small sad rectangle,' I said.

zoo:2.en: A woman came in at midnight carrying a canvas tote printed with giraffes. She bought a banana and handed me a loyalty card already stamped nine times. 'One more and I get a free drink,' she said. 'I work at the *zoo*. Nights are longer when the animals dream loud.'
zoo:2.cnHint: 一位动物园工作人员深夜来买香蕉，她的集点卡还差一格就满了。
zoo:2.hook: Her tenth stamp was dated the same night the store's fish tank went missing.
zoo:2.line: 'The *zoo* at 3 a.m. is quieter than you would think,' she said.

card:2.en: Tucked under the windscreen wiper of a bicycle outside was a small *card* with our store's address printed on it, but the store had not made any such cards. The Manager turned it over twice, said 'hm,' and pinned it to the board above the register without another word.
card:2.cnHint: 店外自行车上夹着一张印有本店地址的卡片，但我们从未印过这种卡。
card:2.hook: By morning, three more identical cards had appeared on three more bicycles.
card:2.line: 'Whoever printed this *card* knows our address better than we do,' said Lin.

gene:2.en: A biology student spread her notes across the corner table for two hours. Her textbook lay open to a chapter on inheritance. 'This one *gene*,' she told me when I brought her a free coffee, 'decides whether you can smell rain before it falls.' Outside, it began to rain.
gene:2.cnHint: 一个生物系学生在角落里温书，告诉我某个基因能决定一个人是否能预感到下雨。
gene:2.hook: She had already packed her umbrella before the first drop hit the window.
gene:2.line: 'One *gene* is a tiny thing to carry so much weather in,' she said.

childhood:2.en: The Manager pulled a small photo from the back of the till. It showed two boys sharing a single ice cream outside a tiny shop. 'This corner,' he said softly, 'is where I spent my *childhood*.' He pinned the photo above the new store plan on the wall.
childhood:2.cnHint: 店长在收银台后面找到一张旧照片，指着它说这条街是他____度过的地方。
childhood:2.hook: The second boy in the photo looked a lot like Lin.
childhood:2.line: 'My *childhood* dream was always to run a shop on this exact corner.'

equal:2.en: Tang lined up two stacks of new product brochures on the counter, one for each proposed branch location. She measured them twice with a ruler. 'Both sites get *equal* attention,' she said firmly, sliding one stack to me. 'Fair is the only way to choose.'
equal:2.cnHint: 阿糖把两个候选分店地址的宣传册摆得整整齐齐，坚持两边要____对待。
equal:2.hook: But one stack had a handwritten note hidden inside.
equal:2.line: 'Every branch deserves *equal* resources, or the whole plan falls apart.'

inspire:2.en: A retired teacher stopped in for warm milk at midnight. She noticed our hand-drawn map of the new branch on the wall and smiled. 'A neighbourhood shop *inspired* me to read as a child,' she said. 'Keep that warmth in the new place.' She left a small bookmarked card on the counter.
inspire:2.cnHint: 一位退休老师深夜来买热牛奶，看着分店地图说小小的街角商店曾____了她。
inspire:2.hook: The card had an address on the back — the same street as Branch Two.
inspire:2.line: 'Places like this *inspire* people more than you ever know.'

narrow:2.en: The Manager spread the floor plan of the second branch across the counter after closing. I leaned in. The entrance passage looked tight. 'That *narrow* corridor worries me,' I said. 'Deliveries will block it every morning.' He tapped the paper and said nothing, staring at it for a long time.
narrow:2.cnHint: 我和店长一起看分店平面图，我指出入口____的走廊可能造成麻烦。
narrow:2.hook: He finally circled the corridor in red and wrote one word: 'Lin.'
narrow:2.line: 'A *narrow* entrance might turn customers away before they even get inside.'

quantity:2.en: A delivery driver dropped off sample goods for the new branch and left a form on the counter. Tang read it and frowned. 'The *quantity* here is half what we ordered,' she said, underlining a number. 'We cannot open a second store with stock this thin.' She reached for her phone.
quantity:2.cnHint: 送货司机送来样品，阿糖发现单据上的____只有订单的一半，皱起了眉头。
quantity:2.hook: The number on the form matched a cancelled order from three weeks ago.
quantity:2.line: 'Check the *quantity* again — someone changed this after we signed.'

sustainable:2.en: Lin appeared just before dawn, coffee in hand, and dropped a thin report on the counter. 'Opening two branches at once is not *sustainable*,' she said, almost kindly. 'The numbers are all here.' She pushed the report toward me and left without buying anything. The pages smelled like fresh printer ink.
sustainable:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在黎明前来到店里，把一份报告放在柜台上，说同时开两家分店并不____。
sustainable:2.hook: The last page of the report had our store's private cost figures on it.
sustainable:2.line: 'A plan that drains everyone is never *sustainable*, no matter how bold it looks.'

delay:2.en: The sign for Branch One was supposed to go up that morning. By noon it still sat in its box near the door. Tang called the fitting crew three times. 'Another *delay* and we miss the weekend opening,' she told me, rubbing her temples. A knock at the door made us both jump.
delay:2.cnHint: 分店一的招牌本该上午装好，但一再____，阿糖急得直揉太阳穴。
delay:2.hook: The person at the door was not the fitting crew.
delay:2.line: 'One more *delay* and we lose the customers we already told about the opening.'

identity:2.en: I found an old staff badge in the lost-and-found box while sorting things for the new branch. The name on it was worn away, but the shop logo was still clear. 'Keeping that logo is important,' the Manager said. '*Identity* travels with the brand, even to a new address.' He pocketed the badge quietly.
identity:2.cnHint: 我在失物箱里发现一枚旧工牌，店长说无论搬到哪里都要保留店铺的____。
identity:2.hook: Later I noticed the badge was gone from his pocket — and so was he.
identity:2.line: 'A store's *identity* is the one thing you cannot pack in a moving box.'

store:2.en: At two in the morning, I found a locked back room behind the freezers. The Manager had mentioned a *store* of emergency supplies kept there — candles, batteries, instant noodles — enough to last a small neighbourhood through a week-long blackout. I counted seven boxes. There were only six yesterday.
store:2.cnHint: 我发现后储藏室里的应急物资少了一箱，不知道是谁拿的。
store:2.hook: The seventh box was gone, and the door had been locked from inside.
store:2.line: 'We keep a *store* of candles back there — never touch them without asking me first.'

budget:2.en: Tang slid a handwritten note across the counter just before her shift ended. It was a rough *budget* for the new branch: rent, staffing, stock, a small sum for signage. Every column was neat except the last one, which had a large question mark circled three times in red ink.
budget:2.cnHint: 同事留下一份新分店的____草案，最后一栏画着大大的问号。
budget:2.hook: Under the question mark, someone had written a name — not Tang's.
budget:2.line: 'I worked out the *budget* myself, but one number just does not add up.'

grant:2.en: A folded letter sat under the register when I arrived. The Manager had applied for a small business *grant* from the city council to help open the second store. The letter said the application was successful. He had not told any of us he had even applied.
grant:2.cnHint: 店长偷偷申请了____，信封静静地压在收银机下面。
grant:2.hook: The amount on the letter was twice what the new branch actually needed.
grant:2.line: 'The council will *grant* us enough to open — if we submit one more form.'

hospital:2.en: Around midnight, a tired man in a green uniform bought four sandwiches and two large coffees. He said he had come straight from the *hospital* across the avenue, where his whole ward had been awake since noon. He paid, smiled faintly, and jogged back into the dark.
hospital:2.cnHint: 一位穿绿色制服的人从街对面的____赶来买宵夜，匆匆离开。
hospital:2.hook: He left his phone on the counter, and it buzzed immediately with an urgent call.
hospital:2.line: 'The *hospital* is full tonight — I barely had time to run over here.'

island:2.en: Lin came in holding a travel magazine folded open to a bright photo. She pointed to a small *island* off the southern coast and said the Manager had once talked about opening a convenience store there, somewhere quiet with only fishing boats and one narrow road in.
island:2.cnHint: 竞争对手拿着杂志，指着一座____，说那是店长曾经提起的地方。
island:2.hook: On the magazine's margin, in the Manager's handwriting, was a date three weeks away.
island:2.line: 'He said he dreamed of a little *island* shop — just him, the sea, and the shelves.'

native:2.en: A quiet older woman bought a jar of pickled vegetables and told me the recipe was a *native* tradition from the village where she grew up, three provinces away. She said no shop here ever stocked the right kind. Then she looked at our shelf and went very still.
native:2.cnHint: 一位老太太说这种泡菜是她家乡____的做法，随后在货架上发现了什么。
native:2.hook: She picked up the jar with shaking hands and whispered a name none of us knew.
native:2.line: 'This flavour is completely *native* to my home village — how did it get here?'

tradition:2.en: The Manager stayed late to rearrange the window display. He lined up the same seven items he arranges every time a new branch opens — a habit so old it had become a *tradition*, he said. He would not explain what the seven items meant, only that the order mattered.
tradition:2.cnHint: 店长按照老____布置橱窗，七件物品的顺序有特殊含义，他却不肯说明。
tradition:2.hook: Tonight, for the first time, he placed the seventh item facing outward.
tradition:2.line: 'It is a *tradition* I started with the very first store — I never break it.'

africa:2.en: A student spread a large map on the counter to show me a geography project. She had traced supply routes from *Africa* all the way to our street, trying to prove that the coffee beans in our cheapest instant packets had travelled further than anyone in this city ever had.
africa:2.cnHint: 一个学生把地图铺在收银台上，追溯咖啡豆从____到我们这条街的旅程。
africa:2.hook: One route on her map ended not at a port, but at our store's exact address.
africa:2.line: 'These beans came all the way from *Africa* — that cup cost less than a bus fare.'

modern:2.en: The Manager spread a large floor plan across the counter. 'The new branch will be *modern*,' he said, pointing to open shelves and a self-checkout screen. I stared at the drawings. Our cosy old store suddenly felt like a museum. Tang leaned over and whispered, 'Do you think they'll keep the cat?'
modern:2.cnHint: 店长展示新分店的设计图，风格十分____。
modern:2.hook: Nobody noticed the small red X marked on our store's location.
modern:2.line: 'The new branch will be *modern*, with screens where the counter used to be.'

officer:2.en: A city *officer* in a neat grey uniform stepped in just before midnight, clipboard in hand. He walked slowly around the store, measuring corners and checking ceiling lights. I followed him like a nervous shadow. He wrote something down, tore off a yellow slip, and placed it on the counter without a word.
officer:2.cnHint: 一位____深夜来到店里，默默检查了一番后留下一张纸条。
officer:2.hook: The yellow slip said only: 'Third visit this month.'
officer:2.line: 'I am a city *officer*. I need to see the back room, please.'

convince:2.en: Tang spent ten minutes trying to *convince* the Manager that the new branch should sell hot soup. 'Soup brings people in on cold nights,' she said, showing him a notebook full of customer comments. The Manager listened, nodded slowly, and then pointed at the shelf of instant noodles. I held my breath.
convince:2.cnHint: 阿糖努力____店长在新分店卖热汤，结果却指向了泡面架。
convince:2.hook: Lin had been standing outside the window, listening to every word.
convince:2.line: 'I can *convince* him if you back me up — just say you love soup.'

directly:2.en: A letter arrived *directly* at the store, addressed not to the Manager but to 'the night clerk'. I was the only night clerk. Inside was a hand-drawn map with a circle around a building two streets away. There was no name, no phone number, just a small smiley face in the corner.
directly:2.cnHint: 一封信____寄给了夜班店员，里面装着一张神秘的手绘地图。
directly:2.hook: The building on the map was where our new branch was supposed to open.
directly:2.line: 'This came *directly* for you — no sender, no stamp, nothing.'

extend:2.en: The Manager called us together before dawn. 'We will *extend* the night shift by two hours at the new branch,' he announced, tapping the schedule on the wall. Tang crossed her arms. I did the maths quietly in my head. Outside, a cat on the kerb seemed to be doing the same.
extend:2.cnHint: 店长宣布新分店要____夜班时间，阿糖听完叉起了手臂。
extend:2.hook: The schedule on the wall had one name crossed out in red ink.
extend:2.line: 'We will *extend* the shift, and yes, that means you two as well.'

rat:2.en: I found a small toy *rat* sitting on top of the new branch's welcome box, which had been delivered that afternoon. It was plastic, painted grey, with tiny red eyes. Tang laughed. The Manager did not laugh. He picked it up carefully with two fingers and dropped it into a bag.
rat:2.cnHint: 新分店的欢迎礼盒上放着一只玩具____，店长的反应很耐人寻味。
rat:2.hook: Tang stopped laughing when she saw the Manager's face go pale.
rat:2.line: 'A toy *rat* on a welcome gift is not a joke — it is a message.'

saturday:2.en: The grand opening was set for *Saturday*, and by Thursday the Manager had already changed the date twice. A handwritten sign on the door still said 'Opening Soon'. Tang updated the sign every morning. On Friday evening, a stranger photographed the sign and walked away without buying anything.
saturday:2.cnHint: 新分店原定____开业，但日期已经改了两次，还来了个神秘拍照的人。
saturday:2.hook: The stranger came back an hour later and photographed it again.
saturday:2.line: 'If it opens on *Saturday*, I want to be the first one through that door.'

april:2.en: Lin slid a printed article across the counter. It reported that three new convenience stores would open on our street before *April*. I read it twice. The Manager was in the back room, on the phone. His voice was low and steady, the way it gets when something is wrong.
april:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿来一篇报道，说在____之前这条街会多出三家便利店。
april:2.hook: One of the three stores on the list shared our Manager's family name.
april:2.line: 'Before *April*, there will be three new stores on this street alone.'

passion:2.en: A folded note fell out of the supply box the Manager sent over from the new branch. It read: 'Stack the noodle cups with *passion* — first impressions matter.' I laughed, then straightened every single cup. Tang leaned over and did the same without a word.
passion:2.cnHint: 店长在补给箱里留了一张纸条，叮嘱我们要用____摆放货品。
passion:2.hook: But the note had a second line none of us had noticed yet.
passion:2.line: 'Stack the noodle cups with *passion* — first impressions matter.'

temperature:2.en: The Manager called from the new branch to say the drinks fridge there had stopped working. 'Check our *temperature* log,' he said. I found the little notebook under the counter and read out every number from the past week. Tang nodded slowly, as if the numbers told a story I could not yet hear.
temperature:2.cnHint: 店长打来电话，让我查看我们这边饮料柜的____记录。
temperature:2.hook: The last entry in the log was written in a hand neither Tang nor I recognised.
temperature:2.line: 'Please check the fridge *temperature* log and read it to me.'

board:2.en: Leaning against the door of the stock room was a wooden *board* covered in little notes — opening times, staff names, a hand-drawn map of the new branch layout. The Manager had left it for us to study. I traced the map with one finger and suddenly felt like a sailor reading a chart before a long voyage.
board:2.cnHint: 库房门边有一块____，上面密密麻麻写满了新分店的信息。
board:2.hook: One name on the staff list was circled in red, with no explanation.
board:2.line: 'Study this *board* carefully — the new branch opens in three days.'

handle:2.en: A small package arrived addressed to the new branch but delivered here by mistake. The label said 'Fragile — *handle* with care.' Tang and I set it on the counter and stared at it. The Manager had not mentioned any package, and neither of us wanted to be the one to call and ask.
handle:2.cnHint: 一个写着"易碎品，请小心____"的包裹被误送到了我们店。
handle:2.hook: The package made a faint ticking sound every few minutes.
handle:2.line: '*Handle* it with care — it says fragile right there on the label.'

ideal:2.en: Tang pointed at the corner spot on the new branch map and said it was the *ideal* place to put the hot-food counter — warm smell would pull people in from the street. I had never thought about a store that way before. I looked at our own corner and saw it, too, like seeing a picture inside a cloud.
ideal:2.cnHint: 阿糖指着地图上的一个角落，说那是摆放热食台的____位置。
ideal:2.hook: Lin walked in just then and had a very different idea about that corner.
ideal:2.line: 'That corner is the *ideal* spot for the hot-food counter, trust me.'

ride:2.en: The Manager asked me to take a box of spare price tags to the new branch on my way home. The *ride* on the night bus was quiet — just me, the box on my lap, and the city sliding past the window in soft orange light. When I arrived, the new store smelled of fresh paint and possibility.
ride:2.cnHint: 店长让我骑车（乘车）把一箱价格标签带去新分店，这段____让我感触颇深。
ride:2.hook: Someone was already inside the new branch, moving around in the dark.
ride:2.line: 'The *ride* over was short — I can bring the next box tomorrow night.'

adjust:2.en: The new branch had sent over its shelf plan, but the measurements were slightly off for our stockroom. Tang said we should *adjust* the plan rather than move the walls — a joke, but also good advice. We spent an hour with a pencil and a ruler, and by the end the numbers fit like a key in a lock.
adjust:2.cnHint: 新分店发来的货架方案尺寸有偏差，我们需要____一下再使用。
adjust:2.hook: The revised plan revealed a gap in the layout big enough to hide something.
adjust:2.line: 'We just need to *adjust* the numbers a little and it will fit perfectly.'

basis:2.en: The Manager pinned a one-page note to the board: the new branch would share stock with us on a weekly *basis* until it found its own suppliers. Tang read it twice, then looked at our shelves with fresh, slightly worried eyes. I counted the instant noodles quietly and said nothing.
basis:2.cnHint: 店长通知我们，新分店将以每周为____从我们这里共享库存。
basis:2.hook: Tang's worried look turned out to be about something other than the noodles.
basis:2.line: 'We will share stock on a weekly *basis* until the new branch is ready.'

artificial:2.en: The Manager left a note on the counter before my shift: 'The flowers by the door are *artificial* — do not water them.' I had been watering them every night for a week. They did look suspiciously perfect. Tang saw my face and tried very hard not to laugh.
artificial:2.cnHint: 店长留了张便条，说门口的花是____的，而我已经浇了一周的水。
artificial:2.hook: Tang's laughter stopped the moment a regular walked in and headed straight for those flowers.
artificial:2.line: 'Don't worry — even I thought the *artificial* ones were real at first.'

confirm:2.en: A delivery driver knocked at two in the morning, holding a clipboard. 'Can you *confirm* the order for this address?' He turned the board around. The address was our store. Nobody had ordered anything. I checked the system twice. Tang leaned over my shoulder, equally puzzled.
confirm:2.cnHint: 一个送货司机深夜来店，要我____一份没人下过的订单。
confirm:2.hook: Then the Manager's name appeared at the bottom of the receipt.
confirm:2.line: 'I just need you to *confirm* the name, and then I can leave it here.'

context:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the shelf of instant noodles — two young people smiling in front of what looked like this very store. Without any *context*, I could not tell who they were or when it was taken. Tang glanced at it and went quiet in a way that felt like a whole story.
context:2.cnHint: 我在货架后发现一张旧照片，没有任何____，无法判断照片里的人是谁。
context:2.hook: Tang slipped the photo into their pocket without a single word.
context:2.line: 'You need the *context* before you start asking questions about that photo.'

date:2.en: A regular came in, bought a small cake, and asked me for a pen. She wrote a *date* on the box in careful numbers — not today's date. She smiled at my curious look. 'It's the day this store first opened,' she said softly, and walked out into the dark street.
date:2.cnHint: 一位常客买了蛋糕，在盒子上郑重写下一个____，那不是今天的日期。
date:2.hook: The date she wrote matched the photo I had found behind the noodle shelf.
date:2.line: 'I always write the *date* on the box so I never forget.'

flexible:2.en: Lin from the convenience store across the street came in to browse, which felt odd. 'Our hours are less *flexible* than yours,' Lin said simply, eyeing our night-shift shelf layout. I smiled and said nothing. Lin spent ten quiet minutes studying how we arranged the drinks.
flexible:2.cnHint: 对面店的隔壁咖啡店的林进来转了转，说他们的营业时间没我们____。
flexible:2.hook: Lin left without buying anything, but came back an hour later with a notebook.
flexible:2.line: 'You have to be *flexible* when you run a small store — I'm still learning that.'

fly:2.en: Just before dawn, a single *fly* appeared from nowhere and circled the bright light above the rice-ball shelf. Tang grabbed a folded newspaper and missed three times. The fourth swing knocked a whole row of rice balls to the floor. We both stared at the mess in silence.
fly:2.cnHint: 快天亮时，一只____出现在货架上方，阿糖抄起报纸，结果把一排饭团打翻了。
fly:2.hook: The regular who always bought the first rice ball of the morning walked in exactly then.
fly:2.line: 'It is just one *fly*, Tang — please put the newspaper down.'

judge:2.en: The Manager stopped by at midnight to check the stock report. I had sorted the snacks by colour instead of by type. I waited for a reaction. The Manager studied the shelf for a long moment. 'I won't *judge* the system until I see the sales numbers,' the Manager said, and left.
judge:2.cnHint: 我把零食按颜色而不是种类摆放，店长说等看了销售数字再____我的方法。
judge:2.hook: The next morning, the colour-sorted snacks had sold out first.
judge:2.line: 'Don't *judge* a new system before you give it one full night.'

oil:2.en: At three in the morning, an older man came in asking for cooking *oil*. Just one small bottle. He told me he was making noodles for his son, who had just come home after two years away. He paid with exact coins he had clearly counted out in advance and thanked me twice.
oil:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一位老人来买____，说儿子阔别两年刚回家，他要亲手做碗面。
oil:2.hook: He came back the next night, bought the same bottle, and said nothing at all.
oil:2.line: 'Just the small *oil*, please — I only need enough for one bowl of noodles.'

comfortable:2.en: The Manager spread a large *comfortable* on the back-room cot and smoothed out every wrinkle. 'Night shifts are long,' she said. 'You should sleep well between rushes.' I had not expected such care from someone who checked the receipt tape every single morning. Clearly there was more to her than spreadsheets.
comfortable:2.cnHint: 店长在后室的小床上铺好____，让夜班员工能好好休息。
comfortable:2.hook: But why did she lock the back-room door before leaving?
comfortable:2.line: 'A good *comfortable* makes the long night shift much easier to bear.'

conclusion:2.en: A folded note sat under the milk shelf. I opened it slowly. It read: 'Check the second freezer.' Inside I found a hidden stock list with every item marked low. Someone had done a full count overnight. My *conclusion* was simple — whoever left that note knew this store far better than I did.
conclusion:2.cnHint: 我在货架下发现一张纸条，读完之后得出了一个____。
conclusion:2.hook: The handwriting looked exactly like Lin's.
conclusion:2.line: 'My *conclusion* is that someone has been watching this store very carefully.'

formal:2.en: A *formal* letter arrived at the store just before midnight, sealed with a red stamp. The Manager held it at arm's length as if it might bite. Tang leaned over my shoulder to read the return address. 'That's the city planning office,' Tang whispered. My stomach dropped — that could only mean one thing for our little corner store.
formal:2.cnHint: 一封____的信函在深夜送到了便利店，店长和同事都看起来很紧张。
formal:2.hook: The Manager slipped the letter into her bag without opening it.
formal:2.line: 'A *formal* letter from the city office is never just a greeting.'

happiness:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the staff notice board — the Manager, much younger, cutting a ribbon in front of this very store. Her *happiness* in that moment lit up her whole face in a way I had never seen at the counter. Tang caught me staring and smiled quietly. 'That was opening day,' Tang said.
happiness:2.cnHint: 我在公告栏后发现一张旧照片，照片里满满的____让我对店长有了新的认识。
happiness:2.hook: Tang's smile faded the moment I asked when the second store had closed.
happiness:2.line: 'That kind of *happiness* on her face — you don't see it often anymore.'

intelligent:2.en: A small handwritten study guide was taped inside the supply closet door — vocabulary lists, grammar notes, and clever memory tricks. Tang said it belonged to the previous night clerk. 'She was very *intelligent*,' Tang added, 'finished her degree while working here alone every night.' The closet suddenly felt less like storage and more like a classroom.
intelligent:2.cnHint: 储物柜门上贴着一份手写学习笔记，唐说上一任夜班员工非常____。
intelligent:2.hook: No one knew why she had left so suddenly.
intelligent:2.line: 'She was so *intelligent* — she studied through every quiet hour of the night.'

novel:2.en: An old hardback sat on the staff shelf with a bookmark near the final chapter. The title was handwritten on the spine in fading ink — someone had made their own *novel* and printed it at home. I opened the first page and read: 'This store, this street, these people.' My hands went a little cold. The clerk in chapter one had my exact shift hours.
novel:2.cnHint: 员工书架上放着一本自制的____，第一章的主人公竟然和我的班次完全一样。
novel:2.hook: Chapter three was torn out cleanly at the binding.
novel:2.line: 'Someone wrote a whole *novel* about working the night shift here.'

political:2.en: Two customers arrived together just after two in the morning, mid-argument. One wanted the store to move its community board to the window; the other said that would block the light. Tang muttered that their *political* fight over one small board had been going on for three years. They both bought the same snack and left still arguing, almost in step.
political:2.cnHint: 两位常客为公告栏的位置争得不可开交，唐说这场____争论已经持续了三年。
political:2.hook: They always arrived together, which made no sense at all.
political:2.line: 'Their *political* battle over that board is older than my contract here.'

property:2.en: The Manager arrived early with a rolled-up map and spread it across the counter. She pointed to a corner two blocks away. 'That *property* is empty,' she said, 'and the rent is low.' Tang and I looked at each other. She was not talking about storage. She was talking about a second store — and the map already had a floor plan sketched on the back.
property:2.cnHint: 店长带来一张地图，指着附近一处空置的____，背面已经画好了平面图。
property:2.hook: Lin's name was written in pencil in the map's top corner.
property:2.line: 'That *property* two blocks over — I have been watching it for months.'

attribute:2.en: A sealed envelope arrived at the store addressed to no one. Inside was a hand-drawn map of the block, with a red star marking our corner. The Manager studied it and said he could *attribute* the neat handwriting to only one person — the owner of the rival shop across the street.
attribute:2.cnHint: 一封神秘信封送到店里，店长说他能将工整的笔迹____给某个特定的人。
attribute:2.hook: The rival's name was not written anywhere, yet everyone knew.
attribute:2.line: 'I can *attribute* this map to exactly one person on this street.'

badly:2.en: I found the stock room during my first night break. Boxes were stacked in every corner, some leaning *badly* to one side, ready to fall. A sticky note on the tallest pile read: 'Do not touch — Manager's system.' I decided that some systems were best left alone.
badly:2.cnHint: 我发现库房里箱子堆得____，一张便条警告我别乱动。
badly:2.hook: Behind the tallest stack, something quietly ticked.
badly:2.line: 'Those boxes are leaning *badly* — one bump and they all come down.'

bridge:2.en: Tang slid a worn card across the counter during a slow hour. 'Do you play *bridge*?' she asked. Before I could answer, she dealt four hands on the empty counter top, explaining that the night shift regulars used to play until a certain customer stopped coming six months ago.
bridge:2.cnHint: 阿糖拿出一副旧扑克牌问我会不会打____，说某位常客六个月前突然消失了。
bridge:2.hook: She never said why that customer had stopped coming.
bridge:2.line: 'We used to play *bridge* here every Thursday night without fail.'

casual:2.en: A man in a *casual* jacket drifted in just after two in the morning, bought a single mint, and left a folded note under the pen cup on the counter. He looked like any ordinary late-night walker. The note, however, contained a six-digit number and the words 'second location.'
casual:2.cnHint: 一个穿____服装的男人深夜买了一粒薄荷糖，悄悄留下一张写有神秘数字的纸条。
casual:2.hook: No one had mentioned a second location to me before tonight.
casual:2.line: 'He always looks *casual*, but he never comes in without a reason.'

closely:2.en: The Manager pinned a printed floor plan to the back wall and asked me to study it *closely*. It showed a space twice the size of our store, with a counter, a cold section, and a small seating area. At the bottom, in red pen, someone had written: 'Opening — sooner than you think.'
closely:2.cnHint: 店长让我____观察一张新店面的平面图，图纸底部有人用红笔写了一句话。
closely:2.hook: The handwriting at the bottom matched the envelope from earlier.
closely:2.line: 'Look *closely* at where the second counter is placed — that detail matters.'

commit:2.en: Tang warned me during our handover that the Manager would not *commit* to an opening date for the new branch until every small detail was settled. She had seen three launch dates come and go. A corkboard in the back room held the evidence: three crossed-out calendar pages, all from different months.
commit:2.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我店长不肯____确定新分店的开业日期，后室的软木板上有三张被划掉的日历页为证。
commit:2.hook: The fourth calendar page was already pinned up, waiting.
commit:2.line: 'He will never *commit* to a date until every shelf is perfectly placed.'

concentrate:2.en: Around three in the morning the street outside went completely silent, and I found it easier to *concentrate* on the new branch paperwork the Manager had left me. One page listed every item to be moved from our store. A single line at the bottom had been circled twice: 'Night-shift clerk — TBD.'
concentrate:2.cnHint: 深夜街道安静下来，我终于能____看新分店的文件，发现最后一行提到"夜班店员——待定"。
concentrate:2.hook: 'TBD' meant the decision had not yet been made about me.
concentrate:2.line: 'It is easier to *concentrate* on the details when the street is this quiet.'

conscious:2.en: Lin appeared at the door at half past three, pressed her face against the glass, and waved. I was *conscious* of the fact that she was studying our new display stand, not greeting me. She pulled out a small notebook, wrote something, and walked away before I could open the door.
conscious:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜贴着玻璃门张望，我____意识到她其实是在打量我们的新展示架，并悄悄记了笔记。
conscious:2.hook: Whatever she wrote, she wrote it very quickly and very carefully.
conscious:2.line: 'Be *conscious* of what she looks at — it always tells you her next move.'

relative:2.en: A handwritten note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'My shop next door pays only half the price for milk. Everything here is *relative*, I suppose.' The Manager peeled it off, sighed, and stuck it on the staff board without a word.
relative:2.cnHint: 后门贴着一张字条，让店长若有所思地把它贴到了员工告示板上。
relative:2.hook: Whose handwriting was it — Lin's, or someone closer?
relative:2.line: 'Everything is *relative*, so why does this note still bother me?'

rent:2.en: I found a torn envelope under the counter while restocking the bottom shelf. Inside was a single line: 'The *rent* goes up again next month.' The Manager's name was on it. I slid it back quietly, but the number I had glimpsed stayed in my head all night.
rent:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现一封信，得知店里面临涨____的压力。
rent:2.hook: Could that number be the reason the Manager looked so tired lately?
rent:2.line: 'The *rent* went up again — I have not told the others yet.'

round:2.en: Each hour I do a *round* of the store — cooler, snack aisle, counter — checking for anything out of place. Tonight, on my third loop, I noticed a small paper crane sitting on top of the instant-noodle shelf. It had not been there before, and no customer had passed that aisle.
round:2.cnHint: 我在例行巡查时，发现货架上多了一只无人认领的纸鹤。
round:2.hook: Someone left it there on purpose — but who, and why?
round:2.line: 'Every *round* I do, I find something new and strange in here.'

structure:2.en: Tucked behind the staff lockers I found a blueprint of the store. Someone had sketched a new *structure* in pencil — an extra room drawn onto the side wall, with a question mark beside it. The Manager's initials were in the corner. I rolled it up carefully and said nothing.
structure:2.cnHint: 我在储物柜后发现了一张图纸，上面画着店铺改建的____。
structure:2.hook: Was that extra room meant for a second branch, or something else?
structure:2.line: 'The *structure* I have in mind will change everything about this store.'

typical:2.en: A regular customer left her umbrella again — third time this week. Tang shook his head. 'So *typical*,' he said, carrying it to the lost-and-found box under the counter. But this time there was a note tied to the handle, and it was addressed to the Manager by name.
typical:2.cnHint: 常客又忘了雨伞，但这次伞上绑着一张写有店长名字的纸条。
typical:2.hook: What message had she hidden inside that folded note?
typical:2.line: 'It is so *typical* of her — but this note is anything but usual.'

vacation:2.en: I was sorting the magazine rack near the window when I spotted a postcard on the floor. The front showed a sunny beach. The back said: 'Took a small *vacation* to think things over. Back soon. — T.' It was addressed to no one. I set it on the counter and waited.
vacation:2.cnHint: 我在杂志架旁捡到一张明信片，上面说某人趁____想清楚了一些事。
vacation:2.hook: 'T' could be Tang — but Tang was standing right beside me.
vacation:2.line: 'A short *vacation* was all I needed to make up my mind.'

acquire:2.en: While wiping down the shelves I found a slim notebook wedged behind the soy sauce. The first page said: 'Skills to *acquire* before we open the new branch.' Below it was a neat list in Lin's handwriting — including one item I did not expect to see my own name beside.
acquire:2.cnHint: 我在货架缝隙里发现了林的笔记本，里面列着开分店前要____的技能。
acquire:2.hook: Why was my name written next to the last item on that list?
acquire:2.line: 'We need to *acquire* these skills fast if the new branch opens in spring.'

adequate:2.en: The Manager left a checklist on the desk before going out. At the top, underlined twice, were the words: 'Is the space *adequate*?' Below that, an address I did not recognise — three streets away. I checked the clock. The Manager had been gone for exactly one hour.
adequate:2.cnHint: 店长留下了一份清单，询问某个地址的空间是否____，随后独自外出。
adequate:2.hook: Three streets away — could that be the site of the new branch?
adequate:2.line: 'Tell me honestly: is the back room *adequate* for a second counter?'

conventional:2.en: The Manager spread a map across the counter and pointed to our store, then to a spot two blocks east. 'The new branch needs a fresh look,' he said. 'Nothing *conventional* — no plain white walls, no standard shelves. We want people to walk in and feel something different.' I stared at the map and tried to imagine it.
conventional:2.cnHint: 店长展开地图，说新分店不能走____的风格。
conventional:2.hook: But Lin had already sketched a very different design.
conventional:2.line: 'Nothing *conventional* — we want every customer to stop and stare.'

disappear:2.en: Tang was restocking the back room when he noticed three boxes of the new store's sample cups were gone. 'They were here an hour ago,' he said, looking pale. Stock does not simply *disappear* from a locked room. I checked the log, found no record of anyone signing them out, and felt a cold knot form in my stomach.
disappear:2.cnHint: 唐发现新店的样品杯凭空____了，没有任何领用记录。
disappear:2.hook: The security camera, we soon found, had been unplugged.
disappear:2.line: 'Things don't just *disappear* — someone took them on purpose.'

district:2.en: The Manager handed me a printed report about foot traffic in the east *district* where the new branch would open. The numbers were strong: office workers at lunch, students in the evening, families on weekends. He tapped the page twice. 'This is why we chose that corner,' he said. I read every line twice.
district:2.cnHint: 店长拿出一份关于新店所在____的人流报告，数据相当亮眼。
district:2.hook: Lin's face stayed blank the whole time the Manager spoke.
district:2.line: 'That *district* has more young customers than anywhere else in town.'

greatly:2.en: After the Manager pinned the new branch's floor plan to the wall, Tang studied it for a long time. 'The storage space is *greatly* improved,' he said, almost to himself. He had complained about our cramped back room for months. I watched his shoulders relax for the first time all week, and thought: maybe he wants to transfer there.
greatly:2.cnHint: 唐看着新分店的平面图，发现储物空间____改善了，神情若有所思。
greatly:2.hook: He folded the plan carefully and slipped it into his pocket.
greatly:2.line: 'The storage here is *greatly* improved — I could actually breathe back there.'

imitate:2.en: Lin arrived late and spent ten minutes studying the display at our store before saying anything. 'The new branch shouldn't just *imitate* us,' she said, setting a folder on the counter. 'Copy the layout and we copy the problems too.' No one answered right away. Outside, a bus rolled past and its headlights swept across the ceiling.
imitate:2.cnHint: 林认为新分店不应该只是____我们现有的布局，否则会复制同样的问题。
imitate:2.hook: Her folder, I noticed, was already full of her own plans.
imitate:2.line: 'Why *imitate* the old store when we can build something better?'

implement:2.en: The Manager placed a worn spatula, a pricing gun, and a box cutter on the counter. 'Every *implement* we use here has to be standard across both stores,' he said. 'Same tools, same steps, same result.' Tang nodded. I picked up the pricing gun and felt, oddly, that holding it made the second store suddenly real.
implement:2.cnHint: 店长把几件常用____摆在柜台上，说两家店的操作规范必须统一。
implement:2.hook: Tang quietly moved the box cutter to the far end of the counter.
implement:2.line: 'Each *implement* gets labeled so nothing wanders between the two stores.'

mood:2.en: I came in for my shift to find the Manager sitting alone at the small corner table, coffee untouched. Tang whispered that the landlord of the new building had called with a problem. The whole store felt the Manager's *mood* — even the hum of the drinks fridge seemed quieter. I made fresh coffee without being asked and slid it over.
mood:2.cnHint: 店长独自坐着不说话，整家店都感受到了他低落的____。
mood:2.hook: He wrapped both hands around the cup and finally looked up.
mood:2.line: 'My *mood* has nothing to do with you two — the landlord is the problem.'

motivation:2.en: Tang pulled me aside near the magazine rack and spoke quietly. 'The Manager is offering a bonus to whoever helps the new branch reach its first-month target,' he said. I felt something light up in my chest. A clear reward is powerful *motivation* — far better than a vague promise. I straightened my name badge and went back to the counter with new energy.
motivation:2.cnHint: 唐悄悄告诉我，店长设了奖金，这给了我强大的____去帮新店完成目标。
motivation:2.hook: Lin was already at the counter, smiling at the Manager.
motivation:2.line: 'A real bonus is the best *motivation* you can give a night-shift clerk.'

worldwide:2.en: Late at night, the Manager unrolled a large map on the counter. Red dots marked cities across every continent. 'Our parent company sells snacks *worldwide*,' he said proudly, tapping a dot near the sea. I stared at all those dots and wondered why our tiny store kept running out of milk.
worldwide:2.cnHint: 店长展开一张地图，自豪地介绍母公司的____业务。
worldwide:2.hook: But one red dot had a question mark drawn over it.
worldwide:2.line: 'Our snacks sell *worldwide*, yet this store can't keep milk stocked!'

accomplish:2.en: Tang taped a handwritten list to the staff-room wall: restock shelves, fix the broken fan, sort expired goods, mop the back room. 'We must *accomplish* all of this before six,' she said calmly. I looked at the clock. It was already four forty-five.
accomplish:2.cnHint: 阿糖贴出任务清单，要求在天亮前____所有工作。
accomplish:2.hook: Then the lights in the back room went out completely.
accomplish:2.line: 'We need to *accomplish* every task before the morning rush arrives.'

address:2.en: A delivery driver handed me a small package and said the *address* on the label did not match any building on our street. I checked twice. The store name was right, but the street number was impossible — our block only went up to forty. Someone had sent this on purpose.
address:2.cnHint: 快递员送来一个包裹，但上面的____让人困惑。
address:2.hook: Inside, folded neatly, was a single key.
address:2.line: 'The *address* on this box makes no sense — your block ends at forty.'

barely:2.en: Lin walked in just as I finished arranging a neat pyramid of canned drinks. She glanced at it and then nudged the bottom can just slightly. The whole pyramid trembled. 'This store can *barely* hold itself together,' she said with a small smile, and walked to the back fridge.
barely:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林轻轻碰了一下饮料堆，笑着说这家店____能维持。
barely:2.hook: She stayed near the back fridge far longer than she needed to.
barely:2.line: 'This display can *barely* survive one customer — let alone a busy morning.'

blame:2.en: A jar of pickles fell from the top shelf and shattered at two in the morning. The Manager appeared from nowhere, looked at the mess, looked at me, then looked at Tang. No one spoke for a moment. 'Let's not *blame* anyone,' Tang said quietly. 'Let's just clean it up.'
blame:2.cnHint: 泡菜罐摔碎了，店长和阿糖都沉默片刻，阿糖说不必互相____。
blame:2.hook: The Manager's eyes, however, stayed on me a second too long.
blame:2.line: 'Let's not *blame* each other — just get the mop and move on.'

chat:2.en: Around three in the morning a man in a raincoat came in, bought nothing, and stood by the magazine rack. After a while he looked up and asked if he could *chat* with someone for a bit. He said the night was very long. I put down my cloth and leaned on the counter.
chat:2.cnHint: 一个雨夜来客什么也不买，只想和人____一会儿。
chat:2.hook: An hour later, he mentioned he used to own this building.
chat:2.line: 'Can I *chat* with you for a while? The night feels very long tonight.'

combat:2.en: Tiny ants had found the honey shelf. Tang pulled on gloves, armed herself with spray and a cloth, and moved with great focus. 'Night-shift *combat*,' she said seriously, without looking up. I handed her a fresh cloth. We worked in silence until every last ant was gone and the shelf shone.
combat:2.cnHint: 蚂蚁入侵了蜂蜜货架，阿糖严肃地把这场清理称为____。
combat:2.hook: In the morning, a whole new line of ants appeared from behind the wall.
combat:2.line: 'Night-shift *combat* — hand me that cloth and don't let them reach the sugar.'

danger:2.en: The Manager called me to the storeroom and pointed at a shelf bending under the weight of too many heavy boxes. 'That is a real *danger*,' he said. 'Do not touch it until I bring a new shelf tomorrow.' He left. I stood there, watching the shelf slowly creak and lean a little more.
danger:2.cnHint: 仓库里有一排超重货架，店长警告那是真正的____。
danger:2.hook: Then one bolt near the bottom quietly pinged across the floor.
danger:2.line: 'That shelf is a real *danger* — stay away from it until tomorrow morning.'

threaten:2.en: A note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'Open a second store on Oak Street and we will take all your customers.' I showed it to the Manager. He read it twice, folded it carefully, and smiled. 'Anyone who has to *threaten* us,' he said, 'is already afraid of us.'
threaten:2.cnHint: 我在后门发现一张字条，有人____要抢走我们所有顾客。
threaten:2.hook: But the Manager's smile faded the moment he thought I wasn't looking.
threaten:2.line: 'Anyone who has to *threaten* us is already afraid of us.'

throw:2.en: Opening a second store felt like a huge *throw* of the dice. The Manager spread maps and cost sheets across the counter at two in the morning, circling numbers and crossing them out. I swept the floor around his papers and said nothing. Some bets, I have learned, are best made in silence.
throw:2.cnHint: 开分店对店长来说是一次巨大的____，他深夜在柜台上研究地图和费用表。
throw:2.hook: Then Lin walked in, glanced at the maps, and her eyes went sharp.
throw:2.line: 'This whole plan is one big *throw* of the dice, Manager.'

unlike:2.en: The new site was on the west side of town. I visited it on my lunch break. It was *unlike* our cosy corner store in every way: wide glass windows, bright overhead lights, a car park outside. I stood on the pavement and tried to imagine Tang stocking shelves in all that cold space.
unlike:2.cnHint: 新选址和我们温馨的角落小店____，我站在门口想象着那里的样子。
unlike:2.hook: A sign on the door said the lease had already been signed by someone else.
unlike:2.line: 'It is so *unlike* our store — I am not sure it feels right.'

vast:2.en: The storeroom in the new location was *vast*. Tang and I walked through it after the Manager got the keys. Our footsteps echoed. Back in our little store, every centimetre of shelf space is fought over. Here, whole walls stood empty, waiting. Tang spread her arms wide and slowly turned around.
vast:2.cnHint: 新店的库房____，唐和我在空荡荡的货架间走着，脚步声回响在空气中。
vast:2.hook: Tang stopped turning and stared at one dark corner without speaking.
vast:2.line: 'The storeroom is *vast* — we could stock enough for a whole neighbourhood.'

absolutely:2.en: The Manager asked if I would take the night shift at the new store once it opened. I looked around our quiet corner: the humming fridge, the stack of warm buns, the regular who always bought one coffee at midnight. I took a slow breath. '*Absolutely*,' I said, and was surprised to mean it.
absolutely:2.cnHint: 店长问我是否愿意去新店上夜班，我____地答应了，自己都感到意外。
absolutely:2.hook: The midnight regular looked up from his coffee with wide eyes.
absolutely:2.line: '*Absolutely* — I will take the night shift at the new store.'

accumulate:2.en: Every evening I found small things left near the register: a lucky coin, a folded paper crane, a tiny potted plant. Regulars had heard about the new store and were offering quiet good wishes. 'Look at all this,' Tang said. 'You *accumulate* supporters without even trying.' I did not know what to say.
accumulate:2.cnHint: 常客们纷纷在收银台旁留下小礼物，唐说我不知不觉____了许多支持者。
accumulate:2.hook: Among the gifts was an unsigned envelope with a key inside.
accumulate:2.line: 'You *accumulate* supporters without even trying — that is a real gift.'

breakfast:2.en: The Manager called a meeting at six in the morning. Tang and I arrived to find him already at the counter, setting out rice porridge and soft eggs. 'We *breakfast* together before the big decision,' he announced. The warm smell filled the store. Outside, the street was pale and quiet and full of possibility.
breakfast:2.cnHint: 店长在清晨六点召集会议，决定大家先一起____，再讨论重要决定。
breakfast:2.hook: Lin pushed open the door just as the Manager lifted his spoon.
breakfast:2.line: 'We *breakfast* together before any big decision — that is our rule.'

capacity:2.en: The Manager unrolled the floor plan on the counter. 'See here,' he said, pointing. 'The new store has three times the *capacity* of this one. Three times the fridges, three times the shelf space.' I studied the numbers. Three times bigger also meant three times more things that could go wrong.
capacity:2.cnHint: 店长展示新店的平面图，指出新店的____是现店的三倍。
capacity:2.hook: Tang quietly circled one room on the plan with a red pen.
capacity:2.line: 'The new store has three times the *capacity* — are we ready for that?'

partly:2.en: The Manager slid a folded paper across the counter. It was a rough map of the new branch location — *partly* drawn in pen, partly left blank where he was still unsure. 'Fill in what you think fits,' he said, tapping the empty spaces with one finger.
partly:2.cnHint: 店长拿出一张____完成的新分店地图，让我补全空白部分。
partly:2.hook: One blank space had a question mark — and my name beside it.
partly:2.line: 'The plan is *partly* done, but I need your eyes on the rest.'

practical:2.en: Tang spread three designs for the new branch layout on the break-room table. Two looked fancy but wasted space. Only one used every corner well. 'This is the most *practical*,' Tang said, pointing at the simple grid plan. The Manager nodded slowly, then circled it in red.
practical:2.cnHint: 阿糖在休息室展示了三套分店布局方案，其中最____的那个被店长圈出来了。
practical:2.hook: But the circled plan had someone else's initials in the corner.
practical:2.line: 'Forget the pretty ones — this layout is the most *practical* of all three.'

profit:2.en: I found a printed report tucked behind the register. It showed last year's numbers for the main store. The *profit* column was thin — barely enough, I thought. A sticky note on top read: 'New branch must do better.' The handwriting was not the Manager's.
profit:2.cnHint: 我在收银台后面发现了一份报告，上面的____数字让人担忧，便利贴上写着新分店必须做得更好。
profit:2.hook: The unknown handwriting made my stomach feel strange.
profit:2.line: 'If the new branch shows no *profit* by spring, we close it.'

promise:2.en: Lin stopped by the store just before dawn, sliding a note under the supply-room door. I found it during my check. It said: 'I *promise* the corner spot is better than yours.' No name, but the ink smelled faintly of the coffee Lin always carried. My hands went cold.
promise:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林悄悄把一张写着____的便条塞进库房门缝，暗示他们的新选址比我们的好。
promise:2.hook: The corner spot Lin meant was directly across our street.
promise:2.line: 'I *promise* you, that location will beat yours by summer.'

rarely:2.en: The Manager came to the night shift to check the new delivery — something he *rarely* did. He said nothing for a long time, just walked each aisle slowly. Then he stopped at the end shelf and stared at the space where a second register might go. I stayed very still.
rarely:2.cnHint: 店长____来夜班巡视，这次他默默地盯着货架尽头，像是在想象分店的样子。
rarely:2.hook: He pulled out a tape measure, and my heart jumped a little.
rarely:2.line: 'I *rarely* visit nights, but this shelf tells me everything I need.'

severe:2.en: A delivery driver knocked and handed me a chipped box with a note clipped to it: 'Handle with care — *severe* damage possible.' Inside were the new branch's custom signs, wrapped in thin paper. One corner was already cracked. I set it down softly and hoped the Manager would not see yet.
severe:2.cnHint: 送货员带来了标有____警告的新分店招牌箱子，但其中一块已经有了裂缝。
severe:2.hook: The Manager's car lights swept across the window just then.
severe:2.line: '*Severe* damage to these signs would delay the whole opening.'

smell:2.en: I opened the supply-room door and stopped. A warm, sweet *smell* floated out — someone had left a small paper bag of pastries on the top shelf with a tag that read: 'For the new branch opening day.' The bag was from the bakery two streets over. Nobody claimed it all week.
smell:2.cnHint: 库房里飘来一股____，架子上有人悄悄放了一袋点心，标签写着新分店开业日用。
smell:2.hook: The bakery two streets over had closed down six months ago.
smell:2.line: 'That *smell* — someone left a gift, and I want to know who.'

socialize:2.en: The new branch plan said staff must *socialize* with neighbours before opening — hand out small gifts, say hello, learn names. Tang read it aloud at the counter and groaned softly. I looked at the quiet street outside, at the old woman who walked past every night, and felt a little hopeful.
socialize:2.cnHint: 新分店计划要求员工提前与附近居民____，阿糖皱起了眉，而我却看向窗外感到有些期待。
socialize:2.hook: The old woman outside paused, looked in, and almost smiled.
socialize:2.line: 'We need to *socialize* with the neighbours before the doors ever open.'

obvious:2.en: A sealed envelope sat on the back shelf, addressed to no one. The Manager had left it there three days ago without a word. It was *obvious* from the worn edges and the careful knot of string that someone had opened and re-tied it more than once. I slid it behind the rice crackers and pretended I had not noticed.
obvious:2.cnHint: 店长留下的信封被人反复打开过，这一点____可见。
obvious:2.hook: By midnight, the envelope was gone — and so was Tang.
obvious:2.line: 'It's *obvious* someone has been reading that letter,' Tang said quietly.

ordinary:2.en: The new branch store guide arrived by post: a thin booklet with a cheerful cover. I flipped through it expecting something special, but every page looked *ordinary* — shelf labels, mop schedules, snack rotation charts. Then I reached the last page, where someone had written a single question in red ink and left it unanswered.
ordinary:2.cnHint: 新分店手册看起来____无奇，直到最后一页出现了一行红字。
ordinary:2.hook: The handwriting on that last page looked exactly like Lin's.
ordinary:2.line: 'Nothing about this feels *ordinary* to me,' Lin said, staring at the red ink.

pace:2.en: Lin arrived at two in the morning, moving fast. She began to *pace* the narrow space between the drinks fridge and the bread rack, four steps one way, four steps back, while I pretended to restock the chewing gum. She was holding a folded map of the new branch location, and her lips were moving, counting something I could not hear.
pace:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿着分店地图在店里____步，嘴里似乎在默默计算什么。
pace:2.hook: She stopped suddenly and pointed at a spot on the map.
pace:2.line: 'I always *pace* when I'm trying to work something out,' she admitted.

participate:2.en: The Manager pinned a notice to the staff board: all clerks were invited to *participate* in the opening-day planning meeting for the new branch. Tang circled it in pencil and added a small star. I read it three times, unsure if 'invited' meant 'required.' The notice had been signed, but the name was smudged beyond reading.
participate:2.cnHint: 店长贴出通知，邀请员工____新分店开业筹备会议。
participate:2.hook: Tang whispered that only one of us would actually be sent there.
participate:2.line: 'I really want to *participate* — this feels important,' Tang said.

pilot:2.en: On the shelf above the register, a small framed photo appeared overnight. It showed a young woman in a flight jacket, grinning beside a small plane. On the back, in neat letters: 'Before the store.' I asked Tang who it was. Tang looked at the photo for a long moment and said only, 'She used to be a *pilot*.'
pilot:2.cnHint: 收银台上方出现了一张旧照片，照片里的人曾经是一名____。
pilot:2.hook: Tang never said whose photo it was.
pilot:2.line: 'She was a *pilot* before any of this,' Tang said softly.

primary:2.en: Tang spread the floor plan of the new branch across the counter. 'The *primary* concern,' Tang said, tapping the paper, 'is where we put the hot-food station.' I leaned over to look. Someone had already drawn a big red circle in the corner nearest the door, then crossed it out, then circled it again.
primary:2.cnHint: 阿糖在柜台上摊开新店平面图，讨论____要解决的问题。
primary:2.hook: The handwriting on the red circles did not belong to Tang.
primary:2.line: 'Our *primary* concern should be that corner spot,' Tang said firmly.

priority:2.en: The Manager left a checklist for the new branch setup and had ranked every item by number. At the top, underlined twice, was one task with no description — just a blank line. I asked Tang what *priority* number one was supposed to be. Tang went very still and said, 'Ask the Manager. Not me.'
priority:2.cnHint: 新分店准备清单上，优先级第一的任务只有空白，____事项不明。
priority:2.hook: That night the Manager came in early and filled in the blank alone.
priority:2.line: 'That task is our top *priority*, and I can't tell you why,' Tang said.

throughout:2.en: The planning folder for the new branch was thick. *Throughout* the whole document, every page about staffing had one column left blank — the column for night-shift clerk. I read it twice to be sure. Tang had signed every other column neatly. I closed the folder and set it back exactly as I had found it.
throughout:2.cnHint: 整份分店规划文件____都有一栏空着，那是夜班员工一栏。
throughout:2.hook: The next morning, my name had appeared in that column.
throughout:2.line: '*Throughout* the whole plan, that one column stays empty,' I said.

dinner:2.en: A folded note dropped through the mail slot at midnight read: 'New branch opens Friday. Staff *dinner* at the noodle place two doors down. Be there.' I turned it over, looking for a name. Nothing. I pinned it above the register and wondered who slipped it in — and why they did not simply knock.
dinner:2.cnHint: 一张字条从信槽滑进来，宣布周五有庆祝____，但没有署名。
dinner:2.hook: The handwriting matched no one I had met — yet.
dinner:2.line: 'Staff *dinner* Friday — don't be the only one who misses it.'

embrace:2.en: The Manager spread both arms wide the moment he stepped through the door of the new branch space, an empty room still smelling of paint. 'We *embrace* every challenge,' he told the bare walls, nodding slowly. Tang caught my eye behind his back and pressed both lips together very hard to keep from laughing.
embrace:2.cnHint: 店长张开双臂，说要____一切挑战，但新店只是一间空屋子。
embrace:2.hook: Then the Manager turned around and asked Tang to price the ceiling tiles.
embrace:2.line: 'We *embrace* every challenge, no matter how empty the room looks.'

explanation:2.en: I found a second set of keys taped under the front counter with a small label: 'Branch B.' Nobody had mentioned a Branch B to me. I asked Tang, who shrugged. I asked the Manager, who gave a long *explanation* about permits and timing that somehow answered nothing. The keys stayed under the counter, waiting.
explanation:2.cnHint: 钥匙上写着"B分店"，店长给了一番____，但什么也没说清楚。
explanation:2.hook: That evening Lin came in and glanced straight at the spot where the keys were hidden.
explanation:2.line: 'The *explanation* is simple — the branch opens when the permit comes through.'

intend:2.en: Lin walked in at two in the morning carrying a floor plan rolled under one arm. She spread it on the counter without asking, pointed to a red circle near the corner, and said she *intended* to put a coffee bar exactly there. I looked at the map. That corner was inside our store.
intend:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带着平面图来，说她____把咖啡台设在地图上圈出的地方。
intend:2.hook: The red circle sat twelve centimetres inside our property line.
intend:2.line: 'I *intend* to have that coffee bar running before your branch even opens.'

leadership:2.en: The Manager pinned a printed chart to the wall showing every task for the new branch opening. His own name sat at the top under the word *leadership*. Below it were two names: Tang and mine. Tang leaned close and whispered, 'Count the tasks under our names. Then count his.' I counted. It was not close.
leadership:2.cnHint: 店长贴出任务表，把____写在自己名字旁边，但任务全落在别人身上。
leadership:2.hook: Tang was already circling three items in red marker.
leadership:2.line: 'Good *leadership* means giving the hard work to the people you trust most.'

locate:2.en: The Manager asked me to *locate* the spare price-tag gun before the new branch opened. I checked every drawer, the back shelf, the box above the freezer, and the locked cabinet that Tang opened with a key from her lanyard. We found it inside a noodle cup on the top shelf. Nobody admitted putting it there.
locate:2.cnHint: 店长让我____备用价格标签枪，最后在一个面杯里找到了它。
locate:2.hook: The noodle cup had been opened and carefully resealed.
locate:2.line: '*Locate* it fast — we need to tag three hundred items by morning.'

original:2.en: Tang held up two logos printed on paper — one clean and modern, one hand-drawn with small stars around the store name. 'The Manager wants the clean one,' she said. 'But this star one is the *original* design, from when he first opened.' She looked at it for a long moment, then rolled it gently and slid it into her bag.
original:2.cnHint: 阿糖展示了两个标志，那个有星星的是店长最____的设计手稿。
original:2.hook: I noticed the roll of paper had a date on it — seven years ago.
original:2.line: 'The *original* design had stars — I think he forgot how much he loved them.'

overcome:2.en: The new branch sign arrived with the store name spelled wrong. The Manager sat on a crate outside and stared at it for three full minutes. Then he stood up, rolled his sleeves, and said we would *overcome* this small problem with a marker pen and a steady hand. Tang offered her hand. The Manager looked at it, then at her neat writing on the task chart.
overcome:2.cnHint: 新店招牌名字拼错了，店长说要____这个小问题，但需要一双稳当的手。
overcome:2.hook: Tang was already uncapping the marker before he finished the sentence.
overcome:2.line: 'We will *overcome* this — hand me the marker and stand back a little.'

consideration:2.en: The Manager spread a hand-drawn map across the counter just after midnight. 'We are opening a second store,' he said proudly. He had marked three possible street corners with small stars. '*Consideration* of foot traffic, nearby schools, and late-night bus stops all pointed to the same spot.' He tapped the middle star twice and smiled.
consideration:2.cnHint: 店长深夜拿出手绘地图，说明选址时综合了多项____。
consideration:2.hook: But the middle star was inside Lin's delivery zone.
consideration:2.line: '*Consideration* of the bus stop alone made this corner the clear winner.'

disaster:2.en: Tang was restocking the instant noodle shelf when a full box slipped from his hands. Cups rolled everywhere, one knocked over a standing sign, and the sign hit a small bottle display. The bottles survived, but the sign did not. Tang stared at the mess. 'That,' he said quietly, 'was a *disaster*.' I handed him a broom without a word.
disaster:2.cnHint: 阿糖理货时一场小小的____让货架区乱成一片。
disaster:2.hook: The Manager's security camera had caught every second of it.
disaster:2.line: 'One dropped box and a total *disaster* — please don't tell the Manager.'

emergency:2.en: A folded note was taped to the staff-room door when I arrived for my shift. It read: 'Second-store opening moved to Friday. Stock transfer Thursday night. This is not an *emergency*, but please do not be late.' The Manager had underlined 'not' three times, which made it feel very much like one.
emergency:2.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了张字条，说分店开业提前了，虽然不是____，但请准时到岗。
emergency:2.hook: Friday was also the night Tang had already booked off.
emergency:2.line: 'It says not an *emergency*, but three underlines say otherwise.'

familiar:2.en: A woman in a yellow coat walked in at two in the morning and went straight to the back shelf without looking at the signs. She picked up a specific brand of canned soup, checked nothing else, and brought it to me. Her face was *familiar* — I was certain I had seen her photo on the new-store planning board pinned in the staff room.
familiar:2.cnHint: 一位穿黄色外套的女士深夜径直走向货架，她的面孔对我来说____，在员工室的公告板上似乎见过。
familiar:2.hook: Her name tag, half hidden by her coat, read 'Site Manager.'
familiar:2.line: 'Your face is *familiar* — have you been in before, or am I imagining things?'

furthermore:2.en: The Manager left a handwritten memo beside the register. It listed the new store's opening hours, its address, and which items would move there. '*Furthermore*,' the last line read, 'the night-shift clerk at the new store will be chosen from current staff.' I read that line four times before Tang leaned over and said, 'That means one of us.'
furthermore:2.cnHint: 店长的便条列出了分店信息，____还提到夜班员工将从现有员工中选出。
furthermore:2.hook: Tang had already circled the new address on his phone map.
furthermore:2.line: '*Furthermore*, the new store is only one bus stop from my apartment.'

hardly:2.en: The supply delivery for the new store arrived at our back door by mistake. There were twelve large boxes stacked in the narrow corridor. I could *hardly* move between them to reach the shelf trolley. Tang squeezed past sideways, knocking a box of rice crackers off the top. We both froze. The box landed perfectly upright.
hardly:2.cnHint: 新分店的备货误送到本店后门，走廊被堆得____能通行。
hardly:2.hook: The delivery note listed one item that was not on our current stock list at all.
hardly:2.line: 'I can *hardly* get past — who ordered twelve boxes for a store that isn't open yet?'

hinder:2.en: Lin appeared at the door just as we were carrying the mislaid boxes back outside. He watched without offering to help. 'I hope the new store does not *hinder* my delivery times,' he said, arms folded. 'Your loading bay and mine share the same alley.' He left before I could answer, which I found both annoying and a little worrying.
hinder:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林出现在门口，担心新分店会____他的配送时间，因为两家共用同一条小巷。
hinder:2.hook: He already had a lawyer's business card in his shirt pocket.
hinder:2.line: 'A second store will *hinder* every driver in this alley, and you know it.'

injury:2.en: While I was moving the last box, I caught my wrist on the door frame. It was not serious, but I held it and winced. Tang looked alarmed. 'No *injury* report, no new-store transfer,' he warned, completely serious. I told him it was fine. He handed me a small bandage anyway, already peeled and ready, which meant he had been carrying one all night.
injury:2.cnHint: 我搬箱子时磕了手腕，阿糖一脸认真地警告说有____记录就别想调去新分店。
injury:2.hook: The bandage had tiny cartoon cats on it, which felt oddly comforting.
injury:2.line: 'Any *injury* on record and the Manager will pull you from the transfer list immediately.'

lift:2.en: The Manager called me to the new branch store across town. There was no *lift* in the building, only a narrow staircase. I carried two heavy boxes of stock up four floors, stopping twice to catch my breath. By the top step, I found a handwritten note taped to the door.
lift:2.cnHint: 我帮店长把货物搬到新分店楼上，在门口发现了一张字条。
lift:2.hook: The note had no name, only three words: 'Don't open yet.'
lift:2.line: 'There is no *lift*, so watch your step on those stairs.'

mainly:2.en: The new branch store was *mainly* full of empty shelves when I arrived for the inspection. A few boxes sat in the corner, but most supplies had not come yet. I walked each aisle, making notes on my clipboard. Then I noticed one shelf already had items on it — things no one had ordered.
mainly:2.cnHint: 新分店的货架____是空的，但有一排货架上已经摆满了没人订购的商品。
mainly:2.hook: Every item on that shelf had the same strange label.
mainly:2.line: 'The store is *mainly* empty, but look at that one shelf over there.'

moral:2.en: Tang found an old notebook in the back room of the new branch store. Inside were short stories, each ending with a *moral* written in careful handwriting. 'Honesty brings more customers than clever tricks,' read one. The last story had no ending — just a question mark on a blank page.
moral:2.cnHint: 唐在新分店的后室发现一本旧笔记本，每个故事都写有____，但最后一篇没有结局。
moral:2.hook: The handwriting in that last story matched the Manager's exactly.
moral:2.line: 'Every story here has a *moral*, except the very last one.'

nor:2.en: I searched the new branch store from front to back. There was no sign of the delivery driver, *nor* any record of yesterday's shipment in the logbook. The loading bay door was unlocked. A single muddy boot print crossed the clean floor and stopped in the middle of the room.
nor:2.cnHint: 我在新分店找不到司机，____有任何送货记录，地板上只有一个泥脚印。
nor:2.hook: The boot print faced the wall, as if someone had walked straight through it.
nor:2.line: 'There is no driver here, *nor* is there any note about the delivery.'

pick:2.en: The Manager told me to *pick* one item from each box and check it before the new branch store opened. I worked through the first row easily enough. But the fifth box was sealed with three layers of tape and had no label on any side. I shook it gently — something shifted inside.
pick:2.cnHint: 店长让我从每箱货里____一件商品检查，但第五个箱子没有标签，里面有东西在晃动。
pick:2.hook: Whatever was inside moved again, all on its own.
pick:2.line: 'Please *pick* one item from each box and bring it to me.'

pollution:2.en: Lin arrived at the new branch store holding a report. 'The site inspection found *pollution* in the soil under the car park,' she said, setting the papers on the counter. Her face was calm, but her hands were not. I looked at the address on the report — it was this building.
pollution:2.cnHint: 林拿着一份报告来到新分店，报告显示停车场地下土壤存在____，地址正是这栋楼。
pollution:2.hook: Lin left without taking the report back with her.
pollution:2.line: 'The test found *pollution* right under where we are standing now.'

quit:2.en: A delivery worker knocked on the door of the new branch store just before dawn. He said he wanted to *quit* and handed me a small envelope for the Manager. 'Tell him I am sorry,' he said, then walked away into the dark street before I could ask his name.
quit:2.cnHint: 天亮前，一名送货员来到新分店，说他想____，留下一个信封就消失在黑暗中。
quit:2.hook: Inside the envelope was a key, not a letter.
quit:2.line: 'I came to say I *quit*, and to leave this for the Manager.'

recall:2.en: Tang stood in the storeroom of the new branch store, staring at an old photograph on the wall. 'I *recall* this corner,' he said quietly. 'We used to sell hot drinks here — years before you started.' In the photo, a younger Manager stood smiling beside someone whose face had been neatly cut away.
recall:2.cnHint: 唐在新分店仓库看到一张老照片，他____这个地方，但照片里有人的脸被剪掉了。
recall:2.hook: Tang would not say who had been standing next to the Manager.
recall:2.line: 'I *recall* working here a long time ago, before everything changed.'

register:2.en: The Manager slid a thick notebook across the counter. 'Every regular customer must be *registered* here,' he said, tapping the page. I opened it and found names, favourite snacks, even allergy notes. The store was opening a second branch, and this list would travel with it.
register:2.cnHint: 店长要求把每位常客的信息____在一本厚厚的笔记本里，为新分店做准备。
register:2.hook: One name on the last page had a question mark beside it.
register:2.line: 'Every regular must be *registered* before the new branch opens.'

skin:2.en: A small jar sat on the staff shelf with a sticky note from Tang: 'For the dry winter — helps your *skin* after long night shifts.' I opened it carefully. It smelled of green tea. Outside, the first trucks were arriving to stock the new branch down the road.
skin:2.cnHint: 阿糖留下了一瓶护肤品，说长夜班会让____变得很干燥。
skin:2.hook: But the handwriting on the note did not look like Tang's at all.
skin:2.line: 'Long night shifts are really tough on your *skin*, trust me.'

spirit:2.en: Lin dropped a small potted plant on the break-room table and said nothing. A card tucked into the soil read: 'To keep the *spirit* of this old store alive in the new one.' The Manager stared at it for a long moment, then quietly moved it to the front window.
spirit:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一盆植物，说要把老店的____带到新分店去。
spirit:2.hook: The Manager's eyes looked unexpectedly soft just then.
spirit:2.line: 'This little plant will carry the *spirit* of the old store with it.'

spread:2.en: By midnight, word had already *spread* through the neighbourhood that a second branch was opening two streets away. Customers came in pairs, whispering and pointing at the hand-drawn map the Manager had taped to the door. I counted eleven visitors in one hour — a new record for a Tuesday.
spread:2.cnHint: 消息已经在街坊邻居之间____开来，大家都在议论新分店的事。
spread:2.hook: One visitor asked for a job application, then left without taking one.
spread:2.line: 'News about the new branch has *spread* faster than I expected.'

totally:2.en: I found an old staff photo tucked behind the milk fridge — six smiling faces I did not recognise. The store looked *totally* different: wooden shelves, no self-checkout, a handwritten price board. Tang leaned over my shoulder and said quietly, 'That was ten years ago. Only the Manager is still here.'
totally:2.cnHint: 我发现了一张老照片，老店当年和现在____不同。
totally:2.hook: The Manager walked past without glancing at the photo once.
totally:2.line: 'The store back then was *totally* different from what you see now.'

tree:2.en: Behind the new branch site, workers had paused their work and gathered around a wide old *tree* that stood exactly where the back wall was planned. The Manager walked over slowly, measured the trunk with his arms, and then told the builders to move the wall one metre to the left.
tree:2.cnHint: 新分店工地后面有一棵大____，挡住了施工计划。
tree:2.hook: Nobody asked the Manager why he cared so much about one tree.
tree:2.line: 'We are building around the *tree*, not cutting it down.'

weigh:2.en: The Manager set two folders on the counter — one for the old store's layout, one for the new — and began to *weigh* each choice slowly, moving sticky notes back and forth. I offered to help. He handed me a pen and said, 'Write down what matters most to you about this place.'
weigh:2.cnHint: 店长把两个方案摆在柜台上，仔细____每一个决定。
weigh:2.hook: I held the pen for a long time before writing anything down.
weigh:2.line: 'We have to *weigh* every detail before the new branch is set.'

alive:2.en: At 3 a.m. the new branch building was dark and empty, but the lights of our store made the whole corner glow. A delivery driver stopped his bike, looked from one building to the other, and smiled. 'Good to see this street feeling *alive* again,' he said, and rode on without buying a thing.
alive:2.cnHint: 深夜，新旧两家店让整条街重新____了起来。
alive:2.hook: The delivery driver's face looked oddly familiar in the lamplight.
alive:2.line: 'It is good to see this street feeling *alive* again at night.'

anyway:2.en: A folded note was taped to the back door when I arrived for my night shift. It said the Manager had gone to check the new branch location and would be late. I did not know what to do at first, but I unlocked the store and started the coffee machine *anyway*, because customers would arrive soon.
anyway:2.cnHint: 我在后门发现了一张纸条，____还是开始了准备工作。
anyway:2.hook: But the note had no date, and the door was already unlocked.
anyway:2.line: 'I was not sure it was the right time, but I came *anyway*.'

arise:2.en: The Manager had sent a floor plan of the new branch by post. I spread it on the counter and studied it during a quiet hour. One question did *arise* as I looked at the tiny back room: where would the staff eat? There was no space marked for a break area at all.
arise:2.cnHint: 我研究新分店的平面图时，一个问题____了。
arise:2.hook: Then I noticed a second floor plan folded inside the first, for a building I did not recognise.
arise:2.line: 'Problems will *arise* if we ignore the break room.'

besides:2.en: Tang slid a handwritten list across the counter just before dawn. It named every item the new branch would need on opening day: cups, bags, price tags, a spare key. *Besides* all that, she had added one extra line at the bottom in smaller writing, underlined twice, that I could not quite read.
besides:2.cnHint: 阿糖交来了新分店的物品清单，____还有一行我看不清的字。
besides:2.hook: She took the list back before I could lean in closer.
besides:2.line: 'We need the usual supplies, and *besides*, something I have not told you yet.'

certainly:2.en: A regular customer noticed the new branch address printed on our paper bags and asked if it would carry the same spicy rice crackers. I said I was not sure. She looked at me steadily.
