'The Manager will *certainly* stock them,' she said, as if she knew something I did not, then paid and left without another word.
certainly:2.cnHint: 一位常客看到新分店的地址后，用肯定的语气说了一句话。
certainly:2.hook: She had paid the exact amount before I even told her the total.
certainly:2.line: 'The Manager will *certainly* stock them there too.'

challenging:2.en: Lin dropped by near midnight carrying a rolled-up poster for his own new shop, which was opening two streets away from our branch. He grinned and said competing in the same small area would be *challenging* for both of us. He left the poster on the counter by mistake, or maybe not by mistake at all.
challenging:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林顺道来访，说在同一片区竞争是件____的事，但他忘了拿走他的海报。
challenging:2.hook: The poster showed our branch address, not his.
challenging:2.line: 'Keeping up with each other will be *challenging*, do you not think?'

circumstance:2.en: The Manager called from the new branch site just after two in the morning. The landlord had changed the lease terms at the last moment. Under this *circumstance*, she said, calmly and without anger, we would need to delay the opening by at least a week. Then she asked if the milk delivery had arrived yet.
circumstance:2.cnHint: 店长打来电话，说在这种____下，新店开业要推迟了。
circumstance:2.hook: The milk had arrived, but it was addressed to the new branch, not ours.
circumstance:2.line: 'Under this *circumstance*, we need to stay calm and wait.'

enrich:2.en: The Manager had pinned a short notice near the time clock: the new branch would trial a small reading corner with free magazines. She wrote that the idea was to *enrich* the experience for customers who stopped in during late hours and needed somewhere calm to sit for a while. I read the notice three times.
enrich:2.cnHint: 店长的公告说，阅读角是为了____深夜顾客的体验。
enrich:2.hook: The last line asked for a volunteer to manage the corner on night shifts.
enrich:2.line: 'A little reading corner will *enrich* the time people spend here.'

facilitate:2.en: A sealed envelope arrived at the store addressed to the Manager. Inside was a floor plan of the new branch location. 'This map will *facilitate* the whole move,' he said, spreading it across the counter. Tang and I leaned in, tracing the little rooms with our fingers.
facilitate:2.cnHint: 店长收到一个信封，里面的东西将____整个搬迁过程。
facilitate:2.hook: But one room on the plan had no label at all.
facilitate:2.line: 'This map will *facilitate* the whole move,' the Manager said quietly.

insight:2.en: Tang found an old notebook wedged behind the storage shelf. Page after page held the previous clerk's notes on every regular customer — their usual orders, their moods, their habits. 'Real *insight* into the people here,' Tang whispered, turning the yellowed pages with care.
insight:2.cnHint: 唐在货架后发现了一本旧笔记本，里面藏着对老顾客的____。
insight:2.hook: The last entry was dated the night the old clerk disappeared.
insight:2.line: Tang murmured, 'This notebook gives real *insight* into everyone here.'

preparation:2.en: I discovered a handwritten checklist taped inside the stock-room door. It listed every step for opening the new branch: cleaning, stocking, signing. The Manager called it his *preparation* guide, built from ten years of small mistakes. I copied it into my own notebook word by word.
preparation:2.cnHint: 我在库房门后发现了店长多年积累的开店____清单。
preparation:2.hook: Step seven was crossed out and rewritten three times.
preparation:2.line: 'This is my *preparation* guide,' the Manager said, 'every word counts.'

separate:2.en: While restocking the drinks fridge at the new branch site, I noticed the shelves were split into two halves with a thin metal divider. The Manager explained that hot and cold snacks must stay *separate* to keep the right temperature. A small detail, but it changed how the whole space felt.
separate:2.cnHint: 我注意到新分店的货架被分成两半，冷热食品必须____放置。
separate:2.hook: Lin arrived and stared at the divider without saying a word.
separate:2.line: 'Hot and cold must stay *separate*,' the Manager said firmly.

tie:2.en: On the stockroom table I found a navy *tie* folded inside a paper bag with a note attached. The note read: 'For the opening day — look sharp.' The handwriting was not the Manager's. Tang picked it up and held it to the light, turning it slowly.
tie:2.cnHint: 我在库房桌上发现了一条____，附着一张神秘的便条。
tie:2.hook: Nobody in our store ever wore a tie to work.
tie:2.line: Tang held it up and said, 'Someone really wants us to wear a *tie*.'

jam:2.en: I pulled a crate from the back corner and found twelve jars of home-made strawberry *jam*, each sealed with a red cloth cap and a handwritten label. No delivery note, no sender's name. The Manager frowned and said nobody had ordered them. They smelled wonderful, though.
jam:2.cnHint: 我在角落发现了十二罐没有来源的手工草莓____。
jam:2.hook: One jar had a tiny folded note pressed under its lid.
jam:2.line: 'Nobody ordered this *jam*,' the Manager said, picking up a jar slowly.

supermarket:2.en: Tucked under the new branch's counter I found a crumpled flyer from the big *supermarket* two streets away. Someone had circled its opening hours in red pen and scrawled 'competition?' across the top. The Manager smoothed it flat and pinned it to the wall without a word.
supermarket:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现了附近____的传单，上面有人用红笔写了一个问题。
supermarket:2.hook: The circled hours matched our quietest shift exactly.
supermarket:2.line: 'Why is a *supermarket* flyer hidden under our counter?' I asked.

debate:2.en: Tang and I found two sets of store-layout sketches left on the back table, each by a different hand. One was neat, the other covered in crossing-out. There was clearly a long *debate* between two people about where the counter should go. We could not tell who had won.
debate:2.cnHint: 唐和我发现了两份关于新店布局的草图，显示出一场激烈的____痕迹。
debate:2.hook: The Manager went pale the moment he saw the sketches.
debate:2.line: Tang said, 'Looks like someone had a serious *debate* about this counter.'

egg:2.en: Behind the back shelf, I found a small basket with a single *egg* sitting inside it. A note was taped to the basket: 'Keep this safe. Do not sell.' The Manager's handwriting. I had no idea why one egg needed guarding, but I put it back carefully.
egg:2.cnHint: 我在货架后面发现了一个篮子，里面放着一颗被特别叮嘱保管的____。
egg:2.hook: Then I noticed the egg was ever so slightly warm.
egg:2.line: 'That *egg* is not for sale — not for any price,' the Manager said.

hire:2.en: A folded letter sat on the back counter, addressed to the Manager. I should not have read it, but the words 'new *hire*' caught my eye. Someone was being brought on for the second branch. The name on the letter made me set it down very quickly.
hire:2.cnHint: 柜台上有一封信，提到新分店即将有新的____加入，那个名字让我大吃一惊。
hire:2.hook: The name on that letter was someone I already knew.
hire:2.line: 'The new *hire* starts next Monday,' Tang told me quietly.

aid:2.en: I was struggling to carry four heavy boxes toward the stock room when Lin appeared in the doorway. Without a word, Lin took two boxes from my arms. That small act of *aid* surprised me, since Lin and I had not exactly been friendly all week.
aid:2.cnHint: 当我搬着沉重的箱子时，隔壁咖啡店的林给予了我意外的____，让我重新看待这个人。
aid:2.hook: Lin glanced back once, as if expecting me to ask a question.
aid:2.line: 'I don't need praise — I just offer *aid* when it matters,' Lin said.

bill:2.en: I was tidying the noticeboard in the staff room when a folded *bill* fell out from behind a pinned note. It was a large one. On the back, someone had written a single address in pencil — the address of the new branch location.
bill:2.cnHint: 我在员工室的公告栏后面发现了一张夹着地址的____，那个地址正是新分店所在地。
bill:2.hook: The pencil writing was still fresh.
bill:2.line: 'Someone left this *bill* hidden here — and I want to know who,' said the Manager.

paint:2.en: The back door of the store led to a narrow alley. I stepped out for air and found Tang crouching beside the wall, using a small brush to *paint* a tiny fish near the base of the bricks. Tang looked up, calm as anything, and simply said it was a good-luck sign for the new branch.
paint:2.cnHint: 阿糖在小巷的墙根处____了一条小鱼，说这是为新分店祈福的记号。
paint:2.hook: But the fish looked exactly like a mark I had seen at the rival shop.
paint:2.line: 'I always *paint* something small when a new place opens,' Tang said softly.

bean:2.en: Restocking the shelves at midnight, I found one tin had been opened and then resealed with tape. Inside, instead of the usual dried *bean* mix, there was a rolled-up note. I smoothed it out under the shelf light and read three words: 'Check the freezer.'
bean:2.cnHint: 我打开一个重新封好的罐子，里面藏着一张纸条，而不是该有的____。
bean:2.hook: Whatever was in the freezer, someone wanted only me to find it.
bean:2.line: 'There was a note inside the *bean* tin — this is not normal,' I whispered to Tang.

birthday:2.en: Tucked under the register I found a small card with 'Happy *Birthday*' printed on the front. Inside, the Manager had written a short message and a date — three days from now. There was no name on it. The card was still sealed, waiting for someone who had not yet arrived.
birthday:2.cnHint: 收银台下藏着一张未送出的____贺卡，收信人的名字一栏空着。
birthday:2.hook: Three days was not long, but the date matched something else entirely.
birthday:2.line: 'A *birthday* card with no name — who is it even for?' I asked the Manager.

flight:2.en: A customer left a printed *flight* confirmation on the counter and rushed out before I could call after them. The destination was a city two hours away — the same city where the Manager had mentioned opening the new branch. The departure time was tomorrow morning.
flight:2.cnHint: 一位顾客遗忘了一张____确认单，目的地正是新分店所在的城市。
flight:2.hook: The passenger name on the confirmation was the Manager's.
flight:2.line: 'This *flight* leaves at six — someone is in a real hurry,' Tang murmured.

housing:2.en: The Manager slid a folded map across the counter. 'The new branch needs staff who can live nearby,' he said. He had circled three areas in red pen. 'Check the *housing* in each zone — cheap rent keeps good workers happy.' I studied the map, wondering which circle held my future.
housing:2.cnHint: 店长给我看地图，让我了解新分店附近的____情况。
housing:2.hook: One circled area had a question mark no one explained.
housing:2.line: The *housing* near the new branch is cheaper than you think.

behaviour:2.en: Tang noticed something odd on the security screen. A man in a yellow jacket had visited the drink fridge four times without buying anything. 'Watch his *behaviour*,' Tang whispered, nudging me. 'Last week someone like him turned out to be a location scout for a rival store.' The man finally bought one bottle of water.
behaviour:2.cnHint: 阿糖让我注意一个可疑顾客的____，怀疑他另有目的。
behaviour:2.hook: The yellow jacket man photographed the shelves before leaving.
behaviour:2.line: His *behaviour* near the fridges is making me nervous.

husband:2.en: A woman rushed in just before two in the morning, cheeks red from the cold. She bought a hot drink and two rice balls. 'My *husband* is outside measuring the empty shop next door,' she said with a tired smile. 'He wants to open something. I told him midnight is not office hours.' She shook her head fondly.
husband:2.cnHint: 一位女顾客的____深夜在外面勘察隔壁空铺，让她又好笑又无奈。
husband:2.hook: The empty shop next door had been on the market for years.
husband:2.line: My *husband* has been staring at that empty shop all night.

tourist:2.en: A young man with a large backpack came in asking for a local bus map. He looked lost and happy at the same time. 'I am a *tourist*,' he explained, spreading his arms at the snack wall, 'but also I am hungry.' He bought six things I could not name and asked me to write down their flavours in English for his notes.
tourist:2.cnHint: 一位____走进来，买了很多零食，还请我帮他记下口味的英文名称。
tourist:2.hook: His notebook already held the names of forty other stores.
tourist:2.line: As a *tourist*, I try every local snack I can find.

agent:2.en: A neat woman in a grey coat came in twice in one hour, each time studying the view from our window. On her second visit she bought coffee and left a card on the counter. She was a property *agent*. The Manager picked up the card slowly and said nothing, but I saw him nod just once, very quietly.
agent:2.cnHint: 一位房产____两次进店，似乎在考察位置，还留下了名片。
agent:2.hook: The Manager locked the card in the drawer under the register.
agent:2.line: I am a property *agent* — I have news about the shop next door.

cash:2.en: Lin came in from the street looking pale. 'The landlord of the new site wants three months up front,' she said, dropping into a chair by the hot-food shelf. 'All in *cash*.' She pressed her palms together. 'Who carries that much cash at a signing meeting?' The Manager set a warm can of tea in front of her and said, 'We do, now.'
cash:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林得知新店房东要求提前付____，感到十分为难。
cash:2.hook: The Manager had already counted the money that morning.
cash:2.line: The landlord wants everything in *cash* before we sign anything.

competition:2.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn chart on the counter. Three other stores sat within five minutes of the planned new branch. 'This is real *competition*,' she said, tapping each dot. 'Two of them close at midnight. One sells hot food.' She looked at me. 'So what do we do that none of them do?' I looked at the chat and thought hard.
competition:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林分析新分店周边的____形势，想找出我们独特的优势。
competition:2.hook: One dot on the chart had a name that made the Manager go still.
competition:2.line: The *competition* around the new branch is stronger than we expected.

farmer:2.en: Just after dawn a quiet old man came in carrying a cloth bag of small sweet potatoes. He set it gently on the counter. 'I am a *farmer* from the village past the ring road,' he said. 'I heard the new shop will open near my land. I brought these as a greeting.' The Manager accepted the bag with both hands.
farmer:2.cnHint: 一位____清早送来自种的红薯，作为对新分店的欢迎礼物。
farmer:2.hook: The sweet potatoes were unlike any variety sold in the city.
farmer:2.line: I am a *farmer* — my land sits right behind your new branch.

collection:2.en: A delivery driver left a heavy box at the back door with a note: 'For the manager.' Inside, wrapped in old newspaper, sat a *collection* of tiny ceramic cats — twenty at least, each one painted a different colour. I lined them up on the shelf above the tea kettles and waited.
collection:2.cnHint: 送货司机留下一箱东西，里面是店长的____，我把它们摆在了货架上。
collection:2.hook: By midnight, one ceramic cat had somehow moved to a different shelf.
collection:2.line: 'This *collection* has been growing for fifteen years,' the Manager said quietly.

depression:2.en: Tang found me sitting on an empty crate behind the store at three in the morning, staring at the dark street. 'First week?' he asked. I nodded. He handed me a warm meat bun without another word. That small act pulled me out of a *depression* I had not even named yet.
depression:2.cnHint: 唐发现我一个人坐在外面，用一个包子把我从____中拉了出来。
depression:2.hook: Tang never explained how he always knew when someone needed that bun.
depression:2.line: 'A little *depression* at three a.m. is basically the store uniform,' Tang said.

foot:2.en: The new branch was one street over, and I walked there on my break to have a look. It was bigger, brighter, and had a coffee machine the size of a small car. Standing at the door, I measured the distance back to our store — exactly one *foot* of pavement for every year the Manager had worked.
foot:2.cnHint: 我步行去看新分店，用____来丈量两家店之间的距离。
foot:2.hook: A handwritten sign on the new door read: 'Opening soon — same family, new address.'
foot:2.line: 'Every *foot* of this street has a story,' the Manager said, looking down.

graduate:2.en: A young woman came in just after midnight, still wearing a gown and a flat cap. She bought a single can of cold coffee, tapped it twice like a toast, and drank it at the counter alone. 'Fresh *graduate*,' Tang whispered to me. 'They all come here on the big night.'
graduate:2.cnHint: 一位刚刚完成学业的____深夜独自来店里买咖啡庆祝。
graduate:2.hook: She left her graduation cap on the counter and never came back for it.
graduate:2.line: 'Every *graduate* needs one quiet moment before the noise starts,' she said.

intake:2.en: The Manager was reviewing a health report at the counter, frowning at a column of numbers. 'Salt,' he muttered, circling something with a red pen. He then looked up at the shelf of instant noodles and sighed. A customer's daily *intake* was apparently the talk of some clinic nearby, and that customer was a regular.
intake:2.cnHint: 店长看着一份健康报告皱眉，某位常客的____引起了附近诊所的关注。
intake:2.hook: The regular walked in right then, reaching for his usual extra-salty pack.
intake:2.line: 'Your daily *intake* is not a personal record to break,' the Manager said firmly.

screen:2.en: A thin folding *screen* stood in the far corner of the store — old, painted with bamboo — and I had never noticed it before. Behind it was a small table, two chairs, and a plug socket. Tang said the Manager sometimes let people sit there to think. No purchase required.
screen:2.cnHint: 店里角落摆着一扇____，后面藏着一张桌子和两把椅子供人静思。
screen:2.hook: Tonight, someone had left a sealed letter on that little table.
screen:2.line: 'The *screen* is there so people can disappear for a while,' the Manager said.

chair:2.en: Lin arrived from the new branch carrying a flat box under one arm. Inside was a folding *chair* — a gift for the opening, she said, for whoever stood longest on the first shift. She set it against the wall with a card that read: 'Sit when you need to. No one is watching.' I liked her immediately.
chair:2.cnHint: 林从新分店带来一把____作为礼物，卡片上写着让人放松的话。
chair:2.hook: The Manager read the card twice, then quietly sat down for the first time all week.
chair:2.line: 'A good *chair* is a way of saying someone matters,' Lin told me, smiling.

court:2.en: Behind the new branch there was a small basketball *court*, cracked and faded, with one bent hoop. Three kids played there every night, and they always came in for water at exactly ten. The Manager had quietly kept the water cold for them all summer, telling no one and charging nothing.
court:2.cnHint: 新分店后面有一块____，店长默默为每晚在那里打球的孩子们免费备水。
court:2.hook: Tonight the three kids came in at ten — and brought a fourth, carrying a mop.
court:2.line: 'That *court* has been here longer than the store,' the Manager said softly.

female:2.en: A delivery box arrived after midnight, addressed to the store. Inside, wrapped in soft cloth, sat a small cage. A tiny *female* rabbit blinked up at me, a note tied to the bars: 'Please keep her safe until I return.' I had no idea who sent her.
female:2.cnHint: 深夜送来一个箱子，里面是一只____兔子，还附有一张字条。
female:2.hook: The note was signed with only a small paw print.
female:2.line: 'She is a *female*, so she needs extra care tonight.'

holiday:2.en: The Manager taped a new sign on the door before dawn: 'Open every *holiday*, no exceptions.' Tang groaned and rested his head on the counter. Outside, families were already walking past with balloons, laughing. I quietly refilled the hot-drink machine and said nothing.
holiday:2.cnHint: 店长贴出告示，说____也照常营业，同事唉声叹气。
holiday:2.hook: Then Tang found a second, hidden note behind the first sign.
holiday:2.line: 'Even on a *holiday*, this store never sleeps,' Tang muttered.

pain:2.en: Lin walked in just before three in the morning, limping slightly. She set a folder on the counter and asked for a hot pack. 'Took *pain* to get these numbers right,' she said, sliding the folder toward me. It was a full sales report — for a second store location.
pain:2.cnHint: 林深夜进店，说整理好那份文件费了不少____，顺手把它放在柜台上。
pain:2.hook: The address on the report was only two streets away.
pain:2.line: 'It was real *pain* putting this together, but it had to be done.'

player:2.en: A teenage boy came in for a bottle of water, still in his sports kit. He was a basketball *player* from the school nearby — I recognised the team logo. He left a crumpled paper on the counter by mistake. Unfolding it, I found a hand-drawn map of the neighbourhood.
player:2.cnHint: 一名篮球____买水后，不小心把一张手绘地图落在了柜台上。
player:2.hook: One spot on the map was circled in red ink.
player:2.line: 'I'm just a *player*, but even I heard about the new place.'

production:2.en: The Manager called me into the back room and pointed at stacked boxes. 'New *production* line from our supplier,' he said proudly. Each box carried a logo I had never seen before. He smiled and told me to stack them neatly. One box at the bottom felt much heavier than the rest.
production:2.cnHint: 店长展示了一批新____，但其中有一箱异常地重。
production:2.hook: The heaviest box had no label at all.
production:2.line: 'This *production* just arrived — handle every box with care.'

secure:2.en: Before his shift ended, Tang tested every window and checked the back lock twice. 'Got to keep the place *secure*,' he said, handing me a small key on a red cord. I did not know what it opened. He pointed at a drawer under the register and then walked out without another word.
secure:2.cnHint: 同事反复检查门窗，说要确保店铺____，然后递给我一把不知用途的小钥匙。
secure:2.hook: The drawer the key opened was already slightly ajar.
secure:2.line: 'Always make sure the store is *secure* before you sit down.'

audience:2.en: At two in the morning the Manager video-called someone and propped his phone on the counter. 'There is an *audience* waiting,' he told me, looking nervous. Faces on the screen leaned closer. He cleared his throat and began describing a new store plan in careful English. I stood very still and listened.
audience:2.cnHint: 店长深夜视频通话，说屏幕那头有一群____正等着听他的新开店计划。
audience:2.hook: One face in the call was Lin, sitting in a brightly lit office.
audience:2.line: 'We have an *audience* on the call — please speak clearly.'

borrow:2.en: Lin knocked on the glass door at half past one, holding nothing but her phone. 'Can I *borrow* your pen and a sheet of paper?' she asked, stepping inside. She wrote quickly, folded the paper, and slid it into an envelope she pulled from her coat. She left before I could ask any questions.
borrow:2.cnHint: 林深夜敲门，说想____一支笔和纸，写完就匆匆离开了。
borrow:2.hook: The envelope was addressed to the Manager, marked 'urgent'.
borrow:2.line: 'I only need to *borrow* it for one minute, I promise.'

burn:2.en: The Manager left a note taped to the coffee machine: 'Handle with care.' I learned why at 2 a.m. when I grabbed the steam pipe without a cloth and felt a sharp *burn* across my palm. I ran cold water over it, then noticed a second note underneath the first: 'Sorry — I forgot to warn the last clerk too.'
burn:2.cnHint: 新店员不小心碰到蒸汽管，手掌留下了____，发现店长早知道这个危险。
burn:2.hook: The last clerk had quit after only one week.
burn:2.line: 'That *burn* on your hand — yeah, we've all been there.'

cook:2.en: A regular came in just before 3 a.m. carrying a small pot and a hopeful look. 'Can I use your back counter?' he asked. 'I like to *cook* ramen here — my kitchen fan broke and the smell drives my wife crazy.' The Manager had apparently said yes for two years. I had no idea what the rules even were in this store.
cook:2.cnHint: 一位常客在店里____方便面，这竟然是店长默许两年的惯例。
cook:2.hook: His wife showed up ten minutes later, looking less than crazy.
cook:2.line: 'I just need to *cook* one small thing — it won't take long, I promise.'

corporate:2.en: A suited woman slid a folder across the counter at midnight. 'We're scouting this block for a *corporate* expansion,' she said with a polished smile. 'How is business here?' I stared at her, then at the hand-drawn shelf labels and the Manager's lucky cat with the broken arm. I said business was fine.
corporate:2.cnHint: 一位女士深夜来店里做____扩张调查，店员望着歪歪扭扭的手写标签，平静回答生意很好。
corporate:2.hook: She wrote something in the folder and did not show me what it was.
corporate:2.line: 'Our *corporate* team has had an eye on this corner for months.'

dangerous:2.en: Tang warned me on my first night: 'The mop bucket near the freezer is *dangerous* — the wheel is broken and it slides into people.' I nodded and forgot completely. By 4 a.m. I had knocked it into three customers and myself. Tang watched each time from behind the snack shelf with a cup of tea and a calm expression.
dangerous:2.cnHint: 同事提醒新店员拖把桶____，但店员完全忘记，一晚上撞倒了好几次。
dangerous:2.hook: Tang had been waiting for someone new to watch this happen.
dangerous:2.line: 'That broken wheel makes the whole thing *dangerous* — trust me on this one.'

debt:2.en: A quiet student came in every night for a small coffee and always paid with exact coins. One night he was two coins short and turned red. 'I have a *debt* to you,' he said seriously, placing an IOU note on the counter. He came back the next night with the coins and a small bag of homemade cookies. The note had already meant more than the money.
debt:2.cnHint: 一位学生少带了零钱，郑重地说自己欠了店员一笔____，第二天还钱时还带来了饼干。
debt:2.hook: His handwriting on the IOU note was surprisingly beautiful.
debt:2.line: 'I don't like having any *debt*, even a small one — here are the coins.'

discipline:2.en: The Manager ran the stockroom with unusual *discipline*: every item faced front, every label aligned, every box dated in red pen. I spent my first hour trying to match it perfectly. When he arrived at dawn and saw my work, he nodded once — which Tang later told me was the highest praise he had ever given a new clerk.
discipline:2.cnHint: 店长用严格的____管理仓库，新店员努力做到完美，换来了店长最高级别的夸奖——点一下头。
discipline:2.hook: Tang had worked here three years and never received that nod.
discipline:2.line: 'Real *discipline* in the stockroom saves you an hour every single week.'

error:2.en: I scanned a bottle of juice twice by *error* and charged a customer double. She noticed before I did, pulled up the receipt on her phone, and showed me with a kind smile. I fixed it and apologized three times. She said it was fine and came back the next night — this time checking her receipt at the counter before she left.
error:2.cnHint: 店员误操作多收了顾客的钱，顾客温和地指出了这个____，第二天还是回来了。
error:2.hook: She always checked her receipt after that, without fail.
error:2.line: 'It was just a small *error* — these things happen on the night shift.'

gym:2.en: A man came in at 5 a.m. soaked in sweat, heading home from the all-night *gym* two streets over. He bought three bananas, a bottle of water, and one small chocolate bar, then stared at the chocolate for a moment. 'Don't tell the gym,' he said. I promised. He came back the next morning with the same look on his face.
gym:2.cnHint: 一位顾客从深夜____回来，买了健康食品，又悄悄买了巧克力，请店员保密。
gym:2.hook: He had clearly been having this same argument with himself for weeks.
gym:2.line: 'I just came from the *gym*, so I think I've earned this chocolate bar.'

mile:2.en: A folded note appeared under the back-room door. I opened it and read: 'The new branch is almost a *mile* away — too far for me to walk at night.' The handwriting looked familiar, but no name was signed. I stared at the map on the wall and started counting blocks.
mile:2.cnHint: 一张没有署名的纸条出现在后室门缝里，说新分店离这儿太____了。
mile:2.hook: Only one person here knew my habit of checking that door.
mile:2.line: 'That new place is a full *mile* away — who decided that?'

movement:2.en: Late at night I noticed a shadow through the front window. A slow, careful *movement* behind the magazine rack — someone was reading without paying. I walked over quietly and found a small boy hiding between the shelves, eyes wide, pretending to be a display stand.
movement:2.cnHint: 我在杂志架后面发现了一个可疑的____，没想到藏着个小孩。
movement:2.hook: The boy pressed a crumpled receipt into my hand and ran.
movement:2.line: 'I saw that *movement* behind the shelf — what are you doing back there?'

party:2.en: Tang waved a bright flyer at me: 'Branch opening *party* this Saturday.' Someone had drawn little balloons on the corners. The Manager had not mentioned a party to me. I checked the staff board — my name was not on the volunteer list, yet my face was on the poster.
party:2.cnHint: 同事拿来一张传单，说新分店要办开业____，但我的名字竟然没被列进去。
party:2.hook: My photo on that poster was taken six months before I was hired.
party:2.line: 'Why is your face on the *party* poster if nobody told you?'

rescue:2.en: The delivery elevator jammed between floors just before dawn. Inside it: three boxes of fresh bread for the new branch's opening day. I called Tang, who called the Manager, and we all stood staring up at the ceiling until the repairman arrived for the *rescue* forty minutes later.
rescue:2.cnHint: 送货电梯卡住了，装着新分店开业面包的箱子需要____。
rescue:2.hook: The repairman opened the doors and said the bread was already gone.
rescue:2.line: 'Good thing I called for the *rescue* — that bread is worth more than my shift pay.'

writing:2.en: I found a torn notebook page taped to the cold drinks fridge. The *writing* on it said: 'Do not stock the green tea on shelf B — that shelf belongs to the new branch's test display.' Nobody I asked knew who had put it there or when the test display had been agreed.
writing:2.cnHint: 冰柜上贴着一张字条，____内容让我对新分店的安排感到困惑。
writing:2.hook: The tape was still warm when I pulled the note free.
writing:2.line: 'Whose *writing* is this? It is not the Manager's hand at all.'

bite:2.en: Lin dropped a small paper bag on the counter. 'Try one,' she said. Inside were samples from the bakery supplier for the new branch — soft rolls the size of a coin. I took a *bite* and immediately understood why the Manager had been smiling all week. They were very, very good.
bite:2.cnHint: 竞争对手带来了新分店供应商的试吃品，我____了一口后明白了一切。
bite:2.hook: Lin watched my face and wrote something down without a word.
bite:2.line: 'Just one *bite* — tell me honestly what you think of it.'

capture:2.en: The Manager set up a small camera above the entrance of the new branch while I held the ladder. 'We need to *capture* every customer who comes in on opening day,' he said, meaning count them on video. I held the ladder steady and wondered if he also meant something more.
capture:2.cnHint: 店长在新分店门口架摄像头，说要____每一位进门的顾客。
capture:2.hook: That evening the camera showed a face neither of us recognised.
capture:2.line: 'We have to *capture* the crowd on opening day — every single face.'

cope:2.en: Opening day at the new branch was tomorrow, and the Manager asked me to cover both stores alone for one hour at noon. 'Can you *cope*?' he asked. I looked at the map — nearly a mile between them — and at the clock, and said yes before my brain could say no.
cope:2.cnHint: 店长问我能否独自____同时照看两家店铺一小时。
cope:2.hook: At noon a customer walked into one store, then the other, within minutes.
cope:2.line: 'I need to know — can you really *cope* with both stores alone?'

salary:2.en: The Manager slid a small envelope across the back-room table. 'Your first *salary*,' he said, looking almost proud. I opened it — the amount was modest, barely enough for rent — but a handwritten note inside said the new branch would need a shift leader. My hands went still.
salary:2.cnHint: 店长把第一份____递给我，信封里还夹着一张意味深长的便条。
salary:2.hook: The note had no signature, only a question mark.
salary:2.line: 'Your *salary* goes up the day the new branch opens.'

shopping:2.en: I found a crumpled list near the door — someone had left it behind. It read: shelf liner, price-gun tape, spare keys, good-luck charm. At the bottom, in red ink: FOR THE NEW STORE. So the *shopping* for the second branch had already begun, quietly, without a single meeting.
shopping:2.cnHint: 我在门口发现一张皱巴巴的____清单，上面写的东西都是新店要用的。
shopping:2.hook: The handwriting matched no one I knew.
shopping:2.line: 'This *shopping* list tells me the new store is closer than we think.'

tendency:2.en: Tang leaned on the mop and watched the late crowd drift in. 'There is a clear *tendency*,' she said, pointing to the corner table where three students had parked themselves with laptops three nights in a row. 'Give them an outlet, and they will come every night.' She smiled like she had already won something.
tendency:2.cnHint: 阿糖观察着顾客的____，觉得新店选址的答案已经很明显了。
tendency:2.hook: She pulled out a small notebook full of careful tallies.
tendency:2.line: 'The *tendency* is obvious — put the new branch near the campus.'

tough:2.en: The delivery arrived at two in the morning, twelve heavy boxes of stock for a trial run at the new site. Lin and I carried them up a narrow stairwell. My arms ached. 'First night is always the *toughest*,' Lin said, not even breathing hard. I decided then that I seriously needed to exercise more.
tough:2.cnHint: 深夜搬货很____，但隔壁咖啡店的林一点都不喘，让我暗暗惭愧。
tough:2.hook: Lin glanced at the last box and said nothing at all.
tough:2.line: '*Tough* work now means smooth opening day later.'

tour:2.en: The Manager led us on a quick *tour* of the empty unit two streets away. White walls, bare shelves, a window facing a bright bus stop. He walked slowly, tapping walls, checking corners. Neither Tang nor I spoke. The space felt full of something that had not happened yet.
tour:2.cnHint: 店长带我们去____了准备开新店的空铺位，大家都沉默着想象未来。
tour:2.hook: He stopped at the back wall and measured it with his hand.
tour:2.line: 'After the *tour*, tell me honestly — can you manage this place?'

wake:2.en: I almost missed it. In the *wake* of the long midnight rush, after the last customer left and the floor was finally clean, I noticed a folded paper tucked under the register. It was a rough floor plan, drawn in pencil, with one room circled and labelled MANAGER OFFICE — my name written lightly beside it.
wake:2.cnHint: 繁忙的夜班____过后，我在收银台下发现了一张标有我名字的平面图。
wake:2.hook: The pencil line under my name was not quite erased.
wake:2.line: 'In the *wake* of every big change, someone has to step up.'

annual:2.en: The Manager pinned a single sheet to the staff board. It was the *annual* review, one line per person. My line was short: 'Reliable. Observant. Ready for more.' Tang read it over my shoulder and raised both eyebrows. 'More,' she repeated softly, as if the word held a door she had been knocking on for a long time.
annual:2.cnHint: 年度____张贴出来，我那一行简短的评语让阿糖意味深长地重复了一个词。
annual:2.hook: The Manager had already left before either of us could ask.
annual:2.line: 'The *annual* review this year has a few surprises in it.'

charity:2.en: A regular — an older woman with a canvas bag — placed a small tin on the counter. 'For the new store opening,' she said. 'Put it toward something nice for the neighbourhood.' It was a *charity* collection tin, nearly full of coins. I had not known she even noticed us struggling to get the branch ready.
charity:2.cnHint: 一位常客把一个装满零钱的____捐款罐放在柜台上，说是为新店开业准备的。
charity:2.hook: She left before I could read the label on the tin.
charity:2.line: 'A little *charity* from the street can open a store better than money.'

strength:2.en: A folded note fell from a box of new stock the Manager had carried in from the delivery truck. I picked it up and read it aloud. It said the new branch would pull staff from our store. 'Do we have the *strength* to run two shops?' I asked myself, staring at the empty shelf.
strength:2.cnHint: 送货箱里藏着一张纸条，让我开始担心咱们店是否有足够的____应对新分店。
strength:2.hook: The Manager's face went still when he saw the note in my hand.
strength:2.line: 'I'm not sure we have the *strength* for this.'

survive:2.en: I found an old schedule pinned behind the back-room door, yellow and curling at the edges. Someone had written across it: 'Night shift will *survive* — just bring snacks.' It made me smile. Outside, a light rain began, and the store felt like a small warm island in the dark street.
survive:2.cnHint: 后室门后藏着一张旧排班表，上面有人留下的字迹，似乎在说夜班能____下去。
survive:2.hook: Below the writing was a name I did not recognise — yet.

touch:2.en: Inside a donated book box left near the counter, I found a handwritten card. It read: 'This store kept me company on hard nights. Thank you.' That small *touch* of kindness from a stranger stopped me mid-task. I set the card on the shelf beside the register where everyone could see it.
touch:2.cnHint: 捐书箱里藏着一张手写卡片，陌生人的一番话给了我小小的____。
touch:2.hook: Tang leaned over, read the card, and said nothing for a long moment.
touch:2.line: 'That little *touch* of kindness really got to me.'

trap:2.en: Lin pointed at a gap between two shelves where stock kept falling and getting lost. 'That corner is a *trap*,' she said flatly. I had already lost three energy drinks and a bag of peanuts there. We measured the space, then dragged a wooden board from the back room to close it off for good.
trap:2.cnHint: 林发现货架之间有个角落就像个____，货物老是掉进去不见了。
trap:2.hook: When we moved the board, something rolled out that had been missing for weeks.
trap:2.line: 'That corner is a *trap* — things vanish in there.'

tv:2.en: A small *tv* mounted high on the back wall of the stockroom flickered on by itself at two in the morning. I was alone, counting boxes of instant noodles. The screen showed only static. I reached up, pressed the power button, and the room went quiet again — except for the hum of the freezer.
tv:2.cnHint: 库房里一台旧____在深夜突然自己亮了，把我吓了一跳。
tv:2.hook: The Manager later said that tv had been unplugged for six months.
tv:2.line: 'Why did the *tv* turn on by itself?'

victim:2.en: A regular customer rushed in waving his phone. He had clicked a fake coupon link for our store and lost some points from his app account. 'I'm a *victim* of my own trust,' he groaned, dropping into the chair by the magazine rack. Tang quietly refilled his coffee while I called the Manager to sort it out.
victim:2.cnHint: 一位常客因为点了假优惠链接，成了网络欺骗的____，无奈地坐在杂志架旁。
victim:2.hook: The fake link had our store's name on it — someone had planned this carefully.
victim:2.line: 'I feel like a complete *victim* of my own trust.'

zone:2.en: The Manager taped a rough map of the new branch to the fridge door in the back room. He had divided the floor into sections with a red pen. 'Each *zone* will need its own clerk,' he said, tapping the map. I counted five zones. We currently had three people on staff. The numbers did not add up.
zone:2.cnHint: 店长把新分店的平面图贴在冰箱上，把店面划分成几个____，我越看越担心人手不够。
zone:2.hook: He circled one zone in red and looked straight at me.

afraid:2.en: Near the end of my shift I found a small envelope wedged under the counter, addressed to 'whoever opens next.' I hesitated. Tang saw me holding it and laughed softly. 'Are you *afraid* of an envelope?' she said. I opened it — inside was a hand-drawn map with a single question mark over the corner plot next door.
afraid:2.cnHint: 我在柜台下发现一个神秘信封，同事问我是不是____开，里面竟然有一张手绘地图。
afraid:2.hook: The corner plot on that map had been empty and locked for two years.
afraid:2.line: 'Are you really *afraid* of a little envelope?'

couple:2.en: A *couple* came in just before midnight, both carrying large paper bags and whispering to each other. They bought two cups of hot tea, spread a city map on the counter, and circled a spot far to the north. The Manager watched them from the back room, his expression unreadable.
couple:2.cnHint: 一对____深夜走进店里，在柜台上摊开地图，低声商量着什么。
couple:2.hook: The circled spot was exactly where our new branch would open.
couple:2.line: 'That *couple* has been in here three nights running,' the Manager said quietly.

definition:2.en: Tang slid a printed form across the counter to me. 'Read clause four,' she said. I read it twice. The *definition* of a 'branch manager' in the company handbook listed twelve duties, but the one that caught my eye was the last: 'responsible for all outcomes, good or bad.' I looked up slowly.
definition:2.cnHint: 同事让我读合同里对____的描述，最后一条让人心里一沉。
definition:2.hook: Tang was already watching my face for a reaction.
definition:2.line: 'The *definition* of this role is not what I expected,' I told Tang.

imagination:2.en: The back storeroom was plain and dusty, just shelves and boxes. But Lin walked in, stood still for a moment, and said the new branch could look completely different. 'Use your *imagination*,' she said, pointing at the bare walls. She pulled out a notebook filled with little drawings of a brighter, warmer space.
imagination:2.cnHint: 竞争对手走进仓库，指着空墙说要靠____把新店变得不一样。
imagination:2.hook: The last drawing in Lin's notebook looked nothing like a convenience store.
imagination:2.line: 'A little *imagination* is all it takes to change a place,' Lin said.

journey:2.en: I found an old photo tucked behind the staff notice board: the Manager, much younger, standing outside a tiny shop in what looked like a mountain town. On the back, in faded ink, someone had written: 'First stop of a long *journey*.' I put it back carefully and said nothing.
journey:2.cnHint: 我在公告板后找到一张旧照片，背面写着这是一段____的起点。
journey:2.hook: I wondered if the new branch was supposed to be the last stop.
journey:2.line: 'Every *journey* starts with one small, unremarkable shop,' the Manager once said.

nearby:2.en: Lin came in holding a printout of a street map and dropped it on the counter. 'There is another convenience store *nearby* — two blocks from our planned branch,' she said. Her finger pressed hard on the red dot. No one spoke. The Manager poured himself a coffee and stared at the map for a long time.
nearby:2.cnHint: 竞争对手带来消息：新店____已经有一家同类便利店。
nearby:2.hook: The red dot on the map had a name I recognised.
nearby:2.line: 'A rival store *nearby* changes everything about this plan,' Lin said firmly.

perspective:2.en: Tang climbed onto a step stool and took a photo of the store from up high. 'Come look at this,' she said, turning the screen toward me. From that *perspective*, the whole shop looked smaller and a little sad — the shelves too close together, the light uneven. 'This is what customers see,' Tang said simply.
perspective:2.cnHint: 同事站高拍了张照片，从那个____看，整家店显得局促又暗淡。
perspective:2.hook: She then showed me a second photo — of an empty room across town.
perspective:2.line: 'From this *perspective*, I think we have been doing things wrong,' Tang said.

requirement:2.en: The Manager pinned a short list to the staff board before dawn. At the top, underlined twice, was one *requirement* for anyone who wanted to run the new branch: one full year of night-shift experience. I counted the months on my fingers and came up one short. Tang pretended not to notice.
requirement:2.cnHint: 店长在公告栏贴出新店负责人的____，我默默数了数自己差了多少。
requirement:2.hook: Tang quietly crossed her own name off the list when she thought no one was looking.
requirement:2.line: 'The first *requirement* is simple, but it cuts out most of us,' Tang admitted.

signal:2.en: Just after three in the morning, the small light above the back-room phone began to blink — the old system the Manager used to *signal* that head office was calling. He had told me it never blinked unless the news was important. I straightened my uniform and waited by the door as he reached for the receiver.
signal:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，总部来电的指示灯突然亮起，用来____有重要消息。
signal:2.hook: The Manager's face went very still before he even said hello.
signal:2.line: 'That blinking light is meant to *signal* something none of us will like,' Tang whispered.

persuade:2.en: A note was taped to the back-room door. The Manager had written it himself: 'I need to *persuade* the landlord to give us the corner unit for the new branch. Meeting at noon. Do NOT disturb.' I read it twice, wondering why he looked so nervous when he left.
persuade:2.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了一张字条，说他要去____房东同意把角落铺位租给新分店。
persuade:2.hook: The landlord arrived at noon — but so did Lin.
persuade:2.line: 'I will *persuade* him with facts, not just hope.'

preference:2.en: The Manager left a printed form on the counter: BRANCH LOCATION SURVEY. Staff were asked to mark their *preference* — the busy shopping street or the quiet university road. Tang circled the university road without hesitating. I stared at the form for a long time before picking up my pen.
preference:2.cnHint: 店长要求员工填表，说明对新分店选址的____。
preference:2.hook: My answer and Tang's were completely opposite.
preference:2.line: 'My *preference* is the university road — students never sleep.'

reliable:2.en: Inside the stockroom I found an old notebook wedged behind the shelf. Every page held careful delivery records in small, neat handwriting. Someone had tracked every order for two years. The Manager, reading over my shoulder, said quietly that a *reliable* record like this was exactly what the new branch would need.
reliable:2.cnHint: 我在库房发现一本旧账本，店长说新分店需要这样____的记录。
reliable:2.hook: The last entry was dated the day the previous clerk disappeared.
reliable:2.line: 'A *reliable* record saves us from a hundred mistakes.'

suspect:2.en: A sealed envelope sat in the lost-and-found box, addressed to no one. I began to *suspect* it had something to do with the new branch plans when I noticed the Manager's handwriting on the back. Tang walked in, saw the envelope, and quietly stepped back out without a word.
suspect:2.cnHint: 我在失物箱里发现一个密封信封，开始____它与新分店计划有关。
suspect:2.hook: Tang's sudden exit made the envelope feel dangerous.
suspect:2.line: 'I *suspect* this letter was never meant to be found.'

yield:2.en: The Manager spread a map across the counter and pointed to two sites. The shopping-street location had higher foot traffic but would *yield* less space for storage. The university-road site was the opposite. He tapped the map and asked which trade-off I could live with. I had not expected him to ask me at all.
yield:2.cnHint: 店长对比两个选址，说购物街那个能____的储物空间更少。
yield:2.hook: My answer seemed to surprise even the Manager.
yield:2.line: 'More customers does not always *yield* more profit.'

abandon:2.en: Halfway through the night I found a half-finished floor plan tucked under the register — someone had sketched a layout for the new branch, then crossed it all out. It felt wrong to *abandon* a plan that had clearly taken hours. I smoothed the paper and left it on the Manager's desk.
abandon:2.cnHint: 我发现了一份被划掉的新分店平面草图，觉得不应该就这样____它。
abandon:2.hook: By morning the paper had vanished from the desk.
abandon:2.line: 'We should not *abandon* a good idea just because it is hard.'

anxious:2.en: Tang arrived an hour early, which never happened. She straightened every shelf twice and kept checking her phone. I asked if she was all right. She admitted she was *anxious* — the Manager was at the bank right now, deciding whether the second branch could open at all. The store felt very quiet after that.
anxious:2.cnHint: 唐提前到岗，一直看手机，因为对新分店能否开张感到____。
anxious:2.hook: Then the Manager's number lit up Tang's screen.
anxious:2.line: 'I am *anxious* because everything depends on one phone call.'

assess:2.en: The Manager came back from the new site carrying a clipboard. He sat at the corner table and began to *assess* the survey forms one by one, placing them in two neat piles. I watched from behind the counter as the pile marked 'NO' grew taller than the one marked 'YES'.
assess:2.cnHint: 店长带着调查表回来，开始逐一____员工对新分店选址的意见。
assess:2.hook: He looked up at me as he placed the very last form.
assess:2.line: 'Let me *assess* the results before anyone makes a decision.'

frame:2.en: Behind the counter, the Manager held up a dusty old photograph. 'This was our first store,' he said quietly. The wooden *frame* around it was cracked and dark with age, but the smiling faces inside were sharp and clear. He set it gently on the shelf above the register.
frame:2.cnHint: 店长拿出一张旧照片，把它放在收银台上方的架子上，照片的____已经裂开了。
frame:2.hook: But one face in the photo looked exactly like Lin.
frame:2.line: 'The *frame* is old, but what's inside still matters.'

friday:2.en: Every *Friday* just before midnight, a quiet man in a grey coat came in and bought the same thing: one rice ball and one small carton of milk. He never spoke. Tonight he paused at the door, turned back, and placed a folded note on the counter before walking away.
friday:2.cnHint: 每个____深夜，一位沉默的男士都会来买相同的东西，今晚他却留下了一张纸条。
friday:2.hook: The note had only four words: 'Check the back room.'
friday:2.line: 'He comes every *Friday*, never once missed a week.'

grain:2.en: Tang was counting bags of rice near the storeroom when one split open and scattered everywhere. 'Every single *grain* on the floor,' she sighed, dropping to her knees with a dustpan. I helped sweep, and under the last small pile we found a small metal key taped to the floor.
grain:2.cnHint: 阿糖在整理米袋时袋子破了，每一____米洒在地上，清扫时发现了一把藏着的钥匙。
grain:2.hook: Neither of us had ever seen that key before.
grain:2.line: 'Every *grain* off this floor before the Manager arrives, please.'

implication:2.en: Lin slid a printed page across the counter without saying a word. It was a lease agreement for the corner unit two blocks away — the exact spot the Manager had mentioned for the new branch. The *implication* was clear: Lin was planning to open a rival store there first and block the expansion.
implication:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林递来一份租约，其____很明显——他打算抢先在那个地点开一家竞争店。
implication:2.hook: The Manager's coffee cup went still in his hand.
implication:2.line: 'The *implication* of this document is hard to ignore, don't you think?'

incredible:2.en: The delivery driver dropped a crate of bottled water and stood staring at the stockroom wall. Someone had pinned a hand-drawn map on it — every convenience store in the district, with our shop circled in red. 'It's *incredible*,' he whispered. 'Whoever drew this spent weeks on it.' No one knew who had put it there.
incredible:2.cnHint: 司机在库房墙上发现了一幅精细的手绘地图，大家都觉得这____，却不知道是谁画的。
incredible:2.hook: Our store was the only one circled twice.
incredible:2.line: '*Incredible* — someone mapped every single store in the whole area.'

net:2.en: I was wiping down the back shelf when I noticed a small *net* bag hanging behind a row of canned goods, nearly invisible. Inside it were six small keys, each tagged with a number. Tang leaned over, eyes wide. 'Those numbers,' she said softly, 'match the locks on the new branch location.'
net:2.cnHint: 我在货架后面发现了一个小____袋，里面装着几把标有编号的钥匙，编号和新分店的锁对上了。
net:2.hook: Tang's hand was shaking as she reached for them.
net:2.line: 'Inside this little *net* bag — keys to the new place, I think.'

obtain:2.en: The Manager spread papers on the counter and tapped one page firmly. 'To open the new branch, we must *obtain* a separate business licence,' he explained. 'It takes three weeks minimum.' Tang and I exchanged a look. Three weeks felt fine. Then Lin walked in holding a manila envelope and smiled without speaking.
obtain:2.cnHint: 店长说开分店必须____一份独立的营业执照，至少需要三周，但隔壁咖啡店的林拿着一个信封笑着走了进来。
obtain:2.hook: Lin's envelope already had an official red stamp on it.
obtain:2.line: 'We need to *obtain* the licence before we can do anything else.'

pair:2.en: Tang pulled a small box from behind the register and opened it on the counter. Inside sat a *pair* of matching door signs — one for this store, one clearly made for a second location — both painted in the same faded green. 'The Manager ordered these months ago,' she said. 'He planned all of this quietly.'
pair:2.cnHint: 阿糖找到一个盒子，里面装着一____门牌，一块是现在这家店的，另一块显然是为新分店准备的。
pair:2.hook: The second sign already had an address painted on the back.
pair:2.line: 'A *pair* of signs — he was planning the new branch all along.'

beautiful:2.en: A folded note slipped under the back door read: 'The new branch will be *beautiful* — trust the plan.' I turned it over, looking for a name. Nothing. The Manager was already watching the security camera monitor with a small, private smile, as if he had been expecting exactly this.
beautiful:2.cnHint: 一张神秘纸条悄悄塞进了后门，店长看到后露出了意味深长的微笑。
beautiful:2.hook: But the handwriting matched no one I knew.
beautiful:2.line: 'It will be *beautiful*, I promise — just wait and see.'

combine:2.en: The Manager spread two maps across the counter: the old store layout and the new branch blueprint. 'We *combine* the storage room here with the staff lounge there,' he said, tapping both sheets at once. Tang leaned in, nodded slowly, then quietly took a photo with his phone.
combine:2.cnHint: 店长把两张图纸摊在柜台上，计划把两个空间____在一起，同事悄悄拍了张照片。
combine:2.hook: Tang sent that photo to someone before I could ask why.
combine:2.line: 'If we *combine* these two spaces, the new branch will have twice the room.'

complicated:2.en: The branch permit forms arrived in a thick envelope. I counted eleven pages of tiny print. 'Is it always this *complicated*?' I asked the Manager. He laughed softly. 'This is the simple version.' He pulled a second, thicker envelope from the drawer and set it beside the first without another word.
complicated:2.cnHint: 分店申请表格厚厚一叠，我问店长手续是不是总是这么____。
complicated:2.hook: The second envelope had a red stamp I did not recognise.
complicated:2.line: 'The paperwork is *complicated*, but every signature matters — do not skip one.'

crash:2.en: At two in the morning I heard a loud *crash* from the storage room at the back. I rushed over and found a whole shelf of boxed supplies on the floor, and in the middle of the mess, a single envelope addressed to the Manager — sealed, undamaged, as if it had been waiting there.
crash:2.cnHint: 凌晨两点，库房传来一声巨响，地上的乱堆里赫然躺着一封写给店长的信。
crash:2.hook: No one else had a key to that storage room.
crash:2.line: 'Did you hear that *crash*? Something in the back just fell over.'

creature:2.en: A small *creature* — some kind of grey cat — had slipped inside through the delivery hatch and curled up on top of a box of branch-opening flyers. It opened one eye, looked at me calmly, then went back to sleep. Tucked under its paw was a USB drive I had never seen before.
creature:2.cnHint: 一只小动物溜进了店里，睡在新分店的传单箱上，爪子下压着一个陌生的U盘。
creature:2.hook: The USB drive had no label, only a tiny red dot.
creature:2.line: 'Look — a little *creature* made itself at home on our flyers.'

crime:2.en: Lin slid a printout across the counter to me without a word. It was a news article: a convenience store chain fined for opening a branch too close to a school. 'Is that a *crime*?' I asked. Lin shrugged. 'Depends who you know.' Then she folded the page and tucked it into her jacket pocket.
crime:2.cnHint: 竞争对手递来一篇报道，讲某便利店因选址违规被罚款，暗示这可能是一种____。
crime:2.hook: Our new branch address was written in the margin.
crime:2.line: 'Ignoring the rules is not just a mistake — it is a *crime*.'

deeply:2.en: The Manager stared at the branch site photos for a long time without speaking. 'You care *deeply* about this one,' Tang said quietly from behind the coffee machine. The Manager did not turn around. He just nodded once and pinned the clearest photo to the board above the register, right at eye level.
deeply:2.cnHint: 店长久久凝视着分店选址的照片，同事说他对这件事____在意。
deeply:2.hook: That photo had a street corner I recognised from somewhere else.
deeply:2.line: 'I *deeply* believe this new branch will change everything for us.'

demonstrate:2.en: Tang set a small cardboard model on the counter — a tiny replica of the planned branch, complete with shelves and a miniature checkout desk. 'Let me *demonstrate* the customer flow,' he said, moving a coin slowly through the model like a person walking. The Manager watched in silence, arms folded, expression unreadable.
demonstrate:2.cnHint: 同事用硬纸板模型向店长____新分店的顾客动线，店长一言不发地看着。
demonstrate:2.hook: The Manager's eyes stopped at the model's back exit.
demonstrate:2.line: 'Allow me to *demonstrate* exactly how customers will move through the new space.'

behave:2.en: The Manager left a note on the back-room door before my first solo shift. It said: 'The microwave will *behave* perfectly as long as you press STOP before the timer hits zero. Do not ask why.' I pressed STOP. The microwave beeped once, almost politely. I decided not to ask why.
behave:2.cnHint: 店长留了一张便条，说微波炉只要操作得当就会乖乖____，但没有解释原因。
behave:2.hook: The note had a second line, crossed out in red ink.
behave:2.line: 'It will *behave* — just never let the timer reach zero.'

cent:2.en: A regular slid exact change across the counter at 2 a.m. — not a *cent* more, not a cent less. I counted it twice. Every coin was from a different year. He watched me stack them, nodded with great satisfaction, and walked out into the rain without an umbrella.
cent:2.cnHint: 一位常客深夜付款，一分不多一分不少，每枚硬币都是不同年份的____。
cent:2.hook: The oldest coin in the stack was dated forty years ago.
cent:2.line: 'Every *cent* is real — I have been saving them for this exact moment.'

commercial:2.en: Tang was stacking juice boxes when the store's little radio switched to a loud *commercial*. She froze, listened closely, then slowly turned to me with wide eyes. 'That is the Manager's voice,' she whispered. I listened. She was absolutely right.
commercial:2.cnHint: 收音机播放的____里传出了一个意外熟悉的声音，让唐大吃一惊。
commercial:2.hook: The Manager had never once mentioned being on the radio.
commercial:2.line: 'That *commercial* — I would know his voice anywhere, even at midnight.'

death:2.en: A man in a heavy coat came in and bought one candle, one box of matches, and a small cake. He set them on the counter and said, 'Today is the *death* anniversary of my old cat. I celebrate it every year.' He smiled. It was the warmest smile I had seen all night.
death:2.cnHint: 一位顾客买了蜡烛和蛋糕，说今天是他老猫____的纪念日。
death:2.hook: He mentioned the cat's name only once, very quietly, at the door.
death:2.line: 'On the *death* anniversary, I always buy this exact cake — he loved the smell.'

escape:2.en: Lin from the store across the street came in just before dawn, slipped behind our magazine rack, and crouched down. A moment later, two very loud neighbors walked past the window. Lin let out a long breath. 'The best *escape* route in the neighborhood,' she said, 'is your magazine section.'
escape:2.cnHint: 林躲进杂志架后面，把便利店当成____吵闹邻居的最佳藏身地。
escape:2.hook: Lin had clearly done this before — she knew exactly which shelf to crouch behind.
escape:2.line: 'Your magazine rack is the perfect *escape* — nobody ever looks back there.'

expose:2.en: I found a gap in the shelf paper near the back wall and pulled it back to *expose* a hand-drawn map of the whole store, dated six years ago. The layout was almost the same, except one room that no longer seemed to exist. Tang walked over, looked at it, and said nothing.
expose:2.cnHint: 我撕开货架的旧纸，____了一张六年前的手绘地图，上面有一个现在找不到的房间。
expose:2.hook: Tang's silence lasted exactly ten seconds — then she walked away fast.
expose:2.line: 'Do not *expose* that wall paper further — just leave it where you found it.'

floor:2.en: At 3 a.m. I heard a soft tap and looked down. A very old cat was sitting on the *floor* just inside the door, staring up at the snack shelf. I had no idea how it got in. It sniffed once at a bag of fish crackers, then sat back down and waited, as if it had done this many times before.
floor:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一只老猫悄悄坐在店里的____上，盯着零食货架等待着。
floor:2.hook: The cat knew exactly which shelf held the fish crackers.
floor:2.line: 'Every night it sits on the *floor* by that shelf — the Manager always pretends not to notice.'

foundation:2.en: The Manager pointed to a thin crack running along the back wall. 'That crack is older than the store,' he said proudly. 'It was here when we built on top of this spot. We left it because it is part of the *foundation* — you remove it, the whole building gets nervous.' He knocked on the wall twice, gently.
foundation:2.cnHint: 店长指着墙上的一条裂缝说，它是整栋楼____的一部分，动不得。
foundation:2.hook: The crack seemed slightly longer than it was in last week's photo on the wall.
foundation:2.line: 'Touch that crack and you touch the *foundation* — so we leave it alone.'

strike:2.en: A delivery notice was taped to the back door. The Manager read it twice and set it down slowly. The drivers were on *strike*, he explained, so our weekend supply of hot buns and milk tea would not arrive. The shelves looked thinner already, just from knowing.
strike:2.cnHint: 店长发现一张通知，说司机们正在____，周末补货要泡汤了。
strike:2.hook: Someone, though, had already emptied the last shelf of milk tea.
strike:2.line: 'The drivers are on *strike*, so we may run out by Sunday.'

television:2.en: Behind the lottery counter there was a small *television* no bigger than a cereal box, showing a late-night weather report nobody watched. I noticed it only because the screen flickered twice, went dark, and then showed a face I did not recognise — smiling straight at the camera.
television:2.cnHint: 收银台后面那台小____突然亮了，出现了一张陌生的笑脸。
television:2.hook: The plug, I then noticed, was not in the wall.
television:2.line: 'That *television* has been off for a month — or so we thought.'

youth:2.en: A group photo was tucked under the glass counter, next to the scratch cards. It showed the Manager looking much younger, standing with three laughing friends outside this very store. On the back someone had written: 'The best part of our *youth*, right here.' The handwriting was not his.
youth:2.cnHint: 柜台玻璃下有张老照片，背面写着这里是他们____最美好的时光，但字迹不是店长的。
youth:2.hook: One of those laughing friends walked in ten minutes later.
youth:2.line: 'We spent our whole *youth* dreaming this corner store into life.'

alter:2.en: Tang arrived for her shift and stopped in the doorway. The aisle layout had changed overnight — someone had moved the snack section two rows to the left. 'Did you *alter* the whole floor plan by yourself?' she asked me, eyebrows raised. I shook my head. Neither of us had.
alter:2.cnHint: 阿糖上班时发现货架布局被人____了，但我们俩都没动过它。
alter:2.hook: The security camera, it turned out, had recorded nothing after midnight.
alter:2.line: 'Who told you to *alter* the layout without asking anyone?'

approximately:2.en: A handwritten note fell out of the newspaper bundle when I cut the string open. It read: 'I left *approximately* three hundred yuan under the blue mat. Please keep it safe until Thursday.' There was no name, no phone number, and the blue mat was at the far end of aisle three.
approximately:2.cnHint: 报纸捆里掉出一张字条，说蓝色垫子下藏着____三百元，请帮忙保管到周四。
approximately:2.hook: Under the mat there was nothing but a key.
approximately:2.line: 'There is *approximately* three hundred yuan hidden here — please guard it.'

attractive:2.en: Lin came in during her break from the rival shop across the street. She set a small potted plant on our counter without a word. 'It makes the space more *attractive*,' she said, already heading for the door. The Manager stared at it for a long moment before checking whether it had a price tag.
attractive:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林悄悄在我们柜台摆了一盆植物，说让店里看起来更____，然后就走了。
attractive:2.hook: The plant had a tiny folded note tucked inside the soil.
attractive:2.line: 'A little green makes any counter more *attractive*, don't you think?'

bag:2.en: A woman rushed in at two in the morning and asked if anyone had handed in a cloth *bag*. Brown, she said, with a broken strap and a important letter inside. I checked under the counter, behind the drinks fridge, and along the window ledge. Then I found it — but the letter was already open.
bag:2.cnHint: 深夜有人来找落下的____，我找到了，但里面的信已经被人拆开过了。
bag:2.hook: The handwriting inside matched the note from the newspaper bundle.
bag:2.line: 'Has anyone brought in a brown *bag* with a letter inside?'

beat:2.en: The old radio on the top shelf picked up a late station, and a slow song filled the empty store. Tang tapped the counter in time, eyes half closed. 'Listen to that *beat*,' she said softly. Outside, a figure stood at the window, perfectly still, listening too — someone we had never seen before.
beat:2.cnHint: 阿糖跟着收音机的____打着节拍，窗外却站着一个从未见过的陌生人在静静聆听。
beat:2.hook: When Tang looked up, the figure was already gone.
beat:2.line: 'Listen to that *beat* — it sounds like the song my old neighbour used to hum.'

bottom:2.en: The Manager left a note at the *bottom* of the supply list on the back-room shelf. I almost missed it. In tiny letters it read: 'Check the left freezer — something important inside.' I opened the freezer door slowly, cold air rushing out, and found a sealed envelope marked 'New Branch Plan.'
bottom:2.cnHint: 店长在备货清单的____留了一张便条，里面藏着一个秘密信封。
bottom:2.hook: The envelope felt heavier than paper should ever feel.
bottom:2.line: 'I wrote it at the *bottom* so only a careful person would find it.'

breed:2.en: A woman came in carrying a small dog and asked if we sold pet snacks. I pointed to aisle three. She smiled and said her dog was a rare *breed* that only ate natural food. I checked the label on every bag for her. Tang leaned over and whispered that the woman visited every new shop on the street this way.
breed:2.cnHint: 一位女士带着一条特殊____的小狗来店里，让我帮她找合适的零食。
breed:2.hook: Tang's eyes said there was more to her visits than snacks.
breed:2.line: 'This *breed* is very picky — only the best will do.'

classify:2.en: The Manager handed me a thick folder and asked me to *classify* all the new product samples by type before morning. I spread them across the counter — drinks, snacks, daily goods, frozen items. Lin walked past, glanced at my piles, and rearranged two stacks without saying a word.
classify:2.cnHint: 店长让我在天亮前把所有新商品样品____好，隔壁咖啡店的林默默动了两堆。
classify:2.hook: Lin's silent correction made me wonder what else she already knew.
classify:2.line: 'Please *classify* the samples before the Manager checks at six.'

comment:2.en: Someone left a folded paper in our suggestion box. I opened it carefully. The *comment* inside said: 'Your night clerk remembered my usual order without asking — five stars.' I felt warm all the way to my toes. Then I noticed the handwriting matched the note on our back-room shelf exactly.
comment:2.cnHint: 意见箱里有人留下了一条____，而那笔迹让我心里一惊。
comment:2.hook: Whose hand wrote both notes, and why the mystery?
comment:2.line: 'That *comment* in the box — did you read it yet?'

component:2.en: The new self-checkout machine arrived in four boxes. Each box held one *component* — screen, base, scanner, and payment pad. I matched every part to the diagram. The last box was empty. I checked the diagram again; a small sticker read 'core unit — delivered separately, see Manager.' The Manager was not answering his phone.
component:2.cnHint: 新的自助结账机分四箱送到，但有一个关键____单独配送，店长却联系不上。
component:2.hook: Without that core unit, opening day could not happen.
component:2.line: 'Every *component* must arrive before we can test the machine.'

contrary:2.en: Lin told me the new branch would be quieter than our store. On *contrary* — the first test night brought twice as many customers, all curious neighbours. I barely kept up. Lin stood by the door looking genuinely surprised. The Manager simply smiled as if he had always known.
contrary:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林以为新店会很冷清，结果____，顾客比预期多了一倍。
contrary:2.hook: The Manager's calm smile hid something he had not shared yet.
contrary:2.line: 'On the *contrary*, I think this branch will be our busiest one.'

deny:2.en: A teenager put a snack in his pocket and headed for the door. I cleared my throat. He stopped, turned red, and tried to *deny* taking anything. I simply pointed at the small mirror in the corner. He placed the snack on the counter quietly. Then he asked, in a very small voice, if we were hiring.
deny:2.cnHint: 一个少年偷拿零食后想____，我只是指了指角落的镜子。
deny:2.hook: His last question was the one I did not expect at all.
deny:2.line: 'I do not *deny* it — I should have just asked the price first.'

depth:2.en: The Manager showed me the blueprint for the new branch. Its storage room had surprising *depth* — almost twice as long as it looked from the door. 'Hidden space,' he said, tapping the paper. I asked what it was for. He rolled the blueprint up, tucked it under his arm, and walked away whistling.
depth:2.cnHint: 新分店的仓库____出乎意料，店长却把图纸卷起来，什么也没解释。
depth:2.hook: A room that deep surely holds more than extra stock.
depth:2.line: 'The *depth* of that storage room surprised even the builders.'

distinguish:2.en: The Manager slid a folder across the counter. 'We have two candidate stores,' he said. 'One site gets morning sun, the other stays in shadow all day. Can you *distinguish* which photo is which?' I studied the pictures carefully — both streets looked almost the same to me.
distinguish:2.cnHint: 店长让我____两张候选新店的照片，但两条街看起来几乎一模一样。
distinguish:2.hook: Then I noticed something odd written on the back of one photo.
distinguish:2.line: 'You must *distinguish* the bright site from the dark one before we sign anything.'

document:2.en: Tang handed me a thick envelope just before dawn. 'The Manager needs this *document* delivered to the new store location before eight,' she said, yawning. I turned it over. A red stamp on the back read: CONFIDENTIAL. I had no idea what was inside, but my shift ended at seven.
document:2.cnHint: 阿糖让我在八点前把一份重要____送到新店地址，但我的班次七点就结束了。
document:2.hook: A corner of the envelope was already torn open.
document:2.line: 'Guard this *document* with your life — the Manager signed it himself.'

dozen:2.en: A delivery truck stopped outside at three in the morning. The driver carried in box after box of branded cups for the new branch. I counted a *dozen* boxes, then another dozen, then lost track entirely. The stock room was already full. I had nowhere left to put them.
dozen:2.cnHint: 凌晨三点，送货司机搬来了一____又一____的新分店用杯子，库房很快就满了。
dozen:2.hook: The last box was labelled with a store address I did not recognise.
dozen:2.line: 'I have one more *dozen* boxes on the truck — where do you want them?'

dull:2.en: Lin came in at two in the morning, looking tired. 'Night shifts are so *dull*,' she said, dropping into a chair near the magazine rack. She worked at a competing store two blocks away. I said nothing, but I was quietly counting how many customers had come in compared to her place.
dull:2.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林说深夜班太____，但我正悄悄在心里比较两家店的客流量。
dull:2.hook: She then asked a question that felt less like small talk and more like a test.
dull:2.line: 'Honestly, don't you find standing here all night just *dull*?'

fortune:2.en: The Manager pinned a red envelope to the notice board. 'A small *fortune* for whoever spots the best location for our new branch,' he announced, grinning. Tang and I exchanged a look. Neither of us had ever explored the neighbourhood that carefully — but we were both thinking the same thing.
fortune:2.cnHint: 店长宣布，谁能找到新分店最佳地址，就能得到一笔小小的____，我和阿糖对视了一眼。
fortune:2.hook: The envelope was thin — but the address written on it was very interesting.
fortune:2.line: 'Find us the right spot and a small *fortune* is yours.'

fulfil:2.en: The Manager left a note taped to the register: 'Night clerk must *fulfil* all tasks on the checklist before six.' I found the checklist. It had fourteen items. I had done three. Outside, the sky was already turning pale grey at the edges, and I still had the stock room to sort.
fulfil:2.cnHint: 店长留了张纸条，要求夜班员工在六点前____清单上的所有任务，但我才完成了三项。
fulfil:2.hook: The last item on the checklist was one nobody had warned me about.
fulfil:2.line: 'I trust you to *fulfil* every item before the morning crew arrives.'

gradually:2.en: The new branch plans were pinned to the back wall of the stock room. Every week the Manager added a detail — a floor map, a staff chart, a price list. The picture *gradually* became clearer, like a photo developing in a darkroom. Tonight a new sheet had appeared: a handwritten opening date.
gradually:2.cnHint: 新分店的计划图____贴满了库房后墙，今晚又多了一张手写的开业日期。
gradually:2.hook: The date was only nine days away, and no one had told the staff yet.
gradually:2.line: 'You will *gradually* see the whole plan — we share it piece by piece.'

incentive:2.en: Tang slapped a printed notice on the counter. 'The Manager is offering a bonus to the clerk who brings in the most new loyalty-card members this month,' she said. 'Real *incentive*, right?' She smiled in a way that was friendly but also slightly competitive. My shift had three hours left.
incentive:2.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我，店长给发展会员最多的员工提供奖金作为____，她的笑容友好却带着一丝竞争意味。
incentive:2.hook: She had already signed up eleven members — and my count was zero.
incentive:2.line: 'A cash bonus is the best *incentive* to make us both work harder.'

lower:2.en: The Manager taped a new price list near the door of the second store. I noticed the numbers on the bottom half — the shelf drinks had a *lower* price than at our main branch. He winked at me. 'Opening week only,' he said. I wondered if Lin knew yet.
lower:2.cnHint: 店长在新店门口贴出价格表，下排商品的____比本店还便宜。
lower:2.hook: Lin's footsteps were already loud on the stairs.
lower:2.line: 'The *lower* price is just for opening week, so don't get used to it.'

naturally:2.en: The new store had a small plant in the window. Nobody had put it there on purpose — Tang said a regular customer just left it one morning. Somehow it made the whole place feel warmer. Customers *naturally* drifted to that corner first, picked things up, and stayed a little longer.
naturally:2.cnHint: 新店角落里多了一盆植物，顾客们____地被吸引过去。
naturally:2.hook: But who was the customer who left it, and why?
naturally:2.line: 'People *naturally* stop here — something about this corner just feels right.'

passionate:2.en: Lin arrived at the new store carrying a folder of handwritten notes. She had mapped every shelf, every fridge, every small display. The Manager looked surprised. 'You didn't have to do all this,' he said. Lin just shrugged. She was *passionate* about store layout, and everyone in the room knew it.
passionate:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了满满一本笔记，对新店的陈列布置____得让店长都惊讶了。
passionate:2.hook: Her last note had a question mark no one could explain.
passionate:2.line: 'I'm *passionate* about layout — a good shelf can double the sales.'

pop:2.en: I was stocking the back fridge at the new store when a screen on the small wall display lit up by itself. A *pop* ad for a new energy drink started playing on a loop. Nobody had switched it on. Tang leaned around the corner, eyes wide. 'That thing wasn't plugged in this morning,' she said.
pop:2.cnHint: 新店仓库里一块广告屏突然自己亮起，播起了____广告。
pop:2.hook: The plug was still lying on the floor, disconnected.
pop:2.line: 'A good *pop* display there would double what we sell before midnight.'

possibly:2.en: We found a locked drawer behind the counter of the new store. The Manager tried every key on his ring — none of them worked. He held one small key up to the light. 'This could *possibly* open it,' he said slowly, 'but I've never seen it before.' Tang and I exchanged a look.
possibly:2.cnHint: 新店柜台后有一个上锁的抽屉，店长拿出一把不知来历的钥匙，说____能打开它。
possibly:2.hook: The key was not on any list the Manager had ever made.
possibly:2.line: 'This could *possibly* open it — but I have no idea where this key came from.'

previously:2.en: The new store stood where a small tea shop used to be. One regular customer walked in, looked around slowly, and touched the far wall with one hand. 'I *previously* came here every Sunday,' she said softly. She bought nothing, just stood there a moment, then walked back out into the night.
previously:2.cnHint: 新店原址____是一家茶馆，一位老顾客进来摸了摸墙，轻声说起旧事。
previously:2.hook: She left a folded paper on the counter without a word.
previously:2.line: 'I *previously* came here every Sunday — the smell was completely different.'

profession:2.en: A man in a neat jacket came in late and asked for a specific brand of pen we didn't carry. He explained his *profession* required exact handwriting tools — he was a contract writer for local businesses. He seemed puzzled that we had run out. He left his card on the counter and promised to return.
profession:2.cnHint: 一位深夜来访的男士说他的____需要特定的钢笔，可惜我们刚好缺货。
profession:2.hook: His business card listed three different names.
profession:2.line: 'My *profession* sounds simple, but the right pen changes everything I write.'

readily:2.en: Tang had visited the new store site the week before and *readily* agreed to help set it up. She showed up early, moved shelves without being asked, and had the back room sorted before noon. The Manager watched her from the doorway and said quietly to me, 'She was made for this kind of work.'
readily:2.cnHint: 阿糖____地答应去新店帮忙布置，提前到场，把一切都安排妥当了。
readily:2.hook: But she had turned down a full-time offer there once before.
readily:2.line: 'I *readily* said yes — setting up a new space is my favourite part of this job.'

preserve:2.en: The Manager found an old photo behind the register. 'We should *preserve* this,' she said, holding it up to the light. It showed the store on opening day, twenty years ago. Tang leaned over to look. 'Is that you in the corner?' The Manager smiled but did not answer.
preserve:2.cnHint: 店长在收银台后面发现了一张旧照片，她说应该____它。
preserve:2.hook: Why won't the Manager talk about that day?
preserve:2.line: 'We should *preserve* this,' she said, holding it up to the light.

procedure:2.en: A delivery truck arrived at dawn with twice the usual boxes. The driver handed me a thick folder. 'New *procedure*,' he explained. 'Every item needs a signature now.' I started signing, but Tang stopped me. 'Wait. Count first.' I opened the first box. Half the order was missing.
procedure:2.cnHint: 送货司机说有新的____，每件商品都需要签名。
procedure:2.hook: Who signed for the missing items last week?
procedure:2.line: 'New *procedure*,' he explained. 'Every item needs a signature now.'

reasonable:2.en: Lin walked in at midnight, which was strange—her own store closed at ten. 'I need twenty batteries,' she said. I named the price. 'That is not *reasonable*!' she replied. Tang appeared from the back room. 'Then why come here?' Lin went quiet and bought them anyway.
reasonable:2.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说价格不____。
reasonable:2.hook: What happened at Lin's store tonight?

reduction:2.en: The Manager put red stickers on the old calendars. '*Reduction* sale,' she announced. 'Fifty percent off.' An old man bought seven of them. 'For my grandchildren,' he said. But when he left, I saw him drop six in the recycling bin outside. He kept only one.
reduction:2.hook: Why did he throw away the other six?

season:2.en: Tang pinned a paper moon on the window. 'Mid-autumn *season*,' he said. 'Customers like it.' By evening, someone had drawn a rabbit on it in pen. Tang laughed when he saw it. 'Now it is perfect.' I checked the security video later. The artist was the Manager.
season:2.cnHint: 阿糖在窗上贴了纸月亮，说是中秋____。
season:2.hook: Why did the Manager draw it in secret?

sector:2.en: The Manager divided the store with tape on the floor. 'Your *sector* is drinks and snacks,' she told me. 'Tang handles the rest.' I nodded. But by noon, Tang was restocking my shelves and I was fixing his. The Manager watched us and smiled. 'Good,' was all she said.
sector:2.cnHint: 店长用胶带把店分成几个____，分配给我和阿糖。
sector:2.hook: Why did she smile when we switched jobs?
sector:2.line: 'Your *sector* is drinks and snacks,' she told me.

setting:2.en: The store lights had three buttons: bright, soft, and night. Tang always chose soft. 'Best *setting* for tired eyes,' he said. One evening, a student fell asleep at the table near the window. Tang dimmed the lights further. The Manager saw but said nothing. The student woke at dawn.
setting:2.cnHint: 阿糖说柔和是疲劳眼睛的最佳____。
setting:2.hook: How many others has Tang let sleep here?

shrink:2.en: I washed my new uniform and hung it to dry. By morning, it had started to *shrink*. The sleeves barely reached my wrists. Tang saw me struggling and laughed. 'Same thing happened to me.' He opened a drawer. Inside were five uniforms, each smaller than the last.
shrink:2.hook: Why does Tang keep all the ruined uniforms?

employment:2.en: I found a folded paper behind the cash register. It was the Manager's old notebook. One page listed everyone's *employment* dates—mine was still blank. Tang started three years ago; someone named 'Wei' left last spring. I wondered if Wei also worked nights, and why they never stayed.
employment:2.cnHint: 我发现了一张记录员工____日期的旧纸条。
employment:2.hook: Who was Wei, and why did they leave?
employment:2.line: The Manager glanced at the page and said, 'Your *employment* here begins when you finish your first month.'

entire:2.en: A cardboard box arrived during my shift. The label said 'For Manager—Private.' Inside were photos of the store's *entire* history: the grand opening, old staff parties, faded faces I'd never met. One picture showed Lin standing inside our store, smiling, wearing our uniform. That made no sense.
entire:2.cnHint: 一个箱子里装着商店____历史的照片。
entire:2.hook: Why was Lin wearing our store uniform years ago?
entire:2.line: Tang saw the photo and whispered, 'That box contains the *entire* truth about Lin.'

gift:2.en: A small wrapped box sat on the counter when I arrived. No note, no name. I opened it carefully—a tiny silver bell, the kind that rings when a door opens. Tang said the old store cat used to wear one. Someone left this *gift* on purpose. But we haven't had a cat in years.
gift:2.cnHint: 有人留下了一个神秘的____在柜台上。
gift:2.hook: Who left the bell, and why now?
